title: Phase P2b Invites
description:
# Phase P2b Invites

## Goal and why

Phase P2b brings new people in. First the **default**: partifactory invite tokens (`/i/<id>`, counted uses), passkey
invite links (single and "up to N") that create **local passkey accounts**, passkey sign-in for local accounts,
"new passkey link" recovery, local `pf-*` groups, linking a local account to an IdP identity, pending-invite cleanup.
Then the **Authentik provisioner**, starting with its permission gate, which decides how much of it ships: the
`partifactory-invite` flow, add-by-email, IdP recovery links and IdP-side `pf-*` groups.

*Why last among the core:* the household already exists in the example deployment's IdP, and invites carry the most
identity work. *Why native invites are in v1:* without them a deployment with plain OIDC and no provisioner couldn't
invite anyone, and invites would quietly depend on Authentik.

*Done when (M2b):* with no provisioner, the admin mints an invite link from the share sheet, a new person creates a
passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out at once; with the Authentik provisioner on, an invited
email enrols the same way and removing them in the IdP locks them out within a minute.

## Members

- T39: Authentik provisioner permission gate against the real IdP; record tier A/B/C
- T40: Authentik invites: `partifactory-invite` flow behind /i/<id>, membership by API after enrolment
- T41: Authentik extras: add by email, IdP recovery links, IdP-side pf-* groups (per gate tier)
- T42: Cleanup lists: never-enrolled invitees, 180-day inactive users, one-click remove
- T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups

Phase exit: M2b: Milestone - P2b Invites done

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".

title: T39: Authentik provisioner permission gate against the real IdP; record tier A/B/C
description:
## Goal and why

With the Authentik provisioner (the example deployment's adapter), partifactory holds an IdP write credential. That credential must be least-privilege, and "that's verified, not assumed". The core's own `pf-*` check is defence in depth only, "because a compromised process would skip it". The gate tests the real IdP and decides how much of the provisioner ships (T40, T41). P2b, after Slice 1. With no provisioner, partifactory holds no IdP write credential at all and this gate doesn't apply.

## Scope

- `partifactory provision --gate` (Authentik plugin): using the **runtime** token (`PF_IDP_PROVISIONER_TOKEN`), try each forbidden operation and expect `403`; then expect `2xx` for creating an invitation, sending a recovery link, and changing membership of a `pf-test` group.
- Intended account: service account `partifactory-provisioner` that can read users/groups, create invitations, send recovery links, and change membership of `pf-*` groups **only** (Authentik object-level permissions on each `pf-*` group).
- Forbidden operations the account must **not** be able to do: add anyone to a non-`pf-*` group, create a group with `is_superuser`, edit flows or stages, create users with elevated attributes, read another application's provider secret. Also check that `pf-*` groups have no privileged parent (Authentik roles inherit down the group hierarchy).
- Outcome tier written to site config `[idp.provisioner] tier = "A" | "B" | "C"`:
  - **A** full: runtime account may create/manage `pf-*` groups and memberships.
  - **B** pre-created groups: `pf-*` groups are created by `provision` (bootstrap token, run by the admin), never at runtime; runtime account = invitations + recovery links + membership of pre-created groups.
  - **C** changes via `provision` only: if even membership can't be object-scoped, add-by-email and new groups are done by the admin through `provision`, not at runtime.
- The runtime reads the tier at start and hides UI for anything that tier must do through `provision`.
- Gate report in site config listing each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status, plus the Authentik version.
- Once run, `doctor` (T68) adds the provisioner 403 probe (plug-in point, no edge).

## Not in scope

The invite flow (T40), extras (T41), the generic native invites (T94), the directory adapter (T92).

## Design notes and decisions

- Unverified Authentik items (object-level permission names, `is_superuser` protection, blueprint-over-API, recovery-link permission) are gates (T03 spike, this gate), not assumptions.
- *(adapter)* §7 line: "The Authentik provisioner gets 403 from the IdP on a non-`pf-*` group, and the core refuses before calling. Gate results are recorded: no non-`pf-*` membership, no `is_superuser` groups, no flow or stage edits, no privileged parent groups."
- Site config is private; the public repo ships the gate code and a report template only.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Gate report in site config lists each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status".

- [ ] Report lists each forbidden op with observed status and the Authentik version; each allowed op with 2xx.
- [ ] Tier recorded; runtime reads it and hides tier-excluded UI.
- [ ] The core independently refuses non-`pf-*` membership changes before calling the IdP.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-adapter-authentik/tests/gate.rs` against a real Authentik in CI (container), plus a mock-server unit test `gate::tests::classifies_tiers`.
- `pf_adapter_authentik::tests::core_refuses_non_pf_group` (no HTTP call made; asserts log `event="provisioner.refused" reason="not_pf_group"`).
- Gate output asserted as JSON (`[{op, expected, observed, ok}]`).

## References

PLAN.md §3a Admin (Authentik adapter only: least-privilege), Invitations (Authentik facts); §5c The provisioner gate; §7 Identity and admin (adapter line); §6 P2b.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2b (epic "P2b Invites"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Gate report in site config lists each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T92: Authentik adapter: Directory over the API (60 s poll) + IdpProvisioner plugin (OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow)
  - T03: Authentik adapter spike: conditional-UI passkeys, blueprint-over-API, groups claim, membership API, recovery links
- Unblocks: 
  - T40: Authentik invites: `partifactory-invite` flow behind /i/<id>, membership by API after enrolment

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Fail closed: with no gate report recorded, the runtime treats the tier as **C** and refuses every IdP write; test `no_report_means_tier_c`.
acceptance_criteria: Gate report in site config lists each forbidden operation and its observed HTTP status

title: T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
description:
## Goal and why

Without native invites, "a deployment with plain OIDC and no provisioner couldn't invite anyone, and invites would quietly depend on Authentik". This is the default invite path (decision 23): partifactory mints its own `/i/<id>` links, registers the invitee's passkey itself (`webauthn-rs`, already in the binary for step-up), creates a local account and lands them on the part already granted. It also makes an IdP-less deployment possible (every person a local account), which the portability lane (T93) exercises. P2b, after Slice 1; feeds T40, T42, T63 and M2b.

- *Why grants in partifactory:* "per-part access never depends on IdP group plumbing (Authentik invitations, for one, can't set groups)".
- *Why multi-use:* "single-use links pasted into family chats lose a race and confuse everyone else."

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after all subtasks are closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T94.a** Invite tokens: `/i/<id>`, kinds, counted uses, status, expiry, revoke, outstanding cap, rate limits; invite card.
- **T94.b** Passkey registration + local accounts + passkey sign-in (discoverable, conditional UI) on the workspace.
- **T94.c** Recovery links ("Send a new passkey link") and linking a local account to an IdP identity.
- **T94.d** Local `pf-*` groups, grants keyed on the invite, the invite UI in the share sheet/admin, and `part_link_for {action: "invite"}`; passkey offer on the device-approval page.

Flow (verbatim §3a): `/i/<id>` → one field ("What should we call you?", username generated) → **passkey creation, required**, which partifactory registers itself (`webauthn-rs`) → a local account is created → land on the part with the invite's grants applied. No email and no password. 7-day default expiry. The dialog offers **"for one person"** (single use) or **"for a group chat: up to N people"**, counted by partifactory. Lost passkey → the admin clicks "Send a new passkey link" on that *existing* person: a single-use `/i/<id>` of kind `recovery` bound to that account, which registers a new passkey and revokes the old ones. A local account can later be **linked to an IdP identity** (sign in with OIDC once while signed in locally). New group: "Make a group for this" creates a local `pf-<name>` group in partifactory's tables. Pending invites show status (sent, opened, enrolled, expired) with one-click revoke.

Tables (verbatim DDL):
```sql
CREATE TABLE invites (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                  -- i_...; handed out as /i/<id>, which records opens
  idp_ref         TEXT,                              -- provisioner only: IdP invitation (unlimited until expiry) or recovery id; NULL for native invites
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('single','multi','email','recovery')),
  max_uses        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,        -- counted here; the IdP has no use count
  uses            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  email           TEXT,
  target_user_id  TEXT REFERENCES users(id),         -- recovery
  land_part_id    TEXT REFERENCES parts(id),
  grant_role      INTEGER CHECK (grant_role BETWEEN 0 AND 3),
  groups          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(groups)),  -- pf-* groups, added by API after enrolment
  status          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sent','opened','enrolled','expired','revoked')),
  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  opened_at       INTEGER,
  expires_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  revoked_at      INTEGER,
  CHECK (uses <= max_uses)
) STRICT;
CREATE TABLE invite_enrolments (
  invite_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES invites(id),
  user_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  at        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (invite_id, user_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
plus `users.auth_source = 'local'` (no `idp_issuer`/`idp_sub`), `passkeys.purpose = 'login'`, `groups.source = 'local'` with `managed = 1` and `name LIKE 'pf-%'`.

Click budgets: Mint a passkey invite link (admin): Share → "Invite someone" → **Copy link** (+ step-up). Accept a passkey invite: open → type a name → **passkey tap** → on the part (§4a.7: "open → name → Create passkey → biometric", **3 + type**).

## Not in scope

The Authentik invite flow and add-by-email (T40/T41), cleanup lists (T42), the invite card's SVG rendering if T119 isn't done (use static text). partifactory sends no email.

## Design notes and decisions

- Inviting new people is admin-only with step-up (outward action); agents can only hand over `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` (decision 34).
- Invite "opened" is recorded by partifactory's `/i/<id>` wrapper because the IdP has no open event; counts live here for every kind.
- §7: "Local accounts: passkey-only (no password path exists), a recovery link revokes the old passkeys, and an invite token beyond its use count is refused."

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "With no provisioner configured, an invitee creates a passkey (virtual authenticator) and lands on the part already granted; status moves sent->opened->enrolled; the N+1th use is refused; a recovery link keeps the same account and grants and revokes the old passkey".

- [ ] All subtasks closed.
- [ ] Each dag criterion verified in e2e on the T24 harness (Chromium virtual authenticator) with no `[idp.provisioner]`, and in the IdP-less portability pass.
- [ ] Click budgets asserted.

## Tests

- e2e `tests/e2e/native_invite.spec.ts` (`invite_single_lands_on_part`, `invite_multi_n_plus_one_refused`, `recovery_keeps_account_revokes_old`), asserting server log events `event="invite.open"`, `event="invite.enrol" outcome="ok"|"uses_exhausted"`, `event="passkey.revoke" reason="recovery"`; artifacts in `target/e2e-logs/<test>/`.
- Unit tests in subtasks.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (Default: native invites), How people sign in (local passkey accounts), UX click budgets; §4a.6 Invites; §4a.7; §5e `invites`, `invite_enrolments`, `users`, `passkeys`, `groups`; §5f Invites + accounts row; §7 Identity; decision 23.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2b (epic "P2b Invites"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): With no provisioner configured, an invitee creates a passkey (virtual authenticator) and lands on the part already granted; status moves sent->opened->enrolled; the N+1th use is refused; a recovery link keeps the same account and grants and revokes the old passkey
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
- Unblocks: 
  - T40: Authentik invites: `partifactory-invite` flow behind /i/<id>, membership by API after enrolment
  - T42: Cleanup lists: never-enrolled invitees, 180-day inactive users, one-click remove
  - T63: Family onboarding: invite into the family space, first-run tour, personal space
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T94.a: Invite tokens /i/<id>: kinds, counted uses, status, expiry, revoke, outstanding cap
  - T94.b: Local passkey accounts: registration, discoverable sign-in with conditional UI (webauthn-rs)
  - T94.c: Recovery links ("Send a new passkey link") and linking a local account to an IdP identity
  - T94.d: Local pf-* groups, invite UI in the share sheet/admin, `part_link_for {action: "invite"}`

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T120 ("Make a group for this" lives in the A-group rung; the invite rung lives in the inward share sheet) and T117 (`#share=invite` relies on the fragment reader). Sibling edges: T94.d depends on T94.b (registration) and T94.c (recovery, "Send a new passkey link").
- Passkey purposes: device approval (T44) and step-up accept **any** non-revoked passkey of the person (`login` or `stepup`); the `/device` "register a passkey" offer applies only to IdP people with none, so a local-account person is never asked for a second passkey.
- T93's IdP-less pass runs this bead's spec (noted there).
acceptance_criteria: With no provisioner configured, an invitee creates a passkey (virtual authenticator) and lands on the part already granted; status moves sent->opened->enrolled; the N+1th use is refused; a recovery link keeps the same account and grants and revokes the old passkey

title: T94.a: Invite tokens /i/<id>: kinds, counted uses, status, expiry, revoke, outstanding cap
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory's own invite link is always `parts.<domain>/i/<id>`, whichever provisioner (if any) runs behind it, so opens, counts and grants live in partifactory's tables.

## Scope

- Mint (admin, step-up): kinds `single` (max_uses 1) and `multi` ("for a group chat: up to N people", default N 5), 7-day default expiry, `land_part_id`, `grant_role`, optional `groups` (pf-*). Copy link shown once, with a QR code.
- `GET /i/<id>`: records `opened_at` and moves `sent → opened`. The page is one centred card in partifactory branding; its og card is the invite card ("You're invited to a part on partifactory", plus the inviter's display name only if they opt in) and never shows the part title until the invitee has enrolled.
- Use counting under the writer (`uses <= max_uses`); the N+1th use → "This invite has been used. Ask whoever sent it for a new one." (`410 · INVITE USED`); expired → `expired`.
- Revoke (one click, 10 s undo toast); cap on outstanding invites; enrolment rate-limited per invite and per IP (T30 route class).
- Status list with chips, sent/opened times.
- Audit rows `invite.create`, `invite.revoke`.

## Not in scope

Passkey registration and account creation (T94.b), recovery (T94.c), the invite UI in the share sheet (T94.d), the Authentik-backed invitation behind `/i/<id>` (T40), cleanup lists (T42).

## Design notes and decisions

- Counts live in partifactory for every invite kind because native invites have no IdP and Authentik has no use count.
- Uses are incremented inside the single writer, so concurrent enrolments on a multi-use link can't overshoot `max_uses` (the CHECK is a backstop).
- Multi-use links exist because single-use links pasted into family chats lose a race.
- Expired or used links show the same plain page whatever the reason, so they don't reveal the part.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Status transitions sent→opened→enrolled; N+1th use refused; expired and revoked links refused.

## Tests

`pf_auth::invites::tests::use_count_race` (1,000 concurrent enrolments on max_uses N -> exactly N succeed), `::expiry`, `::revoke`; logs `event="invite.open"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations; §4a.6 Invites, Error pages (410 · INVITE USED); §4c Invite card; §5d Abuse (invites); §5e `invites`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Decided: the outstanding-invites cap defaults to 50 (`[limits] invites_outstanding`), error `quota_exceeded {kind: "invites"}`; enrolment is rate-limited per invite and per IP under the T30 route class `invite_enrol`.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Status transitions sent→opened→enrolled; N+1th use refused; expired and revoked links refused.

title: T94.b: Local passkey accounts: registration, discoverable sign-in with conditional UI (webauthn-rs)
description:
## Goal and why

A person with no IdP account (or a deployment with no IdP) needs a real account, passkey-only, created by partifactory itself.

## Scope

- Registration during invite acceptance: one field "What should we call you?" (display name; username generated, unique), then `webauthn-rs` 0.5 passkey creation (discoverable credential, required), `rp.id` = `[domain] apex`; create `users` row with `auth_source='local'`, `passkeys` row `purpose='login'`; insert `invite_enrolments`; apply grants; land on the part.
- Sign-in on the workspace for local accounts: discoverable credentials + conditional UI (autofill), 2-interaction budget ("pick the passkey from autofill + biometric").
- Sessions as for OIDC users (`__Host-pf_session`, 30 days sliding).
- No password path exists anywhere.
- IdP-less deployments: with no `[idp]`, every person is a local account; admin via `partifactory admin bootstrap` (T28).
- Local accounts count in `everyone-signed-in`.

## Not in scope

Invite token handling (T94.a), recovery and IdP linking (T94.c), admin step-up passkeys (T28, `purpose='stepup'`), `admin bootstrap` (T28).

## Design notes and decisions

- Passkey-only: no password path exists anywhere (§7), which also makes phishing via parts inert.
- `rp.id` is the apex, matching step-up (T28), so one credential model serves the workspace and part-host wrappers.
- Conditional UI (autofill) keeps sign-in at 2 interactions, per §3a's budget.
- Local accounts are first-class: they count in `everyone-signed-in` and work in an IdP-less deployment, which the portability lane exercises.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Invitee creates a passkey with the virtual authenticator and lands on the part already granted; can sign in again later with the passkey alone.

## Tests

`pf_auth::local::tests::register_and_login` (webauthn-rs soft authenticator); e2e via T94 spec; logs `event="passkey.register" purpose="login"`, `event="session.create" auth_source="local"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a How people sign in (local passkey accounts), Invitations step 1; §5e `users`, `passkeys`; §5f People sign-in row.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T94.a: Invite tokens /i/<id>: kinds, counted uses, status, expiry, revoke, outstanding cap

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Reserved usernames: local-account creation refuses the `svc-` prefix (reserved for service identities, T64.b) with `invalid_input`.

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Tests add the e2e `local_signin_two_interactions` (conditional UI + biometric, the §3a budget of 2).
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Invitee creates a passkey with the virtual authenticator and lands on the part already granted; can sign in again later with the passkey alone.

title: T94.c: Recovery links ("Send a new passkey link") and linking a local account to an IdP identity
description:
## Goal and why

A lost passkey must not create a zombie second account or lose history; a household that later adopts an IdP keeps everyone's history.

## Scope

- Admin clicks "Send a new passkey link" on an existing person: a single-use `/i/<id>` with `kind='recovery'`, `target_user_id` set; opening it registers a new passkey for that same account and sets `revoked_at` on all old passkeys; grants and history unchanged. Step-up required.
- Link to IdP: while signed in locally, sign in with OIDC once; the `users` row gains `idp_issuer`/`idp_sub` and `auth_source` changes to `'oidc'` (respecting the CHECK), keeping the user id; refuse if that IdP identity already belongs to another user.
- Audit rows for both.

## Not in scope

First-time registration (T94.b); IdP-side recovery for IdP people (T41, via `POST /api/v3/core/users/{id}/recovery/`); cleanup of stale accounts (T42).

## Design notes and decisions

- Recovery binds to the existing account (`target_user_id`) so history and grants stay and no zombie account appears (round 1 review S4).
- Old passkeys are revoked in the same transaction that registers the new one, so a stolen device stops working the moment recovery completes.
- Linking to an IdP keeps the user id stable, so grants, authorship and connections carry over when a household adopts an IdP.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recovery keeps the same user id and grants and revokes the old passkey (old passkey assertion fails).
- [ ] Linked account signs in via OIDC and keeps its parts and grants.

## Tests

`pf_auth::recovery::tests::revokes_old_passkeys`, `pf_auth::link::tests::link_local_to_oidc` (with the Dex harness); logs `event="passkey.revoke" reason="recovery"`, `event="account.link" outcome="ok"|"identity_in_use"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (Lost passkey; linking), §7 Identity (recovery revokes old passkeys); §5c Identity and DR.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T94.b: Local passkey accounts: registration, discoverable sign-in with conditional UI (webauthn-rs)

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- After linking a local account to an OIDC identity (`auth_source` → `oidc`), the person's `login` passkeys keep working: sign-in accepts either path.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Recovery keeps the same user id and grants and revokes the old passkey (old passkey assertion fails).
- [ ] Linked account signs in via OIDC and keeps its parts and grants.

title: T94.d: Local pf-* groups, invite UI in the share sheet/admin, `part_link_for {action: "invite"}`
description:
## Goal and why

Close the loop in the UI: the admin can invite from where they share, make a group for a part, and an agent can point the admin at the right sheet.

## Scope

- Local groups: "Make a group for this" (admin) creates `groups` row `source='local'`, `managed=1`, name `pf-<name>`; membership edits change instantly and bump part epochs for affected parts (directory diff).
- Share sheet: "Invite someone" (admin, step-up in-sheet) → `Invite link` ("For one person" / "For a group chat: up to [5] people", expiry 7 days, what they'll get, **Copy link** once, QR) and `By email` (only with a provisioner; otherwise the sheet offers the invite link instead). Pending invites for this part with status and revoke. Admin → Invites list with status chips, "Send a new passkey link", "Clean up" (T42).
- Deep link fragment `#share=invite` opens the sheet on that rung.
- Op: `part_link_for {action: "invite", name}` → `https://<name>-part.<domain>/#share=invite`, `who: "admin"`; contract section updated in the same change.
- Device-approval page (`/device`): for a person without a partifactory passkey, offer to register one for next time (from T94, per §3b).

## Not in scope

Token mechanics (T94.a), registration (T94.b), IdP-side pf-* groups and add-by-email (T41), the other share-sheet rungs (T31, T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- Inviting and group creation are outward actions: admin-only with step-up, never an agent op (decision 34); agents get the `#share=invite` deep link instead.
- Local `pf-*` groups live in partifactory's tables and change instantly, with epoch bumps for affected parts, so removal takes effect at once.
- 'By email' is shown only when a provisioner exists, because partifactory never sends email.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Click budget: Share → "Invite someone" → Copy link (+ step-up).
- [ ] `part_link_for {action: "invite"}` returns the deep link; the link grants nothing (non-admin sees the sheet without the option).
- [ ] No agent op can create an invite or group on any surface.

## Tests

e2e `tests/e2e/invite_ui.spec.ts` (click budget counter), `crates/pf-ops/tests/part_link_for_invite.rs`, `crates/pf-ops/tests/no_agent_invites.rs`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (New group), Share sheet; §4a.6 Share sheet, Invites; §4 `part_link_for`; §3b Device grant (approval page passkey offer).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T94.a: Invite tokens /i/<id>: kinds, counted uses, status, expiry, revoke, outstanding cap

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

- [ ] Click budget: Share → "Invite someone" → Copy link (+ step-up).

title: T40: Authentik invites: `partifactory-invite` flow behind /i/<id>, membership by API after enrolment
description:
## Goal and why

For the example deployment, invitees should become real IdP users (SSO with the other household services) while the invite link, counts and grants stay partifactory's own. This is the Authentik provisioner adapter's invite path; it sits behind the same `/i/<id>` tokens as native invites (T94) and ships to the extent the gate (T39) allows. P2b, after Slice 1.

## Scope

Verbatim facts it's built on (§3a, checked 2026-10-23): Authentik invitations **can't set groups** (custom attributes become user attributes, groups come from the User Write stage), and there's **no use count**, only single-use or unlimited-until-expiry.
- `/i/<id>` 302s to an Authentik invitation bound to a dedicated **`partifactory-invite`** flow: invitation → one field → **passkey enrolment, required** → user write (into one holding group) → login → land on the part.
- After the first login, partifactory matches the new `sub` to the invite (carried in the login `state`), applies the invite's grants, and adds any `pf-*` memberships by API (per gate tier: A runtime; B pre-created groups only; C via `provision`).
- The Authentik invitation is unlimited-until-expiry, and partifactory deletes it at the Nth enrolment (`invites.idp_ref`, `max_uses`, `uses`).
- The flow is partifactory-owned (cloned/provisioned by T92's `IdpProvisioner`), with partifactory branding; shared flows untouched.
- Selected by `[idp.provisioner] kind = "authentik"`; with `none`, T94's native path is used.

## Not in scope

Add-by-email, IdP recovery links, IdP-side group management (T41); native invites (T94); the gate (T39).

## Design notes and decisions

- Grants never depend on IdP groups; the holding group just satisfies the flow's User Write stage.
- The `state` parameter binds the login to the invite; a mismatch or replay grants nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "With the Authentik provisioner on, an invitee enrols with a virtual authenticator through the IdP and lands on the part already granted; the Authentik invitation is deleted at the Nth enrolment".

- [ ] e2e against a real Authentik container: enrol via passkey (virtual authenticator) → land on the part granted; `invites.status` enrolled; for a multi invite with max N, the Authentik invitation is deleted after the Nth enrolment and the N+1th use is refused by partifactory.
- [ ] `pf-*` memberships applied per tier.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/authentik_invite.spec.ts` (adapter lane, not in the portability lane); asserts logs `event="invite.idp_redirect"`, `event="invite.enrol" source="authentik"`, `event="provisioner.invitation_delete"`; artifacts include Authentik container logs.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (Adapter: the Authentik provisioner); §5c provision Order (invite flow); §5e `invites.idp_ref`; §6 P2b.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2b (epic "P2b Invites"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): With the Authentik provisioner on, an invitee enrols with a virtual authenticator through the IdP and lands on the part already granted; the Authentik invitation is deleted at the Nth enrolment
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T39: Authentik provisioner permission gate against the real IdP; record tier A/B/C
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
- Unblocks: 
  - T41: Authentik extras: add by email, IdP recovery links, IdP-side pf-* groups (per gate tier)

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- N+1 race: the Authentik invitation is deleted only at the Nth enrolment, so an N+1th person can finish IdP enrolment first. The OIDC callback with an exhausted invite in `state` shows `410 · INVITE USED`, creates no grants, and the orphan IdP user appears in T42's never-enrolled list (deleted in the IdP per tier). Test `n_plus_one_mid_flow_no_grants`.
acceptance_criteria: With the Authentik provisioner on, an invitee enrols with a virtual authenticator through the IdP and lands on the part already granted; the Authentik invitation is deleted at the Nth enrolment

title: T41: Authentik extras: add by email, IdP recovery links, IdP-side pf-* groups (per gate tier)
description:
## Goal and why

The remaining provisioner features for IdP people: inviting by email (the IdP sends it; partifactory sends no email), recovering a lost passkey without a new account, and `pf-*` groups manageable from either side, each only as far as the gate tier allows. Completes P2b with T42 (milestone M2b).

## Scope

- **Add by email** (admin, step-up): creates the IdP user + `pf-*` groups, then triggers the IdP's "set up your account" email; tracked as `invites.kind='email'`. Without a provisioner the share sheet offers the invite link instead. Click budget: Share → "Invite someone" → email → **Send** (+ step-up).
- **Lost passkey** for IdP people uses an IdP recovery link (`POST /api/v3/core/users/{id}/recovery/`) bound to the same user ("new passkey link"), `invites.kind='recovery'`, `idp_ref` = recovery id; same `sub`, same grants.
- **New groups** are IdP groups named `pf-<name>` (`groups.source='idp_api'`, `managed=1`, `idp_id` set), manageable from either side.
- Tier handling: tier A does these at runtime; tier B/C hand group creation (B) or also add-by-email and membership (C) to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP; the UI hides what the tier excludes.

## Not in scope

The invite flow (T40), cleanup lists (T42), the gate (T39).

## Design notes and decisions

- Every runtime IdP write goes through the gate tier recorded by T39; the tier is read at start, and the UI hides what it excludes, so a tier-C deployment never shows a button that would fail.
- Deferred changes are emitted as `provision` items the admin runs with the bootstrap token, because `pf-*` group creation is exactly the privilege the runtime account may lack.
- Recovery uses the IdP's own recovery link so the `sub` (and so every grant keyed on it) is preserved; a new account would orphan history.
- partifactory never sends email itself (§9); add-by-email only triggers the IdP's own mail.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "A recovery link keeps the same `sub` and grants; tier-B/C paths hand the change to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP".

- [ ] Recovery: same `sub`, same grants, new passkey works.
- [ ] Tier B/C: no runtime IdP write call is made for excluded operations (mock asserts zero calls); the change is emitted as a `provision` item.
- [ ] Add-by-email triggers the IdP email (Authentik test mail sink).

## Tests

`crates/pf-adapter-authentik/tests/extras.rs` with tier fixtures A/B/C; e2e `tests/e2e/authentik_recovery.spec.ts`; logs `event="provisioner.call" op=...` and `event="provisioner.deferred_to_provision" tier="B"|"C"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (Add by email; Adapter: Lost passkey, Add by email, New groups), Admin (tier fallbacks); §4a.7 budgets; §6 P2b.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2b (epic "P2b Invites"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A recovery link keeps the same `sub` and grants; tier-B/C paths hand the change to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T40: Authentik invites: `partifactory-invite` flow behind /i/<id>, membership by API after enrolment
- Unblocks: 
  - M2b: Milestone - P2b Invites done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Email invites never pass through `/i/<id>`, so grants apply at first OIDC login by matching a verified `email` claim to an open `kind = 'email'` invite (or by making the IdP flow's post-enrolment redirect `/i/<id>`); status moves to `enrolled`. Test added.
- Deferred tier-B/C changes live in a `kv` entry `provision_pending`, rendered on Admin → People/Groups with the exact `partifactory provision apply …` command and cleared when `provision` reports it applied. This is an admin-side ops list, not an approval queue.
acceptance_criteria: A recovery link keeps the same `sub` and grants; tier-B/C paths hand the change to `provision`, run by the admin, instead of calling the IdP

title: T42: Cleanup lists: never-enrolled invitees, 180-day inactive users, one-click remove
description:
## Goal and why

Invites and accounts accumulate; "invitees who never enrolled, and people inactive for 180 days, are listed for one-click cleanup", so access doesn't silently linger on a box that's left alone for years.

## Scope

- Admin → Invites "Clean up" and Admin → People lists:
  - never-enrolled invitees: invites in `sent`/`opened` past expiry (or old), with revoke;
  - inactive users: `users.last_seen_at` older than 180 days (status `active`).
- One-click remove (10 s undo toast instead of a confirm): sets `users.status = 'removed'`, revokes sessions (bumps minter epochs `minter:sess:<id>`), revokes the user's grants (part epochs bumped for affected parts), revokes their agent connections (cascade), writes an audit row per revoked grant. With the Authentik provisioner, also offers the IdP-side removal per tier.
- Works with no provisioner (local accounts and IdP users alike).

## Not in scope

Invite minting (T94), IdP extras (T41).

## Design notes and decisions

- Removal is a revoke, not a delete: `users.status='removed'` keeps history and authorship labels intact, while epoch bumps make it take effect on the very next request.
- 180 days is the plan's fixed default; it is computed from `last_seen_at`, which is updated on session use (batched), so the list is accurate to within a day.
- No confirmation dialog: one click with a 10 s undo toast, per the 'Revoke anything' budget; undo re-grants exactly what was revoked (from the audit rows).
- Agent connections of a removed person are revoked by the same cascade as §3b, so an agent can't keep acting for someone who's gone.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Fixture users appear in the right list and removal revokes their grants with audit rows".

- [ ] Fixtures: an expired never-enrolled invite and a 181-day-inactive user appear; a 179-day user doesn't.
- [ ] Removal: their next part request fails (epoch bump), sessions dead, one audit row per revoked grant; undo within 10 s restores.

## Tests

`pf_policy::cleanup::tests::lists_with_test_clock`, `::remove_revokes_and_audits`; e2e `tests/e2e/cleanup.spec.ts`; logs `event="user.remove" grants_revoked=N`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations (Either way: cleanup), UX (Revoke anything); §4a.6 Invites ("Clean up"); §5e `users`, `invites`, `audit`; §6 P2b.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2b (epic "P2b Invites"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Fixture users appear in the right list and removal revokes their grants with audit rows
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
- Unblocks: 
  - M2b: Milestone - P2b Invites done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- `users.last_seen_at` is written (batched) by the session extractor (T24.a); if it is missing there, this task adds it.
- A `removed` user signing in again via OIDC stays removed (403, no re-activation) until the admin restores them from Admin → People; test `removed_user_oidc_login_refused`.
- Undo restores grants and status only; sessions stay dead (people re-sign-in).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture users appear in the right list and removal revokes their grants with audit rows

title: M2b: Milestone - P2b Invites done
description:
## Goal and why

Exit of phase **P2b Invites**: the admin can bring new people in, with no provisioner by default (native invites + local passkey accounts, decision 23), and optionally through the Authentik provisioner adapter whose permission gate decides how much ships.

## Scope (what P2b contains)

First the default: partifactory invite tokens (`/i/<id>`, counted uses), passkey invite links (single and "up to N") that create local passkey accounts, passkey sign-in for local accounts, "new passkey link" recovery, local `pf-*` groups, linking a local account to an IdP identity, pending-invite cleanup. Then the Authentik provisioner, starting with its permission gate: the `partifactory-invite` flow, add-by-email, IdP recovery links and IdP-side `pf-*` groups.

Direct dependencies: T41, T42.

## Acceptance criteria (P2b "Done when")

- [ ] With no provisioner configured, the admin mints an invite link from the share sheet, a new person creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out at once.
- [ ] With the Authentik provisioner on, an invited email address enrols the same way, and removing them in the IdP locks them out within a minute.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Invitations, §6 Phases (P2b), §5c provisioner gate.

## Dependency context

- This milestone depends on (blocks edges): 
  - T41: Authentik extras: add by email, IdP recovery links, IdP-side pf-* groups (per gate tier)
  - T42: Cleanup lists: never-enrolled invitees, 180-day inactive users, one-click remove
- Unblocks: nothing

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans).
acceptance_criteria: With no provisioner, the admin mints an invite link, a new person creates a passkey and lands on the part, and removing them locks them out at once; with the Authentik provisioner, an invited email enrols and removing them in the IdP locks them out within a minute

title: Phase P0 Core (local)
description:
# Phase P0 Core (local)

## Goal and why

Phase P0 builds the local core: repo, schema + migrations, blob store (temp -> fsync -> rename), source manifests + build
records, the build child process, HTML/Markdown/text/SVG/code **and TSX** kinds with the golden corpus, mirror-on-build,
the content listener with **path caps and the canonical sandbox CSP**, the prelude with the `localStorage` shim and
`runtime_errors`, the operation registry, the HTTPS API with `/openapi.json`, the `part` CLI (dev token), logs + metrics,
and a same-machine regression bench. Spikes: rolldown/oxc, rmcp, Leptos vs templates, **the sandbox on real browsers**
(including the wrapper flow), and the Authentik adapter spike.

*Why the sandbox and TSX in P0:* the serving model and the compiler are the two things most likely to force a redesign.
Finding a rolldown or Safari problem in P3 would be finding it last. Slice 1 keeps the compiler spike (T02) and runs the
`tsx` kind itself (T60) right after S1 (decision 39, provisional), so P0's "Done when" (milestone M0) is met just after
the slice ships.

*Done when (M0):* `part put x.html --name packing` opens at `packing-part.localhost:8081/c/<cap>/` under the sandbox, a
Claude-written page using `localStorage` and a CDN `<script>` runs unchanged there, and the TSX corpus compiles.

- T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
- T09: Name rules, permanent reservation, title->name derivation, deterministic ranked alternatives
- T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
- T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
- T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
- T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
- T14: Mirror-on-build: fetch allowlisted CDN refs in the parent, pin by hash, rewrite build output only
- T15: Capability tokens: path caps, HMAC with daily HKDF kid keys, deterministic windows, epochs + boot floor
- T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
- T17: Shared blob host (blobs-part): serve only shared_blobs hashes, public immutable, ACAO *
- T18: Logs + metrics: redacted JSON tracing, Prometheus on :9090 behind PF_METRICS_TOKEN, /healthz, /readyz skeleton
- T19: Dev/test identity fake: Authn + Directory traits with a static-file implementation
- T20: Operation registry crate (pf-ops): typed ops, scopes, hints, executable examples, one error catalogue
- T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
- T22: `part` CLI generated from the registry (`part <op> --json`) + ergonomic aliases, env-based auth, dev token
- T23: Regression bench: same-machine content-path bench vs previous release, fail on >10 % regression
- T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps
- T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
- T72: Spike: opaque-origin sandbox, wrapper flow and apex-rp.id WebAuthn on real browsers
- T118: Kind renderers after Slice 1: svg (sandboxed document) and code (syntect viewer)
- G06: Toolchain upgrade: background rebuild of live parts with golden diff, never auto-switching live
- G08: Sandbox compat corpus: 30 Claude-written artifacts and 10 Vite builds rendered under the sandbox in CI

It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard

title: T01: Cargo workspace, crate layout, CI (fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit), Renovate
description:
## Goal and why

Create the repository skeleton every other task builds in: one Cargo workspace that produces **one static binary** (`partifactory`, with `part` as a CLI alias, every asset embedded, the build worker being the same binary re-exec'd), a crate layout that keeps the core free of vendor adapters, and a CI pipeline that enforces formatting, lints, tests, licences and advisories from the first commit.

Why it matters: partifactory is a household server that is "set up once and then left alone", so dependency hygiene (Renovate + `cargo audit` + `cargo deny`, base images pinned by digest) has to be automatic from day one, not retrofitted. Portability (decision 22) also starts here: the core crates must never import adapter types (Cloudflare, Authentik), and CI must not depend on any one CI vendor's API. T01 is the first task on the Slice 1 critical path (T01 -> T05 -> T06 -> T08 -> T12 -> T13 -> T16 -> T17 -> T62 -> T77 -> T96 -> T95 -> T97 -> S1); every task depends on it transitively.

## Scope

- A Cargo workspace at the repo root with `resolver = "2"`, a pinned toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml`, stable, with `rustfmt`, `clippy`), and `[profile.release]` with `panic = "abort"` (the plan relies on build panics killing only the build child, never the server; see T13) plus LTO/strip suitable for a ~20 MB `FROM scratch` musl image (T37).
- Crate layout (empty crates with a `lib.rs` doc comment stating each crate's responsibility; names are the shared convention used by every bead):
  - `crates/pf-config`, `crates/pf-db`, `crates/pf-blobs`, `crates/pf-model`, `crates/pf-build`, `crates/pf-caps`, `crates/pf-serve`, `crates/pf-prelude`, `crates/pf-ops`, `crates/pf-api`, `crates/pf-mcp`, `crates/pf-cli`, `crates/pf-auth`, `crates/pf-policy`, `crates/pf-oauth`, `crates/pf-ui`, `crates/pf-obs`, `crates/pf-janitor`, `crates/pf-backup`, `crates/pf-provision`, `crates/pf-adapter-cloudflare`, `crates/pf-adapter-authentik`, `crates/pf-render`, `crates/pf-runner`, `crates/partifactory` (the binary).
  - A hello-world `partifactory` binary with subcommand stubs via `clap`: `serve`, `build-worker`, `runner`, `export`, `import`, `migrate`, `healthcheck`, `provision`, `doctor`, `deploy`, `config check`, `admin bootstrap`, `admin break-glass`, `bench`, `logs` (each prints "not implemented" and exits non-zero), and `argv[0] == "part"` dispatching to the CLI stub.
  - Directory placeholders: `tests/e2e/`, `tests/agent_surfaces/`, `tests/golden/`, `docs/spikes/`, `deploy/`, `deploy/proxy/`, `examples/ci/`.
- An architecture-boundary check: a CI step (e.g. `cargo deny` bans or a small `cargo metadata` script) that fails if any core crate (`pf-*` except `pf-adapter-*` and `partifactory`) depends on an adapter crate. Adapters plug in through traits defined in the core.
- CI jobs, written as plain scripts under `ci/` (`ci/fmt.sh`, `ci/clippy.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, `ci/deny.sh`, `ci/audit.sh`) so they run identically on a laptop, any forge's runner, or none; plus one workflow file for the forge in use that only calls those scripts:
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo nextest run --workspace` (nextest is the test runner for the whole project)
  - `cargo deny check` (licences, advisories, bans, sources) with a `deny.toml` that allows the licences the plan needs (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib, Unicode, MPL-2.0 if needed) and denies unknown git sources
  - `cargo audit`
- Renovate config (`renovate.json`): Cargo, Dockerfile base images pinned by digest, GitHub-Actions-style/Gitea workflow pins; grouping for the `oxc`/`rolldown` family must be **exact-pin only and never automerged** (their Rust APIs are 0.x and not semver-stable; T02/T60 pin and vendor them).
- Licence/credit housekeeping already in the repo stays: `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` (shartifacts by Lane Birmingham, MIT, credited for any adapted code or text), README credit line.

## Not in scope

- Any real functionality: config (T04), SQLite (T05), blobs (T07), logging (T18), etc.
- The release pipeline, OCI image, compose file and release assets (T37); arm64, SBOM, cosign and the example CI workflows `examples/ci/gitea-actions.yml` / `github-actions.yml` (T126).
- The same-machine regression bench (T23) and the portability lane (T93).

## Design notes and decisions

- **One binary** (§5): `rmcp`, `oxc`, `rolldown`, `resvg` and `webauthn-rs` live in the same static binary instead of sidecars; the build worker is `partifactory build-worker` re-exec'd. Keep compile times sane by isolating heavy deps (oxc/rolldown in `pf-build` only, behind a feature if needed).
- **CI is an example, not a dependency** (§5b, §5f): nothing reads a CI vendor's API. The source of truth is a private forge with a passive public GitHub mirror that runs **no Actions and holds no secrets**; so the gating workflow lives on the private forge, and the scripts are what matter. Document in the README how to run `ci/*.sh` locally.
- **Rust, not Go** (decision 2): static `FROM scratch` binary, memory safety on an internet-facing authorization server. Bend 2 was considered and set aside (I/O-bound service).
- Pick `cargo nextest` profiles: `default` and `ci` (retries 0, fail-fast off, JUnit output to `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` kept as an artifact).
- Renovate "runs against any forge", so it's compatible with the portability goal.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "CI green on a hello-world binary; `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` run in CI; Renovate opens a PR on a pinned dep".

- [ ] `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo nextest run --workspace` pass on a clean checkout.
- [ ] Every crate in the layout above exists with a responsibility doc comment.
- [ ] CI runs fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`), nextest, `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit`, each as a separate visible step, all green.
- [ ] A deliberately mis-formatted file or a clippy warning fails CI (verified once, then reverted).
- [ ] The adapter-boundary check fails when a core crate adds a dependency on `pf-adapter-cloudflare` (verified once).
- [ ] Renovate opens at least one PR against a deliberately outdated pinned dependency.
- [ ] `partifactory --help` lists the subcommand stubs; invoking the binary as `part` reaches the CLI stub.
- [ ] `ci/*.sh` run locally with the same results as CI.

## Tests

- `crates/partifactory/tests/cli_smoke.rs::help_lists_subcommands` - runs the binary with `--help`, asserts each stub name.
- `crates/partifactory/tests/cli_smoke.rs::argv0_part_dispatches_to_cli` - symlinks the binary as `part` in a temp dir and asserts the CLI stub banner.
- `ci/check-boundaries.sh` self-test: a fixture `Cargo.toml` that adds an adapter dep to `pf-model` makes it exit non-zero.
- CI keeps `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml` and the clippy/deny/audit outputs as artifacts on failure.

title: T09: Name rules, permanent reservation, title->name derivation, deterministic ranked alternatives
description:
## Goal and why

A part's name **is** its hostname, and its hostname is its link: `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`. Names are semantic and chosen by agents ("Sleep chart" -> `sleep-chart`), so they must be valid DNS labels, never collide with an old redirect, and a clash must come back with ready-to-use alternatives so the agent retries in one step. In Slice 1; consumed by T11 (create), T70 (renames), T29 (host -> part routing).

## Scope

- Module `pf_model::names`.
- **Rules**: `[a-z0-9-]`, 1–58 chars, no leading/trailing/double hyphens. (58 so that `<name>-part` fits a 63-char DNS label.) The same rule is enforced by the `parts.name` CHECK in T06.
- **Reserved in code, regardless of config**: `blobs` (the shared blob host `blobs-part.<domain>`). **Reserved by site config** (`[names] reserved`): infrastructure words and names that mirror existing services.
- **Ever-used names stay reserved**: the `names` table records every name ever used (`state` `active | redirect | tombstone`), never deleted; a retired/renamed/purged part's name is never reusable ("so a future part can't collide with an old redirect"). A purged part's name stays reserved forever.
- **Availability**: `check(name) -> Available | Invalid{reason} | Taken | Reserved`. Taken covers active, redirect and tombstone names.
- **Derivation**: `derive(title) -> name`: lowercase, transliterate/strip diacritics, non-alphanumerics -> `-`, collapse runs, trim hyphens, truncate to 58 at a hyphen boundary where possible; empty result -> `part`.
- **Alternatives** (`part_create {check_only: true, name?, title?, description?}` -> available? If not, ranked alternatives that are valid and free right now). "The generator is deterministic, with no LLM: drop stop words, try 2- and 3-token subsets of the title and description, then the space as a prefix, then numeric suffixes last." Output order is stable for the same inputs and DB state. **`name_taken` returns >= 3 valid free suggestions** (`details.suggestions`).
- Error shapes from the catalogue (T20): `name_taken` (HTTP 409, CLI exit 5, `details.suggestions`), `invalid_input` (400, `details.path = "name"`, `details.suggestion`).

## Not in scope

- The `part_create` op wiring (T11/T20); renames and 301s (T70); site-config parsing (T04 owns `[names] reserved`).

## Design notes and decisions

- **Names are not secret.** A private part's name is in its URL, and unfurlers show URLs. The agent contract tells agents to pick a neutral name for sensitive parts (Rule 7).
- Why deterministic alternatives: reproducible tests, no model dependency, and agents get the same answer on retry.
- Why reserve forever: renames 301 forever (T70), so reusing a name would hijack old links and home-screen installs.
- Reservation check and insert happen in the same writer transaction as part creation (unique constraint on `parts.name` and `names.name`), so two concurrent creates of one name can't both win.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Rule table test (length, hyphens, reserved list from site config); `blobs` is `name_taken` with no config; a retired name is rejected; `name_taken` returns >= 3 valid free suggestions".

- [ ] A table-driven rule test covers valid/invalid names (length 0, 1, 58, 59; leading/trailing/double hyphen; uppercase; underscore; unicode).
- [ ] `blobs` is rejected as `name_taken` with an empty site config; site-config reserved names are rejected.
- [ ] A name whose `names.state` is `redirect` or `tombstone` is rejected.
- [ ] For a taken name, >= 3 suggestions are returned, each valid and free at that moment, in a stable order.
- [ ] `derive("Sleep chart") == "sleep-chart"`; derivation output always passes the rule.

## Tests

- `pf_model::names::tests::rule_table`, `blobs_reserved_without_config`, `config_reserved`, `retired_name_rejected`.
- `pf_model::names::tests::suggestions_at_least_three_valid_free_stable` (fixture DB with many taken names; run twice, compare).
- `pf_model::names::tests::derive_property` (property test: any title derives to a valid name).
- `pf_model::names::tests::concurrent_create_same_name_one_wins` (two writers; one gets `name_taken`).

## References

PLAN.md §4 Names: semantic, chosen by the agent; §2 The link to post; §3e (purged names stay reserved); §5e `names`, `parts` CHECK; docs/agent-contract.md `part_create` (`name`, `check_only`, `name_taken`), Rule 7; §4b error table.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Rule table test (length, hyphens, reserved list from site config); `blobs` is `name_taken` with no config; a retired name is rejected; `name_taken` returns >= 3 valid free suggestions
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
- Unblocks: 
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
  - T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

title: T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
description:
## Goal and why

Spaces are one of the five core concepts: a named container with grants of its own, a quota and one owner; every part is in exactly one space. **Effective access = the highest role from the part's own grants and its space's grants, inherited live.** In Slice 1 there are personal spaces only (every person gets one at first sign-in); `family` and `system` are created later by `provision` (T32). "Moving a part to Family is how most household sharing happens", so getting the live-inheritance model right now keeps later sharing a one-tap action. In Slice 1; consumed by T11 (create lands in a space), T26 (policy), T32 (provision), T33 (quotas).

## Scope

- Module `pf_model::spaces` over the `spaces` and `grants` tables (T06).
- **Personal space per person**: `ensure_personal_space(user)` creates `spaces{kind: 'personal', slug: '~<username>', owner_user_id: user, title}` idempotently (unique partial index `spaces_one_personal`). Called on first sign-in (T24) and when a local account is created (T94), and by the dev identity fake (T19).
- **Default space**: `part_create` without `space` uses the creator's personal space; an agent acting for a person defaults to that person's personal space.
- **Space grants**: rows in `grants` with `target_kind = 'space'`. Provide `space_grants(space)`, `effective_role(subject_set, part)` helper that returns `max(part grants, space grants)` — reading the space grants at decision time (never copying them onto parts). A grant added to a space applies to its existing parts at once. (The full policy engine with subjects, groups, everyone-signed-in, expiry and audit is T26; T10 supplies the data access and the max rule.)
- Space table (verbatim):

| Space | Created by | Grants | Who may write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Personal (`~<username>`, one per person) | first sign-in | only its owner | the owner, and agents the owner connected |
| `family` | `provision` | `group:<household> → edit` | the household, and agents consented into it |
| `system` | `provision` | everyone signed in → view | the admin (holds Jig, the design-system part) |
| more | the admin | as set | as granted |

- **Per-space quota config**: `spaces.quota_parts`, `quota_bytes`, `quota_versions_day`; NULL means the default: a personal space 2,000 parts, 20 GiB and 1,000 versions a day. T10 exposes `effective_quota(space)`; **enforcement is T33**. Unlimited needs `[unsafe] quotas = "off"` (T114 registry).
- **Move a part** primitive: `move_part(part, to_space)` updates `parts.space_id` and bumps `epochs['part:<id>']` (access may have narrowed); permission check ("needs write access to both spaces") is the caller's via T26.

## Not in scope

- Creating `family` and `system` (T32, §3a). The policy engine (T26). Quota enforcement and Health entries (T33). Move to Family UI (T120); agent `move` via `part_share` (T52).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why live inheritance:* "everything in Family is the family's" has to stay true when someone joins the family later. Copying grants at creation would quietly leave new members out.
- There's no per-part "restrict below the space" in v1.
- Agent consent is limited to spaces: a connection for `~<owner>` + `family` can't see another person's personal space (enforced in T26/T43 using the space ids recorded on the connection).
- A space-grant change bumps the epoch of every part in that space so already-minted caps re-check (the epoch bump itself is T26's; T10 provides `parts_in_space`).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A part created without `space` lands in the creator's personal space; a grant added to a space applies to its existing parts at once".

- [ ] First sign-in creates exactly one personal space; repeated calls are no-ops.
- [ ] A part created without `space` is in the creator's personal space (and, for an agent, its person's).
- [ ] Adding a space grant `group:x -> view` makes `effective_role` return `view` for members on every existing part in the space, with no per-part rows written.
- [ ] `effective_quota` returns defaults for NULL columns and overrides otherwise.
- [ ] `move_part` bumps the part epoch.

## Tests

- `pf_model::spaces::tests::personal_space_idempotent`, `default_space_for_person_and_agent`.
- `pf_model::spaces::tests::space_grant_applies_live` (create 3 parts, add a space grant, check all 3; remove it, check all 3 drop).
- `pf_model::spaces::tests::effective_role_is_max` (property test over random part/space grant sets).
- `pf_model::spaces::tests::quota_defaults`, `move_bumps_epoch`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 The core idea (Space; Why live inheritance), §3a Spaces, §5d Quotas (defaults; NULL = default), §5e `spaces`, `grants`, Modelling decisions, Slice 1 "Personal spaces only".

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.

  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
- Unblocks: 
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
  - T33: Quotas per space and per agent connection (parts, versions/day, bytes), hits on Health
  - T63: Family onboarding: invite into the family space, first-run tour, personal space

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

title: T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
description:
## Goal and why

The domain service behind the core ops: create a part (link first, build second), read it, list its history, diff any two versions, soft-delete it to the 30-day bin, bring it back, and restore an old version as a new one. Every write is idempotent by `request_id`. This is what makes the agent contract's promises true at the model level: "a link right away, robustly", "you never lose work", "restore = append". It is surface-independent: T20/T21/T53 expose it as `part_create`, `part_get` and the `restore`/`delete`/`undelete` modes of `part_edit` (anchor edits themselves are T46). In Slice 1; consumed by T21, T46, T49, T76, T34.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- **T11.a** - create: name reservation, v0 placeholder, optional v1 from `content`/`files`, `from` fork, `expires_in` scratch parts, `check_only`, and the shared **idempotency layer** for every write.
- **T11.b** - read: get (version selection, files, content for small parts, file/range), history, diff of any two versions.
- **T11.c** - lifecycle: soft delete to the 30-day bin, undelete, purge eligibility, scratch expiry to the bin, restore-as-new-version.

Shared contract (verbatim from the agent contract):
- Results that change or describe a part carry the **mutation shape**: `{name, url, head, live, build: {id, status, warnings, errors}}`. `head` is the newest saved version number; `live` is the version people see (`null` until the first one goes live); `build` is the build of `head` (`queued`, `running`, `ok`, `failed`, `timeout`, `superseded`), or `null` before v1. `url` is always `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`.
- `request_id` is 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, unique per intended change, scoped to the connection (or person), kept 24 h. "Only a committed write uses up its id."
- Authorization: callers pass a resolved principal; the policy check (T26) and scope check (T43) wrap these functions. Until T26 lands, tests use an allow-all policy fake from T19.

## Not in scope

- Anchor edits, write/delete/rename file ops, rebase (T46); builds (T13); policy (T26); quotas (T33); the HTTP/MCP/CLI surfaces (T21, T53, T22); notes and `render: "text"` (T122); FTS (T76); the versions rail and bin UI (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- Creation returns **in < 10 ms**, before anything is built; the part's host works immediately with a "being made…" placeholder (T51 live-updates it).
- Fork writes zero new blobs: a new manifest pointing at the same hashes, with lineage in `parts.forked_from`.
- Restore is non-destructive and goes through the build like any other version.
- Deleted parts are hidden from search and the gallery, restorable by the owner or the admin, purged after 30 days (purge itself is a janitor job, T113); a purged part's name stays reserved forever (T09).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Retried create with the same request_id returns the same part; restore of v3 creates v(n+1) equal to v3; a fork writes zero new blobs; undelete at 29 days works, at 31 fails".

- [ ] All criteria of T11.a-c pass.
- [ ] One integration test drives create -> two versions -> diff -> delete -> undelete -> restore v1 through the service API with a fixed clock.

## Tests

`crates/pf-model/tests/part_service.rs::lifecycle_end_to_end` (test clock), asserting one structured log line per write (`event="part.write" op=… outcome=… request_id=… replayed=…`).

## References

PLAN.md §3d Creation contract, Idempotent every write, Latest vs live; §3e Versions and rollback, the bin; §4 op table (`part_create`, `part_get`, `part_edit` modes); docs/agent-contract.md `part_create`, `part_get`, `part_edit` (restore/delete/undelete), Rule 1; §5e `parts`, `versions`, `idempotency`.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Retried create with the same request_id returns the same part; restore of v3 creates v(n+1) equal to v3; a fork writes zero new blobs; undelete at 29 days works, at 31 fails
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
  - T09: Name rules, permanent reservation, title->name derivation, deterministic ranked alternatives
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
- Unblocks: 
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
  - T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T49: Agent read path (Slice 1): part_get full content <= 32 KiB, file/range, version, history, diff, build log, runtime_errors
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T11.a: Part create: name reservation, v0 placeholder, v1 from content/files, fork, scratch, check_only, idempotency layer

title: T11.a: Part create: name reservation, v0 placeholder, v1 from content/files, fork, scratch, check_only, idempotency layer
description:
## Goal and why

"Reserve a name and get the part's link at once, optionally with its first version. Returns in under 10 ms; any build happens after." This lets an agent hand the person the link first and build second, and a retried create after a timeout never makes a duplicate.

## Scope

- `create_part(principal, input)` with the `part_create` fields (verbatim from the agent contract):

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | str | yes (or `name` with `check_only`) | — | shown to people |
| `name` | str | no | derived from `title` | the host label: `[a-z0-9-]`, 1–58 chars, no leading, trailing or double hyphens |
| `kind` | `html` \| `markdown` \| `text` \| `files` | no | detected from the entry file | required with `content`; `tsx` comes after Slice 1 |
| `content` | str | no | — | the text of a one-file part |
| `files` | `{path: str \| {blob: sha256}}` | no | — | several files; text inline, bytes uploaded first |
| `space` | str | no | your person's personal space | a space slug your connection may write |
| `from` | str | no | — | fork: `"name"` or `"name@n"` |
| `expires_in` | str | no | — | scratch part: `"<n>h"` or `"<n>d"`, then it moves to the bin |
| `tags` | [str] | no | `[]` | |
| `description` | str | no | `""` | |
| `snapshots` | `daily` \| `hourly` \| `off` | no | `daily` | data snapshots of the part's shared data |
| `shared_data_writers` | `editors` \| `viewers` | no | `viewers` | who may write shared data besides editors |
| `live` | `always` \| `after_check` | no | `always` | `after_check`: the first version goes live only once its check passes |
| `check_only` | bool | no | `false` | test a name only; nothing is created and no `request_id` is needed |
| `request_id` | str | yes (not with `check_only`) | — | |

- Output: `{id, name, url, head, live, build}`, plus `replayed: true` on a replay. With no files, `head: 0`, `live: null`, `build: null` (the link shows "being made…" until v1 lands); with files, v1 commits before the call returns and builds after (`head: 1`, `build.status: "queued"`). With `check_only`: `{available, name, suggestions}` (T09).
- `content` needs `kind`; the file is named `index.html`, `index.md` or `index.txt` (`App.tsx` once `tsx` exists). `files` is never detected: a bundle is sent with `kind: "files"` and an `index.html` entry. Kind detection from the entry file otherwise (T12 owns the table).
- Fork: `from: <name>[@n]` copies that version's manifest (new part id, `n = 1`, `parent = null`, same blob hashes), records `parts.forked_from = <version id>`; `not_found` if the source doesn't exist or isn't visible.
- Scratch: `expires_in` sets `parts.expires_at`; the janitor (T113) moves it to the bin when due; shown with a badge and extendable (UI later).
- `snapshots` other than `daily` writes a `data_snapshot_policies` row (no row = daily keep 7).
- Ownership: `owner_user_id` = the person the creating agent acted for; `created_by_user`/`created_by_conn` recorded.
- Name reservation in the same writer transaction (unique constraints on `parts.name` and `names.name`).
- Errors: `invalid_input`, `unknown_field`, `name_taken` (`details.suggestions`), `not_found` (the `from` part), `forbidden` (`scope_needed` or `space`), `request_id_reused`, `quota_exceeded`, `rate_limited`, `too_large`, `storage_full`.
- **Idempotency layer** (shared by every write op, incl. T46, T96): `with_idempotency(principal, request_id, op, args_hash, f)`: in the writer, look up `idempotency(principal, request_id)`; if present and same op+args -> return stored response with `replayed: true`; if present with different args -> `request_id_reused` (409); else run `f` and insert the response **in the same transaction as the commit**. Rejected writes (any 4xx, or a 5xx before commit) store nothing, so the fixed retry may reuse the id. Rows purged after 24 h (janitor). Validate the `request_id` format.

## Not in scope

Builds (T13), live gate check (T80), quotas (T33), policy (T26).

## Design notes and decisions

- A timed-out write retried after the network recovers returns the stored result ("already applied"), never a confusing second error; this is why the stored response is written in the commit transaction.
- `args_hash` is a hash of the canonical JSON input minus `request_id`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retried create with the same request_id returns the same part with `replayed: true`; with different args -> `request_id_reused`.
- [ ] A create rejected with `name_taken` stores nothing; resending the fixed call with the same id succeeds.
- [ ] A fork writes zero new blobs and records `forked_from`.
- [ ] No-files create returns `head: 0, live: null, build: null` in < 10 ms p99 (bench in test).

## Tests

`pf_model::create::tests::replay_same_request_id`, `request_id_reused_on_different_args`, `rejected_write_does_not_consume_id`, `fork_zero_new_blobs`, `content_requires_kind`, `files_never_detected`, `expires_in_sets_expires_at`, `create_latency_under_10ms`; log assertion `event="part.write" op="part_create" replayed=true`.

## References

docs/agent-contract.md `part_create`, Rule 1; PLAN.md §3d Creation contract, Fork, Scratch parts, Idempotent every write; §4 Names; §5e `idempotency`, `parts`, `data_snapshot_policies`.

- Also waits for: nothing else
