title: T11.b: Part read: get with version selection, small-part full content, history ledger, diff of any two versions
description:
## Goal and why

Reading a part must be cheap for an agent ("change that thing from last week"): everything for a small part in one call, the file list plus the slice you ask for otherwise, and history/diff so "what changed?" always has an answer. This is the model behind `part_get` (T49 wires the agent read path and adds `build` logs and `runtime_errors`).

## Scope

- `get_part(principal, {name, version?, file?, range?, history?, diff_from?, diff_to?})`:
  - `version`: `"head"` (default) | `"live"` | int n. Unknown version -> `not_found`.
  - Output fields: `{id, name, url, title, kind, space, version, head, live, build, files, content?, history?, diff?}`. `files` is `{path: {hash, size, mime}}` (agents use `hash` as `if_match`). `content` is `{path: text}` for every text file **when the part is <= 32 KiB in total**, otherwise only for the `file` (or `range`) asked for.
  - `range`: `[first, last]`, 1-based inclusive lines, needs `file`; returns exactly those lines.
  - A part the caller can't see (or outside the connection's spaces) is `not_found`, never `forbidden` ("an error never confirms what's behind a name").
- **History**: `[{n, author, actor, via, message, created_at, build_status}]`, newest first; `message` is the agent's edit message or an auto summary (e.g. `"app.tsx +14 −3"`).
- **Diff** any two versions: `{from, to, files: [{path, status, added, removed, patch}]}`; `status` added/modified/deleted/renamed; unified diff `patch` for text; binary files show size changes (`patch: null`). `diff_to` defaults to head.
- Errors: `invalid_input`, `unknown_field`, `not_found`, `file_not_found`, `forbidden`.

## Not in scope

`runtime_errors` and `build: <id>` with logs (T49); notes, outline with symbols, `render: "text"` (T122); UI (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- 32 KiB threshold: the common single-file case comes back whole, so an agent can anchor-edit without a second call.
- Diff uses a line diff (e.g. `similar` crate) with 3 lines of context; binary detection via mime + NUL sniffing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 20 KiB single-file part returns its content; a 100 KiB part returns the file list and a `range` returns exactly those lines.
- [ ] Diff between v1 and v3 lists each changed file with correct `+/-` counts.
- [ ] An invisible part is `not_found`.

## Tests

`pf_model::read::tests::small_part_full_content`, `large_part_file_list_only`, `range_exact_lines`, `history_shape_and_order`, `diff_any_two_versions` (golden diffs in `tests/golden/diffs/`), `invisible_is_not_found`.

## References

docs/agent-contract.md `part_get`; PLAN.md §3c Read only what's needed; §3e History, Diff; §4b Errors (not_found vs forbidden).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T11.a: Part create: name reservation, v0 placeholder, v1 from content/files, fork, scratch, check_only, idempotency layer
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A 20 KiB single-file part returns its content; a 100 KiB part returns the file list and a `range` returns exactly those lines.
- [ ] Diff between v1 and v3 lists each changed file with correct `+/-` counts.
- [ ] An invisible part is `not_found`.

title: T11.c: Part lifecycle: soft delete to 30-day bin, undelete, scratch expiry, restore-as-new-version
description:
## Goal and why

Nothing is ever lost by accident: deletes go to a 30-day bin, and restoring an old version appends a new one instead of rewriting history. These back the `part_edit` mode fields `restore: n`, `delete: true`, `undelete: true` (T46 routes them; `parts:delete` scope for delete/undelete).

## Scope

- `delete_part(principal, name, request_id)`: sets `parts.deleted_at`; hidden from search and the gallery; the host stops serving content (T16 checks `deleted_at` via the live cache); bumps `epochs['part:<id>']`; event `part.deleted`. Returns the mutation shape.
- `undelete_part(principal, name, request_id)`: allowed for the owner or the admin while `now - deleted_at < 30 days`; clears `deleted_at`; event `part.undeleted`. At or after 30 days -> `not_found` (the part is purge-eligible; purge is a janitor job, T113, and the name stays reserved forever, T09).
- `restore_version(principal, name, n, request_id)`: commits a **new version whose manifest equals the old one's files/kind/entry/meta** (`n = head + 1`, `parent = head`, `restored_from = <old version id>`, `via = 'restore'`), then queues a build like any other version. "Shows 'Restored as REV 13 · Undo'" in the UI later.
- Scratch expiry primitive `expire_due_parts(now)` used by the janitor: soft-deletes parts with `expires_at <= now`.
- All three are idempotent via T11.a's layer.

## Not in scope

Purge job and bin listing UI (T113, T120); build of the restored version (T13).

## Design notes and decisions

- Restore = append keeps history immutable and the "undo" of a restore is just another restore.
- The 30-day boundary uses the injected clock; tests use a fixed clock.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore of v3 on a part at v5 creates v6 whose `version_files` equal v3's.
- [ ] Undelete at 29 days works; at 31 days fails with `not_found`.
- [ ] Delete bumps the part epoch; a deleted part is excluded from list queries.
- [ ] `expire_due_parts` moves due scratch parts to the bin.

## Tests

`pf_model::lifecycle::tests::restore_v3_creates_v_n_plus_1_equal_v3`, `undelete_29_days_ok_31_days_fails` (fixed clock), `delete_bumps_epoch`, `expire_due_parts_to_bin`, `restore_idempotent_replay`.

## References

PLAN.md §3e Versions and rollback (Restore), Deleted parts go to a 30-day bin; §3d Scratch parts; docs/agent-contract.md `part_edit` mode fields; §3b Scopes (`parts:delete`).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T11.a: Part create: name reservation, v0 placeholder, v1 from content/files, fork, scratch, check_only, idempotency layer

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Restore of v3 on a part at v5 creates v6 whose `version_files` equal v3's.
- [ ] Undelete at 29 days works; at 31 days fails with `not_found`.
- [ ] Delete bumps the part epoch; a deleted part is excluded from list queries.
- [ ] `expire_due_parts` moves due scratch parts to the bin.

title: T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
description: ## Goal and why Every part has a **kind**, and every kind is **built**, so `live` only ever moves through a successful build. This task delivers the renderers (the "build work" column of the kinds table) for the four kinds Slice 1 ships: `html`, `text`, `markdown` and `files`. They run inside the build child (T13) and produce the build output the content listener (T16) serves. Why it matters: Slice 1's agents send `html` (the pixel board is one `index.html`), chat agents mostly make notes and lists (`text`, `markdown`), and anything needing real npm packages is built locally (`vite build`, `base: './'`) and uploaded as `files`. `tsx` comes right after Slice 1 (T60), `svg` and `code` in T118. T12 is on the Slice 1 critical path (T08 → T12 → T13 → T16 ...), so it must be small, deterministic and golden-tested. *Why `text` is its own kind:* notes, lists and logs are the most common thing a chat agent makes. Rendering them as is, with line anchors, is faster and more faithful than wrapping them in Markdown (decision 30). ## Scope Kinds table rows owned here (verbatim from PLAN.md §2 Kinds): | kind | entry | build work | served as | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `html` | `index.html` | mirror CDN refs, sandbox rewrites (root-relative → relative, `crossorigin` on ``), brotli for every file but the entry | the HTML, with the prelude tag, import map and `pf-boot` inserted at serve time | | `markdown` | `*.md` | comrak render into the built-in shell (`pf-shell.css`, a shared blob); Jig styles (T54), block ids (T48), Mermaid/KaTeX (T66) | rendered HTML shell | | `text` | `*.txt` (or `kind: text`) | none beyond brotli, so it's instant | the text as is, in the built-in shell (`pf-shell.css`; Jig typography from T54) with a monospace toggle and line numbers for line-anchored comments and edits | | `files` | a built bundle (e.g. `vite build`) | sandbox rewrites only, no bundling | as uploaded | Build: - **Kind detection** from the entry file; `kind` overrides. `part_create {content}` is shorthand for a one-file part and needs `kind`; the file is named `index.html`, `index.md` or `index.txt` (and `App.tsx` once T60 lands). **`files` is never detected**: a bundle is sent with `kind: "files"` and an `index.html` entry. Detection table: `index.html` → html, `*.md` → markdown, `*.txt` → text; anything else is an error in Slice 1 (`svg`/`code` arrive in T118). - A `Renderer` trait in `pf-build` (`fn render(&self, input: &SourceView, mirror: &MirrorMap) -> Result`), pure and deterministic (no clock, no network, no randomness), called by the build child. Output = files `{path → bytes, content_type}` + warnings + errors with `{file, line, col, message}`. - **Sandbox rewrites** (shared by `html` and `files`): root-relative `src`/`href`/`srcset`/CSS `url()` rewritten to relative form; `crossorigin` added on ``; a build lint warns `root_relative_url` about string literals none of the four mechanisms can reach. (The other three mechanisms are the served import map `"/": "/c//", "/c/": "/c/"` (T16), and the prelude's fetch prefixing (T62).) The entry HTML is stored **as written** with only these rewrites; the prelude tag, import map and `pf-boot` are inserted at serve time (T16), never at build time, so a prelude fix needs no rebuild. - Mirrored CDN URLs: `html` and `files` consume the `{url → hash}` map produced by mirror-on-build (T14) and rewrite references in **build output only** (the rewrite pass itself lives in T14; T12 calls it). - **`text`**: bytes served byte-for-byte as written inside the built-in shell document; the shell is a small HTML wrapper referencing `pf-shell.css` (a shared blob, seeded via T17's `shared_blobs` with `source = 'seed'`) with a monospace toggle and line numbers; each line has a stable anchor (`#L`, id `L`) so comments and edits can address lines. The raw text is also kept as a file so `?raw` / agents see exactly what was written. - **`markdown`**: comrak (GFM extensions: tables, strikethrough, autolinks, task lists, footnotes) rendered server-side into the same shell (`pf-shell.css`). Raw HTML in Markdown is allowed (the part is sandboxed like everything else). Hooks left for later: T54 swaps the shell for `jig.css`, T48 adds block ids (`.pf/blocks.json` sidecar), T66 adds Mermaid/KaTeX. - **`files`**: prebuilt bundle; sandbox rewrites only, no bundling; `index.html` entry required (error otherwise). - **Brotli** is applied by T13 to every file but the entry (quality 11 for text ≤ 1 MiB, 5 above, skipped for already-compressed types); renderers mark which file is the entry. - `pf-shell.css`: authored in-repo (`crates/pf-build/assets/pf-shell.css`), neutral (not the Stockroom chrome; parts are never themed by the workspace), light/dark via `prefers-color-scheme`, system fonts, readable measure. ## Not in scope - The build child process, state machine, brotli, live switch: T13. Mirror fetching and the reference rewrite pass: T14. Serve-time templating: T16. - `tsx`: T60. `svg`, `code`: T118. `slides`, Mermaid, KaTeX: T66. Jig styling: T54. Block ids: T48. ## Design notes and decisions - Renderers are pure functions of (source manifest, mirror map, toolchain version): this is what makes the build cache key `sha256(source_manifest_hash ‖ toolchain_version ‖ library_set_version ‖ mirror_resolution_hash)` sound. Any renderer change bumps `toolchain_version`. - `text` must be byte-exact: no newline normalisation, no trimming, BOM preserved in the raw file. HTML-escape for display only. - Line anchors must be stable across edits that don't change the line count above them; they're 1-based line numbers, matching `part_get {range}` (1-based inclusive). - A `vite build` with `base: './'` already uses relative URLs; root-relative leftovers get the rewrite or the lint warning. - Errors from a renderer end the build `failed` with `build.errors: [{file, line, col, message}]`; a build failure is not an API error (the version was saved). ## Acceptance criteria dag2.py: "Golden render corpus passes for each kind; a `.txt` part renders byte-for-byte as written, with stable line anchors; a `vite build` (`base: './'`) uploaded as `files` serves with no broken URL". - [ ] Kind detection: `index.html` → html, `*.md` → markdown, `*.txt` → text; `files` never detected; `content` without `kind` rejected upstream with `invalid_input`. - [ ] Golden corpus under `tests/golden/render/{html,markdown,text,files}/` passes, output byte-stable across runs and machines. - [ ] `.txt` raw output equals input bytes exactly (incl. trailing whitespace, CRLF, unicode); anchors `L1..Ln` present. - [ ] Root-relative URLs in html/files rewritten to relative; `` gets `crossorigin`; `root_relative_url` warning for unreachable literals. - [ ] A real `vite build` fixture served through T16 loads every asset (no 404, no CSP violation) in the e2e browser. - [ ] Entry HTML stored unmodified apart from the sandbox rewrites (no prelude tag at build time). ## Tests - `pf_build::kinds::detect_tests::table` (table-driven detection). - `pf_build::kinds::text::tests::byte_exact_roundtrip` (proptest over arbitrary UTF-8 incl. CRLF/BOM), `line_anchor_stability`. - `pf_build::kinds::markdown::tests::golden` (comrak GFM corpus), `pf_build::rewrite::tests::root_relative_to_relative`, `img_crossorigin`, `lint_root_relative_literal`. - Golden: `tests/golden/render/` runner (`cargo nextest run -p pf-build golden_render`) with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` to bless; diffs printed on failure. - Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/vite_files.rs`: renders a checked-in `vite build` output; asserts every referenced URL resolves to a file in the output. - E2E `tests/e2e/kinds_files_vite.spec.ts` (after T16): opens the files part under the sandbox, asserts zero failed requests and zero console errors; server log events `event="build.finished" kind="files" outcome="ok"` asserted from `target/e2e-logs/kinds_files_vite/server.jsonl`; Playwright trace + HAR kept on failure. ## References PLAN.md §2 Kinds; §2 Serving a part ("The entry document is templated at serve time", root-relative URLs covered four ways); §3d The build worker; §5 Stack (comrak); §8 decision 30; Final round F06 (`pf-shell.css`); docs/agent-contract.md "Kinds". ## Dependency context (from the task graph) - Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0. - Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Golden render corpus passes for each kind; a `.txt` part renders byte-for-byte as written, with stable line anchors; a `vite build` (`base: './'`) uploaded as `files` serves with no broken URL - Depends on (must be closed first): - T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers - Unblocks: - T118: Kind renderers after Slice 1: svg (sandboxed document) and code (syntect viewer) - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch - T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar - T66: Slides kind plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides (block = slide) - G08: Sandbox compat corpus: 30 Claude-written artifacts and 10 Vite builds rendered under the sandbox in CI
acceptance_criteria: Golden render corpus passes for each kind; a `.txt` part renders byte-for-byte as written, with stable line anchors; a `vite build` (`base: './'`) uploaded as `files` serves with no broken URL

title: T118: Kind renderers after Slice 1: svg (sandboxed document) and code (syntect viewer)
description:
## Goal and why

The remainder of T12, split off at the Slice 1 freeze ("after Slice 1"). Adds two kinds so agents can post diagrams and source files directly: `svg` (an image an agent drew) and `code` (any other text file, shown highlighted, read-only). It feeds milestone M0 (P0 done-when). Not needed by the pixel test, hence after S1.

## Scope

Kinds table rows (verbatim, PLAN.md §2 Kinds):

| kind | entry | build work | served as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `svg` | `*.svg` | none beyond brotli (it's sandboxed like everything else) | the SVG as a sandboxed document |
| `code` | any other text file | syntect highlight | read-only viewer shell |

- Extend kind detection (T12): `*.svg` → `svg`; any other text file (UTF-8 decodable, not html/md/txt) → `code`. `kind` overrides.
- `svg`: the SVG file is the entry and is served **as a document** (`Content-Type: image/svg+xml`) with the canonical part CSP including `sandbox` (T16 applies the CSP to "an SVG served as a document"). No rewriting of the SVG beyond what's needed for mirrored URLs (T14 map) and root-relative `href`s.
- `code`: `syntect` highlighting server-side (pinned syntax set + theme, embedded), rendered into a read-only viewer shell (shares `pf-shell.css` from T12) with line numbers and stable `#L<n>` anchors; language from extension, fallback plain text.
- Bin codes for the UI: `SVG`, `CODE`.

## Not in scope

`slides`/Mermaid/KaTeX (T66); Jig typography (T54); the source editor (T55); serving and CSP (T16).

## Design notes and decisions

- An SVG can carry `<script>`. It is safe because it is served under the canonical sandbox CSP (opaque origin, no cookies, egress confined to own host + blob host), exactly like an HTML part; inline script in SVG therefore runs only under the canonical sandbox CSP. Never serve a part SVG without the CSP (e.g. from the shared blob host): part SVGs are part blobs, never in `shared_blobs`.
- syntect is chosen over client-side highlighting so the viewer needs no JS and the output is cacheable; the syntax set version is part of `toolchain_version`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Golden render corpus passes for `svg` and `code`; an SVG carrying a script runs only under the canonical sandbox CSP".
- [ ] Detection table extended; golden corpus `tests/golden/render/{svg,code}/` passes.
- [ ] A `.svg` with `<script>` served from its part host carries the full canonical CSP with `sandbox`; in the browser `document.cookie` is inert and a `fetch` to another origin is blocked.
- [ ] Code viewer has line anchors and no external requests.

## Tests

- `pf_build::kinds::code::tests::golden_syntect`, `language_from_extension`.
- `pf_build::kinds::svg::tests::passthrough_golden`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/svg_csp.rs`: GET the SVG entry, assert the CSP header string equals the canonical template.
- E2E `tests/e2e/kinds_svg_script.spec.ts`: script inside the SVG tries `document.cookie = "x=1"`, `fetch("https://evil.example")`; asserts both fail, collects the CSP violation; server log `event="serve.entry" kind="svg"` asserted.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Kinds; §2 Serving a part (canonical CSP applies to "an SVG served as a document"); §5 Stack (syntect); Slice 1 freeze split T12 → T118.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Golden render corpus passes for `svg` and `code`; an SVG carrying a script runs only under the canonical sandbox CSP
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
- Unblocks: 
  - M0: Milestone - P0 Core (local) done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Keep PLAN §2's kinds row literal: `svg` build work is **none beyond brotli** (sandbox rewrites of root-relative `href`s only). External `<image href>`/`<script href>` in an SVG are CSP-blocked (`blocked_load`), not mirrored; agents bundle assets into the part. Mirroring SVG references is not in scope here.
- The prelude is injected into **HTML documents only**: an SVG served as a document gets no `localStorage` shim, no fetch prefixing and no `runtime_errors` reporting. Tests must not expect a `blocked_load` row from an SVG; assert the CSP header and that the script ran in an opaque origin instead.
- Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` lists `svg` and `code` under "After Slice 1" and its kinds table lacks their rows. Acceptance adds: the kinds table gains both rows, they leave the not-yet list, and T56's registry-match test stays green.
acceptance_criteria: Golden render corpus passes for `svg` and `code`; an SVG carrying a script runs only under the canonical sandbox CSP

title: T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
description:
## Goal and why

Every kind is built, and `live` only moves through an `ok` build, so a broken save never replaces a working page. The build worker turns a committed source version into a build record and its output files, safely. It is on the Slice 1 critical path (T08 → T12 → **T13** → T16) and is a bottleneck for M2 too, so start it early.

*Why a child process (decision 20):* oxc and rolldown are young. A hang can't be killed in-process (a `spawn_blocking` timeout only abandons the thread), and a panic under `panic = "abort"` would take the content listener down with it. Spawning a static binary costs 1–2 ms, so the TSX target survives, and the esbuild fallback becomes a drop-in for the same protocol.
*Why build records keyed by toolchain:* compile output depends on the toolchain. Keying on the manifest alone would serve stale output after an upgrade. A toolchain upgrade rebuilds live parts in the background, diffs the output against the golden corpus, and never switches what's live on its own.

## Scope

Verbatim from PLAN.md §3d "The build worker":
- **States**: `queued → running → ok | failed | timeout | superseded`. A queued build is `superseded` (and skipped) once a newer version of the same part is queued. A running build is never cancelled.
- **Isolation**: each build runs in a **child process of the same binary** (`partifactory build-worker`, re-exec'd), with length-prefixed CBOR over stdin/stdout, a **10 s deadline**, a memory cap (`RLIMIT_AS` 1 GiB) and `SIGKILL` on breach. A crash marks the build `failed` with `code: "builder_crashed"`. Pool size `max(1, min(2, cores/2))`, pre-forked.
- **Mirroring runs in the parent**, which is the only process with egress, before the child is spawned (T14): 30 s budget, hands the child the `{url → hash}` map. The child has no network, and its 10 s deadline covers compile and rewrite only. A build's wall-clock bound is therefore 40 s; `wait: true` still returns at 2 s with `status: running`.
- **Cache key**: `sha256(source_manifest_hash ‖ toolchain_version ‖ library_set_version ‖ mirror_resolution_hash)`. An identical key reuses the output.
- **Output**: a build manifest `{files: {path → {hash, br_hash?, type}}, import_map?, warnings[], errors[], mirrored: [{url, resolved, hash}]}`, stored as a blob and referenced from `builds.output_hash`.
- **Brotli**: quality 11 for text ≤ 1 MiB, 5 above that, skipped for already-compressed types. Every file but the entry document (which is templated at serve time, T16).
- **Live switch**: on `ok`, inside the writer: `if version.n > live.n then live = version`, unless the version was saved with `live: "after_check"`, in which case the switch waits for its check to pass (or be skipped). Emit `build.finished` and, on a switch, `part.live_changed`.
- **`wait: true`** (the default for agents) blocks ≤ 2 s on `build.finished`; `check: true` or `live: "after_check"` extends the wait to the build plus the check, up to 15 s. If still running, the result says `build: {status: "running", id}`. `wait: false` returns at once.

Schema used (from T06, verbatim):
```sql
CREATE TABLE builds (
  id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  version_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  cache_key        TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- sha256(src manifest || toolchain || libset || mirror resolution)
  toolchain        TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- pinned oxc/rolldown/builder version id
  target           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'frontend' CHECK (target IN ('frontend','backend')),
  method           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('server_build','prebuilt_files','prebuilt_image','uploaded_image')),
  status           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','ok','failed','timeout','superseded')),
  output_hash      TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  log_hash         TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),      -- build log; last 20 builds per part kept (janitor)
  warnings         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(warnings)),
  errors           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(errors)),
  gate_check       TEXT CHECK (gate_check IN ('pending','passed','failed','skipped')),
  queued_at INTEGER NOT NULL, started_at INTEGER, finished_at INTEGER,
  UNIQUE (version_id, cache_key)
) STRICT;
CREATE TABLE build_files (build_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES builds(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, path TEXT NOT NULL,
  blob_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash), br_hash TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash), content_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (build_id, path)) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
plus `parts.live_version_id`, `parts.live_build_id`, `versions.live_gate`.

`builds.method` for frontends: `server_build` for html/markdown/text/tsx, `prebuilt_files` for `files`.

**Subtasks** (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- `T13.a` child-process protocol and isolation (re-exec, CBOR framing, deadline, RLIMIT_AS, SIGKILL, pre-forked pool, crash handling).
- `T13.b` build queue, state machine, build records, cache key, superseding, build logs.
- `T13.c` output: brotli, build manifest blob + `build_files`, live-pointer switch in the writer (incl. the `after_check` gate hook), events, `wait` semantics.

## Not in scope

Mirror fetching (T14, runs before the child); kind renderers (T12, T118, T60); the `after_check` check itself (T80 supplies it; T13 provides the gate state `gate_check` and the hook); backend builds with BuildKit (T99); toolchain-upgrade background rebuild orchestration beyond keying (later, with T60's golden corpus).

## Design notes and decisions

- Re-exec of the same static binary keeps one deliverable and makes esbuild-as-subprocess a drop-in behind the same protocol.
- The child gets no network (no sockets inherited; on Linux optionally `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)` when permitted, else rely on the parent being the only process with egress by construction: the child never opens connections).
- Live switch must be inside the single writer to stay linearisable with commits (T05).
- "A running build is never cancelled": superseding only skips queued builds; a newer ok build of a lower `n` never moves live backwards (`version.n > live.n`).
- Build log (stdout/stderr of the child, warnings) stored as a blob in `builds.log_hash`; the janitor keeps the last 20 per part, 30 days (T113).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A build that panics, hangs or exceeds memory marks the build failed/timeout, the server keeps serving, and `live` is unchanged; `wait:true` returns within 2 s or `build.status=running`".
- [ ] Panic → `failed` with `builder_crashed`; hang > 10 s → `timeout`; > 1 GiB → killed, `failed`; server still serves other parts; `live` unchanged.
- [ ] Queued build superseded by a newer version is skipped with `superseded`; running build completes.
- [ ] Identical cache key reuses output (no child spawned).
- [ ] Brotli variants exist for every non-entry compressible file with the specified qualities.
- [ ] `live` moves only to a higher `n` with `ok`; with `live_gate = after_check` it waits on `gate_check ∈ {passed, skipped}`.
- [ ] `wait: true` returns ≤ 2 s (or ≤ 15 s with check) with `status: running` when unfinished.

## Tests

Owned by subtasks; the parent adds `crates/pf-build/tests/worker_e2e.rs::panic_hang_oom_server_survives` (spawns the real binary, injects three fault fixtures via a test-only renderer, asserts statuses, asserts a concurrent content-listener request returns 200, asserts log events `event="build.finished" outcome="builder_crashed"|"timeout"` and that `parts.live_version_id` is unchanged).

title: T13.a: Build child process: re-exec protocol, CBOR framing, 10 s deadline, RLIMIT_AS, pre-forked pool
description:
## Goal and why

Isolate young compiler code (oxc, rolldown, comrak) so a hang or panic costs one build, never the server. This is the process boundary everything in T13 relies on.

## Scope

- Subcommand `partifactory build-worker` (same static binary, re-exec'd via `/proc/self/exe` or `std::env::current_exe()`).
- Protocol: **length-prefixed CBOR over stdin/stdout** (u32 big-endian length + CBOR body). Request `{job_id, toolchain, kind, entry, files: {path → bytes|blob_ref}, mirror_map: {url → hash}, import_map_seed?}`; response `{job_id, status: ok|failed, files: {path → {bytes, content_type, is_entry}}, warnings[], errors[{file,line,col,message}], log}`. Versioned with a `proto: 1` field.
- Limits: **10 s deadline** (parent timer → `SIGKILL`), **`RLIMIT_AS` 1 GiB** set in the child before reading input, `SIGKILL` on breach. No network: the child never opens sockets (and inherits none).
- Pool: **`max(1, min(2, cores/2))`**, pre-forked workers waiting on stdin; a worker is replaced after any kill/crash; optionally recycled after N jobs.
- Crash (non-zero exit, signal, malformed frame) → result `failed` with `code: "builder_crashed"`; deadline → `timeout`.
- Release builds of the worker use `panic = "abort"` safely because it's a separate process.

## Not in scope

Queueing and state (T13.b); brotli/live switch (T13.c); renderers (T12); mirroring (T14).

## Design notes and decisions

- Static binary spawn costs 1–2 ms, so pre-forking is mostly for the TSX p50 < 150 ms target.
- esbuild fallback can implement the same protocol later without parent changes.
- Large inputs: pass blob paths (read-only open fds or paths under `/data/blobs`) rather than bytes when a file > 1 MiB, to keep frames small; the child only reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Panic, infinite loop, and 2 GiB allocation fixtures each yield `failed/builder_crashed`, `timeout`, `failed` respectively, within deadline + 100 ms.
- [ ] Pool size formula verified for 1, 2, 4, 16 cores.
- [ ] A killed worker is replaced; subsequent builds succeed.

## Tests

- `pf_build::worker::proto::tests::cbor_roundtrip`, `frame_too_large_rejected`.
- `pf_build::worker::pool::tests::pool_size_formula`.
- Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/child_faults.rs::{panic,hang,oom,garbage_output}` using test-only renderer kinds compiled behind `#[cfg(feature = "fault-injection")]`; asserts log events `event="build.child" outcome=...` with `job_id` and `latency_us`.

## References

PLAN.md §3d The build worker (Isolation, Why a child process); §5 Stack; Final round F16 (`max(1, …)` pool).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T02.a (the compiler spike): its length-prefixed CBOR child protocol, deadline/`RLIMIT_AS` handling and spawn-cost measurements are this subtask's design input; copy the note's consequences into this bead before starting.

- [ ] Panic, infinite loop, and 2 GiB allocation fixtures each yield `failed/builder_crashed`, `timeout`, `failed` respectively, within deadline + 100 ms.
- [ ] Pool size formula verified for 1, 2, 4, 16 cores.
- [ ] A killed worker is replaced; subsequent builds succeed.

title: T13.b: Build queue and state machine: build records, cache key, superseding, build logs
description:
## Goal and why

Turn committed versions into durable `builds` rows that move through a strict state machine, reuse identical output, and never waste work on stale versions.

## Scope

- States: `queued → running → ok | failed | timeout | superseded`. A queued build is `superseded` (skipped) once a newer version of the same part is queued. **A running build is never cancelled.**
- On version commit (T11/T46 call `enqueue_build(version_id)`): compute **cache key** `sha256(source_manifest_hash ‖ toolchain_version ‖ library_set_version ‖ mirror_resolution_hash)`. The mirror resolution hash comes from T14 (run in the parent before spawning); if an `ok` build with the same key exists (`builds_cache` index), reuse its output (new `builds` row pointing at same `output_hash`, or reuse per `UNIQUE(version_id, cache_key)`).
- Dispatcher: polls `builds_queue` index (`status IN ('queued','running')`), FIFO by `queued_at`, respects the pool size from T13.a; on start sets `started_at`, `status='running'`; on finish `finished_at`, `status`, `warnings`, `errors` (JSON), `log_hash`.
- `builds.method`: `server_build` (html, markdown, text, svg, code, tsx) or `prebuilt_files` (`files`); `target = 'frontend'`.
- Recovery at boot: rows left `running` from a crash are re-queued (or marked `failed` with `builder_crashed` if their version is no longer the newest).
- Build log blob: child log + warnings, stored via BlobStore, referenced from `log_hash`.
- All state writes go through the single writer task (T05).

## Not in scope

Output storage and live switch (T13.c); mirroring (T14).

## Design notes and decisions

- `toolchain_version` is a constant compiled into the binary (builder + renderer versions); `library_set_version` from `libset.toml` (T60; a fixed `none` in Slice 1).
- Superseding is per part, only for `queued` rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Commit v1, v2, v3 quickly with one worker busy: v2 ends `superseded`, v1 and v3 build.
- [ ] Same source rebuilt (e.g. restore of v1 as v4, identical manifest) reuses output with no child spawn.
- [ ] Boot recovery re-queues stale `running` rows.

## Tests

- `pf_build::queue::tests::state_transitions_are_legal` (proptest on event sequences; illegal transitions impossible).
- `pf_build::queue::tests::supersede_only_queued`, `cache_key_inputs` (golden hash).
- Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/queue.rs::restore_reuses_build` asserting `event="build.cache_hit"` in captured logs.

## References

PLAN.md §3d The build worker (States, Cache key); §5e `builds`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T13.a: Build child process: re-exec protocol, CBOR framing, 10 s deadline, RLIMIT_AS, pre-forked pool

- [ ] Commit v1, v2, v3 quickly with one worker busy: v2 ends `superseded`, v1 and v3 build.
- [ ] Same source rebuilt (e.g. restore of v1 as v4, identical manifest) reuses output with no child spawn.
- [ ] Boot recovery re-queues stale `running` rows.

title: T13.c: Build output: brotli, build manifest + build_files, live switch with after_check gate, wait semantics
description:
## Goal and why

Make a finished build servable and move `live` safely: the content listener (T16) serves only what `build_files` lists for the live build, and `live` never regresses or points at a broken build.

## Scope

- **Brotli**: quality 11 for text ≤ 1 MiB, 5 above that, skipped for already-compressed types (png, jpg, webp, woff2, gz, br, zip, mp4...). Every file but the entry document. `br_hash` recorded per file.
- **Build manifest** blob `{files: {path → {hash, br_hash?, type}}, import_map?, warnings[], errors[], mirrored: [{url, resolved, hash}]}` → `builds.output_hash`; `build_files` rows for every served path.
- **Live switch** inside the writer: on `ok`, `if version.n > live.n then live = version` (set `parts.live_version_id`, `parts.live_build_id`), unless `versions.live_gate = 'after_check'`, in which case set `builds.gate_check = 'pending'` and switch only when the check sets it to `passed` or `skipped` (T80 calls `gate_result(build_id, passed|failed|skipped)`; if the renderer is off, T13 marks `skipped` immediately and adds warning `check_skipped`). Emit `build.finished` always and `part.live_changed` on a switch (events table + in-memory broadcast, T51 consumes; invalidate the in-memory `part → live` cache used by T16).
- **`wait`** semantics for the mutation shape: `wait: true` blocks ≤ 2 s on `build.finished` for that build; `check: true` or `live: "after_check"` extends to build + check, ≤ 15 s; otherwise returns `build: {status: "running", id}`. `wait: false` returns at once. Exposed as `BuildWaiter::wait(build_id, deadline)` for T11/T46/T21.
- Mutation shape fields produced: `{head, live, build: {id, status, warnings, errors}}`; a build failure is not an error (200 with `status: "failed"`).

## Not in scope

The check itself (T80); event delivery (T51); serving (T16).

## Design notes and decisions

- Live pair is `(live_version_id, live_build_id)`; head and live differ while a build runs or after a failure.
- Precompressing at build time is how serving stays "negotiation + a file read" (§5a).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Failed build of v3 leaves live at v2; ok build of v2 arriving after v3 is live does not move live back.
- [ ] `after_check` version with failed gate stays off live; with renderer absent goes live with `check_skipped`.
- [ ] `wait` returns within 2 s / 15 s bounds (test clock).
- [ ] `part.live_changed` emitted exactly once per switch.

## Tests

- `pf_build::output::tests::brotli_quality_by_size`, `skip_precompressed_types`.
- `pf_model::live::tests::monotonic_live_switch` (proptest over interleavings of build completions).
- Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/live_gate.rs::{after_check_failed_keeps_live, renderer_absent_skips}` asserting `event="part.live_changed"` count and `warnings` contains `check_skipped`.

## References

PLAN.md §3d The build worker (Output, Brotli, Live switch, wait); §3d "Latest vs live", `live: "always" | "after_check"`; §5e `builds.gate_check`, `versions.live_gate`.

## Dependency context

- Also waits for: T13.b: Build queue and state machine: build records, cache key, superseding, build logs

title: T14: Mirror-on-build: fetch allowlisted CDN refs in the parent, pin by hash, rewrite build output only
description:
## Goal and why

Claude-written HTML is full of CDN `<script>`/`<link>` tags. Mirror-on-build makes them work unchanged while parts load **nothing from third parties at runtime**, so the canonical CSP has no third-party origins and private viewers are never tracked by a CDN. It replaces both a CDN allowlist in CSP and a hand-maintained vendor list. It's a direct dependency of S1 (T14 → S1) and M0, and of T60 (TSX aliasing).

*Why in the build, not the source:* the agent's next `old_str` anchor contains the original CDN URL. Rewriting the source would break it. The source version commits before any fetch, so a slow CDN never slows a save.
*Why in the parent process:* the parent is the only process with egress; the build child has no network (T13).

## Scope

Verbatim from PLAN.md §2 "Mirror-on-build":
- When a part references `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/…`, jsDelivr `/npm/…`, unpkg, esm.sh or Google Fonts, the **build step** fetches it once, stores it as a shared blob and rewrites the URL **in the build output only**.
- **Rewritten**: HTML `script[src]`, `link[href]` (stylesheet, preload, modulepreload, icon), `img/source/video/audio[src|srcset]`, `import`/`export … from`/literal `import("…")` in inline and fetched module scripts, CSS `@import` and `url()` in inline and fetched CSS (recursively), and root-relative paths inside fetched files from the same CDN host. `sourceMappingURL` comments are stripped. URLs built at runtime (`fetch(cdn + x)`) aren't rewritten. CSP blocks them, and they show up in `runtime_errors` as `blocked_load`.
- **Allowlist** (site config `[mirror] allowlist`): `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net` **`/npm/` paths only** (its `/gh/` paths serve any GitHub repo, which would make the edge-cached blob host into arbitrary file hosting), `unpkg.com`, `esm.sh`, `fonts.googleapis.com` + `fonts.gstatic.com`. https only.
- **Egress guard**, shared with CIMD fetches (T124): we resolve DNS ourselves and refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses, allow ≤ 3 redirects and only within the allowlist, a 10 s timeout and ≤ 10 MiB per asset. Per build: ≤ 200 assets, ≤ 50 MiB, depth ≤ 8, 30 s total.
- **SRI**: when the source has `integrity=`, a mismatch fails the build. Otherwise the fetched hash is recorded in the build record.
- **Floating versions** (`react@18`, `@latest`, none): resolved to the pinned URL the CDN redirects to, recorded as `(requested → pinned → hash)` in `mirror_cache`, and reported as a `cdn_unpinned` warning. An exact version is cached forever. A floating one is re-resolved at most once per 24 h, and the resolution is written into the build, so every build is reproducible from its record.
- **Fonts**: Google Fonts CSS is fetched with a fixed modern User-Agent (so it returns woff2), then each `url()` it references is mirrored one level deep. KaTeX and Font Awesome webfonts come through the same pass.
- **Failure**: the source version still commits, the build ends `failed` with `{code: "mirror_failed", url, reason: "not_allowlisted" | "private_address" | "too_large" | "timeout" | "integrity_mismatch" | "http_<status>"}`, and `live` doesn't move.
- Mirrored blobs are inserted into `shared_blobs` with `source = 'mirror'` and a `label` like `react@18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js`, and served from `https://blobs-part.<domain>/b/<hash>` (T17).
- The parent hands the child the `{url → hash}` map; the **rewrite of build output happens in the child** using that map (the rewriter is a pure library in `pf-build::mirror::rewrite`); the `mirror_resolution_hash` (sha256 of the sorted map) feeds the T13 cache key; the build manifest records `mirrored: [{url, resolved, hash}]`.

Schema (T06, verbatim):
```sql
CREATE TABLE mirror_cache (
  url          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  resolved_url TEXT NOT NULL,
  hash         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  content_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  integrity    TEXT,
  pinned       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (pinned IN (0,1)),  -- exact version: cache forever
  fetched_at   INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

**Subtasks** (parent = integration/closure bead; close after both subtasks close and the acceptance passes end to end):
- `T14.a` the egress guard + fetcher + `mirror_cache` + floating-version resolution + per-build budgets (parent process).
- `T14.b` reference discovery and rewriting of build output (HTML, JS modules, CSS recursion, fonts one level, SRI, sourcemap stripping, failure reporting).

## Not in scope

The library-set aliasing (one React; `duplicate_library` warning; `libset.toml`) arrives with T60; until then every mirrored URL is mirrored as is. Import maps for module scripts are frozen per build in T60 (Slice 1 HTML with `<script type="module">` uses the served import map from T16 only for the cap prefix). Shared blob serving: T17. CIMD fetching: T124 (reuses the guard).

## Design notes and decisions

- One egress guard for every outbound fetch (mirror, CIMD) so neither can reach internal addresses (§5d Abuse prevention).
- DNS resolved by us and the connection made to the vetted IP (no TOCTOU re-resolution): use a custom resolver in the HTTP client that rejects private ranges, and pin the connect address.
- Redirects followed manually so each hop is re-checked against the allowlist and the IP guard.
- jsDelivr `/gh/` is refused (`not_allowlisted`) on purpose.
- The source is never touched: the agent's anchors keep matching.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Fixture page with a cdnjs `<script>`, Google Fonts CSS and a jsDelivr `+esm` module renders with zero third-party requests; the source's anchors still match; an off-allowlist redirect and a private-IP resolution fail with `mirror_failed`".
- [ ] The fixture renders in the e2e browser with zero requests to any host other than the part host and `blobs-part`.
- [ ] `part_get` on the source still contains the original CDN URLs; an anchor edit on one succeeds.
- [ ] Redirect to an off-allowlist host → `mirror_failed {reason: "not_allowlisted"}`; DNS resolving to 10.x/127.x/169.254.x/fc00::/fe80:: → `private_address`; > 10 MiB → `too_large`; slow → `timeout`; SRI mismatch → `integrity_mismatch`; 404 → `http_404`; `live` unchanged in each.
- [ ] Floating `react@18` resolves to a pinned URL, records `mirror_cache.pinned=0`, warns `cdn_unpinned`; re-resolved ≤ once per 24 h.
- [ ] Per-build budgets enforced (200 assets, 50 MiB, depth 8, 30 s).

## Tests

Subtask unit tests, plus parent integration `crates/pf-build/tests/mirror_fixture.rs` using a local fake CDN (rustls test server with a test CA, DNS override mapping `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` etc. to it) serving cdnjs/Google Fonts/jsDelivr `+esm` fixtures; asserts build ok, `shared_blobs` rows, rewritten output, and log events `event="mirror.fetch" url_host=... outcome=...`.
E2E `tests/e2e/mirror_zero_third_party.spec.ts`: opens the fixture part, records all network requests, asserts the host set ⊆ {part host, blobs host}; keeps HAR + `target/e2e-logs/mirror_zero_third_party/server.jsonl` on failure.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "Mirror-on-build, instead of a CDN allowlist"; §3d The build worker ("Mirroring runs in the parent"); §5d Abuse prevention (Outbound fetches); §5e `mirror_cache`, `shared_blobs`; Final round F03.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Fixture page with a cdnjs `<script>`, Google Fonts CSS and a jsDelivr `+esm` module renders with zero third-party requests; the source's anchors still match; an off-allowlist redirect and a private-IP resolution fail with `mirror_failed`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
  - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
- Unblocks: 
  - T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps
  - M0: Milestone - P0 Core (local) done
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)

title: T14.a: Egress guard and mirror fetcher: allowlist, SSRF guard, limits, mirror_cache, floating-version pinning
description:
## Goal and why

The single outbound-fetch path for the server (mirror now, CIMD in T124). It must never reach an internal address and must make every build reproducible from its record.

## Scope

- `pf_build::egress::Guard`: https only; host must match `[mirror] allowlist` (default `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net` with path prefix `/npm/` only, `unpkg.com`, `esm.sh`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`); **resolve DNS ourselves** and refuse private (RFC 1918), loopback, link-local (incl. `169.254.169.254`), CGNAT, ULA and IPv6 link-local addresses; connect to the vetted address; **≤ 3 redirects, each within the allowlist and re-vetted**; **10 s timeout and ≤ 10 MiB per asset** (streamed, aborted at the limit). Configurable profile so CIMD can use `≤ 5 KiB, 3 s, no redirects`.
- Per-build budget object: **≤ 200 assets, ≤ 50 MiB, depth ≤ 8, 30 s total**.
- Failure reasons: `not_allowlisted`, `private_address`, `too_large`, `timeout`, `http_<status>` (plus `integrity_mismatch` from T14.b).
- `mirror_cache` lookups/writes: exact versions (`pinned = 1`) cached forever; floating versions (`react@18`, `@latest`, no version) resolved via the CDN's redirect to a pinned URL, recorded `(requested → pinned → hash)`, `pinned = 0`, re-resolved at most once per 24 h; produce a `cdn_unpinned` warning.
- Store bodies via BlobStore (T07) and insert `shared_blobs (hash, source='mirror', label, added_at)`.
- Google Fonts CSS requests use a fixed modern User-Agent so woff2 is returned.
- Output to the build: `{url → hash}` map and `mirror_resolution_hash = sha256(sorted map)`.

## Not in scope

Finding and rewriting references (T14.b).

## Design notes and decisions

- Shared with CIMD per §3b: one guard, two profiles. Metrics: `pf_mirror_fetch_total{outcome}`, bytes.
- Concurrency: fetch up to 8 assets in parallel within the 30 s budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each failure reason produced by a dedicated fixture; private IP via DNS rebinding fixture (first lookup public, second private) still refused because connection uses the vetted IP.
- [ ] jsDelivr `/gh/...` refused; `/npm/...` allowed.
- [ ] Floating resolution re-uses cache within 24 h (test clock).

## Tests

- `pf_build::egress::tests::ip_ranges` (table of v4/v6 addresses), `allowlist_paths`, `redirect_limit`, `size_limit_streaming`.
- Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/egress.rs::{dns_rebinding, redirect_off_allowlist, timeout}` against a local fake CDN; captured logs assert `event="egress.refused" reason=...` and never log full query strings.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Mirror-on-build (Allowlist, Egress guard, Floating versions, Fonts); §3b CIMD fetches; §5d Abuse prevention; §5e `mirror_cache`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T14: Mirror-on-build: fetch allowlisted CDN refs in the parent, pin by hash, rewrite build output only (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T14.b: Mirror reference discovery and transitive rewrite of build output (HTML, JS, CSS, fonts, SRI)
description:
## Goal and why

Find every CDN reference a page actually loads, fetch it (via T14.a) and rewrite the **build output only** to `https://blobs-part.<domain>/b/<hash>`, transitively, so the page runs with zero third-party requests and the source stays anchor-compatible.

## Scope

- Discovery (parent side, before spawning the child) and rewrite (pure library used in the child with the `{url → hash}` map):
  - HTML `script[src]`, `link[href]` (stylesheet, preload, modulepreload, icon), `img/source/video/audio[src|srcset]`;
  - `import`/`export … from` / literal `import("…")` in inline and fetched module scripts (parse with oxc's parser in the child; a lightweight lexer for discovery in the parent);
  - CSS `@import` and `url()` in inline and fetched CSS, **recursively**;
  - root-relative paths inside fetched files from the same CDN host (e.g. esm.sh `/v135/...`) resolved against that host;
  - Google Fonts CSS → each `url()` mirrored **one level deep**; KaTeX and Font Awesome webfonts through the same pass;
  - strip `sourceMappingURL` comments from fetched files.
- Fetched files that themselves reference URLs are rewritten too (their rewritten bytes become the stored shared blob; the hash recorded is of the rewritten bytes, and `mirror_cache` keys the original URL).
- **SRI**: when the source tag has `integrity=`, verify against the fetched bytes; mismatch → build `failed {code: "mirror_failed", url, reason: "integrity_mismatch"}`. Otherwise record the fetched hash in the build record. Rewritten tags drop `integrity` only when we rewrote the content (record why).
- Runtime-constructed URLs are not rewritten (CSP will block; `blocked_load` in `runtime_errors`).
- Failure shape: `{code: "mirror_failed", url, reason}` in `build.errors`; source version still committed; `live` unchanged.
- Build manifest `mirrored: [{url, resolved, hash}]`.

## Not in scope

Library-set aliasing and frozen import maps (T60).

## Design notes and decisions

- Depth ≤ 8 bounds recursion; cycles detected by URL set.
- Rewriting changes bytes, so SRI attributes on rewritten tags must be updated to the new hash (`sha384` of the served bytes) or removed; prefer updating so the browser still verifies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden fixtures: cdnjs `<script>`, Google Fonts CSS with woff2, jsDelivr `+esm` module importing further modules, CSS `@import` chain, srcset — output references only `blobs-part` URLs.
- [ ] Source manifest unchanged byte-for-byte.
- [ ] SRI mismatch fixture fails with `integrity_mismatch`.

## Tests

- `pf_build::mirror::rewrite::tests::{html_attrs, srcset, css_url_recursive, js_static_imports, dynamic_import_literal, sourcemap_stripped}` (golden in `tests/golden/mirror/`).
- `pf_build::mirror::discover::tests::esm_root_relative_same_host`.
- Integration `crates/pf-build/tests/mirror_transitive.rs` with captured logs asserting `event="mirror.rewrite" refs=<n>`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Mirror-on-build (Rewritten, SRI, Fonts, Failure).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T14: Mirror-on-build: fetch allowlisted CDN refs in the parent, pin by hash, rewrite build output only (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T14.a: Egress guard and mirror fetcher: allowlist, SSRF guard, limits, mirror_cache, floating-version pinning

- [ ] Source manifest unchanged byte-for-byte.
- [ ] SRI mismatch fixture fails with `integrity_mismatch`.

title: T15: Capability tokens: path caps, HMAC with daily HKDF kid keys, deterministic windows, epochs + boot floor
description:
## Goal and why

A capability ("cap") is a signed, host-bound token in the URL path that carries a decided grant to a part's host, so the content listener never needs the database to authorise a request, and so no part host ever needs a cookie. Caps make the hot path DB-free (one HMAC verify plus four integer compares) while revocation stays instant through epochs. Used by T16 (verify), T27 (mint at `/grant`), T29 (public links, wrapper), T80 (render caps), T95 (guest caps), T101 (backends).

*Why deterministic windows:* the same subject, part, epochs and 12 h window give the **same cap**, so `private, immutable` part blobs stay in the browser cache across repeat opens.
*Why a boot-epoch floor:* a restored or rolled-back database can never resurrect a revoked cap. The cost is one silent re-grant per open tab after a deploy.

## Scope

Verbatim from PLAN.md §2 "Capabilities live in the path":
- URLs: `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap>/<path>`. The cap is never in a cookie.
- **Format**: `v1.<kid>.<payload>.<mac>`, all base64url, ≤ 300 bytes. `mac = HMAC-SHA256(key[kid], "v1." + kid + "." + payload)`, truncated to 16 bytes.
  `payload` is canonical CBOR: `{p: part_id, h: host_label, s: subject ("user:u_…" | "link:l_…" | "conn:c_…" | "render"), r: role (0 view … 3 manage), ro?: read_only, dw?: shared-data write (a "can contribute" link), g?: guest id, e: part_epoch, m: minter ("sess:<id>" | "link:<id>" | "conn:<id>" | "render"), me: minter_epoch, b: boot_epoch, w: window end (unix minutes), v?: pinned version_id, d?: draft id}`.
- **Keys**: `kid` is the UTC day number, and `key[kid] = HKDF-SHA256(PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY, info = "pf-cap/" ‖ kid)`. The verifier accepts `kid` and `kid − 1` (at least 25 h, longer than any 13 h cap). Rotating the root secret rotates every key, and a retired `kid` is never accepted again. Windows are 12 h for `user`, `link` and `conn` subjects and 60 s for `render`.
- **Deterministic and windowed**: no random nonce. A cap is valid until its window ends. A cap minted in the last hour of a window uses the next window, so a fresh cap always has at least an hour left.
- **Verify** (no DB): known `kid` → MAC → `h` equals the request's host label → `e ≥ epoch[part]` → `me ≥ epoch[minter]` → `b ≥ boot_floor` → window not over.
- **Revocation** through in-memory epochs, persisted in SQLite: per part (any revoke or unshare), per minter (revoking a session, a link or an agent connection), and global. Boot-epoch floor bumped on every start and every import.
- Outcomes for T16: `unknown_kid`/`bad_mac` → caller returns 404 (indistinguishable from a missing part); `wrong_host`, `stale_epoch`, `expired` → re-grant path (302 or 401).

Schema (T06, verbatim):
```sql
CREATE TABLE epochs (
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- 'part:<id>' | 'minter:sess:<id>' | 'minter:conn:<id>' | 'minter:link:<id>' | 'global' | 'boot'
  epoch INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- `pf-caps` crate API: `mint(&Claims, now) -> Cap`, `verify(&str, host_label, now, &EpochView) -> Result<Claims, CapError>`, `EpochStore` (in-memory `DashMap`/RwLock mirror loaded at start, write-through via the single writer), `bump_part`, `bump_minter`, `bump_global`, `bump_boot` (called at start and by T35 import).
- HMAC via `ring`; HKDF via `ring::hkdf`; CBOR canonical encoding (deterministic map key order, shortest ints).
- Secret `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY` (and `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY_FILE`) from T04, redacted type.

## Not in scope

The policy decision (T26) and the `/grant` hand-off (T27); public-link tokens (random DB tokens, not HMAC-signed, so rotation never affects them; T29); grant-expiry timer that bumps part epochs (T26); serving (T16).

## Design notes and decisions

- 16-byte truncated MAC is ample for an online-only token; constant-time compare.
- `w` is a window **end** in unix minutes; window boundaries aligned to UTC (00:00/12:00 for 12 h).
- `global` epoch is checked as part of `e` semantics: treat `epoch[part]` effective as `max(part, global)`? Decision: verify checks `e ≥ max(epoch[part], epoch[global])` so a global bump kills every cap; record this as the implementation of "and global".
- Caps carry the role so the content listener and `/_rt` can enforce the role × runtime matrix without the DB.
- Leaked URLs give the copier's role on one part until the window ends (≤ 13 h) unless an epoch is bumped: accepted, documented.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Property test: a cap for part A never verifies on host B; same subject+window gives the same cap; bumping an epoch or the boot epoch rejects older caps; a rotated key verifies for 25 h then fails".
- [ ] Encoded cap ≤ 300 bytes for the largest claim set (with `v`, `d`, `g`, `dw`).
- [ ] Host binding, determinism, epoch/boot/global rejection, window expiry, kid acceptance (`kid`, `kid−1` only) all hold.
- [ ] Minting in the last hour of a window yields the next window.
- [ ] Changing `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY` invalidates every outstanding cap.
- [ ] Verify performs zero DB queries (query counter) and < 10 µs p99 in a microbench.

## Tests

- Property tests `pf_caps::tests::prop_host_bound`, `prop_deterministic_in_window`, `prop_epoch_monotonic_rejects`, `prop_tamper_any_byte_fails` (proptest).
- `pf_caps::keys::tests::kid_rotation_25h` (test clock), `hkdf_vector` (golden).
- `pf_caps::tests::last_hour_uses_next_window`, `size_limit_300`.
- Integration `crates/pf-caps/tests/epoch_persistence.rs`: bump in SQLite, restart, verify rejection; bump boot at start; captured logs assert `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_epoch"` and that the cap string never appears in logs.
- Bench `benches/cap_verify.rs` (feeds T23).

## References

PLAN.md §2 Serving a part ("Capabilities live in the path", Keys, Verify, Revocation, Signing keys); §5a Lean hot path; §5e `epochs`, "Capability claims"; §7 Part hosts (caps host-bound, dead after bumps); Final round F10.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Property test: a cap for part A never verifies on host B; same subject+window gives the same cap; bumping an epoch or the boot epoch rejects older caps; a rotated key verifies for 25 h then fails
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T04: Config + secrets loader: site.toml + PF_* env + PF_*_FILE, redaction, docs/env.md, config check
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
- Unblocks: 
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
  - T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report
  - T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
acceptance_criteria: Property test: a cap for part A never verifies on host B; same subject+window gives the same cap; bumping an epoch or the boot epoch rejects older caps; a rotated key verifies for 25 h then fails

title: T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
description:
## Goal and why

The content listener is the heart of partifactory's security model and its performance story: every part runs **sandboxed in an opaque origin with no cookies**, on its own host `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, authorised by a capability in the path, served without a DB read for blobs. It is on the Slice 1 critical path (T13 → **T16** → T17 → T62 → ...) and gated by the sandbox spike T72 (items 1, 9, 10, 12 decide details). Start it as soon as T72's results land.

*Why no cookies on part hosts (decision 10):* agent-written JS is untrusted by default. The sandbox removes the cookie attacks without buying a second domain. *Why one hostname per part:* `connect-src 'self'` and `form-action 'self'` mean *this part only*; caps are host-bound and host → part is a pure function of the hostname (no routing table); per-part cache rules are two host rules; `unsandboxed` needs a real origin; the name is the link.

## Scope

Listener `:8081` (axum + tokio + tower). Routing for `*.<domain>` (Host header preserved by the ingress):
- Only labels ending `-part` are answered; any other label → 404 and increments the **non-part hit metric** (`pf_nonpart_host_hits_total{host}`), "a future service whose DNS record is missing shows up here first".
- `<name>-part`: `/c/<cap>/<path>` = sandboxed content; `/` and any other path outside reserved prefixes (`/c/`, `/l/`, `/_pf/`) = the wrapper (served by T29; T16 provides the route slot); `/l/<token>` public links (T29).
- `blobs-part`: shared blob host (T17).

Canonical part CSP, sent on every part document (HTML entry, any navigable HTML file, an SVG served as a document), verbatim:
```
Content-Security-Policy:
  sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-modals
          allow-downloads allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation;
  default-src 'none';
  script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob: <blob>;
  style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <blob>;
  img-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>;
  media-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>;
  font-src 'self' data: <blob>;
  connect-src 'self' <blob>;
  worker-src 'self' blob:;
  frame-src 'self';
  form-action 'self';
  base-uri 'none';
  object-src 'none';
  frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace> <embedders>
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```
`<blob>` = `https://blobs-part.<domain>`, `<self-host>` = `https://<name>-part.<domain>`, `<workspace>` = `https://parts.<domain>`, `<embedders>` = `[embed] frame_ancestors` (empty by default).

Other rules (verbatim/condensed from §2):
- Responses to `Origin: null` echo `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` and `Vary: Origin`, **never** `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. **Part responses never carry `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`**. No part response ever has `Set-Cookie`; a request carrying any cookie (e.g. an old `__Host-pf_cap`) is treated exactly like one without.
- Errors: a top-level navigation to `/c/…` with an expired window or stale epoch → **302 to `/grant?mode=direct`** (on the workspace: `https://parts.<domain>/grant?part=<name>&path=<path>&mode=direct`). A subresource → **401 with `X-PF-Reauth: 1`**. A request is a navigation when `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is `document` or `iframe`, or, without `Sec-Fetch-*` headers, when `Accept` includes `text/html`. Unknown `kid` or bad MAC → **404**, same as a part that doesn't exist.
- Non-null foreign `Origin` (e.g. `https://evil.example`) on `/c/` requests is rejected (403) before reading any body; `Origin: null` accepted; the part's own origin accepted only for `unsandboxed` parts.
- **Entry document templated at serve time**: the build stores the entry as written; at serve time insert `<script src="<blob>/b/<prelude-hash>">` **first in `<head>`**, the import map (with the cap prefix: `"/": "/c/<cap>/", "/c/": "/c/"`, merged with a build's frozen import map once T60 lands) and the `pf-boot` snapshot `<script type="application/json" id="pf-boot">` (≤ 256 KiB of this person's personal `__storage` docs for this part; empty for `link:`, `render` and guest subjects), then compress on the fly. Every other HTML file a part serves gets the same prelude tag. `toolchain` excludes the prelude, so a prelude fix ships with a deploy and needs no rebuild.
- **DB-free blob paths**: cap check + in-memory `part → live (version, build)` cache + build-manifest LRU (`path → hash`), invalidated from the events stream; the entry document does **one indexed read** (the `data_docs` primary key for this person's `__storage` personal docs, cached per cap). 304 on matching ETag (= hash) answered from the ETag alone. Hot small blobs in an **mmap'd LRU** (+ `pread` for others).
- Caching headers: part blobs `Cache-Control: private, immutable` (with max-age bound to the cap window), never `public`; entry documents `private, no-cache` (they embed `pf-boot`).
- Pinned versions/drafts: a cap with `v` serves that version's build; `d` serves a draft preview (T55 later; route accepts the claim).
- `?dl=1` → `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=<basename>` (sandbox loses `<a download>` filenames for own-host URLs).
- **`unsandboxed` flag** (`parts.isolation = 'unsandboxed'`, admin-only, off by default): drops `sandbox` from the CSP for that host only; everything else (no cookies, caps in path) unchanged.
- `/_rt/v1` and `/_rt/events` routes under `/c/<cap>/` are mounted here (handlers in T62, T51).

**Subtasks** (parent = integration/closure bead; close after all subtasks close and the parent acceptance passes end to end, incl. the T72-informed browser checks):
- `T16.a` host routing, cap extraction/verification, navigation-vs-subresource rule, 302/401/404, Origin rules, non-part metric.
- `T16.b` response headers: canonical CSP template, ACAO null + Vary, no CORP, no Set-Cookie, Referrer/robots/nosniff, `unsandboxed`, `?dl=1`.
- `T16.c` serve-time entry templating: prelude tag, import map with cap prefix, `pf-boot` snapshot, on-the-fly compression.
- `T16.d` the hot path: live-version cache, build-manifest LRU, ETag/304, mmap LRU, brotli negotiation, query counter.

## Not in scope

The wrapper page, `/l/` public links, chrome API (T29); `/grant` (T27); shared blob host (T17); prelude and `/_rt` handlers (T62); events SSE (T51); backend routing `/c/<cap>/api/*` (T101); ingress/client-IP (T89).

## Design notes and decisions

- `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` are deliberate: the threat is the part itself and its author is an agent; CSP here is an **egress** policy. The opaque origin keeps the viewer's credentials away.
- `frame-ancestors` lists the part's own host explicitly because `'self'` in a sandboxed document's policy is a spike item (T72 item 1).
- No `Sec-Fetch-Site` check on `/c/`: opaque-origin requests are `cross-site` even to their own host.
- The response never depends on the User-Agent.
- Logs redact `/c/<…>/` by route (T18).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "`curl -H "Accept: text/html"` on `/c/` with an expired cap -> 302 to /grant?mode=direct, and without that header -> 401 + `X-PF-Reauth`; with a cap -> 200 + the canonical CSP and no `Set-Cookie`; `Origin: https://evil.example` is rejected; a blob path and a 304 on matching ETag make no DB query (query counter); a prelude change reaches a live part with no rebuild".
- [ ] All five dag2 checks pass as integration tests.
- [ ] Non-`-part` host → 404 + metric increment.
- [ ] Unknown kid / bad MAC → 404 byte-identical to a nonexistent part.
- [ ] Every part document carries the exact canonical CSP; `unsandboxed` lacks only `sandbox`.
- [ ] `Origin: null` → ACAO null + `Vary: Origin`, no ACAC, no CORP anywhere.
- [ ] Entry contains the prelude tag first in `<head>`, the import map and `pf-boot`.

## Tests

Subtask tests, plus parent e2e `tests/e2e/content_listener_sandbox.spec.ts` (Chromium, WebKit, Gecko): opens `/c/<cap>/`, asserts `document.cookie` writes have no effect, `localStorage` is the shim (after T62), `parent` access fails, no `Set-Cookie` in HAR; logs from `target/e2e-logs/content_listener_sandbox/server.jsonl` asserted for `event="serve.entry"` with `route_class="content"` and no cap substring.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Serving a part (all of it: canonical CSP, capabilities, errors, framed expiry, runtime calls, entry templating, known losses, unsandboxed, why one hostname per part); §3 Topology; §5a Performance (lean hot path, two-step serving); §5e hot-path rules; §7 Part hosts and the sandbox; decision 10; Final round F01, F02, F13.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): `curl -H "Accept: text/html"` on `/c/` with an expired cap -> 302 to /grant?mode=direct, and without that header -> 401 + `X-PF-Reauth`; with a cap -> 200 + the canonical CSP and no `Set-Cookie`; `Origin: https://evil.example` is rejected; a blob path and a 304 on matching ETag make no DB query (query counter); a prelude change reaches a live part with no rebuild

  - T15: Capability tokens: path caps, HMAC with daily HKDF kid keys, deterministic windows, epochs + boot floor
  - T72: Spike: opaque-origin sandbox, wrapper flow and apex-rp.id WebAuthn on real browsers
- Unblocks: 
  - T17: Shared blob host (blobs-part): serve only shared_blobs hashes, public immutable, ACAO *
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
