title: T16.a: Part-host routing, cap verification, navigation-vs-subresource re-grant rule, Origin checks
description:
## Goal and why

Decide, without the DB, which part a request is for and whether it may proceed, and send expired viewers back through `/grant` the right way (navigation vs subresource).

## Scope

- Host parsing: `<label>.<domain>` (from `[domain] apex`, `part_suffix` = `-part`). Labels not ending `-part` → 404, `pf_nonpart_host_hits_total{host}` incremented. `blobs-part` → T17 router. Otherwise name = label minus `-part`.
- Path dispatch: `/c/<cap>/…` → content; `/l/…`, `/_pf/…`, `/` and other paths → wrapper routes (T29 stubs).
- Cap: split `/c/<cap>/rest`, call `pf_caps::verify(cap, host_label, now, epochs)`.
  - `unknown_kid` / `bad_mac` → **404** (same body as a nonexistent part).
  - expired window / stale epoch (part, minter, boot, global) → if navigation: **302** `https://parts.<domain>/grant?part=<name>&path=<rest>&mode=direct` (path ≤ 2 KiB, starts with `/`); else **401** with `X-PF-Reauth: 1`.
  - Navigation = `Sec-Fetch-Dest` ∈ {`document`, `iframe`}, or with no `Sec-Fetch-*` headers, `Accept` contains `text/html`.
- Origin: `Origin: null` accepted; for `unsandboxed` parts the part's own origin also accepted; any other non-null `Origin` → 403 before reading the body. If `Sec-Fetch-Mode` present on `/_rt`, it must be `cors` (enforced in T62's handler; T16.a exposes the parsed headers). **No `Sec-Fetch-Site` check.**
- Name → part id resolution from the in-memory `name → part` cache (T16.d); a cap's `p` must equal it.
- Request extension `PartRequest {part_id, name, claims, is_navigation, rest_path}` for downstream handlers.

## Not in scope

Headers (T16.b), templating (T16.c), caches (T16.d).

## Design notes and decisions

- 404 for bad MAC so caps can't be used as an oracle for part existence.
- Redirect target host is always the workspace (config), and the path is only the request path, so no open redirect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `curl -H "Accept: text/html"` with an expired cap → 302 to `/grant?...&mode=direct`; without → 401 + `X-PF-Reauth: 1`.
- [ ] `Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe` treated as navigation; `Sec-Fetch-Dest: script` as subresource.
- [ ] `Origin: https://evil.example` → 403; `Origin: null` → allowed.
- [ ] Cap for part A on host B → re-grant path (wrong host), never content.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::route::tests::{host_parse_table, nav_detection_table, origin_table}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/regrant.rs::{expired_nav_302, expired_sub_401, bad_mac_404_identical, foreign_origin_403}` with captured logs asserting `event="cap.verify" outcome=...` and that no log line contains the cap.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Serving a part ("Errors on the part host", "Runtime calls: Auth"); §3 Topology; §5d Metrics (non-part hits); §7 Part hosts.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `curl -H "Accept: text/html"` with an expired cap → 302 to `/grant?...&mode=direct`; without → 401 + `X-PF-Reauth: 1`.
- [ ] `Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe` treated as navigation; `Sec-Fetch-Dest: script` as subresource.
- [ ] `Origin: https://evil.example` → 403; `Origin: null` → allowed.
- [ ] Cap for part A on host B → re-grant path (wrong host), never content.

title: T16.b: Part response headers: canonical CSP template, ACAO null, no CORP, no Set-Cookie, unsandboxed, ?dl=1
description:
## Goal and why

One canonical header set, written once, applied to every part response, so the sandbox and egress policy can't drift between handlers.

## Scope

- `pf_serve::headers::part_document_headers(name, cfg, isolation)` producing exactly (verbatim template, `<…>` substituted):
```
Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-modals allow-downloads allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation; default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob: <blob>; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <blob>; img-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>; media-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>; font-src 'self' data: <blob>; connect-src 'self' <blob>; worker-src 'self' blob:; frame-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace> <embedders>
Referrer-Policy: no-referrer
X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```
  Applied to the HTML entry, any navigable HTML file, and SVG served as a document. Non-document subresources get `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Robots-Tag`, `nosniff` (CSP harmless but optional; send it on all part responses for simplicity unless T72 shows a problem).
- `unsandboxed` (`parts.isolation`): identical minus the `sandbox …;` directive.
- CORS: if request `Origin: null` → `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` + `Vary: Origin`; never `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`; never `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`. (The workspace host never answers `Origin: null` with CORS — asserted in T29/T38.)
- A tower layer that **strips any `Set-Cookie`** from part-host responses (defence in depth) and ignores request cookies entirely.
- `?dl=1` → `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<basename>"`.
- `X-PF-Request-Id` on responses once T106 lands (pass-through of the request id from T89 now).

## Not in scope

Wrapper CSP (T29), blob host headers (T17).

## Design notes and decisions

- `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` lets `target=_blank` open a normal site; `allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation` lets a tapped `target=_top` link work while script-driven top navigation stays blocked.
- CSP from the header (not `<meta>`, not Report-Only): spike item 9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden header snapshot for a sandboxed and an unsandboxed part.
- [ ] No response from `:8081` part hosts ever contains `Set-Cookie` or `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` or `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` (property over all routes).

## Tests

- `pf_serve::headers::tests::{csp_golden, unsandboxed_drops_sandbox_only, embedders_from_config}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/headers_all_routes.rs`: iterate every route class with/without `Origin: null`; assert invariants; captured logs include `route_class`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The canonical part CSP" and its Why lines; "Escape hatch: unsandboxed"; "Known losses" (`?dl=1`); §7 Part hosts.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T16.a: Part-host routing, cap verification, navigation-vs-subresource re-grant rule, Origin checks
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Golden header snapshot for a sandboxed and an unsandboxed part.
- [ ] No response from `:8081` part hosts ever contains `Set-Cookie` or `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` or `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` (property over all routes).

title: T16.c: Serve-time entry templating: prelude tag first in head, cap-prefixed import map, pf-boot snapshot
description:
## Goal and why

Make the runtime prelude and the cap prefix arrive in every HTML document without baking them into builds, so a prelude fix ships with a deploy and needs no rebuild, and root-relative URLs keep working under `/c/<cap>/`.

## Scope

- For the entry document and every other HTML file a part serves, insert at serve time, in this order, as the **first children of `<head>`** (creating `<head>` if absent; streaming HTML rewriter such as `lol_html`):
  1. `<script src="https://blobs-part.<domain>/b/<prelude-hash>"></script>` (the current prelude blob hash from T62/T17; not part of the build cache key);
  2. `<script type="importmap">{"imports": {"/": "/c/<cap>/", "/c/": "/c/", …build import map (T60)…}}</script>` — only where it doesn't conflict with an existing author import map (merge; author entries win except `/` and `/c/`);
  3. `<script type="application/json" id="pf-boot">{…}</script>`: the bootstrap snapshot: ≤ 256 KiB of this person's personal state for this part (the `data_docs` rows `scope='personal', owner=<user>, collection='__storage'`), plus `{part, name, base_path: "/c/<cap>/", subject_kind, role, dw, guest_label?, version, live}` the prelude needs. **Empty storage for `link:`, `render` and guest subjects.** JSON escaped for `</script>`.
- The one indexed DB read: `data_docs` primary-key range for this person's `__storage` personal docs, **cached per cap** (small LRU keyed by cap string hash, invalidated on personal writes from `/_rt`).
- Compress on the fly (brotli q4-5 or gzip by `Accept-Encoding`); `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` for templated documents; `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
- `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`.

## Not in scope

The prelude itself (T62); frozen build import maps (T60).

## Design notes and decisions

- Prelude first so `localStorage` is redefined before any page script runs (spike item 4).
- The snapshot is what makes `localStorage` synchronous and "personal, synced across your devices".
- Under `/c/` only blob paths are DB-free; the entry does this one read (Final round F01).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Changing the prelude blob hash changes the served entry of an existing live part with no new build row (dag2 check).
- [ ] Snapshot ≤ 256 KiB; empty for link/render/guest caps.
- [ ] HTML without `<head>` and with an existing import map handled (golden).

## Tests

- `pf_serve::template::tests::{insert_order_golden, no_head, merge_author_importmap, script_close_escaping}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/prelude_no_rebuild.rs`: swap prelude hash, GET entry, assert new tag and `builds` count unchanged; logs `event="serve.entry" boot_bytes=<n>`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The entry document is templated at serve time"; "The prelude" (`pf-boot` ≤ 256 KiB); root-relative URLs four ways; §2 link section (DB reads for entry); Final round F01, F02.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T16.a: Part-host routing, cap verification, navigation-vs-subresource re-grant rule, Origin checks
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Changing the prelude blob hash changes the served entry of an existing live part with no new build row (dag2 check).
- [ ] Snapshot ≤ 256 KiB; empty for link/render/guest caps.
- [ ] HTML without `<head>` and with an existing import map handled (golden).

title: T16.d: Content hot path: live-version cache, build-manifest LRU, ETag/304, mmap LRU, brotli negotiation
description:
## Goal and why

Keep blob serving DB-free and allocation-light: the target is part blob p99 < 200 µs server time (warm) and parity with nginx on static files (T23, T74).

## Scope

- **Serving a part is two steps**: an in-memory `part → live (version, build)` cache (+ `name → part_id`) resolves the entry without a DB read, then the build-manifest LRU resolves `path → {hash, br_hash, content_type}`. Both filled lazily, **invalidated from the events stream** (`part.live_changed`, rename, delete) via the in-memory broadcast.
- Version-pinned caps (`v`) look up that version's ok build; drafts (`d`) handled once T55 exists (return 404 until then).
- ETag = blob hash (strong). `If-None-Match` match → 304 from the ETag alone (no DB, no file read).
- Encoding: if `br_hash` exists and `Accept-Encoding` includes `br`, serve it with `Content-Encoding: br`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
- **mmap'd LRU** for hot small blobs (configurable budget, default 256 MiB, ≤ 1 MiB per entry), `pread`/`tokio::fs` streaming for others; verify-on-read is done by T07 at fill time.
- `Cache-Control: private, immutable, max-age=<seconds until the cap window end>` for part blobs; never `public`.
- Range requests (`Range: bytes=`) for media.
- A **query counter** (test feature in `pf-db`, counts SQLite statements per request) used by tests.

## Not in scope

Shared blob host caching (T17); bench harness (T23).

## Design notes and decisions

- Deterministic 12 h caps keep `private, immutable` part blobs cached in the browser across repeat opens; they re-download on window roll, revocation, deploy (boot epoch).
- hyper copies through userspace; mmap + pread is enough for v1 (§5a "Honest about zero-copy").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Blob path and 304 make zero DB queries (query counter = 0).
- [ ] After `part.live_changed`, the next request serves the new build.
- [ ] Brotli variant served when accepted.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::cache::tests::{invalidate_on_live_changed, lru_eviction}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/hot_path.rs::{blob_zero_queries, etag_304_zero_queries, br_negotiation, range_request}`; captured logs assert `latency_us` present and `outcome="not_modified"`.
- Microbench `benches/serve_blob.rs` (consumed by T23).

## References

PLAN.md §5a Performance (lean hot path, serving in two steps, repeat opens); §5e hot-path rules; §2 link section (blob paths DB-free).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T16.a: Part-host routing, cap verification, navigation-vs-subresource re-grant rule, Origin checks
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Blob path and 304 make zero DB queries (query counter = 0).
- [ ] After `part.live_changed`, the next request serves the new build.
- [ ] Brotli variant served when accepted.

title: T17: Shared blob host (blobs-part): serve only shared_blobs hashes, public immutable, ACAO *
description:
## Goal and why

Third-party libraries, fonts, the runtime prelude, the wrapper's script/styles, `pf-shell.css` and later Jig are **shared blobs**: not private to anyone, cached once across all parts, cacheable forever by the browser and any CDN in front. Part blobs must never be served here. T17 is on the Slice 1 critical path because the prelude (T62) is a shared blob loaded from this host.

*Why the class is per reference, not per blob:* one hash can be both (an agent uploads its own copy of `react.production.min.js`). Serving rules then follow what refers to it (`shared_blobs` vs `build_files`), not an accident of upload order.

## Scope

- Host `blobs-part.<domain>` on `:8081` (`blobs` is a name reserved in code, T09). Routes: `GET /b/<hash>` and `GET /b/<hash>/<filename>` (the optional trailing name, e.g. `/b/<hash>/jig.css`, for readability and content-type), `HEAD`.
- Serves **only hashes present in `shared_blobs`**; anything else → 404 (identical to a missing hash), even if the blob exists as a part blob.
- Headers: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (no credentials ever); `ETag` = hash; `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; correct `Content-Type` from `shared_blobs.label`/extension (JS `text/javascript`, CSS, woff2 `font/woff2`, ...); brotli variant when available; **never `Set-Cookie`**; no CORP (opaque-origin parts load these no-cors/cors).
- 304 on ETag; lookup of membership via an in-memory set loaded from `shared_blobs` and updated on insert (mirror, seed, runtime).
- Seeding API for other tasks: `SharedBlobs::seed(label, bytes) -> hash` with `source='seed'` (prelude, wrapper bundle, `pf-shell.css`), `source='mirror'` (T14), `source='runtime'`.

Schema (T06, verbatim):
```sql
CREATE TABLE shared_blobs (                          -- class is per reference: only these are served by blobs-part
  hash       TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  source     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('seed','mirror','runtime')),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- 'react@18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js'
  added_at   INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

## Not in scope

Edge cache rules for `/b/*` (T91 adapter); the content listener routing (T16); the library set (T60).

## Design notes and decisions

- Edge caching is an optimisation, never required: correct `Cache-Control` is enough (a CDN that honours it caches; Cloudflare needs the explicit rule because it caches by extension, T91).
- ACAO `*` is safe because nothing here is private and no credentials are involved.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A part-class hash returns 404 on the blob host; a shared hash returns `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and never `Set-Cookie`".
- [ ] Part-only hash → 404; unknown hash → identical 404.
- [ ] Shared hash → 200 with the exact Cache-Control, ACAO `*`, correct content type, no Set-Cookie.
- [ ] Same hash both shared and part-referenced: served here, and still served `private` on the part host.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::blobhost::tests::{only_shared_served, headers_golden, content_type_from_label}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/blob_host.rs::{part_hash_404, shared_hash_public_immutable, dual_class_hash}` with captured logs `event="blobhost.serve" outcome="not_shared"`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 The core idea (Blob: shared vs part); §3 Topology (`blobs-part`); §5e `shared_blobs`; §7 Caching and blobs.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A part-class hash returns 404 on the blob host; a shared hash returns `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and never `Set-Cookie`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
- Unblocks: 
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps
  - T23: Regression bench: same-machine content-path bench vs previous release, fail on >10 % regression
  - T54: Jig design system: jig.css shared blob, @partifactory/jig, presets, design_system op, Jig as a part
acceptance_criteria: A part-class hash returns 404 on the blob host; a shared hash returns `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and never `Set-Cookie`

title: T02: Spikes: rolldown/oxc as libraries, rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos SSR vs askama+islands
description:
## Goal and why

Three one-day maturity spikes, run before P0 freezes, each ending in a go/no-go note with a runnable example. They de-risk the three young dependencies the plan bets on: the TSX compiler (oxc + rolldown as Rust libraries), the MCP server SDK (rmcp 3.x, stateless Streamable HTTP), and the workspace UI framework (Leptos 0.8 SSR + hydration vs `askama`/`maud` templates + vanilla-JS islands).

Why now: "the serving model and the compiler are the two things most likely to force a redesign. Finding a rolldown or Safari problem in P3 would be finding it last" (§6). Slice 1 keeps the compiler spike even though the `tsx` kind itself (T60) moved to right after Slice 1 (decision 39), "so a rolldown or oxc problem still shows up first". The rmcp spike gates T53 (MCP server, on the Slice 1 critical path), and the Leptos spike gates T31 (workspace UI). T02 is in Slice 1.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and all three notes are merged):
- **T02.a** - rolldown/oxc as libraries: go/no-go note `docs/spikes/compiler.md` + runnable example.
- **T02.b** - rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP: note `docs/spikes/mcp.md` + runnable example server.
- **T02.c** - Leptos SSR vs askama + islands, applying the §5 decision rule: note `docs/spikes/ui.md` + runnable example.

Each note has the same shape: question, versions tested (exact crate versions and git commits), what was built, measurements, findings, risks, **decision (go / no-go / go-with-fallback)**, and what the dependent tasks must do differently. Each example is a `cargo run -p spike-<name>` (or `examples/` under the relevant crate) that a reviewer can run in under five minutes.

Time box: one day each. If a spike overruns, record the overrun itself as a finding (it is evidence for the decision rule in T02.c).

## Not in scope

- Implementing the build worker (T13), the TSX kind (T60), the MCP server (T53) or the workspace UI (T31). Spike code is throwaway and lives outside the shipped crates (or behind a `spike` feature) so it never reaches the release binary.
- The browser sandbox spike (T72) and the Authentik spike (T03), which are separate tasks.

## Design notes and decisions

- §5 "Maturity check before P0 freezes": one-day spikes on rolldown/oxc as libraries, rmcp stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos SSR vs templates, and the sandbox on real browsers (T72).
- A no-go is a valid outcome. The plan already names the fallbacks: esbuild-as-subprocess behind the same child protocol (compiler); askama/maud + small vanilla-JS islands (UI). There is no named fallback for rmcp; a no-go there means hand-writing the stateless Streamable HTTP endpoint over axum using rmcp's types only, and the note must say so.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Three go/no-go notes in docs/spikes/, each with a runnable example; the Leptos note applies the §5 decision rule".

- [ ] `docs/spikes/compiler.md`, `docs/spikes/mcp.md`, `docs/spikes/ui.md` merged, each with an explicit decision line.
- [ ] Each note links a runnable example and the exact command to run it; a second person ran it.
- [ ] The UI note states both decision-rule numbers (days of friction for the share sheet; hydrated part-view bundle size in KB brotli) and the resulting choice.
- [ ] Dependent tasks (T13, T60, T53, T31) have the notes' consequences copied into their beads (comment or description update).

## Tests

Spikes are evidence, not product code; each subtask lists the checks its example runs. The parent's only test is that the three examples build in CI (`cargo build -p spike-compiler -p spike-mcp -p spike-ui`) until they're deleted after the dependent tasks land.

## References

PLAN.md §5 Stack (table rows TSX/JSX, MCP, Workspace UI; "Why Leptos, and when it loses"; "Maturity check before P0 freezes"), §6 P0 and "Why the sandbox and TSX in P0", §8 decision 39, Slice 1 "What's in it" (T02 stays in the slice).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Three go/no-go notes in docs/spikes/, each with a runnable example; the Leptos note applies the §5 decision rule
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T01: Cargo workspace, crate layout, CI (fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit), Renovate
- Unblocks: 
  - T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T02.a: Spike: oxc transform + rolldown bundle as Rust libraries in a child process
  - T02.b: Spike: rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP server on axum with bearer auth
  - T02.c: Spike: Leptos 0.8 SSR + hydration vs askama/maud + vanilla-JS islands (decision rule)

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria: Three go/no-go notes in docs/spikes/, each with a runnable example; the Leptos note applies the §5 decision rule

title: T02.a: Spike: oxc transform + rolldown bundle as Rust libraries in a child process
description:
## Goal and why

Prove (or disprove) that `oxc` (umbrella crate, `transformer` feature: transform + minify) and `rolldown` (bundle) can be driven as Rust libraries from a child process of the same binary, within the build worker's limits, so the `tsx` kind (T60) and the build worker protocol (T13) can be designed with confidence. The plan pins and vendors them because "oxc is 0.x with breaking releases, and rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate".

## Scope

- Build `spike-compiler`: a binary that re-execs itself as a child (`spike-compiler worker`), sends a request over **length-prefixed CBOR on stdin/stdout** (the T13 protocol shape), and in the child:
  - transforms a TSX entry `App.tsx` (default export) with oxc (JSX automatic runtime, TypeScript stripping),
  - bundles with rolldown against a **virtual module set** (an in-memory map standing in for the shared library set: `react`, `react-dom` 18.3 resolved to local files, no network, no `node_modules` walk),
  - emits ESM output plus a generated import map, minified with oxc.
- Enforce the T13 limits in the example: 10 s deadline, `RLIMIT_AS` 1 GiB, `SIGKILL` on breach; show a deliberate infinite-loop plugin or pathological input being killed and reported, and a deliberate panic surfacing as a failed build rather than killing the parent.
- Measure: child spawn cost (plan claims 1-2 ms for a static binary), cold and warm compile+bundle time for (1) a 50-line component, (2) a component importing `recharts`-sized code, (3) 5 files. Compare to the targets: TSX `part_edit` incl. compile + bundle + brotli p50 < 150 ms / p99 < 1 s.
- Record exact crate versions/commits pinned; whether the Rust APIs needed (transformer options, rolldown `Bundler` with in-memory input and resolve hooks) exist and how stable they look; licence check via `cargo deny`.
- Try one esbuild-as-subprocess run of the same input behind the same CBOR protocol, to confirm the fallback is a drop-in.

## Not in scope

The real library set (`libset.toml`), CDN aliasing, golden corpus and Tailwind (T60, T61); mirroring (T14).

## Design notes and decisions

title: T02.b: Spike: rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP server on axum with bearer auth
description:
## Goal and why

Prove that `rmcp` 3.x (the official Rust MCP SDK) can serve partifactory's MCP surface the way the plan requires: **Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, stateless**, spec revision **2026-07-28** and compatible with **2025-11-25**, mounted inside the existing axum workspace listener, with tools generated from `schemars` types and authentication failures as plain HTTP 401s. T53 (MCP server, on the Slice 1 critical path) depends on this.

## Scope

- Build `spike-mcp`: an axum app on `:8080` mounting rmcp's Streamable HTTP service at `/mcp` in stateless mode, exposing two tools whose input/output are `#[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` structs (e.g. a toy `part_get` and `part_create`).
- Check and record:
  1. stateless operation: no session id required; any request can hit any process; `server/discover` and the `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers of the 2026-07-28 revision are supported (or what's missing);
  2. `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` come from `schemars`, and the `outputSchema` root must be an object (the plan says non-object outputs are wrapped) - confirm and show the wrapping;
  3. tool annotations (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`) can be set;
  4. errors as tool results with `isError: true` + `structuredContent` + a one-line text rendering;
  5. **auth failure is HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://parts.<domain>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`** and a JSON body, raised by an axum middleware before rmcp sees the request - never a tool result;
  6. image content blocks (for `part_check` screenshots, PNG <= 1 MB) can be returned;
  7. server `instructions` can be a long markdown string (the agent contract);
  8. MCP resources (`part://recent`, `part://<name>`) as projections.
- Connect with Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http spike http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer test"`) and with rmcp's own client; record versions.

## Not in scope

The operation registry (T20), real auth (T43), discovery documents (T56).

## Design notes and decisions

- "No operation depends on an MCP-only feature: no sampling, no elicitation, no notifications" (§4b). Stateless Streamable HTTP has no server push anyway; `part_watch` long-poll replaces it (T123).
- rmcp's OAuth support is client-side only, so partifactory's AS is hand-written (T43); the spike only needs bearer extraction.
- If rmcp can't do stateless or 401-before-dispatch, the fallback recorded in the note is to hand-write the JSON-RPC endpoint over axum, reusing rmcp's protocol types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/spikes/mcp.md` with go/no-go and a table of the eight checks (pass/fail/workaround) and versions.

title: T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
description:
## Goal and why

Claude-written pages expect `localStorage`, `fetch('/data.json')`, `new Worker('./w.js')` and friends; inside an opaque-origin sandbox those break. The **prelude** is partifactory's small runtime, a shared blob injected first in `<head>` of every served HTML document (T16.c), that makes such pages run unchanged, and `/_rt/v1` is its one server endpoint. It also closes the loop for agents: uncaught errors are reported to `runtime_errors`, which `part_get` returns. On the Slice 1 critical path (T17 → **T62** → T77/T80/T96 → ...).

*Semantics change, stated plainly:* `localStorage` becomes "personal, synced across your devices", not "per device". That's what Claude-written code expects anyway, because claude.ai artifacts can't use `localStorage` either.

## Scope

The prelude (verbatim from PLAN.md §2 "The prelude"):
- installs `window.storage`, `claude.use(...)` and `window.partifactory`: `ready()` (call it when the page has finished its first render; `part_check` stops waiting then), `basePath`, and `on("data.changed", fn)` (wired to `/_rt/events` in T51/T96);
- redefines `localStorage` as a synchronous in-memory `Storage` seeded from the bootstrap snapshot (≤ 256 KiB of the person's state for this part, in `<script type="application/json" id="pf-boot">`), written behind to personal state on `/_rt` (debounced, plus a `pagehide` flush via `sendBeacon`); `sessionStorage` is memory only; `document.cookie` is an inert in-memory string; `indexedDB` and `caches` are `undefined`, so feature detection falls back. Public-link viewers (no person) get memory-only storage;
- wraps `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest.open` and `EventSource` to add the `/c/<cap>/` prefix to same-host root-relative URLs, wraps `Worker`/`SharedWorker` to fetch the script and start it from a `blob:` URL, and sets `crossOrigin = "anonymous"` on script-created `Image`s;
- reports uncaught errors, unhandled rejections and blocked loads to `runtime_errors`, and handles `pf:regrant`, `pf:version` (live reload) and the wrapper's postMessage schema.

`/_rt` (verbatim from §2 "Runtime calls"): `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` with `Content-Type: text/plain` and a JSON body `{op, args}` — a CORS-simple request, so **no preflight**. Auth is the cap in the path, bound to this host; accept `Origin: null` (or the part's own origin for `unsandboxed`), reject any other non-null `Origin` before reading the body; if `Sec-Fetch-Mode` is present it must be `cors`; no `Sec-Fetch-Site` check. Ops: `storage.get/getMany/set/delete/list` (personal and shared), `db.*`, `comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`. **T62 implements**: the endpoint, dispatch, role checks via cap claims, personal `storage.*` (backing the `localStorage` shim), `errors.report`, `refresh` (a fresh cap for the same subject: the credentialed regrant for standalone documents); shared `storage.*` and `data.changed` are T96, `db.*`/`user`/`comments`/`artifact` are T73/T50.

**Subtasks** (parent = integration/closure bead; close after all subtasks close and the acceptance passes end to end in real browsers):
- `T62.a` `/_rt/v1` server endpoint: text/plain JSON dispatch, Origin/Sec-Fetch rules, cap-role checks, personal storage ops, `refresh`, body caps, rate limits hook.
- `T62.b` prelude storage shims: `localStorage` (seeded from `pf-boot`, write-behind, `sendBeacon` flush), `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie`, `indexedDB`/`caches` removal, `window.storage` personal API.
- `T62.c` prelude network and lifecycle: fetch/XHR/EventSource prefixing, blob-URL workers, `crossOrigin` images, `partifactory.ready()/basePath/on`, `pf:regrant`, `pf:version`, postMessage schema.
- `T62.d` runtime error reporting: `errors.report` client capture + `runtime_errors` store (fingerprint, count, 1,000 cap trigger, rate limit ≤ 10/min/part).

Build of the prelude: TypeScript/JS source in `crates/pf-prelude/src/`, bundled + minified at build time of the binary (oxc), embedded, seeded as a shared blob at start (`shared_blobs.source = 'seed'`, label `prelude@<version>.js`); its hash is what T16.c inserts. Size budget: ≤ 12 KiB brotli.

## Not in scope

Shared `window.storage` writes, limits, `PfError` codes for shared data, `data.changed` (T96); `/_rt/events` SSE (T51); `claude.use("db"|"user"|"comments"|"artifact")` (T73); assets (T83); the wrapper side of `pf:regrant` (T29); live reload UX (T79).

## Design notes and decisions

- `text/plain` POST avoids a preflight through the proxy; CSRF is moot because there's no ambient credential, and a sibling part can't reach this host (`connect-src 'self'`) and its cap verifies only for its own host.
- Framed parts never navigate themselves to `/grant` (a subframe navigation from an opaque origin is cross-site for `SameSite=Lax`, so a login page would render inside the frame): the prelude posts `{type: "pf:regrant"}` to the parent; standalone documents call `refresh` or reload through `/grant`.
- Root-relative URLs are covered four ways (build rewrite, served import map, prelude prefixing, build lint).
- Known losses under the sandbox: service workers, remembered device permissions, persistent IndexedDB, `<a download>` filenames.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A Claude-written page that uses `localStorage` keeps its state across reload and across two browsers for the same person; no `OPTIONS` request is ever sent; uncaught errors appear in `runtime_errors`".
- [ ] `localStorage` state persists across reload and appears in a second browser (same person) after reload.
- [ ] HAR of a full session contains zero `OPTIONS` requests.
- [ ] Throw, unhandled rejection and a blocked third-party load each create/increment a `runtime_errors` row with correct `kind`.
- [ ] `document.cookie = "a=b"` then reading returns only the in-memory string; no request carries a Cookie.
- [ ] `fetch('/data.json')` resolves under `/c/<cap>/`; `new Worker('./w.js')` works on Chromium, WebKit, Gecko.
- [ ] Prelude ≤ 12 KiB brotli.

## Tests

Subtask tests plus e2e `tests/e2e/prelude_claude_compat.spec.ts` over a corpus of Claude-written artifacts (the sandbox compat corpus: 30 real Claude-written artifacts and 10 Vite builds, zero uncaught errors), in Chromium, WebKit and Gecko, two browser contexts for the same fixture user; asserts zero `OPTIONS` in HAR, persistence, and server log events `event="rt.call" op="storage.set" outcome="ok"`; keeps traces/HAR/`server.jsonl` under `target/e2e-logs/prelude_claude_compat/`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Serving a part ("Runtime calls: /_rt", "The prelude", "Framed expiry", root-relative URLs, "Known losses"); §3a role × runtime matrix; §3c errors close the loop; §5 Stack (sandbox compat corpus); §5e `runtime_errors`, `data_docs`; §7 Part hosts; Final round F13, F32.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A Claude-written page that uses `localStorage` keeps its state across reload and across two browsers for the same person; no `OPTIONS` request is ever sent; uncaught errors appear in `runtime_errors`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T17: Shared blob host (blobs-part): serve only shared_blobs hashes, public immutable, ACAO *
  - T19: Dev/test identity fake (fixture users for `refresh` and for the two-browser e2e; the real policy check arrives with T26)
- Unblocks: 
  - M0: Milestone - P0 Core (local) done
  - T77: Per-part data snapshots of shared docs: on by default (daily keep 7), roll back, reset, JSON download
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
  - T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
  - T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
  - T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
  - T83: Viewer asset uploads: assets.put over /_rt, /_a/<id>, quota, listed and deletable by agents
  - T85: Phone editing: tap-to-edit text as anchor edits, long-press point-and-comment
  - G08: Sandbox compat corpus: 30 Claude-written artifacts and 10 Vite builds rendered under the sandbox in CI
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T62.a: /_rt/v1 endpoint: text/plain JSON dispatch, Origin rules, role checks, personal storage, refresh
  - T62.b: Prelude storage shims: synced localStorage, memory sessionStorage, inert cookie, no indexedDB/caches
  - T62.c: Prelude network and lifecycle: URL prefixing, blob workers, crossOrigin images, ready(), pf:regrant, pf:version
  - T62.d: Runtime error reporting: prelude capture, errors.report, runtime_errors store with 1,000-per-part cap
acceptance_criteria: A Claude-written page that uses `localStorage` keeps its state across reload and across two browsers for the same person; no `OPTIONS` request is ever sent; uncaught errors appear in `runtime_errors`

title: T62.a: /_rt/v1 endpoint: text/plain JSON dispatch, Origin rules, role checks, personal storage, refresh
description:
## Goal and why

The single runtime endpoint every part page calls, designed so it never needs a CORS preflight and never trusts anything but the host-bound cap.

## Scope

- Route `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` on `:8081`; request `Content-Type: text/plain` (also accept `text/plain;charset=UTF-8`), body JSON `{op, args}`; response JSON `{ok: true, result}` or `{ok: false, error: {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}}` (codes from the T20 error catalogue), with ACAO `null` + `Vary: Origin` for `Origin: null` (T16.b).
- Checks before reading the body: cap verified (T16.a); `Origin` must be `null` (or the part's own origin if `unsandboxed`); if `Sec-Fetch-Mode` present it must be `cors`; **no `Sec-Fetch-Site` check**. Body cap 512 KiB (a 256 KiB value + JSON overhead), enforced before parse.
- Ops in this subtask:
  - personal `storage.get`, `storage.getMany` (≤ 500 keys), `storage.set`, `storage.delete`, `storage.list` (prefix, cursor, limit ≤ 1000, values) on `data_docs (scope='personal', owner=<user id>, collection='__storage', doc_id=<key>)`, `rev` incremented, `updated_by = 'user:<id>'`; also a bulk `storage.syncLocal` used by the shim's write-behind (set/delete batch). Only for subjects with a person (`user:`); `link:`/guest/`render` subjects get `forbidden` for personal writes (their storage is memory only in the prelude).
  - `refresh`: returns a fresh cap for the same subject (re-mints via T15 if the subject's grant still allows it; for `user:` subjects this needs the policy check, so it calls the T26 decision API once that lands; until then for fixture users from T19), "the credentialed regrant for standalone documents"; not a data op.
  - `errors.report` (T62.d implements the store).
  - every other op name → `invalid_input` with the list of known ops; guest caps calling any non-data op → `403` (T95 extends).
- Limits from §3a: key 1–512 bytes UTF-8, no control chars; value string ≤ 256 KiB; personal data ≤ 256 KiB per person per part (`quota_exceeded`); `storage_full` from the disk budget (T114 hook).
- All writes through the single writer; invalidate the per-cap `pf-boot` cache (T16.c).

## Not in scope

Shared storage and `data.changed` (T96); `db.*`, `user`, `comments.*`, `artifact.publish` (T73, T50).

## Design notes and decisions

- One op-dispatch table keyed by op name with a role requirement per op (the role × runtime matrix in §3a); cap `r`, `ro`, `dw`, `s` decide.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Simple-request shape verified (no preflight in browsers); non-null foreign Origin → 403 without parsing.
- [ ] Personal storage round trip; limits produce the right codes.
- [ ] `refresh` returns a valid new cap; after an epoch bump it returns `forbidden` if access was revoked.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::rt::tests::{dispatch_unknown_op, origin_rules, sec_fetch_mode, key_value_limits}`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_personal.rs::{set_get_list_cursor, quota_256k, refresh_after_revoke}` asserting `event="rt.call" op=... outcome=...` with no values in logs.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "Runtime calls: /_rt, one simple request"; §3a role × runtime matrix and shared-data limits; §3c window.storage API; docs/agent-contract.md "Shared data from inside a part", "Limits".

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Simple-request shape verified (no preflight in browsers); non-null foreign Origin → 403 without parsing.
- [ ] Personal storage round trip; limits produce the right codes.
- [ ] `refresh` returns a valid new cap; after an epoch bump it returns `forbidden` if access was revoked.

title: T62.b: Prelude storage shims: synced localStorage, memory sessionStorage, inert cookie, no indexedDB/caches
description:
## Goal and why

Make storage-using Claude pages work in an opaque origin, where the real `localStorage` throws, with semantics people actually want: personal state that follows them across devices.

## Scope

In `crates/pf-prelude/src/storage.ts`, executed before any page script (prelude is first in `<head>`):
- Parse `#pf-boot` JSON once; build a synchronous in-memory `Storage` implementation (full interface: `getItem`, `setItem`, `removeItem`, `clear`, `key`, `length`, property access via Proxy) seeded from the snapshot; install with `Object.defineProperty(window, "localStorage", {value, configurable: false})` (spike item 4 verifies visibility to later inline scripts).
- **Write-behind** to personal state via `/_rt` `storage.syncLocal` (T62.a): debounced (e.g. 500 ms), plus a `pagehide` flush via `navigator.sendBeacon` (text/plain body, so still a simple request). Enforce the 256 KiB per person per part budget client side too (throw `QuotaExceededError` like a browser).
- Public-link viewers, guests and `render` subjects (no person; `pf-boot.subject_kind`) get **memory-only** storage with no write-behind.
- `sessionStorage`: memory only (per tab).
- `document.cookie`: getter/setter over an inert in-memory string, never sent anywhere. `cookieStore` (if present) made inert/undefined.
- `indexedDB` and `caches` set to `undefined` so feature detection falls back.
- `window.storage` personal methods (`get(key)`, `set(key, value)`, `delete(key)`, `list(prefix?)`, `getMany`) calling `/_rt` with `shared = false`; shared variants added by T96 (the API shape is Claude's: `get` resolves to `{key, value, shared}` or `null`).

## Not in scope

Shared storage (T96); `claude.use` (T73).

## Design notes and decisions

- A `storage` event isn't fired across tabs for the shim; cross-device sync is on reload (snapshot). Live personal sync isn't promised.
- Values coerced to strings like the real API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Page writing `localStorage` then reloading sees its state; a second browser for the same person sees it after load.
- [ ] Closing the tab within 100 ms of a write still persists (sendBeacon).
- [ ] Feature-detect patterns (`'indexedDB' in window && indexedDB`) fall back cleanly.

## Tests

title: T62.c: Prelude network and lifecycle: URL prefixing, blob workers, crossOrigin images, ready(), pf:regrant, pf:version
description:
## Goal and why

Root-relative URLs and workers must keep working under `/c/<cap>/`, and an expired cap must be renewed without a navigation inside a frame.

## Scope

- Wrap `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open` and `EventSource` so same-host root-relative URLs (`/x`, `https://<self-host>/x`) get the `/c/<cap>/` prefix (from `pf-boot.base_path`); URLs already under `/c/` untouched; other origins untouched (CSP decides).
- Wrap `Worker`/`SharedWorker`: fetch the script (prefixed), start it from a `blob:` URL (`worker-src 'self' blob:`), preserving `type: "module"` where possible (WebKit has open bugs here: spike item 5 result decides the fallback).
- Patch `Image` constructor / `HTMLImageElement` created by script to set `crossOrigin = "anonymous"`.
- On a `401` with `X-PF-Reauth: 1` from any wrapped request: if framed (`window.parent !== window`), `parent.postMessage({type: "pf:regrant"}, "*")` and wait for `{type: "pf:cap", cap}` (the wrapper answers with a credentialed POST to `https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` and either re-sets the frame `src` or sends the cap, per T29's schema); if standalone, call `/_rt` `refresh` and retry once, else reload via `/grant`.
- `window.partifactory = {ready(), basePath, on(event, fn)}`: `ready()` sets a flag + posts `{type: "pf:ready"}` (the render sidecar and wrapper listen); `on("data.changed", fn)` registry (event source wired by T96/T51); `pf:version` handling hook for live reload (T79 decides UX; T62 just forwards to the wrapper / reloads when standalone and no unsaved state).
- postMessage schema (documented in `crates/pf-prelude/PROTOCOL.md`): messages `pf:regrant`, `pf:cap`, `pf:ready`, `pf:version`, `pf:error`; the wrapper identifies the frame by `event.source === frame.contentWindow`, never by `event.origin` (`"null"`).

## Not in scope

Wrapper side (T29), live reload UX (T79), event stream (T51).

## Design notes and decisions

- Framed expiry never navigates the frame to `/grant` (SameSite=Lax cookies aren't sent from an opaque-origin subframe navigation).
- Runtime-built third-party URLs are not rewritten; CSP blocks them and T62.d reports `blocked_load`/`csp`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fetch('/data.json')`, XHR and `EventSource('/x')` hit `/c/<cap>/…`.
- [ ] `new Worker('./w.js')` and module workers run in Chromium, WebKit (or documented fallback), Gecko.
- [ ] Expired cap in a framed part triggers exactly one `pf:regrant` and the page continues without navigation.

## Tests

- Unit `crates/pf-prelude/tests/{prefix_urls, worker_wrap, image_crossorigin}`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/prelude_network.spec.ts`: fixture page with fetch/XHR/worker/image; second test fast-forwards the server clock past the window and asserts the regrant flow; server events `event="cap.verify" outcome="expired"` followed by `event="chrome.grant"`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The prelude" (wraps fetch…), "Framed expiry", root-relative URLs, wrapper `event.source` rule (§4a.6 Frame); §5 spike items 3, 5.

title: T62.d: Runtime error reporting: prelude capture, errors.report, runtime_errors store with 1,000-per-part cap
description:
## Goal and why

"Errors close the loop": viewers' browsers report uncaught errors and blocked loads, which `part_get` returns as `runtime_errors` (T49), so an agent learns its page is broken without a browser.

## Scope

- Prelude captures `window.onerror` / `error` events (incl. resource load errors), `unhandledrejection`, CSP `securitypolicyviolation` (`kind: "csp"`), and failed loads of URLs the page tried to reach (`kind: "blocked_load"`); batches and sends via `/_rt` `errors.report` (≤ 1 request per 5 s, ≤ 20 errors per batch, messages truncated to 2 KiB, stacks to 8 KiB, URLs stripped of the `/c/<cap>/` segment). Not sent from guest tabs (round 2c interpretation: runtime errors from guest tabs aren't collected; guests get 403 on `errors.report`). Can-view public-link viewers do report (recommended default; the plan only excludes guests).
- Server: `errors.report` upserts by `fingerprint = hash(kind, message, top frame)`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE runtime_errors (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, version_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer' CHECK (source IN ('viewer','render')),
  fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('error','unhandledrejection','blocked_load','csp')),
  message TEXT NOT NULL, stack TEXT, url TEXT, count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (part_id, version_id, source, fingerprint)
) STRICT;
CREATE TRIGGER runtime_errors_keep1000 AFTER INSERT ON runtime_errors BEGIN
  DELETE FROM runtime_errors WHERE part_id = NEW.part_id AND id NOT IN
    (SELECT id FROM runtime_errors WHERE part_id = NEW.part_id ORDER BY last_at DESC LIMIT 1000);
END;
```
  (table/trigger created by T06). Inserts rate-limited per part **≤ 10/min** (excess counted into `count` of existing rows or dropped); the janitor drops rows > 30 days (T113).
- Read API for T49: latest 20 per part `[{kind, message, stack, url, count, source, version, last_at}]`.
- `source: render` rows come from T80 via the same store function.

## Not in scope

`part_get` exposure (T49); Details tick in the wrapper (T120/T31); janitor job (T113).

## Design notes and decisions

- Error text is page-generated and could contain part content; it is stored for the agent but must never reach logs/metrics (T112 canaries): log only fingerprint and kind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Throw, rejection, CSP block and blocked load each recorded with the right `kind`; repeats increment `count`.
- [ ] 1,001st distinct error evicts the oldest; > 10 inserts/min/part limited.
- [ ] URLs stored without the cap.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::rt::errors::tests::{fingerprint_stable, rate_limit, cap_stripped}`; `pf_db` trigger test `runtime_errors_keep1000`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/runtime_errors.spec.ts`: page throws; poll DB/test API for the row; captured logs assert `event="rt.error_reported" kind="error"` and no message text in logs.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The prelude" (reports uncaught errors…); §3c "Errors close the loop"; §5e `runtime_errors` + modelling decision (trigger + janitor, ≤ 10/min); §5h Browser runtime errors row.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T62.a: /_rt/v1 endpoint: text/plain JSON dispatch, Origin rules, role checks, personal storage, refresh

title: T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps
description:
## Goal and why

React/TSX is how Claude writes most artifacts (`App.tsx` with a default export). This task makes those run unchanged: compile with oxc, bundle with rolldown against one shared library set, and freeze the import map into the build record so a later release never changes which library an old part loads. It closes M0 ("the TSX corpus compiles").

**Placement (decision 39, provisional pending the admin):** `tsx` is **right after Slice 1**. It depends on `S1`; the compiler spike T02 stays in P0 and in the slice, so a rolldown or oxc problem still shows up first. In Slice 1 agents send `html` (React through the mirrored UMD build via a cdnjs/jsDelivr `<script>` works).
*Why the sandbox and TSX in P0 at all:* the serving model and the compiler are the two things most likely to force a redesign.

## Scope

Kinds row (verbatim): `tsx` | `App.tsx`/`.jsx` (default export) | oxc transform, rolldown bundle against the shared library set, a generated HTML shell (`#root`, Tailwind per §6 P3) | generated shell, with the prelude inserted at serve time.
- `part_create {content, kind: "tsx"}` names the file `App.tsx`. Detection: entry `App.tsx`/`App.jsx`.
- In the build child (T13 protocol): `oxc` (umbrella crate, `transformer` feature; transform + minify) + `rolldown` (bundle). **Exact versions pinned and vendored** (oxc is 0.x with breaking releases; rolldown's semver promise covers its JS API, not the Rust crate). esbuild-as-subprocess is the fallback behind the same child protocol (per the T02 go/no-go note).
- **One library set** (`libset.toml`, its version is `library_set_version`, part of the build cache key): `react` and `react-dom` 18.3, `lucide-react`, `recharts`, `d3`, `lodash`, `papaparse`, `mathjs`, `three`, `chart.js`, `tone`, `plotly.js` and `xlsx` (shartifacts' compatibility matrix, credited); shadcn and Tailwind join in T61. Pre-seeded as **shared blobs** (`shared_blobs.source = 'seed'`) served from `blobs-part` (T17), ESM builds.
- **CDN-URL aliasing**: if a mirrored URL (T14) is a package in the bundled set with the same major version, the build maps it to the bundled shared blob, so CDN `react@18` and bare `react` resolve to one module. A different major is mirrored as is, with a `duplicate_library` warning.
- **Import maps** for HTML parts with `<script type="module">` and for TSX bundles are **frozen into the build record** (`import_map` in the build manifest); T16.c merges it with the cap-prefix entries at serve time. `part_edit {rebuild: true}` opts a part into the current set.
- Generated HTML shell with `#root`, mounting the default export; prelude inserted at serve time like any entry.
- **Golden compile corpus** (`tests/golden/tsx/`: shartifacts' compat-matrix artifacts + Claude-written samples) runs on every upgrade; a toolchain upgrade rebuilds live parts in the background, diffs output against the golden corpus, and never switches what's live on its own.
- Build errors as `{file, line, col, message}`. Performance target: `part_edit` TSX incl. compile + bundle + brotli p50 < 150 ms / p99 < 1 s.

## Not in scope

Tailwind/shadcn (T61); Jig `@partifactory/jig` import (T54); Mermaid/KaTeX (T66).

## Design notes and decisions

- Bundling in the child keeps the server alive through compiler hangs/panics (decision 20).
- Frozen import maps are the reproducibility guarantee: old builds keep their libraries.
- A part that needs real npm packages is built locally (`vite build`, `base: './'`) and uploaded as `files`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Golden corpus (compat matrix + Claude samples) compiles; a page importing React from a CDN URL and bare `react` loads one React; a library upgrade leaves old builds' import maps unchanged".
- [ ] Every corpus entry compiles and renders with zero uncaught errors (sandbox e2e).
- [ ] CDN React + bare `react` → one module instance (`React === window.__r2` check in fixture).
- [ ] Bumping `libset.toml` changes new builds only; existing builds' `import_map` byte-identical.
- [ ] Different-major CDN import → `duplicate_library` warning.
- [ ] Toolchain versions pinned exactly in `Cargo.toml` with vendored sources.

## Tests

- `pf_build::kinds::tsx::tests::{default_export_shell, jsx_runtime, syntax_error_location}`.
- `pf_build::libset::tests::{alias_same_major, duplicate_library_warning, version_in_cache_key}`.
- Golden `tests/golden/tsx/` runner (`cargo nextest run -p pf-build golden_tsx`).
- E2E `tests/e2e/tsx_corpus.spec.ts`: renders each corpus part, asserts no errors; logs `event="build.finished" kind="tsx" latency_us` recorded for perf tracking.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Kinds; §2 Mirror-on-build (One library set, Import maps); §3d The build worker; §5 Stack (TSX/JSX → JS); §5a targets; §6 P0; §8 decision 39; Slice 1 "Decided for the slice" (tsx right after).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Golden corpus (compat matrix + Claude samples) compiles; a page importing React from a CDN URL and bare `react` loads one React; a library upgrade leaves old builds' import maps unchanged
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T02: Spikes: rolldown/oxc as libraries, rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos SSR vs askama+islands
  - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
  - T14: Mirror-on-build: fetch allowlisted CDN refs in the parent, pin by hash, rewrite build output only
  - T17: Shared blob host (blobs-part): serve only shared_blobs hashes, public immutable, ACAO *
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
- Unblocks: 
  - M0: Milestone - P0 Core (local) done
  - T61: Tailwind + shadcn support for Claude-written parts, mechanism chosen on evidence
  - G06: Toolchain upgrade: background rebuild of live parts with golden diff, never auto-switching live

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Ownership: the background rebuild of live parts after a toolchain upgrade (golden diff, never auto-switching live) is **G06's**, not this task's; T60 ships only the golden corpus runner that G06 reuses. `part_edit {rebuild: true}` (T46) means "rebuild against the current library set/import map" here; G06 owns "against a new toolchain".
- Contract: `tsx` is currently "after Slice 1" in `docs/agent-contract.md`. Acceptance adds: `part_create.kind` enum, the kinds table row (`App.tsx`/`.jsx` entry, default export, generated shell), the `duplicate_library` and `cdn_unpinned` warnings, and T56's test green.
- The esbuild-as-subprocess fallback: the `FROM scratch` image has no esbuild binary; the fallback is dev/CI only unless the release image deliberately ships esbuild (say which in the note).
- Split into T60.a / T60.b / T60.c (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: Golden corpus (compat matrix + Claude samples) compiles; a page importing React from a CDN URL and bare `react` loads one React; a library upgrade leaves old builds' import maps unchanged
