title: T05: SQLite layer: read pool, single writer task, pragmas, embedded forward-only migrations
description:
## Goal and why

The storage foundation for `partifactory.db` (and, with its own instance, `insights.db`): WAL-mode SQLite with a read pool and **exactly one writer task that serialises every commit**. That single writer is what makes every part's version sequence strict (`n, n+1, …`, no lost updates), what makes rebase safe (it runs inside the writer's critical section, T46), and what makes "durable when acknowledged" true (`synchronous=FULL` on the writer). T05 is on the Slice 1 critical path (T01 -> T05 -> T06 -> …).

## Scope

- Crate `pf-db` over `rusqlite` (bundled, with FTS5 enabled). "No storage-backend abstraction until there's a second backend."
- **Pragmas**: `journal_mode=WAL`; `foreign_keys=ON`; `synchronous=FULL` on the single writer connection; readers `query_only=ON`; `busy_timeout`; `mmap_size` (configurable); `wal_autocheckpoint` (the janitor, T113, also runs a scheduled checkpoint and monthly `VACUUM` when free pages > 20 %); cached prepared statements on every connection.
- **Read pool**: N read-only connections (default `max(2, cores)`), async access via `spawn_blocking` or a dedicated thread pool.
- **Single writer task**: an owned connection on a dedicated thread; callers submit closures `FnOnce(&Transaction) -> Result<T>` over an mpsc channel and await a oneshot result; each closure runs in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT`; the result is returned only after the commit is fsynced. Backpressure via a bounded channel; metrics hooks (queue depth, commit latency) for T18.
- **Migrations**: embedded (`include_str!` of `crates/pf-db/migrations/NNNN_name.sql`), **forward-only**, run at start **inside a transaction**, tracked in a `schema_migrations(version, name, applied_at, sha256)` table; a changed already-applied migration (sha mismatch) is a hard error. Migrations must be forward-compatible with the previous binary, because `partifactory deploy` runs them before the health-gated switch (§5b) and may roll back the binary.
- A second, independent `Db` instance type for `insights.db` (its own writer) so T105 can reuse the layer.
- An in-memory/tempfile test helper `pf_db::testing::temp_db()` used by every later task's tests.

## Not in scope

- The schema itself (T06). The insights schema and its writer wiring (T105).
- Backups/`VACUUM INTO` copies (T34); janitor scheduling (T113).

## Design notes and decisions

- Why one writer: SQLite has one writer anyway; owning it in a task turns contention into a queue and gives linearisable writes (§3d "Linearisable writes"). Scale is "a few people and agents, about 10k parts" - a single writer handles thousands of small writes/s.
- Why `synchronous=FULL`: "Acknowledged means it survives a power cut." No save ever waits on a backup target.
- Readers must never block the writer: WAL + `VACUUM INTO` for backups reads a snapshot without blocking.
- `frankensqlite` and io_uring were considered and parked (round 1, O2).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Migrations apply from empty and from N-1 in a test; 1,000 concurrent commits through the writer produce a gap-free sequence".

- [ ] Migrations apply cleanly to an empty file and to a DB at N-1.
- [ ] A modified already-applied migration fails start with a clear error.
- [ ] 1,000 concurrent tasks each committing "next n" through the writer produce exactly 1..1000 with no gaps or duplicates.
- [ ] Pragmas verified at runtime (`PRAGMA journal_mode`, `foreign_keys`, `synchronous` on the writer).
- [ ] A failed closure rolls back and the writer keeps serving.

## Tests

- `pf_db::tests::migrate_from_empty`, `migrate_from_n_minus_1` (fixture DB at N-1 checked into `tests/golden/db/`), `altered_migration_rejected`.
- `pf_db::tests::writer_gap_free_1000` (spawn 1,000 tokio tasks, each inserting `max(n)+1` in its closure; assert the set is exactly 1..=1000).
- `pf_db::tests::pragmas_applied`, `writer_survives_closure_error`, `reader_not_blocked_during_long_write`.
- Logs: assert a `event="db.migrate" version=… outcome="ok"` line per migration via the capture subscriber (T18) once available.

## References

PLAN.md §5 Stack (Storage row), §3d Durable when acknowledged, Concurrency contract (Linearisable writes), §5a SQLite for reads, §5b (migrations before the switch), §5d Migrations, §5d Scale, §5h SQLite WAL row.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Migrations apply from empty and from N-1 in a test; 1,000 concurrent commits through the writer produce a gap-free sequence
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T01: Cargo workspace, crate layout, CI (fmt, clippy, nextest, deny, audit), Renovate
- Unblocks: 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups
acceptance_criteria: Migrations apply from empty and from N-1 in a test; 1,000 concurrent commits through the writer produce a gap-free sequence

title: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
description:
## Goal and why

Write partifactory's schema v1 as the first embedded migration, exactly as the data model specifies, and a `schema_test` that asserts every table, index and `CHECK` exists and that foreign keys are enforced. Everything downstream (versions, builds, grants, caps' epochs, tokens, data docs, snapshots, events) writes into these tables, so getting the shapes right once, with constraints in the database rather than only in code, is what lets later tasks trust their invariants (e.g. a part name can't violate the hostname rule even through a bug; a shared data doc can't carry an owner; a personal space must have an owner). T06 is on the Slice 1 critical path (T05 -> T06 -> T08 …). "The backend tables are created in P0 and used from P2a."

## Scope

Principles the schema encodes (from the data model):
- SQLite holds metadata. Bytes live in the blob store: manifests, files, build outputs, data snapshots, assets, screenshots.
- Secrets are stored only as sha256. Capabilities aren't stored: they're stateless HMAC tokens in the path; the DB holds only what revokes them (`epochs`).
- Cookies exist only on the workspace host (`sessions`). Part hosts never set or read a cookie.
- Shared vs part blob class is a property of the reference (`shared_blobs`, `build_files`), not of the blob.
- `versions.id` is the hash of a manifest that includes `part_id`, `parent` and `n`, so two parts never share a version id.
- Agents are `agent_connections`, one per (agent, person) or per service; every token hangs off one.
- No preview tokens; the only bearer links are `public_links` (admin-only). No request or approval queues; the only pending state a person sees is `access_asks`.
- Analytics/observability live in a second file, `/data/insights.db`, so their write load never contends with the main writer.
- Part secrets are write-only: stored encrypted, and no query path returns a value to any op.
- Conventions: SQLite >= 3.45, WAL, `foreign_keys=ON`, **STRICT tables**; ids are prefixed ULIDs as TEXT (`u_`, `p_`, `sp_`, `c_`, …); times are unix ms INTEGER; secrets (session ids, tokens, codes) only as sha256 BLOB(32); JSON columns are TEXT checked with `json_valid`.

Deliverables:
- `crates/pf-db/migrations/0001_schema_v1.sql`: the main DDL, verbatim from the plan (split across the subtasks below, concatenated in this order).
- `crates/pf-db/migrations/insights/0001_insights_v1.sql`: the `insights.db` DDL (T06.e), applied by T105's own writer.
- `crates/pf-db/tests/schema_test.rs`: introspects `sqlite_schema`, `pragma_table_info`, `pragma_index_list`/`index_info` and the stored SQL to assert every table, column, index (incl. partial `WHERE` clauses), trigger and `CHECK` in the DDL exists; inserts violating each `CHECK` and each FK fail.
- **No FTS triggers** in T06 (round-final F18): `parts_fts` is populated by T76 at the application level.

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and `schema_test` passes on the concatenated migration):
- **T06.a** - identity tables + spaces, parts, names, tags, notes; also the `schema_test` harness.
- **T06.b** - versions, builds, blobs (incl. `shared_blobs`, `mirror_cache`, `drafts`) + access (`grants`, `public_links`, `epochs`, `access_asks`, `invites`, `invite_enrolments`, `audit`).
- **T06.c** - agents (OAuth AS + personal tokens: `oauth_clients`, `agent_connections`, `oauth_tokens`, `oauth_codes`, `device_codes`, `idempotency`, `leases`) + collaboration and runtime state (`comments`, `data_docs`, `data_leases`, `data_snapshot_policies`, `data_snapshots`, `assets`, `runtime_errors` + trigger).
- **T06.d** - backends (`backend_images`, `container_sets`, `containers`, `part_volumes`, `part_secrets`, `lan_allow`) + events, webhooks, jobs (`events`, `webhook_deliveries`, `render_jobs`, `kv`) + search (`parts_fts`).
- **T06.e** - the `insights.db` DDL (`events_raw`, `rollups_daily`, `traces`, `spans`, `log_segments`, `janitor_runs`) as a separate migration set.

Note on ordering: some tables reference tables defined later (e.g. `parts.forked_from REFERENCES versions(id)`, `version_files.blob_hash REFERENCES blobs(hash)`). SQLite allows forward references in `REFERENCES` because FKs are checked at DML time, so the plan's order works as-is; keep it.

## Not in scope

- Populating anything (T08-T11 and later). FTS population (T76). Insights writer (T105).
- Later schema changes: every later task that needs a column adds a new forward-only migration (`0002_…`), never edits 0001 once released.

## Design notes and decisions (modelling decisions, verbatim)

| Behaviour | How the schema holds it |
| --- | --- |
| Space grants are inherited live | `grants.target_kind = 'space'`; effective role = max over the part's and its space's grants |
| Quotas "per agent" | keyed on `agent_connections.id` (`versions_actor_day`), because tokens rotate hourly. Storage per connection is approximated by the blobs its versions introduced |
| Block ids | `.pf/blocks.json` inside the manifest. `comments.anchor` and `leases.scope_ref` hold ids as text, with no FK. Re-anchoring is application logic |
| Invite "opened" | set by the `/i/<id>` wrapper (`invites.opened_at`), because the IdP has no open event |
| Invite "up to N people" | `invites.max_uses`/`uses`, counted here for every invite kind |
| People from an IdP and local accounts | `users.auth_source`; IdP people keyed by `(idp_issuer, idp_sub)`; local accounts sign in with `passkeys.purpose = 'login'` |
| Groups from a claim, an IdP API, or partifactory | `groups.source`; local `pf-*` groups need no IdP at all |
| Data snapshots on by default | no `data_snapshot_policies` row = `daily`, keep 7; a row records only an explicit change |
| `provision` before-states | in `provision-log/*.jsonl` in the site repo, not in this schema |
| `runtime_errors`: 1,000 per part, 30 days; `part_get` shows the latest 20 | a trigger for the count (inserts rate-limited per part, <= 10/min), the janitor for the age |
| Public-link and guest uniques | in `insights.db`: a hash with an in-memory salt that rotates daily and is lost on restart |
| Guests | no table: a guest is a `public_links` row in `contribute` mode plus the signed `g` claim; writes labelled `guest:<link>:<g>` |
| No approval queues | there is no `share_requests` table |
| Build method per version | `builds.method`, one build per target (`frontend`, `backend`) per version |
| Write-only secrets | `part_secrets.value_enc` is read only by the runner's deploy path; no op's output type has a field for it |
| Backend data vs part data | `data_docs` (snapshotted) vs `part_volumes` (folder backups and exports only) |
| Agent-made grants | `grants.created_by_conn` labels them and drives "Undo all" on a revoked connection |
| Every version kept | GC marks from `version_files`, `build_files`, `builds.log_hash`, `drafts`, `data_snapshots`, `assets` and unpruned `backend_images.tar_hash` |

Hot-path rules that stay outside the DB: `epochs`, the `part -> live (version, build)` map and live build manifests are cached in memory and invalidated from the events stream; grant/public-link expiry is enforced by a timer that bumps the part epoch; the boot epoch is bumped on every start and every import. The plan states both DDL blocks load cleanly in SQLite 3.54 (`sqlite3 :memory:`); the bundled rusqlite SQLite must be >= 3.45.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "`schema_test` asserts every table, index and CHECK in §5e exists; FK violations fail".

- [ ] `0001_schema_v1.sql` is byte-equivalent (modulo whitespace) to the plan's main DDL; `insights/0001_insights_v1.sql` to the insights DDL.
- [ ] Both load in `sqlite3 :memory:` and via `pf-db` migrations from empty.
- [ ] `schema_test` lists every table, index, trigger and CHECK and fails if any is missing or altered.
- [ ] For every FK, an insert referencing a missing row fails; for every CHECK, a violating insert fails.
- [ ] `runtime_errors_keep1000` trigger keeps at most 1,000 rows per part.
- [ ] No triggers on `parts_fts`.

## Tests

- `pf_db::schema_test::all_tables_present`, `all_indexes_present` (including partial-index predicates), `all_checks_enforced` (table-driven: one violating row per CHECK), `all_fks_enforced`, `strict_tables`, `runtime_errors_trigger_caps_1000`, `no_fts_triggers`, `insights_schema_loads`.
- `pf_db::schema_test::ddl_matches_plan_snapshot`: compares normalized `sqlite_schema.sql` to a checked-in snapshot `tests/golden/db/schema_v1.sql` so accidental edits fail CI.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model (Principles, both DDL blocks, Hot-path rules, Modelling decisions); §2 Capabilities; §3a; §5c data snapshots; §5g; §5h; §10 final round (F18, schema notes).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): `schema_test` asserts every table, index and CHECK in §5e exists; FK violations fail
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T05: SQLite layer: read pool, single writer task, pragmas, embedded forward-only migrations
- Unblocks: 
  - T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
  - T09: Name rules, permanent reservation, title->name derivation, deterministic ranked alternatives
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
  - T15: Capability tokens: path caps, HMAC with daily HKDF kid keys, deterministic windows, epochs + boot floor
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test)
  - T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
  - T77: Per-part data snapshots of shared docs: on by default (daily keep 7), roll back, reset, JSON download
  - T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T06.a: Schema v1 part 1: identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes + schema_test harness
  - T06.b: Schema v1 part 2: versions, builds, blobs, mirror cache, drafts + grants, links, epochs, invites, audit
  - T06.c: Schema v1 part 3: OAuth clients, connections, tokens, codes, idempotency, leases + comments, data, snapshots, assets, runtime errors
  - T06.d: Schema v1 part 4: backend tables, events, webhooks, render jobs, kv + parts_fts (no triggers)
  - T06.e: Insights schema v1: events_raw, rollups_daily, traces, spans, log_segments, janitor_runs (insights.db)

title: T06.a: Schema v1 part 1: identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes + schema_test harness
description:
## Goal and why

The first slice of schema v1 and the test harness the other schema subtasks extend. Identity tables hold people from any OIDC IdP *and* local passkey accounts (portability: grants refer to provider-neutral subjects, so changing IdP changes config, not policy data). `parts` encodes the hostname rule in a `CHECK`, so no code path can create a part whose name isn't a valid `<name>-part` label.

## Scope

Write this DDL verbatim into `crates/pf-db/migrations/0001_schema_v1.sql` (it opens the file; T06.b-d append in order):

```sql
-- partifactory schema v1 (SQLite >= 3.45, WAL, foreign_keys=ON, STRICT tables). Everything lives under /data.
-- Conventions: ids are prefixed ULIDs as TEXT ('u_', 'p_', 'sp_', 'c_', ...); times are unix ms INTEGER;
-- secrets (session ids, tokens, codes) are stored only as sha256 BLOB(32); JSON columns are TEXT checked with json_valid.
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ identity
CREATE TABLE users (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- u_...
  auth_source   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (auth_source IN ('oidc','local')),
  idp_issuer    TEXT,                                -- OIDC issuer URL; NULL for local accounts
  idp_sub       TEXT,                                -- immutable IdP subject; NULL for local accounts
  username      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  display_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  email         TEXT,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','disabled','removed')),
  in_audience   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,          -- member of site audience_group (everyone-signed-in)
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at  INTEGER,
  synced_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK ((auth_source = 'oidc') = (idp_issuer IS NOT NULL AND idp_sub IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_idp ON users(idp_issuer, idp_sub) WHERE idp_sub IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX users_email ON users(email);

CREATE TABLE groups (
  name       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                       -- IdP group name, or a local pf-* group
  source     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('claim','idp_api','local')),  -- groups claim, provisioner API, or partifactory's own
  idp_id     TEXT UNIQUE,                            -- set only for source = 'idp_api'
  managed    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (managed IN (0,1)),  -- 1 = pf-* group partifactory may edit
  synced_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (managed = 0 OR name LIKE 'pf-%'),
  CHECK (source <> 'local' OR managed = 1)
) STRICT;

CREATE TABLE group_members (
  group_name TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES groups(name) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  PRIMARY KEY (group_name, user_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX group_members_user ON group_members(user_id);

CREATE TABLE sessions (                              -- workspace host only: part hosts never set cookies
  id_hash      BLOB PRIMARY KEY,                     -- sha256(__Host-pf_session value)
  user_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,                     -- 30 d sliding
  stepup_at    INTEGER,                              -- last admin WebAuthn assertion (valid 10 min)
  idp_refresh_enc BLOB,                              -- OIDC refresh token, encrypted with PF_SESSION_KEY; re-read groups every 15 min
  idp_checked_at  INTEGER,                           -- last successful claims re-read (NULL for local accounts)
  ua_summary   TEXT,
  revoked_at   INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX sessions_user ON sessions(user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE passkeys (                              -- webauthn-rs passkeys partifactory registered itself
  cred_id     BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  purpose     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('login','stepup')),  -- login: local accounts; stepup: step-up and device approval, for any person who registered one (rp.id = the apex)
  passkey     BLOB NOT NULL,                         -- serialized webauthn-rs Passkey
  label       TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER,
  revoked_at  INTEGER                                -- set by a recovery link or by the admin
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX passkeys_user ON passkeys(user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE break_glass (
  code_hash  BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- +5 min
  used_at    INTEGER
) STRICT;
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ spaces, parts, names
CREATE TABLE spaces (
  id                 TEXT PRIMARY KEY,               -- sp_...
  slug               TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- '~<owner>', 'family', 'system'
  kind               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('personal','shared','system')),
  title              TEXT NOT NULL,
  owner_user_id      TEXT REFERENCES users(id),      -- personal: the person; shared: NULL (the admin administers)
  quota_parts        INTEGER,                        -- quota_*: NULL = the §5d default
  quota_bytes        INTEGER,
  quota_versions_day INTEGER,
  created_at         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (kind <> 'personal' OR owner_user_id IS NOT NULL)
) STRICT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX spaces_one_personal ON spaces(owner_user_id) WHERE kind = 'personal';

CREATE TABLE parts (
  id               TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                 -- p_...
  name             TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,             -- current hostname label (without -part)
  space_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id),
  title            TEXT NOT NULL,
  description      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  kind             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('html','markdown','text','svg','code','tsx','slides','files')),
  head_version_id  TEXT,                             -- newest committed source version (NULL = v0 placeholder)
  live_version_id  TEXT,                             -- newest version with an ok build
  live_build_id    INTEGER,                          -- the live pair is (live_version_id, live_build_id)
  head_n           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  owner_user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), -- the person it was made for; shares inward
  steward_conn     TEXT,                             -- agent that receives to_agent comments (P3)
  shared_data_writers TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewers' CHECK (shared_data_writers IN ('editors','viewers')),  -- who below edit may write shared data (§3a)
  link_comments    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,       -- opt-in: public-link viewers may comment
  isolation        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sandbox' CHECK (isolation IN ('sandbox','unsandboxed')),  -- admin-only flag
  shared_data_cap  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5242880,  -- bytes of shared data_docs; guests get quota_exceeded past it
  backend_lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' CHECK (backend_lifecycle IN ('none','scale_to_zero','always_on')),
  api_prefix       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '/api/' CHECK (api_prefix GLOB '/*/'),  -- backend route under /c/<cap>/
  forked_from      TEXT REFERENCES versions(id),     -- part_create {from}
  expires_at       INTEGER,                          -- part_create {expires_in}: moves to the bin when due
  created_by_user  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  created_by_conn  TEXT,                             -- agent_connections.id or NULL
  created_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  deleted_at       INTEGER,                          -- the 30-day bin; purge after 30 d
  CHECK (name GLOB '[a-z0-9]*' AND name NOT GLOB '*[^a-z0-9-]*' AND length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 58
         AND name NOT LIKE '-%' AND name NOT LIKE '%-' AND instr(name,'--') = 0)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX parts_space_updated ON parts(space_id, updated_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX parts_deleted ON parts(deleted_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX parts_expiring ON parts(expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE names (                                 -- every name ever used; never deleted
  name        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id),
  state       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('active','redirect','tombstone')),
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  retired_at  INTEGER
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX names_one_active ON names(part_id) WHERE state = 'active';

CREATE TABLE part_tags (
  part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  tag     TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, tag)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX part_tags_tag ON part_tags(tag);

CREATE TABLE part_notes (                            -- agent notes: versioned separately from content
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  n          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  body       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) <= 16384),
  author_user TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  actor_conn TEXT,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, n)
) STRICT;
```

Also build the harness `crates/pf-db/tests/schema_test.rs`: helpers `assert_table(name, columns)`, `assert_index(name, table, cols, where)`, `assert_check_rejects(table, row)`, `assert_fk_rejects(table, row)`, and the golden snapshot comparison against `tests/golden/db/schema_v1.sql`. T06.b-e add their assertions using these helpers.

## Not in scope

The remaining tables (T06.b-e). Populating users/spaces (T10, T24).

## Design notes and decisions

- `users`: `CHECK ((auth_source = 'oidc') = (idp_issuer IS NOT NULL AND idp_sub IS NOT NULL))`; the unique partial index `users_idp` keys IdP people by `(issuer, sub)` so a second IdP never collides. `in_audience` backs `everyone-signed-in` (members of the `audience_group`, plus every active local account).
- `groups`: `managed = 1` only for `pf-*` names; local groups are always managed. Any IdP group can be *granted*; only `pf-*` groups can be created/edited by partifactory.
- `sessions` is the only cookie-backed state (`__Host-pf_session`, stored hashed), with `stepup_at` (10-minute admin window) and the encrypted IdP refresh token for the 15-minute claims re-read.
- `passkeys.purpose`: `login` (local accounts) vs `stepup` (step-up and device approval; `rp.id` = the apex).
- `spaces`: personal spaces must have an owner (`spaces_one_personal` makes it one per person); `quota_*` NULL means the default (personal space 2,000 parts, 20 GiB, 1,000 versions a day).
- `parts.shared_data_writers` default `'viewers'`, `shared_data_cap` 5242880 (5 MiB), `isolation` default `'sandbox'`, `api_prefix` default `'/api/'`.
- `names` keeps every name ever used (never deleted); `blobs` is additionally reserved in code (T09).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DDL above present and loading; harness helpers exist and are used for every table/index/CHECK in this subtask.
- [ ] CHECK rejections tested: `users` oidc without sub; `groups` managed non-`pf-` name; `groups` local unmanaged; `spaces` personal without owner; `parts` names `-a`, `a-`, `a--b`, `A`, 59 chars, `a_b`; `names` bad state; `part_notes` body > 16384.

## Tests

`schema_test::identity_tables`, `schema_test::spaces_parts_names`, `schema_test::parts_name_check_table` (table-driven over valid/invalid names, mirroring T09's rule table), `schema_test::one_personal_space_per_user`, `schema_test::golden_snapshot`.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model: identity; spaces, parts, names; Conventions header.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T06.b: Schema v1 part 2: versions, builds, blobs, mirror cache, drafts + grants, links, epochs, invites, audit
description:
## Goal and why

The content-addressed version model and the access model. Versions are immutable source manifests; builds are keyed by `hash(manifest, toolchain)` so a toolchain upgrade never serves stale output; the live pair is `(live_version_id, live_build_id)`. Access is grants on parts and spaces (inherited live), admin-only public links stored as hashed tokens, and the `epochs` table that makes stateless caps revocable.

## Scope

Append this DDL verbatim to `0001_schema_v1.sql`:

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ versions, builds, blobs
CREATE TABLE versions (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- sha256 hex of canonical manifest
  part_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id),
  n             INTEGER NOT NULL,
  parent_id     TEXT REFERENCES versions(id),
  manifest_hash TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- = id; manifest bytes live in blobs
  entry         TEXT NOT NULL,
  author_user   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  actor_conn    TEXT,                                -- NULL = the person directly
  via           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (via IN ('api','mcp','cli','editor','self_publish','restore')),
  message       TEXT,
  rebased_from  TEXT,
  restored_from TEXT,
  live_gate     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'always' CHECK (live_gate IN ('always','after_check')),  -- part_create/part_edit {live}
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (part_id, n)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX versions_actor_day ON versions(actor_conn, created_at);  -- quotas: versions/day per token

CREATE TABLE version_files (                         -- denormalized manifest for diff, GC, FTS, serving
  version_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  path       TEXT NOT NULL,
  blob_hash  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  size       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  mime       TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (version_id, path)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX version_files_blob ON version_files(blob_hash);

CREATE TABLE builds (
  id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  version_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  cache_key        TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- sha256(src manifest || toolchain || libset || mirror resolution)
  toolchain        TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- pinned oxc/rolldown/builder version id
  target           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'frontend' CHECK (target IN ('frontend','backend')),
  method           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('server_build','prebuilt_files','prebuilt_image','uploaded_image')),  -- for Insights
  status           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','ok','failed','timeout','superseded')),
  output_hash      TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),      -- build manifest blob (frontend) or image manifest (backend)
  log_hash         TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),      -- build log; last 20 builds per part kept (janitor)
  warnings         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(warnings)),
  errors           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(errors)),
  gate_check       TEXT CHECK (gate_check IN ('pending','passed','failed','skipped')),  -- live_gate = after_check only
  queued_at        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  started_at       INTEGER,
  finished_at      INTEGER,
  UNIQUE (version_id, cache_key)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX builds_queue ON builds(status, queued_at) WHERE status IN ('queued','running');
CREATE INDEX builds_cache ON builds(cache_key) WHERE status = 'ok';

CREATE TABLE build_files (                           -- what the part host may serve for a build
  build_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES builds(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  path      TEXT NOT NULL,
  blob_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  br_hash   TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  content_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (build_id, path)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX build_files_blob ON build_files(blob_hash);

CREATE TABLE blobs (
  hash        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- sha256 hex of plaintext
  size        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  gc_mark     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  unref_since INTEGER                                -- set by sweep; delete after 7 d grace
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX blobs_unref ON blobs(unref_since) WHERE unref_since IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE shared_blobs (                          -- class is per reference: only these are served by blobs-part
  hash       TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  source     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('seed','mirror','runtime')),
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- 'react@18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js'
  added_at   INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE mirror_cache (
  url          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  resolved_url TEXT NOT NULL,
  hash         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  content_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  integrity    TEXT,
  pinned       INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (pinned IN (0,1)),  -- exact version: cache forever
  fetched_at   INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE drafts (                                -- workspace editor drafts, per person per part
  user_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  base_version_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id),
  files      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(files)),  -- {path: text}; previewed via a cap with a d claim
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, part_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ access
CREATE TABLE grants (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  target_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (target_kind IN ('part','space')),
  target_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (subject GLOB 'user:*' OR subject GLOB 'group:*' OR subject = 'everyone-signed-in'),
  role        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (role BETWEEN 0 AND 3),  -- view, comment, edit, manage
  expires_at  INTEGER,
  created_by  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),   -- the person
  created_by_conn TEXT,                              -- set when an agent made it (share:household): labelled, undoable
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (target_kind, target_id, subject)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX grants_subject ON grants(subject);
CREATE INDEX grants_expiry ON grants(expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL;

-- Public links: Admin-only, made once the part has a live version, no expiry by default. There are no agent-minted preview links.
CREATE TABLE public_links (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- l_...; also the cap subject link:<id> and minter
  token_hash    BLOB NOT NULL UNIQUE,                -- sha256 of the 128-bit /l/<token>
  part_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (role IN (0,1)),  -- view; comment only with parts.link_comments
  mode          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'view' CHECK (mode IN ('view','contribute')),  -- contribute: guests write shared data
  frozen_at     INTEGER,                             -- last Freeze (contribute -> view); bumps minter:link:<id>
  screenshot_og INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,          -- opt-in: screenshot as the link preview
  created_by    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),  -- always the admin
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at    INTEGER,                             -- NULL = never (the default)
  revoked_at    INTEGER,
  open_count    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,          -- counted on POST /l/<token>/go
  last_opened_at INTEGER,
  request_cap   INTEGER                              -- optional per-link request limit
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX public_links_part ON public_links(part_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;


-- Capabilities are stateless (in the path, never in a cookie). Only their revocation state is stored.
CREATE TABLE epochs (
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                            -- 'part:<id>' | 'minter:sess:<id>' | 'minter:conn:<id>' | 'minter:link:<id>' | 'global' | 'boot'
  epoch INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE access_asks (                          -- 'Ask for access' from a signed-in person; person-to-person, no agent rows
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  note        TEXT CHECK (note IS NULL OR length(note) <= 280),
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  closed_at   INTEGER,                               -- Add (an ordinary grant) or Dismiss
  closed_as   TEXT CHECK (closed_as IN ('added','dismissed')),
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, user_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX access_asks_open ON access_asks(part_id) WHERE closed_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE invites (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                  -- i_...; handed out as /i/<id>, which records opens
  idp_ref         TEXT,                              -- provisioner only: IdP invitation (unlimited until expiry) or recovery id; NULL for native invites
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('single','multi','email','recovery')),
  max_uses        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,        -- counted here; the IdP has no use count
  uses            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  email           TEXT,
  target_user_id  TEXT REFERENCES users(id),         -- recovery
  land_part_id    TEXT REFERENCES parts(id),
  grant_role      INTEGER CHECK (grant_role BETWEEN 0 AND 3),
  groups          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(groups)),  -- pf-* groups, added by API after enrolment
  status          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sent','opened','enrolled','expired','revoked')),
  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  opened_at       INTEGER,
  expires_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  revoked_at      INTEGER,
  CHECK (uses <= max_uses)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX invites_open ON invites(expires_at) WHERE status IN ('sent','opened');

CREATE TABLE invite_enrolments (
  invite_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES invites(id),
  user_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  at        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (invite_id, user_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE audit (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  user_id     TEXT,                                  -- the person (author)
  actor       TEXT,                                  -- 'conn:<id>' | 'break-glass' | 'system' | NULL
  action      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'grant.set', 'link.revoke', 'invite.create', ...
  target_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  before      TEXT CHECK (before IS NULL OR json_valid(before)),
  after       TEXT CHECK (after IS NULL OR json_valid(after)),
  request_id  TEXT
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX audit_target ON audit(target_kind, target_id, at DESC);
```

## Not in scope

Writing versions/builds (T08, T13), the policy engine (T26), public links (T29), invites (T94).

## Design notes and decisions

- `versions.via` covers `api, mcp, cli, editor, self_publish, restore`; `live_gate` records `part_create`/`part_edit {live}`; `builds.gate_check` (`pending|passed|failed|skipped`) only for `after_check`.
- `builds.method` (`server_build|prebuilt_files|prebuilt_image|uploaded_image`) and `target` (`frontend|backend`) feed Insights; `log_hash` keeps build logs (last 20 builds per part, janitor).
- `shared_blobs` is the only list the blob host serves (`source` `seed|mirror|runtime`). `blobs.unref_since` drives the 7-day GC grace (T59).
- `grants.subject` is `user:*`, `group:*` or `everyone-signed-in`; links and connections are cap subjects, not grant subjects. `grants.created_by_conn` labels agent-made grants (undoable, "Undo all").
- `public_links`: `role` 0/1 (comment only with `parts.link_comments`), `mode` `view|contribute`, `frozen_at` (Freeze bumps `minter:link:<id>`), `screenshot_og`, `open_count`/`last_opened_at` counted on `POST /l/<token>/go`, `expires_at` NULL = never (the default).
- `epochs.key`: `'part:<id>' | 'minter:sess:<id>' | 'minter:conn:<id>' | 'minter:link:<id>' | 'global' | 'boot'`.
- `access_asks` has no agent rows (person-to-person). `invites.kind` `single|multi|email|recovery`, `CHECK (uses <= max_uses)`. `audit` keeps `request_id` (formerly the vendor-specific `cf_ray`, renamed for portability).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DDL present; `schema_test` assertions for every table/index/CHECK here, including partial indexes `builds_queue`, `builds_cache`, `blobs_unref`, `grants_expiry`, `public_links_part`, `access_asks_open`, `invites_open`.
- [ ] CHECK rejections: bad `via`, bad build `status`/`method`/`target`/`gate_check`, invalid JSON in `warnings`/`errors`/`files`/`groups`/`before`/`after`, grant subject `link:x`, role 4, public link role 2 or mode `edit`, invite `uses > max_uses`, access ask note > 280 chars.
- [ ] FK rejections: `version_files.blob_hash` to a missing blob; `builds.version_id` to a missing version.

## Tests

`schema_test::versions_builds_blobs`, `schema_test::access_tables`, `schema_test::json_checks_reject_invalid`, `schema_test::fk_version_files_blob`.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model: versions, builds, blobs; access; §2 (part version, build records, live pair; capabilities and epochs).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T06.a: Schema v1 part 1: identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes + schema_test harness
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] DDL present; `schema_test` assertions for every table/index/CHECK here, including partial indexes `builds_queue`, `builds_cache`, `blobs_unref`, `grants_expiry`, `public_links_part`, `access_asks_open`, `invites_open`.
- [ ] CHECK rejections: bad `via`, bad build `status`/`method`/`target`/`gate_check`, invalid JSON in `warnings`/`errors`/`files`/`groups`/`before`/`after`, grant subject `link:x`, role 4, public link role 2 or mode `edit`, invite `uses > max_uses`, access ask note > 280 chars.
- [ ] FK rejections: `version_files.blob_hash` to a missing blob; `builds.version_id` to a missing version.

title: T06.c: Schema v1 part 3: OAuth clients, connections, tokens, codes, idempotency, leases + comments, data, snapshots, assets, runtime errors
description:
## Goal and why

The agent identity model (every token hangs off one `agent_connections` row, so one revoke covers everything an agent holds) and the runtime state that survives versions: `window.storage`/`db` documents, data snapshots (on by default), comments with provenance, viewer assets and browser runtime errors.

## Scope

Append this DDL verbatim to `0001_schema_v1.sql`:

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ agents (OAuth AS + personal tokens)
CREATE TABLE oauth_clients (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- client_id (CIMD URL, DCR id, manual id, or 'part-cli')
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('cimd','dcr','manual','builtin')),
  client_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
  metadata      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(metadata)),
  redirect_uris TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' CHECK (json_valid(redirect_uris)),
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  consented_at  INTEGER,                             -- NULL + older than 1 h => purged
  secret_hash   BLOB,                                -- manual confidential clients only
  reg_ip_hash   BLOB
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX oauth_clients_unconsented ON oauth_clients(created_at) WHERE consented_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE agent_connections (                     -- one row per (agent, person); the 'act' and minter for agents
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- c_...
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('oauth_code','device','pat')),
  principal_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'person' CHECK (principal_kind IN ('person','service')),
  client_id   TEXT REFERENCES oauth_clients(id),     -- NULL for pat
  user_id     TEXT REFERENCES users(id),             -- the person it acts for; NULL for a service identity
  agent_name  TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- e.g. 'Claude Code', 'Hermes'; shown as '<agent> for <person>'
  software    TEXT,                                  -- self-reported, e.g. 'hermes/1.4' (unverified)
  scopes      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(scopes)),
  spaces      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(spaces)),
  expires_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,                      -- consented lifetime
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER,
  revoked_at  INTEGER,
  quota_versions_day INTEGER,                         -- NULL = the §5d default
  CHECK ((principal_kind = 'person') = (user_id IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX agent_connections_user ON agent_connections(user_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE oauth_tokens (
  hash        BLOB PRIMARY KEY,                      -- sha256 of opaque token
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('access','refresh','pat')),
  prefix      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'pf_at_' | 'pf_rt_' | 'pf_pat_' (secret scanning, logs)
  connection_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agent_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  family_id   TEXT,                                  -- refresh rotation family
  resource    TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- RFC 8707 audience: always the workspace origin, e.g. https://parts.<domain>/
  issued_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at     INTEGER,                               -- refresh: set on rotation; reuse => revoke family
  revoked_at  INTEGER
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX oauth_tokens_family ON oauth_tokens(family_id) WHERE family_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX oauth_tokens_conn ON oauth_tokens(connection_id);

CREATE TABLE oauth_codes (
  hash          BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  client_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oauth_clients(id),
  user_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  redirect_uri  TEXT NOT NULL,
  code_challenge TEXT NOT NULL,
  scopes        TEXT NOT NULL,
  spaces        TEXT NOT NULL,
  resource      TEXT NOT NULL,
  lifetime_ms   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,                    -- 60 s
  used_at       INTEGER
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE device_codes (
  device_hash   BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  user_code     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,                -- XXXX-XXXX
  client_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES oauth_clients(id),
  agent_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
  software      TEXT,
  req_scopes    TEXT NOT NULL,
  req_geo       TEXT,                                -- coarse country/network from proxy headers or GeoIP; NULL if unknown
  status        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','denied','expired','consumed')),
  connection_id TEXT REFERENCES agent_connections(id),
  interval_s    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
  last_poll_at  INTEGER,
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at    INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE idempotency (                           -- every write's request_id; a row is stored only when the write commits
  principal  TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- 'user:<id>' or 'conn:<id>'
  request_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  operation  TEXT NOT NULL,
  response   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(response)),
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- purge after 24 h
  PRIMARY KEY (principal, request_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE leases (                                -- part_edit {claim}; advisory
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'part' CHECK (scope IN ('part','file','block')),
  scope_ref  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- path or block id
  holder_user TEXT REFERENCES users(id),
  holder_conn TEXT,
  holder_label TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- <= created_at + 10 min
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (part_id, scope, scope_ref)
) STRICT;
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ collaboration + runtime state
CREATE TABLE comments (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  thread_id   TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- = id of root
  parent_id   TEXT REFERENCES comments(id),
  version_id  TEXT REFERENCES versions(id),
  anchor      TEXT CHECK (anchor IS NULL OR json_valid(anchor)),  -- {block?|file,lines?, quote}
  body        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) <= 16384),
  provenance  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provenance IN ('person','agent','link_viewer')),
  author_user TEXT REFERENCES users(id),
  author_conn TEXT,
  author_link TEXT REFERENCES public_links(id),
  to_agent    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  agent_state TEXT CHECK (agent_state IN ('open','claimed','answered')),  -- inbox (P3); resolved = resolved_at
  resolved_at INTEGER,
  resolved_by TEXT,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  deleted_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX comments_part ON comments(part_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX comments_to_agent ON comments(part_id) WHERE to_agent = 1 AND resolved_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE data_docs (                             -- window.storage + claude.use("db"); survives versions
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('shared','personal')),
  owner      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- user id for personal, '' for shared
  collection TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- '__storage' for window.storage
  doc_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  body       BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) <= 262144),
  rev        INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- CAS
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_by TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | link:<id> | guest:<link>:<g>
  CHECK ((scope = 'shared') = (owner = '')),
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, scope, owner, collection, doc_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE data_leases (
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
  collection TEXT NOT NULL,
  doc_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  holder     TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, collection, doc_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

-- Per-part data snapshots: ON by default (daily, keep 7), for undoing a bad write (not disaster recovery).
-- A part with no row uses the default; a row exists only once someone changes it.
CREATE TABLE data_snapshot_policies (
  part_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  mode        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'daily' CHECK (mode IN ('off','daily','hourly')),  -- daily keep 7, hourly keep 48
  keep        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 7,
  expire_days INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 90,           -- stop after N days unopened; keep the last one
  set_by      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- user:<id> | conn:<id> (agents may request at create)
  set_at      INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE data_snapshots (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  taken_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled' CHECK (reason IN ('scheduled','contribute','before_restore','before_reset')),  -- only 'scheduled' counts against keep
  blob_hash  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),   -- canonical JSON of the part's shared data_docs
  docs       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  bytes      INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX data_snapshots_part ON data_snapshots(part_id, taken_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE assets (                                -- viewer uploads (P3)
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- a_...; served at /_a/<id>
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  blob_hash   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  mime        TEXT NOT NULL,
  size        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (size <= 26214400),
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  uploaded_by TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- user:<id> | conn:<id>
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  deleted_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX assets_part ON assets(part_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE runtime_errors (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  source      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer' CHECK (source IN ('viewer','render')),
  fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- hash(kind, message, top frame)
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('error','unhandledrejection','blocked_load','csp')),
  message     TEXT NOT NULL,
  stack       TEXT,
  url         TEXT,
  count       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (part_id, version_id, source, fingerprint)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX runtime_errors_part ON runtime_errors(part_id, last_at DESC);
CREATE TRIGGER runtime_errors_keep1000 AFTER INSERT ON runtime_errors BEGIN   -- cap 1,000 per part; the janitor drops > 30 d
  DELETE FROM runtime_errors WHERE part_id = NEW.part_id AND id NOT IN
    (SELECT id FROM runtime_errors WHERE part_id = NEW.part_id ORDER BY last_at DESC LIMIT 1000);
END;
```

## Not in scope

The token service (T43), device grant (T44), PATs (T45), idempotency/leases logic (T11, T46, T47), shared data (T96), snapshots (T77), comments (T50), assets (T83).

## Design notes and decisions

- `oauth_clients.kind` `cimd|dcr|manual|builtin` (`part-cli` is the builtin device-code client); unconsented clients (`consented_at` NULL) are purged after 1 h.
- `agent_connections`: `kind` `oauth_code|device|pat`, `principal_kind` `person|service` with `CHECK ((principal_kind = 'person') = (user_id IS NOT NULL))`; `quota_versions_day` NULL = the default (a connection: 500 versions a day and 2 GiB introduced).
- `oauth_tokens.prefix` `pf_at_|pf_rt_|pf_pat_` (secret scanning, log redaction); `resource` is always the workspace origin (RFC 8707); `used_at` on a refresh token marks rotation, and reuse revokes the family.
- `idempotency`: a row is stored **only when the write commits** (a rejected write doesn't use up its `request_id`), keyed `(principal, request_id)`, purged after 24 h.
- `data_docs`: `body` <= 262144 bytes (256 KiB), `CHECK ((scope = 'shared') = (owner = ''))`, `rev` for CAS, `updated_by` `user:<id> | conn:<id> | link:<id> | guest:<link>:<g>`.
- `data_snapshot_policies`: no row = daily keep 7; `data_snapshots.reason` `scheduled|contribute|before_restore|before_reset` (only `scheduled` counts against keep).
- `runtime_errors`: `UNIQUE (part_id, version_id, source, fingerprint)`; trigger `runtime_errors_keep1000` caps 1,000 per part (the janitor drops > 30 d).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DDL present with `schema_test` coverage of every table/index/trigger/CHECK here.
- [ ] CHECK rejections: connection `person` without user; token kind `id`; shared doc with owner; doc body 262145 bytes; snapshot reason `manual`; asset size 26214401; comment provenance `guest`; lease scope `dir`.
- [ ] Trigger test: inserting 1,001 runtime errors for one part leaves 1,000 (the oldest by `last_at` dropped).

## Tests

`schema_test::agent_tables`, `schema_test::collab_runtime_tables`, `schema_test::data_docs_scope_owner_check`, `schema_test::runtime_errors_trigger_caps_1000`.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model: agents (OAuth AS + personal tokens); collaboration + runtime state; §3b Tokens; §3d Idempotent, every write; §5c data snapshots.

- Parent task: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T06.b: Schema v1 part 2: versions, builds, blobs, mirror cache, drafts + grants, links, epochs, invites, audit

title: T06.d: Schema v1 part 4: backend tables, events, webhooks, render jobs, kv + parts_fts (no triggers)
description:
## Goal and why

The last block of the main schema: backend tables (created in P0, used from P2a, so P2a needs no disruptive migration), the append-only event log that feeds SSE, `part_watch` and webhooks, the render-sidecar queue, singleton state, and the FTS5 search table.

## Scope

Append this DDL verbatim to `0001_schema_v1.sql`:

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ backends (P2a; only the runner touches the Engine API)
CREATE TABLE backend_images (
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  digest      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'sha256:...' as the runtime reports it
  source      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('server_build','prebuilt_image','uploaded_image')),
  ref         TEXT,                                  -- registry ref as written (prebuilt_image)
  tar_hash    TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),           -- uploaded_image: the docker-save tarball
  size        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pruned_at   INTEGER,                               -- removed from the runtime; kept: live + previous 2 versions
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, digest)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE container_sets (                        -- one per (part, version) that has been started
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id),
  state           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('starting','healthy','unhealthy','draining','stopped','failed')),
  started_at      INTEGER,
  healthy_at      INTEGER,
  last_request_at INTEGER,                           -- scale-to-zero idle timer (15 min)
  stopped_at      INTEGER,
  cold_starts     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  UNIQUE (part_id, version_id)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX container_sets_running ON container_sets(state) WHERE state IN ('starting','healthy','draining');

CREATE TABLE containers (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                     -- the runtime's container id
  set_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES container_sets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  service      TEXT NOT NULL,
  role         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('main','worker','cron','dependency')),
  image_digest TEXT NOT NULL,
  state        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('created','running','exited','dead')),
  restarts     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  started_at   INTEGER,
  exited_at    INTEGER,
  exit_code    INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX containers_set ON containers(set_id);

CREATE TABLE part_volumes (                          -- /data/parts/<id>/vol/<service>; one named volume per service
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  service     TEXT NOT NULL,
  quota_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1073741824,
  used_bytes  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  measured_at INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, service)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE part_secrets (                          -- write-only: set or replaced by agents (backends:deploy) or people (edit); never read back
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (name GLOB '[A-Z_]*' AND name NOT GLOB '*[^A-Z0-9_]*' AND length(name) <= 64),
  value_enc   BLOB NOT NULL,                         -- encrypted with PF_SESSION_KEY; no op returns it
  inject_as   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'env' CHECK (inject_as IN ('env','file')),
  set_by_user TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),    -- the person (author)
  set_by_conn TEXT,                                  -- agent connection, if an agent set it
  set_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, name)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE lan_allow (                             -- per-part exceptions to the LAN block; set by a person (admin UI), never an agent
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'host:port' or a CIDR
  note        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'may reach the home-automation server'
  added_by    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  added_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  revoked_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX lan_allow_part ON lan_allow(part_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ events, webhooks, jobs
CREATE TABLE events (
  seq        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,      -- cursor for part_watch / SSE Last-Event-ID; kept 30 d
  at         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  part_id    TEXT,
  space_id   TEXT,
  type       TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- part.created, version.committed, build.finished, part.live_changed, comment.added, data.changed, backend.started, ...
  actor      TEXT,                                   -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | guest:<link>:<g> | system
  payload    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(payload))
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX events_part ON events(part_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX events_space ON events(space_id, seq);

CREATE TABLE webhook_deliveries (                    -- targets live in site config, never in DB
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  target     TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- site-config target name
  event_seq  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES events(seq),
  attempts   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  next_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','ok','dead')),
  last_error TEXT,
  UNIQUE (target, event_seq)
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX webhook_due ON webhook_deliveries(next_at) WHERE status = 'pending';

CREATE TABLE render_jobs (                           -- tier (b) sidecar queue; concurrency 1, coalesced per part
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  viewport    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (viewport IN ('mobile','desktop')),
  purpose     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('check','gate','thumbnail','og')),  -- gate: the live = after_check check
  requested_by TEXT,                                 -- conn:<id> for part_check
  request     TEXT CHECK (request IS NULL OR json_valid(request)),  -- {wait_ms, actions}
  status      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','ok','failed','superseded')),
  result      TEXT CHECK (result IS NULL OR json_valid(result)),  -- {screenshot_hash, blank, errors, console, failed_requests, actions, timing}; GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>
  queued_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  finished_at INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX render_jobs_queue ON render_jobs(status, queued_at) WHERE status IN ('queued','running');

CREATE TABLE kv (                                    -- singletons: directory poll cursor + staleness, provisioner tier, last export, last drill, alert state, disk budget state
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

```sql
------------------------------------------------------------------ search
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE parts_fts USING fts5(
  part_id UNINDEXED, title, description, tags, body, notes, comments,   -- body = extracted readable text, not code
  tokenize = 'unicode61 remove_diacritics 2', prefix = '2 3'
);
```

## Not in scope

Runner/backends logic (T98-T104), event delivery (T51, T123), render queue (T80), FTS population and ranking (T76).

## Design notes and decisions

- `part_secrets.name` must match `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`, <= 64 chars; `value_enc` encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY`, never returned by any op.
- `lan_allow` rows are set by a person (admin UI), never an agent.
- `events.seq` AUTOINCREMENT is the cursor for `part_watch`/SSE `Last-Event-ID`; kept 30 days. Surfaces render `actor` as `{kind, id, on_behalf_of}`.
- `webhook_deliveries.target` is a site-config target name; targets live in config, never in the DB (rules out SSRF).
- `render_jobs.purpose` `check|gate|thumbnail|og` (`gate` = the `live: "after_check"` check); `request` holds `{wait_ms, actions}`.
- `kv`: directory poll cursor + staleness, provisioner tier, last export, last drill, alert state, disk budget state.
- `parts_fts`: `body` = extracted readable text, not code; tokenizer `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, `prefix = '2 3'`. **No triggers** (round-final F18): T76 maintains it in application code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DDL present with `schema_test` coverage; `parts_fts` exists as an fts5 virtual table with the listed columns; no trigger references it.
- [ ] CHECK rejections: `part_secrets` name `lower` and a 65-char name; container role `sidecar`; render purpose `screenshot`; webhook status `failed`; event payload invalid JSON; `api_prefix`-style checks covered in T06.a.

## Tests

`schema_test::backend_tables`, `schema_test::events_jobs_kv`, `schema_test::fts_table_shape`, `schema_test::no_fts_triggers`.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model: backends; events, webhooks, jobs; search; §3f Backends; §4 Events; §4c render queue; §3e Search; §10 final round F18.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T06.c: Schema v1 part 3: OAuth clients, connections, tokens, codes, idempotency, leases + comments, data, snapshots, assets, runtime errors

title: T06.e: Insights schema v1: events_raw, rollups_daily, traces, spans, log_segments, janitor_runs (insights.db)
description:
## Goal and why

The second database file, `/data/insights.db`, holds analytics and observability with its own writer, so "a busy day of views and traces" never adds latency to the save path, and losing it loses nothing anyone needs to restore. The plan names both DDL blocks as the source for T06's migration and schema test, so T06 ships this migration set and its test; T113.a opens the file (the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there from Slice 1) and T105 starts writing analytics into it.

## Scope

Write this DDL verbatim into `crates/pf-db/migrations/insights/0001_insights_v1.sql` (a separate migration set applied to `insights.db` by a second `pf-db` instance):

```sql
-- /data/insights.db: analytics and observability (§5g). A separate file with its own writer.
-- Never part content: ids, op names, argument keys, sizes, statuses and timings only (a CI fuzz test checks it).
CREATE TABLE events_raw (                            -- kept 30 d, then only in rollups_daily
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'view','op','rt','grant_decision','build','backend','link_open', ...
  surface     TEXT CHECK (surface IN ('mcp','http','cli','ui','part','rt','backend')),
  op          TEXT,                                  -- registry op name or route class
  part_id     TEXT,
  actor       TEXT,                                  -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | guest:<link>:<g> | link:<id> | NULL
  viewer_key  BLOB,                                  -- public viewers and guests: hash(truncated IP, UA, rotating salt)
  status      TEXT,                                  -- 'ok' or an error code
  latency_us  INTEGER,
  bytes_in    INTEGER,
  bytes_out   INTEGER,
  request_id  TEXT,
  attrs       TEXT CHECK (attrs IS NULL OR json_valid(attrs))  -- {arg_keys, build_method, kind, ...}; never values
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX events_raw_at ON events_raw(at);
CREATE INDEX events_raw_part ON events_raw(part_id, at) WHERE part_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX events_raw_actor ON events_raw(actor, at) WHERE actor IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE rollups_daily (                         -- kept indefinitely; small
  day     INTEGER NOT NULL,                          -- days since epoch, UTC
  metric  TEXT NOT NULL,                             -- 'views','uniques','ops','errors','builds_ok','cold_starts','guest_writes', ...
  dim     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',                  -- 'part:<id>' | 'conn:<id>' | 'op:<name>' | 'method:server_build' | ''
  value   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (day, metric, dim)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE traces (                                -- tail-sampled: every error, every slow request, 1 % of the rest; 7 d, 2 GiB
  trace_id     BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  request_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  duration_us  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  root         TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- route class or op
  status       TEXT NOT NULL,
  part_id      TEXT,
  actor        TEXT,
  kept_because TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kept_because IN ('error','slow','sample'))
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX traces_at ON traces(started_at);
CREATE INDEX traces_request ON traces(request_id);

CREATE TABLE spans (
  trace_id    BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES traces(trace_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  span_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  parent_id   INTEGER,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'policy.decide','sqlite.write','build.child','runner.start', ...
  start_us    INTEGER NOT NULL,                      -- offset from the trace start
  duration_us INTEGER NOT NULL,
  fields      TEXT CHECK (fields IS NULL OR json_valid(fields)),
  PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE log_segments (                          -- index over /data/logs/**/*.jsonl.zst; the lines live in the files
  path      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                        -- 'app/2026-10-23T14-0001.jsonl.zst' | 'parts/<id>/backend-0042.jsonl.zst'
  stream    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (stream IN ('app','backend')),
  part_id   TEXT,
  first_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  bytes     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lines     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  max_level TEXT CHECK (max_level IN ('trace','debug','info','warn','error')),
  CHECK ((stream = 'backend') = (part_id IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX log_segments_stream ON log_segments(stream, part_id, first_at);

CREATE TABLE janitor_runs (                          -- what each retention job freed (§5h)
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  store       TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- a row of the §5h retention table
  action      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('prune','rotate','gc','checkpoint','vacuum','image_prune','cache_prune')),
  items       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  freed_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
  size_after  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cap_bytes   INTEGER,
  error       TEXT
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX janitor_runs_store ON janitor_runs(store, at);
```

## Not in scope

The insights writer, collection, rollups and salts (T105); the trace store (T106); log segments (T107); the janitor (T113).

## Design notes and decisions

- "Never part content: ids, op names, argument keys, sizes, statuses and timings only (a CI fuzz test checks it)" - T112. No column can hold a value or a raw IP: `viewer_key` is `hash(truncated IP, UA, rotating salt)`.
- `traces.kept_because` `error|slow|sample` (tail sampling: all errors, all over the slow threshold, 1 % of the rest; 7 days / 2 GiB).
- `log_segments`: `CHECK ((stream = 'backend') = (part_id IS NOT NULL))`.
- `janitor_runs.action` `prune|rotate|gc|checkpoint|vacuum|image_prune|cache_prune`.
- Decided (polish round): T06 owns the DDL file and its schema test; **T113.a** opens `/data/insights.db` and applies this migration set at start (the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there from Slice 1); T105 adopts the same handle for collection. The plan was silent on placement; this avoids ever moving `janitor_runs` between files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration set loads from empty into a separate file; `schema_test::insights_*` asserts every table/index/CHECK.
- [ ] Guard: no column in insights.db is named like `ip`, `body`, `content` or `value` (supports T112's rule).

## Tests

`schema_test::insights_tables`, `schema_test::insights_checks`, `schema_test::insights_has_no_content_columns`.

## References

PLAN.md §5e Data model (the insights DDL block), §5g Insights, §5h Disk safety.

- Parent task: T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T06.a: Schema v1 part 1: identity, spaces, parts, names, tags, notes + schema_test harness

title: T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
description:
## Goal and why

The content-addressed store for every byte partifactory keeps: part files, manifests, build outputs, brotli variants, data snapshots, assets, screenshots, cards. Blobs are named by `sha256`, stored once, written atomically and durably, and verified when read. This is what makes versions cheap ("a one-line edit to a 40-file part stores one new blob plus one tiny manifest"), backups simple (`blobs/` is write-once, so any copy is safe), and the "durable when acknowledged" promise true. In Slice 1; feeds T08, T14, T17, T34, T75.

## Scope

- Crate `pf-blobs`. A `BlobStore` trait (async): `put(bytes | stream) -> {hash, size}`, `put_verified(expected_hash, stream)`, `has(hash)`, `get(hash) -> verified reader/bytes`, `open_mmap(hash)` (for T16's mmap LRU), `size(hash)`, `delete(hash)` (used only by GC, T59), `list_iter()` (for GC/export), `usage()`.
- **Local implementation**: layout `/data/blobs/ab/cd/<sha256>` (two-level fan-out by the first two byte-pairs of the hex hash).
- **Write path**: write to a temp file in the same filesystem (`/data/blobs/tmp/<random>`), `fsync` the file, **hash-verify** the bytes written, `rename` into place, `fsync` the parent directory. "So a partial blob never appears under its hash."
- **Idempotent concurrent puts**: two writers of the same hash both succeed; the second rename either replaces with identical bytes or is skipped when the target exists and verifies; no torn file is ever visible.
- **Verify-on-read**: `get` streams while hashing and returns an integrity error (and logs `event="blob.corrupt"` with the hash) if the computed hash differs; a bit flip on disk is detected, never served. For mmap'd hot blobs, verify once on first map and record it.
- **Disk pressure hook**: before a write, consult a `DiskBudget` trait (implemented for real by T114: a global budget, default 80 % of the volume; warn at 80 % of the budget, refuse at 95 %). T07 ships a simple implementation using filesystem free space so the behaviour exists now: **a write at 95 % returns `storage_full`** (catalogue code, HTTP 507, CLI exit 7). Reads and deletes are never refused.
- `blobs` table bookkeeping (insert `{hash, size, created_at}` on first put) is done by the caller inside its writer transaction (T08), not by the store; the store is filesystem-only so it can be reused by export/import (T34/T35).

## Not in scope

- Shared-vs-part blob class (a property of the reference: `shared_blobs` and `build_files`, T08/T17).
- GC (T59), the full disk budget and store caps (T114), S3 or other backends ("`BlobStore` trait: a local directory under `/data/blobs` in v1").

## Design notes and decisions

- Why content addressing: dedup across versions and parts (a fork writes zero new blobs), cache-forever URLs for shared blobs (`/b/<hash>`, `public, immutable`), and integrity for free.
- Why verify on read: a household box runs for years on consumer disks; serving a silently corrupted part is worse than a 500 with a logged hash.
- Why temp -> fsync -> verify -> rename: the round-1 design ordered blobs vs a remote store; that's gone, but the local atomicity rule stays. A call returns only after the blobs are durable and the manifest commit is fsynced.
- Brotli variants are separate blobs (`br_hash` in `build_files`), produced by T13.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "put/has/get round trip; concurrent put of the same hash is idempotent; a flipped byte on disk is detected; a write at 95 % returns `storage_full`".

- [ ] put/has/get round-trips arbitrary bytes (0 B to 25 MiB) and streams.
- [ ] 32 concurrent puts of the same content all succeed and leave one file with the right hash; no temp files remain.
- [ ] Flipping one byte of a stored blob makes `get` return an integrity error and logs `blob.corrupt`.
- [ ] With the budget fake at 95 %, `put` returns `storage_full`; `get` and `delete` still work.
- [ ] A crash between temp write and rename (simulated by killing the process) leaves no file under the hash; a startup sweep removes stale temps older than 1 h.

## Tests

- `pf_blobs::tests::roundtrip_sizes` (property test over random byte vectors), `put_stream_matches_put_bytes`.
- `pf_blobs::tests::concurrent_same_hash_idempotent` (32 tasks).
