title: T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
description:
## Goal and why

Define and implement the immutable **part version**: a canonical source manifest whose hash is the version id. "Every version is a manifest of hashes" is one of partifactory's founding promises: you never lose work, you can always say what changed, restore is just appending an old manifest, and history is cheap because blobs are deduplicated. Head/live pointers make "a broken save never replaces a working page" structural. On the Slice 1 critical path (T06 -> T08 -> T12 -> T13 …).

## Scope

- Crate `pf-model`, module `manifest`/`version`.
- **Manifest shape** (verbatim): `{part_id, n, kind, entry, files: {path → {hash, size, mime}}, meta, parent, author, actor, created_at}`, **canonicalised as JCS (RFC 8785)**. "Its hash (so it covers the part id, `parent` and `n`) is the version id, and `n` is the readable counter agents use."
  - `kind` one of `html | markdown | text | svg | code | tsx | slides | files`; `entry` the entry file path; `meta` holds title/tags/description and later fields (e.g. `meta.thumbnail`, `meta.jig_version`); `parent` = previous version id or null; `author` = the person (`user:<id>`); `actor` = the connection (`conn:<id>`) or null.
  - Paths: relative, `/`-separated, no `..`, no leading `/`, NFC, <= 512 bytes; `.pf/blocks.json` is a reserved path (block-id sidecar, T48) that lives inside the manifest.
  - mime detection by extension with a fixed table (text files get `; charset=utf-8`).
- **Commit a version** (`commit_version`), run inside the single writer (T05): given `{part_id, base head, files map (path → bytes or existing hash), kind, entry, meta, author, actor, via, message, rebased_from?, restored_from?, live_gate}`:
  1. write new blobs through T07 *before* entering the writer (durable first);
  2. in the writer transaction: read head, assign `n = head_n + 1`, build the manifest, hash it, store the manifest bytes as a blob, insert `blobs` rows (if new), `versions` (with `manifest_hash = id`), `version_files` (denormalized manifest for diff, GC, FTS, serving), update `parts.head_version_id`, `parts.head_n`, `parts.updated_at`; append a `version.committed` event (T51 consumes events; the row can be written now).
  3. return `{version_id, n}` after commit (fsynced).
- **Pointers**: `head` is the newest committed version; `live` is the newest one with an `ok` build: `(parts.live_version_id, parts.live_build_id)`. T08 provides the setter `set_live_if_newer(part, version, build)` (`if version.n > live.n then live = version`), used by T13 after a build; with `live_gate = 'after_check'` the switch waits for the gate (T80). T08 does not build.
- **v0 placeholder**: a part with no version has `head_n = 0`, `head_version_id = NULL`; `head: 0`, `live: null`, `build: null` in outputs.
- Golden fixtures in `tests/golden/manifests/`: manifest JSON + expected hash for several parts.

## Not in scope

- Build records and the build pipeline (T13), kinds (T12), names (T09), spaces (T10), the part service ops (T11), `part_edit` anchor edits (T46), block ids (T48).

## Design notes and decisions

- Why JCS: deterministic bytes across serde versions and platforms, so the hash is stable forever; any change in key order or number formatting would silently change version ids.
- Why the manifest includes `part_id`, `parent` and `n`: two parts with identical files never share a version id, and a version id fully identifies a place in one part's history.
- Why build records are separate (T13): compile output depends on the toolchain; keying output on the manifest alone would serve stale output after an upgrade.
- "Keep all versions." There's no version pruning in v1 (non-goal); GC collects only unreferenced blobs (T59).
- `version_files` duplicates the manifest on purpose (fast diff, GC marks, FTS, serving without parsing JSON).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Golden manifest hashes stable across runs; a one-line edit to a 40-file part writes exactly 1 blob + 1 manifest".

- [ ] Golden manifests hash to the checked-in ids on every platform and run.
- [ ] Editing one line of one file in a 40-file part creates exactly 2 new blobs (the changed file + the manifest) and 40 `version_files` rows.
- [ ] `n` is strictly sequential per part under concurrent commits (via T05's writer).
- [ ] `set_live_if_newer` never moves live backwards.
- [ ] Paths with `..`, absolute paths and non-NFC names are rejected with `invalid_input`.

## Tests

- `pf_model::manifest::tests::golden_hashes` (fixtures in `tests/golden/manifests/*.json` + `*.sha256`).
- `pf_model::manifest::tests::jcs_key_order_and_numbers` (property test: permuted maps hash equal).
- `pf_model::version::tests::one_line_edit_writes_one_blob_one_manifest` (counts `blobs` inserts and files under `/data/blobs`).
- `pf_model::version::tests::concurrent_commits_sequential_n`, `live_never_moves_backwards`, `path_rules`.
- Log assertion: one `event="version.committed" part_id=… n=… outcome="ok"` per commit (capture subscriber).

## References

PLAN.md §2 The core idea (Part version; head/live; build records), §3d Durable when acknowledged, Latest vs live, §3e Versions and rollback, §5e `versions`, `version_files`, `parts` pointers, §10 final round F17 (manifest lists `part_id` and `n`; JCS).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P0 (epic "P0 Core (local)"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Golden manifest hashes stable across runs; a one-line edit to a 40-file part writes exactly 1 blob + 1 manifest
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
- Unblocks: 
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
  - T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
  - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
acceptance_criteria: Golden manifest hashes stable across runs; a one-line edit to a 40-file part writes exactly 1 blob + 1 manifest

title: S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
description:
## Goal and why

Slice 1 is the first shippable cut through phases P0, P1 and P2, frozen on 2026-10-23 (decision 35). It is **exactly what the `communal_pixel_editor` acceptance test (T97) needs, and nothing more**. The phases stay as the full roadmap; Slice 1 is their first shippable cut.

*Why freeze a slice:* the plan is large, and the pixel board exercises every risky layer at once: the opaque-origin sandbox, path capabilities, builds, agent connections, guests on public links, live shared data, and data rollback. Shipping that end to end first proves the core before anything is built on top of it. Adding anything to the slice takes a decision from the admin (the owner). Tasks that straddled the line were split, so every task is either in the slice or after it (the remainders are T118-T126, each named "after Slice 1").

This bead closes when the Slice 1 definition of done holds. It depends (blocks edges) on T97, T117, T57, T44, T35, T38, T59, T115 and T14, and therefore transitively on all **58 Slice 1 tasks** (every bead labelled `slice1`).

## Scope: what is in Slice 1 (58 tasks)

| Area | What ships | Tasks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core store, versions, the bin | blob store, manifests, versions, names, personal spaces, create (incl. fork and scratch parts), history, diff, restore, the 30-day bin, idempotent writes | T01, T04-T11, T19 |
| Builds | the build child process; kinds `html`, `markdown`, `text`, plus prebuilt `files`; mirror-on-build (in the parent process); the shared blob host. `tsx` (T60) comes right after Slice 1, and its compiler spike (T02) stays in | T12, T13, T14, T17 |
| Sandboxed part host | path caps, the content listener with the canonical CSP and the serve-time entry document, the prelude and `/_rt`, the trusted wrapper with its chrome API, the content-free card (two static PNGs) | T15, T16, T29, T62, T72, T75 |
| Shared data, live | `window.storage` (personal and shared) over `/_rt`, `data.changed` on `/_rt/events`, `shared_data_writers`, `part_data` for agents (incl. snapshot list, restore and reset) | T51 (Slice 1 part), T96 |

## Not in scope (after Slice 1, all still planned in their phase)

- Backends (P2a, all of it) and the backend pixel test (T104).
- Insights beyond Health: T105-T112, T108-T110, the OTLP adapter (T111).
- Identity extras: native invites and local passkey accounts (T94), the Authentik directory adapter and provisioner (T03, T92, T39-T42), cleanup lists, `provision` (T32), the Cloudflare adapter (T91), `doctor` (T68), the portability lane (T93).
- Agent extras: OAuth authorization code (T124), comments (T50), inward sharing by agents (T52), leases (T47), block ids (T48), notes / `render: "text"` / `part_find` (T122), `part_watch` and event SSE (T123), other `part_link_for` actions (T125), Jig and `design_system` (T54), the Hermes skill (T58).
- Workspace extras: versions rail and bin view, search, diff, preview of old versions, comments rail, agent activity, inward sharing rungs, Move to Family, Ask for access, install as app (T120); source editor (T55); live reload (T79); renames (T70).
- Notifications: the ops-alert webhook (T121) and signed event webhooks for agents (T123).
- Previews beyond the content-free card: T119, T81. More kinds: `tsx` (T60, first after the slice), `svg`/`code` (T118), `slides` (T66). Shipping extras (T126). P3, P4, P5. The bench (T23) and the nginx/HAProxy comparison (T74).

## Design notes and decisions (decided for the slice)

- **A person connects every agent once, by design.** No unattended bootstrap: the device code needs a person's Allow and a personal token is made by a person in the UI. Unattended agents run on a personal token. MCP clients other than Claude Code use a personal token in Slice 1.
- **Agents connect by device code or personal token**; OAuth authorization code (CIMD, DCR, manual clients) is T124. Every MCP client the slice needs accepts a static `Authorization` header. The token service (T43's Slice 1 part) is built as the OAuth AS's token side, so T124 adds an endpoint, not a redesign. The authorization endpoint is the largest new attack surface in the plan and none of it is exercised by the test (decision 37).
- **Personal spaces only.** `family` and `system` are created by `provision` (T32), after Slice 1.
- **Every card is content-free.** A part with a public link unfurls with the content-free card in its public-link audience ("Anyone with the link", no title, name or thumbnail). The titled card is T119 (decision 40: two static PNGs).
- **No search.** Agents address parts by name. FTS5 and `part_find` come with T76 and T122.
- **Ingress through the contract only.** The example deployment's tunnel runs as a plain proxy meeting the ingress contract, configured by hand; its two DNS records are made by hand.
- **`window.storage` is the part's data API.** `claude.use("db")` and `/_rt` `db.*` are T73 (P3).
- **Telegram in-app browser**: a 5-minute real-phone passkey test stays in T38; if it fails, Telegram is set to open links in the normal browser and Hermes' messages hint "open in browser". The person-bound-link fallback is rejected (decision 36).
- **Provisional, pending the admin (decisions 39-42)**: `tsx` right after the slice (T02 spike stays in); the preview card is two static PNGs; the retention chain T113 -> T114 -> T115 stays in the slice and sets S1's date (it is as long as the pixel test's path: shipping uncapped stores to a box that is then left alone for years is the failure the plan exists to avoid); the versions rail/bin view (T120) and the deliverable extras (T126) are deferred.
- **Critical path to S1 (14 steps)**: T01 -> T05 -> T06 -> T08 -> T12 -> T13 -> T16 -> T17 -> T62 -> T77 -> T96 -> T95 -> T97 -> S1, tied with the retention chain (... T62 -> T77 -> T113 -> T114 -> T115); the conformance chain (... T43 -> T53 -> T56 -> T57) is shorter since the polish round: MCP (T53) no longer waits for the render sidecar, and T80.d wires `part_check` into MCP when it lands. The P0 tasks carry these paths; start the build worker (T13), content listener (T16) and prelude (T62) first.

## Acceptance criteria (the Slice 1 definition of done)

dag2.py: "`communal_pixel_editor` (T97) passes in CI and against the example deployment; the Slice 1 definition of done holds."

- [ ] 1. **`communal_pixel_editor` passes in CI on every PR** (on the T24 harness: Dex and Caddy with an internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`; the admin's sign-in, step-up, share, roll back and freeze run on Chromium with the virtual authenticator, and the signed-out guest runs on a mobile WebKit profile): an agent connected by device code creates the board in one `part_create`, runs `part_check`, posts `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`; the admin does Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy (4 interactions + 1 biometric); a signed-out browser paints and the admin's open tab shows it within 1 s; the admin rolls back one snapshot and freezes the link, and the guest's next write is refused.
- [ ] 2. **The same flow passes once by hand on the example deployment** (its IdP as plain OIDC, its tunnel as the proxy): a real agent, the admin on a phone, a signed-out phone on mobile data.
- [ ] 3. **Every acceptance test of the 58 Slice 1 tasks passes**, including cross-surface conformance over MCP, HTTP, the CLI and `/skill.md` with device-code and personal tokens.
- [ ] 4. **The security checklist lines for what exists pass from outside** (T38), and the guest, agent and render-sidecar lines pass in T95, T43-T45, T53 and T80. No agent token, scope or op can make a public link.
- [ ] 5. **Export and import round-trip**: the nightly export imported into a fresh container brings back every part, version, data document and snapshot, and every cap minted before it is dead.
- [ ] 6. **Every store that exists is capped** and passes its fill-past-cap case (T115); the Health page shows each one, the backup layers and the disk budget; no `[unsafe]` key is set.
- [ ] 7. **`/skill.md` is `docs/agent-contract.md`**, and the test that regenerates its op reference from the registry passes.
- [ ] 8. **The Telegram passkey test is recorded** (pass, or fail with the two fixes applied and re-tested).

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` (T97) green on the latest main and on the release candidate; keep the run's `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor/server.jsonl`, Playwright traces and click-budget counts as release evidence.

## References

## Dependency context

  - T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
  - T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
  - T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
  - T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
  - T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
  - T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
  - T115: Retention table test: every existing §5h store filled past its cap comes back under

- Unblocks: T60: tsx kind (right after Slice 1): oxc + rolldown in the build child, library set, frozen import maps

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".
acceptance_criteria: `communal_pixel_editor` (T97) passes in CI and against the example deployment; the Slice 1 definition of done holds

description:
# Phase P1 Edge + identity

## Goal and why

Phase P1 puts partifactory on the internet safely: the ingress contract with example proxy configs, `provision` with the
manual and Cloudflare providers, generic OIDC login + the claims re-read directory, the Authentik directory adapter,
`/grant` -> the part host, the **part-host wrapper** with its chrome API and CORS, the policy engine + audience ladder +
spaces + the role x runtime matrix, the admin pin + native passkey step-up, the Stockroom workspace (gallery, search,
history, diff, preview old versions, restore, bin, share sheet, Move to Family), admin-only public links on the part host
with open counts, tier (a) cards, rate limits, quotas, the Health page with optional ops alerts, backups (consistent DB
copy, `export`/`import`, the nightly export on by default, per-part data snapshots on by default), the first drill on a

ids, traces and the log pipeline, the janitor, the disk budget and the retention test, the no-content-in-logs fuzz test,

- G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change

- G03: Visual regression suite for workspace and wrapper screens (light, dark, 360 px)

- G07: One-screen regrant UI after a parts-only import

Phase exit: M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".

title: T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test)
description:
## Goal and why

Make people able to sign in with **any** OIDC provider (generic OIDC is the identity baseline, decision 23), give them the one and only cookie partifactory sets (the workspace session), and build the end-to-end test harness every browser test in the project runs on.

Why:
- **Portability**: the workspace host is the only OIDC client, configured purely from the provider's discovery document. The example deployment's Authentik is used as plain OIDC in Slice 1; Dex is used in CI; the same binary must sign in against a second provider config with no code change.
- **Cookies only on the workspace host**: `__Host-pf_session` is the only cookie partifactory sets; part hosts never set or read cookies. Same-site `SameSite=Lax` with every part host is what lets `/grant` and the wrapper's chrome API work.
- **Revocation**: "sign out everywhere" revokes all sessions and bumps the user's minter epoch so every cap minted through those sessions dies on its next request.
- **Testing reality**: the pixel test (T97), the §7 suite (T38) and the portability lane (T93) need real TLS, real hostnames (`parts.pf.test`, `*-part.pf.test`), a real OIDC provider and two browser engines. Building that harness once, here, is what makes every later e2e test cheap. In Slice 1 (on the sign-in lane T24 → T25 → T26 → T27).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead; close it only after both subtasks are closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- **T24.a** — generic OIDC client, workspace sessions, sign-in/sign-out routes, sign out everywhere.
- **T24.b** — the e2e harness: Dex, Caddy with an internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`, browser host resolution (Chromium `--host-resolver-rules`, WebKit `/etc/hosts`), virtual WebAuthn, log/trace capture; reused by T38, T97, T93.

Shared facts both subtasks rely on:
- Config: `[idp]` (issuer, client_id, groups_claim, audience_group; optional), client secret from env (`PF_IDP_CLIENT_SECRET` or its `_FILE` form, per the T04 env contract). No `[idp]` → IdP-less deployment (local accounts, T94; admin bootstrap, T28).
- Session cookie: `__Host-pf_session`, `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`, stored hashed server-side, 30 days sliding.
- `sessions` table (T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE sessions (
  id_hash      BLOB PRIMARY KEY,                     -- sha256(__Host-pf_session value)
  user_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,                     -- 30 d sliding
  stepup_at    INTEGER,                              -- last admin WebAuthn assertion (valid 10 min)
  idp_refresh_enc BLOB,                              -- OIDC refresh token, encrypted with PF_SESSION_KEY; re-read groups every 15 min
  idp_checked_at  INTEGER,
  ua_summary   TEXT,
  revoked_at   INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
- Epoch keys (T15): `minter:sess:<id>` per session; "sign out everywhere" bumps every session's minter epoch for the user.

## Not in scope

- Group re-read every 15 min, `invalid_grant` handling, epoch bumps on membership diffs (T25); policy decisions (T26); `/grant` (T27); admin pin and WebAuthn step-up (T28); local passkey accounts and invites (T94); Authentik flows/adapter (T92); the §7 lines themselves (T38).

## Design notes and decisions

- **One OIDC client, one redirect URI**, no per-part or wildcard redirect URIs: part hosts never authenticate people, they receive caps from `/grant`.
- Confidential client + PKCE; implicit consent where the IdP supports it, so there's no consent screen for people (click budget "sign in after session expiry: 2 interactions").
- An IdP that issues no refresh tokens gets **12-hour** sessions instead of 30-day ones, so membership is re-read at least that often (T25 relies on this).
- Admin step-up and IdP login are separate, so the IdP's `max_age`/`prompt=login` behaviour isn't load-bearing (T28).
- The harness uses a real TLS chain (internal CA) rather than `--ignore-certificate-errors`, so secure-context, `__Host-` cookie and `SameSite` behaviour are exercised as in production.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Login round trip in e2e against Dex on `parts.pf.test` over TLS, in Chromium and WebKit; the same binary signs in against a second provider config with no code change; sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps the user's minter epoch".

- [ ] T24.a and T24.b closed.
- [ ] e2e `login_roundtrip` passes on Chromium and WebKit against Dex at `https://parts.pf.test`.
- [ ] A second Dex config (different issuer, client id and claim names) signs in with no code change.
- [ ] Sign out everywhere revokes every session of the user and bumps their minter epochs; a cap minted before it is rejected afterwards.

## Tests

See subtasks; the parent runs `tests/e2e/identity/login_roundtrip.spec.ts` on both engines and `crates/pf-auth/tests/second_provider.rs` as its closing check.

## References

PLAN.md §3a How people sign in; §3 Topology (workspace is the only host with cookies); §5f Portability lane (Dex, Caddy, local cert); Slice 1 Definition of done item 1 (the harness); final-round finding F23; §5e `sessions`. Decisions 7, 23, 24. dag2.py T24.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Login round trip in e2e against Dex on `parts.pf.test` over TLS, in Chromium and WebKit; the same binary signs in against a second provider config with no code change; sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps the user's minter epoch
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T19: Dev/test identity fake: Authn + Directory traits with a static-file implementation
- Unblocks: 
  - T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T24.a: Generic OIDC client (discovery, confidential + PKCE), workspace sessions, sign out everywhere
  - T24.b: E2E harness: Dex, Caddy with internal-CA wildcard cert for pf.test, per-browser host resolution, virtual WebAuthn
acceptance_criteria: Login round trip in e2e against Dex on `parts.pf.test` over TLS, in Chromium and WebKit; the same binary signs in against a second provider config with no code change; sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps the user's minter epoch

title: T24.a: Generic OIDC client (discovery, confidential + PKCE), workspace sessions, sign out everywhere
description:
## Goal and why

Implement sign-in for people against any OIDC provider and the workspace session model. This is the generic `Authn` (T19 trait) used in production; vendor extras live in adapters (Authentik, T92). Without it nobody can reach `/grant`, the gallery or the share sheet.

## Scope

- `openidconnect` crate client in `pf-auth`, configured from the discovery document at `[idp] issuer`; `client_id` from config; client secret from env/`_FILE`; scopes `openid profile email` plus `offline_access` (refresh tokens) where offered; the **groups claim name** from `[idp] groups_claim`; other claim names (username, display name, email) from config with sensible defaults (`preferred_username`, `name`, `email`).
- Routes on the workspace host (`parts.<domain>`):
  - `GET /signin?return=<path>`: sign-in page (Stockroom; the content-free card in og tags; passkey/local-account entry is T94) with "Continue" starting the OIDC flow; `return` is path-only (must start with `/`, ≤ 2 KiB) to avoid open redirects.
  - `GET /oidc/callback`: code exchange with PKCE (S256) and `state`/`nonce` checks; upsert `users` by `(idp_issuer, idp_sub)` (`auth_source='oidc'`), record groups from the claim (`groups.source='claim'`, `group_members`), set `in_audience` from `audience_group`; create a `sessions` row; set the cookie; redirect to `return`.
  - `POST /signout` (this session) and `POST /signout/everywhere` (all of the user's sessions).
- Session cookie `__Host-pf_session`: 256-bit random value, `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, stored only as `sha256` in `sessions.id_hash`; **30 days sliding** (`last_used_at` / `expires_at` updated at most once per N minutes to limit writes); **12 h** when the IdP issued no refresh token. The OIDC refresh token is stored encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY` in `sessions.idp_refresh_enc` (consumed by T25).
- Session extractor for axum used by every workspace route and the chrome API; revoked/expired sessions are rejected.
- **Sign out everywhere**: set `revoked_at` on every active session of the user and bump `epochs['minter:sess:<id>']` for each (T15 epoch store), so every cap minted through them fails verification on its next request.
- Audit rows (`audit` table) for sign-in, sign-out, sign-out-everywhere (`action` `session.create`, `session.revoke`, `session.revoke_all`).
- Never log tokens, codes, cookies (T18 redaction types).

## Not in scope

- Periodic group re-read and `invalid_grant` (T25), WebAuthn (T28, T94), the harness (T24.b).

## Design notes and decisions

- Upsert key `(idp_issuer, idp_sub)` so changing IdP never collides (`users_idp` unique index); username collisions get a numeric suffix.
- The workspace is the only OIDC client: no per-part redirect URIs.
- Implicit consent is configured in the IdP; partifactory shows no consent screen of its own for people.
- `SameSite=Lax` (not `None; Partitioned`) because the workspace and every part host are same-site; this is what the chrome API and `/grant` rely on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sign-in round trip against a discovery-document provider creates a user, a session and the cookie with exactly the attributes above.
- [ ] A second provider config (different issuer, claim names) works with no code change.
- [ ] Sessions slide to 30 days; a no-refresh-token IdP yields 12-hour sessions.
- [ ] Sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps their minter epochs (verified by a cap minted before failing after).
- [ ] `return` cannot redirect off the workspace host (fuzzed).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-auth/tests/oidc_mock.rs::callback_creates_user_and_session` (against an in-process mock OIDC provider), `pkce_and_state_enforced`, `nonce_mismatch_rejected`.
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/second_provider.rs::claim_names_from_config` (two configs, same binary).
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/sessions.rs::cookie_attributes`, `sliding_expiry`, `twelve_hour_without_refresh_token`, `stored_only_as_hash`.
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/signout.rs::signout_everywhere_bumps_minter_epochs` (asserts `event="session.revoke_all" principal="user:u_..." sessions=N` and that a pre-minted cap gets `stale_epoch`).
- `pf_auth::return_path::tests::fuzz_return_param` (property test: Location always on the workspace host).

## References

PLAN.md §3a How people sign in; §5e `users`, `sessions`, `groups`, `group_members`, `audit`, `epochs`; §2 Capabilities (minter epochs); §3a UX click budgets. dag2.py T24.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

- [ ] Sign-in round trip against a discovery-document provider creates a user, a session and the cookie with exactly the attributes above.
- [ ] A second provider config (different issuer, claim names) works with no code change.
- [ ] Sessions slide to 30 days; a no-refresh-token IdP yields 12-hour sessions.
- [ ] Sign out everywhere revokes all sessions and bumps their minter epochs (verified by a cap minted before failing after).
- [ ] `return` cannot redirect off the workspace host (fuzzed).

title: T24.b: E2E harness: Dex, Caddy with internal-CA wildcard cert for pf.test, per-browser host resolution, virtual WebAuthn
description:
## Goal and why

Build the browser end-to-end harness that every e2e test in the project runs on: the pixel test (T97), the §7 security suite (T38), the portability lane (T93) and every UI flow with a click budget. It must look like production: real TLS, real hostnames (`parts.pf.test`, `<name>-part.pf.test`, `blobs-part.pf.test`), a real OIDC provider, a reverse proxy meeting the ingress contract, and two browser engines (Chromium for the admin's flows with a virtual authenticator, mobile WebKit for the signed-out guest).

Why: the riskiest layers (sandbox, caps, `SameSite` cookies, the wrapper's `#pf=` hop, WebAuthn with `rp.id` = apex) only behave correctly under a real secure context and real hostnames. A harness with `localhost` and ignored cert errors would pass tests production fails.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/harness/` (scripted with Docker Compose or a shell script; the same steps run locally and in CI):
  - **Dex** as the OIDC provider: static users and groups matching the T19 fixtures (admin, two household members, outsider), refresh tokens on, groups claim on; a second Dex config for the "second provider" test.
  - **Caddy** in front, routing `parts.pf.test` → `:8080` and `*.pf.test` → `:8081`, preserving `Host`, with a **locally issued internal-CA wildcard cert** for `*.pf.test` + `pf.test`, passing the client IP as `X-Forwarded-For` (`[ingress] client_ip_header`, `trusted_proxies` = the Caddy address), SSE-friendly timeouts and 8 MiB bodies. This Caddyfile is the first draft of `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile`: T89 takes it over as the one shipped example (never two Caddy configs), and the harness then mounts T89's file with its cert paths overridden.
  - The internal CA is generated per run; its root is trusted by the browsers (Chromium via NSS db / policy, WebKit via the system trust store in the CI image), never via `--ignore-certificate-errors`.
  - **Host resolution**: Chromium launched with `--host-resolver-rules="MAP *.pf.test <caddy-ip>, MAP pf.test <caddy-ip>"`; WebKit via `/etc/hosts` entries written by the harness (WebKit has no resolver flag) for `parts.pf.test`, `blobs-part.pf.test` and each test part host (written per test, or a local dnsmasq for wildcards).
  - Playwright projects: `chromium-desktop` (admin flows, virtual WebAuthn authenticator via CDP `WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator`), `webkit-mobile` (signed-out guest; mobile viewport and UA profile).
  - partifactory started from the compose file with secrets as `_FILE` mounts (the portability lane, T93, reuses this exactly).
- **Click-budget helper**: counts `click`/`press`/WebAuthn events along a scripted path and asserts the §4a.7 budget (used by T31, T97, T120).
- **Log and artifact capture**: per test, server JSONL logs to `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/server.jsonl`, Playwright trace, screenshots and HAR on failure; the request ids of failing requests printed in the test output (from `X-PF-Request-Id`).
- First tests using it: `tests/e2e/harness/self_test.spec.ts` (needs no partifactory sign-in code: TLS chain, host resolution, a dev-only stub route that sets a `__Host-` test cookie, the virtual authenticator, the click counter) and, once T24.a lands, `tests/e2e/identity/login_roundtrip.spec.ts` (sign in via Dex on both projects, land on the gallery, sign out), which is the parent T24's closing check.

## Not in scope

- The tests of later tasks (they add their specs); the Cloudflare/Authentik staging runs (T38, adapters); Podman backends pass (T93/T104).

## Design notes and decisions

- Final-round finding F23 made the harness part of T24: "the e2e harness (Dex, Caddy, an internal-CA cert for `pf.test`, host resolution per browser) is part of T24; the admin's steps run on Chromium with the virtual authenticator, the guest on WebKit."
- `pf.test` uses the reserved `.test` TLD, so nothing resolves publicly.
- The harness is vendor-free by construction (no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea), which is what the portability lane needs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `harness/self_test.spec.ts` passes on `chromium-desktop` and `webkit-mobile` over TLS at `https://parts.pf.test` (`login_roundtrip` is the parent T24's closing check and needs T24.a as well).
- [ ] A virtual authenticator can be added in Chromium tests (smoke assertion; used by T28/T31/T97).
- [ ] A test part host `<name>-part.pf.test` resolves in both browsers.
- [ ] Failing tests leave server JSONL, trace, screenshots and HAR under `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/`.
- [ ] The click-budget helper fails a test when a scripted path exceeds its budget.
- [ ] Harness runs with no external network access other than pulling images.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/identity/login_roundtrip.spec.ts` (both projects; asserts server log `event="session.created"` and `route_class="workspace_ui" status=200` for `/`).
- `tests/e2e/harness/self_test.spec.ts`: TLS chain valid (no cert errors), `__Host-pf_session` set with `Secure`, part-host resolution, virtual authenticator present, click counter counts a 2-click path as 2.
- `tests/e2e/harness/second_provider.spec.ts`: restarts with the second Dex config and signs in.

## References

PLAN.md Slice 1 Definition of done item 1; §5f Proving it: the portability lane; §3 ingress contract; §3a UX: click budgets, tested end to end; §4a.7 Click budgets; §10 Final round F23. dag2.py T24 (harness "reused by T38, T97 and T93").

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else (polish round: the harness runs in parallel with T24.a; only the parent's `login_roundtrip` closing check needs both)

- [ ] `harness/self_test.spec.ts` passes on `chromium-desktop` and `webkit-mobile` over TLS at `https://parts.pf.test` (`login_roundtrip` is the parent T24's closing check and needs T24.a as well).
- [ ] A virtual authenticator can be added in Chromium tests (smoke assertion; used by T28/T31/T97).
- [ ] A test part host `<name>-part.pf.test` resolves in both browsers.
- [ ] Failing tests leave server JSONL, trace, screenshots and HAR under `target/e2e-logs/<test-name>/`.

title: T30: Rate limits (governor, per route and principal, trusted client IP) + pre-auth body caps
description:
## Goal and why

In-process rate limits are **the real abuse control** for a server reachable from the internet. Edge rules are an optional backstop, and Cloudflare Free allows only one. Every limited route must return 429 at its threshold, keyed on the trusted client address (T89) and the principal, so a looping agent, a guest painting too fast or a brute-forcer on device codes is stopped by the server itself. Body caps before auth stop unauthenticated clients from making the server buffer large bodies. In Slice 1 the guest write limits are part of what makes Can-contribute links safe (T95), and §7 needs "Rate limits trip at the configured thresholds".

## Scope

- `governor` keyed limiters (per IP from `ClientAddr`, per principal `user:`/`conn:`/`guest:<link>:<g>`, per part where stated) as a `tower` layer plus explicit calls inside handlers that know the principal.
- Limited routes (from the plan): `/grant`, `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/l/*`, `/mcp`, `/api`, `/_rt` writes (and per guest), backend requests per part (registered later by T101), invite acceptance (T94) and comments (T50). Each has a config default and is in the safe-defaults registry (T114).
- Known thresholds (verbatim):
  - `window.storage` writes: 60 a minute per guest (300 per IP), 600 a minute per signed-in person per part. Reads: 600 requests a minute per viewer per part, where a `getMany` or a `list` page counts as one. (Enforcement hooks for T96/T95 to call.)
  - `part_check`: 30 per hour per connection (T80 calls the limiter).
  - Device code manual entry: 5 attempts per minute per session (T44).
  - `runtime_errors` inserts: <= 10/min per part.
  - DCR registration rate-limited (T124).
- Response: HTTP `429` + `Retry-After`, error `rate_limited` with `details: {kind, limit, retry_after}` (CLI exit 6). The UI shows `429 · SLOW DOWN` ("Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.").
- Pre-auth body caps (verbatim §5d): 2 MiB per source file, 25 MiB per media blob or asset, 8 MiB per request, 256 KiB per db document (and per `window.storage` value), 512 bytes per `window.storage` key. **Request bodies are capped before auth on unauthenticated routes.** `too_large` (413) with `details.limit`.
- Turning rate limits off needs `[unsafe] rate_limits = "off"` and shows on Health and in `doctor` (T114 registry).
- Metrics: `pf_rate_limited_total{route_class, key_kind}`.

## Not in scope

Quotas (T33). Guest-specific shared-data cap (T95). The single edge rule (T91). Backend per-part request limits (T101 registers them).

## Design notes and decisions

- Key on the trusted client-IP header only from trusted proxies. Otherwise everyone behind the proxy shares one bucket, or an attacker spoofs.
- Limits are generous for people and tight for unauthenticated or guest traffic. Agents that loop hit quotas (T33) as well as rate limits.
- Limiter state is in memory (single node by design). A restart resets buckets, accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Each limited route returns 429 at its threshold in a test".

- [ ] A table-driven test per limited route returns 429 with `Retry-After` at exactly threshold + 1.
- [ ] Guest per-guest and per-IP write limits are enforced independently.
- [ ] Oversized unauthenticated bodies are rejected before any auth or DB work (no DB query, checked with the query counter).
- [ ] The rate-limit config cannot be disabled without the `[unsafe]` key (`config check` fails).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rate_limits.rs`: a table of (route, key, threshold) driving a test clock. Asserts `event="ratelimit.trip" route_class=... key_kind=ip|principal|guest` log lines and the `rate_limited` error shape.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/preauth_body_caps.rs`: a 9 MiB body to `/oauth/token` and `/l/x/go` gets 413 with zero DB queries.
- Unit `xff_key_from_trusted_only` (reuses T89).

## References

title: T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
description:
## Goal and why

"Change that thing from last week" starts with finding it. One SQLite FTS5 index serves both the workspace search box (T120) and the agents' `part_find` (T122). It is after Slice 1: in the slice, agents address parts by name. Search must match what people read, not code: a search for "map" shouldn't hit every `.map(` call. It must also rank recent work first, and stay fast at the expected scale (~10k parts).

## Scope

- Index table (created empty by T06; T76 populates it):
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE parts_fts USING fts5(
  part_id UNINDEXED, title, description, tags, body, notes, comments,   -- body = extracted readable text, not code
  tokenize = 'unicode61 remove_diacritics 2', prefix = '2 3'
);
```
- **Indexed**: title, description, tags, agent notes, comments, and the **extracted readable text** of HTML and Markdown parts (text nodes after rendering, minus `<script>`/`<style>`). `text` kind: the text itself. Code (`tsx`, `code`, JS inside HTML) is not indexed as text.
- Updates: when a version goes live (`part.live_changed`), and when notes or comments change. Application-level updates through the writer, **no FTS triggers in T06** (F18). Deleted (binned) parts are removed from results (hidden from search and the gallery).
- The text extractor is shared with `part_get {render: "text"}` (T122), so they return the same text.
- **Filters**: `space:`, `kind:`, `by:` (an agent or a person, e.g. `by:hermes`, `by:me`), `updated:` (today/week/month or a date range), `has:data`, `has:comments`, `tag:`.
- **Ranking**: `bm25` with column weights (title 10, tags 5, description 4, notes 3, text 1, comments 2) multiplied by a recency factor `1 / (1 + age_days / 30)` on the last live change. No query means "recent, by me or this agent".
- **Visibility**: results are filtered by the policy engine (only parts the caller can see, within the connection's spaces). A part the caller can't see is never revealed.
- A query service API `search(principal, query, filters, cursor, limit) -> hits {part_id, score, matched_in: [title|text|comment|notes], snippet}` with highlight offsets for the UI (`signal-wash` marks) and "where it matched".

## Not in scope

The search sheet UI (T120.b). The `part_find` op and its MCP/HTTP/CLI exposure (T122). Semantic search (T88, P5). "Did you mean" typo suggestions (UI, T120.b, using names and titles).

## Design notes and decisions

- FTS5 because it's in the bundled SQLite and needs no second system (decision 18).
- Readable text, not code, so queries mean what people expect.
- Recency factor on the last live change, not on creation.
- Prefix indexes `2 3` support results-as-you-type (80 ms debounce in the UI).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Over a 10k-part fixture p99 < 5 ms; code inside a TSX file does not match; a newer part outranks an equally relevant older one".

- [ ] Index populated on live change, notes change and comment change. Binned parts are excluded.
- [ ] All filters work, alone and combined.
- [ ] p99 < 5 ms over a 10k-part fixture (bench).
- [ ] TSX code and inline `<script>` text never match. Rendered Markdown text does.
- [ ] Equal relevance: the newer part ranks first.
- [ ] Results never include parts outside the caller's grants or spaces.

## Tests

- `pf_model::search::tests::extract_text_html_strips_script_style`, `extract_text_markdown_rendered`.
- `search::tests::filters_table` (each filter key), `ranking_recency_breaks_ties`, `column_weights_title_beats_body`.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/search_visibility.rs`: user A's private part is never in user B's results (property test over random grants).
- Bench `search_10k_p99` (T23 harness): fails over 5 ms. Logs `event="search.query" latency_us hits` asserted present, with no query text logged (content rule).

## References

PLAN.md §3e Search, §5e `parts_fts`, §5a (`part_find` over 10k parts p99 < 5 ms), §3c (`render: "text"`), final round F18; decision 18.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Over a 10k-part fixture p99 < 5 ms; code inside a TSX file does not match; a newer part outranks an equally relevant older one
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
- Unblocks: 
  - T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install
  - T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
  - T88: Semantic search (embeddings) alongside FTS5, hybrid ranking, off by default

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T26 (results are filtered by the policy engine; the `search_visibility.rs` property test needs real grants).
- Notes and comments are P2 (T122, T50): this task exposes `index_notes(part_id, text)` and `index_comments(part_id, text)` hooks tested with fixture rows; T122 and T50.a call them when they land (noted in their beads).
- The 10k-part p99 < 5 ms check is a plain timing test in `pf-model` with a generated fixture (no dependency on the T23 bench harness).
acceptance_criteria: Over a 10k-part fixture p99 < 5 ms; code inside a TSX file does not match; a newer part outranks an equally relevant older one

title: T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
description:
## Goal and why

People see partifactory through two surfaces. One is the workspace on `parts.<domain>` (sign-in, the gallery of parts). The other is the thin chrome inside each part host's wrapper (title, audience chip, Share). T31 is the Slice 1 cut of that UI, in the approved **Stockroom** theme. It covers exactly what the pixel test and the Slice 1 definition of done need. The admin signs in, finds the part in the gallery, opens it at its own host, and does Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy. That is 4 interactions plus 1 biometric, with in-sheet passkey step-up. Later the admin revokes the link, and can switch "Data: view only".

Everything else in the UI (the versions rail, bin view, search, diff, comments, inward rungs, Move to Family, Ask for access, install) is T120. Roll back data, Reset data and Freeze are T95 (decision 42, F19).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and the end-to-end acceptance passes):
- **T31.a**: Stockroom foundation and workspace pages: `tokens.css` (light and dark), self-hosted IBM Plex, the icon sprite, the brand mark, the 48 px top bar, the sign-in page, the gallery (cards and list linking to part hosts), the empty state, error pages, and the contrast test in CI.
- **T31.b**: the wrapper's chrome bar inside the part host (44 px bar desktop, 40 px phone): back to Parts, tag chip, title, name, `REV n`, the audience chip, Share, ⋯ menu (Copy link, Open standalone), the frame corner ticks, the "being made…" placeholder styling, and the `#share=` deep-link handling.
- **T31.c**: the share sheet, Slice 1 rungs: the ladder control with `Only me` and `Anyone with the link` (admin only), the live sentence, the public link panel (Can view / Can contribute, Copy, opened N times · last …, Revoke with a 10 s undo toast), in-sheet step-up ("Confirm it's you"), the "Data: view only" switch (`shared_data_writers`), and deep-link fragments `#share=public` and `#share=contribute`.

UI technology: **Leptos 0.8 (SSR + hydration) or `askama`/`maud` templates plus small vanilla-JS islands**, per the T02 spike's decision rule: "if building the share sheet costs more than a day of framework friction, or the hydrated bundle for the part view exceeds 300 KB brotli, use askama/maud server templates plus small vanilla-JS islands (share sheet, editor, SSE). It's still Rust." The wrapper bundle is a small standalone bundle of the same Stockroom components (a shared blob, no framework hydration), talking to the workspace only through the chrome API (T29.b).

Click budgets that must be asserted (§4a.7; counted as `click`/`press`/WebAuthn events along the scripted path):

| Flow | Path | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open a recent part | Gallery -> card | **1** |
| Open a link posted in chat | tap link | **1** (0 more if signed in; the first open in a tab adds one silent redirect hop, not an interaction) |
| See who can see a part | glance at the audience chip | **0** |
| Make a public link + copy (admin) | Share -> Anyone with the link -> Copy | **3** (+1 biometric) |
| Revoke a public link | Share -> Revoke link | **2**, undo toast |
| Make a public link guests can contribute to (admin) | Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy | **4** (+1 biometric) |
| Do what an agent's deep link asks | tap the link -> confirm in the pre-filled sheet | **2** (+1 biometric for admin actions) |
| Copy the link to post | ⋯ -> Copy link, or copy the address bar (it's already clean) | **2**, or **0** |

Identity budgets (§3a): open a part I may see, already signed in = **0** (silent redirects only); sign in after session expiry = **2** interactions (pick the passkey from autofill + biometric; no "stay signed in?", no consent).

## Not in scope

T120 (versions rail and restore, bin view, search sheet, history ledger and diff, preview old versions, comments rail, agent activity, inward rungs People / A group / Everyone signed in, Move to Family, Ask for access and access asks, install). T95 (Roll back data, Reset data, Freeze, guest copy). T55 (editor). T108/T109 (Insights, Debug). The admin pages beyond what the share sheet needs. Invites UI (T94).

## Design notes and decisions

- Stockroom (decision 19): a well-kept workshop parts cabinet. The metaphor lives in information design (part numbers `P-0142`, `REV 12`, bin codes `HTML`/`TSX`/`MD`/`TXT`/`FILES`, the manila tag chip, the 6 px tag notch, hairline rules, registration corner ticks), never in decoration (no wood grain, rivets, hazard stripes, stencil fonts, skeuomorphic drawers).
- **Amber is reserved** for "Public link" and nothing else, so amber always means "outside the house". Agents get **blueprint blue**.
- Copy voice: plain, specific, short, sentence case, no exclamation marks, no "Oops". Numbers get units and real counts.
- The published mockup is a static reference. Where it differs from the plan, the plan wins.
- Parts are never themed by Stockroom: no `--pf-*` token reaches part content.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "e2e: open a part host from the gallery, make a Can-contribute public link with in-sheet step-up and revoke it; the §4a.7 budgets for these flows asserted; contrast test passes".

- [ ] All subtask criteria pass.
- [ ] E2E (Chromium with the virtual authenticator, T24 harness): sign in, gallery, open the part (1 click), Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy (4 + 1 biometric), revoke (2 + undo toast). Every budget is asserted by the interaction counter.
- [ ] The contrast test passes for every pair in §4a.3, light and dark.
- [ ] Visual regression snapshots (gallery, part view, share sheet) in light, dark and at 360 px are committed and compared per PR.

## Tests

- E2E `tests/e2e/slice1_share_public.spec.ts` with the shared interaction counter helper `tests/e2e/lib/budget.ts` (counts `click`, `press` and WebAuthn ceremonies). Logs to `target/e2e-logs/slice1_share_public/server.jsonl`. Asserts the server events `event="link.create" mode="contribute"`, `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"` and `event="link.revoke"`.
- `crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs`: parses `tokens.css` and asserts every §4a.3 pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 `rule-strong`).
- Playwright visual regression `tests/e2e/visual/*.spec.ts`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a (4a.2 Stockroom, 4a.3 tokens, 4a.4 type, 4a.5 spacing, 4a.6 screens, 4a.7 click budgets, 4a.9 copy voice and build notes), §3a UX click budgets and share sheet, §5 Leptos decision rule, "Slice 1" (T31 Slice 1 part), decisions 19, 42; final round F19.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): e2e: open a part host from the gallery, make a Can-contribute public link with in-sheet step-up and revoke it; the §4a.7 budgets for these flows asserted; contrast test passes
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T02: Spikes: rolldown/oxc as libraries, rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos SSR vs askama+islands
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
- Unblocks: 
  - T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install
  - T93: Portability lane: full e2e with no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea (Dex, IdP-less, Caddy, local exports)
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - T45: Personal agent tokens (pf_pat_) and the Connected agents page (list, revoke with cascade, New personal token)
  - T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
  - T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
  - T108: Insights UI (admin-only, Stockroom): Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds pages with table views and CSV/JSON export
  - T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
  - T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
  - T85: Phone editing: tap-to-edit text as anchor edits, long-press point-and-comment
  - G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change
  - G02: Workspace error pages (404 NOT IN STOCK, 410, 429, 500 with request id) and workspace PWA install
  - G03: Visual regression suite for workspace and wrapper screens (light, dark, 360 px)
  - G04: Part menu extras: ?dl=1 downloads, Download as zip, Pin, Open standalone, thumbnails endpoint with SVG spec-sheet thumbs, view counts
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T31.a: Stockroom foundation + workspace pages: tokens.css, Plex, sign-in, gallery, error pages, contrast test
  - T31.b: Wrapper chrome bar on the part host: tag, title, REV, audience chip, Share, ⋯, frame ticks

title: T31.a: Stockroom foundation + workspace pages: tokens.css, Plex, sign-in, gallery, error pages, contrast test
description:
## Goal and why

Every other screen is built from this foundation. It covers the Stockroom design tokens, the self-hosted fonts, the icon sprite and the brand mark, plus the two workspace pages Slice 1 needs: the sign-in page (the only place a signed-out person lands, carrying the content-free card) and the gallery (where the admin finds the pixel board and opens it at its own host).

## Scope

- `crates/pf-ui/assets/tokens.css`, embedded in the binary, the single source for light and dark. The dark block is generated from the same source. The values are verbatim from §4a.3, for example:
```css
:root { color-scheme: light;
  --pf-paper:#f4f3ee; --pf-raised:#fbfbf8; --pf-sunk:#e9e8e1; --pf-rule:#d6d4ca; --pf-rule-strong:#8e8b80; --pf-scrim:rgb(20 22 24 / 40%);
  --pf-ink:#191b1d; --pf-ink-2:#3a3d41; --pf-ink-3:#5c5f64; --pf-tag:#ecdcae; --pf-on-tag:#3b3015;
  --pf-signal:#1c6a47; --pf-on-signal:#ffffff; --pf-signal-text:#1c6a47; --pf-signal-wash:#dbeae1; --pf-on-wash:#14503a;
  --pf-public:#f0b43c; --pf-on-public:#1f1606; --pf-public-text:#8a5200; --pf-public-wash:#fbecc8;
  --pf-agent:#1f5d8c; --pf-agent-wash:#dde8f2; --pf-danger:#b02a20; --pf-danger-wash:#f6dedb;
  --pf-diff-add:#d9ecdf; --pf-diff-del:#f5dcd8; --pf-focus:0 0 0 2px var(--pf-paper), 0 0 0 4px var(--pf-signal); }
:root[data-theme="dark"] { color-scheme: dark;
  --pf-paper:#121416; --pf-raised:#1a1d20; --pf-sunk:#0d0f10; --pf-rule:#2b2f34; --pf-rule-strong:#6b7078; --pf-scrim:rgb(0 0 0 / 60%);
  --pf-ink:#ecebe6; --pf-ink-2:#c8c7c0; --pf-ink-3:#9b9da1; --pf-tag:#3e3722; --pf-on-tag:#efe0b4;
  --pf-signal:#62c495; --pf-on-signal:#0b1d14; --pf-signal-text:#6fd0a1; --pf-signal-wash:#173327; --pf-on-wash:#a9e6c8;
  --pf-public:#eab040; --pf-on-public:#1f1606; --pf-public-text:#f2c25e; --pf-public-wash:#3a2e12;
  --pf-agent:#86bde6; --pf-agent-wash:#16293a; --pf-danger:#ff8b80; --pf-danger-wash:#3a1916; --pf-diff-add:#15301f; --pf-diff-del:#3a1b18; }
```
  Dark applies under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` unless `data-theme="light"`. The person's choice is stored per device in `localStorage` on the workspace origin, with a server-side preference as the default for new devices.
- Spacing/radius/elevation/motion tokens verbatim (`--pf-s-1..8` 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64 px; `--pf-r-1..4` 3/5/8/14 px; `--pf-notch: 6px`; `--pf-e-1..3`; `--pf-ease: cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`; `--pf-d-1..3` 120/200/320 ms, all 0 under `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- Type: **self-hosted IBM Plex** (SIL OFL 1.1, licence in `NOTICE` and at `/licenses/fonts`), Latin + Latin-Extended `woff2` subsets embedded in the binary, `font-display: swap`, served `immutable`. **No third-party font CDN, ever.** Families `--pf-font-sans` (Plex Sans 400/500/600), `--pf-font-label` (Plex Sans Condensed 500/600), `--pf-font-mono` (Plex Mono 400/500). Type scale tokens `--pf-t-display` 32/36 ... `--pf-t-mono` 12.5/16 `tnum`. Budget about 160 KB for five cuts. Agreed fallback if too heavy: Plex Mono only, plus system sans. Numbers are tabular everywhere. Relative times carry an absolute `title`/`datetime`.
- Icons: one inline SVG sprite, 1.5 px stroke on a 20 px grid, square caps, mitred joins, `currentColor`, about 40 glyphs. Hand-drawn or adapted from Lucide (ISC) / Tabler (MIT) with the licence noted. The agent glyph is a "node" (a circle with three spokes). Emoji are never icons. Brand mark: a drawer front (a rounded square, a label slot in the upper third, a short pull), one path, works at 16 px, monochrome, green only in the favicon. Wordmark `partifactory` lowercase, Plex Sans Condensed SemiBold, tracking −0.01 em.
- Shared chrome: a **48 px top bar** with mark + wordmark (home), search placeholder (wired in T120), theme toggle, and avatar menu (sign out, sign out everywhere, Connected agents link for T45, admin for the admin). Keyboard: `g p` parts (`/` search arrives with T120).
- **Sign-in page** on `parts.<domain>`: the mark, "Parts, made by you and your agents.", sign in via OIDC (T24) with passkey-first where the IdP offers it, og tags from T75's private card (text matches exactly). It returns to `/grant`'s pending part after sign-in.
- **Gallery (`/`, "Parts")**: a header "Parts" plus a mono count; segmented filter `Recent · Mine · Shared with me` (Family appears once `family` exists, T32/T120); grid/list toggle (grid on desktop, list on phones). **Card = drawer front** (`raised`, `r-3`, hairline, tag notch): a 16:10 thumbnail (Slice 1: the server-drawn SVG spec-sheet thumb or a neutral placeholder, never a broken hole); a label strip (tag chip with part number and bin code, title, name in mono); a foot (audience chip, `REV 12`, "Hermes · 3 min ago"); "being made…" on v0; an expiry badge on scratch parts. Sections grouped by day (`TODAY`, `YESTERDAY`, `THIS WEEK`, `EARLIER`). List view: 56 px rows, 72x45 thumbnail. **Each card links straight to its part host.** Layout `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr))`, 16 px gaps, gutters 24/16 px, max 1280 px.
- Empty gallery: the mark at 64 px, "No parts yet. Parts are made by your agents. Connect one, then ask it for something." with **Connect an agent** and a copyable `claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp`. Loading: skeleton drawer fronts with no shimmer.
- Error pages (paper, the mark, a mono status line, one sentence, one action): `404 · NOT IN STOCK`, `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` (rendering only; Ask for access is T120), `410 · LINK EXPIRED`, `429 · SLOW DOWN`, `500 · SOMETHING BROKE` (with the request id `req 8f1c…`).
- Mobile: tested at 360 x 740, a 56 px bar, list view by default, horizontally scrolling filter chips, hit targets >= 44x44, safe-area insets.
- **Contrast test in CI**: parses `tokens.css` and asserts every pair in the §4a.3 table (fails under 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for `rule-strong`).

## Not in scope

The search sheet, Bin view and Pinned section (T120). Screenshot thumbnails (T81). Invites (T94). Admin area pages (T120 / later).

## Design notes and decisions

Colour is never the only signal: the audience chip always has an icon and words. `--pf-rule` is decorative only. Leptos vs templates is decided by T02.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contrast test is green, light and dark.
- [ ] Fonts are served from the binary only. No request leaves the workspace origin for fonts (asserted in e2e).
- [ ] The gallery card opens the part host in 1 click.
- [ ] The sign-in page og tags equal the private card text.
- [ ] Visual snapshots at 360 px, light and dark.

## Tests

`crates/pf-ui/tests/contrast.rs`; `tests/e2e/gallery_open.spec.ts` (budget 1, asserts no third-party requests via the HAR); `tests/e2e/visual/gallery.spec.ts`; `pf_ui::tests::og_sign_in_matches_card`. Server logs are asserted for `event="ui.render" page="gallery"` with `request_id`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.2–4a.6 (Gallery, Empty states, Error pages, Mobile), §4a.9 build notes, §4c (card text), §5 Workspace UI row.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T31.b: Wrapper chrome bar on the part host: tag, title, REV, audience chip, Share, ⋯, frame ticks
description:
## Goal and why

On a part host, "the part is the page". The wrapper adds **one thin bar** of trusted chrome and keeps everything else in sheets and rails that close. Slice 1 needs the bar to say what the part is and who can see it (the audience chip, 0-interaction budget), and to open Share and Copy link.

## Scope

- A small standalone bundle of the Stockroom components (`crates/pf-ui/wrapper/`), built to shared blobs (JS + CSS) referenced by T29.a's wrapper HTML. **No framework hydration.** It talks to the workspace only through the chrome API (T29.b).
- Desktop bar **44 px** (verbatim layout):
```
│ [mark] ‹ Parts │ [P-0142 TSX] Photo finder  photofinder · REV 12 ▾ │ ● Hermes is editing app.tsx │ Family │ Share │ Edit │ Comments 3 │ ⋯ │
```
  Slice 1 renders: back (`‹ Parts` -> workspace gallery), the tag (part number + bin code), the title, the name in mono, `REV n` (the head/live revision; the version chip's history rail is T120), the **audience chip** (icon + words: `Only me`, `3 people`, `Family`, `Everyone signed in · 15`, `Public link` in amber; click opens Share), **Share**, and **⋯** with Open standalone ↗ and Copy link (always `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`). Edit, Comments and the agent-activity area are rendered only when the chrome API's `/summary.features` (T29.b) lists them: the bar builds its control set from that list (Slice 1: Share, Copy link, Open standalone). The saved/didn't-build activity states arrive with T120.c, Comments with T50.b, Edit with T55, the lease state with T47.
- Phone: a **40 px bar** (back, tag + title, audience icon, ⋯) that hides on scroll down. ⋯ opens a bottom sheet (Share, Copy link, Open standalone) with a grab handle, 85 % max height, primary action in thumb reach.
- Frame decoration: registration **corner ticks** just outside the frame, marking the boundary between our chrome and someone else's page. A new version cross-fades the frame (`d-3`), never a flash of blank. The frame shows the tag, title and corner ticks at once, with no spinner for the first 400 ms.
- "Being made…" (v0): the drafting sheet with a faint 8 px grid and a title block bottom-right (`P-0215 · grocery-planner · REV 0 · Hermes for <person>`) and "Hermes is making this. It'll appear here as soon as the first version lands." It cross-fades to REV 1 on `pf:version` (T51 delivers the live update). If the first version doesn't build: "The first version didn't build. Hermes has the error."

- Runtime errors indicator: a danger tick on ⋯ (from `runtime_errors` via `part_get`) is optional in Slice 1. The full Details sheet is T120.

The versions rail, comments rail, agent activity, Details, Edit, Download zip, Pin, Delete (T120, T55). Install manifest (T29.a serves it; install UX is T120).

## Design notes and decisions

Rails (later) are 360 px and push the frame narrower rather than covering it. Messages from the frame are matched by `event.source`, never `event.origin`.

- [ ] The audience chip shows the correct words and icon for Only me, and for Public link (amber) after a link is made.

title: T31.c: Share sheet, Slice 1 rungs: public link (Can view / Can contribute), in-sheet step-up, Data: view only
description:
## Goal and why

The share sheet is where data leaves the house, so it has to be both quick and honest. In Slice 1 it carries the pixel test's key interaction: Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy, which is **4 interactions + 1 biometric** for the admin. It also carries revoke and the "Data: view only" switch.

## Scope

- One sheet, 480 px on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones, opening inside the wrapper (and on `parts.<domain>` for unsandboxed parts). Top to bottom, Slice 1 subset (verbatim order):
  1. "Share *Photo finder*" with the tag chip.
  2. **The ladder**, a segmented control narrow -> wide: `Only me` · `People` · `A group` · `Everyone signed in` · `Anyone with the link`. In Slice 1, People / A group / Everyone signed in are rendered but disabled or "coming later" (T120 adds them). `Anyone with the link` shows **only for the admin**, in amber, with "The worst option: no sign-in, anyone who gets the link can open it."
  3. **The live sentence**, in `t-heading`: e.g. "**Only you** can see this." / "**Anyone with the link** can open this." It updates before anything is saved.
  5. Rung detail for *Anyone with the link* (admin): mode **`Can view` (default) · `Can contribute`**, with "Anyone with the link can use it. Only you and people you add can change it." under Can contribute. Expiry picker `Never` (default) · 1 day · 7 days · 30 days. The URL with **Copy**. **opened 14 times · last 2 h ago** (from `public_links.open_count`/`last_opened_at`). **Revoke link**. Under Can contribute the sheet also says that switching sets data writers to viewers. (Roll back data, Reset data and Freeze are added by T95 into this panel.)
  6. **Data: view only** switch (`shared_data_writers: "editors"`; off by default, so viewers can write). It is visible to people with edit/manage. Setting it while a contribute link is active freezes that link (T95 implements the freeze, and this switch calls the same path).
  10. Footer: "Changes save as you go." Revocations show a **10 s undo toast** instead of a confirm dialog. Revocation applies at once (epoch bump), and undo re-grants.
- **Step-up is in-sheet**: when the 10-minute window has lapsed, "Confirm it's you" with a passkey button inline. The WebAuthn assertion (`rp.id` = the apex) goes to `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/stepup` (T28), and the action then completes after the biometric, with **no navigation**.
- Deep links: opens at a rung from `#share=public` or `#share=contribute`, with nothing saved until the person confirms (Copy or the mode toggle counts as confirm). Opened by someone without the right, the sheet shows without that option (the normal view).
- Backend calls go through the chrome API session-only handlers (T29.b/T29.c) and `part_edit {meta: {shared_data_writers}}` for the switch.

## Not in scope

People / group / everyone rungs, Move to Family, agent-made grants, access asks, pending invites (T120, T52, T94). Roll back, Reset, Freeze controls and guest copy (T95). The comment opt-in for links (later). "Use a screenshot as the preview" (T81). The `unsandboxed` flag toggle (admin, later).

## Design notes and decisions

Amber means "outside the house". Undo instead of confirm (§3a "Revoke anything": one click, 10 s undo toast). Contribute requires the part to have a live version (public links need one).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Make a Can-contribute link: exactly 4 interactions + 1 biometric (with step-up lapsed). 3 + 1 for Can view.
- [ ] Revoke: 2 interactions plus an undo toast. Undo within 10 s restores the link, and after that the link is 404.
- [ ] A non-admin never sees the `Anyone with the link` rung, and the server refuses the handler anyway.
- [ ] The "Data: view only" switch toggles `shared_data_writers` and the live sentence or data note updates.
- [ ] Step-up happens in-sheet with no navigation (no `framenavigated` event on the top frame).

## Tests

`tests/e2e/share_sheet_public.spec.ts` (Chromium + virtual authenticator) using the budget counter. It asserts server events `event="stepup.verify"`, `event="link.create" mode="contribute"`, `event="link.revoke"`, `event="link.restore"` (undo), and `event="part.meta" field="shared_data_writers"`. A non-admin variant asserts the rung is absent and a direct POST returns 403. Visual snapshots of the sheet, light, dark and 360 px.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Share sheet, §4a.7 budgets, §3a audience ladder, "Can contribute" links, admin step-up, UX click budgets; contract "Who can write shared data".

- Parent task: T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).

Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
