title: T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install
description:
## Goal and why

The Slice 1 UI (T31) covers only what the pixel test needs. T120 completes the everyday workspace from P1: getting work back (versions rail with restore, the bin), finding things (search), seeing what changed (history ledger, diff any two, preview old versions), seeing agents at work (agent activity; the comments rail lands with its backend in T50.b), and sharing inside the household (People, A group, Everyone signed in, Move to Family). It also adds the person-to-person **Ask for access** list and installing a part as a home-screen app. It feeds M1 and its click budgets, and T93's portability lane runs these flows.

Why these were deferred (decision 42): the ops behind restore, delete and undelete already work through `part_edit`, so the pixel test didn't need their UI.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close only after all subtasks are closed and the e2e below passes):
- **T120.a**: versions rail (revision ledger) with Restore, Compare (diff any two), preview old versions, and the Bin view with Restore.
- **T120.b**: the search sheet (top-bar `/`, results as you type, chips, "where it matched", did-you-mean, empty-result prompt) over T76.
- **T120.c**: agent activity in the wrapper bar (saved / didn't-build states from T51 events; the lease state is filled by T47), the Details sheet basics, ⋯ extras (Download as zip, Pin, Delete), and install as a home-screen app per part host. (Polish round: the comments rail moved to T50.b so it lands with its backend.)
- **T120.d**: the inward rungs of the share sheet (People, A group, Everyone signed in), Move to Family, the agent-made grants list with Undo, Ask for access on the 403 page, and the access-asks list (Add / Dismiss).

Click budgets asserted (§4a.7):

| Flow | Path | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find a part by name | `/` -> type -> Enter | **1 keystroke + type + 1** |
| Share with the family | Share -> Move to Family | **2** |
| Share with one person in the household | Share -> People -> pick | **3** |
| Answer an ask for access | Share -> Add (or Dismiss) | **2** |
| See what changed in the last version | `REV` chip -> Compare | **2** |
| Restore an older version | `REV` chip -> row -> Restore | **3**, undo toast |
| Undelete from the bin | Bin -> Restore | **2** |
| Comment for the agent | asserted by T50.b, where the comments rail lands with its backend | **3 + type** |

## Not in scope

The source editor (T55), live reload toasts (T79), Insights and Debug (T108, T109), invites UI (T94), the admin-area pages for groups and users (T94/T42), the titled card (T119), screenshot thumbnails (T81), renames (T70).

## Design notes and decisions

- No notifications and no approval queues: Ask for access is a note from one person to another, and nobody is messaged. Agents never appear in the access-asks list.
- Owners and `manage` grantees share inward without the admin, because inward grants can't leak beyond people who already have accounts. Outward stays admin-only.
- `everyone-signed-in` is admin-only and shown with a live count ("15 people") so it's never vague.
- Move to Family needs write access to both spaces. `family` exists only after `provision` (T32).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "e2e: restore v1 as v4 from the versions rail, delete and undelete from the bin, search, compare v1 vs v3, preview v2, move to Family from the wrapper's share sheet, Ask for access adds one entry to the owner's list (no message, no queue); §4a.7 click budgets asserted".

- [ ] All subtask criteria pass.
- [ ] One e2e scenario runs every listed flow with its budget asserted.
- [ ] Ask for access creates exactly one `access_asks` row. No events go to any notifier or webhook, and no queue table exists.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/workspace_after_slice1.spec.ts` (Chromium + WebKit, T24 harness, budget counter) runs all flows, with server logs at `target/e2e-logs/workspace_after_slice1/server.jsonl`. It asserts events `version.committed via=restore`, `part.deleted`/`part.undeleted`, `grant.set`, `part.moved`, `access_ask.created`. Visual snapshots of the history rail, search sheet, agent-activity states and share sheet rungs.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 (Gallery Bin, Search, Part view, Share sheet, Version history, Comments), §4a.7, §3a (spaces, audience ladder, Ask for access), §3e, "Slice 1: After Slice 1", decision 42.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): e2e: restore v1 as v4 from the versions rail, delete and undelete from the bin, search, compare v1 vs v3, preview v2, move to Family from the wrapper's share sheet, Ask for access adds one entry to the owner's list (no message, no queue); §4a.7 click budgets asserted
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
- Unblocks: 
  - T93: Portability lane: full e2e with no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea (Dex, IdP-less, Caddy, local exports)
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - T125: part_link_for after Slice 1: group, everyone and admin actions
  - G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)

title: T120.a: Versions rail: revision ledger, restore, compare any two, preview old versions; Bin view
description:
## Goal and why

"You never lose work, and you can say what changed." Every version is immutable and kept, and restore is append-only. This subtask puts that in people's hands in the wrapper and the workspace.

## Scope

- **History rail** opens from the `REV 12 ▾` chip (360 px on desktop, pushes the frame narrower; a bottom sheet on phones). A vertical **revision ledger**: each row `REV 12` · "Hermes for <person>" · relative time · a one-line summary (the agent's edit message or an auto summary like "app.tsx +14 −3"), a green `LIVE` tag on the live version and a danger `DIDN'T BUILD` tag on failed ones. Data from `part_get {history: true}`: `[{n, author, actor, via, message, created_at, build_status}]`.
- **Preview**: clicking a row previews it in the frame via a cap pinned to that version (`v` claim). The chip turns tag-coloured: `Viewing REV 9 of 12 · Back to latest`. People with `view` can preview versions that were once live. Drafts and never-live versions need `edit`. `[` and `]` step through versions.
- **Compare** picks any two rows (default: selected vs live): a file list with `+/−` counts and a unified diff (side-by-side >= 1100 px), hunks collapsed beyond 3 lines of context. Binary files show size changes and before/after thumbnails for images. Diff lines have `+`/`−` gutters (colour is never the only signal), using `--pf-diff-add`/`--pf-diff-del`. Data from `part_get {diff_from, diff_to}` -> `{from, to, files: [{path, status, added, removed, patch}]}`.
- **Restore REV 9** appends REV 13 (`part_edit {restore: 9}`) and shows "Restored as REV 13 · Undo". It goes through the build like any other version.
- **Bin view** (workspace gallery): lists deleted parts with days left (30-day bin) and **Restore** (`part_edit {undelete: true}`), for the owner or the admin. Purged parts' names stay reserved forever.
- Delete to the bin from ⋯ -> Delete (with an undo toast).

## Not in scope

Ops semantics (T11, T46). Draft previews (T55).

## Design notes and decisions

Restore is non-destructive. There is no version pruning in v1 (every version kept, blobs deduplicated).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore v1 creates v4 equal to v1 (manifest equal), live after build. Undo works.
- [ ] Compare v1 vs v3 shows the correct counts and patches. Preview v2 shows v2 and the "Viewing REV 2 of N" chip.
- [ ] A view-only person cannot preview a never-live version (403/hidden).
- [ ] Bin: delete and then undelete, 2 interactions. A part at 29 days is restorable.
- [ ] Budgets: Compare 2, Restore 3, Undelete 2.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/versions_rail.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/bin.spec.ts` with the budget counter. Server events asserted: `version.committed via=restore restored_from`, `part.undeleted`. Unit `pf_ui::history::tests::summary_line_format`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Version history, diff and restore; Gallery (Bin); §3e Versions and rollback; contract `part_get` history/diff shapes.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

title: T120.b: Search sheet: instant results, filter chips, where it matched, did-you-mean
description:
## Goal and why

Finding a part by name should be one keystroke, typing and Enter. This is the workspace face of T76's FTS5 index.

## Scope

- The top-bar field (`/` to focus, from any workspace page) expands into a **results sheet** as you type, debounced 80 ms.
- Each hit: thumbnail, title with matches marked (`signal-wash`), a 2-line snippet, and where it matched (title, text, comment, agent notes).
- Filters typed or clicked as chips: `kind:tsx`, `space:family`, `by:hermes`, `by:me`, `has:data`, `has:comments`, `updated:week`, `tag:`.
- "Did you mean …" for zero-result typos (nearest names or titles the person can see). An empty result offers "Ask an agent to make it", which copies a prompt.
- Enter opens the top hit at its part host. Arrow keys move the selection. Results respect visibility (T76 filters by policy).
- Phone: a full-height bottom sheet.

## Not in scope

The index and ranking (T76). `part_find` (T122).

## Design notes and decisions

Results never reveal parts the person can't see. Did-you-mean draws only from visible names.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/` -> type -> Enter opens the part: budget 1 keystroke + type + 1.
- [ ] Chips filter correctly and round-trip into typed syntax.
- [ ] A zero-result typo shows did-you-mean, and the empty state offers the copy-prompt action.

title: T120.c: Agent activity in the bar, Details sheet, install part as home-screen app, ⋯ extras
description:
## Goal and why

Show agents at work in the bar, add the ⋯ -> Details sheet, let a person install a part as its own home-screen app, and finish the ⋯ menu. (The comments rail moved to T50.b in the polish round so that it lands together with its backend and is testable end to end; see the ordering note below.)

## Scope

- **Comments rail**: moved to **T50.b** (lands with the `part_comments` backend). The wrapper shows `Comments` only when the chrome API `/summary` lists the `comments` feature (T29.b).
- **Agent activity** in the bar: "Claude Code saved REV 12 · just now" for 30 s (from `version.committed`/`part.live_changed` on `/_rt/events`, T51, relayed by the frame's prelude `pf:version` or read through the chrome API), or "Didn't build in REV 13: still showing REV 12" in danger colour (from `build.finished` with a failed status), linking to the error. Both states are buildable and e2e-testable in P1 against T51. The lease-holder state (blue pulse dot + "Hermes is editing *app.tsx*") is a `leases` slot that **T47 fills** when leases land (T47 depends on this subtask and adds its e2e case).
- **Details** (⋯ -> Details): agent notes (from T122 when it lands; the section is empty until then), runtime errors (the "Send to agent" button, which files a `to_agent` comment with the stack, is added by T50.b), files, data documents, data snapshots with the snapshot-policy switch (T77: daily / hourly / off, and the JSON download); for a backend part its state, logs, secret names and the note that volumes are covered by exports, not snapshots (when T102 lands). A danger tick on ⋯ when runtime errors exist ("2 runtime errors").
- **Install as app**: the wrapper's per-part web app manifest (`/_pf/manifest.webmanifest`, `id` and `scope` = `/`, name, icon, theme colour; served by T29.a). The UI offers "Install" where the browser supports it. Each part is its own origin, so each installs as its own app. The workspace also installs as a PWA.
- ⋯ menu adds: Download as zip, Pin (gallery "Pinned" section), Delete (to the bin).

## Not in scope

The comments rail and "Send to agent" (T50.b). Leases and the lease-holder state (T47). Agent-facing event delivery (T123). Phone point-and-comment (T85). Analytics in Details (T108).

## Design notes and decisions

- **Ordering (decided in the polish round):** T120 sits in P1 (feeding M1) while comments (T50) and leases (T47) are P2, and no edge may pull P2 into M1. Instead of building UI against an absent backend, each backend task ships its own UI slot: the comments rail is T50.b (T50 now depends on T31), and the lease-holder state is filled by T47 (which depends on this subtask). What this subtask ships is fully testable in P1: the saved / didn't-build activity states (T51 events exist in Slice 1), Details, install and the ⋯ items. The chrome API's `features` list (T29.b) hides a control until its backend exists, so nothing ships half-wired.
- The trusted UI stays outside the part: anchors from the frame arrive over the wrapper <-> part postMessage channel. Content from others is untrusted for agents (provenance).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent activity shows "<agent> saved REV n · just now" within 1 s of a `part.live_changed` event and "Didn't build in REV n" on a failed build, in Chromium and mobile WebKit.
- [ ] `Comments` and the lease state are absent from the bar while `/summary.features` lacks `comments`/`leases` (fixture), present when it lists them.
- [ ] The manifest validates, and the part installs as a separate app (manual pass on a real phone, recorded).
- [ ] The Details sheet lists runtime errors, files, data documents and snapshots (with the policy switch); Download as zip, Pin and Delete work from ⋯.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/agent_activity.spec.ts` (asserts `event="part.live_changed"` / `event="build.finished" outcome="failed"` on the server and the bar text within 1 s), `tests/e2e/details_sheet.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/features_gate.spec.ts` (a fixture `features` list toggles controls), a manifest lint test, and an install smoke on a real phone (recorded). Visual snapshots of the bar states and the Details sheet. Server logs under `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Part view (agent activity, ⋯, runtime errors, install), Comments; §3c (live reload, provenance); §2 Known losses (install via the wrapper).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Pin storage: a `pins(user_id, part_id, at)` table added by a forward-only migration in this subtask (the v1 DDL has none); the gallery's Pinned section reads it. (G04 was re-scoped to thumbnails + view counts.)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Agent activity shows "<agent> saved REV n · just now" within 1 s of a `part.live_changed` event and "Didn't build in REV n" on a failed build, in Chromium and mobile WebKit.

title: T120.d: Inward share rungs (People, A group, Everyone signed in), Move to Family, Ask for access
description:
## Goal and why

Most household sharing is inward: with people who already have accounts, or by moving a part into Family. It must be quick (2-3 interactions) and must never need step-up. Ask for access lets a signed-in person who hits a 403 ask the owner without anyone being messaged.

## Scope

- Share sheet rungs (extending T31.c):
  - **People**: directory type-ahead with a per-person role (`view` < `comment` < `edit` < `manage`). Writes an ordinary grant `{subject: user:<id>, role}`.
  - **A group**: a picker with live member counts. Any IdP group can be *granted*. "Make a group for this" (admin only) creates a local `pf-<name>` group (with the local groups from T94/T25).
  - **Everyone signed in** (admin only, step-up): count and role. Shown with the live count ("15 people").
  - The live sentence updates before saving: "**You and 3 people** can see this. **A family member** can also edit."
- **Move to Family**: one button when the part is in a personal space. It needs write access to both spaces. Effective access is then inherited live from `family`'s grants (`group:<household> -> edit`).
- **Agent-made grants** list: "Hermes shared this with the Family group · Undo" (from `grants.created_by_conn`, T52).
- **Access asks**: on the `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` page ("This part exists, but it isn't shared with you." with no title), an **Ask for access** button (plus "Sign in as someone else"). It writes one row:
```sql
CREATE TABLE access_asks (
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  note        TEXT CHECK (note IS NULL OR length(note) <= 280),
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  closed_at   INTEGER,
  closed_as   TEXT CHECK (closed_as IN ('added','dismissed')),
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, user_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
  The share sheet's **Access asks** section shows "A family member asked for access" with **Add** (an ordinary inward grant) and **Dismiss**. Nobody is messaged. Agents never appear in it. Public-link holders never see it (a revoked link is a plain 404). Asking again while open is idempotent (primary key).
- Every grant change writes one `audit` row (T26). Revocations: one click, a 10 s undo toast, an epoch bump at once.

## Not in scope

The policy engine (T26). Agent sharing ops (T52). Invites ("Invite someone", T94). The groups admin page (T94/T42).

## Design notes and decisions

The agent-made grants list renders empty until T52 (P2) produces agent grants. There is no edge, for the same reason as in T120.c. Step-up is for admin actions only (everyone-signed-in, groups). Household sharing never asks. There are no approval queues: `access_asks` is the only pending state a person sees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Share with the family: 2 interactions. Share with one person: 3. No step-up prompt in either.
- [ ] Ask for access adds exactly one entry. Answering takes 2 interactions. Add creates a grant and the asker can open the part on the next request.
- [ ] The 403 page never shows the title.
- [ ] A non-admin cannot see or use Everyone signed in or Make a group (the server refuses too).

## Tests

`tests/e2e/share_inward.spec.ts` (budgets; asserts `event="grant.set"` and `audit` rows), `tests/e2e/ask_for_access.spec.ts` (403 page has no title text, one `access_asks` row, no webhook or notifier calls observed, Add then 200 on the next open).

## References

PLAN.md §3a Spaces, audience ladder, Ask for access, UX click budgets; §4a.6 Share sheet items 2–8, Error pages; §5e `access_asks`, `grants`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Share with the family: 2 interactions. Share with one person: 3. No step-up prompt in either.
- [ ] Ask for access adds exactly one entry. Answering takes 2 interactions. Add creates a grant and the asker can open the part on the next request.
- [ ] The 403 page never shows the title.
- [ ] A non-admin cannot see or use Everyone signed in or Make a group (the server refuses too).

title: T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
description:
## Goal and why

"From nothing to running" should take an OCI host, a domain with a wildcard record and cert, and optionally an OIDC client. With provider plugins, one DNS token and one IdP token should be enough to create the rest. `partifactory provision` is an idempotent **create-if-missing / update-if-owned script** driven by `site.toml`. It is honest about being a script rather than Terraform: it manages only resources it owns, so reapplying is safe, and it never "reconciles" shared IdP flows. T32 builds the framework and the vendor-free **`manual`** providers, which print what to create and then verify it. That keeps every deployment possible with no vendor (decision 22). It also creates the shared spaces `family` and `system`, which Slice 1 deliberately lacks. Adapters (Cloudflare T91, Authentik T92) plug into its traits.

## Scope

- Traits: `DnsProvider` (records; for the Cloudflare plugin also tunnel, cache rules, rate rule, fallback Worker, health check) and `IdpProvisioner` (OIDC client registration, flows, provisioner account). The core never imports an adapter's types. Adapters are chosen in `site.toml`.
- **Providers**: DNS `manual` (the default: prints the two records, `parts.<domain>` and `*.<domain>`, and the cert names to create, then checks them with a DNS lookup). IdP `manual` (the default: prints the redirect URI and scopes to register in any OIDC provider; the workspace host is the only OIDC client: confidential + PKCE, one redirect URI). More plugins are additive.
- `site.toml` sections it reads (verbatim): `[domain]` (apex, workspace_host, part_suffix), `[ingress]` (kind = proxy | cloudflare-tunnel | acme, client_ip_header, trusted_proxies, request_id_header), `[dns] provider` (+ `[dns.cloudflare]` account_id, zone_id, plan, tunnel_name), `[idp]` (issuer, client_id, groups_claim, audience_group; optional), `[idp.provisioner]` (kind = none | authentik, base_url, flows.*, tier), `[admin] subject`, `[embed] frame_ancestors`, `[alerts] webhook_url`, `[backup]` (host_snapshots, export_schedule, export_dir, export_keep, age_recipient), `[deploy]` (host), `[names] reserved`, `[webhooks]`, `[mirror] allowlist`, `[render] enabled`.
- **Ownership**: a resource counts as owned if its id is in `provision-state.json` (committed to the site repo by the run) *or* its name starts with `partifactory-`. DNS records also carry the comment `managed-by:partifactory` where the provider supports comments. It deletes only resources that are both owned and listed as `created_by_provision`.
- **Order** (each provider skips what it doesn't do): ingress (Cloudflare: tunnel) -> IdP (Authentik: OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow, provisioner account and role) -> deploy -> wait for `/readyz` -> `parts` record -> wildcard record -> Cloudflare only: cache rules -> one rate-limit rule -> fallback Worker route -> health check or an external uptime probe. Each step is idempotent, so a failed run is fixed by re-running.
- `--dry-run` prints one line per resource: `+ create`, `~ update (field: old → new)`, `= unchanged`, `! not owned, skipped`. A real run appends `{ts, resource, before, after}` to `provision-log/<ts>.jsonl` in the site repo. **Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 3 drift on a resource it doesn't own.**
- **Spaces**: creates the `family` space (`kind = 'shared'`, grant `group:<household> → edit`, where the household group name is site config) and the `system` space (`kind = 'system'`, grant `everyone-signed-in → view`; it holds Jig). Both are idempotent (slug unique) and are an internal step against the partifactory DB/API (the admin token or a local CLI call), not a DNS/IdP provider step.
- The provisioner gate (`provision --gate`) entry point exists as a trait hook. Its Authentik implementation is T39.

## Not in scope

The Cloudflare plugin (T91) and Authentik plugin (T92). The gate run (T39). ACME (T90). `doctor` (T68, which reuses the verification lookups).

## Design notes and decisions

- Before-states go to the site repo's run log, not the schema, because `provision` can run in CI (§5e modelling decisions).
- Never touch shared IdP flows except for changes the admin explicitly wants globally.
- There is no DNS token at runtime. A new part is live the instant it's saved (wildcard).
- Slice 1 does without it: the example deployment's two DNS records are made by hand, and parts live in personal spaces only.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Manual mode prints exactly the two records and the redirect URI and verifies them by lookup; a second run is a no-op (`--dry-run` shows no changes); only owned resources are modified; before-states go to the site repo's run log".

- [ ] Manual DNS prints exactly `parts.<domain>` and `*.<domain>` (plus cert names) and verifies them with a lookup against a test resolver.
- [ ] Manual IdP prints the redirect URI and scopes.
- [ ] A second run is a no-op. `--dry-run` shows only `=` lines.
- [ ] A fake provider with a non-owned resource is never modified (`!` line, exit 3 on drift).
- [ ] The run log has `{ts, resource, before, after}` for each change.
- [ ] `family` and `system` exist with their grants after the first run, unchanged after the second.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-provision/tests/manual_providers.rs` with a stub DNS resolver: prints, verifies, exit codes.
- `crates/pf-provision/tests/ownership.rs` with an in-memory fake provider: the owned/unowned matrix, delete only `created_by_provision`, drift exit 3.
- `crates/pf-provision/tests/idempotent.rs`: run twice, and the second dry-run diff is empty. Asserts structured events `event="provision.step" resource=... action="create"|"update"|"unchanged"|"skipped"`.
- `spaces_created_once`: the `family` and `system` rows and grants.

## References

PLAN.md §5c "From nothing to running" / `partifactory provision`; §3a Spaces table; §3 Hostnames; §5f DNS + provisioning row; "Slice 1" (personal spaces only; ingress through the contract); decision 22.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Manual mode prints exactly the two records and the redirect URI and verifies them by lookup; a second run is a no-op (`--dry-run` shows no changes); only owned resources are modified; before-states go to the site repo's run log
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T04: Config + secrets loader: site.toml + PF_* env + PF_*_FILE, redaction, docs/env.md, config check
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
- Unblocks: 
  - T91: Cloudflare adapter: tunnel ingress, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe
  - T92: Authentik adapter: Directory over the API (60 s poll) + IdpProvisioner plugin (OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow)
  - T68: `partifactory doctor`: config, DNS, ingress, certs, IdP, backup layers, disk, store caps, safe defaults
  - T90: Built-in ACME DNS-01 TLS (wildcard cert via a DNS provider plugin) for hosts with no proxy
acceptance_criteria: Manual mode prints exactly the two records and the redirect URI and verifies them by lookup; a second run is a no-op (`--dry-run` shows no changes); only owned resources are modified; before-states go to the site repo's run log

title: T91: Cloudflare adapter: tunnel ingress, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe
description:
## Goal and why

The example deployment runs behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. Cloudflare is an **adapter behind config**, never a dependency (decision 22): everything it does is an optimisation or convenience over the generic ingress contract (T89) and the manual provider (T32). T91 implements the Cloudflare `DnsProvider` plugin and the tunnel ingress kind. `provision` can then create and own the tunnel ingress, the two DNS records (gated on `/readyz`), cache rules for shared blobs and cards, the single combined edge rate-limit rule, the maintenance fallback Worker, and a health check. The adapter's §7 lines *(adapter)* run here.

## Scope

- Ingress kind `cloudflare-tunnel`: `cloudflared` next to the app (QUIC), routing `parts.<domain>` -> :8080 and `*.<domain>` -> :8081 with Host preserved. `[ingress] client_ip_header = "CF-Connecting-IP"` as the adapter default, trusted only from the tunnel's local address in `trusted_proxies`. `PF_TUNNEL_TOKEN` (env or `_FILE`).
- DNS plugin (`PF_DNS_API_TOKEN`; `[dns.cloudflare]` account_id, zone_id, plan, tunnel_name): the `parts` record and the wildcard `*` record as CNAMEs to `<tunnel>.cfargotunnel.com`, created **only after `/readyz` passes**, with the comment `managed-by:partifactory`. *The wildcard CNAME to the tunnel works in practice but isn't documented; T72 item 11 verifies it, and the adapter relies on that result.*
- Cache rules: `blobs-part/b/*` and `parts/og/*`, "eligible for cache", because Cloudflare caches by file extension and these paths have none. Part hosts are bypassed ("bypass cache on `*-part` except `blobs-part`" is two host rules). Part blobs carry `Cache-Control: private` and must never be HIT.
- **One** combined rate-limit rule. Cloudflare Free allows one (IP only, 10 s window), so the adapter installs one combined expression over `/grant`, `/oauth/*`, `/device`, `/l/*`, `/mcp`, `/api`, `/_rt` writes. It is a coarse backstop. `governor` (T30) is the real control.
- Fallback Worker route: serves the static maintenance page (`deploy/proxy/maintenance.html`, T89) when the origin is down, instead of a 1033.
- Health: Cloudflare health checks on Pro and up, or an external uptime probe against `/healthz` on Free (`plan` from config).
- Edge cache hit ratio metric only with a separate read-only `PF_CDN_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` (else the metric is dropped).
- Optional device-connect origin: the Cloudflare country header feeds the coarse origin on `/device` (T44 reads it as "proxy headers").
- Moving hosts: `provision` re-points the tunnel. The runbook then rotates the tunnel connector token and deletes old connections, so a zombie connector can't take traffic (the drill checklist, T35).
- Ownership and idempotency follow T32: names start `partifactory-` or ids are in `provision-state.json`.

## Not in scope

The generic contract and Caddy (T89). The provision framework (T32). The Authentik adapter (T92). nginx/Traefik (T126).

## Design notes and decisions

- Edge caching is never required for correctness. Every response already carries the right `Cache-Control`.
- Grounding facts: Cloudflare Free has one rate-limit rule, and Cloudflare caches by extension (round 2 G A3, G A6).
- The adapter lands after its generic default (§6 rule: adapters never before the default).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Against a test zone: a second run is a no-op; only owned resources change; a shared blob shows `cf-cache-status: HIT` on the second fetch and a part blob never does".

- [ ] Against a test zone the first run creates tunnel ingress, records (after readyz), cache rules, one rate rule, the Worker route and the probe. A second run is all `=`.
- [ ] A pre-existing non-owned record is reported `!` and untouched.
- [ ] A shared blob is `HIT` on the second fetch. A part blob is never `HIT` (*(adapter)* §7 lines).
- [ ] The maintenance page is served by the Worker when the origin is stopped.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-adapter-cloudflare/tests/plan_diff.rs` with a recorded or mocked Cloudflare API: idempotency and the ownership matrix. Asserts `event="provision.step" provider="cloudflare"`.
- A live test-zone job (manual or nightly, not gating PRs, gated by the token's presence): runs provision twice and curls `cf-cache-status`. Artifacts: the run log JSONL plus response headers.
- The §7 *(adapter)* lines run in T38's suite when this adapter is configured.

## References

PLAN.md §3 Topology and Hostnames (wildcard CNAME note), §5c provision Order/Ownership, §5d Abuse prevention (one CF rule), Health (Worker, health checks), Metrics (edge cache hit ratio), §5f Ingress + Edge rows, §5 spike item 11, §7 Caching and blobs *(adapter)*; decisions 6, 22.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Against a test zone: a second run is a no-op; only owned resources change; a shared blob shows `cf-cache-status: HIT` on the second fetch and a part blob never does
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
  - T89: Ingress contract: trusted client-IP header, request ids, Caddy example + maintenance page
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Ingress kind `cloudflare-tunnel` needs a `cloudflared` service in `deploy/compose.yaml` behind a `tunnel` profile (`PF_TUNNEL_TOKEN` / `_FILE`); this task owns it. Acceptance adds: `--profile tunnel` brings up cloudflared and both records resolve through the tunnel.
- Tests add the §7 *(adapter)* line "a part blob is never `cf-cache-status: HIT`": a second fetch of a `/c/<cap>/` blob, with the headers recorded as artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Against a test zone: a second run is a no-op; only owned resources change; a shared blob shows `cf-cache-status: HIT` on the second fetch and a part blob never does

title: T92: Authentik adapter: Directory over the API (60 s poll) + IdpProvisioner plugin (OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow)
description:
## Goal and why

The example deployment's IdP is Authentik. With the generic directory (T25), removing someone from a group takes effect only at the next 15-minute claims re-read. With the Authentik adapter's **60 s directory poll**, it takes about a minute. T92 also gives `provision` an Authentik `IdpProvisioner` plugin, so partifactory gets **its own cloned authentication and authorization flows** that it owns and tunes (implicit consent, passkey-first identification with conditional UI, a no-prompt invalidation flow, partifactory branding), instead of editing flows shared with every other service on the IdP. It is optional, behind config. Nothing outside the adapter depends on it.

## Scope

- **`Directory` over the Authentik API**: the same `groups` claim at login, plus a **60 s poll** of users and group memberships (via `/api/v3/core/users/` and `/api/v3/core/groups/`, read-only), cached. A membership diff bumps `epochs['part:<id>']` for every part whose grants (or whose space's grants) mention an affected user or group (T25's diff logic). Group rows have `groups.source = 'idp_api'` with `idp_id`.
- **Fail open on an unreachable IdP**: a failed poll keeps the last known membership, marks it stale (`kv` staleness entry, shown on Health), **never bumps an epoch**, and raises an ops alert after 10 minutes (T121). A definite "user gone" (API says deleted or disabled) fails closed: the user's sessions end and their minter epoch is bumped.
- **`IdpProvisioner` plugin** (`PF_IDP_PROVISIONER_TOKEN`, `[idp.provisioner] kind = "authentik", base_url, flows.*`):
  - the OIDC application/provider for the workspace host (confidential + PKCE, one redirect URI, implicit consent);
  - **cloned** authentication and authorization flows named `partifactory-*` (owned): passkey-first identification with conditional UI (supported since Authentik 2025.12 when a WebAuthn validation stage is set on the identification stage; verified in T03), implicit consent, no-prompt invalidation, branding;
  - the `partifactory-invite` flow (invitation -> one field -> **passkey enrolment, required** -> user write into one holding group -> login), used by T40;
  - the `partifactory-provisioner` service account and its role (least-privilege intent; verified by the gate T39).
  - Uses blueprints if they can be applied over the API, otherwise direct API calls (per the T03 spike result).
- Shared flows are touched only for changes the admin explicitly wants globally (so far: no "Stay signed in?" prompt, with its before-state in site config).
- Idempotent and ownership-aware per T32. A second provision run is a no-op.

## Not in scope

The provisioner permission gate and tier (T39). Authentik invites (T40). Add-by-email, IdP recovery links and IdP-side `pf-*` groups (T41). The generic OIDC client and claims re-read (T24, T25).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why fail open:* an IdP outage must not lock the household out of what they could already see. Removals still need the IdP to be up, which is the same window as before.
- Authentik facts (checked 2026-10-23): invitations can't set groups and have no use count. Grants and counts live in partifactory, and membership is added by API after enrolment.
- Authentik's DCR needs an authenticated user and creates a provider + app per registration, so it can't serve MCP clients directly. partifactory stays the AS facade.
- The runtime credential is least privilege, verified rather than assumed (T39). With no provisioner, partifactory holds no IdP write credential at all.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Removing a user from a granted group fails their next part request within 70 s; with Authentik down, sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped; provisioning twice is a no-op".

- [ ] Remove a user from a granted group in Authentik, and their next part request fails within 70 s (60 s poll + cap check).
- [ ] With Authentik unreachable, existing sessions and caps work, the stale flag shows on Health, and the epoch counters are unchanged.
- [ ] Provision creates the OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow and provisioner account. A second run is all `=`.
- [ ] No shared flow is modified by provision (diff of non-owned flows is empty).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-adapter-authentik/tests/directory_poll.rs` against a mocked API (wiremock) with a test clock: membership diff -> epoch bumps, failed poll -> stale and no bumps. Asserts `event="directory.poll" outcome="ok"|"stale"` and `event="epoch.bump" reason="membership"`.
- A live Authentik job (the same Authentik version recorded by T03, in a container, nightly and on adapter changes): remove-from-group within 70 s, provision twice. Artifacts: the provision log and the server JSONL.
- The §7 *(adapter)* lines join T38 when configured.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Three layers, How people sign in (Authentik adapter 60 s poll, fail open), UX "Authentik adapter: click reduction", Admin (provisioner least privilege), Invitations (Authentik facts); §5c provision Order; §5f Directory + groups row; decision 23.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Removing a user from a granted group fails their next part request within 70 s; with Authentik down, sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped; provisioning twice is a no-op
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T03: Authentik adapter spike: conditional-UI passkeys, blueprint-over-API, groups claim, membership API, recovery links
  - T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
  - T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - T39: Authentik provisioner permission gate against the real IdP; record tier A/B/C

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Naming aligned with T25 and T121: staleness is the `kv` key `directory.stale_since` (T25's); the 10-minute condition is the alert `idp_unreachable_10m` (one name in T25, T92, T36 and T121).
- The live-Authentik job is **skipped, not failed**, when the Authentik image is unavailable, so no PR gate depends on an external image.
acceptance_criteria: Removing a user from a granted group fails their next part request within 70 s; with Authentik down, sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped; provisioning twice is a no-op

title: T33: Quotas per space and per agent connection (parts, versions/day, bytes), hits on Health
description:
## Goal and why

A household server is set up once and then left alone for years. The way it dies is a disk filled by something nobody was watching, and the most likely culprit is an agent caught in a loop ("create a part, it failed, create another"). Quotas turn that failure into a clear `quota_exceeded` error the agent can read and stop on, plus one row on the admin Health page, long before the disk fills.

This is a Slice 1 task (P1). The pixel-board acceptance test (T97) does not exercise quotas directly, but the Slice 1 definition of done requires that every protection is on by default ("Defaults are the safe choice"), and quotas are one of the listed safe defaults. T115's retention work and the T38 §7 line "quotas stop a looping agent" depend on it.

## Scope

Enforce quotas on every write path that creates parts, versions or stored bytes, keyed on two principals:

- **Per space** (`spaces.quota_parts`, `spaces.quota_bytes`, `spaces.quota_versions_day`).
- **Per agent connection** (`agent_connections.quota_versions_day`, plus bytes introduced), keyed on `agent_connections.id` and not on tokens, because tokens rotate hourly.

Defaults (PLAN §5d, verbatim): "a personal space 2,000 parts, 20 GiB and 1,000 versions a day; a connection 500 versions a day and 2 GiB introduced. NULL in `spaces.quota_*` and `agent_connections.quota_versions_day` means the default; unlimited needs `[unsafe] quotas = "off"`."

Schema already created by T06 (verbatim):
```sql
CREATE TABLE spaces (
  ...
  quota_parts        INTEGER,                        -- quota_*: NULL = the §5d default
  quota_bytes        INTEGER,
  quota_versions_day INTEGER,
  ...
);
CREATE TABLE agent_connections (
  ...
  quota_versions_day INTEGER,                         -- NULL = the §5d default
  ...
);
CREATE INDEX versions_actor_day ON versions(actor_conn, created_at);  -- quotas: versions/day per token
```

What to build:
- A `Quotas` service in `crates/pf-model` (or `pf-janitor` for config wiring) with `check_create_part(space, conn)`, `check_new_version(space, conn)`, `check_bytes(space, conn, new_bytes)`, called inside the single writer before commit (so concurrent writes can't overshoot).
- Counting:
  - parts per space: live and binned parts in the space (binned parts still hold storage until purged);
  - versions per day: `versions` rows by `space` (via `parts.space_id`) and by `actor_conn` with `created_at` in the last 24 h UTC day (use `versions_actor_day`);
  - bytes: per space, the sum of sizes of blobs its versions introduced (dedup: a blob counts once per space); per connection, "Storage per connection is approximated by the blobs its versions introduced" (PLAN §5e modelling decisions). Keep a running counter updated in the writer rather than recomputing on every write; reconcile nightly in the janitor (T113) if drift is found.
- Error: `quota_exceeded` with details `kind`, `limit`, `retry_after` (HTTP 429 + `Retry-After`, CLI exit 6), from the T20 error catalogue. `kind` is one of `parts`, `versions_day`, `bytes` (and later `shared_data`, `backend_memory` etc. owned by other tasks). For the daily limit, `retry_after` is seconds until the window frees a slot; for parts/bytes it is omitted (deleting is the fix) and the hint says so.
- Health: every quota hit records one entry (per principal, per kind, per day: deduplicated) visible on the Health page (T36 shows the list "quota hits"), and a metric `pf_quota_hits_total{kind,principal_kind}`.
- Config: per-space overrides set by the admin (admin UI later; config/DB value now); `[unsafe] quotas = "off"` disables enforcement and is registered in the safe-defaults registry (T114 owns the registry; this task registers the `quotas` key and shows the warning through it once T114 lands — until then a `config check` warning).
- Agent quotas apply to every surface identically (MCP, HTTP, CLI) because they are enforced below the op registry.

## Not in scope

- Rate limits (requests per minute) — T30.
- Shared-data cap per part (5 MiB) and personal data cap (256 KiB) — T96; guest limits — T95.
- Backend quotas (CPU, memory, images) — T102.
- The global disk budget and `storage_full` at 95 % — T114 (quotas are per principal; the budget is per volume).
- The Health page itself — T36 (this task feeds it data).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why quotas per connection, not per token:* tokens rotate hourly (`pf_at_` 1 h, single-use refresh), so a token-keyed quota would reset every hour. The connection is the agent's identity (one per (agent, person)).
- *Why enforce in the writer:* the single writer task serialises commits, so a check-then-commit inside it is race-free; checking in the handler would let 10 parallel creates each pass.
- *Why `quota_exceeded` is retryable only for the daily window:* an agent that loops must stop; the error's hint says "stop looping; ask your person" and the agent contract's table says "wait `details.retry_after` seconds; stop looping".
- Binned parts count toward `quota_parts` and bytes until purged; undelete must re-check nothing (it frees nothing, adds nothing).
- Forks (`part_create {from}`) introduce zero new blobs and so zero new bytes, but do count as a part and a version.
- A rejected write (quota) stores no idempotency row, so the same `request_id` may be retried later (agent contract Rule 1).
- Unlimited is never a NULL: NULL means default. Only `[unsafe] quotas = "off"` removes the limit, and that shows as a warning on Health and in `doctor`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A loop of 10k creates stops at the quota with `quota_exceeded` and one Health-page entry".

- [ ] With defaults, the 2,001st part in a personal space is refused with `quota_exceeded {kind: "parts", limit: 2000}` (HTTP 429, CLI exit 6).
- [ ] A connection's 501st version in a day is refused with `quota_exceeded {kind: "versions_day", limit: 500, retry_after}` and `Retry-After` header.
- [ ] Bytes quota: a write that would take the space past 20 GiB (configurable small in tests) is refused before any blob is referenced.
- [ ] 10k creates in a loop stop at the quota; exactly one Health entry per (principal, kind, day) is recorded; the metric increments per hit.
- [ ] Concurrent creates (100 in parallel at quota − 1) admit exactly one.
- [ ] NULL quota columns use the defaults; a per-space override takes effect without restart.
- [ ] `[unsafe] quotas = "off"` disables enforcement and is reported as a switched-off safe default.
- [ ] Same behaviour on MCP, HTTP and CLI (one enforcement point).

## Tests

- `pf_model::quotas::tests::defaults_apply_when_null`, `::override_per_space`, `::versions_day_window_rolls` (test clock), `::fork_adds_no_bytes`, `::binned_parts_still_count`.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/quota_concurrency.rs::parallel_creates_at_limit_admit_one` (100 tasks through the writer).
- `crates/pf-api/tests/quota_loop.rs::ten_thousand_creates_stop_at_quota`: small configured quota, loop via the HTTP API; asserts 429 + `Retry-After` where applicable, error body shape `{error: {code: "quota_exceeded", details: {kind, limit}}}`, exactly one Health row, and captured logs contain `event="quota.hit" kind="parts" principal="conn:c_.." outcome="quota_exceeded"` exactly once per (principal, kind, day) at `warn` and per request at `info` without content.
- `tests/agent_surfaces` scenario step (joins T57): a quota error has identical normalised shape over MCP, HTTP and CLI (CLI exit 6).
- Config test: `config_check_rejects_quotas_off_without_unsafe_key`.

## References

PLAN.md §5d Operations ("Quotas per space and per agent connection"), §5e Data model (`spaces`, `agent_connections`, `versions_actor_day`, modelling decisions "Quotas per agent"), §4b error catalogue (`quota_exceeded` 429, exit 6), §5h safe defaults and `[unsafe]`, §7 Operations ("quotas stop a looping agent"); docs/agent-contract.md Errors table; decision 33.

- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
- Unblocks: 
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test

title: T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
description:
## Goal and why

**Backup = the `/data` folder.** Everything partifactory knows lives under one volume, so backing up is whatever the host already does, with no second system to run. This task provides partifactory's own two layers on top: a consistent DB copy that non-atomic host tools (rsync, restic) can safely take, and a self-contained, host-portable **export** file that is the off-site and move-to-another-host path, scheduled nightly **on by default**.

Why it matters: a household server is left alone for years; nobody remembers to set up backups before they need them, so the safe default is "a nightly export exists, keep 7". And **no save ever waits on a backup target**: backups read snapshots, never sit on the write path.

Slice 1 (P1). The Slice 1 definition of done item 5: "the nightly export imported into a fresh container brings back every part, version, data document and snapshot, and every cap minted before it is dead" (import is T35). Feeds T35 (import + drill), T36 (backup-layer status on Health), T59 (blob GC marks what exports reference), T113 (janitor rotates exports), T68 (doctor checks export freshness), T87 (S3 upload, P5).

## Scope

Data layout (PLAN §5c, verbatim):
```
/data/
  partifactory.db (+ -wal, -shm)   all metadata, grants, tokens, comments, per-part data
  blobs/ab/cd/<sha256>             content-addressed, write-once
  insights.db (+ -wal, -shm)       analytics, traces, janitor runs (§5g); its own writer
  logs/                            rotating zstd JSON segments: app/ and parts/<id>/ (§5h)
  parts/<id>/vol/<svc>/            backend volumes (§3f)
  backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite   hourly consistent VACUUM INTO copy (for non-atomic host tools)
  exports/partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst   nightly export, keep 7 (on by default)
```

Backup layers (verbatim table summary): **1. Host backups of `/data`** (the host's job: ZFS snapshots, rsync, restic; a non-atomic copy "must take `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite`, never the live `.db` file. Blobs are write-once, so any copy of `blobs/` is safe"); **2. `partifactory export`** (partifactory's job); **3. Optional upload** to S3-compatible storage (P5, T87).

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead: close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- **T34.a** — hourly consistent copy `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite` via `VACUUM INTO`.
- **T34.b** — `partifactory export`: archive format, full mode, `--parts-only`, `--encrypt` (age), `--include-insights`, `--include-secrets`.
- **T34.c** — the scheduled nightly export (on by default, keep 7), its config keys, metrics and same-disk detection.

Export format `partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst` (verbatim):
- `MANIFEST.json` (format version, created, binary version, counts, and a sha256 per entry);
- `db.sqlite`, a consistent `VACUUM INTO` copy checked with `PRAGMA integrity_check` (it reads a snapshot under WAL without blocking the writer);
- `blobs/<sha256>` for every blob referenced by any version, build, draft, data snapshot or asset;
- `parts/<id>/vol/<svc>/` for every backend volume, taken consistently (the service's export hook, or stop, copy, start) — the hook mechanism lands with backends (T102); this task leaves an extension point and exports existing volume directories when none run;
- `insights.db` only with `--include-insights`, and part secrets only with `--include-secrets`, which requires `--encrypt`.
- **Parts only** mode (`--parts-only`) writes part manifests, files, notes, titles, spaces by slug and tags as JSON instead of the DB. It has **no access records, tokens or people**.
- **Optional age encryption** (`--encrypt`, or always on in site config) to an age **recipient public key** (`[backup] age_recipient`), so the box never holds the decryption key.
- **Scheduled, on by default**: nightly to `/data/exports`, keep 7 (`backup.export_schedule`, `backup.export_dir`, `backup.export_keep`). Turning it off is an explicit key and shows as a warning on Health. The newest export's time and size are metrics.

## Not in scope

- `partifactory import`, the drill and the boot-epoch bump on import — T35.
- Per-part data snapshots (undo, not DR) — T77.
- Backend volume export hooks (`x-pf.export`, e.g. `pg_dump`) — T102.
- S3 upload of exports — T87 (P5).
- Rotation of old exports by the janitor beyond keep-N at write time — T113 registers the job (this task implements keep-N deletion inside the scheduled export; T113 adopts it as a janitor job).
- Health rows and doctor checks — T36, T68 (this task exposes the data: last export time, size, location, same-disk flag).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why `/data` + export, not git archive / Litestream / streaming sinks:* rejected in round 2 (§10): the owner wants no git or Gitea dependency for part content; Litestream v0.5 dropped age encryption; an async sink outbox on the core path was replaced by export + host backups (decision 17).
- *Why `VACUUM INTO`:* it produces a consistent single-file copy from a WAL snapshot without blocking the single writer.
- *Why age to a public recipient:* the box never holds the decryption identity; the identity lives offline in the password manager alongside the site config offline copy.
- *Why parts-only mode:* a file you can hand to someone else or keep somewhere less trusted; the honest cost is re-granting on import (T35's helper).
- An export written to the same filesystem as `/data` is "a convenience, not a backup": Health shows it amber, never green (T36), so record whether `export_dir` shares a device with `/data` (`st_dev` comparison).
- Blob set: walk the same reference set GC marks from (versions' `version_files`, `build_files`, `builds.log_hash`, `drafts`, `data_snapshots`, `assets`, unpruned `backend_images.tar_hash`), so export and GC agree on "referenced". Share the mark function with T59.
- Exports stream (tar → zstd → optional age) to a temp file, fsync, then rename; a partial export never appears under its final name.
- Exports must not include `backup/`, `exports/` or `logs/`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "An export taken during a write burst imports to an identical part set; a parts-only export contains no grants or tokens (schema test); a fresh install with no backup config runs the nightly export and keeps exactly 7 files".

- [ ] `partifactory export` during a sustained write burst completes without blocking writes (writer p99 unchanged within noise) and the archive's `db.sqlite` passes `PRAGMA integrity_check`.
- [ ] Every `MANIFEST.json` entry's sha256 matches its archive member; every referenced blob is present; no unreferenced blob is required.
- [ ] Importing it (T35) yields an identical part set (parts, versions, manifests, data docs, snapshots).
- [ ] `--parts-only` output contains no grants, tokens, sessions, passkeys, public links or people (schema test over the JSON).
- [ ] `--include-secrets` without `--encrypt` is refused; `--encrypt` output decrypts only with the matching age identity.
- [ ] `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite` is refreshed hourly and is always a complete, integrity-checked database.
- [ ] A fresh install with no `[backup]` config writes a nightly export to `/data/exports` and keeps exactly 7 files.
- [ ] Metrics `pf_export_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, `pf_export_last_bytes` exist.

## Tests

See subtasks for per-piece tests. End-to-end:
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/export_during_burst.rs::export_consistent_under_writes`: a writer loop commits versions and data docs while export runs; asserts integrity, manifest hashes, and that captured logs contain `event="export.finished" outcome="ok" entries=<n> bytes=<b>` and no part content.
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/parts_only_schema.rs::no_access_records`: parses the JSON and asserts the absence of every access/identity key.
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/nightly_default.rs::fresh_install_keeps_seven` (test clock advances 9 days).

## References

PLAN.md §5c Backups, recovery and self-provisioning (layers table, `partifactory export`, data layout), §5h Disk safety ("Scheduled exports keep 7"), §5e modelling decisions ("Every version kept" GC sources), §10 Round 2 rejected list, decision 17; Slice 1 definition of done item 5.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): An export taken during a write burst imports to an identical part set; a parts-only export contains no grants or tokens (schema test); a fresh install with no backup config runs the nightly export and keeps exactly 7 files
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T05: SQLite layer: read pool, single writer task, pragmas, embedded forward-only migrations
  - T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
  - T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
- Unblocks: 
  - T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report
  - T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
  - T68: `partifactory doctor`: config, DNS, ingress, certs, IdP, backup layers, disk, store caps, safe defaults
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
  - T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
  - T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
  - T87: Optional S3-compatible upload of scheduled exports, and import --from s3://
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T34.a: Hourly consistent DB copy `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite` via VACUUM INTO
  - T34.b: `partifactory export` archive: MANIFEST, db.sqlite, blobs, volumes, --parts-only, --encrypt (age)
  - T34.c: Scheduled nightly export on by default (keep 7), config keys, metrics, same-disk flag
acceptance_criteria: An export taken during a write burst imports to an identical part set; a parts-only export contains no grants or tokens (schema test); a fresh install with no backup config runs the nightly export and keeps exactly 7 files

title: T34.a: Hourly consistent DB copy `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite` via VACUUM INTO
description:
## Goal and why

Host backup tools that aren't atomic (rsync, restic, an appdata backup job) must never copy the live `partifactory.db` + WAL: the copy could be torn. An hourly consistent single-file copy gives them something safe to take. Atomic snapshots (ZFS) of the live WAL database are crash-consistent anyway; this layer is for everyone else.

## Scope

- Every hour (configurable, default `1h`), run `VACUUM INTO '/data/backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite.tmp'` on a read connection, then `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the copy, fsync, and atomically rename to `/data/backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite`.
- Never blocks the single writer (VACUUM INTO reads a WAL snapshot).
- On failure: keep the previous copy, log `event="backup.copy" outcome="failed" reason=...`, and expose `pf_backup_copy_last_success_timestamp_seconds`; T36 shows staleness.
- `insights.db` is not copied (losing it loses nothing anyone needs to restore).
- Register as a scheduled job via the job scheduler the janitor uses (T113 adopts it; until then a tokio interval task).
- Disk: the copy counts against the disk budget (T114); if the budget refuses writes, skip the copy and log it (never fill the disk with a backup).

## Not in scope

The export archive (T34.b), the schedule for exports (T34.c), host snapshot configuration (`backup.host_snapshots` is reported by T36/T68).

## Design notes and decisions

- Write to `.tmp` then rename so a reader never sees a partial file.
- Document in `docs/` (operator notes) that rsync users must exclude `partifactory.db*` and include `backup/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an hour (test clock), the copy exists, opens, and passes `integrity_check`.
- [ ] A copy taken while the writer commits 1,000 versions contains a prefix-consistent state (every version row has its `version_files`).
- [ ] A failed copy leaves the previous file intact and raises the metric staleness.

## Tests

- `pf_backup::copy::tests::vacuum_into_atomic_rename`.
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/hourly_copy.rs::consistent_under_writes`: asserts referential completeness in the copy; captured logs include `event="backup.copy" outcome="ok" bytes=..`.
- `::failure_keeps_previous` (inject an I/O error via a failing dir).

## References

PLAN.md §5c (data layout: `backup/partifactory-latest.sqlite`; layer 1 note about non-atomic copies).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T34.b: `partifactory export` archive: MANIFEST, db.sqlite, blobs, volumes, --parts-only, --encrypt (age)
description:
## Goal and why

One self-contained, host-portable file that restores a whole partifactory on any OCI host (T35), or a parts-only file safe to hand to someone else. It is the off-site and move-host path.

## Scope

CLI: `partifactory export [--out <path>] [--parts-only] [--encrypt] [--include-insights] [--include-secrets]`.

Archive `partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst` (ts = UTC `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`), members:
- `MANIFEST.json`: `{format_version: 1, created_at, binary_version, mode: "full"|"parts_only", counts: {parts, versions, blobs, data_docs, data_snapshots, volumes}, entries: {path: sha256}}`.
- `db.sqlite`: `VACUUM INTO` copy, then `PRAGMA integrity_check` must return `ok` (else abort).
- `blobs/<sha256>`: every blob referenced by any version, build, draft, data snapshot or asset (the GC mark set; share the function with T59).
- `parts/<id>/vol/<svc>/`: existing backend volume dirs; a hook trait `VolumeExporter` (default: stop-copy-start via the runner once T102 exists; no-op when no backends).
- `insights.db` only with `--include-insights`.
- Part secrets only with `--include-secrets`, which requires `--encrypt` (refuse otherwise with exit 2 and a message).
- `--parts-only`: instead of `db.sqlite`, write `parts/<id>/part.json` with manifests of every version, files (as blob refs, blobs included), agent notes, titles, description, tags, space by slug, author labels and timestamps, data docs and snapshots. **No access records, tokens or people** (no grants, public_links, sessions, passkeys, oauth_*, agent_connections, users beyond display labels on versions).
- `--encrypt` (or `[backup] always_encrypt = true`): pipe through age to `[backup] age_recipient` (a public key; not a secret). Output name gains `.age`.
- Streaming: tar → zstd (level 3, long window) → optional age → temp file in the target dir → fsync → rename.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 bad flags/config.

## Not in scope

Import (T35); scheduling and rotation (T34.c); real volume export hooks (T102).

## Design notes and decisions

- Read from a single WAL read snapshot so DB and blob set agree: compute the blob set from the `VACUUM INTO` copy, not from the live DB.
- Blobs are write-once, so they can be read live without locking.
- Secrets in exports are opt-in and always encrypted (decision on write-only secrets, §3f).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every manifest entry hash verifies; `db.sqlite` integrity ok.
- [ ] Parts-only JSON contains none of the forbidden keys (schema test).
- [ ] `--include-secrets` without `--encrypt` exits 2.
- [ ] Encrypted export decrypts only with the matching identity.
- [ ] Blob set equals the GC mark set on a fixture with versions, builds, drafts, snapshots, assets.

## Tests

- `pf_backup::export::tests::manifest_hashes_match`, `::blob_set_equals_gc_marks`, `::secrets_require_encrypt`.
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/parts_only_schema.rs::no_access_records` (walks all JSON keys against a deny list).
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/age_roundtrip.rs::decrypt_with_identity_only`.
- Logs: `event="export.started" mode=..`, `event="export.finished" outcome=ok entries=.. bytes=.. duration_ms=..`; assert canary part content never appears in logs.

## References

PLAN.md §5c "`partifactory export` writes …", "Parts only mode", "Optional age encryption"; §3f Secrets (export only with `--include-secrets --encrypt`); §5e GC sources.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

- [ ] Every manifest entry hash verifies; `db.sqlite` integrity ok.
- [ ] Parts-only JSON contains none of the forbidden keys (schema test).
- [ ] `--include-secrets` without `--encrypt` exits 2.
- [ ] Encrypted export decrypts only with the matching identity.

title: T34.c: Scheduled nightly export on by default (keep 7), config keys, metrics, same-disk flag
description:
## Goal and why

Nobody remembers to set up backups before they need one, so a fresh install with no backup config must already export nightly and keep a bounded number of files.

## Scope

- Config (`[backup]` in `site.toml`, all with defaults): `export_schedule` (default nightly, e.g. `"03:30"` UTC), `export_dir` (default `/data/exports`), `export_keep` (default 7), `age_recipient` (optional), `host_snapshots` (`on`/`off`/`unknown`, reported only).
- Turning the scheduled export off requires `[unsafe] nightly_export = "off"` (registered in the safe-defaults registry, T114); without it `config check` fails.
- After a successful export, delete the oldest exports in `export_dir` beyond `export_keep` (only files matching `partifactory-*.tar.zst[.age]`).
- Record in `kv`: `last_export_at`, `last_export_bytes`, `last_export_path`, `last_export_same_disk` (true when `export_dir` and `/data` share a device). Metrics: `pf_export_last_success_timestamp_seconds`, `pf_export_last_bytes`, `pf_export_same_disk`.
- On failure: log, keep older exports, and let T36 show amber (no export in 48 h).

## Not in scope

Health rendering (T36), alert webhook (T121), janitor adoption (T113), S3 upload (T87).

## Design notes and decisions

- Same disk = amber, never green: it's a convenience, not a backup (§5c).
- Rotation happens only after the new export is fully renamed into place, so there are never fewer than `keep` good files after day 7.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh install with no `[backup]` section produces one export per night and exactly 7 files after 9 days (test clock).
- [ ] `kv` and metrics reflect the newest export; the same-disk flag is true in the default layout.
- [ ] Removing the schedule without the `[unsafe]` key fails `config check`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-backup/tests/nightly_default.rs::fresh_install_keeps_seven`, `::rotation_only_after_success`, `::same_disk_detected`.
- `pf_config::tests::nightly_export_off_requires_unsafe`.
- Logs asserted: `event="export.scheduled" outcome=ok`, `event="export.rotated" deleted=2`.

## References

PLAN.md §5c ("Scheduled, on by default"), §5h ("Scheduled exports keep 7", safe defaults), §5d Health.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T34.b: `partifactory export` archive: MANIFEST, db.sqlite, blobs, volumes, --parts-only, --encrypt (age)

- [ ] A fresh install with no `[backup]` section produces one export per night and exactly 7 files after 9 days (test clock).

title: T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report
description:
## Goal and why

An export is only a backup if it restores. This task builds `partifactory import`, which brings a full export (or a parts-only one) back on any OCI host, and the **laptop-driven drill** that proves it monthly against a throwaway container on a different host, with an RTO target under 15 minutes.

The safety property: an import **bumps the boot epoch**, so no capability minted before the export (or before a rollback of the database) can ever come back to life. This is what makes "restore an old database" safe in a cap-in-the-path design.

Slice 1 (P1). Definition of done item 5: "Export and import round-trip: the nightly export imported into a fresh container brings back every part, version, data document and snapshot, and every cap minted before it is dead." Feeds M1 ("the drill restores everything on a second OCI host"), T93 (portability lane uses local exports + import), T68 (doctor reports the last drill).

## Scope

`partifactory import <file> [--parts-only-into <fresh /data>]` restores on any OCI host (PLAN §5c, verbatim steps):
1. verify every entry's hash against `MANIFEST.json`;
2. load `db.sqlite` into `/data` and run forward migrations;
3. write blobs (temp → fsync → rename);
4. **bump the boot epoch**, so caps minted before the export can never come back;
5. start serving. `/readyz` reports `importing=true` until blobs are verified.

- Refuses to import over a non-empty `/data` unless `--force` (and then moves the old DB aside, never deletes it).
- Encrypted exports: `--identity <age identity file>` (the identity lives offline; never stored on the box).
- "Sessions and OAuth tokens in the export are valid again, which is the point of a full export. Refresh tokens issued after the export point are unknown, so those agents sign in again, and **refresh-reuse detection is suspended for 24 h after an import** to avoid mass family revocations." Record `kv.import_at` so T43's reuse detection can read it.
- **Parts-only import** "recreates every part with its full version history, author labels and timestamps, in a fresh DB. Access must then be re-granted and agents reconnected." Users referenced by author labels are created as placeholder records only as needed for FKs (status `disabled`, no credentials), or mapped onto existing accounts when importing into a DB that has people.
- **Regrant-by-name helper**: "A helper proposes grants by matching stored audience names (groups by name, people by username or email), and the admin applies them on one screen." In Slice 1 the helper is a CLI report + apply command (`partifactory import regrant --plan` / `--apply plan.json`); the one-screen UI can come with the admin area later.
- **Drill script** `scripts/drill.sh` (runs from a laptop, not CI, "because the CI system (and its secrets) may be on the host that died"): takes the newest export, the image and CLI from release assets, and site config from the offline copy; imports into a throwaway container on a different OCI host (`DOCKER_HOST=ssh://...`); runs the e2e suite against it; writes `{ok, rto_s, failures}` to `backup/drills/<ts>.json` on the restored instance (or uploads it via an admin CLI call), which the server exports as `pf_last_drill_ok` and `pf_last_drill_age_s`.
- **Moving checklist** documented in `docs/ops/moving.md` (verbatim steps from §5c "Moving to another host", including: with the Cloudflare adapter, re-point the tunnel, then **rotate the tunnel connector token** and delete the old host's connections so a zombie connector can't take traffic; check `/readyz` directly; run `doctor`; re-enable host snapshots).

## Not in scope

- Producing exports — T34.
- The e2e suite itself — T24 harness, T97 and others; the drill only runs it.
- Backend volume restore hooks — T102 (import restores the directories; hooks are its concern).
- The doctor check for drill freshness — T68.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why bump the boot epoch:* caps are stateless HMAC tokens verified against in-memory epochs; a restored DB has older epochs, so without a floor bump a revoked cap could verify again. Cost: one silent re-grant per open tab.
- *Why the drill runs from a laptop:* avoids circular DR dependencies (review D5); the release assets on the passive mirror mean the drill doesn't depend on the CI host.
- *Why suspend reuse detection for 24 h:* after a restore, many agents present refresh tokens the DB considers already used (rotated after the export); revoking all their families would be a mass outage.
- Migrations are forward-only and run inside a transaction; the drill against a production-shaped export is what tests them (§5d Maintenance).
- Identity DR: IdP users are keyed by `(issuer, sub)`; if the IdP is restored the same subs come back; otherwise the regrant helper rebinds by email/username as people re-enrol (§5c).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Drill imports the newest export into a throwaway container on another OCI host in < 15 min and the e2e suite passes; the drill result appears in /metrics".

- [ ] Import of a full export restores every part, version, data doc and data snapshot (row-for-row equality on a fixture, blob hashes verified).
- [ ] A cap minted before the export returns 404/302 after import (boot epoch bumped); a fresh `/grant` works.
- [ ] A corrupted member (flipped byte) aborts the import before anything is written to `/data`.
- [ ] `/readyz` reports `importing=true` until blob verification completes.
- [ ] Refresh-token reuse within 24 h of import does not revoke the family; after 24 h it does.
- [ ] Parts-only import recreates history and labels; no grants exist afterwards; the regrant plan lists proposed grants by name.
- [ ] The drill finishes in < 15 min, the e2e suite passes, `backup/drills/<ts>.json` is written, and `/metrics` shows `pf_last_drill_ok 1` and `pf_last_drill_age_s`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-backup/tests/roundtrip.rs::full_export_import_identical`: fixture with parts, versions, builds, data docs, snapshots; compares table contents; logs asserted: `event="import.verify" outcome=ok entries=..`, `event="import.boot_epoch_bump" new_floor=..`, `event="import.finished"`.
- `::old_caps_dead_after_import`: mints a cap, exports, imports, requests `/c/<cap>/` and expects the navigation → 302 / subresource → 401 behaviour, with `event="cap.verify" outcome="stale_boot"`.
- `::corrupted_member_aborts` (no writes to target dir).
- `::reuse_detection_suspended_24h` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/parts_only_import.rs::history_kept_no_grants` + `::regrant_plan_matches_names`.
- Drill: `scripts/drill.sh` emits a JSON report; CI runs a local variant (`drill.sh --local`, same host, two containers) nightly, non-gating, keeping server logs under `target/e2e-logs/drill/`.

## References
