title: T35.a: `partifactory import`: full and parts-only restore, manifest verification, boot-epoch bump, importing=true readiness, reuse-detection suspension
description:
## Goal and why

An export is only a backup if it restores. `partifactory import` brings a full export (or a parts-only one) back on any OCI host, and does the one thing that makes restoring a cap-in-the-path system safe: it **bumps the boot epoch**, so no capability minted before the export (or before a database rollback) can ever come back to life. This subtask is the command itself; the regrant helper is T35.b and the drill is T35.c. Slice 1 definition of done item 5 ("the nightly export imported into a fresh container brings back every part, version, data document and snapshot, and every cap minted before it is dead") is proven here.

## Scope

`partifactory import <file> [--identity <age identity file>] [--force] [--parts-only-into <fresh /data>]` (PLAN §5c, verbatim steps):
1. verify every entry's hash against `MANIFEST.json` (a corrupted member aborts before anything is written to `/data`);
2. load `db.sqlite` into `/data` and run forward migrations (T05);
3. write blobs (temp → fsync → verify → rename, through the T07 store);
4. **bump the boot epoch** (`epochs['boot']`, T15 `bump_boot`), so caps minted before the export can never come back;
5. start serving. `/readyz` reports `importing=true` (503) until blobs are verified (T36 reads the flag).

- Refuses to import over a non-empty `/data` unless `--force`, and then moves the old DB aside (`partifactory.db.pre-import-<ts>`), never deletes it.
- Encrypted exports (`.age`): `--identity` points at the age identity file; the identity lives offline and is never stored on the box.
- Sessions and OAuth tokens in a full export are valid again (the point of a full export). Refresh tokens issued after the export point are unknown, so those agents sign in again; **refresh-reuse detection is suspended for 24 h after an import** (record `kv.import_at`; T43.a reads it) to avoid mass family revocations.
- **Parts-only import** recreates every part with its full version history, author labels and timestamps in a fresh DB. Users referenced only by author labels are created as placeholder records as needed for FKs (`status = 'disabled'`, no credentials, `in_audience = 0`), or mapped onto existing accounts (by `(issuer, sub)`, then username, then email) when importing into a DB that has people. No grants, tokens or sessions exist afterwards (that is the honest cost; T35.b proposes grants).
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 bad flags, 3 verification failed (nothing written).
- Logs: `event="import.verify" outcome=ok entries=<n>`, `event="import.boot_epoch_bump" new_floor=<n>`, `event="import.finished" mode=full|parts_only duration_ms=<ms>`; never part content.

## Not in scope

The regrant-by-name plan and apply (T35.b); the laptop drill, its report and metrics, and the moving checklist (T35.c); producing exports (T34); backend volume restore hooks (T102).

## Design notes and decisions

- Why bump the boot epoch: caps are stateless HMAC tokens verified against in-memory epochs; a restored DB has older epochs, so without a floor bump a revoked cap could verify again. Cost: one silent re-grant per open tab.
- Why suspend reuse detection: after a restore, many agents present refresh tokens the DB considers already used (rotated after the export); revoking all their families would be a mass outage.
- Migrations are forward-only and run inside a transaction; the drill (T35.c) against a production-shaped export is what tests them against real data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Import of a full export restores every part, version, data doc and data snapshot (row-for-row equality on a fixture; blob hashes verified).
- [ ] A cap minted before the export returns 302 (navigation) / 401 (subresource) after import; a fresh `/grant` works.
- [ ] A corrupted member (flipped byte) aborts with exit 3 before anything is written to `/data`.
- [ ] `/readyz` reports `importing=true` (503) until blob verification completes, then 200.
- [ ] Refresh-token reuse within 24 h of import does not revoke the family; after 24 h it does.
- [ ] Parts-only import recreates history and author labels; no grants, tokens or sessions exist afterwards.
- [ ] `--force` is required over a non-empty `/data` and preserves the old DB file.

title: T35.b: Regrant-by-name helper after a parts-only import (`import regrant --plan` / `--apply`)
description:
## Goal and why

A parts-only export carries no access records, tokens or people, so after importing one "access must then be re-granted and agents reconnected" (PLAN §5c). This helper makes that honest cost small: it proposes grants by matching the audience names stored with the parts (groups by name, people by username or email) against the people and groups the new deployment knows, and the admin applies the plan in one step. In Slice 1 it is a CLI plan/apply; the one-screen UI is G07.

## Scope

- `partifactory import regrant --plan [--out plan.json]`: reads the stored audience labels of every imported part (space slug, owner label, group names, person usernames/emails recorded in the parts-only `part.json`), matches them against `users`/`groups` in the current DB (exact `(issuer, sub)`, then username, then email; groups by name), and writes a plan: `[{part, proposed: [{subject, role, matched_by}], unmatched: [label]}]`. Nothing is written to `grants`.
- `partifactory import regrant --apply plan.json`: applies the plan as ordinary inward grants (`set_grant`, T26), writing one `audit` row per grant with `actor = 'system'` and `request_id`; prints what was applied and what stayed unmatched. Admin-only (host console). Idempotent: re-applying the same plan changes nothing.
- Owner mapping: an imported part whose owner label matches a current person gets `owner_user_id` set to them; otherwise it stays with the admin, listed in the plan under `unmatched`.
- Agents are never reconnected by the helper (a person connects every agent once, by design); the plan output ends with the list of agent names that were connected before, so people know whom to reconnect.
- Logs: `event="import.regrant" phase=plan|apply parts=<n> grants=<n> unmatched=<n>` (labels only, never content).

## Not in scope

The import itself (T35.a); the one-screen regrant UI (G07, which renders this same plan); invites for people who don't exist yet (T94).

## Design notes and decisions

- Plan then apply (two commands, a reviewable JSON in between) because grants are a security boundary: nothing is granted without the admin seeing the proposal.
- Matching by `(issuer, sub)` first keeps IdP-restored households exact; username/email matching is a fallback for a changed IdP (§5c Identity and DR).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fixture (3 parts, 2 people, 1 group, one unknown person) `--plan` proposes exactly the matching grants and lists the unknown label as unmatched.
- [ ] `--apply` creates those grants with audit rows; re-applying is a no-op; the asker can open the part on the next request.
- [ ] No grant is ever created by `--plan`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-backup/tests/regrant.rs::plan_matches_names`, `::apply_creates_grants_and_audit`, `::apply_idempotent`, `::plan_writes_nothing`; logs asserted for both phases.

## References

PLAN.md §5c "Parts-only import … A helper proposes grants by matching stored audience names (groups by name, people by username or email), and the admin applies them on one screen"; §5c Identity and DR; §3a audience ladder; §5e `grants`, `audit`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T35 (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T35.a (the parts-only import it reads from).

title: T35.c: Laptop drill script + report and pf_last_drill_* metrics, moving checklist and backup operator notes
description:
## Goal and why

A backup is proven by a restore nobody is watching. The monthly **drill runs from a laptop, not CI**, "because the CI system (and its secrets) may be on the host that died": it takes the newest export, the image and CLI from the release assets (T37) and site config from the offline copy, imports into a throwaway container on a different OCI host, runs the e2e suite, and reports `{ok, rto_s, failures}` so the server can show it. RTO target < 15 minutes. The M1 done-when ("the drill restores everything on a second OCI host in < 15 min") and the T35 acceptance test live here.

## Scope

Steps: pull the image by digest, start a throwaway stack from `deploy/compose.yaml` with `_FILE` secrets, `partifactory import` (T35.a), wait for `/readyz` without `importing`, run the e2e suite that exists (at minimum the T24.b harness self-test and `login_roundtrip`; `communal_pixel_editor` joins when T97 lands) against the restored instance, then tear down.

The import command (T35.a); the regrant helper (T35.b); the release pipeline that publishes the assets (T37.a); the e2e suite's own contents (T24.b, T97).

title: T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
description:
## Goal and why

Keep group membership (and therefore access) current with **any** OIDC provider, without a vendor API: read the `groups` claim at login, re-read it every 15 minutes per active session through an OIDC refresh-token grant, end a session the IdP says is gone, and bump capability epochs for every part whose effective access changed. Also own partifactory's local `pf-*` groups.

Why:
- Access in partifactory is decided per request through caps that verify without the DB; revocation stays instant only if membership changes bump epochs (`epochs['part:<id>']`).
- Generic OIDC is the baseline (decision 23); the Authentik adapter's 60 s poll (T92) is an optional faster directory. With the generic directory, removals take up to 15 minutes (or 12 h without refresh tokens) instead of about 1, an accepted portability trade-off (§5f).
- **Fail open on an unreachable IdP**: an IdP outage must not lock the household out of what they could already see. A definite "this person is gone" (`invalid_grant`) is not an outage, and fails closed.
- In Slice 1; required by the policy engine (T26), `/grant` (T27) and the Authentik adapter (T92).

## Scope

- Implementation of the `Directory` trait (T19) in `pf-auth` as `ClaimsDirectory`:
  - At login (T24.a): record groups from the configured claim (`[idp] groups_claim`), `groups.source='claim'`, `group_members` rows, `users.in_audience` from `[idp] audience_group`.
  - **Re-read every 15 minutes per active session**: a background scheduler takes sessions with `idp_checked_at` older than 15 min and recent `last_used_at`, decrypts `sessions.idp_refresh_enc` (encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY`), performs the refresh-token grant, reads the new ID token/userinfo groups claim, stores the rotated refresh token re-encrypted, sets `idp_checked_at`.
  - Refresh returns **`invalid_grant`** (person disabled or removed): end that session (`revoked_at`), bump `epochs['minter:sess:<id>']`, mark the user `status` as appropriate only if the IdP says so (user record kept), audit `session.revoke reason=invalid_grant`.
  - Refresh fails because the IdP is **unreachable** (network/5xx/timeout): keep last-known membership, set a **stale** flag (`kv` key `directory.stale_since` + per-session flag), **never bump an epoch**, and raise the degraded indicator; after **10 minutes** of unreachability an ops alert condition fires (consumed by T36/T121).
  - IdPs that issue no refresh tokens: sessions are 12 h (T24.a), so membership is re-read at least that often (on next login).
- **Membership diff → epoch bumps**: compute the diff of (user, group) membership; for every part whose grants (or whose space's grants) mention an affected user or group, bump `epochs['part:<id>']` (in-memory mirror + SQLite). Also bump for `everyone-signed-in` changes (audience membership).
- **Local `pf-*` groups**: partifactory's own groups (`groups.source='local'`, `managed=1`, name `pf-%`), membership changes take effect instantly (same diff → epoch bump path). Creation of groups is admin-only (UI in T120 / T94 "Make a group for this"); this task provides the store and API (`create_local_group`, `add_member`, `remove_member`) with the CHECKs from the DDL:
```sql
CREATE TABLE groups (
  name       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  source     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('claim','idp_api','local')),
  idp_id     TEXT UNIQUE,
  managed    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (managed IN (0,1)),
  synced_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  CHECK (managed = 0 OR name LIKE 'pf-%'),
  CHECK (source <> 'local' OR managed = 1)
) STRICT;
```
- Metrics: `pf_directory_refresh_total{outcome}`, `pf_directory_stale` gauge, `pf_epoch_bumps_total{reason}`.

## Not in scope

- Authentik API poll (T92); policy evaluation itself (T26); UI for groups (T120, T94); invites (T94); ops-alert webhook delivery (T121) and the Health page (T36), which display the stale/degraded state.

## Design notes and decisions

- Refresh-token re-read (not a vendor directory API) keeps the default vendor-free; the refresh token is stored encrypted, never logged.
- "A failed poll or re-read changes nothing" (§5e hot-path rules): no epoch bumps on errors, only on definite diffs.
- Cached membership is in memory; the 15-minute re-read refreshes it; local groups change in place.
- Bumping per affected part (not global) keeps unrelated tabs from re-granting.
- Test clock: the scheduler takes an injectable clock so the 15-minute and 10-minute timers are testable.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Removing a user from a Dex group fails their next part request after the next re-read (test clock); deleting the user ends the session on `invalid_grant`; with the IdP down, existing sessions keep working and no epoch is bumped".

- [ ] Groups from the claim are recorded at login; claim name comes from config.
- [ ] After removal from a Dex group and one re-read (advanced test clock), the user's next request to a part granted only via that group is denied (cap rejected for stale epoch, re-grant refused).
- [ ] Deleting the user in Dex → next re-read gets `invalid_grant` → session revoked, minter epoch bumped, audited.
- [ ] IdP down: sessions keep working, membership marked stale, zero epoch bumps; degraded indicator set; after 10 min the alert condition is raised.
- [ ] Local `pf-*` group membership changes bump affected part epochs immediately; CHECK constraints reject a local group not named `pf-*`.

## Tests

Decision 23. dag2.py T25.

title: T77: Per-part data snapshots of shared docs: on by default (daily keep 7), roll back, reset, JSON download
description:
## Goal and why

A part's shared data (`window.storage` shared keys, later `db` documents) is written by many hands: the agent, signed-in viewers, and on a Can-contribute link, anonymous guests. A bad write — an agent bug, a viewer mistake, a vandalised pixel board — needs a one-action undo. Data snapshots are that undo: **for undoing a bad write, not for disaster recovery** (exports, T34, do DR).

They are **on by default** because "nobody remembers to opt in before they need it" (adopted in round 2b, decision 26). The pixel-board test (T97) ends with the admin rolling back one snapshot; T95's "Can contribute" switch takes a snapshot first so there is always a "before the guests" point; T96's `part_data` agent ops `snapshot_list`, `snapshot_restore` and `reset` are the agent face of this backend.

Slice 1 (P1), on the S1 critical path (T62 → T77 → T96 → T95 → T97, and T77 → T113 → T114 → T115).

## Scope

Schema (from T06, verbatim):
```sql
-- Per-part data snapshots: ON by default (daily, keep 7), for undoing a bad write (not disaster recovery).
-- A part with no row uses the default; a row exists only once someone changes it.
CREATE TABLE data_snapshot_policies (
  part_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  mode        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'daily' CHECK (mode IN ('off','daily','hourly')),  -- daily keep 7, hourly keep 48
  keep        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 7,
  expire_days INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 90,           -- stop after N days unopened; keep the last one
  set_by      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- user:<id> | conn:<id> (agents may request at create)
  set_at      INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE data_snapshots (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  taken_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reason     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled' CHECK (reason IN ('scheduled','contribute','before_restore','before_reset')),  -- only 'scheduled' counts against keep
  blob_hash  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),   -- canonical JSON of the part's shared data_docs
  docs       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  bytes      INTEGER NOT NULL
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX data_snapshots_part ON data_snapshots(part_id, taken_at DESC);
```
`data_docs` rows with `scope = 'shared'` (owner `''`) are what is snapshotted.

Behaviour (PLAN §5c, verbatim where quoted):
- "**on by default**: `daily`, keep 7, starting the first time a part stores data. Nobody is asked." Switch off per part (Details, later UI) or an agent sets `snapshots: "off"` at create (`part_create {snapshots: daily|hourly|off}`, default `daily`); `hourly` (keep 48) is the other option. A policy row is written only on an explicit change.
- "stored as blobs (canonical JSON of the part's documents), and skipped on days when the data didn't change, so an idle part costs nothing new" — compare the canonical JSON hash with the latest snapshot; skip if equal.
- "it stops after N days (default 90) without the part being opened, and **after that keeps the single most recent snapshot** until the part is deleted and leaves the 30-day bin" — needs a "last opened" signal: the content listener's entry-document serve (or `/grant` mint) updates `parts`-side last-opened (store in `kv`-like column or a small `part_opened` cache flushed to DB; record the choice).
- "a snapshot is the part's **shared** `data_docs`: personal docs are each person's own and never rolled back by someone else".
- **Roll back**: "snapshots the current data (`reason: before_restore`), replaces the shared docs with the snapshot's (new `rev`s), and emits a `data.changed` for every affected key, so open pages repaint" — keys present now but absent in the snapshot are deleted (`op: "delete"`), keys whose value differs are set (`op: "set"`), unchanged keys keep their rev and emit nothing. Event `data.changed {key, op, by}` with `by` = the acting person/agent.
- **Reset**: snapshot first (`before_reset`), then delete every shared doc, one `data.changed {op: "delete"}` per key.
- "switching a public link to Can contribute takes one first (§3a). These on-demand snapshots (and the ones before a roll back or reset) don't count against `keep`" — expose `take_snapshot(part, reason)` for T95.
- **Download the data as JSON** any time: an endpoint/service function returning the canonical JSON of current shared docs or of a snapshot (UI wiring later; agents get it through `part_data list`).
- "**they don't cover backend volumes**, which folder backups and exports do (§3f)."
- Scheduling: one scheduler pass (hourly) takes due snapshots for parts with policy daily/hourly whose data changed; pruning beyond `keep` among `reason='scheduled'` and the 90-day idle rule run as janitor jobs (T113 registers them; this task provides the functions).
- Writes go through the single writer; restore and reset are atomic (one transaction for the doc replacement, events emitted after commit).
- Respect the disk budget: snapshots are writes and are refused under `storage_full` (T114) except that roll back/reset must still work? Decision: roll back writes a `before_restore` snapshot, which is a new blob; under `storage_full` the restore is refused with `storage_full` (reads and deletes continue; reset of data is a delete but also snapshots first — refuse too, and say so in the hint).

## Not in scope

- `part_data` op fields and `/_rt` storage ops — T96 (this task is the service they call).
- Share-sheet controls Roll back data, Reset data, Freeze — T95.
- The Details UI switch — T120 (Details sheet, after Slice 1).
- Janitor scheduling framework — T113.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why not personal docs:* personal state is each person's own; another person must never roll it back.
- *Why on-demand snapshots outside `keep`:* so an admin's "before the guests" point isn't pruned by seven days of scheduled snapshots.
- *Why skip unchanged days:* bounded cost for idle parts; with the 90-day idle stop and keep-the-last-one rule the store is capped (§5h row "Data snapshots: daily keep 7 / hourly keep 48; the last one kept after 90 days idle").
- Canonical JSON: sorted keys, `{v:1, part_id, docs: [{collection, doc_id, data, rev, updated_at, updated_by}]}`; use JCS like manifests.
- Snapshot blobs are part blobs, referenced from `data_snapshots.blob_hash`, so GC (T59) and export (T34) keep them.
- Open tabs repaint because roll back emits per-key `data.changed` (the final round chose per-key events over one bulk event, F12).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A part that never touched its settings has daily snapshots; a bad shared-data write is undone from the snapshot in one action and an open tab repaints; personal docs are untouched by a roll back; switching a part off stops new snapshots; after expiry exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin".

- [ ] No policy row → daily snapshots begin after the first shared write; unchanged days write nothing.
- [ ] `hourly` keeps 48; `daily` keeps 7 scheduled snapshots; on-demand ones are not pruned by keep.
- [ ] Roll back: one call, new revs, a `data.changed` per affected key only; a subscribed tab repaints.
- [ ] Personal docs unchanged by roll back and reset.
- [ ] `off` stops new snapshots (existing ones remain until pruned by the janitor rules).
- [ ] After 90 days unopened, exactly one snapshot remains, until the part is purged from the bin.
- [ ] JSON download equals the canonical form.

## Tests

- `pf_backup::snapshots::tests::skip_unchanged_day`, `::keep_counts_only_scheduled`, `::canonical_json_stable` (golden), `::idle_keeps_last_one` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-backup/tests/rollback.rs::rollback_emits_per_key_events`: seeds shared and personal docs, writes a bad value, restores; asserts revs, events (`event="data.changed" key=.. op=set by=..` in the events table and captured logs `event="snapshot.restore" outcome=ok keys_changed=3`), personal docs untouched.
- `::reset_snapshots_first_then_deletes`.
- e2e (in T97's harness): open a tab, roll back via the backend, assert repaint within 1 s; artifacts under `target/e2e-logs/snapshot_rollback/`.

## References

PLAN.md §5c "Per-part data", "Data snapshots" (bullets), §3a "Can contribute" (snapshot on switch, roll back, reset), §5e `data_snapshot_policies`, `data_snapshots`, `data_docs`, §5h retention row, §10 Final round F12, decision 26; docs/agent-contract.md `part_data`.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A part that never touched its settings has daily snapshots; a bad shared-data write is undone from the snapshot in one action and an open tab repaints; personal docs are untouched by a roll back; switching a part off stops new snapshots; after expiry exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
- Unblocks: 
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
acceptance_criteria: A part that never touched its settings has daily snapshots; a bad shared-data write is undone from the snapshot in one action and an open tab repaints; personal docs are untouched by a roll back; switching a part off stops new snapshots; after expiry exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin

title: T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
description:
## Goal and why

The admin needs one place that says whether the box is healthy, and the deploy gate (T37 `partifactory deploy`) needs a readiness probe that only fails when the product is actually broken. Two rules shape it:

1. **Readiness ignores the IdP.** "IdP reachability, the directory poll and backup freshness are degraded indicators, not readiness: when the IdP is down, existing sessions, caps and agent refresh tokens keep working and only new sign-ins fail." *Why:* tying readiness to the IdP would roll back deploys and show the maintenance page exactly when the product is fine.
2. **Everything an alert would say is already on the page.** The optional ops webhook (T121) only mirrors Health rows, so nothing depends on the webhook.

Slice 1 (P1). Definition of done item 6: "the Health page shows each [store], the backup layers and the disk budget; no `[unsafe]` key is set". Feeds T37 (health-gated deploy), T121, T68, T114.

## Scope

Endpoints on the ops listener `:9090` (local network only, never routed through the ingress) — `/healthz` skeleton exists from T18:
- `/healthz`: process up (200).
- `/readyz`: 200 only if **DB writable** (a write probe through the writer, e.g. bump a `kv` heartbeat), **blob store OK** (put/has/get of a tiny probe blob, or a stat of the blob root + free-space check), **disk headroom > 5 %**; plus `importing=true` → 503 until blob verification completes (T35). Body: JSON `{ready, checks: [{name, ok, detail}], degraded: [...]}`. Never includes the IdP.

Admin Health page on the workspace (`/admin/health`, admin only, behind the T28 admin pin; reading it needs no step-up):
- `/readyz` checks.
- **Degraded indicators**: IdP reachability (discovery fetch age/result), directory staleness (last successful claims re-read / poll; T25 marks `stale`), backup freshness.
- **Backup layers** (§5c): layer 1 host snapshots as **on / off / unknown** from `backup.host_snapshots`; layer 2 the age and size of the newest export, its location, and whether it's on the same filesystem as `/data`. "An export on the same disk as `/data` shows amber, never green." "No export in 48 h is amber too." Layer 3 (S3) "not configured".
- **Disk**: total use, naming the biggest spaces and parts; once T114 lands, the disk budget and each store's size against its cap (rows reserved now: show size even before caps exist).
- **Quota hits** (from T33), **error-rate spikes** (5xx rate over the last hour from metrics), **version**, **last drill** (`pf_last_drill_ok`, age, from T35), **break-glass uses** (from T28 audit), **any safe default switched off** (from the T114 registry; until then, the `[unsafe]` table contents).
- **Runtime log levels**: change the log level filter at runtime from the admin area (folded here per §6a "runtime log levels (T36)"); audited.
- Stockroom styling basic: a table of rows with status chip (ok / amber / red, always with an icon + words, never colour only).

Every condition the ops-alert webhook (T121) will cover must already show as a row: disk budget at 80 %, any store at 80 % of its cap, no export in 48 h, the build worker or a backend crash-looping, the IdP unreachable for 10 min.

Metrics (if not already in T18): `pf_ready`, `pf_idp_reachable`, `pf_directory_stale_seconds`, `pf_disk_free_ratio`.

## Not in scope

- Disk budget enforcement and store caps — T114 (this page renders them).
- The webhook — T121.
- Full Insights pages — T108.
- `doctor` — T68 (shares the check functions; put checks in a `pf-janitor`/`pf-obs` `health` module both use).

## Design notes and decisions

- One `HealthCheck` trait (`name`, `kind: readiness | degraded | info`, `run() -> Status{level, detail}`) so `/readyz`, the page, `doctor` and the webhook share one implementation.
- Readiness probes must be cheap (< 50 ms) since deploy polls them.
- Failing open on an unreachable IdP is a deliberate decision (§3a): outages must not lock the household out.
- Page is admin-only: the Health page reveals sizes of spaces and part names, which is admin information.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "IdP down -> /readyz still 200 and a degraded row; no export in 48 h -> amber; every condition the ops-alert webhook (T121) will cover already shows as a Health row".

- [ ] With the IdP unreachable, `/readyz` is 200 and Health shows a degraded IdP row.
- [ ] DB unwritable, blob store unreadable, or disk headroom ≤ 5 % → `/readyz` 503 with the failing check named.
- [ ] No export in 48 h → amber; export on the same disk → amber, never green.
- [ ] Rows exist for: disk budget, each store vs cap, export age, build worker crash-loop, backend crash-loop (placeholder until P2a), IdP unreachable ≥ 10 min.
- [ ] Log level change at runtime takes effect without restart and writes an audit row.
- [ ] Non-admin gets 403 on `/admin/health` (PLAN §7: an IdP-admin user still gets 403; aligned across the admin area, G01).

## Tests

- `pf_obs::health::tests::readyz_ignores_idp`, `::disk_headroom_threshold`, `::importing_not_ready`.
- `crates/partifactory/tests/health_page.rs::rows_cover_alert_conditions`: a table-driven test listing T121's conditions, asserting each maps to a Health row id (keeps T36/T121 in sync).
- Integration with a stopped Dex: `idp_down_readyz_200_degraded_row`; captured logs `event="health.check" name="idp" outcome="degraded"`.
- `::export_amber_when_stale_or_same_disk` (test clock).
- e2e: admin opens Health; screenshot kept under `target/e2e-logs/health_page/`.

## References

PLAN.md §5d Health and alerting, §5c (doctor and the Health page report which layers are active; same disk amber), §5h (store sizes, `[unsafe]`), §4a.6 Admin (Health), §3a (fail open on an unreachable IdP), §6a notes ("runtime log levels (T36)"); Slice 1 definition of done item 6.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): IdP down -> /readyz still 200 and a degraded row; no export in 48 h -> amber; every condition the ops-alert webhook (T121) will cover already shows as a Health row
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T18: Logs + metrics: redacted JSON tracing, Prometheus on :9090 behind PF_METRICS_TOKEN, /healthz, /readyz skeleton
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass
- Unblocks: 
  - T121: Optional ops-alert webhook (off by default): HMAC-signed `{alert, severity, detail, at}`
  - T37: Deliverable: amd64 OCI image + deploy/compose.yaml + env contract + `partifactory deploy` with auto rollback
  - T68: `partifactory doctor`: config, DNS, ingress, certs, IdP, backup layers, disk, store caps, safe defaults
  - T114: Disk budget (warn 80 %, storage_full at 95 %), per-store caps on Health, and the [unsafe] safe-defaults registry
acceptance_criteria: IdP down -> /readyz still 200 and a degraded row; no export in 48 h -> amber; every condition the ops-alert webhook (T121) will cover already shows as a Health row

title: T121: Optional ops-alert webhook (off by default): HMAC-signed `{alert, severity, detail, at}`
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory sends people no notifications, by design (decision 27): no web push, no email, no chat bot. The **only push** is an optional webhook for the admin about operational trouble, off by default, so ntfy, Hermes or anything that accepts a JSON POST can relay it. The Health page always shows the same conditions, so nothing depends on the webhook.

After Slice 1 (P1, split from T36). Feeds M1.

## Scope

- Config: `[alerts] webhook_url` (unset by default → nothing is ever sent); secret `PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (env or `PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_FILE`), required if `webhook_url` is set (`config check` fails otherwise).
- Payload (verbatim): HMAC-signed JSON `{alert, severity, detail, at}`. Signature header `X-PF-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)>` plus `X-PF-Timestamp`; documented in `docs/alerts.md` so any consumer can verify. `detail` never contains part content, tokens or secrets (ids and numbers only).
- Conditions (verbatim): "the disk budget at 80 %, any store at 80 % of its cap, no export in 48 h, the build worker or a backend crash-looping, the IdP unreachable 10 min". Alert names: `disk_budget_80`, `store_cap_80` (detail names the store), `export_stale_48h`, `build_worker_crashloop`, `backend_crashloop` (detail names the part id; fires once backends exist, T110), `idp_unreachable_10m`.
- Edge-triggered with state in `kv` (alert state): one POST when a condition starts, one `severity: "resolved"` POST when it clears; no repeats while it persists (optional daily reminder off by default). Retries with backoff (3 attempts), then logged as failed and shown on Health.
- Severity: `warning` (80 % thresholds, export stale), `critical` (crash-loops, IdP 10 min), `resolved`.
- The URL is site config only; never set by agents or via an API (no SSRF surface beyond the admin's own target).
- Evaluated by the same `HealthCheck` set as T36, on a 1-minute tick.

## Not in scope

The checks themselves and the Health page (T36); store caps and the disk budget (T114); agent event webhooks (T123).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why one generic webhook:* every owned channel is another integration to run and another place a title could leak (§4 "No notifications for people").
- *Why share checks with Health:* guarantees "with it unset, Health shows the same rows".
- Crash-loop definition: ≥ 3 builder child crashes (`builder_crashed`) within 10 minutes, or (backends) ≥ 5 restarts in 10 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "With the webhook set, each condition produces exactly one signed POST; with it unset, nothing is sent and Health shows the same rows".

- [ ] Each of the six conditions, induced in a test, yields exactly one POST with a valid signature; clearing it yields one `resolved` POST.
- [ ] Unset `webhook_url` → zero outbound requests (asserted with a recording server) and identical Health rows.
- [ ] `webhook_url` without the secret fails `config check` naming `PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- [ ] Payloads contain no canary content.

## Tests

- `pf_obs::alerts::tests::edge_triggered_once`, `::signature_verifies` (golden vector), `::resolved_sent_once`.
- `crates/partifactory/tests/alerts.rs::each_condition_one_post` with a local HTTP sink; captured logs `event="alert.sent" alert="disk_budget_80" outcome=ok`.
- `::unset_sends_nothing`.

## References

PLAN.md §4 "The only push: optional ops alerts for the admin", §5d Health and alerting, §5f table row "Ops alerts", §5b env contract (`PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), decision 27.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): With the webhook set, each condition produces exactly one signed POST; with it unset, nothing is sent and Health shows the same rows
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
  - T114: Disk budget (warn 80 %, storage_full at 95 %), per-store caps on Health, and the [unsafe] safe-defaults registry
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- In P1 five conditions are induced in tests; `backend_crashloop` is added by T110 (P2a), which depends on this task.
- One webhook signature format for ops alerts and agent webhooks (T123): `X-PF-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256(secret, t + "." + body)>`, one signer helper in `pf-obs`, documented once in `docs/webhooks.md` (T123 and this task both link it).
- Alert names: `idp_unreachable_10m`, `disk_budget_80`, `store_cap_80:<store>`, `export_stale_48h`, `build_worker_crashloop`, `backend_crashloop`.
acceptance_criteria: With the webhook set, each condition produces exactly one signed POST; with it unset, nothing is sent and Health shows the same rows

title: T37: Deliverable: amd64 OCI image + deploy/compose.yaml + env contract + `partifactory deploy` with auto rollback
description:
## Goal and why

The product is shipped as **three things, none tied to a CI vendor**: an OCI image, a compose file, and a documented env contract. Deploying is `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`, which works by hand, from cron or from any CI. `partifactory deploy` wraps that with a health gate and automatic rollback, so a broken release never stays live. Release assets (image + `part` CLI) are what the laptop drill (T35) uses when the CI host is the thing that died.

This serves portability (decision 22: no hard dependency on the current stack; any OCI host with compose) and safe defaults (log limits so the Docker daemon's own logs can't fill the disk).

Slice 1 (P1), the "Slice 1 part" of the deliverable: amd64 only. arm64, SBOM, `cosign` signing and example CI workflows are T126. The runner's compose service is added by T98. Feeds T38 (staging is the example deployment built from this), T93, T98, T126.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead: close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T37.a** — the image: `cargo-chef` layer caching → static musl binary → `FROM scratch` (~20 MB), amd64, every asset embedded, deployed **by digest, never `:latest`**; tag → release assets (image tarball/digest + `part` CLI binaries).
- **T37.b** — `deploy/compose.yaml` + env contract wiring: partifactory, the `/data` volume, optional render sidecar behind a profile, optional Caddy proxy behind a profile, `json-file` log limits on every service; `docs/env.md` cross-check.
- **T37.c** — `partifactory deploy`: compose pull/up with a health-gated switch and automatic rollback within 2 minutes.

Verbatim requirements (PLAN §5b):
- "**Image**: `cargo-chef` layer caching → static musl binary → `FROM scratch` image (~20 MB) … pushed to any OCI registry and **deployed by digest**, never `:latest`. Every tag also publishes the image and the `part` CLI as release assets (the passive GitHub mirror's Releases in the example deployment), so a laptop drill doesn't depend on the CI host."
- "**Compose file** (`deploy/compose.yaml`): partifactory, the `/data` volume, … the optional render sidecar behind a profile, and an optional proxy service (Caddy by default, behind a profile) for hosts that have none. Every service sets `json-file` logging with `max-size=10m` and `max-file=3`."
- "**Env contract** (`docs/env.md`, generated from the config loader so it can't drift): `site.toml` (path `PF_SITE_TOML`, default `/data/site.toml`) is the config, and every key is also settable as `PF_<SECTION>_<KEY>`, env winning. Secrets are env or `_FILE` only … Required: `PF_SESSION_KEY`, `PF_CAP_HMAC_KEY`, `PF_DOMAIN_APEX`, `PF_METRICS_TOKEN`, the OIDC client secret if `[idp]` is set, and `PF_RUNNER_KEY` if the runner is on. Optional per adapter: `PF_DNS_API_TOKEN`, `PF_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, `PF_IDP_PROVISIONER_TOKEN`, `PF_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `PF_CDN_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`."
- "`partifactory deploy` wraps it with a health gate: start the new container next to the old one, wait for `/readyz`, switch, and **roll back automatically** if health fails within 2 minutes. Schema migrations run before the switch and must be forward-compatible with the previous binary."
- **Host contract** (documented in `docs/host.md`): an OCI runtime with compose (Docker or Podman) and, for backends, the Engine API socket mounted into the runner only; one data volume at `/data`; env vars or secret files per the env contract; inbound HTTP from the proxy or outbound network for a tunnel adapter. partifactory never calls ZFS, TrueNAS or any host API.

Listeners in the container: `:8080` workspace, `:8081` content, `:9090` ops (never published through the ingress; compose binds it to the host's local interface only or leaves it on the internal network).

## Not in scope

arm64, SBOM, cosign, nginx/Traefik configs, CI examples (T126); the runner service (T98); the render sidecar's own hardening (T80, which adds its service definition under the profile); proxy contract and Caddy example config (T89; T37's Caddy service references `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` from T89).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why by digest:* reproducible, rollback-able deploys; `:latest` makes "what's running" unknowable.
- *Why `FROM scratch`:* one static binary with everything embedded; no OS packages to patch; fonts bundled (cards need them).
- *Why log limits everywhere:* §5h "Container stdout from the Docker daemon: `json-file` with `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`".
- *Why forward-compatible migrations:* rollback runs the old binary against the migrated DB.
- *Why CI is an example, not a dependency:* decision 22; nothing reads a CI vendor's API.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "`docker compose pull && up -d` from the published compose file serves a part with only env/`_FILE` secrets; a deliberately failing /readyz build rolls back within 2 min and the old digest keeps serving; a tag produces release assets; `docker inspect` shows `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3` on every service".

- [ ] Fresh host: copy `deploy/compose.yaml`, provide secrets as `_FILE` mounts only, `pull && up -d`, create and open a part.
- [ ] `partifactory deploy` with an image whose `/readyz` fails reverts to the previous digest within 2 min; the old digest serves throughout.
- [ ] A git tag produces release assets: image digest (and pushed image), `part` CLI binaries for linux-amd64 (darwin builds best-effort), checksums.
- [ ] `docker inspect` on every service shows `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`.
- [ ] Image is `FROM scratch`, ≤ ~30 MB, runs as non-root.

## Tests

- `tests/deploy/compose_smoke.sh` (CI job): brings up the compose file with `_FILE` secrets, runs `part put` + `curl` checks; logs saved to `target/e2e-logs/compose_smoke/`.
- `tests/deploy/rollback.sh`: builds a deliberately broken image (env flag forces `/readyz` 503), runs `partifactory deploy`, asserts rollback timing and that `event="deploy.rollback" from=<digest> to=<digest> reason="readyz_failed"` is logged.
- `tests/deploy/log_limits.sh`: `docker inspect` assertion across services.
- `crates/partifactory/tests/deploy_cmd.rs` unit tests for the state machine (start-new, wait-ready, switch, verify, rollback) with a fake compose runner.

## References

PLAN.md §5b Builds and deploys (deliverable, image, compose, env contract, deploy, host contract), §3 Topology (listeners), §5h (container stdout row), §5f Build + deploy row, decisions 3, 22; Slice 1 "Shipping it" row; final round decision 42 (deferred extras to T126).

title: T37.a: amd64 OCI image (cargo-chef, static musl, FROM scratch, by digest) + release assets on tag
description:
## Goal and why

One small, static, reproducible image that is the whole product, deployed by digest; and release assets so a laptop drill can restore without the CI host.

## Scope

- `Dockerfile` (multi-stage): `cargo-chef` planner/cook stages for dependency caching → build `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --release` with every asset embedded (UI, fonts, prelude, wrapper, card PNGs, tokens.css) → `FROM scratch` final stage with the binary, CA certificates (needed for OIDC discovery and mirror fetches), `/data` as the working volume, `USER 65532:65532`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/partifactory","serve"]`.
- Base builder images pinned by digest (§5d Dependencies).
- Release workflow script `scripts/release.sh` (CI-agnostic; the example CI files are T126): on a tag `vX.Y.Z`, build, push to the configured registry, record the digest in `release/digest.txt`, build `part` CLI binaries (linux-amd64 static; darwin-arm64/amd64 when a mac runner exists), write `SHA256SUMS`, and upload assets to the forge release (the example deployment uses the passive GitHub mirror's Releases; the upload step is a pluggable command).
- `part` is the same binary invoked as `part` (argv[0] alias) or a thin CLI build; document which.
- `cargo binstall` metadata in the CLI crate.

## Not in scope

arm64, SBOM, cosign (T126); compose (T37.b); deploy (T37.c).

## Design notes and decisions

- No libc, no shell in the image: health checks are done by `partifactory deploy`/compose `healthcheck` using the binary itself (`partifactory healthcheck` subcommand hitting `:9090/readyz`), since `curl` isn't available.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Image builds reproducibly in CI with cached dependency layers; final image `FROM scratch`, non-root, ~20 MB.
- [ ] Tag produces pushed image + digest file + CLI binaries + checksums as release assets.

## Tests

- `tests/deploy/image_checks.sh`: inspect layers (single binary + certs), user, size budget; run `partifactory --version` and `healthcheck` against a started container; logs kept in `target/e2e-logs/image_checks/`.

title: T37.b: deploy/compose.yaml (profiles, /data volume, _FILE secrets, json-file 10m x 3) + env contract check
description:
## Goal and why

The compose file is the deployment unit any OCI host can run. It must be safe by default (log limits, ops port not exposed) and work with secrets mounted as files.

## Scope

`deploy/compose.yaml`:
- `partifactory` service: image by digest (`${PF_IMAGE:?}` with a pinned default digest written by the release), volume `pf-data:/data`, ports `8080` and `8081` published only to the proxy network (or `127.0.0.1` when the proxy is on the same host), `9090` bound to the host's local interface only, never to the proxy; `environment:` lists non-secret `PF_*`; `secrets:` maps `pf_session_key`, `pf_cap_hmac_key`, `pf_metrics_token`, optional `pf_oidc_client_secret` to `PF_SESSION_KEY_FILE`, etc.; `healthcheck` uses `partifactory healthcheck`.
- `render` service behind profile `render` (definition filled in by T80; leave a stub with the profile and the `internal: true` network).
- `proxy` service (Caddy) behind profile `proxy`, mounting `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile` (from T89) and serving `deploy/proxy/maintenance.html` when the origin is down.
- Networks: `edge` (proxy ↔ app), `render-internal` (`internal: true`).
- **Every service**: `logging: {driver: json-file, options: {max-size: "10m", max-file: "3"}}` (YAML anchor).
- The runner service is NOT here; T98 adds it behind the `backends` profile.
- `deploy/.env.example` with every non-secret variable and comments; secrets documented as `_FILE`.
- CI check: `docs/env.md` (generated by T04) lists every variable the compose file references, and vice versa (`scripts/check_env_contract.sh`).

## Not in scope

The proxy config contents (T89), render sidecar settings (T80), runner (T98).

## Design notes and decisions

- `:9090` never through the ingress (§3): `/metrics` also requires `PF_METRICS_TOKEN` (T18), but exposure is minimised too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker compose config` validates; `docker inspect` shows `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3` on every running service, with and without profiles.

title: T37.c: `partifactory deploy`: compose pull/up, health-gated switch, auto rollback within 2 min
description:
## Goal and why

A deploy that fails health must undo itself, because nobody is watching a household server at 3 a.m.

## Scope

`partifactory deploy [--image <ref@digest>] [--compose deploy/compose.yaml] [--host <docker host>]`:
1. Record the current digest (from the running container) as `previous`.
2. `docker compose pull` the target digest.
3. Run migrations via a one-shot `partifactory migrate` container against `/data` (forward-only; must be compatible with the previous binary).
4. Start the new container next to the old one (a second compose project or a blue/green service name), on alternate internal ports.
5. Wait for its `/readyz` (via `partifactory healthcheck`) up to 60 s.
6. Switch: point the proxy upstream / swap services (the documented mechanism: compose `up -d` of the target, with the old container kept stopped-not-removed), then re-check `/readyz` through the public path for 2 minutes.
7. On any failure within 2 minutes: switch back to `previous`, log `deploy.rollback`, exit non-zero.
- Works with Docker or Podman compose; `--host` accepts `ssh://` (for CI over SSH, the example workflow is T126).
- Writes a deploy record to stdout as JSON and to `/data/backup/deploys.jsonl` is not needed; log events suffice.

## Not in scope

CI workflows (T126), image build (T37.a).

## Design notes and decisions

- Readiness ignores the IdP (T36), so an IdP outage never triggers a rollback.
- Because the content listener caps include a boot epoch bumped on start, every deploy costs open tabs one silent re-grant; that is expected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Good image: switch completes, old container removed after success.
- [ ] Image with failing `/readyz`: rollback to `previous` within 2 min; the old digest serves throughout (no 5xx gap beyond the switch).
- [ ] Image that becomes unready 60 s after switch: rolled back.

## Tests

- `crates/partifactory/tests/deploy_cmd.rs::state_machine_*` with a fake compose driver (success, readyz never ready, regresses after switch).
- `tests/deploy/rollback.sh` real Docker: asserts timing and `event="deploy.rollback" reason="readyz_failed"`; keeps `docker compose logs` under `target/e2e-logs/deploy_rollback/`.

## References

PLAN.md §5b ("Deploying is `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`… `partifactory deploy` wraps it with a health gate"), §5d Health (readiness not tied to the IdP).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T37: Deliverable: amd64 OCI image + deploy/compose.yaml + env contract + `partifactory deploy` with auto rollback (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T37.b: deploy/compose.yaml (profiles, /data volume, _FILE secrets, json-file 10m x 3) + env contract check
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Good image: switch completes, old container removed after success.
- [ ] Image with failing `/readyz`: rollback to `previous` within 2 min; the old digest serves throughout (no 5xx gap beyond the switch).
- [ ] Image that becomes unready 60 s after switch: rolled back.

title: T126: Deliverable extras after Slice 1: nginx/Traefik configs, arm64, SBOM, cosign, example CI workflows
description:
## Goal and why

Slice 1 ships Caddy and an amd64 image (T37, T89). This task completes the deliverable promised by the plan so partifactory runs behind any common proxy, on arm64 hosts, with a verifiable supply chain, and with copy-paste CI examples — while keeping CI an **example, not a dependency** (decision 22). It was split out in the final round (decision 42, provisional) because neither the pixel test nor the Slice 1 definition of done needs it. It gates T93 (the portability lane exercises every example proxy config) and M1.

## Scope

- `deploy/proxy/nginx.conf` and `deploy/proxy/traefik/` (static + dynamic config) meeting the **ingress contract** (§3, verbatim):
  - route `parts.<domain>` to `:8080` and `*.<domain>` to `:8081`, preserving `Host`; terminate TLS with a cert covering both (one wildcard cert does);
  - pass the client address in one header named in config (`[ingress] client_ip_header`, e.g. `X-Forwarded-For` or `CF-Connecting-IP`), trusted only from `[ingress] trusted_proxies`;
  - optionally pass a request id (`[ingress] request_id_header`);
  - allow long-lived responses (SSE, long-poll ≤ 50 s) and request bodies up to 8 MiB.
  - serve `deploy/proxy/maintenance.html` (from T89) when the origin is down.
- Each config passes the T89 smoke test (routing by Host, SSE survives 60 s, 8 MiB body) — reuse T89's test script with a `--proxy nginx|traefik` flag.
- **arm64** images (`aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`) and a multi-arch manifest; deployed by digest as before.
- **SBOM** per image (SPDX or CycloneDX via `cargo-cyclonedx`/`syft`), attached to the release and as an OCI attestation.
- **`cosign` signing** of image digests (keyless or key-based; document both; the public repo must not contain private keys) and `cosign verify` instructions in `docs/release.md`.
- **Example CI workflows**: `examples/ci/gitea-actions.yml` ("what the example deployment runs: build, sign, push, then `partifactory deploy` over SSH from a protected runner") and `examples/ci/github-actions.yml`. Secrets come from the CI's own store as env vars or files. **Nothing reads a CI vendor's API.**

## Not in scope

Caddy config and the ingress contract code (T89); the amd64 image/compose/deploy (T37); the portability lane job itself (T93).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why examples only:* a hidden CI dependency is exactly what the portability lane exists to catch; examples call only the same scripts a shell would (`scripts/release.sh`, `partifactory deploy`).
- The GitHub mirror is passive (no Actions secrets in the example deployment); the GitHub example is for other adopters.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each example proxy config passes the T89 smoke test; `cosign verify` passes on a tagged image; amd64 and arm64 images both serve the e2e suite; no CI example reads a CI vendor API".

- [ ] nginx and Traefik configs pass the smoke test (Host routing, SSE ≥ 60 s, 8 MiB body, trusted client-IP header).
- [ ] `cosign verify` passes on a tagged multi-arch image; SBOM attached.
- [ ] e2e suite passes on amd64 and on arm64 (QEMU or a native runner).
- [ ] A lint (`scripts/lint_ci_examples.sh`) greps the CI examples for vendor API calls (`api.github.com`, Gitea API paths, `gh api`) and finds none.

## Tests

- `tests/proxy/smoke.sh --proxy nginx|traefik|caddy`: logs at `target/e2e-logs/proxy_<name>/` including proxy access logs and server JSONL with `request_id` propagation asserted.
- `tests/deploy/arm64_e2e.sh` (nightly if native runners are scarce).
- `scripts/lint_ci_examples.sh` in CI.

PLAN.md §3 ingress contract, §5b (image amd64 + arm64, SBOM, cosign; "CI is an example, not a dependency"), §5f Ingress row, §6a notes ("arm64 images, SBOM, cosign and the example CI workflows (T126)"), §10 Final round, decisions 22, 42.

title: T68: `partifactory doctor`: config, DNS, ingress, certs, IdP, backup layers, disk, store caps, safe defaults
description:
## Goal and why

`doctor` is the one command that tells an operator (or the admin on a laptop) whether a deployment is set up correctly and safely, with a specific exit code and message per failure. It encodes the plan's safe-default principle: **`doctor` fails if any store is uncapped or a safe default is switched off without its explicit key**, and it reports backup layers honestly (host snapshots on/off/unknown). Because the ops listener is reachable on the local network, `doctor` and a laptop can tell ingress-down from box-down.

After Slice 1 (P1); on the M1 critical path (… T113 → T114 → T68 → M1).

## Scope

`partifactory doctor [--json] [--only <check>]`, checks (PLAN §5d, verbatim list): "config and the env contract, DNS records for `parts` and the wildcard, ingress (a request through the public name reaches the right listener with the trusted client-IP header; the tunnel, with that adapter), cert coverage and expiry, IdP discovery and reachability, provisioner permissions (Authentik: expects 403 on a forbidden group op, once the gate has run), backup layers, export freshness, disk, **every store capped**, any safe default switched off, and (with backends) the runner's firewall rules."

Per check:
- **config**: `partifactory config check` logic (T04): required `PF_*` present (env or `_FILE`), types valid, `[unsafe]` keys listed.
- **dns**: resolve `parts.<domain>` and a random `doctor-<rand>-part.<domain>`; both must reach the deployment (compare against expected targets from `[dns]` or the ingress address).
- **ingress**: request `https://parts.<domain>/_pf_doctor` and `https://doctor-x-part.<domain>/_pf_doctor` (a doctor-only echo route with a one-time nonce) and verify each landed on the right listener (`:8080` vs `:8081`) and that the trusted client-IP header arrived from a trusted proxy; with the Cloudflare adapter, the tunnel is connected.
- **certs**: the served cert covers `parts.<domain>` and `*.<domain>`; expiry > 14 days (warn), > 0 (fail).
- **idp**: discovery document fetch and parse (skipped when no `[idp]`).
- **provisioner** (Authentik, once T39 exists): expects 403 on a forbidden group op; plugs in without an edge (§6a note: "`doctor` (T68, P1) adds the provisioner probe once the gate (T39, P2b) has run").
- **backup layers**: layer 1 from `backup.host_snapshots` as **on / off / unknown**; export freshness (< 48 h); exports on the same filesystem as `/data` → warning ("convenience, not a backup").
- **disk**: headroom vs the budget (T114).
- **store caps**: every store in the §5h table that exists has a cap and a retention job registered (from the T114/T113 registries); an uncapped store fails.
- **safe defaults**: any safe default switched off without its `[unsafe]` key fails; switched off with the key → warning.
- **runner firewall** (once T98 exists): the runner reports its drop rules installed (`DOCKER-USER` / nftables table) for every part network.

Output: one line per check (`ok`, `warn`, `fail` + message + fix hint), `--json` for machines. Exit codes: 0 all ok, specific non-zero per failing check family (document the table in `docs/doctor.md`, e.g. 10 config, 11 dns, 12 ingress, 13 certs, 14 idp, 15 provisioner, 16 backup, 17 disk, 18 store caps, 19 safe defaults, 20 runner firewall; the first failure's code wins, all failures listed).

## Not in scope

Fixing anything (doctor is read-only); `provision` (T32); the checks' own runtime implementations where they live (T36's `HealthCheck`s are reused).

## Design notes and decisions

- Reuse T36's health checks so Health and doctor never disagree.
- Doctor runs from inside the container (`docker exec`) or from a laptop with `--remote https://parts.<domain>` plus the ops URL; checks needing local access skip with "unknown" remotely.
- Read-only: never writes except its probe nonce in memory.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each check has a failing fixture with a specific non-zero exit and message; the layer report shows host snapshots as on/off/unknown; an uncapped store or a safe default switched off without its explicit key fails".

- [ ] Every check has a passing and a failing fixture; each failing fixture returns its documented exit code and message.
- [ ] Layer 1 shows on/off/unknown from config.
- [ ] A store registered without a cap fails `doctor` (exit 18); an `[unsafe]`-less switched-off default fails (exit 19).
- [ ] `--json` output schema-validated.

## Tests

- `crates/partifactory/tests/doctor.rs::check_<name>_fails_with_code` (table-driven over fixtures: missing env, wrong DNS via a stub resolver, ingress landing on the wrong listener, expired cert from a test CA, IdP discovery 500, stale export, same-disk export, uncapped store, unsafe default).
- Captured logs assert `event="doctor.check" name=.. outcome=fail code=..`.
- Portability lane (T93) runs `doctor` against the Caddy deployment and expects all-ok except layer 1 "unknown".

## References

PLAN.md §5d Maintenance (`partifactory doctor`), §5c (doctor reports layers; same disk amber), §5h ("`doctor` fails if any store is uncapped", `[unsafe]`), §3f Network (doctor checks the rules), §6a notes, §7 Operations.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Each check has a failing fixture with a specific non-zero exit and message; the layer report shows host snapshots as on/off/unknown; an uncapped store or a safe default switched off without its explicit key fails
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
  - T89: Ingress contract: trusted client-IP header, request ids, Caddy example + maintenance page
  - T114: Disk budget (warn 80 %, storage_full at 95 %), per-store caps on Health, and the [unsafe] safe-defaults registry
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- The ingress probe route on the content listener lives under the reserved `/_pf/` prefix (`/_pf/doctor`): unauthenticated, content-free, byte-identical whether `<label>-part` exists or not (no part-existence oracle). Acceptance adds that identity check.
- Split into T68.a / T68.b (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: Each check has a failing fixture with a specific non-zero exit and message; the layer report shows host snapshots as on/off/unknown; an uncapped store or a safe default switched off without its explicit key fails

title: T68.a: doctor framework (--json, --only, exit-code table, docs/doctor.md) + config, dns, ingress (/_pf/doctor), certs and idp checks
description:
## Goal and why

One command that tells an operator, in plain words with a fix hint, whether the deployment is wired correctly: the framework and the five network/identity checks.

## Scope

- `partifactory doctor [--json] [--only <check>] [--remote <url>]`: a `Check` trait (`name`, `run() -> Ok | Warn | Fail {message, fix_hint}`), one line per check, `--json` for machines, the exit-code table from the parent (first failure's code wins; all failures listed), `docs/doctor.md`.
- **config**: `config check` logic (T04) incl. `[unsafe]` keys listed.
- **dns**: resolve `parts.<domain>` and a random `doctor-<rand>-part.<domain>` against the expected targets.
- **ingress**: `GET https://parts.<domain>/_pf/doctor` and `https://doctor-x-part.<domain>/_pf/doctor`: an unauthenticated, content-free echo route (under T29's reserved `/_pf/` prefix on the content listener) with a one-time nonce, **byte-identical whether `<label>-part` exists or not** (no part-existence oracle); verifies the right listener (`:8080` vs `:8081`) and that the trusted client-IP header arrived from a trusted proxy; with the Cloudflare adapter, the tunnel is connected (T91 hook).
- **certs**: coverage of `parts.<domain>` and `*.<domain>`; expiry > 14 days (warn), > 0 (fail).
- **idp**: discovery document fetch and parse (skipped without `[idp]`).

## Not in scope

Backup/disk/store/safe-default checks and the provisioner/runner hooks (T68.b).

## Acceptance criteria

title: T74: nginx + HAProxy comparison on the real content path (cap check, /c/ prefix, brotli), same box
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory serves a reduced subset of HTTP (fixed route table, precompressed immutable responses, no upstream hop), so on its own workload it should match or beat general-purpose proxies. The comparison is a **regression guard that keeps the hot path DB-free and allocation-light**; "parity with nginx is the sanity bar, not a product requirement". It runs after P1 on the real content path because that's the number worth knowing. After Slice 1 (P1), feeds M1.

## Scope

- Bench harness (extends T23's `partifactory bench`): same machine, same files, three servers:
  1. partifactory content listener: `GET https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap>/<path>` with a real cap check (HMAC verify + epoch compares), manifest LRU, brotli negotiation (`Accept-Encoding: br`), ETag/304.
  2. nginx serving the same precompressed files (`brotli_static on` or `gzip_static`-equivalent with the brotli module; `sendfile on`), with a location that strips a `/c/<token>/` prefix (and a variant with an `auth_request`-free HMAC check via njs if practical; record which).
  3. HAProxy serving the same via its cache or as a front to a static server; record the config honestly.
- Workloads: small part blob (2 KiB), medium (64 KiB), large (2 MiB), 304 revalidation, entry document (templated; partifactory-only row).
- Load generator: `oha` or `wrk2` at fixed rates, measuring p50/p99 latency and max throughput; plus server-side timing for partifactory.
- Outputs: `bench/results/comparison-<date>.json` and a markdown comparison table committed in `docs/perf/comparison.md`; fill in the §5a static-file row ("Static-file throughput vs nginx and HAProxy on the same box and files: ≥ parity").
- Tracked targets from §5a: part blob from origin p99 server time (warm) < 200 µs (a hypothesis until measured).

## Not in scope

The same-machine regression bench gate (T23); release gating (results are tracked, not gated).

## Design notes and decisions

- Honest about zero-copy: v1 uses mmap'd LRU + `pread`; nginx `sendfile` is near the syscall floor, so parity is the target on raw files.
- Shared CI runners are too noisy: run on the deploy host off-hours (§5a "How it's gated").
- Configs for nginx/HAProxy committed under `bench/configs/` so the comparison is reproducible.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Results JSON and a comparison table are committed; the §5a static-file row is filled in".

- [ ] Results JSON with environment details (CPU, kernel, versions, configs' hashes) committed.
- [ ] Comparison table committed; the static-file row filled with measured numbers.
- [ ] The partifactory path measured includes cap verification and `/c/` routing (asserted by a request counter on cap verifies).

## Tests

- `bench/run_comparison.sh` (manual/off-hours), self-checks that each server returns byte-identical bodies and correct `Content-Encoding: br` before measuring; logs saved under `target/bench-logs/`.

## References

PLAN.md §5a Performance (why the comparison exists, lean hot path, targets table, how it's gated), §6 P1, decision 21.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Results JSON and a comparison table are committed; the §5a static-file row is filled in
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T23: Regression bench: same-machine content-path bench vs previous release, fail on >10 % regression
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

title: T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory is reachable from the internet, runs agent-written JavaScript, and holds a household's private things. The §7 checklist is the list of properties that must hold **from outside the network**, against a real deployment, not just in unit tests. This task turns every §7 line for what exists in Slice 1 into an automated test (or a recorded manual result where only a real device can tell), runs it against staging (the example deployment) in CI, and runs it in the portability lane (no vendor) for every line not marked *(adapter)*, so no protection depends on an adapter.

It also owns the **real-device pass** (iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, the Telegram in-app browser) and the **5-minute Telegram in-app-browser passkey test** decided for Slice 1 (decision 36).

Slice 1 (P1). Definition of done item 4: "The §7 lines for what exists pass from outside (T38), and the guest, agent and render-sidecar lines pass in T95, T43–T45, T53 and T80. No agent token, scope or op can make a public link." Item 8: "The Telegram passkey test is recorded." Lines marked *(adapter)* run when their adapter lands (T91, T92). Backend lines are T103.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead: close it only after every subtask is closed and every §7 line for what exists is an automated test or a recorded manual result):
- **T38.a** — the outside-in harness + Part hosts and the sandbox, Caching and blobs, Links and cards lines.
- **T38.b** — Identity and admin, Agents, Guests, Render sidecar, Operations lines (those that exist in Slice 1), cross-checking the per-task suites (T95, T43–T45, T53, T80).
- **T38.c** — the real-device pass and the Telegram in-app-browser passkey test, recorded.

Harness: `tests/security/` — a Rust (or Playwright + Rust) suite parameterised by `PF_TARGET=https://parts.<domain>` and a test-account config; runs from a CI runner **outside** the deployment's network against staging, and in the portability lane against the Caddy + Dex deployment. Every line in §7 gets a stable id (`SEC-PH-01` …) mapped in `tests/security/checklist.yaml` to its test name or manual-record file, so a test proves coverage: "every §7 line for what exists is an automated test or a recorded manual result".

The §7 lines in scope are copied verbatim into the subtasks. Lines for things that don't exist yet are listed in `checklist.yaml` with `status: pending(<owning T-id>)`, so the suite shows the gap rather than hiding it.

## Not in scope

- §7 Backends lines — T103.
- *(adapter)* lines for Cloudflare and Authentik — run in T91, T92 (listed here as pending until those land).
- Fixing failures found (file bugs against the owning task).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why from outside:* a misconfigured edge (proxy forwarding `:9090`, trusting a spoofed client-IP header, caching private blobs) only shows up through the real ingress.
- *Why in the portability lane too:* decision 24; protections must not depend on Cloudflare or Authentik.
- *Telegram decision (the admin, 2026-10-23):* a 5-minute real-phone test of passkey sign-in in Telegram's in-app browser. If it fails, the fixes are (1) set Telegram to open links in the normal browser, and (2) Hermes' messages hint "open in browser". **The person-bound-link fallback is rejected** (§10). The test is then re-run with the fixes applied.
- Real-device pass is manual by nature (a virtual authenticator can't see OS prompts); results are recorded as dated markdown files with device, OS and browser versions.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Every §7 line for what exists is an automated test or a recorded manual result; the Telegram passkey result is recorded, and if it fails, Telegram is set to open links in the normal browser and Hermes' messages say 'open in browser', and the test is re-run".

- [ ] Suite green against staging and in the portability lane (non-adapter lines).
- [ ] Real-device pass recorded for: standalone open, part-host open (first open and reload), embedding (pending T64), invite acceptance (pending T94), sign-in.
- [ ] Telegram passkey result recorded; on failure, fixes applied and re-test recorded.
- [ ] "No agent token, scope or op can make a public link" is tested on every surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI, `/skill.md` commands).

## Tests

See subtasks. Every automated check logs `event="sec.check" id="SEC-.." outcome=pass|fail target=..` to `target/e2e-logs/security/<id>/` along with request/response captures (headers only, caps redacted) and server request ids of failing requests.

## References
