title: T38.a: Outside-in security harness + §7 part-host/sandbox, caching/blobs and links/cards lines
description:
## Goal and why

Build the reusable outside-in harness and prove the serving-side properties that make agent-written JS safe: the canonical sandbox CSP, no cookies on part hosts, host-bound caps, no open redirect, the wrapper's isolation, and private blobs never in a shared cache.

## Scope

Harness: `tests/security/` with `checklist.yaml` (id → test or manual record), a client that can send raw requests with arbitrary `Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Accept`, `Host` headers, a Playwright driver for Chromium, WebKit and Gecko, and a canary service on a sibling `<domain>` host that records any cookies it receives.

§7 lines (verbatim), each one test:
**Part hosts and the sandbox**
- Every part document response carries the canonical CSP (§2), including `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin`. Only `unsandboxed` parts lack it, and the admin page lists them.
- Part hosts never emit `Set-Cookie`. A request carrying an old `__Host-pf_cap` cookie is treated exactly like one without. In the e2e suite on Chromium, WebKit and Gecko, `document.cookie` and `cookieStore.set` writes from a part have no effect, and `localStorage` is the shim.
- A part's fetch/POST toward another `<domain>` service, or toward the workspace, carries no `SameSite=Lax` cookies (tested against a canary service).
- `/_rt/v1` rejects a missing cap, a cap bound to another host, an expired window, a stale epoch, and any non-null `Origin` (other than the part's own for `unsandboxed`). A sibling part's page can't read or write another part's data. No `OPTIONS` preflight is ever needed.
- Part responses to `Origin: null` carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` and never `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` or `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`. The workspace host never emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null`.
- Caps are host-bound (a cap for A is rejected on B), deterministic within a window, and dead after an epoch bump, a boot-epoch bump or an import. An unknown `kid` or bad MAC → 404.
- `/grant` can't redirect off the part's own host (fuzzed), and in `wrap` mode the cap appears only in the fragment. Without a session, `/grant` → sign-in, never content.
- **The wrapper**: the part host root is served without `sandbox` but with its own strict CSP (scripts only from the shared blob host, `connect-src` only the workspace, `frame-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors` from config). It never sets a cookie, removes `#pf=` before any other script runs, and holds only its own part's cap. Content framed inside it can't read it (a test script in the part tries `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage` and fails).
- **Chrome-API CORS**: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` + `Allow-Credentials` are sent only for an active, sandboxed part's own host, and only on that part's chrome routes. `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, an old redirecting name and any other origin get no CORS headers (fuzzed). Writes need `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site`.
- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on every part response. Logs never contain `/c/<cap>/` segments (canary test).
**Caching and blobs**
- Part blobs always carry `Cache-Control: private` and the shared blob host serves only hashes in `shared_blobs`. *(adapter, T91)* never `cf-cache-status: HIT`.
- Shared blobs carry `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and never `Set-Cookie`. *(adapter, T91)* `HIT` on the second fetch.
**Links and cards**
- A part host root fetched by a signed-out client returns the content-free card (or the public card while a public link is active) and no part bytes. Bot and browser User-Agents get byte-identical responses for the root and `/l/`. Neither page's HTML contains a cap or a hop-target URL.
- `/p/<name>` on the workspace only redirects to the part host, and reveals nothing else.
- A private card's input struct has no part-derived field (unit test; referenced from T75/T119).
- Only the admin's session can create a public link. No agent scope, token or op can (tested on every surface). A revoked public link → 404 within seconds. The kill switch revokes all.

The canonical CSP to assert byte-for-byte (with `<blob>`, `<self-host>`, `<workspace>`, `<embedders>` substituted):
```
sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-modals allow-downloads allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation;
default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob: <blob>; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <blob>;
img-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>; media-src 'self' data: blob: <blob>; font-src 'self' data: <blob>; connect-src 'self' <blob>;
worker-src 'self' blob:; frame-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace> <embedders>
```
plus `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

## Not in scope

Identity/agents/guests/ops lines (T38.b), devices (T38.c), backend lines (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

- Open-redirect fuzz: generate paths with `//evil`, `\\evil`, `%2f%2f`, `@evil`, CRLF, unicode dots; assert `Location` host is always `<name>-part.<domain>`.
- CORS fuzz: origins list from all part names, `null`, `blobs-part`, renamed names, lookalikes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every line above has a test id in `checklist.yaml` and passes against staging and the portability lane (adapter lines marked pending until T91).

## Tests

`tests/security/part_hosts.rs::sec_ph_01_canonical_csp` … `sec_ph_10_no_cap_in_logs`, `tests/security/caching.rs::sec_cb_*`, `tests/security/links.rs::sec_lc_*`, `tests/e2e/security/sandbox_cookies.spec.ts` (3 engines). Logs and captures under `target/e2e-logs/security/<id>/`; the canary-in-logs test greps the server JSONL for cap substrings.

## References

PLAN.md §7 (Part hosts and the sandbox; Caching and blobs; Links and cards), §2 canonical CSP, chrome API CORS, Leaked URLs.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every line above has a test id in `checklist.yaml` and passes against staging and the portability lane (adapter lines marked pending until T91).

title: T38.b: §7 identity/admin, agents, guests, render sidecar and operations lines from outside
description:
## Goal and why

Prove from outside that only the admin administers, agents can't escalate or reach outward actions, guests can only write shared data, the renderer can't leak, and operations are safe (no exposed ops port, no content in logs, limits trip).

## Scope

§7 lines (verbatim), for what exists in Slice 1; the rest marked pending with their owner:
**Identity and admin**
- Only the admin's pinned subject reaches admin. An IdP-admin user still gets 403. An admin action without a fresh (10 min) partifactory passkey assertion → `step_up_required`. Household sharing never asks.
- *(adapter, T92)* The Authentik provisioner gets 403 from the IdP on a non-`pf-*` group, and the core refuses before calling. Gate results recorded.
- With the IdP down, `/readyz` stays 200, existing sessions work, and no epoch is bumped. A refresh that returns `invalid_grant` ends that session.
- Local accounts: passkey-only (no password path exists), a recovery link revokes the old passkeys, and an invite token beyond its use count is refused. *(pending T94)*
**Agents**
- Agent tokens: audience-bound to the workspace origin (rejected on part hosts and on `/oauth/*`), scope- and space-limited, no admin scopes obtainable, refresh reuse → the whole token family is revoked.
- An agent without `share:household` can't grant. With it, only to existing people and groups, only within its spaces, labelled and listed. *(pending T52)*
- No agent scope, token or op can make a public link, an invite, a group, an `everyone-signed-in` grant or a LAN allowlist entry, on any surface. `part_link_for` returns a link that grants nothing by itself: opened by someone without the right, it shows the normal 403. There is no request table for an agent to write to (schema test).
- Unconsented OAuth clients can do nothing. Registration rate-limited. A CIMD URL resolving to a private address is refused. The consent sheet shows the redirect host. *(pending T124)*
- Device codes: single use, 10-minute expiry, `slow_down` enforced, manual entry limited to 5 per minute; the stale and different-network banners appear when they should.
- A `pf_pat_` token is redacted in logs, scope- and space-limited like OAuth tokens, and revoked by the same cascade.
- Authentication failures are HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` on `/mcp` and `/api`, never a tool result.
- Discovery documents are reachable unauthenticated and contain no site secrets or user data.
**Guests ("Can contribute" links)**
- A guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) gets `403`, and so does any `/api` or `/mcp` request from a guest's context.
- A Can-view link's cap can't write shared data. A forged or replayed guest id (`g`) fails the cap's MAC.
- Guest writes past the per-guest or per-IP limit get `429`; past the part's shared-data cap, `quota_exceeded`. After **Freeze**, an open guest tab can't write on its next request.
- Guests never see history, source or the share sheet.
**Render sidecar**
- The renderer has no route off the internal Docker network (egress canary fails). Renderer caps can't persist `/_rt` writes. A public link without the screenshot opt-in never gets a screenshot card *(pending T81)*.
**Operations**
- The origin is reachable only through the configured ingress (a direct connection to the listeners from outside fails). `:9090` is never routed. A client-IP header from an address outside `trusted_proxies` is ignored.
- No tokens, caps, cookies, secrets or part content in logs, traces, `insights.db` or `/metrics` (T112 owns the fuzz; this line checks the staging deployment's `/metrics` and a log sample with canaries). `/metrics` refuses a request without the admin metrics token.
- Rate limits trip at the configured thresholds, and quotas stop a looping agent. At 95 % of the disk budget, writes get `storage_full` while reads and deletes continue (staging uses a small test budget volume).
- Every growing store has a cap (`doctor` fails otherwise) and passes its fill-past-cap case (T115; referenced, not re-run). A safe default switched off without its `[unsafe]` key fails `config check`.
- A parts-only export contains no grants, tokens, sessions or people (schema test, T34).

Where a per-task suite already covers a line (T95, T43–T45, T53, T80), this subtask either re-runs it from outside against staging or links it in `checklist.yaml` as `covered_by: <test>` with a CI check that the referenced test exists and passed in the same pipeline.

## Not in scope

Sandbox/caching/links lines (T38.a); devices (T38.c); backends (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

- Step-up tests use a WebAuthn virtual authenticator on Chromium; the IdP-down test stops Dex in the portability lane and uses a staging maintenance flag only if safe (otherwise run in the lane only and record).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every line above for an existing feature passes against staging and the portability lane, or is `covered_by` a passing test; pending lines name their owner.

## Tests

`tests/security/identity.rs::sec_id_*`, `agents.rs::sec_ag_*` (each surface: MCP via rmcp client, HTTP, CLI, skill.md commands for the public-link refusal), `guests.rs::sec_gu_*`, `render.rs::sec_rs_*`, `ops.rs::sec_op_*`. Each logs `event="sec.check"` and saves headers/bodies (secrets redacted) to `target/e2e-logs/security/<id>/`.

## References

title: T38.c: Real-device pass (iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, Telegram in-app) + 5-minute Telegram passkey test
description:
## Goal and why

A virtual authenticator can't see OS prompts, Safari's tracking prevention or Telegram's in-app webview. The household opens links on phones, often from chat, so these must be checked on real devices before each phase's sign-off, and the Telegram passkey question must have a recorded answer for Slice 1.

## Scope

- Checklist file `tests/manual/real-device-pass.md` and dated results `tests/manual/results/<date>-<device>.md` (device, OS version, browser/app version, tester role "the admin" or "a family member", pass/fail per item, notes, screenshots stored outside the public repo if they show anything private).
- Items (verbatim from §7): standalone open, part-host open (first open and reload), embedding (pending T64), invite acceptance (pending T94), sign-in. Plus the §3a/§4a.7 budgets observable only on devices: sign in after session expiry = 2 interactions (passkey from autofill + biometric); open a part I may see when signed in = 0 interactions; public link + copy (admin) = 3 + 1 biometric.
- **Telegram in-app browser passkey test (5 minutes, real phone):** open a part link posted in Telegram while signed out, sign in with a passkey inside Telegram's in-app browser, land on the part. Record pass/fail with versions.
  - If it fails: (1) set Telegram to open links in the normal browser (document the setting per platform in `docs/ops/telegram.md`), and (2) Hermes' messages hint "open in browser" (file the change against T58, the Hermes skill; until T58 lands, record it as a required behaviour). Then **re-run the test** with the fixes and record the second result.
  - The person-bound-link fallback is rejected; do not build it.
- Run the pass against the example deployment and once against the portability-lane deployment exposed via a test domain if feasible.

## Not in scope

Automated e2e (T38.a/b, T97); Hermes code (T58).

## Design notes and decisions

- Keep results free of personal data (public repo): no names, no real part titles, no account identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dated result exists for iPhone Safari, Android Chrome and Telegram in-app browser covering every existing item.
- [ ] The Telegram passkey result is recorded; on failure, both fixes are applied/documented and a re-test is recorded.

## Tests

Manual by design; `tests/security/checklist.yaml` points at the result files, and a CI check (`scripts/check_manual_records.sh`) fails if a required record for the current phase is missing or older than the phase's sign-off date.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "Telegram in-app browser and passkeys: decided", §3a UX click budgets (manual pass on a real iPhone, an Android phone and the Telegram in-app browser), §7 Operations (real-device pass), §5f (Telegram stays in the matrix), decision 36; Slice 1 definition of done item 8.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A dated result exists for iPhone Safari, Android Chrome and Telegram in-app browser covering every existing item.
- [ ] The Telegram passkey result is recorded; on failure, both fixes are applied/documented and a re-test is recorded.

title: T93: Portability lane: full e2e with no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea (Dex, IdP-less, Caddy, local exports)
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory must not depend on the stack its first deployment happens to run (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes, the Nest). Each is an adapter behind config with a vendor-free default (decision 22). The **portability lane** proves it: a CI job runs the **full e2e suite** with none of those vendors, from the published compose file, and it **gates every release** (decision 24), "so a hidden dependency on the example deployment's stack fails CI the day it's introduced".

After Slice 1 (P1); feeds M1 ("the portability lane is green").

## Scope

The lane (PLAN §5f, verbatim): runs "the **full e2e suite** (the §4a.7 click budgets, the §7 checks that don't name an adapter, cross-surface conformance and an export/import round trip) with **no Cloudflare, no Authentik and no Gitea**":
- **Dex** as the OIDC provider (static users and groups, refresh tokens on), with a second pass using no IdP at all (local passkey accounts only, admin via `partifactory admin bootstrap`);
- **Caddy** in front with a locally issued wildcard cert for a test domain, using `X-Forwarded-For` as the client-IP header;
- **local exports** to a folder, then `import` into a fresh container;
- **Podman** instead of Docker for the backends pass (joins when P2a lands: both pixel-editor tests, T97 and T104);
- run from the published compose file with secrets as `_FILE` mounts, on a stock CI runner (the workflow is written for GitHub Actions, the same steps a shell script runs locally: `scripts/portability_lane.sh`).

Reuses the T24 e2e harness (Dex, Caddy with an internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`, `--host-resolver-rules` for Chromium and `/etc/hosts` for WebKit).

Concretely:
- `scripts/portability_lane.sh`: build image → `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --profile proxy up` with a lane override (Dex service, Caddy using `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile`, `_FILE` secrets) → run suites → export → bring up a fresh container → import → re-run a smoke subset → repeat with the IdP-less config.
- Suites run: T97 `communal_pixel_editor`, T57 cross-surface conformance, T38 non-adapter §7 lines, the §4a.7 click-budget specs from T31/T120, T35 round trip, `doctor` (T68) expecting all-ok except layer 1 "unknown", and each example proxy config smoke test (Caddy here; nginx/Traefik from T126).
- **No-vendor guard**: a script greps the lane's compose override, env and `site.toml` for Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea settings (`cloudflare`, `cfargotunnel`, `authentik`, `gitea`, `PF_TUNNEL_TOKEN`, `PF_DNS_API_TOKEN`, `PF_IDP_PROVISIONER_TOKEN`, `PF_CDN_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`) and fails on any match.
- **Adapter-removal build**: the lane builds the binary with the adapter crates (`pf-adapter-cloudflare`, `pf-adapter-authentik`) excluded via cargo features and runs the suite against that build.
- **No network to vendor APIs**: the runner's egress to vendor API hosts is blocked (or the job runs with a network policy / `--network` restriction) and the lane still passes.
- Release gate: the release script refuses to tag unless the lane passed on the same commit.

## Not in scope

The e2e harness itself (T24), the individual suites (their tasks), adapter-specific lines (T91, T92), nginx/Traefik configs (T126).

## Design notes and decisions

- *What stays coupled on purpose* (§5f): one registrable domain (cookie model needs same-site), WebAuthn passkeys, OCI + compose, the default mirror CDNs (a compatibility target; in the lane, mirror fetches go to a local fixture CDN via the allowlist config so the lane has no internet dependency), the Telegram in-app browser in the manual matrix.
- Device-connect origin without proxy geo headers shows "origin unknown" in the lane; the request-age banner still fires.
- Keep the lane's runtime under ~30 minutes; parallelise the Dex and IdP-less passes.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "The lane passes on a stock CI runner with no network access to any vendor API; grepping the lane's config and env finds no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea setting; removing any adapter crate from the build leaves it green".

- [ ] Lane green with Dex and with no IdP, from the published compose file with `_FILE` secrets.
- [ ] Export → fresh container → import round trip passes inside the lane.
- [ ] No-vendor grep passes; a deliberately added Cloudflare key makes it fail (self-test).
- [ ] Build without adapter crates passes the suite.
- [ ] Vendor API egress blocked; lane still green.
- [ ] Release tagging refuses a commit without a green lane.

## Tests

- `.github/workflows/portability.yml` invoking `scripts/portability_lane.sh` (example workflow; the script is the contract).
- `scripts/check_no_vendor.sh` with a self-test fixture.
- Artifacts per suite under `target/e2e-logs/portability/<pass>/<suite>/` (server JSONL, Caddy access log, Dex log, Playwright traces), and a summary JSON `{pass, suites: [{name, ok, duration_s}]}`.

## References

PLAN.md §5f Portability (table, "Proving it: the portability lane", "What stays coupled, on purpose"), §7 intro (non-adapter lines run in the lane), §3a (IdP-less deployment, `admin bootstrap`), §6 P1 Done when, decisions 22, 24.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): The lane passes on a stock CI runner with no network access to any vendor API; grepping the lane's config and env finds no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea setting; removing any adapter crate from the build leaves it green
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report
  - T37: Deliverable: amd64 OCI image + deploy/compose.yaml + env contract + `partifactory deploy` with auto rollback
  - T89: Ingress contract: trusted client-IP header, request ids, Caddy example + maintenance page
  - T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install
  - T126: Deliverable extras after Slice 1: nginx/Traefik configs, arm64, SBOM, cosign, example CI workflows
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: S1 (the lane runs `communal_pixel_editor`, the conformance suite, the §7 non-adapter lines and the retention test) and T68 (the lane runs `doctor` and expects all-ok).
- Tests add: every `event="mirror.fetch"` in the lane names the local fixture CDN host only (no internet dependency).
- Split into T93.a / T93.b (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: The lane passes on a stock CI runner with no network access to any vendor API; grepping the lane's config and env finds no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea setting; removing any adapter crate from the build leaves it green

title: T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups
description:
## Goal and why

Give partifactory a first-party, admin-only analytics and observability store that never touches the main database's writer and never holds part content. Every later Insights feature (traces T106, the log index T107, the Insights pages T108, the Debug tab T109, backend observability T110, the OTLP adapter T111) writes to or reads from this file.

Why a second SQLite file: a busy day of views and traces is many small writes. Keeping them off `partifactory.db` keeps the save path's latency where the performance targets say it is (`part_edit` small edit p99 < 10 ms), and losing `insights.db` loses nothing anyone needs to restore. It is in exports only with `--include-insights` (T34).

Why collect from P1 even though the pages land in P2 (T108): "Collection starts in P1 (in the content listener), so nothing is lost before the Insights pages land." This task is after Slice 1 (not in `S1`), in phase P1, milestone M1 via T112.

Overarching goals served: self-hosted, no third parties, no content in logs or analytics ("only ids, op names, argument keys, sizes, statuses and timings"), safe defaults, every growing store capped (its prune and rollup jobs plug into the janitor T113).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead: close it only after both subtasks are closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- `T105.a` — the `insights.db` file, its own writer task, schema migration and the `events_raw` collection API, wired into every surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI-driven HTTP, UI, part host, `/_rt`; backends from P2a) including view and public-link-open collection in the content listener.
- `T105.b` — viewer-key hashing with the rotating in-memory salt, the daily rollup job into `rollups_daily`, and the prune job (raw events 30 days) registered with the janitor.

The file and its DDL (verbatim, first two tables; the rest belong to T106/T107/T113 but are created by the same migration set):

```sql
-- /data/insights.db: analytics and observability (§5g). A separate file with its own writer.
-- Never part content: ids, op names, argument keys, sizes, statuses and timings only (a CI fuzz test checks it).
CREATE TABLE events_raw (                            -- kept 30 d, then only in rollups_daily
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'view','op','rt','grant_decision','build','backend','link_open', ...
  surface     TEXT CHECK (surface IN ('mcp','http','cli','ui','part','rt','backend')),
  op          TEXT,                                  -- registry op name or route class
  part_id     TEXT,
  actor       TEXT,                                  -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | guest:<link>:<g> | link:<id> | NULL
  viewer_key  BLOB,                                  -- public viewers and guests: hash(truncated IP, UA, rotating salt)
  status      TEXT,                                  -- 'ok' or an error code
  latency_us  INTEGER,
  bytes_in    INTEGER,
  bytes_out   INTEGER,
  request_id  TEXT,
  attrs       TEXT CHECK (attrs IS NULL OR json_valid(attrs))  -- {arg_keys, build_method, kind, ...}; never values
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX events_raw_at ON events_raw(at);
CREATE INDEX events_raw_part ON events_raw(part_id, at) WHERE part_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX events_raw_actor ON events_raw(actor, at) WHERE actor IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE rollups_daily (                         -- kept indefinitely; small
  day     INTEGER NOT NULL,                          -- days since epoch, UTC
  metric  TEXT NOT NULL,                             -- 'views','uniques','ops','errors','builds_ok','cold_starts','guest_writes', ...
  dim     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',                  -- 'part:<id>' | 'conn:<id>' | 'op:<name>' | 'method:server_build' | ''
  value   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (day, metric, dim)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

The migration set for `insights.db` also creates `traces`, `spans` (used by T106), `log_segments` (T107) and `janitor_runs` (T113) exactly as in the plan's insights DDL block, so the file has one schema version.

Analytics content (from the plan): views per part per day and unique viewers (signed-in = principal; public-link viewers and guests = a hash of the truncated IP + UA with a salt that lives in memory and rotates daily), per-public-link open count and last opened (the authoritative counter is `public_links.open_count` in the main DB, incremented by T29; this store records a `link_open` event for charts), and last viewed. Per-part counts also show on each part's Details and are readable by agents via `part_get` (exposed by later UI/op work; this task provides the query). No third-party scripts, no cross-part tracking.

Retention: raw events kept 30 days, daily rollups indefinitely (§5h rows "Insights raw events: 30 days, prune job, CSV/JSON export from Insights" and "Insights daily rollups: indefinitely (tiny)").

## Not in scope

- Traces and spans persistence (T106), log segments (T107), the content-free fuzz test (T112).
- The janitor framework itself (T113) — this task registers jobs with it without a dag edge ("its prune and rollup jobs plug into the janitor (T113) without an edge"). If T113 has not landed when this is built, register via the job trait T113 defines, or leave a TODO bead comment; the jobs must be registered before T115's retention test row for Insights raw events is added.
- Insights UI pages (T108), backend metrics (T110), OTLP export (T111).
- `--include-insights` export flag plumbing is T34; this task only guarantees the file is self-contained and closeable for a consistent `VACUUM INTO`.

## Design notes and decisions

- Separate writer: same pattern as T05 (one writer task, a read pool), but a separate connection set and file. Writes are batched (e.g. an mpsc channel drained every 50 ms or 500 events) so a burst doesn't create per-event transactions. If the channel is full, drop events and increment `pf_insights_dropped_total` rather than block a request: analytics must never back-pressure serving.
- `synchronous=NORMAL` is acceptable here (losing the last second of analytics on power loss is fine), unlike the main DB's `synchronous=FULL`.
- Never content: the collection API takes typed fields only (`ArgKeys(Vec<&'static str>)` derived from the op's input schema field names, sizes as integers). There is no `String` field for free text except `status` (an error code enum) and `op` (a registry name or route class). Make wrong use a compile error, not a convention.
- IP handling: truncate (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48), concatenate with UA, HMAC-SHA256 with a 32-byte salt generated in memory at start and rotated daily at UTC midnight; the old salt is zeroized and dropped. Uniques therefore over-count on restart days ("Accepted", §5e modelling decisions). No raw IP is ever written.
- The client IP comes from the trusted ingress header (T89); without a trusted header, no viewer key is computed (NULL).
- Rollup job: idempotent per day (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`), recomputes yesterday and today so late events land; metrics at least `views`, `uniques`, `ops`, `errors`, `builds_ok`, `guest_writes`, `link_opens`, with dims as in the DDL comment.
- Collection hooks are a `tower` layer on the workspace listener (ops, UI) and on the content listener (views of entry documents, `/l/<token>/go` opens, `/_rt` calls), plus explicit calls from the build worker and grant decisions. A "view" is one served entry document (not each blob).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A burst of 10k events leaves `partifactory.db` writer latency unchanged; rollups match a fixture; no raw IP is stored (schema test); a rotated salt is gone from memory."

- [ ] `/data/insights.db` is created and migrated at start, independent of `partifactory.db`, with its own writer task.
- [ ] A 10k-event burst does not change the main writer's p99 commit latency beyond noise (≤ 5 % in the bench harness) and never blocks a request.
- [ ] Every surface records `events_raw` rows with op, surface, actor, status, latency, sizes, arg keys and request id; never values.
- [ ] Views and public-link opens are collected in the content listener.
- [ ] `viewer_key` is an HMAC with the daily in-memory salt; no column or attr anywhere holds an IP (schema test + row scan).
- [ ] After rotation the previous salt bytes are zeroized (test via a debug hook).
- [ ] Daily rollups match a fixture exactly; re-running a rollup is idempotent.
- [ ] Prune (30 d) and rollup jobs are registered with the janitor and write `janitor_runs` rows.

## Tests

- `pf_obs::insights::tests::schema_has_no_ip_columns` — introspects every table/column; fails on names like `ip`, `addr`, `remote`.
- `pf_obs::insights::tests::viewer_key_salt_rotation` — key changes across rotation; old salt zeroized.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/insights_burst.rs::burst_10k_does_not_slow_main_writer` — measures main writer commit p99 with and without the burst; asserts log event `event="insights.batch_flushed"` counts and no `event="insights.dropped"` at that rate.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/rollups_fixture.rs::rollups_match_fixture` — golden `tests/golden/insights/rollups_2026-10-23.json`.
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/view_collection.rs::entry_view_and_link_open_recorded` — asserts `kind=view`/`link_open` rows with request ids matching the response `X-Request-Id`.
- Log assertions: `event="insights.salt_rotated"` (no salt value logged), `event="janitor.job" store="insights_raw"`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g Insights; §5e Data model (insights.db DDL; modelling decision "Public-link and guest uniques"); §5d Analytics; §5h Disk safety (Insights rows); §6 P1; §6a notes ("the Insights store (T105) ... add their janitor jobs"); decision 32.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A burst of 10k events leaves `partifactory.db` writer latency unchanged; rollups match a fixture; no raw IP is stored (schema test); a rotated salt is gone from memory
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T05: SQLite layer: read pool, single writer task, pragmas, embedded forward-only migrations
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T18: Logs + metrics: redacted JSON tracing, Prometheus on :9090 behind PF_METRICS_TOKEN, /healthz, /readyz skeleton
- Unblocks: 
  - T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
  - T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters
  - T112: No-content-in-logs fuzz test: canaries across every surface never reach logs, traces, insights.db or /metrics
  - T108: Insights UI (admin-only, Stockroom): Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds pages with table views and CSV/JSON export
  - G04: Part menu extras: ?dl=1 downloads, Download as zip, Pin, Open standalone, thumbnails endpoint with SVG spec-sheet thumbs, view counts
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T105.a: insights.db file, its own writer, migrations and events_raw collection on every surface
  - T105.b: Salted viewer keys, daily rollups into rollups_daily, and the 30-day raw-event prune job

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T29 (link-open collection on `POST /l/<token>/go`).
- `insights.db` already exists when this task starts: T113.a opens it and applies T06.e's migration set (the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there from Slice 1). T105.a **adopts that handle** for `events_raw`, rollups, traces and segments; it does not re-author the DDL or move any table.

title: T105.a: insights.db file, its own writer, migrations and events_raw collection on every surface
description:
## Goal and why

Create the second SQLite file and the typed, content-free collection path that every surface uses. Keeping analytics writes off the main writer protects the save path (`part_edit` p99 < 10 ms) and keeps `insights.db` disposable.

## Scope

- Open `/data/insights.db` (WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`, STRICT tables) with its own writer task and read pool, reusing T05's pool/writer pattern but fully separate connections.
- Embedded forward-only migrations for the whole insights DDL block: `events_raw` (+ indexes `events_raw_at`, `events_raw_part`, `events_raw_actor`), `rollups_daily`, `traces` (+ `traces_at`, `traces_request`), `spans`, `log_segments` (+ `log_segments_stream`), `janitor_runs` (+ `janitor_runs_store`), verbatim from the plan.
- `InsightsSink` API: `record(Event)` where `Event` is a typed struct: `kind` (enum: view, op, rt, grant_decision, build, backend, link_open, ...), `surface` (enum mcp|http|cli|ui|part|rt|backend), `op` (registry name or route class, `&'static str`), `part_id`, `actor`, `viewer_key: Option<[u8;32]>`, `status` (`ok` or an error-catalogue code enum), `latency_us`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `request_id`, `attrs` (typed: `arg_keys`, `build_method`, `kind`). No free-text field.
- Bounded channel + batch flush (≤ 50 ms or 500 rows per transaction); on overflow drop and count (`pf_insights_dropped_total`).
- Hooks: a `tower` layer on the workspace listener (API ops with arg keys from the registry input schema, MCP tool calls, UI routes) and on the content listener (entry-document views, `POST /l/<token>/go` link opens, `/_rt` ops by op name), plus calls from grant decisions and the build worker. Backends are wired later (T110).

## Not in scope

Salt/viewer-key computation and rollups (T105.b), traces (T106), log segments (T107), UI (T108).

## Design notes and decisions

- Types make content leaks a compile error; `attrs` is a serde struct, not a free JSON map.
- Analytics must never back-pressure serving: drop, don't block.
- A view = one served entry document (not every blob request), so counts mean "opens".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The file is created and migrated at start; a test opens both DBs and asserts disjoint connections.
- [ ] Every surface produces `events_raw` rows with request ids; arg keys present, values absent.
- [ ] 10k-event burst: main writer p99 unchanged (≤ 5 %).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-obs/tests/insights_migrations.rs::applies_from_empty_and_n_minus_1`.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/insights_burst.rs::burst_10k_does_not_slow_main_writer` (asserts `event="insights.batch_flushed"`, no `insights.dropped`).
- `crates/pf-api/tests/insights_hooks.rs::op_call_records_arg_keys_not_values` (canary value in input never appears in the row).
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/view_collection.rs::entry_view_and_link_open_recorded`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g; §5e insights.db DDL; §5d Analytics; §5a performance targets.

- Parent task: T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Apply, don't author: the insights migration set is T06.e's and is already applied at start by T113.a. This subtask reuses that `Db` handle (its writer task) for collection and adds no second migration set. Test `insights_db_shared_with_janitor`: `janitor_runs` and `events_raw` live in the same file.

title: T105.b: Salted viewer keys, daily rollups into rollups_daily, and the 30-day raw-event prune job
description:
## Goal and why

Count unique public viewers and guests without ever storing an IP, and keep only small daily rollups beyond 30 days, so the store stays bounded (every growing store is capped) and privacy-preserving.

## Scope

- Viewer key: `HMAC-SHA256(salt, truncated_ip || 0x00 || user_agent)`; IPv4 truncated to /24, IPv6 to /48; IP from the trusted client-IP header only (T89); NULL when untrusted/absent. Signed-in viewers use their principal as the actor instead.
- Salt: 32 random bytes in memory only, rotated daily at 00:00 UTC and at start; the old salt is zeroized (`zeroize` crate) and dropped. Uniques over-count on restart days (accepted in the plan).
- Rollup job (`insights_rollup`, daily + on demand): recompute yesterday and today into `rollups_daily(day, metric, dim, value)` with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`. Metrics: `views`, `uniques`, `ops`, `errors`, `builds_ok`, `guest_writes`, `link_opens` (more added by later tasks, e.g. `cold_starts` in T110); dims `part:<id>`, `conn:<id>`, `op:<name>`, `method:<build method>`, `''`.
- Prune job (`insights_raw`): delete `events_raw` rows older than 30 days, only after the rollup for those days exists. Both jobs are registered with the janitor (T113) through its job trait (no dag edge) and record `janitor_runs` rows (`action` = `prune`).

## Not in scope

Rollup UI and CSV/JSON export (T108); traces/log retention (T106/T107).

## Design notes and decisions

- Prune never runs ahead of rollup, so no data is lost from charts.
- No raw IP anywhere: not in rows, attrs, logs or metrics (T112 also fuzzes this).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rollups match a fixture; re-running is idempotent.
- [ ] No raw IP stored (schema test + scanning all rows/attrs for the test IPs).
- [ ] A rotated salt is gone from memory.
- [ ] Raw events older than 30 days are pruned only after rollup; `janitor_runs` records it.

## Tests

- `pf_obs::insights::viewer_key::tests::truncation_and_hmac`, `::salt_rotation_zeroizes`.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/rollups_fixture.rs::rollups_match_fixture` (golden `tests/golden/insights/rollups.json`), `::rollup_idempotent`.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/insights_prune.rs::prune_after_rollup_only` (asserts `event="janitor.job" store="insights_raw" action="prune" items=N`).
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/insights_no_ip.rs::no_ip_anywhere` with test IPs `203.0.113.7` / `2001:db8::7` searched in every column.

## References

PLAN.md §5g rules; §5d Analytics; §5e modelling decision "Public-link and guest uniques"; §5h Insights rows.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T105.a: insights.db file, its own writer, migrations and events_raw collection on every surface

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- `viewer_key` is NULL (not a hash of an empty string) when the trusted client-IP header is absent; test `no_trusted_header_no_viewer_key`.

title: T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
description:
## Goal and why

One provider-neutral policy engine that answers "may this principal do this to this part?" for every surface: `/grant` (T27), every op (T20+), `/_rt` (T62, T96), the chrome API (T29), guests (T95) and backends (T101). Sharing is a security boundary in partifactory (it's reachable from the internet with per-person audiences), so the engine is central to the threat model.

Why:
- Grants refer to provider-neutral subjects (`user:<id>`, `group:<name>`, `everyone-signed-in`, `link:<id>`, `conn:<id>`), so changing IdP changes config, not policy data.
- **Space grants are inherited live** ("everything in Family is the family's" has to stay true when someone joins later; copying grants at creation would quietly leave new members out).
- The **role × runtime matrix** is what makes communal pages work (viewers may write shared data by default, as in Claude) while keeping code changes to editors, and it defines exactly what guests can and can't do.
- Every grant change is audited ("who, actor, what, before → after").
- In Slice 1; on the sign-in lane (T25 → T26 → T27) and required by T31, T43, T50, T52, T83, T94, T96, T101.

## Scope

- Crate `pf-policy`. Inputs: principal (person via session, agent connection = person + scopes + spaces, link viewer, guest `{link, g}`, `render`), target part (or space), action.
- **Roles**: `view` (0) < `comment` (1) < `edit` (2) < `manage` (3). **Effective role = max(part grants, space grants)** for all subjects matching the principal: `user:<id>`, each `group:<name>` the user is in (from the directory, T25), `everyone-signed-in` (members of `audience_group` + every active local account). Owner (`parts.owner_user_id`) has `manage` on their own parts; the admin (T28) is checked separately for admin actions (not via grants). No per-part "restrict below the space" in v1.
- Agents: an agent can't see or do more than its person; effective = person's role ∩ connection scopes, and the part's space must be in the connection's `spaces` (else `not_found` for reads — an error never confirms what's behind a name — and `forbidden {space}` for writes into a space).
- `grants` table (T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE grants (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  target_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (target_kind IN ('part','space')),
  target_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (subject GLOB 'user:*' OR subject GLOB 'group:*' OR subject = 'everyone-signed-in'),
  role        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (role BETWEEN 0 AND 3),  -- view, comment, edit, manage
  expires_at  INTEGER,
  created_by  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  created_by_conn TEXT,                              -- set when an agent made it (share:household)
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (target_kind, target_id, subject)
) STRICT;
```
- **Role × runtime matrix** (enforced in `/_rt` and every op), exposed as `policy.rt_allowed(principal, part, rt_op)`:

| | personal state | shared `storage` / `db` | comments | self-publish | source edit | assets upload | backend calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| public-link viewer (Can view) | memory only | read | only if opted in | no | no | no | as `role: public` |
| public-link guest (Can contribute) | memory only | read, **write** (rate-limited, size-capped) | no | no | no | no | as `role: guest` |
| `view` | read/write | read, **write unless `shared_data_writers: "editors"`** | no | no | no | no | as `role: view` |
| `comment` | read/write | as `view` | yes | no | no | yes | as `role: comment` |
| `edit` / `manage` | read/write | read/write | yes | yes | yes | yes | as `role: edit` / `manage` |

- **Who may write shared data**: `parts.shared_data_writers` `'editors' | 'viewers'` (default `'viewers'`): edit/manage and owner always; signed-in view/comment unless `editors`; Can-view link guests never; Can-contribute guests yes within limits. Switching a link to Can contribute sets `viewers`; setting `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes that link (the coupling itself is implemented in T95; the engine exposes the rule).
- Guests: a guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) → 403; guests hold no token so `/api` and `/mcp` are closed.
- `manage` in v1 = edit + see the audit log + change inward grants; never outward sharing. Owners and `manage` grantees share inward; only the admin shares outward (public links, everyone-signed-in, invites, groups).
- **Grant API** (used by the share sheet T31/T120 and agents T52): `set_grant`, `revoke_grant`, `move_part(space)` (needs write on both spaces). Every change writes **one `audit` row** (`user_id`, `actor` `conn:<id>`|`break-glass`|`system`|NULL, `action` e.g. `grant.set`/`grant.revoke`/`part.move`, `target_kind`, `target_id`, `before`/`after` JSON, `request_id`) and bumps `epochs['part:<id>']` (or every part in the space for space grants) on any revoke or narrowing.
- **Expiry timer**: grants (and public links, T29) with `expires_at` are enforced by a timer that bumps the part epoch when the expiry passes (otherwise a cap minted before expiry would outlive the grant until its window ends).
- Decision records: every decision returns a structured `Decision {allowed, role, reason, matched_grants}`; denials are logged (`event="policy.decide" outcome="deny" reason=...`) so the Debug tab (T109) can show "the cap and grant decisions that denied access".

## Not in scope

- `/grant` and cap minting (T27); public links and guests (T29, T95); admin pin and step-up (T28); the share-sheet UI (T31, T120); agent sharing ops `part_share` (T52); ask for access (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why owners can share inward without the admin:* sharing with someone who already has an account can't leak beyond the household, and gating it made the common case slow. Everything outward stays with the admin because that's where data leaves.
- `not_found` for parts outside a principal's view, never `forbidden`.
- Live inheritance over copy-at-create (round 2, V over F).
- Viewer-writable data by default matches Claude's artifact semantics (a poll works for everyone who can see it); `editors` makes a dashboard read-only.
- Round-1 O5 ("grants are admin-only in v1") was superseded: owners share inward; outward is admin-only.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Property test: no subject gets a role above its best matching grant; a `view` grantee can write shared data only while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a Can-view guest never writes; every grant change writes one audit row".

- [ ] Effective role = max over matching part and space grants; space grants inherited live (a grant added to a space applies to its parts at once).
- [ ] Property test: no principal ever gets a role above its best matching grant; agents never exceed their person.
- [ ] The full role × runtime matrix is table-tested, including guest rows.
- [ ] `shared_data_writers` toggling changes view-grantee writes exactly as specified.
- [ ] Every grant set/revoke/move writes exactly one audit row with before/after; revokes bump the part epoch.
- [ ] Expired grants stop working at expiry (epoch bump by the timer), tested with a test clock.
- [ ] `everyone-signed-in` resolves to audience members + active local accounts only.

## Tests

- `pf_policy::tests::prop_no_role_above_best_grant` (proptest over random grant sets, groups and spaces).
- `pf_policy::tests::rt_matrix_table` (every row × column), `shared_data_writers_toggle`, `guest_non_data_ops_forbidden`, `agent_bounded_by_person_and_spaces`.
- `pf_policy::tests::space_grant_live_inheritance`, `move_needs_both_spaces`.
- `crates/pf-policy/tests/audit.rs::one_audit_row_per_change` (asserts `event="grant.set"` log line and the audit row content).
- `crates/pf-policy/tests/expiry.rs::grant_expiry_bumps_epoch` (test clock; asserts `event="epoch.bump" reason="grant_expired"`).
- `everyone_signed_in_excludes_non_audience`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Who can see a part: the audience ladder; What each role can do at runtime; Who may write shared data; Spaces; "Can contribute" public links; §2 core idea (Grant, Space); §5e `grants`, `audit`, `epochs`, hot-path rules (expiry timer); docs/agent-contract.md "Who can write shared data". Decisions 13, 15. dag2.py T26.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Property test: no subject gets a role above its best matching grant; a `view` grantee can write shared data only while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a Can-view guest never writes; every grant change writes one audit row
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
  - T25: Generic directory: groups claim + 15-min refresh re-read, invalid_grant ends session, local pf-* groups, epoch bumps, fail open when IdP down
- Unblocks: 
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
  - T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
  - T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
  - T83: Viewer asset uploads: assets.put over /_rt, /_a/<id>, quota, listed and deletable by agents
  - G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change
acceptance_criteria: Property test: no subject gets a role above its best matching grant; a `view` grantee can write shared data only while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a Can-view guest never writes; every grant change writes one audit row

title: T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
description:
## Goal and why

Make "why did this break?" answerable from a single id. Every request gets a request id that is shown to people (error pages, API errors) and carried into builds, `/_rt` and (P2a) backends; its `tracing` spans are kept when they matter (every error, every slow request, a 1 % sample). The trace waterfall (T109) and "from a 403 page's request id, reach the denying decision in 3 clicks" depend on this.

After Slice 1 (P1, feeds M1 via T112, and T109/T111/T101). Serves the "Insights in the workspace" goal without any third-party tracing backend (OTLP export is the optional T111).

## Scope

Request ids:
- Taken from the ingress header named by `[ingress] request_id_header` (e.g. `CF-Ray` or `X-Request-Id`) when present from a trusted proxy (T89), otherwise generated (ULID-like, prefixed `req_`).
- Present in: every JSON log line (`request_id` field), the response header `X-Request-Id`, every API/MCP error body (`details.request_id` on `internal`; the 500 page "partifactory hit an error. It's been logged as `req 8f1c…`."), every error page, `audit.request_id`, `events_raw.request_id`.
- Propagated: to the build child (in the CBOR job envelope; the child logs with it), to `/_rt` handlers, to render jobs, and from P2a to backends as `X-PF-Request-Id` (T101 adds the header; this task provides the propagation context).

Trace store (in `insights.db`, DDL verbatim):

```sql
CREATE TABLE traces (                                -- tail-sampled: every error, every slow request, 1 % of the rest; 7 d, 2 GiB
  trace_id     BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  request_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  duration_us  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  root         TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- route class or op
  status       TEXT NOT NULL,
  part_id      TEXT,
  actor        TEXT,
  kept_because TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kept_because IN ('error','slow','sample'))
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX traces_at ON traces(started_at);
CREATE INDEX traces_request ON traces(request_id);

CREATE TABLE spans (
  trace_id    BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES traces(trace_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  span_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  parent_id   INTEGER,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'policy.decide','sqlite.write','build.child','runner.start', ...
  start_us    INTEGER NOT NULL,                      -- offset from the trace start
  duration_us INTEGER NOT NULL,
  fields      TEXT CHECK (fields IS NULL OR json_valid(fields)),
  PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

- A `tracing` `Layer` collects spans per request into an in-memory ring buffer (bounded; e.g. 64 MiB / N in-flight requests); at request end a tail-sampling decision keeps the trace if status is an error, duration > slow threshold (**500 ms by default**, config `[insights] slow_ms`), or a 1 % random sample; otherwise discarded.
- Kept traces are written through the insights writer (T105). Span `fields` hold only the redacted, typed fields allowed in logs (ids, op names, arg keys, sizes, statuses, timings).
- Retention: 7 days and 2 GiB total (whichever first), as a janitor prune job (`traces`), oldest first; `janitor_runs` rows.
- Download a trace as JSON (API for T109; UI in T109).

## Not in scope

The waterfall UI (T109), OTLP export (T111), the log pipeline (T107), backend header injection itself (T101), the fuzz test (T112).

## Design notes and decisions

- Tail sampling (decide after the request) is what makes "every error is kept" possible with bounded storage; head sampling would lose rare failures.
- Spans are shared with logs: the same `tracing` instrumentation feeds JSON logs (T18) and the ring; no second instrumentation API.
- Request id from ingress only when the sender is in `trusted_proxies`; a spoofed header from elsewhere is ignored (same rule as the client-IP header).
- Overhead target: the ring layer must not move the part-blob p99 (< 200 µs tracked); spans on the DB-free blob path are minimal (one span).
- Size cap enforced both by the janitor and by a write-time check (refuse to persist sampled-only traces when over 2 GiB; errors still kept by dropping oldest first).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A failing request's id from its error page finds its full trace; a slow request is always kept and a fast ok one about 1 % of the time; the store stays under 2 GiB in a load test."

- [ ] Every response carries `X-Request-Id`; error pages and API errors show it; logs, audit rows and events_raw carry it.
- [ ] Ingress-supplied ids are used only from trusted proxies.
- [ ] The id reaches the build child logs, `/_rt` handler logs and render-job logs.
- [ ] Error traces kept 100 %; > 500 ms kept 100 %; fast ok ≈ 1 % (binomial test).
- [ ] Load test keeps traces + spans < 2 GiB and prunes past 7 days.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-obs/tests/request_id.rs::generated_when_absent`, `::ingress_header_trusted_only`, `::propagated_to_build_child` (asserts the child's log line carries the same `request_id`).
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/tail_sampling.rs::errors_and_slow_always_kept`, `::sample_rate_about_one_percent` (10k fast requests, expect 100 ± 40).
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/trace_store_cap.rs::stays_under_2gib` (scaled-down cap in test config, same code path) and `::prunes_after_7_days` (test clock).
- E2E `tests/e2e/error_page_request_id.spec.ts`: provoke a 500 via a test hook, read `req …` from the page, fetch the trace by request id via the admin API; artifacts: `target/e2e-logs/error_page_request_id/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g Debugging; §5d Logs; §3 ingress contract (`request_id_header`); §5e insights.db DDL (`traces`, `spans`); §5h "Traces and spans: 7 days, 2 GiB, tail-sampled"; §4a.6 error pages.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A failing request's id from its error page finds its full trace; a slow request is always kept and a fast ok one about 1 % of the time; the store stays under 2 GiB in a load test
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T18: Logs + metrics: redacted JSON tracing, Prometheus on :9090 behind PF_METRICS_TOKEN, /healthz, /readyz skeleton
  - T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups
  - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
- Unblocks: 
  - T112: No-content-in-logs fuzz test: canaries across every surface never reach logs, traces, insights.db or /metrics
  - T109: Debugging UI: trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab (incl. denying decisions), per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail
  - T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
  - T111: Optional OTLP export adapter (traces, logs, metrics) to any collector; off by default, never required
  - G02: Workspace error pages (404 NOT IN STOCK, 410, 429, 500 with request id) and workspace PWA install

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Request-id ownership: T18 generates ids (`r_` + ULID) and puts them in the log field; T89 ingests the ingress header from trusted proxies; this task owns propagation (the build child's CBOR envelope, `/_rt`, render jobs, the backend header context) and the trace store. One prefix, `r_`; error pages show `req r_8f1c…`.
- The e2e that reads the id from a 500 page belongs to the error-page owner (T31.a/G02); this task's test is API-based: an `internal` error's `details.request_id` finds its trace through the admin API.
- `[insights] slow_ms` is a new config key: add `PF_INSIGHTS_SLOW_MS` to the generated env contract (T04's `docs/env.md`).
acceptance_criteria: A failing request's id from its error page finds its full trace; a slow request is always kept and a fast ok one about 1 % of the time; the store stays under 2 GiB in a load test

title: T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters
description:
## Goal and why

Keep a bounded, searchable on-disk copy of the app's structured logs so the admin can debug from the workspace (log viewer, T109) and export ranges, while stdout JSON stays on for any host collector. Logs are one of the stores that grow forever unless capped; this caps them at 7 days or 1 GiB.

After Slice 1 (P1; feeds T109, T111, T112 and M1). Portable: works with `docker logs`, any host collector, or optional push adapters, with no vendor dependency.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close after both subtasks close and acceptance passes end to end):
- `T107.a` — rotating zstd segment writer + `log_segments` index + janitor job and retention-test row.
- `T107.b` — `partifactory logs export --since|--part` and `logs tail`, and the optional push adapters (OTLP logs, syslog, HTTP JSON).

Verbatim from the plan:
- "JSON to stdout always; rotating zstd segments under `/data/logs` (daily + size, 7 days or 1 GiB) with a `log_segments` index; `partifactory logs export --since|--part` and `logs tail`; optional push adapters (OTLP logs, syslog, HTTP JSON); its janitor jobs and retention-test rows plug into T113 and T115 without an edge."
- §5h row: "App logs (structured JSON) | 7 days or 1 GiB in total, whichever comes first | size + daily rotation, zstd-compressed segments | the log viewer's 'download range'; `partifactory logs export --since`; stdout always (so `docker logs` and host collectors work); optional OTLP, syslog or HTTP JSON push".
- Layout: `/data/logs/` holds `app/` and `parts/<id>/` (the latter for backend logs, T110).

```sql
CREATE TABLE log_segments (                          -- index over /data/logs/**/*.jsonl.zst; the lines live in the files
  path      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                        -- 'app/2026-10-23T14-0001.jsonl.zst' | 'parts/<id>/backend-0042.jsonl.zst'
  stream    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (stream IN ('app','backend')),
  part_id   TEXT,
  first_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  bytes     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  lines     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  max_level TEXT CHECK (max_level IN ('trace','debug','info','warn','error')),
  CHECK ((stream = 'backend') = (part_id IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX log_segments_stream ON log_segments(stream, part_id, first_at);
```

## Not in scope

The log viewer UI and live tail in the browser (T109), backend log capture into `parts/<id>/` (T110; this task builds the segment writer it reuses), OTLP traces/metrics (T111 — T107.b's OTLP logs push should share T111's exporter config when it lands), redaction rules (T18).

## Design notes and decisions

- Stdout carries every line regardless of push adapters or disk segments ("stdout carries every line with a push adapter on or off"), so disabling the pipeline can never blind a host collector.
- Segments are written by a dedicated task from a bounded channel; on overflow the file sink drops (counted, `pf_log_segment_dropped_total`) but stdout still gets the line.
- The redaction happens before any sink (T18 layer), so segments and adapters inherit "no tokens, caps, cookies, content".
- The `log_segments` row is written when a segment closes (and updated periodically for the open one), so export can pick files by time without decompressing.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Segments rotate on size and on day and never exceed the cap; `logs export --since 1h` returns exactly the lines in range; stdout carries every line with a push adapter on or off."

- [ ] Rotation on UTC day change and on segment size; total ≤ 1 GiB and ≤ 7 days after the janitor runs.
- [ ] `logs export --since 1h` output equals the lines in range exactly (golden); `--part <name>` filters by part.
- [ ] `logs tail` streams new lines.
- [ ] Stdout line count equals produced line count with each adapter on and off.
- [ ] Janitor job and T115 retention row registered.

## Tests

See subtasks; plus `crates/pf-obs/tests/log_pipeline_e2e.rs::stdout_complete_with_adapters` (counts lines on stdout vs a deterministic generator with syslog + HTTP push enabled against local test receivers).

## References

PLAN.md §5h Disk safety (App logs row, "Logs out"); §5g Debugging (log viewer); §5d Logs; §5e insights.db `log_segments`; §5f Telemetry export row.

title: T107.a: Rotating zstd log segments under /data/logs with the log_segments index and cap job
description:
## Goal and why

Persist structured logs to disk in compressed, indexed segments, bounded at 7 days or 1 GiB, so the log viewer and exports work without an external log stack and the disk can't fill.

## Scope

- A `tracing` writer sink (after T18's redaction layer) that appends JSON lines into `/data/logs/app/<UTC ts>-<seq>.jsonl.zst`, rotating on UTC day change and when the current segment reaches a size threshold (default 16 MiB uncompressed or 64k lines; configurable within bounds).
- zstd streaming compression with periodic flush points (so an open segment is readable up to the last flush).
- Index rows in `insights.db` `log_segments(path, stream, part_id, first_at, last_at, bytes, lines, max_level)` written on close and updated for the open segment every 10 s.
- A reusable `SegmentWriter` with a `stream` parameter (`app` | `backend` + `part_id`) so T110 writes `parts/<id>/backend-NNNN.jsonl.zst` with the same code.
- Janitor job `app_logs`: delete oldest segments until total ≤ 1 GiB and none older than 7 days; record `janitor_runs` (`action` = `rotate`/`prune`). Register with T113 by its job trait (no dag edge) and add the "App logs" row to the T115 retention table test.

## Not in scope

Export/tail CLI and push adapters (T107.b); backend log capture (T110).

## Design notes and decisions

- Bounded channel; overflow drops to the file sink only (stdout unaffected), counted in metrics.
- Never exceed the cap even between janitor runs: the writer checks total bytes on rotation and triggers an early prune.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rotation on size and on day (test clock).
- [ ] Total never exceeds 1 GiB (scaled-down cap in test) and 7 days.
- [ ] `log_segments` rows match the files.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-obs/tests/log_segments.rs::rotates_on_size`, `::rotates_on_utc_day`, `::index_matches_files`, `::cap_enforced_on_rotation`.
- Retention row in `crates/pf-janitor/tests/retention_table.rs` (`app_logs` fill-past-cap case).
- Asserts log events `event="logs.segment_rotated" reason="size|day"` and `event="janitor.job" store="app_logs"`.

## References

PLAN.md §5h App logs row; §5e `log_segments` DDL.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Rotation on size and on day (test clock).
- [ ] Total never exceeds 1 GiB (scaled-down cap in test) and 7 days.
- [ ] `log_segments` rows match the files.

title: T107.b: partifactory logs export/tail and optional push adapters (OTLP logs, syslog, HTTP JSON)
description:
## Goal and why

Get logs out of the box in standard ways — a CLI for ranges and live tail, and optional pushes to whatever collector the operator runs — without making any of them required. "Logs out" is part of every store having an export path.

## Scope

- `partifactory logs export --since <dur|ts> [--until ...] [--part <name>] [--level <lvl>] [--request-id <id>] [-o file]`: selects segments via `log_segments` (time range, stream, part), decompresses, filters, writes JSON lines (or `.jsonl.zst` with `--zstd`). `--part` covers both app lines tagged with that part and its backend stream (`logs export --part` is also the export path for container stdout and backend logs per §5h).
- `partifactory logs tail [--part ...] [--level ...]`: follows the open segment (or an in-process broadcast when run against the server's ops listener).
- The same range-export function backs the log viewer's "download range" (UI in T109) through an admin API endpoint.
- Push adapters, all optional and off by default, configured in `site.toml` (e.g. `[logs.push] otlp_endpoint`, `syslog = "udp://host:514"` / tcp, `http_json_url` + HMAC or bearer secret from `PF_*` env/`_FILE`): batch, retry with backoff, bounded buffer, drop-and-count when the target is down. Never block stdout or the file sink.

## Not in scope

Log viewer UI (T109); OTLP traces/metrics (T111, which should reuse the OTLP logs exporter config).

## Design notes and decisions

- Exactness: export must return exactly the lines in range — boundary handling by line `ts`, not segment times.
- Adapters are part of the portability story (§5f Telemetry export row): none is required, all are vendor-neutral protocols.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `logs export --since 1h` returns exactly the lines in range (golden over a deterministic generator with a test clock).
- [ ] `--part` filtering works for app and backend streams.
- [ ] `logs tail` shows a new line within 1 s.
- [ ] With each adapter on and off, stdout carries every line; an unreachable target drops and counts without blocking.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-obs/tests/logs_export.rs::since_1h_exact`, `::part_filter`, `::request_id_filter`.
- `crates/partifactory/tests/cli_logs.rs::tail_shows_new_line_within_1s`.
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/push_adapters.rs::syslog_receives_lines`, `::http_json_receives_batches`, `::otlp_logs_to_local_collector`, `::target_down_does_not_block_stdout` (asserts `event="logs.push_dropped"` counts).

## References

PLAN.md §5h "Logs out" and App logs row; §5f Telemetry export row; §5g log viewer.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T107.a: Rotating zstd log segments under /data/logs with the log_segments index and cap job

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- OTLP logs use T111's `[otlp]` config section (`endpoint`, `protocol`, `headers`, `logs = true`); there is no `[logs.push] otlp_endpoint`. T111 later adds traces and metrics to the same exporter.
- `partifactory logs tail` talks to the ops listener behind `PF_METRICS_TOKEN` and is never routed through the ingress.

- [ ] `logs export --since 1h` returns exactly the lines in range (golden over a deterministic generator with a test clock).
- [ ] `--part` filtering works for app and backend streams.

title: T112: No-content-in-logs fuzz test: canaries across every surface never reach logs, traces, insights.db or /metrics
description:
## Goal and why

Turn the rule "no part content in logs or analytics; no tokens, caps, cookies or secrets anywhere in telemetry" from a convention into a CI gate. Agents write untrusted content; viewers type into parts; a single debug `?` in a log line could leak a family member's data into a log file that lives for 7 days and is exported. A fuzz test with canary values catches that the day it's introduced.

After Slice 1 (P1), part of M1's done-when ("§7 passes"); it implements the §7 Operations line "No tokens, caps, cookies, secrets or part content in logs, traces, `insights.db` or `/metrics` (fuzzed with canary values across every surface, T112)".

## Scope

- A test harness that boots a full server (main DB, insights.db, log segments, metrics) in-process or as a subprocess, with the stdout JSON captured, and drives every surface with generated inputs that embed unique canary strings:
  - **MCP** (via the `rmcp` client), **HTTP** (`POST /api/v1/{op}`), **CLI** (`part <op> --json`), **the UI** (workspace and wrapper/chrome API routes, form posts), **`/_rt`** (`storage.set/get/list/getMany/delete`, `errors.report`, `refresh`), and from P2a **backends** (requests through `/c/<cap>/api/*`, backend stdout).
  - Canaries placed in: part titles, descriptions, tags, file contents, file paths, `old_str`/`new_str`, `window.storage` keys and values, `part_data` docs, comments (when T50 exists), runtime error messages and stacks, query strings, header values, plus credentials: session cookie values, `pf_at_`/`pf_rt_`/`pf_pat_` tokens, caps in `/c/<cap>/` paths and `#pf=` fragments, part secrets (P2a), the admin metrics token.
  - Fuzzing: property-based generation (`proptest`) of op inputs from the registry's JSON Schemas (T20) so new ops and fields are covered automatically; canaries wrapped in unicode, JSON-escaped, base64'd and URL-encoded variants.
- Sinks scanned after each run: stdout lines, every `/data/logs/**/*.jsonl.zst` segment (decompressed), every table/column of `insights.db` (`events_raw`, `rollups_daily`, `traces`, `spans`, `log_segments`, `janitor_runs`), the `/metrics` exposition (labels and values), and build-child stderr.
- Matching: exact canary and each encoded variant; also a check that `/c/<…>/` path segments appear only as the redacted form.
- Runs on every PR; any match fails with the sink, location and the surface/op that produced it.

## Not in scope

Writing the redaction itself (T18 type-based redaction, T106 span fields, T107 sinks) — this task finds failures, the owning task fixes them. Backend coverage is added when P2a lands (T101/T110) — the harness exposes a `Surface::Backend` driver slot from day one.

## Design notes and decisions

- Schema-driven generation means "adding an op without being fuzzed" is impossible: the op list comes from the registry.
- Error messages are a classic leak path ("anchor not found: <old_str>…"): the error catalogue's `message` may quote content back to the *caller* in the response, but logs must log the code and sizes, not the message text. The test must therefore send content that triggers errors (`anchor_not_found`, `invalid_input`, `too_large`).
- `details.context` in `anchor_not_found` contains current file text by design in the response; it must not be logged.
- Deterministic seeds in CI with a seed printed on failure; a nightly run with random seeds (not gating).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Runs on every PR and fails on any canary match; covers MCP, HTTP, CLI, the UI and `/_rt` (backends from P2a)."

- [ ] CI job `no-content-in-logs` runs on every PR and fails on any match, printing sink, location, surface, op and seed.
- [ ] Coverage report lists every registry op and every `/_rt` op exercised at least once.
- [ ] Sinks covered: stdout, log segments, all insights.db tables, `/metrics`, build-child output.
- [ ] Credential canaries (cookie, `pf_*` tokens, caps, metrics token) covered.
- [ ] A deliberately inserted `info!(content = %body)` in a test branch makes the job fail (mutation check).

## Tests

- `tests/no_content/main.rs::fuzz_all_surfaces` (proptest, 256 cases per op in CI).
- `tests/no_content/main.rs::credential_canaries_redacted`.
- `tests/no_content/main.rs::error_paths_do_not_log_content` (anchor_not_found, invalid_input, too_large).
- `tests/no_content/main.rs::coverage_lists_every_op` (fails if an op in the registry is untested).
- UI driver: `tests/e2e/no_content_ui.spec.ts` (Playwright types canaries into the share sheet, comments and a part page); keeps `target/e2e-logs/no_content_ui/` on failure.
- Structured log assertions: the harness itself asserts presence of expected events (`event="op.done" op="part_create" outcome="ok"`) to prove logs were actually produced (a silent logger would pass vacuously).

## References

PLAN.md §5g "Tested" (fuzz test); §7 Operations; §5d Logs (redaction by type and pattern); §5e insights.db header comment ("a CI fuzz test checks it"); §6a T112 row.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Runs on every PR and fails on any canary match; covers MCP, HTTP, CLI, the UI and `/_rt` (backends from P2a)
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups
  - T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
  - T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: S1 (the fuzz drives MCP, the CLI, the UI and `/_rt`, which exist only with Slice 1).
- Also assert that `anchor_not_found.details.context` **does** appear in the HTTP response (proving the leak path exists) and in no sink.
- Split into T112.a / T112.b (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: Runs on every PR and fails on any canary match; covers MCP, HTTP, CLI, the UI and `/_rt` (backends from P2a)
