title: T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
description:
## Goal and why

"The way a self-hosted service dies is a full disk, months after anyone last looked." Every growing store needs a retention rule run by something; the janitor is that one thing. It runs every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job on a schedule, records what it freed, and **never deletes anything a live or binned item references**.

**In Slice 1, on the critical path** (T62 → T77 → T113 → T114 → T115 is as long as the pixel test's own path; decision 41: "shipping uncapped stores to a box that's then left alone for years is the failure the plan exists to avoid, so S1 waits for them"). Start it as soon as data snapshots (T77) land. Feeds T114, T115, T59 (blob GC is a janitor job), T116.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close only after all subtasks close and the acceptance passes end to end):
- `T113.a` — janitor framework: the `JanitorJob` trait and registry, scheduler, `janitor_runs` recording, metrics, the reference-safety guard, admin "run now".
- `T113.b` — main-DB prune jobs: events (30 d), build logs (last 20 builds per part, 30 d), runtime errors (> 30 d; count capped by trigger), audit segments (1 year, yearly segments), idempotency keys (24 h), scratch expiry (moves due `expires_in` parts to the bin), bin purge (30 d).
- `T113.c` — data-snapshot retention, scheduled-export rotation, WAL checkpoint and monthly VACUUM for both SQLite files.

Jobs for stores that exist in Slice 1 (verbatim list from the task): "events, build logs, runtime errors, audit segments, data snapshots, scheduled exports, bin purge, scratch expiry, idempotency keys, WAL checkpoint, monthly VACUUM". **Later stores register their jobs when they land** (no edges): Insights raw events and rollups (T105), traces (T106), log segments (T107), backend rings/images/BuildKit cache (T110/T116), blob GC (T59).

`janitor_runs` lives in `insights.db` from day one (DDL verbatim below). **Decided (polish round):** T113.a opens `/data/insights.db` through `pf-db`'s second `Db` instance (T05) and applies the insights migration set shipped by T06.e; the janitor writes `janitor_runs` there. T105 later adopts that handle for `events_raw` and the rest, so the table never moves and the Health page has one place to read. (The alternative, a temporary main-DB table moved by T105's migration, was rejected: two homes for one table and a data move for no gain.)

```sql
CREATE TABLE janitor_runs (                          -- what each retention job freed (§5h)
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  at          INTEGER NOT NULL,
  store       TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- a row of the §5h retention table
  action      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('prune','rotate','gc','checkpoint','vacuum','image_prune','cache_prune')),
  items       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  freed_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
  size_after  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cap_bytes   INTEGER,
  error       TEXT
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX janitor_runs_store ON janitor_runs(store, at);
```

The §5h retention table (the janitor's spec; rows whose stores exist in Slice 1 are this task's): Build logs "the last 20 builds per part, 30 days | prune job"; Browser runtime errors "1,000 per part, 30 days | prune job"; Audit log "1 year (security-relevant) | yearly segments | export (JSONL)"; Events log "30 days, then `cursor_expired` | prune job"; Versions and blobs "every version kept (deduplicated); the bin for 30 days; unreferenced blobs collected | GC job"; Data snapshots "daily keep 7 / hourly keep 48; the last one kept after 90 days idle | prune job"; Scheduled exports "keep 7 | rotation"; SQLite WAL (both files) "a scheduled checkpoint + `wal_autocheckpoint`; `VACUUM` monthly when free pages > 20 %".

## Not in scope

Blob GC mark-and-sweep (T59, a janitor job), the disk budget and store caps on Health (T114), the fill-past-cap retention test (T115), Insights/trace/log jobs (T105–T107), backend retention (T116), the export itself (T34) and snapshot taking (T77).

## Design notes and decisions

- One task, many jobs: a single scheduler avoids N timers fighting for the writer; each job is a small transaction batch (e.g. ≤ 1,000 rows per tx) so the save path never waits behind a long delete.
- **Reference safety is structural**: every destructive job declares the reference queries it must respect; the framework runs them inside the same writer transaction. Example: a blob or snapshot referenced by a binned part survives; a part in the bin is purged only at 30 days, and only then do its versions' blobs become GC candidates.
- `janitor_runs` is in `insights.db` from Slice 1 (see Scope). The janitor stays independent of T105, as the Slice 1 freeze requires ("the janitor (T113) and retention test (T115) no longer wait on Insights (T105)"), with no later data move. `insights.db` is in exports only with `--include-insights`, which is right for observability rows, and `partifactory.db` stays free of analytics writes.
- Metrics: `pf_janitor_freed_bytes_total{store}`, `pf_janitor_items_total{store,action}`, `pf_janitor_last_run_timestamp{store}`, `pf_janitor_errors_total{store}`.
- A failing job records `error` and continues with the others; repeated failures surface on Health (T36/T114).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each job frees the expected items on a fixture; a blob referenced only by a binned part survives; `janitor_runs` and /metrics show the bytes freed."

- [ ] Every listed job exists, is scheduled, and frees exactly the expected items on a fixture.
- [ ] Nothing referenced by a live or binned item is deleted (a blob/snapshot referenced only by a binned part survives).
- [ ] Each run writes `janitor_runs` rows and updates metrics with bytes freed.
- [ ] A failing job doesn't stop others and shows its error.
- [ ] Later stores can register jobs without changing the framework (a test job registers via the trait).

## Tests

title: T113.a: Janitor framework: job trait, scheduler, reference-safety guard, janitor_runs and metrics
description:
## Goal and why

One scheduler and one interface for every retention job, so later stores (insights, traces, logs, backends, blob GC) plug in without new plumbing, and every job is recorded and observable.

## Scope

- `crates/pf-janitor`: `trait JanitorJob { fn store(&self) -> &'static str; fn action(&self) -> Action; fn schedule(&self) -> Schedule; fn cap(&self) -> Option<u64>; async fn run(&self, ctx: &JanitorCtx) -> Result<RunReport>; }` with `RunReport {items, freed_bytes, size_after}`; `Action` ∈ `prune | rotate | gc | checkpoint | vacuum | image_prune | cache_prune`.
- Registry populated at start; jobs from later tasks register via the same trait (feature-gated modules or `inventory`).
- Scheduler: per-job schedule (hourly, daily at a jittered off-hour, weekly, monthly), one job at a time, writer work done in small batches (≤ 1,000 rows/tx) to keep commit latency flat.
- Reference-safety guard: destructive jobs pass candidate ids through a declared `references()` check executed inside the writer transaction; anything referenced by a live or binned part (versions, builds, drafts, data snapshots, assets, kept image tarballs) is excluded.
- `janitor_runs` table (DDL as in the parent) in `/data/insights.db`: this subtask opens the file through `pf-db`'s second `Db` instance (its own writer task, T05), applies the `crates/pf-db/migrations/insights/` set (T06.e) at start, and writes one row per job run (with `error` on failure). T105 later reuses the same handle; the table never moves. The insights file is registered as a store for the WAL checkpoint job (T113.c) and the store registry (T114.b).
- Metrics `pf_janitor_*` (freed bytes, items, last run, errors) on `:9090/metrics`.
- Admin API `POST /api/admin/janitor/run {store?}` for "run now" (admin session + step-up not needed: it only frees what retention already allows; recommended default admin-only).

## Not in scope

The individual jobs (T113.b, T113.c, and later tasks).

## Design notes and decisions

- Single runner avoids contention on the single writer.
- A job error is isolated, recorded and surfaced on Health; the next job still runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test job registered through the trait runs on schedule and writes a `janitor_runs` row and metrics.
- [ ] The guard keeps a candidate referenced only by a binned part.
- [ ] A panicking/failing job records `error` and the scheduler continues.
- [ ] `/data/insights.db` is created on first start with the T06.e schema; `janitor_runs` rows land there; `partifactory.db` has no `janitor_runs` table (schema test).

## Tests

- `pf_janitor::tests::registers_and_runs_test_job`, `::failing_job_isolated`, `::reference_guard_keeps_binned_refs`.
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/metrics.rs::freed_bytes_exported` (scrapes `/metrics` with the metrics token).

title: T113.b: Main-DB prune jobs: events, build logs, runtime errors, audit segments, idempotency, scratch expiry, bin purge
description:
## Goal and why

Implement the retention rules for every main-database store that exists in Slice 1, exactly as the §5h table states, so none grows without bound.

## Scope

Jobs (store name → rule):
- `events` — delete `events` rows older than 30 days (`events.at`); `part_watch`/SSE cursors older than the oldest kept `seq` get `cursor_expired {oldest}` (that error is raised by T123; this job just prunes).
- `build_logs` — keep the build log blob reference (`builds.log_hash`) only for the last 20 builds per part and only 30 days; clear `log_hash` beyond that (the blob becomes a GC candidate for T59). Build records themselves stay.
- `runtime_errors` — delete rows with `last_at` older than 30 days (the 1,000-per-part count cap is the `runtime_errors_keep1000` trigger from T06).
- `audit` — 1 year retention in yearly segments: rows older than 1 year are exported to a JSONL segment (`/data/backup/audit-<year>.jsonl.zst`, recommended location) then deleted; the segment counts toward the store size.
- `idempotency` — delete `idempotency` rows with `created_at` older than 24 h.
- `scratch_expiry` — parts with `expires_at <= now AND deleted_at IS NULL` move to the bin (`deleted_at = now`), emit an event, bump the part epoch (so caps die).
- `bin_purge` — parts with `deleted_at` older than 30 days are purged: rows removed (cascade), names kept in `names` with `state='tombstone'` ("A purged part's name stays reserved forever"); their blobs become GC candidates (T59). Undelete at 29 days works; at 31 fails (matches T11's acceptance).

## Not in scope

Data snapshots, exports, WAL/VACUUM (T113.c); blob GC (T59).

## Design notes and decisions

- Every delete runs in small batches through the reference guard.
- Bin purge must not touch blobs directly: GC (T59) does that after its 7-day grace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fixture each job frees exactly the expected rows; a 31-day-old event is pruned, a 29-day one kept.
- [ ] Only the newest 20 builds' logs per part remain referenced.
- [ ] Purged part names stay reserved (tombstone); undelete at 29 d ok, 31 d fails.
- [ ] Each job writes `janitor_runs`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/jobs_main_db.rs::events_30d`, `::build_logs_last_20`, `::runtime_errors_30d`, `::audit_yearly_segment`, `::idempotency_24h`, `::scratch_expiry_moves_to_bin_and_bumps_epoch`, `::bin_purge_30d_keeps_name_tombstone`.
- Test clock injected; asserts `event="janitor.job" store="<name>" items=N`.

## References

PLAN.md §5h table; §3d scratch parts and idempotency (24 h); §3e the bin; §4 Events (30 days, `cursor_expired`); §5e `events`, `builds.log_hash`, `runtime_errors`, `audit`, `idempotency`, `names`.

title: T113.c: Data-snapshot retention, scheduled-export rotation, WAL checkpoint and monthly VACUUM
description:
## Goal and why

Bound the stores created by data snapshots (T77) and nightly exports (T34), and keep both SQLite files compact, so undo history and backups never become the thing that fills the disk.

## Scope

- `data_snapshots` job — per part, per its policy (`data_snapshot_policies`; no row = `daily`, keep 7; `hourly` keep 48; `off`): delete `scheduled` snapshots beyond `keep` (oldest first). On-demand snapshots (`reason` in `contribute`, `before_restore`, `before_reset`) don't count against `keep` (recommended: they expire with the same age horizon as the oldest kept scheduled snapshot, never the newest one). **Idle rule:** after `expire_days` (default 90) without the part being opened, snapshotting stops (T77) and this job keeps **the single most recent snapshot** until the part is deleted and leaves the 30-day bin. Snapshot blobs become GC candidates once rows are gone.
- `exports` job — rotate `/data/exports/partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst` (`backup.export_dir`), keeping `backup.export_keep` (default 7) newest; never delete the only export.
- `wal_checkpoint` job — scheduled `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on both `partifactory.db` and `insights.db` (the latter exists from T113.a) plus `wal_autocheckpoint` set at open.
- `vacuum` job — monthly `VACUUM` when free pages > 20 % (`PRAGMA freelist_count` / `page_count`), at an off-hour; skipped if disk headroom is too low for the copy.

## Not in scope

Taking snapshots and exports (T77, T34); blob deletion (T59).

## Design notes and decisions

- "keep the last one" protects a part nobody opens from losing its only undo point.
- VACUUM needs up to the DB size in free space; check headroom first and record a skipped run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A daily part keeps exactly 7 scheduled snapshots; hourly keeps 48; on-demand ones aren't counted.
- [ ] After 90 days idle exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin.
- [ ] A fresh install's nightly export dir holds exactly 7 files.
- [ ] Checkpoint and VACUUM run, VACUUM only above 20 % free pages; `janitor_runs` rows with `checkpoint`/`vacuum`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/jobs_snapshots.rs::daily_keep_7`, `::hourly_keep_48`, `::on_demand_outside_keep`, `::idle_keeps_last_one`.
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/jobs_exports.rs::keeps_7`.
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/jobs_sqlite.rs::checkpoint_truncates_wal`, `::vacuum_only_above_20pct_free`, `::vacuum_skipped_low_headroom`.

## References

PLAN.md §5c data snapshots and scheduled export; §5h table (Data snapshots, Scheduled exports, SQLite WAL rows); §5e `data_snapshot_policies`, `data_snapshots`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T113.a: Janitor framework: job trait, scheduler, reference-safety guard, janitor_runs and metrics

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

- [ ] A daily part keeps exactly 7 scheduled snapshots; hourly keeps 48; on-demand ones aren't counted.
- [ ] After 90 days idle exactly one snapshot remains until the part leaves the bin.
- [ ] A fresh install's nightly export dir holds exactly 7 files.

title: T114: Disk budget (warn 80 %, storage_full at 95 %), per-store caps on Health, and the [unsafe] safe-defaults registry
description:
## Goal and why

Two principles from the top of the plan become enforceable code here: **every growing store is capped** and **defaults are the safe choice**. A global disk budget turns "the disk filled up" into an amber Health row at 80 % and a clean `storage_full` refusal at 95 %, while reads and deletes keep working so a person can always free space. A safe-defaults registry makes it impossible to switch off a protection by typo or a copied snippet.

**In Slice 1, on the critical path** (retention chain T113 → T114 → T115; definition of done item 6: "Every store that exists is capped … the Health page shows each one, the backup layers and the disk budget; no `[unsafe]` key is set"). Feeds T115, T121 (alerts at 80 %), T68 (`doctor` checks every store capped and safe defaults on).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close after both subtasks close and the acceptance passes end to end):
- `T114.a` — the global disk budget and the `storage_full` write refusal.
- `T114.b` — the per-store cap registry with sizes on Health (and Insights once T108 lands), and the safe-defaults registry with `[unsafe]` keys, Health warnings and `config check` failures.

Verbatim:
- "**The global disk budget**: partifactory may use at most 80 % of its volume by default (`[disk] budget_percent`), counting `/data` plus the runner's images and build cache. It warns at 80 % of the budget, and at 95 % **refuses new writes** (versions, assets, builds, deploys, `/_rt` writes) with `storage_full`. It **never refuses reads or deletes**, so a person can always free space."
- "**At 95 % of the disk budget (§5h) the writer refuses new versions, assets, builds, deploys and `/_rt` writes with `storage_full`**, while reads, deletes, grants and revocations continue."
- Error catalogue: `storage_full` → HTTP 507, CLI exit 7; contract: "`storage_full` | 507 | stop and tell the person". `PfError` code `storage_full` in the prelude.
- Interpretation stated in the plan: "The disk budget defaults to 80 % of the volume, and the 80 % warning and 95 % refusal are fractions of that budget."
- "**Safe defaults, enforced**: secure headers, rate limits, quotas, the container hardening template, the nightly export (to `/data/exports`, keep 7, with 'same disk = amber'), the ingress contract's TLS assumptions, log redaction and these retention caps are all on in the default config. Turning any of them off needs an explicit key (`[unsafe] <name> = "off"`), and shows as a warning on Health and in `doctor`." Also `[unsafe] quotas = "off"` for unlimited quotas (§5d).
- "Config can only tighten or loosen them within sane bounds, and `doctor` fails if any store is uncapped."

## Not in scope

The janitor jobs that bring stores back under caps (T113 and later tasks); the alert webhook (T121); `doctor` (T68, which reads this registry); Insights charts of store sizes (T108); runner image/cache accounting (T116 adds those stores; this task counts their bytes in the budget via a hook once the runner exists).

## Design notes and decisions

- Budget arithmetic: `used = du(/data) + runner_images + buildkit_cache` (runner figures via its `stats` API from P2a; zero before). `budget = budget_percent × volume_size` (statvfs). States: ok < 80 % of budget ≤ warn < 95 % ≤ full.
- Measurement is periodic (e.g. every 30 s, plus on each blob put via a cheap counter) — never a `du` on the hot path. T07 already returns `storage_full` at 95 % of the volume for blob puts; this task replaces that local check with the budget state so there's one rule.
- Refusal happens in the writer before work starts (no half-written version), for: `part_create`/`part_edit` new versions, `part_data` set, `/_rt` storage writes, asset uploads, builds, backend deploys. Allowed in `full`: all reads, `part_edit {delete: true}`, bin purge, grants/revocations, janitor jobs, sign-in.
- Store caps registry: each store declares `{name, size_fn, cap_bytes, retention}`; Health shows size/cap with amber at 80 %; `doctor` and T115 enumerate the registry, so a new store without a cap fails tests.
- Safe-defaults registry: each protection declares its config key and its `[unsafe]` override name; `config check` fails if a protection is turned off without the matching `[unsafe]` key (e.g. `rate_limits.enabled = false` alone fails).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "At 95 % of the budget a create returns `storage_full` while a delete and a read succeed; a store at 80 % of its cap shows amber on Health; switching rate limits off without the explicit key fails `config check`."

- [ ] Budget computed from config and volume; 80 % warn row on Health; 95 % refuses every write class listed with `storage_full` (507 / exit 7 / `PfError`).
- [ ] Reads, deletes, grants, revocations and janitor runs succeed at 95 %.
- [ ] Every existing store appears on Health with size vs cap; 80 % of a cap is amber.
- [ ] Turning off a safe default without its `[unsafe]` key fails `partifactory config check` with exit 2 and the key name; with the key it passes and shows a warning row on Health.

## Tests

See subtasks; plus e2e `tests/e2e/disk_full.spec.ts`: fills a small loopback test volume to 95 % of the budget, asserts the wrapper still opens a part, `part_create` gets 507 `storage_full`, `part_edit {delete:true}` succeeds, and Health shows the red budget row; server logs under `target/e2e-logs/disk_full/` assert `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `event="op.done" op="part_create" outcome="storage_full"`.

## References

PLAN.md §5h Disk safety (global disk budget; Safe defaults, enforced; `[unsafe]` table rationale); top-of-plan "Defaults are the safe choice"; §5d Disk pressure and Quotas; §4b error table; §6a; Slice 1 definition of done item 6; decision 33.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): At 95 % of the budget a create returns `storage_full` while a delete and a read succeed; a store at 80 % of its cap shows amber on Health; switching rate limits off without the explicit key fails `config check`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
- Unblocks: 
  - T121: Optional ops-alert webhook (off by default): HMAC-signed `{alert, severity, detail, at}`
  - T68: `partifactory doctor`: config, DNS, ingress, certs, IdP, backup layers, disk, store caps, safe defaults
  - T115: Retention table test: every existing §5h store filled past its cap comes back under
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):

  - T114.b: Store-cap registry on Health and the safe-defaults registry with [unsafe] keys and config check

title: T114.a: Global disk budget and the storage_full refusal for every write class (reads and deletes never refused)
description:
## Goal and why

Make a full disk a controlled, recoverable state: warn early, refuse new writes cleanly at 95 % of the budget, and keep reads and deletes working so a person can free space.

## Scope

- Config `[disk] budget_percent` (default 80, bounded e.g. 10–95). Budget = that % of the `/data` volume (statvfs); used = `/data` bytes + runner images + BuildKit cache (hook returns 0 until the runner exists, T98/T116).
- Background measurer (every 30 s, plus incremental counters on blob put/delete) publishing a state `ok | warn (≥ 80 % of budget) | full (≥ 95 %)` in memory and in `kv` (`disk budget state`).
- Writer-side gate: in `full`, refuse new versions (`part_create`, `part_edit` edits/restore/rebuild), `part_data` set/snapshot_restore, `/_rt` `storage.set` (a `storage.delete` frees space and stays allowed — the plan's "never refuses deletes"), assets, builds, backend deploys with `storage_full` (HTTP 507, CLI exit 7, MCP `isError`, prelude `PfError {code: "storage_full", retryable: false}`). Allowed: reads, `part_edit {delete: true}`, bin purge, grants and revocations, sign-in, janitor.
- Replace T07's local 95 %-of-volume check with this state so there is one rule.
- Metrics: `pf_disk_budget_bytes`, `pf_disk_used_bytes`, `pf_disk_budget_state`.

## Not in scope

Per-store caps and safe-defaults (T114.b); alerts (T121).

## Design notes and decisions

- No `du` on the hot path; the gate reads an atomic.
- Refuse before any blob is written so nothing half-commits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At 95 % a create returns `storage_full` while a delete and a read succeed.
- [ ] Warn state at 80 % appears on Health.
- [ ] Every write class listed is refused in `full`; every allowed class succeeds.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-api/tests/storage_full.rs::create_refused_read_delete_ok`, `::rt_write_refused`, `::grant_and_revoke_still_work` (fake volume provider); asserts `event="disk.budget_state" state="full"` and `outcome="storage_full"`.

## References

Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

title: T114.b: Store-cap registry on Health and the safe-defaults registry with [unsafe] keys and config check
description:
## Goal and why

Make "every store is capped" and "every protection is on unless explicitly, visibly switched off" machine-checkable, so Health, `doctor` (T68) and the retention test (T115) can enumerate them.

## Scope

- `StoreRegistry`: each growing store registers `{name (a §5h row), size_fn, cap_bytes or count cap, retention text}`. Slice 1 stores: build logs, runtime errors, audit log, events log, versions and blobs, data snapshots, scheduled exports, SQLite WAL (both files: `partifactory.db` and `insights.db`), container log limits of partifactory's own compose services (static `json-file` 10m×3, checked not measured). Later tasks register theirs (Insights raw events, rollups, traces, app log segments, backend logs, BuildKit cache, images, volumes).
- Health page section "Stores": each store's size against its cap (amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 100 %), plus the disk budget row (from T114.a). Insights shows the same once T108 lands.
- `SafeDefaults` registry: each protection `{name, config key(s), unsafe_key}`; protections: secure headers, rate limits, quotas, the container hardening template, the nightly export, the ingress TLS assumptions, log redaction, retention caps. Turning one off requires `[unsafe] <name> = "off"`; `partifactory config check` fails (exit 2, naming the key) otherwise. With the key, Health shows a warning row "<name> is switched off" and `doctor` warns.
- Config bounds: caps can be tightened or loosened only within declared min/max.

- One `[unsafe]` table "reads as what it is", so every exception is visible in review.
- Registry-driven: adding a growing store without registering it fails T115.

title: T115: Retention table test: every existing §5h store filled past its cap comes back under
description:
## Goal and why

Prove, in CI, that the caps aren't just numbers on a page: for each growing store that exists, fill it past its cap and show that the janitor (T113) and the caps (T114) bring it back under, without deleting anything referenced. And make the test itself the gate that stops anyone adding a new growing store without a cap.

**In Slice 1, on the critical path** (the retention chain's end; Slice 1 definition of done item 6: "Every store that exists is capped and passes its fill-past-cap case (T115)"). Feeds S1 and M1; T116 adds the backend rows.

## Scope

- A table-driven test where each row is a §5h store that exists, with: how to fill it past its cap (fixture generator), the expected post-janitor bound, and the reference-safety assertion. Rows for Slice 1 stores:
  - Build logs: "the last 20 builds per part, 30 days" → create 30 builds on one part; after a run only 20 logs referenced, none older than 30 d.
  - Browser runtime errors: "1,000 per part, 30 days" → insert 1,200 + old rows; ≤ 1,000 per part, none > 30 d.
  - Audit log: "1 year (security-relevant), yearly segments".
  - Events log: "30 days, then `cursor_expired`".
  - Versions and blobs: "every version kept (deduplicated); the bin for 30 days; unreferenced blobs collected" (with T59's GC: unreferenced blob deleted after 7-day grace; a blob referenced only by a binned part survives).
  - Data snapshots: "daily keep 7 / hourly keep 48; the last one kept after 90 days idle".
  - Scheduled exports: "keep 7".
  - SQLite WAL: "a scheduled checkpoint + `wal_autocheckpoint`; `VACUUM` monthly when free pages > 20 %".
  - Container stdout of partifactory's own compose services: `json-file` `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3` asserted from `deploy/compose.yaml` (static check).
  - Idempotency keys (24 h) and scratch/bin rows.
- Rows added later by their owners without a dag edge: App logs (T107: "7 days or 1 GiB"), Traces and spans (T106: "7 days, 2 GiB"), Insights raw events (T105: 30 days), backend rows (T116: backend logs 50 MiB per part / 7 days, BuildKit cache 10 GiB, images live + previous 2, volumes quota).
- A **completeness check**: the test enumerates the store registry (T114.b) and fails if any registered store has no row, and a lint fails if a migration adds a table matching growth patterns (append-only/log-like, declared via an annotation) without registering a store — "adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the test".
- Caps are scaled down via test config (same code paths) so the test runs in seconds.

## Not in scope

Writing the jobs (T113 and later), the backend rows (T116), the disk budget (T114).

## Design notes and decisions

- Test clock + scaled caps keep it fast and deterministic.
- Every case also asserts `janitor_runs` rows and `pf_janitor_freed_bytes_total` increments, so observability of retention is tested too.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Every §5h row whose store exists has a passing fill-past-cap case; adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the test."

- [ ] One passing case per existing §5h store (list above).
- [ ] Registry completeness check fails on an unregistered or case-less store (proved with a test-only dummy store).
- [ ] Referenced items survive in every case.
- [ ] Runs on every PR in < 60 s.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/retention_table.rs::fill_past_cap::<store>` (one generated test per row).
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/retention_table.rs::every_registered_store_has_a_case`.
- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/retention_table.rs::dummy_uncapped_store_fails` (negative test behind a test feature).
- Each case asserts log `event="janitor.job" store=<row> outcome="ok"` and `size_after <= cap`; on failure dumps the fixture `/data` tree under `target/test-artifacts/retention/<store>/`.

## References

PLAN.md §5h table; §7 Operations ("Every growing store has a cap (`doctor` fails otherwise), and each one, filled past its cap in a test, comes back under (T115, T116)"); Slice 1 definition of done item 6; §6a notes (T105/T107 add rows without edges).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Every §5h row whose store exists has a passing fill-past-cap case; adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the test
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
  - T114: Disk budget (warn 80 %, storage_full at 95 %), per-store caps on Health, and the [unsafe] safe-defaults registry
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
  - T116: Runner retention: image pruning (live + previous 2), BuildKit cache 10 GiB LRU, backend log rings, volume quotas
acceptance_criteria: Every §5h row whose store exists has a passing fill-past-cap case; adding a growing store without a cap and a case fails the test

title: G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change
description:
## Goal and why

The plan describes an admin area at `parts.<domain>/admin`, for the admin only, but no task in the task graph builds its shell or several of its pages. Individual tasks own fragments: the public-link list and kill switch (T29), the Health page (T36), Insights (T108), Invites (T94), Backends/LAN (T102.d) and the cleanup lists (T42). This bead owns the shell those pages plug into, and the pages nobody else owns. The admin is the only person who can act outward (public links, invites, groups, `everyone-signed-in`, `unsandboxed`, renames), so a single, legible admin area with an always-visible step-up state is what makes those powers auditable and hard to misuse. The audit table already records every grant change, but without a ledger UI nobody can read it.

## Scope

- **Shell**: `/admin` with tabs **People · Groups · Invites · Agents · Public links · Backends · Audit · Health · Insights**. Tabs whose pages belong to later tasks show "arrives with T<n>" until those land (Invites T94, Backends T102.d, Insights T108). A persistent step-up chip: `Admin unlocked · 8 min` (minutes left in the 10-minute step-up window from `sessions.stepup_at`) or `Locked` with a passkey button (in-page WebAuthn via T28.b). Non-admin sessions get 404 for every `/admin` route, not 403, so the area's existence isn't confirmed.
- **People**: every `users` row (`username`, `display_name`, `auth_source` oidc/local, `status` active/disabled/removed, `in_audience`, `last_seen_at`), with disable (sets `status = 'disabled'`, bumps that user's minter epochs, ends sessions; step-up required) and a link to the T42 cleanup lists once they exist.
- **Groups**: `groups` rows with `source` (`claim`, `idp_api`, `local`), member counts, the `managed` flag; creating local `pf-*` groups is T94.d, so this page lists and links.
- **Agents**: every `agent_connections` row across people (`agent_name`, "for <person>" or service, `kind` oauth_code/device/pat, scopes, spaces, `last_used_at`, `expires_at`), with Revoke (same cascade as Connected agents, T45) and the grants each made (`grants.created_by_conn`) with "Undo all".
- **Audit**: a filterable ledger over `audit`: "who · as whom · what · before -> after · when", in mono (`--pf-font-mono`), filters by `action`, `target_kind`/`target_id`, `user_id`, `actor`, date range and `request_id`; paged by `id` descending; JSON before/after rendered as a compact diff.
- **Unsandboxed parts**: the admin lists every part with `parts.isolation = 'unsandboxed'`; the flag is toggled from the share sheet (danger red) with step-up, and every toggle writes an audit row.
- **Owner change**: the plan says a part's owner is "the person it was made for … the admin can change it". Add an admin action on a part (from Admin or the share sheet's admin section) that updates `parts.owner_user_id`, writes `audit` (`part.owner_set`, before -> after) and bumps the part epoch.

## Not in scope

Health (T36), Insights (T108), Public links list + kill switch (T29.c), invite minting (T94), Backends/LAN page (T102.d), cleanup lists (T42).

## Design notes and decisions

- Admin is pinned to one immutable subject (`[admin] subject`), never a group; every mutating admin action requires a passkey assertion within 10 minutes (`step_up_required` otherwise).
- 404 for non-admins mirrors the "not_found, never forbidden" rule for things a caller can't see.
- Copy voice per Stockroom: plain, specific ("Disabled a family member · Undo"); revocations use a 10 s undo toast, never a confirm dialog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A non-admin (including an IdP-admin user) gets 404 on every `/admin/*` route.
- [ ] The step-up chip shows the minutes left and flips to `Locked` at 10 minutes; a mutating action while locked prompts in-page step-up and completes after the biometric.
- [ ] Disabling a person ends their sessions and their next part request fails; one audit row is written.
- [ ] The Audit ledger finds a grant change by request id and shows before -> after.
- [ ] Changing a part's owner updates `owner_user_id`, writes an audit row and bumps the part epoch.

## Tests

- `pf-ui` integration `admin_routes_404_for_non_admin` (fixture users from T19), asserting `outcome="not_found"` log events.
- e2e `tests/e2e/admin_area.spec.ts` on the T24 harness: step-up chip countdown (test clock), disable person, audit filter by request id, owner change; keeps `target/e2e-logs/admin_area/server.jsonl` and traces.
- Contrast test covers the admin pages' tokens.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Screens "Admin (/admin, admin only)"; §3a "Admin is the admin, and only the admin", audience ladder (owner change); §2 Escape hatch `unsandboxed`; §5e `audit`, `users`, `groups`, `agent_connections`.

## Dependency context

- Gap bead: a plan item that no task in the task graph owned; added during bead conversion.
- Depends on: T26, T28, T31
- Feeds milestone(s): M1

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Non-admins get **403** on `/admin/*` (PLAN §7: "An IdP-admin user still gets 403"; T28's test), never 404; T36 and T108 are aligned to this.
- This bead owns the `unsandboxed` toggle (share sheet, danger red, admin + step-up, session-only handler, audit row, part-epoch bump) as well as the list of unsandboxed parts.
- Tests add: disabling a person revokes their agent connections' tokens (T45's cascade); the Agents page shows "for <person>" from `agent_connections.user_id`.
- Split into G01.a / G01.b / G01.c (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A non-admin (including an IdP-admin user) gets 404 on every `/admin/*` route.
- [ ] The step-up chip shows the minutes left and flips to `Locked` at 10 minutes; a mutating action while locked prompts in-page step-up and completes after the biometric.
- [ ] Disabling a person ends their sessions and their next part request fails; one audit row is written.
- [ ] The Audit ledger finds a grant change by request id and shows before -> after.
- [ ] Changing a part's owner updates `owner_user_id`, writes an audit row and bumps the part epoch.

title: G01.a: /admin shell, tabs, step-up chip, 403 gate, Audit ledger with filters (incl. request_id)
description:
## Goal and why

The admin's one place: a shell with tabs, a visible step-up state, a hard gate, and the audit ledger that answers "who did what, as whom, when".

## Scope

- `/admin` with tabs **People · Groups · Invites · Agents · Public links · Backends · Audit · Health · Insights**; tabs owned by later tasks show "arrives with T<n>" (Invites T94, Backends T102.d, Insights T108).
- Step-up chip: `Admin unlocked · 8 min` (from `sessions.stepup_at`) or `Locked` with an in-page passkey button (T28.b).
- Gate: non-admin sessions get **403** on every `/admin/*` route (PLAN §7, T28's test); agents never reach it.
- **Audit ledger**: filterable over `audit` ("who · as whom · what · before → after · when", mono), filters by `action`, `target_kind`/`target_id`, `user_id`, `actor`, date range and `request_id`; paged by `id` desc; JSON before/after as a compact diff.

## Not in scope

People/Groups/Agents pages (G01.b); the unsandboxed list and toggle, owner change (G01.c).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-admin → 403 on every admin route; admin without step-up sees `Locked` and admin writes return `step_up_required`.
- [ ] The ledger filters by each field and renders before/after diffs; a `request_id` filter finds the row for a failing request.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/admin_shell.spec.ts` (403 for a household user; chip states; ledger filters); `crates/pf-ui/tests/audit_ledger.rs::filters_and_paging`; logs `event="ui.render" page="admin.audit"`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: G01: Admin area shell (/admin) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies; the parent holds the verbatim spec and is the integration/closure bead).
- Also waits for: nothing else.

title: G01.b: People (disable cascade), Groups, Agents (revoke cascade + Undo all) admin pages
description:
## Goal and why

Manage the household from one screen: who exists, which groups there are, and every agent connection across people, with the cascades that actually revoke access.

## Scope

- **People**: every `users` row (`username`, `display_name`, `auth_source`, `status`, `in_audience`, `last_seen_at`); disable (step-up) sets `status = 'disabled'`, ends sessions, bumps the user's minter epochs and **revokes their agent connections' tokens** (T45's cascade); link to T42's cleanup lists once they exist; service users (`svc-*`, T64.b) excluded.
- **Groups**: `groups` rows with `source`, member counts, `managed`; creating local `pf-*` groups is T94.d (this page lists and links).
- **Agents**: every `agent_connections` row across people (`agent_name`, "for <person>" from `agent_connections.user_id` or the service label, `kind`, scopes, spaces, `last_used_at`, `expires_at`), Revoke (T45 cascade) and the grants each made (`grants.created_by_conn`) with "Undo all".

## Not in scope

The shell and ledger (G01.a); unsandboxed list/toggle and owner change (G01.c).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabling a person ends their sessions, bumps their epochs and revokes their connections' tokens (next agent call 401).
- [ ] The Agents page shows "for <person>" and "Undo all" revokes exactly the grants that connection made (audit rows).

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/admin_people_agents.spec.ts`; `crates/pf-api/tests/admin_disable_cascade.rs`; logs `event="audit" action="user.disable"`, `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: G01: Admin area shell (/admin) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies; the parent holds the verbatim spec and is the integration/closure bead).
- Also waits for: G01.a (the shell).
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] The Agents page shows "for <person>" and "Undo all" revokes exactly the grants that connection made (audit rows).

title: G01.c: unsandboxed parts list + the unsandboxed toggle (danger red, step-up, audit, epoch bump), owner change
description:
## Goal and why

Two admin-only switches that change a part's trust boundary, each visible, audited and immediate.

## Scope

- **Unsandboxed list**: every part with `parts.isolation = 'unsandboxed'`.
- **Toggle** (share sheet admin section and the admin page, danger red): session-only handler, admin + step-up, writes `audit` (`part.isolation`, before → after), bumps the part epoch so open tabs re-grant, and the chrome CORS set drops the part's origin at once (T29.b).
- **Owner change**: updates `parts.owner_user_id`, writes `audit` (`part.owner_set`), bumps the part epoch; the new owner sees the part in "Mine".

## Not in scope

The shell (G01.a); People/Groups/Agents (G01.b).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Toggling unsandboxed writes an audit row, bumps the epoch, and the next chrome-API preflight from that origin gets no CORS headers.
- [ ] Owner change is audited and effective on the next request; non-admin attempts get 403.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/admin_unsandboxed_owner.spec.ts`; `crates/pf-api/tests/unsandboxed_toggle.rs::{audit_row, epoch_bump, cors_dropped}`; logs `event="audit" action="part.isolation"`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: G01: Admin area shell (/admin) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies; the parent holds the verbatim spec and is the integration/closure bead).
- Also waits for: G01.a (the shell).
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] Owner change is audited and effective on the next request; non-admin attempts get 403.

title: G02: Workspace PWA install + the cross-page error-page e2e (request id on 500, no-leak 404 suggestions, identical part-host 404s, 429)
description:
## Goal and why

The plan specifies a family of Stockroom error pages, but only the 403 page (T27) and the 503 maintenance page (T89) have owners. Errors are where people and agents get stuck; a consistent page with a catalogue-style status line, one sentence and one action, plus the request id, makes every failure self-explanatory and debuggable (the admin can paste the id into the Debug tab, T109). The workspace also installs as a PWA, which no task owns (T120 covers per-part installs only).

## Scope

Error pages: paper background, the mark, a mono status line like a catalogue code, one sentence, one action:

| Code | Line | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `404 · NOT IN STOCK` | "There's no part called *grocery-planr*." + up to 3 close names you can see | Back to Parts |
| `410 · LINK EXPIRED` | "This link expired on 12 Oct." (only for public links with an expiry) | Ask the sender for a new one |
| `410 · INVITE USED` | "This invite has been used. Ask whoever sent it for a new one." | — |
| `429 · SLOW DOWN` | "Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again." | — |
| `500 · SOMETHING BROKE` | "partifactory hit an error. It's been logged as `req 8f1c…`." (the request id) | Try again |

- Close names: only names of parts the viewer can see (never leak existence), ranked by edit distance, at most 3.
- Errors inside a part stay inside its frame; the wrapper only adds the Details tick.
- Same templates on the workspace host and the part host (the part-host variants carry no cookies and no part content).
- Workspace PWA: a web app manifest for `parts.<domain>` (name, icons from the drawer mark, theme colour `--pf-signal`, `display: standalone`, scope `/`).

## Not in scope

403 page and Ask for access (T27/T120), 503 maintenance page (T89), per-part manifests (T29/T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- 404 on a part host for an unknown `kid`/bad MAC looks identical to a missing part (no oracle).
- The request id comes from the ingress header or is generated (T89/T106) and is always shown on 500.
- Copy: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no "Oops".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each code renders its line and action in light and dark and at 360 px; a 500 shows the request id that appears in the server log line for that request.
- [ ] The 404 suggestions never include a part the viewer can't see (test with a private part one edit away).
- [ ] The workspace installs as a PWA in Chromium (manifest valid).

## Tests

- `pf-ui` unit `error_page_templates_render` (golden HTML per code) and `close_names_respect_visibility`.
- e2e `tests/e2e/error_pages.spec.ts`: triggers each error, asserts the request id on the page matches `request_id` in `target/e2e-logs/error_pages/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 "Error pages", "Mobile" (workspace installs as a PWA); §5d Logs (request id on every error page).

## Dependency context

- Gap bead: a plan item that no task in the task graph owned; added during bead conversion.
- Depends on: T27, T31, T106
- Feeds milestone(s): M1

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

**Re-scoped (polish round).** The 404/403/410/429/500 page templates are owned by T31.a (rendering, golden HTML, the close-names visibility rule); T27 and T30 only reference them; `410 · INVITE USED` is T94.a's to wire and test. This bead keeps:
- the **workspace PWA**: `parts.<domain>` web app manifest (`display: standalone`, scope `/`, icons, theme colour) and the install affordance;
- the cross-page e2e `tests/e2e/error_pages.spec.ts`: the 500 page's request id equals the `request_id` in `target/e2e-logs/error_pages/server.jsonl`; the 404 page's suggestions never include a part the person can't see; the part-host 404 is byte-identical for a bad `kid` and a missing part; the 429 page after T30's limiter trips (edge added: T30).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each code renders its line and action in light and dark and at 360 px; a 500 shows the request id that appears in the server log line for that request.
- [ ] The 404 suggestions never include a part the viewer can't see (test with a private part one edit away).
- [ ] The workspace installs as a PWA in Chromium (manifest valid).

title: G03: Visual regression suite for workspace and wrapper screens (light, dark, 360 px)
description:
## Goal and why

The plan's build notes require visual regression: Playwright screenshots of the gallery, part view, share sheet and `/device` in light, dark and at 360 px, compared per PR. UI beads mention it but no task owns the job. A regression in the Stockroom chrome (the amber "public" signal, the audience chip, the share-sheet ladder) is a safety regression, not only cosmetic, because colour and placement carry meaning (amber always means "outside the house").

## Scope

- Playwright project `tests/e2e/visual/` on the T24 harness with fixture data (deterministic part numbers, frozen clock, fonts embedded).
- Screens: gallery (grid and list), part view wrapper, share sheet (each rung, Can contribute selected), `/device` approval page, sign-in page; each in light, dark and at 360 x 740.
- Baselines checked in under `tests/e2e/visual/__screenshots__/`; diff threshold small (e.g. 0.1 % pixels) with masks for live counters.
- CI job on every PR, uploading diffs as artifacts; a documented `--update-snapshots` flow.

## Not in scope

Building the screens (T31, T44, T120); the contrast test (T31).

## Design notes and decisions

Determinism matters more than coverage: freeze time, seed ids, disable the agent pulse animation via `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The job runs on every PR and fails on an intentional token change; passes on main.
- [ ] Each listed screen x theme x viewport has a baseline.

## Tests

The suite itself; a self-test PR changing `--pf-public` must fail it. On failure keep the diff PNGs, the trace and `target/e2e-logs/visual/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.9 Copy voice and build notes (visual regression, contrast test); §4a.3 tokens.

## Dependency context

- Gap bead: a plan item that no task in the task graph owned; added during bead conversion.
- Depends on: T31, T44
- Feeds milestone(s): M1

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T120 (the inward rungs, versions rail and comments rail are its screens). The 403/404 error pages (T31.a) join the screen list: colour and placement carry meaning there too.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The job runs on every PR and fails on an intentional token change; passes on main.
- [ ] Each listed screen x theme x viewport has a baseline.

title: G04: Thumbnails endpoint with the SVG spec-sheet thumb, and `views?` in part_get
description:
## Goal and why

Several small plan items around the part view and gallery have no task: the `?dl=1` download path the sandbox needs (since `<a download>` filenames are lost for own-host URLs), the ⋯ menu's Download as zip, Pin and Open standalone, the gallery thumbnail endpoint with its server-drawn SVG fallback (T81 assumes it), and per-part view counts on Details and in `part_get`. Each is small; together they close the gaps between the wrapper, the gallery and Insights.

## Scope

- **`?dl=1`**: on the content listener, a part file requested with `?dl=1` under a valid cap is served with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<basename>"` (the sandbox loses `<a download>` filenames for own-host URLs).
- **⋯ menu**: Open standalone ↗ (opens `/c/<cap>/` in a new tab, the only place a cap is visible), Download as zip (all files of the viewed version, streamed), Pin (per-person pinned list shown first in the gallery's "Pinned" section).
- **Thumbnails**: `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>` on the workspace, session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`, never edge-cached. Order of preference: sidecar screenshot (T81), the agent's own `meta.thumbnail` (PNG/WebP ≤ 256 KB), else a server-drawn SVG spec-sheet thumb (title, first heading, kind, first lines, a colour strip from the part's CSS), so the grid never has holes.
- **View counts**: per-part views per day and unique viewers from Insights rollups (T105) shown in Details and returned by `part_get` (a small `views` object), never cross-part tracking.

## Not in scope

Screenshot thumbnails (T81), Details sheet layout (T120.c), Insights pages (T108).

## Design notes and decisions

- Pin storage: a small per-person table or `kv` entry; recommend a `pins(user_id, part_id, at)` table added by migration.
- Thumbnails are part-derived content, so they are never `public` and never on the blob host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `?dl=1` returns `Content-Disposition: attachment` with the file's name and still carries no `Set-Cookie`.
- [ ] A gallery of parts with no screenshots and no agent thumbnails shows SVG thumbs, no holes; a viewer without access gets 404 on the thumb URL.
- [ ] Pinned parts appear first; Download as zip contains exactly the version's files.
- [ ] `part_get` returns view counts matching the T105 rollup fixture.

## Tests

`pf-serve` integration `download_param_sets_content_disposition`; `pf-ui` integration `thumbs_grant_checked_private_immutable`; golden SVG thumb test; e2e pin + zip in `tests/e2e/part_menu.spec.ts` with server JSONL kept.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Known losses under the sandbox (`?dl=1`); §4a.6 Gallery thumbnails, Part view ⋯ menu; §5d Analytics (per-part counts on Details, readable via `part_get`).

## Dependency context

- Gap bead: a plan item that no task in the task graph owned; added during bead conversion.
- Depends on: T16, T31, T105
- Feeds milestone(s): M1

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

**Re-scoped (polish round).** `?dl=1` is T16.b's, "Open standalone" is T31.b's, "Download as zip" and "Pin" (with the gallery Pinned section and a `pins(user_id, part_id, at)` table added by migration) are T120.c's, analytics in Details is T108's. This bead keeps:
- the thumbnails endpoint `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>` on the workspace: session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`, never edge-cached, preference order render-sidecar screenshot (T81) → `meta.thumbnail` (≤ 256 KB, T81 adds the field) → the server-drawn SVG spec-sheet thumb (title, first heading, kind, first lines, a colour strip from the part's CSS), so the grid never has holes;

title: T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
description:
## Goal and why

`/grant` is the one place on the workspace host (where the session cookie lives) that turns "this signed-in person wants to open this part" into a capability for that part's host. It's how every human view begins: the part host's wrapper (T29) has no cap on first open, so it sends the browser to `/grant`, which authenticates, asks the policy engine (T26), mints the cap (T15) and sends the browser back with the cap in a URL fragment that never reaches a server or a `Referer`.

Why: caps in the path let the content listener authorise requests without the DB, and the part host never sets or reads cookies; `/grant` is the bridge between the cookie world (workspace) and the cookie-free world (part hosts). It must be impossible to use as an open redirect, and it must never reveal what a person can't see. In Slice 1 (sign-in lane; required by T29, T30, T38, T70, T73, T64).

## Scope

- Route on the workspace host: `GET /grant?part=<name>&path=<path>&mode=wrap|direct`.
  - **Path-only input**: `path` ≤ 2 KiB and must start with `/`; the target host is **derived from the name** (`https://<name>-part.<domain>`), so `/grant` **can't act as an open redirect**. Unknown/invalid name → the 404 page (`404 · NOT IN STOCK`), never a redirect.
  - Authenticates with the workspace session (T24.a). **Signed out** → the sign-in page carrying the **content-free card** (T75), then returns to `/grant` with the same parameters after sign-in. Never content.
  - Asks the policy engine for the effective role. **Signed in and allowed** → mint a cap (T15) with subject `user:<id>`, minter `sess:<id>`, the role, epochs, window, and:
    - **`wrap` mode** (default, used by the wrapper): `302` to `https://<name>-part.<domain><path>#pf=<cap>`. The cap appears **only in the fragment**.
    - **`direct` mode** (a standalone `/c/` URL that lost its cap): `302` to `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap><path>`.
  - **Signed in but not allowed** → `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` page: "This part exists, but it isn't shared with you." with **no title**, and "Sign in as someone else". (**Ask for access** button arrives with T120.)
  - No one-time code: it existed only to set a cookie (round 2 removed it).
- **Silent re-entry**: a top-level navigation to `/c/…` with an expired window or stale epoch on the part host 302s to `/grant?mode=direct` (implemented in T16); if still allowed, `/grant` returns straight back with a fresh cap — zero interactions (click budget "Open a part I may see, already signed in: 0").
- **Credentialed regrant endpoint** for wrappers and embedders: `POST https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` (same-site credentialed fetch carrying the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie) → JSON `{cap, expires_at}` for the same path/role; the wrapper (T29) and `pf-embed.js` (T64) set a freshly minted frame `src` with no navigation when the prelude posts `{type: "pf:regrant"}`. CORS and CSRF rules for `/api/chrome/v1/*` are owned by T29; this task implements the handler and its policy check.
- Error pages in the Stockroom style for these outcomes (paper, the mark, a mono status line, one sentence, one action): `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU`, `404 · NOT IN STOCK` (with up to 3 close names the person can see), `429 · SLOW DOWN` (rate limits in T30), `500 · SOMETHING BROKE` with the request id.
- Metrics/logs: `/grant` decision + 302 p99 target < 1 ms server time (tracked); `event="grant.decide" outcome=allow|deny|signin` with `part_id`, never the cap.

## Not in scope

- The wrapper page and `#pf=` handling client-side (T29); cap format/verification (T15); content-listener navigation-vs-subresource rule (T16); Ask for access and access asks (T120); rate limits on `/grant` (T30); public links `/l/<token>` (T29); embedders (T64).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why the fragment:* browsers strip fragments from requests and `Referer`, and the wrapper removes it with `history.replaceState` before any other code runs, so the cap never appears in server logs or address bars.
- The "no cap → `/grant`" hop must be client-side (`location.replace` in the wrapper), because the server never sees the fragment and can't tell a cap-carrying load from a bare one (round 2b correction).
- *Cost, stated:* the first open in a tab costs one extra redirect hop; reloads reuse the wrapper's stored cap.
- Framed parts never navigate themselves to `/grant`: a subframe navigation from an opaque origin is cross-site for `SameSite=Lax`, so the session cookie wouldn't be sent and a login page would render inside the frame. Hence the credentialed regrant endpoint.
- The 403 page never reveals the title; public-link holders never see it (a revoked link is a plain 404).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Open-redirect fuzz: no input yields a Location outside the part's host; `wrap` puts the cap only in the fragment; an expired cap on a navigation re-enters /grant silently; a signed-in person without access gets `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with no title".

- [ ] Fuzzed `part`/`path`/`mode` inputs never yield a `Location` outside `https://<name>-part.<domain>` (or the workspace sign-in page).
- [ ] `wrap` → `Location` with `#pf=<cap>` and no cap in path or query; `direct` → `/c/<cap><path>`.
- [ ] Signed out → sign-in page with content-free card; after sign-in, back to the part.
- [ ] An expired cap on a top-level navigation completes the round trip silently (no interaction).
- [ ] Not allowed → 403 page with no title or name of the part beyond what's in the URL.
- [ ] `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed session and 403 otherwise.
- [ ] Logs never contain the cap.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-auth/tests/grant_fuzz.rs::no_open_redirect` (proptest over names, paths with `//`, `\`, `%2F`, `@`, unicode, overlong; asserts the Location host).
- `grant_wrap_fragment_only`, `grant_direct_path_cap`, `grant_signed_out_shows_signin_card`, `grant_forbidden_no_title`, `grant_unknown_name_404`.
- `regrant_endpoint_mints_fresh_cap` (asserts `event="grant.decide" mode="regrant" outcome="allow"`).
- `grant_logs_never_contain_cap` (canary cap secret; uses `capture_logs()`).
- e2e `tests/e2e/identity/grant_flow.spec.ts` (T24 harness): open `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` signed in → one hop → clean address bar; expire caps via test clock → reload re-enters silently; outsider user → 403 page text and no title in DOM. Keeps trace/HAR showing the 302 chain.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Serving a part: Hand-off, Errors on the part host, Framed expiry, Leaked URLs; §2 The link to post: the flow on first open; §4a.6 Error pages; §3a UX click budgets; §7 Part hosts and the sandbox (`/grant` can't redirect off host, fuzzed). Decision 25. dag2.py T27.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Open-redirect fuzz: no input yields a Location outside the part's host; `wrap` puts the cap only in the fragment; an expired cap on a navigation re-enters /grant silently; a signed-in person without access gets `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with no title
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test)
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
- Unblocks: 
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T30: Rate limits (governor, per route and principal, trusted client IP) + pre-auth body caps
  - T74: nginx + HAProxy comparison on the real content path (cap check, /c/ prefix, brotli), same box
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
  - T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved
  - T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
  - T64: Embedding via [embed] frame_ancestors and pf-embed.js, plus service identities (the Nest first)
  - G02: Workspace error pages (404 NOT IN STOCK, 410, 429, 500 with request id) and workspace PWA install

title: G07: One-screen regrant UI after a parts-only import
description:
## Goal and why

A parts-only import recreates every part and its history but carries no access records, by design. description:
## Goal and why

Exit of phase **P1 Edge + identity**: partifactory is reachable from the internet through any ingress, people sign in through generic OIDC, the part-host wrapper and public links work, backups/exports/drills are real, observability and disk safety are in place, and portability is proven by a vendor-free CI lane. Adapters for the example deployment (Cloudflare, Authentik) land in the same phase as the generic default they sit beside, never before it. Critical path to M1 (14 steps): ... T16 -> T17 -> T62 -> T77 -> T113 -> T114 -> T68 -> M1; the janitor and disk budget sit on it because `doctor` checks that every store is capped.

## Scope (what P1 contains)

The ingress contract with example proxy configs, `provision` with the manual and Cloudflare providers, generic OIDC login + the claims re-read directory, the Authentik directory adapter, `/grant` -> the part host, the part-host wrapper with its chrome API and CORS, policy engine + audience ladder + spaces + the role x runtime matrix, admin pin + native passkey step-up, the Stockroom workspace (gallery, search, history, diff, preview old versions, restore, bin, share sheet, Move to Family), admin-only public links on the part host with open counts, tier (a) cards, rate limits, quotas, Health page with optional ops alerts, backups (consistent DB copy, `export`/`import`, nightly export on by default, per-part data snapshots on by default), the first drill on a second OCI host, the image + compose + env contract with an example CI workflow, `doctor`, the Insights store with request ids, traces and the log pipeline, the janitor, the disk budget and the retention test, the no-content-in-logs fuzz test, the portability lane, and the nginx/HAProxy comparison on the real content path. Real-device pass including the 5-minute Telegram in-app-browser passkey test.

Direct dependencies: T31, T35, T38, T68, T74, T77, T92, T93, T112, T115, T91, T119, T120, T121.

## Not in scope

Agents (P2), backends (P2a), invites (P2b).

## Acceptance criteria (P1 "Done when")

dag2.py: "the admin opens a part on a phone at its own host link via SSO; the portability lane is green; a public link opens from mobile data with no login and unfurls as a card; the security checklist passes; the drill restores everything on a second OCI host."

  - T35: `partifactory import` (full or parts-only, boot-epoch bump, regrant helper) + laptop drill and report

  - T92: Authentik adapter: Directory over the API (60 s poll) + IdpProvisioner plugin (OIDC app, cloned flows, invite flow)
  - T93: Portability lane: full e2e with no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea (Dex, IdP-less, Caddy, local exports)
  - T112: No-content-in-logs fuzz test: canaries across every surface never reach logs, traces, insights.db or /metrics
  - T115: Retention table test: every existing §5h store filled past its cap comes back under
  - T91: Cloudflare adapter: tunnel ingress, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe
  - T119: Card pipeline (SVG -> resvg PNG) and the titled public-link card
  - T120: Workspace UI after Slice 1: versions rail, bin, search, diff, comments, inward sharing, Ask for access, install
  - T121: Optional ops-alert webhook (off by default): HMAC-signed `{alert, severity, detail, at}`
  - G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change
  - G02: Workspace error pages (404 NOT IN STOCK, 410, 429, 500 with request id) and workspace PWA install

- Unblocks: nothing

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans).

title: T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass
description:
## Goal and why

Make "admin is the owner, and only the owner" true and cheap to verify: admin rights come from **one pinned immutable subject** in site config, admin actions require a **fresh partifactory-native passkey assertion** (within 10 minutes), an IdP-less deployment can bootstrap its admin from the host console, and a console **break-glass** login exists for when the IdP is down.

Why:
- The admin is the only one who can make data leave the house (public links, everyone-signed-in, invites, groups, LAN allowlist, `unsandboxed`, renames). If membership in any IdP group (including the IdP's own admins) granted admin, a compromised or misconfigured IdP would hand out the keys. Pinning the subject means **being added to any IdP group grants nothing here**.
- **Step-up is native WebAuthn, not trust in IdP claims** (`max_age`/`amr` behaviour isn't load-bearing). A stolen session can't administer without the admin's passkey.
- *Why one 10-minute window:* short enough that a stolen session can't administer, long enough for a batch of admin changes. (Round 1 said 30 in one table and 10 in another; it's 10.)
- `rp.id` = the apex lets **one passkey** serve the workspace and every part-host wrapper, so the in-sheet step-up in the share sheet works on the part host (the Slice 1 pixel test: Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy, 4 interactions + 1 biometric).
- Household sharing never needs step-up.
- In Slice 1 (sign-in lane; required by T29, T36, T38, T43, T70, T94).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after both subtasks close and the parent acceptance passes end to end):
- **T28.a** — admin pin, `is_admin` checks, `partifactory admin bootstrap`, `partifactory admin break-glass`.
- **T28.b** — WebAuthn (`webauthn-rs` 0.5) admin passkey registration and step-up assertion with `rp.id` = `[domain] apex`, accepted from the workspace origin and every active sandboxed part-host origin, verified at `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/stepup` (and the workspace equivalent), setting `sessions.stepup_at`; `step_up_required` enforcement.

**Admin actions that need an assertion within 10 minutes** (the list the enforcement covers): public links (and switching one to Can contribute), `everyone-signed-in`, invites, add-by-email, groups, users, LAN allowlist entries for backends, agent consent into spaces the consenting person doesn't own, `unsandboxed`, renames. Without a fresh assertion → `step_up_required` (HTTP 403, CLI exit 3).

## Not in scope

- The share sheet UI (T31) beyond exposing step-up endpoints; local passkey accounts for invitees (`purpose='login'`, T94); device-approval passkey use (T44 consumes `purpose='stepup'` passkeys); the Health page display of break-glass use (T36 shows it from the audit log).

## Design notes and decisions

- Pin format: `[admin] subject = "oidc:<issuer>#<sub>"` or `"local:<id>"` — immutable identifiers, never a username or group.
- The admin subject pin lives in site config, which has an offline copy (password manager) for DR.
- Break-glass needs local shell access, works when the IdP is down, and is logged and shown on the Health page and in the audit log.
- Allowed-origin set for assertions equals the chrome CORS set (T29): the workspace and every active, sandboxed part host — never an `unsandboxed` part's origin (its code is same-origin with its wrapper).
- Real-device check: the T72 spike item 13 verifies a WebAuthn assertion from the wrapper origin with `rp.id` = apex on Safari and the Telegram webview; T38 re-checks on real phones.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "IdP-admin user gets 403; an admin action without a fresh assertion returns `step_up_required`; a passkey registered on the workspace asserts from a part-host wrapper (virtual authenticator); household sharing never asks; `admin bootstrap` registers a local admin passkey once; break-glass works once within 5 min and is audited".

- [ ] T28.a and T28.b closed.
- [ ] A user in the IdP's admin group (not the pinned subject) gets 403 on every admin route.
- [ ] Admin action without assertion → `step_up_required`; with one < 10 min old → allowed; at 10 min + 1 s → `step_up_required` again.
- [ ] A passkey registered on `https://parts.pf.test` asserts from `https://pixel-part.pf.test/` (virtual authenticator, Chromium).
- [ ] Inward household sharing never triggers step-up.
- [ ] `admin bootstrap` works exactly once on an IdP-less deployment; break-glass works once within 5 minutes and writes an audit row.

## Tests

- Parent closing check: `tests/e2e/identity/stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts` (T24 harness, Chromium + virtual authenticator): register admin passkey on the workspace, open a part host, trigger an admin action in the share sheet, complete in-sheet step-up with no navigation; asserts server log `event="stepup.verify" origin="https://pixel-part.pf.test" outcome="ok"`.
- Subtask tests as listed in T28.a and T28.b.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Admin is the admin, and only the admin; §3a UX click budgets (step-up is in-page WebAuthn); §4a.6 Share sheet (in-sheet step-up), Admin (step-up chip); §5e `passkeys`, `break_glass`, `sessions.stepup_at`; §4b error catalogue (`step_up_required`); §7 Identity and admin; §5 spike item 13; §10 final round F04. Decision 7. dag2.py T28.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): IdP-admin user gets 403; an admin action without a fresh assertion returns `step_up_required`; a passkey registered on the workspace asserts from a part-host wrapper (virtual authenticator); household sharing never asks; `admin bootstrap` registers a local admin passkey once; break-glass works once within 5 min and is audited
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T24: Generic OIDC client, workspace session cookie, sign out everywhere, and the TLS e2e harness (Dex + Caddy + pf.test)
- Unblocks: 
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T36: Health page (basic), /readyz (DB, blobs, disk; not the IdP), degraded indicators, backup layers, store sizes
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
  - G01: Admin area shell (/admin): People, Groups, Agents, Audit ledger, step-up chip, unsandboxed list, owner change
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T28.a: Admin subject pin, is_admin checks, `partifactory admin bootstrap` and `admin break-glass`

title: T28.a: Admin subject pin, is_admin checks, `partifactory admin bootstrap` and `admin break-glass`
description:
## Goal and why

Implement the identity side of "only the owner is admin": a pinned immutable subject, a single `is_admin(principal)` check used by every admin route, a one-time console bootstrap for IdP-less deployments, and a console break-glass login for IdP outages. These are the recovery and bootstrap paths that make the pin safe to rely on.

## Scope

- Config `[admin] subject = "oidc:<issuer>#<sub>" | "local:<id>"` (validated by `partifactory config check`, T04). `is_admin(principal)` is true only when the session's user matches the pinned subject exactly (`users.idp_issuer`/`idp_sub` for OIDC, `users.id` for local). Agents are never admin (no admin scopes obtainable).
- Admin route guard (`RequireAdmin` extractor) for `/admin/*`, admin chrome-API handlers and admin-only ops paths; combined with T28.b's `RequireStepUp` for the step-up list.
- **`partifactory admin bootstrap`** (host console): only when no admin passkey exists yet and `[admin] subject` is `local:<id>` or unset on an IdP-less deployment; creates the local admin user (`users.auth_source='local'`) if needed and prints a **one-time link** (short expiry, single use, stored hashed) to register the admin's passkey as a local account (`passkeys.purpose='login'` and `'stepup'`, registration flow from T28.b). A second run after success refuses ("admin already bootstrapped"). Audit `admin.bootstrap`.
- **`partifactory admin break-glass`** (host console): prints a one-time admin login **valid for 5 minutes**:
```sql
CREATE TABLE break_glass (
  code_hash  BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- +5 min
  used_at    INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
  Redeeming it at `GET /admin/break-glass?code=…` creates an admin session (with `stepup_at` = now, since possession of the console is the stronger factor) and sets `used_at`; second use or after 5 min → refused. Works when the IdP is down. Audited with `actor='break-glass'` and surfaced on the Health page (T36) and in the audit log.
- Both commands talk to the DB directly through the single writer path (they run in the same container via `docker compose exec`).

## Not in scope

- WebAuthn ceremonies (T28.b), the Health page rendering (T36), admin UI pages (T120 etc.).

## Design notes and decisions

- Pin, not group: being added to any IdP group (including the IdP's own admins) grants nothing here.
- Break-glass requires local shell, so its threat model is "someone with the host already"; it's for IdP outages and lost passkeys.
- Codes stored only as sha256 (secrets are stored only as sha256 per §5e principles); printed once.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An IdP-admin-group user who isn't the pinned subject gets 403 on every admin route.
- [ ] `admin bootstrap` registers a local admin passkey once; a second run refuses.
- [ ] Break-glass code works once within 5 minutes, fails after use or expiry, and writes an audit row with `actor='break-glass'`.
- [ ] Config check rejects a malformed `[admin] subject`.

## Tests

- `pf_auth::admin::tests::pin_matches_exact_subject_only` (oidc and local forms; similar-looking subjects rejected).
- `crates/partifactory/tests/admin_cli.rs::bootstrap_once` (runs the subcommand twice; asserts the one-time link redeems once), `break_glass_once_within_5_min` (test clock at +4m59s ok, reuse fails, +5m01s fails; asserts `event="admin.break_glass" outcome=...` and the audit row).
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/admin_guard.rs::idp_admin_group_gets_403`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Admin is the admin, and only the admin (pin, bootstrap, break-glass); §5e `break_glass`, `users`, `audit`; §7 Identity and admin; §5f portability lane (IdP-less pass uses `admin bootstrap`). dag2.py T28.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
