title: T28.b: WebAuthn step-up: admin passkey registration, rp.id = apex, assertions from workspace + sandboxed part-host origins, step_up_required
description:
## Goal and why

Native passkey step-up for admin actions, built on `webauthn-rs` 0.5, so admin power requires the admin's own passkey within the last 10 minutes regardless of what the IdP says. `rp.id` = the apex makes one passkey usable from the workspace and from every part-host wrapper, so the share sheet on the part host can step up in-sheet with no navigation.

## Scope

- `passkeys` table (T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE passkeys (
  cred_id     BLOB PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  purpose     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('login','stepup')),  -- login: local accounts; stepup: step-up and device approval, for any person who registered one (rp.id = the apex)
  passkey     BLOB NOT NULL,                         -- serialized webauthn-rs Passkey
  label       TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_used_at INTEGER,
  revoked_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
- Relying party: `rp.id` = `[domain] apex` (e.g. `<domain>`), `rp.name` "partifactory"; discoverable credentials; user verification required.
- **Registration** (signed-in person, on the workspace): `POST /api/v1/webauthn/register/start|finish` (session-only handlers) → `purpose='stepup'` passkey. The admin always has one (bootstrap via T28.a for local admins).
- **Assertion / step-up**:
  - Workspace: `POST /api/session/stepup/start|finish`.
  - Part-host wrapper: `POST https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/stepup` (start/finish), credentialed same-site fetch; the chrome CORS and CSRF rules of T29 apply.
  - Accepted origins in client data: the workspace origin `https://parts.<domain>` **and every active, sandboxed part-host origin** `https://<label>-part.<domain>` (same set the chrome CORS admits: active part name, not `blobs`, not a redirecting old name, not `unsandboxed`). Any other origin → rejected.
  - On success set `sessions.stepup_at = now` and `passkeys.last_used_at`.
- **Enforcement**: `RequireStepUp` guard: `now - sessions.stepup_at <= 10 min` else `step_up_required` (403). Applied to: public links (create, switch to Can contribute), `everyone-signed-in`, invites, add-by-email, groups, users, LAN allowlist entries, agent consent into spaces the consenting person doesn't own, `unsandboxed`, renames. Never to household (inward) sharing.
- Expose `step_up_status` for the UI chip (`Admin unlocked · 8 min` / `Locked`).
- Audit `stepup.verify` (outcome, origin) without credential material.

## Not in scope

- Local passkey sign-in accounts and recovery (T94); device-approval use of passkeys (T44); the share sheet UI (T31); the T72 real-browser spike (separate task).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why native WebAuthn:* the IdP's `max_age`/`prompt=login` behaviour varies by provider and isn't load-bearing; a passkey assertion is.
- Accepting assertions from sandboxed part-host origins is safe because only the wrapper's own code runs with that origin (part content runs in an opaque origin and sends `Origin: null`); unsandboxed parts are excluded because their code is same-origin with the wrapper.
- One 10-minute window for all admin actions.
- Risk: Safari/Telegram webview behaviour with `rp.id` = apex from a subdomain (spike T72 item 13; real-device pass T38).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A passkey registered on the workspace asserts successfully from a part-host wrapper origin (virtual authenticator in Chromium).
- [ ] Assertions from `Origin: null`, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, a redirecting old name or a foreign origin are rejected.
- [ ] Admin action without fresh assertion → `step_up_required`; within 10 min → allowed.
- [ ] Household sharing never asks for step-up.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-auth/tests/webauthn.rs::register_and_assert_virtual` (webauthn-rs soft authenticator), `origin_allowlist` (table of allowed/refused origins), `stepup_window_10_min` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-auth/tests/stepup_guard.rs::admin_routes_require_stepup` (iterates the admin action list), `household_share_no_stepup`.
- e2e `tests/e2e/identity/stepup_from_wrapper.spec.ts` (shared with the parent; Chromium virtual authenticator; asserts `event="stepup.verify" outcome="ok"` and that no navigation occurred).

## References

PLAN.md §3a Admin is the admin, and only the admin (step-up, `rp.id`, `/api/chrome/v1/<part>/stepup`); §2 Chrome actions (allowed origin set); §5e `passkeys`, `sessions.stepup_at`; §5 spike item 13; §10 final round F04. dag2.py T28.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T28.a: Admin subject pin, is_admin checks, `partifactory admin bootstrap` and `admin break-glass`

- [ ] Assertions from `Origin: null`, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, a redirecting old name or a foreign origin are rejected.
- [ ] Admin action without fresh assertion → `step_up_required`; within 10 min → allowed.
- [ ] Household sharing never asks for step-up.

title: T75: Content-free preview cards (Slice 1): two static 1200x630 PNGs at /og/<sha256>.png
description:
## Goal and why

Every link people post is a part's own host, `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, and chat apps unfurl it. The unfurl must never leak what a private part is. T75 is the Slice 1 part of the tier (a) preview cards: **two static 1200x630 PNG images embedded in the binary**. Both are the content-free card, one with the private audience line and one with the public-link line ("Anyone with the link"). Neither carries a title, a name or a thumbnail. Each is served at a content-addressed URL `/og/<sha256>.png`, together with og tags that say exactly what the image says.

Why static PNGs in Slice 1 (decision 40, provisional): in Slice 1 both card variants are content-free with fixed text, so a render pipeline would only draw two fixed images. The SVG -> resvg pipeline, bundled fonts and Rust-side wrapping move to T119, where fields first vary (the titled public-link card). The design rule still holds: **the audience decides the card, never the User-Agent**. Bots and browsers get byte-identical HTML, because unfurl-bot detection is unreliable (iMessage fetches from the sender's device, and several apps use browser-like UAs).

This serves the Slice 1 definition of done. A part with a public link unfurls with the content-free card in its public-link audience. The §7 "Links and cards" lines also need it: a signed-out fetch of a part root returns the content-free card and no part bytes. The wrapper (T29) and the sign-in page (T31) consume it.

## Scope

- Two PNGs, 1200 x 630, committed as golden files under `crates/pf-serve/assets/og/` (or `pf-ui`), embedded with `include_bytes!`:
  - **Private** variant: the mark, "A private part", "Sign in to open it", the workspace host name, a lock glyph. Never: title, name, part number, thumbnail, description, author, audience, counts.
  - **Public-link (content-free) variant**: the same content-free layout with the audience line "Anyone with the link". It has no title, name or thumbnail. (The titled public card is T119.)
- The frame shared by every variant, from the plan: `paper` background (Stockroom `--pf-paper` #f4f3ee), the 8 px drafting grid at 4 % ink, corner ticks 40 px in, the mark and wordmark top-left (`partifactory`, lowercase, Plex Sans Condensed SemiBold), and a catalogue-style title block bottom-right. The tagline "Parts, made by you and your agents." may appear (it is the plan's sign-in/card wordmark line).
- The workspace host name in the private card is site config (`[domain] workspace_host`). Because the PNGs are static, a generic host-agnostic text is acceptable, or the PNG says "partifactory" only. **Design note:** if the host name must appear, generate the two PNGs at build time per deployment. That is impossible with static embedded files, so the Slice 1 card omits the host and the og:description carries it instead (text tags must match the image, so the og text omits it too). Record the choice in the bead's closing comment.
- Serving: `GET /og/<sha256>.png` on the **workspace host** (`parts.<domain>`). Part-host pages reference cards by **absolute https URL**. The sha256 is the hash of the PNG bytes, so content-addressing is free. Response headers: `Content-Type: image/png`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (private and content-free cards are generic, so `/og/*` may sit in any shared cache), and no `Set-Cookie`. An unknown hash returns 404.
- og tag helper (a function in `pf-serve`/`pf-ui` used by T29's wrapper root, T31's sign-in page and `/grant`'s sign-in page): it emits `og:title` and `og:description` that **match the card text exactly**, `og:image` (absolute https), `og:image:width=1200`, `og:image:height=630`, `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. Pages carrying cards also send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
- A card-selection function `card_for(audience: Audience) -> CardRef` with `Audience::{Private, PublicLink}`. Its input type has **no part-derived field** (no title, name, kind, rev, thumbnail), so the content-free guarantee can be checked at compile and test time.

## Not in scope

- The SVG template, resvg/usvg, `fontdb`, `rustybuzz` wrapping, the titled public-link card and the `sha256(template_version, fields)` cache: T119.
- The invite card (`/i/<id>`): it arrives with invites (T94/T119 pipeline).
- Screenshot og:images and gallery thumbnails: T81.
- Deciding which audience applies to a given request (whether a public link is active): T29 (wrapper root) and T29.c (`/l/`).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 40 (provisional, pending the admin): two static PNGs in Slice 1, pipeline in T119. It removes `resvg`, font bundling and wrapping from the critical Slice 1 path.
- Content-addressed URLs mean a changed image is a new URL, so unfurl caches never go stale.
- The PNGs are designed artwork. Commit them with their source (an SVG in `assets/og/src/`) so T119 can reuse the frame, but nothing at runtime reads the SVG in Slice 1.
- Keep each PNG <= 150 KB (the plan's card output budget).
- Amber is reserved for "Public link" in Stockroom. The public-link variant may use the amber `--pf-public` accent on the audience line, and the private one must not.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Both PNGs are golden files with fixed text only; the og:title/og:description on the root and sign-in pages match the card text exactly; the private and public-link variants differ only in the audience line".

- [ ] Two PNGs at 1200x630, each <= 150 KB, embedded in the binary, committed as golden files.
- [ ] `GET /og/<sha256>.png` serves each one with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `image/png` and no `Set-Cookie`. Any other hash returns 404.
- [ ] The og tag helper output matches the card text exactly for both audiences, and includes `twitter:card=summary_large_image` and an absolute https `og:image`.
- [ ] A pixel diff shows the two variants differ only inside the audience-line region.
- [ ] The card input type has no part-derived field (unit test plus review).

## Tests

- `pf_serve::og::tests::golden_pngs_have_expected_dimensions_and_size`: decodes both PNGs and asserts 1200x630 and <= 150 KB.
- `pf_serve::og::tests::variants_differ_only_in_audience_line`: pixel diff, with a mask of the audience-line rectangle.
- `pf_serve::og::tests::og_tags_match_card_text`: for each `Audience`, the og:title and og:description equal the constants used to author the PNG text (one source-of-truth constant module `og_text.rs`).
- `pf_serve::og::tests::card_input_has_no_part_fields`: a compile-time and struct-field reflection check (or a `static_assertions` style test) that `CardInput` contains only `audience`.
- Integration test `crates/pf-serve/tests/og_route.rs`: GET each hash checks the headers and that there is no `Set-Cookie`, and GET an unknown hash returns 404. It asserts the log event `event="og.serve" outcome="ok"|"not_found"` with `route_class="og"`.
- Used by the T29 test that a signed-out root fetch returns the private card, and by §7 (T38).

## References

PLAN.md §4c Tier (a) (variants table, frame, og tag rules); "Slice 1: Decided for the slice" (every card is content-free); §2 "The link to post" (audience decides the card, not the UA); §4a.2/4a.3 Stockroom tokens; §5a card render target; decision 40; §7 Links and cards.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Both PNGs are golden files with fixed text only; the og:title/og:description on the root and sign-in pages match the card text exactly; the private and public-link variants differ only in the audience line
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T07: BlobStore trait + local impl: sha256, fan-out dirs, atomic durable writes, verify-on-read, storage_full
- Unblocks: 
  - T119: Card pipeline (SVG -> resvg PNG) and the titled public-link card
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
acceptance_criteria: Both PNGs are golden files with fixed text only; the og:title/og:description on the root and sign-in pages match the card text exactly; the private and public-link variants differ only in the audience line

title: T119: Card pipeline (SVG -> resvg PNG) and the titled public-link card
description:
## Goal and why

After Slice 1, a part with an active public link should unfurl with a **titled public card**: its title, kind bin code, revision, a short description and a thumbnail frame. Its title is already public at that point, so showing it is honest. Once card fields vary per part, static PNGs (T75) can't do the job. T119 builds the tier (a) render pipeline in the binary, with no browser: SVG template -> `usvg`/`resvg` -> 1200x630 PNG. Fonts are bundled (a `FROM scratch` image has no system fonts), and wrapping is done in Rust because resvg doesn't wrap. Output is cached and served content-addressed.

This keeps the plan's principle that **the audience decides the card**. The private card stays content-free. The public card appears only while a public link is active, and it goes back to content-free the moment the last link is revoked. It feeds M1 ("a public link opens from mobile data with no login and unfurls as a card").

## Scope

- Template: an SVG template (versioned constant `template_version`) that reproduces the shared frame: `paper`, the 8 px drafting grid at 4 % ink, corner ticks 40 px in, the mark and wordmark top-left, and a catalogue-style title block bottom-right. Reuse T75's SVG source.
- Render: `usvg` parse -> `resvg` render -> PNG 1200 x 630, output <= 150 KB, in a few ms.
- Fonts: bundled IBM Plex (Sans, Sans Condensed, Mono subsets; SIL OFL 1.1, licence in `NOTICE`) loaded into a `fontdb::Database` built once at start. There are no system fonts.
- Wrapping: titles are wrapped to <= 2 lines and ellipsised in Rust, measuring glyph advances with `rustybuzz`. Description: 2-3 lines.
- **Inputs are fixed fields, never part content**: `{template_version, audience, title?, description?, kind_label?, rev?, thumbnail?}`. The designer owns the template and the mechanics own the inputs.
- Cache: cache key `sha256(template_version, fields)`. The card is stored as a blob and served at **content-addressed `/og/<sha256>.png`** on the workspace host, so a new title or version means a new URL and unfurl caches never go stale.
- Variants:
  - Private (unchanged meaning; now rendered by the pipeline, or still T75's PNG): never title, name, part number, thumbnail, description, author, audience or counts.
  - **Public link**: shown on `https://<name>-part.<domain>/l/<token>`, and on the part host root while the part has an active public link. It shows the title, kind bin code (`HTML`, `TSX`, `MD`, `TXT`, `SVG`, `DECK`, `MMD`, `CODE`, `FILES`), `REV n`, a 2-3 line description, the thumbnail in a framed window, and "Anyone with the link · view only" (or the contribute wording). It never shows comments, data, who else has access, or agent notes.
- Thumbnail source (in order): the agent's own `meta.thumbnail` (PNG/WebP <= 256 KB), else a server-drawn SVG spec-sheet thumb, else an empty framed window. Screenshot thumbnails are T81.
- Wiring: T29.a's wrapper root and T29.c's `/l/` page call the card selector. While a public link is active the root carries the public card, and revoking the last public link puts the content-free card back on the root on the next request (the root reads through a cache that is invalidated on link change).
- og tags still match the card text exactly. They carry `noindex`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` and `twitter:card=summary_large_image`.

## Not in scope

- The static Slice 1 PNGs and the og tag helper: T75 (reused here).
- Screenshot og:images (opt-in per link) and gallery screenshot thumbnails: T81.
- The invite card text belongs with invites (T94), though it can use this pipeline.

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 40 moved the pipeline here. Card render target: < 20 ms p99 (§5a).
- The content-free guarantee is checkable by type: the private card's input struct must have no part-derived field. Keep separate input types per audience (`PrivateCardInput` with only `template_version`, `PublicCardInput` with fields), so the guarantee is enforced by the compiler.
- **Never derive the card from the User-Agent.** Bot and browser responses are byte-identical.
- Cards are part-independent for the private variant, so they are publicly cacheable. The public variant is public anyway because the link is public. `/og/*` is `public, immutable` (and is in the Cloudflare adapter's cache rules, T91).
- Unbounded card cache growth: card blobs are GC-able like any unreferenced blob (T59). Keep only the cards referenced by active links.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "A content-free card's input struct has no part-derived field (test); a title change yields a new image URL; the card never carries comments, data, agent notes or who else has access; revoking the last public link puts the content-free card back on the root; render < 20 ms p99".

- [ ] The SVG template plus resvg render produces 1200x630 PNGs <= 150 KB with bundled fonts only.
- [ ] Titles wrap to <= 2 lines with an ellipsis (rustybuzz measured) and descriptions to 2-3 lines.
- [ ] Changing the title, rev or description changes the `/og/<sha256>.png` URL.
- [ ] The root shows the public card only while an active public link exists, and the content-free card again after the last revoke.
- [ ] Render p99 < 20 ms (bench).

## Tests

- `pf_serve::cards::tests::private_input_has_no_part_fields` (type-level).
- `pf_serve::cards::tests::wrap_title_two_lines_ellipsis`: golden strings, including CJK and very long words.
- Golden image tests `tests/golden/cards/*.png` with a tolerance-based diff, for several titles, kinds and rev numbers, light only.
- `pf_serve::cards::tests::url_changes_with_fields`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/public_card_lifecycle.rs`: create a part, then a public link, and the root og:image is the public card. Revoke it and the root og:image is the content-free card. It asserts the log events `event="card.render" cache="miss"|"hit" latency_us`. The canary title appears in the PNG input only for the public variant.
- Bench `cards_render_p99` in the T23 bench harness: fails above 20 ms p99.

## References

PLAN.md §4c Tier (a) (pipeline, variants table, inputs rule); §5 Stack (Cards: resvg + usvg + fontdb + rustybuzz); §5a (card render < 20 ms); §4a.4 Type (Plex, OFL); §4a.5 kind bin codes; "Slice 1" (titled public card is T119); decision 40; §7 Links and cards.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A content-free card's input struct has no part-derived field (test); a title change yields a new image URL; the card never carries comments, data, agent notes or who else has access; revoking the last public link puts the content-free card back on the root; render < 20 ms p99
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T75: Content-free preview cards (Slice 1): two static 1200x630 PNGs at /og/<sha256>.png
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
- Unblocks: 
  - M1: Milestone - P1 Edge + identity done
  - T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
acceptance_criteria: A content-free card's input struct has no part-derived field (test); a title change yields a new image URL; the card never carries comments, data, agent notes or who else has access; revoking the last public link puts the content-free card back on the root; render < 20 ms p99

title: T89: Ingress contract: trusted client-IP header, request ids, Caddy example + maintenance page
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory takes no hard dependency on any one ingress vendor. The core asks one small **ingress contract** of whatever sits in front of it (Caddy, nginx, Traefik, or the Cloudflare tunnel adapter), and it ships a working example. T89 implements the core side of that contract (trusted client-IP extraction, request-id intake) and ships the reference proxy config (Caddy) plus the static maintenance page, all in `deploy/proxy/`.

Why it matters: rate limits (T30), analytics (T105) and the device-approval origin hints all key on the real client address. Behind a proxy, every request comes *from the proxy*, so trusting a header from anyone would let any client spoof its IP. Request ids tie a person's error page to the log line and trace (T106). This task is in Slice 1: the example deployment's tunnel runs as a plain proxy meeting this contract, configured by hand ("Ingress through the contract only").

## Scope

The contract (verbatim from the plan):
- route `parts.<domain>` to `:8080` and `*.<domain>` to `:8081`, preserving `Host`; terminate TLS with a cert covering both (one wildcard cert does);
- pass the client address in one header named in config (`[ingress] client_ip_header`, e.g. `X-Forwarded-For` or `CF-Connecting-IP`), trusted only from `[ingress] trusted_proxies`. Rate limits and analytics key on it;
- optionally pass a request id (`[ingress] request_id_header`); without one, partifactory makes its own. Logs and error pages show it;
- allow long-lived responses (SSE, long-poll <= 50 s) and request bodies up to 8 MiB.

Core implementation:
- A `tower` layer on both public listeners (:8080 workspace, :8081 content) that computes `ClientAddr`. If the TCP peer is in `trusted_proxies` (a CIDR list), parse `client_ip_header`. For `X-Forwarded-For`, take the right-most address not in `trusted_proxies`. Otherwise use the TCP peer and ignore the header entirely. The result goes into request extensions for T30, T105 and T44.
- A request-id layer: use `request_id_header`'s value when present, length <= 128 and printable; else generate (ULID or 128-bit random). Put it in the request extension and the tracing span field `request_id`, echo it as a response header (`X-Request-Id`), and expose it to error page templates.
- Config keys under `[ingress]`: `kind = proxy | cloudflare-tunnel | acme`, `client_ip_header`, `trusted_proxies`, `request_id_header` (T04 loads them).
- `:9090` (ops) is never routed through the ingress. The example configs must not expose it.
- `deploy/proxy/Caddyfile`: the example Caddy config (wildcard cert, two site blocks routed by Host, `X-Forwarded-For`, flush for SSE, body limit 8 MiB, timeouts allowing 60 s streams). It serves the maintenance page when the upstream is down. Start from the T24.b harness Caddyfile and make it the one shipped config: the harness then mounts this file (cert paths overridden), so the repo has exactly one Caddy config.
- `deploy/proxy/maintenance.html`: the static `503 · DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE` page in Stockroom style with inlined CSS (paper, the mark, a mono status line like a catalogue code, one sentence). No external assets.
- A smoke test script `deploy/proxy/smoke.sh` (or a Rust integration test) that the T126 nginx/Traefik configs and the portability lane (T93) reuse.

## Not in scope

- nginx and Traefik example configs: T126 (decision 42).
- The Cloudflare tunnel adapter, its fallback Worker and `CF-Connecting-IP` default: T91.
- Built-in ACME for hosts without a proxy: T90 (P5).
- Rate limit logic itself: T30. Trace store: T106.

## Design notes and decisions

- Edge caching is an optimisation, never required for correctness. Every response already carries the right `Cache-Control`.
- DNS wildcards must be a whole label (`*-part` isn't valid), so routing is one `*.<domain>` record plus one `parts.<domain>` record. The content listener answers only names ending `-part` (else 404) and counts non-part hits (T16/T18).
- Fail closed on spoofing: an untrusted peer's header is ignored, not partially used.
- The request id appears on every error page (`500 · SOMETHING BROKE ... logged as req 8f1c…`) and in API errors (`details.request_id`).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "The Caddy config passes a smoke test (routing by Host, SSE survives 60 s, 8 MiB body); a spoofed client-IP header from an untrusted address is ignored; the request id appears in logs and error pages".

- [ ] The Caddy example routes `parts.pf.test` to :8080 and `x-part.pf.test` to :8081 with `Host` preserved, over TLS with an internal-CA wildcard cert.
- [ ] An SSE stream through Caddy survives 60 s, and an 8 MiB request body is accepted (8 MiB + 1 is rejected by partifactory's own cap).
- [ ] A client-IP header from an untrusted peer is ignored. From a trusted peer it is used.
- [ ] An ingress request id is propagated to logs, the response header and error pages. A request without one gets a generated id.
- [ ] Caddy serves the maintenance page when the origin is down.

## Tests

- Unit `pf_serve::ingress::tests::xff_rightmost_untrusted`, `untrusted_peer_header_ignored`, `cf_connecting_ip_single_value`, `request_id_sanitised_or_generated`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/ingress_contract.rs`: start the listeners, send from a "trusted" and an "untrusted" loopback alias, and assert `ClientAddr` through a debug echo route. It asserts log fields `client_ip` (truncated form) and `request_id` on the access-log event `event="http.request"`.
- E2E smoke `tests/e2e/proxy_smoke.spec.ts` (or `deploy/proxy/smoke.sh`) on the T24 harness: Host routing, a 60 s SSE hold, an 8 MiB POST, and the maintenance page with the upstream stopped. Server logs go to `target/e2e-logs/proxy_smoke/server.jsonl`. On failure it keeps the Caddy log.

  - T18: Logs + metrics: redacted JSON tracing, Prometheus on :9090 behind PF_METRICS_TOKEN, /healthz, /readyz skeleton
  - T24: Generic OIDC client + the TLS e2e harness (the smoke test runs on the harness and this task adopts its Caddyfile)

  - T30: Rate limits (governor, per route and principal, trusted client IP) + pre-auth body caps
  - T91: Cloudflare adapter: tunnel ingress, DNS plugin, cache rules, one rate rule, fallback Worker, health probe

title: T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
description:
## Goal and why

**The link to post is the part's own host**, `https://<name>-part.<domain>/` (decision 25). It follows the live version, and the access decision happens when someone opens it, made for whoever opens it. T29 builds what lives at that root: a small **trusted, unsandboxed wrapper page** (partifactory's own code) that frames the sandboxed content at `/c/<cap>/…` on the same host. It also builds the **chrome API** on the workspace that the wrapper's UI talks to (with CORS for exactly the sandboxed part-host origins), the `/p/<name>` redirect, and the **admin-only public links** at `<name>-part.<domain>/l/<token>`.

Why one link: every other shape (per-version previews, minted links) goes stale after the first fix, and agents would have to know which one to post. Why a wrapper: the address bar should never show a cap, and the Stockroom chrome (title, audience chip, Share) should be present without letting part code touch it.

In Slice 1: the pixel test posts `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`, the admin's Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy goes through the chrome API, and the guest opens `/l/<token>`. T29 feeds T31 (wrapper chrome UI), T95 (contribute links), T117 (deep links), T38 and T93.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- **T29.a**: the wrapper page at `/` (and any non-reserved path): cap from `#pf=` then `sessionStorage`, `location.replace` to `/grant`, `replaceState`, deep-link paths, `#share=` kept across the hop, the frame, wrapper CSP, content-free og tags, `<noscript>`, `/_pf/` static files and the per-part web app manifest.
- **T29.b**: the chrome API `https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/…` (including `POST …/grant`), CORS for exactly active sandboxed part-host origins, the origin-to-part binding and the CSRF rules.
- **T29.c**: admin-only public links: `/l/<token>` (the wrapper in public mode), `POST /l/<token>/go`, open count and last opened, revoke (404 on next request), the "Revoke all public links" kill switch, no default expiry; and `/p/<name>` on the workspace (302 to the part host only).

Who gets what (verbatim table):

| Who opens it | What they get |
| --- | --- |
| Signed in, with access | the wrapper with their own role, the part framed inside it (one hop on first open) |
| Signed in, no access | `/grant` shows `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` with **Ask for access** (a note to the owner). The title isn't revealed |
| Not signed in | `/grant` shows a sign-in page carrying the **content-free card**, then returns to the part |
| An unfurler or any client without JS | the wrapper HTML, whose og tags are the **content-free card**, or the **public card** if the part has an active public link, plus a `<noscript>` "Sign in to open" link |

Invariants across all subtasks:
- **The part host never sets or reads a cookie.** The wrapper's state is a `sessionStorage` entry on the part host. The session cookie stays on the workspace host.
- **The response never depends on the User-Agent.** Bots and people get byte-identical HTML for the root and for `/l/`.
- Reserved prefixes on the part host: `/c/` (content, T16), `/l/` (public links), `/_pf/` (wrapper static). Every other path is the wrapper, and the path is passed on to the frame.
- The root `/` and `/l/` read the DB through a cache (live version, public-link state).

## Not in scope

- The content listener under `/c/` (caps, CSP, serving): T16. `/grant` itself (policy decision, 302, 403 page): T27.
- The wrapper's visible chrome UI (title, audience chip, share sheet): T31 (public rung) and T120 (versions rail, comments, inward rungs).
- Can-contribute mode, guest caps, freeze: T95. The titled public card: T119 (T29 uses T75's content-free cards).
- `unsandboxed` toggling UI: T31/T120. Its CORS exclusion is here.

## Design notes and decisions

- *The no-cap hop is client-side, by necessity:* the server never sees the fragment, so it can't tell a cap-carrying load from a bare one, and it serves the same wrapper HTML to both (round 2b correction).
- Cost, stated: the first open in a tab costs one extra redirect hop (wrapper -> `/grant` -> wrapper). Reloads reuse the stored cap. Expiry and deploys re-grant over the credentialed chrome-API grant fetch, with no navigation.
- The fragment never reaches a server or a `Referer`, and the wrapper removes it before any other code runs.
- Chrome CORS **never admits an unsandboxed part's origin**: that part's code is same-origin with its wrapper and would otherwise ride the viewer's session. Its wrapper falls back to opening Share and Comments on the workspace host.
- Public links are random DB tokens (128-bit), not HMAC-signed, so cap key rotation never affects them.
- Depends on T72's spike results (items 10 and 13: fragment survives the 302, `replaceState`, explicit `frame-ancestors`, credentialed same-site fetch carries the Lax cookie on Safari).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "A signed-out fetch of a part root returns the private card and no part bytes; the address bar ends clean after first open and a reload makes no /grant hop; the chrome API refuses `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin and any non-part origin; a public link opens from a fresh browser with no login and its open count increments; revoked -> 404 on the next request; bot and browser get byte-identical responses".

- [ ] All subtask criteria pass.
- [ ] E2E: open from the gallery or a chat link, then a silent hop, a clean address bar, the part framed. Reload in the same tab: no `/grant` request.
- [ ] A signed-out curl of the root returns the wrapper HTML with the private card og tags and no part bytes and no cap.
- [ ] The chrome API CORS fuzz passes. A public link opens in a fresh browser context, and its open count goes +1. Revoke, then 404.
- [ ] Root and `/l/` are byte-identical for bot and browser UAs.

## Tests

- E2E `tests/e2e/wrapper_first_open.spec.ts` (Chromium + WebKit, T24 harness): asserts the navigation sequence (wrapper -> `/grant` -> wrapper#pf=), `location.hash === ""` after load, no `/grant` on reload, a frame src under `/c/`. Logs: `event="grant.decide" outcome="allow" mode="wrap"` once, then zero on reload.
- `tests/e2e/public_link_open.spec.ts`: a fresh context with no session opens `/l/<token>`, the part renders, and `public_links.open_count` increments. Revoke, then the next `/l/` and `/c/` request returns 404. Asserts `event="link.open"`.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/root_ua_independence.rs`: fetches root and `/l/` with five UAs (curl, Telegram bot, Slack bot, iPhone Safari, Chrome) and asserts identical bytes.
- The CORS fuzz is in T29.b. The open-redirect fuzz is in T27.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The link to post: the part's own host" (wrapper, flow on first open, chrome actions, public links), §2 Serving (framed expiry, `pf:regrant`), §3a public links and ask for access, §4a.6 Part view, §4c cards, §5 spike items 10 and 13, §7 "Part hosts and the sandbox", "Links and cards"; decision 25; round 2b change log.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P1 (epic "P1 Edge + identity"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A signed-out fetch of a part root returns the private card and no part bytes; the address bar ends clean after first open and a reload makes no /grant hop; the chrome API refuses `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin and any non-part origin; a public link opens from a fresh browser with no login and its open count increments; revoked -> 404 on the next request; bot and browser get byte-identical responses
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T28: Admin pin + native WebAuthn step-up (10 min, rp.id = apex, from workspace and part-host wrappers) + admin bootstrap + break-glass
  - T75: Content-free preview cards (Slice 1): two static 1200x630 PNGs at /og/<sha256>.png
- Unblocks: 
  - T119: Card pipeline (SVG -> resvg PNG) and the titled public-link card
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T38: Security checklist suite (§7) from outside against staging + real-device pass + Telegram passkey test
  - T93: Portability lane: full e2e with no Cloudflare, Authentik or Gitea (Dex, IdP-less, Caddy, local exports)
  - T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
  - T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T29.a: Wrapper page at the part-host root: #pf= cap hand-off, frame, wrapper CSP, og tags, /_pf/
  - T29.b: Chrome API /api/chrome/v1/<part>/* with CORS for exactly sandboxed part-host origins
  - T29.c: Admin-only public links at <name>-part/l/<token> (open counts, revoke, kill switch) + /p/<name>

title: T29.a: Wrapper page at the part-host root: #pf= cap hand-off, frame, wrapper CSP, og tags, /_pf/
description:
## Goal and why

The trusted wrapper is what a person (or an unfurler) gets at `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`. It turns the one link to post into a sandboxed frame with the Stockroom chrome around it, with no cap ever visible in the address bar. It is the trust boundary between partifactory's chrome and someone else's page.

## Scope

- Served by the content listener (:8081) at `/` and at **any path outside the reserved prefixes** (`/c/`, `/l/`, `/_pf/`). The requested path is passed on to the frame, so deep links work.
- The HTML is generated per part (title for the chrome and og tags as decided by audience). It carries **no part content unless the part has an active public link**. The wrapper's script and styles are **shared blobs** on `blobs-part.<domain>`.
- Flow on first open (verbatim):
  1. The wrapper looks for a cap in the `#pf=` fragment, then in its own `sessionStorage`. With none, it does `location.replace("https://parts.<domain>/grant?part=<name>&path=<path>&mode=wrap")`. Before hopping, it stores any non-`pf` fragment (`share=…`) in its `sessionStorage` under the part name, and re-applies it after the cap is read, so an agent's deep link survives first open and sign-in.
  2. `/grant` (T27) 302s back to `https://<name>-part.<domain>/<path>#pf=<cap>`.
  3. The wrapper reads the fragment, calls `history.replaceState` so the address bar shows the clean link, keeps the cap in its own `sessionStorage` (so a reload needs no hop), and sets the iframe `src` to `/c/<cap><path>`.
  The fragment is removed **before any other script runs** (the fragment-reading script is the first, inline-hashed or the first blob script).
- Frame: `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-modals allow-downloads allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation">` (belt and braces with the CSP header), `src` = `/c/<cap><path>`. Messages from the frame are identified by `event.source === frame.contentWindow`, **never** by `event.origin` (which is `"null"`). The wrapper answers the prelude's `{type: "pf:regrant"}` with a credentialed `POST https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` (T29.b) and sets a freshly minted `src`, with no navigation.
- Wrapper CSP (no `sandbox`): scripts and styles only from the shared blob host, `connect-src` only the workspace, `frame-src 'self'`, `frame-ancestors` = `<workspace> <embedders>` (`[embed] frame_ancestors`, empty by default). Plus `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`. **No `Set-Cookie`, ever.**
- og tags via T75's helper: the content-free private card for every part without an active public link. With an active public link, the public card (T75's content-free public-link variant in Slice 1, T119's titled card later).
- `<noscript>`: a "Sign in to open" link to `/grant?part=<name>&path=/&mode=wrap`.
- `/_pf/` static prefix: `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` (per-part web app manifest: `id` and `scope` = `/` on the part host, name, icon, theme colour) and icons. Every part is its own origin, so each installs as its own home-screen app. (The install UX itself is T120.)
- The "being made…" placeholder for v0 lives in the framed content, served by T16/T51, not in the wrapper.
- `unsandboxed` parts: the wrapper falls back to opening Share and Comments on the workspace host, because chrome CORS refuses that origin.

## Not in scope

The chrome bar UI components (T31). The chrome API server side (T29.b). Public mode `/l/` (T29.c). `/grant` (T27).

## Design notes and decisions

- One extra hop on first open in a tab, accepted (decision 25).
- `sessionStorage` (per tab, part host origin) holds only this part's cap. Content framed inside can't read it, because the framed document has an opaque origin.
- Embedders (the Nest, T64) frame this root or `/c/` directly. `frame-ancestors` comes from config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After first open the address bar shows `https://<name>-part.<domain>/<path>` with no fragment. A reload makes no `/grant` request.
- [ ] A `#share=public` deep link survives the `/grant` hop and is re-applied (T31 opens the sheet).
- [ ] A test script inside the part tries `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage` and fails.
- [ ] The wrapper response has the strict wrapper CSP and no `Set-Cookie`. The root contains no cap and no part bytes when signed out.
- [ ] `/_pf/manifest.webmanifest` has `scope: "/"` and `id: "/"`.

## Tests

- E2E `tests/e2e/wrapper_fragment.spec.ts` (Chromium, WebKit): asserts `location.hash` is empty at `DOMContentLoaded` of any later script (an instrumentation hook), the sessionStorage key exists, and a reload has zero navigations to `parts.pf.test`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/wrapper_isolation.spec.ts`: a fixture part tries `parent.document` and `parent.sessionStorage` and reports via postMessage. Both throw.
- E2E `tests/e2e/wrapper_share_fragment.spec.ts`: opening `/#share=contribute` signed out goes through sign-in, back, and the sheet opens on the contribute rung.
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/wrapper_headers.rs`: exact CSP string, no Set-Cookie, `noindex`, and for a bare root no `/c/` substring in the body. Logs `event="wrapper.serve" audience="private"|"public"`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "The link to post" (flow on first open, wrapper CSP), §2 Serving (framed expiry), §4a.6 Part view (frame, install), §5 spike item 10, §7 "The wrapper".

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T29.b: Chrome API /api/chrome/v1/<part>/* with CORS for exactly sandboxed part-host origins
description:
## Goal and why

The wrapper's chrome actions (share, comments, versions, agent activity, regrant, step-up) need the viewer's workspace session. The part host and the workspace are **same-site**, so a credentialed fetch carries the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie. The workspace must answer CORS for **exactly** the part-host origins whose code is partifactory's own wrapper and nothing else. A loose rule here would hand the viewer's session to part code or to another site.

## Scope

- Routes on the workspace host: `https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/…`, called with `fetch(…, {credentials: "include"})`. Slice 1 needs at least:
  - `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant`: mounts **T27's** credentialed regrant handler (T27 owns the handler and its policy check; this subtask owns the route, CORS and CSRF around it). It mints a fresh cap for the same subject (the wrapper's answer to `pf:regrant`, and the expiry/deploy re-grant) through the session and the policy engine (T26) exactly like `/grant`.
  - `GET /api/chrome/v1/<part>/summary`: the wrapper's one bootstrap read: `{title, name, part_number, kind, head, live, build_status, audience: {sentence, chip}, role, features: [..]}`. `features` lists the chrome capabilities this build serves (Slice 1: `share`, `public_links`, `grant`, `stepup`; later tasks add `comments` (T50), `leases` (T47), `events` (T123), `versions` (T120), `edit` (T55), `backend` (T102)). The wrapper renders only controls whose feature is listed, so UI never ships half-wired to an absent backend (a fixture `features` list drives the T31.b/T120.c gate tests).
  - `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/stepup`: verifies a WebAuthn assertion and sets `sessions.stepup_at` (handler from T28).
  - Thin views used by the share sheet's public rung (T31/T95): public link create/revoke/mode/list. These are **session-only handlers** that the share sheet on `parts.<domain>` also uses (people-only actions have no op on purpose).
  - Thin views over registry ops as they land: `part_get` (title, rev, audience sentence), `part_share`, `part_comments`, `part_data`. **Nothing an agent may do exists only here.**
- CORS rules (verbatim):
  - `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoes the request's `Origin` only if it matches `https://<label>-part.<domain>`, `<label>` is an active part name (not `blobs`, not a redirecting old name), and that part is **not `unsandboxed`**. Otherwise **no CORS headers at all**.
  - `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, `Vary: Origin`, methods `GET, POST`, headers `Content-Type`, preflight `max-age` 600. Never `*`, never `null`.
  - **Origin binds to part**: a request from `https://photofinder-part.<domain>` may only touch `/api/chrome/v1/photofinder/…`.
- CSRF: chrome-API writes require `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` (or `same-origin`) and an allowed `Origin`. A `Content-Type: application/json` body forces a preflight, so a plain cross-site form can't reach them. Non-JSON writes are rejected.
- The workspace host **never** answers `Origin: null` with CORS headers (part content has an opaque origin, so its requests carry `Origin: null`, and it can't script the wrapper).
- Every call goes through the viewer's session and the policy engine. Failures use the standard error shape.

## Not in scope

The UI that calls these (T31, T120). Step-up verification internals (T28). Public link storage and `/l/` (T29.c). Comments, sharing and version ops themselves (T50, T52, T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why this is safe:* only the wrapper's own code can send a request whose `Origin` is a sandboxed part's host. The part's content runs in an opaque origin, so its requests carry `Origin: null`, which the workspace refuses.
- The unsandboxed exclusion was added beyond the round 2b brief: that part is same-origin with its wrapper.
- The active-name check uses the in-memory names cache (`names.state = 'active'`, `parts.isolation = 'sandbox'`, not deleted). A redirecting old name or `blobs` gets nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CORS headers are present only for the active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes.
- [ ] `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, an old redirecting name, `https://evil.example`, and `http://` variants all get no CORS headers.
- [ ] A write without `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin`, or without a JSON body, is refused.
- [ ] `POST …/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed viewer and the standard 403/401 shape otherwise.

## Tests

- Property/fuzz `crates/pf-serve/tests/chrome_cors_fuzz.rs`: generates origins (random labels, the right label on the wrong route, case variants, ports, trailing dots, `null`, punycode) times routes, and asserts the header presence matrix. It asserts the log event `event="chrome.cors" decision="deny" reason=...` for denials.
- Unit `pf_api::chrome::tests::origin_binds_to_part`.
- Integration `chrome_csrf.rs`: a form-encoded POST and a missing `Sec-Fetch-Site` are rejected with 403.
- E2E `tests/e2e/wrapper_regrant.spec.ts`: advance the test clock past the cap window. The prelude posts `pf:regrant`, the wrapper calls `/grant` on the chrome API, and the frame gets a new src without top navigation. Asserts `event="chrome.grant" outcome="ok"`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 "Chrome actions" (CORS rules, origin binding, CSRF, why safe), §2 Serving (framed expiry), §3a admin step-up endpoint, §7 "Chrome-API CORS"; round 2b and final round F05/F07.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CORS headers are present only for the active, sandboxed part's own origin on its own routes.
- [ ] `Origin: null`, a sibling part's origin, an unsandboxed part's origin, `blobs-part`, an old redirecting name, `https://evil.example`, and `http://` variants all get no CORS headers.
- [ ] A write without `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site|same-origin`, or without a JSON body, is refused.
- [ ] `POST …/grant` returns a fresh cap for an allowed viewer and the standard 403/401 shape otherwise.

title: T29.c: Admin-only public links at <name>-part/l/<token> (open counts, revoke, kill switch) + /p/<name>
description:
## Goal and why

Public links are the one way a part leaves the house, so they are **admin-only**, made once the part has a live version, unlisted, `noindex`, revocable, with **no expiry by default**, and with an open count so the admin can see who's using them. In Slice 1 the pixel board's guests come in through one. This subtask builds the `/l/<token>` page, the go-hop that mints the link cap, counting, revocation and the kill switch, plus the legacy `/p/<name>` redirect on the workspace.

## Scope

- Storage: the `public_links` table (T06), verbatim:
```sql
CREATE TABLE public_links (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- l_...; also the cap subject link:<id> and minter
  token_hash    BLOB NOT NULL UNIQUE,                -- sha256 of the 128-bit /l/<token>
  part_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (role IN (0,1)),  -- view; comment only with parts.link_comments
  mode          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'view' CHECK (mode IN ('view','contribute')),
  frozen_at     INTEGER,
  screenshot_og INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_by    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),  -- always the admin
  created_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at    INTEGER,                             -- NULL = never (the default)
  revoked_at    INTEGER,
  open_count    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,          -- counted on POST /l/<token>/go
  last_opened_at INTEGER,
  request_cap   INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
- Create (session-only handler, used by the share sheet via T29.b): only the admin's session (pinned subject, T28) with a fresh step-up (10 min). Only when the part has a live version. Token: 128 random bits, base64url, shown in the URL `https://<name>-part.<domain>/l/<token>`. Only `sha256(token)` is stored. Optional expiry (`Never` default, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days). Audit row `link.create`.
- `GET /l/<token>` on the part host: the wrapper in **public mode** (title, no share or comments unless opted in), carrying the public card (T75 content-free public-link variant in Slice 1), plus a JS hop. **No `<meta refresh>` and no target URL in the HTML**, so a crawler finds nothing to follow. Byte-identical for every UA. `noindex` and `X-Robots-Tag`.
- `POST /l/<token>/go` (same host): validates the token (not revoked, not expired) and returns a cap with subject `link:<id>`, minter `link:<id>` and role from the link. In contribute mode it adds the `dw` claim and guest id `g`, which is T95's extension point. **This call is what counts an open**: `open_count += 1` and `last_opened_at` are written through the writer. Event `link_open` to Insights (T105 later).
- Revoke: sets `revoked_at` and bumps `epochs['minter:link:<id>']` (and the part epoch), so open tabs die on their next request. Then `/l/<token>` and `/l/<token>/go` return a plain **404** (a revoked link never shows Ask for access). An expired link: `410 · LINK EXPIRED` ("This link expired on 12 Oct.").
- Kill switch: "Revoke all public links" (admin area, hold to confirm 1 s) revokes every active link and bumps each minter epoch. Audited.
- The root of a part with an active public link carries the public card instead of the private one (cache invalidated on create and revoke).
- `/p/<name>` on the workspace: **only** a 302 to `https://<name>-part.<domain>/`. It reveals nothing else. The same response is used for an unknown name, to avoid an existence oracle: the part host 404s or the wrapper hops.
- **No agent path**: no op, scope or token can create a public link (agents use `part_link_for`, T117).

## Not in scope

Can-contribute mode, guest limits, freeze: T95. The share-sheet UI for links: T31.c. The admin "Public links" list page beyond the kill switch: T120/admin pages. Titled card: T119.

## Design notes and decisions

- Public links are DB tokens, not HMAC caps, so cap key rotation never affects them.
- Counting on the `go` POST (not the GET) keeps unfurlers from inflating counts.
- Amber in the UI means "outside the house".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh browser with no session opens `/l/<token>` and sees the part. `open_count` increments by exactly 1 per go-hop.
- [ ] After revoke, the next `/l/` and the next `/c/` request with the link cap return 404 within seconds.
- [ ] The `/l/` HTML contains no cap, no hop-target URL and no `<meta refresh>`, and is identical across UAs.
- [ ] Only the admin session with a fresh step-up can create one. Without step-up: `step_up_required`. Non-admin: 403. Any agent token: refused on every surface.
- [ ] The kill switch revokes all and writes audit rows.

## Tests

- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/public_link_lifecycle.rs`: create, open (go), count, revoke, then 404, plus expiry and 410. Asserts events `event="link.go" outcome="ok"|"revoked"|"expired"` and audit rows.
- Unit `token_stored_hashed_only`: no raw token in the DB dump.
- E2E (part of T29's `public_link_open.spec.ts`): a fresh WebKit context.
- Security (T38): the agent surfaces cannot make a link (MCP, HTTP, CLI).

## References

PLAN.md §2 "Public links are separate and admin-only", §3a audience ladder (public link row), §4a.6 Admin "Public links", error pages (`410 · LINK EXPIRED`), §5e `public_links`, §7 Links and cards; decision 12.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T29.a: Wrapper page at the part-host root: #pf= cap hand-off, frame, wrapper CSP, og tags, /_pf/

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A fresh browser with no session opens `/l/<token>` and sees the part. `open_count` increments by exactly 1 per go-hop.
- [ ] After revoke, the next `/l/` and the next `/c/` request with the link cap return 404 within seconds.
- [ ] The `/l/` HTML contains no cap, no hop-target URL and no `<meta refresh>`, and is identical across UAs.
- [ ] Only the admin session with a fresh step-up can create one. Without step-up: `step_up_required`. Non-admin: 403. Any agent token: refused on every surface.
- [ ] The kill switch revokes all and writes audit rows.

title: Phase P2 Agents + the household loop
description:
# Phase P2 Agents + the household loop

## Goal and why

Phase P2 is the daily loop: OAuth AS (device grant first, then auth code + PKCE + CIMD/DCR + manual clients), personal
agent tokens, one connection per (agent, person) and service identities, MCP + discovery + the error contract +
cross-surface conformance, `part_edit` with rebase, block ids, leases, notes, `part_get` full content and
`render: "text"`, comments with provenance, the event log (long-poll, SSE, webhooks), live reload, inward agent sharing
(`share:household`) and `part_link_for` deep links for people-only actions, **`part_check` + the render sidecar (the P2
headline)**, Jig, the source editor with drafts, renames, shared data over `/_rt` with live `data.changed`,
"Can contribute" public links for guests, the Insights pages and debugging UI, and the Hermes skill with per-person
pairing.

*Why agents before invites:* the first moment of daily value is "an agent makes a thing from chat and I open it on my
phone". Invites serve people who aren't users yet and carry the most identity work.

*Done when (M2):* a household member pairs with Hermes, asks for a packing list shared with the family, Hermes checks
its own render and posts the part's link, another family member opens it on a phone, comments and watches the fix land;
Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow and edits a week-old part in one call; and the named e2e test
`communal_pixel_editor` passes in CI.

## Members

- T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
- T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
- T45: Personal agent tokens (pf_pat_) and the Connected agents page (list, revoke with cascade, New personal token)
- T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
- T47: Leases: part scope by default, optional file/block, TTL <= 10 min, person override, release on commit
- T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar
- T49: Agent read path (Slice 1): part_get full content <= 32 KiB, file/range, version, history, diff, build log, runtime_errors
- T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
- T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
- T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
- T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- T54: Jig design system: jig.css shared blob, @partifactory/jig, presets, design_system op, Jig as a part
- T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
- T56: Discovery: Markdown GET /, llms.txt, /skill.md = agent contract, server.json, 401 bodies, op-section test
- T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
- T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
- T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
- T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved
- T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
- T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
- T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
- T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
- T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
- T108: Insights UI (admin-only, Stockroom): Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds pages with table views and CSV/JSON export
- T109: Debugging UI: trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab (incl. denying decisions), per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail
- T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
- T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
- T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
- T124: OAuth authorization code after Slice 1: /oauth/authorize + PKCE S256, iss, CIMD, DCR, manual clients
- T125: part_link_for after Slice 1: group, everyone and admin actions
- G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)

Phase exit: M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".

title: T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
description:
## Goal and why

Agents get **their own identity**, not a shared admin key. Every agent connection (one per agent and person) is scoped, space-limited, revocable and labelled "<agent> for <person>", and the same token works on MCP, the HTTPS API and the `part` CLI. This bead is the **token side of a small OAuth 2.1 authorization server** that partifactory runs itself (it is also the resource server for `/mcp` and `/api`). It is the Slice 1 part: it issues and validates tokens, rotates refresh tokens, revokes, publishes metadata, answers 401s correctly, and renders the consent sheet that the device grant (T44) and personal tokens (T45) reuse. The authorization-code endpoint (`/oauth/authorize`, PKCE, CIMD, DCR, manual clients) is T124 after Slice 1; this bead is built so T124 "adds an endpoint, not a redesign".

Why it matters: shartifacts' static all-powerful tokens could make public links; partifactory's agents read untrusted web content and can be prompt-injected, so agent identity must be scoped and revocable (§1, §3b). The pixel-board test (T97) drives MCP with a device-code token, so the slice needs exactly this. Target MCP authorization spec revision **2026-07-28**, compatible with **2025-11-25**.

Feeds: T44, T45, T52, T53, T56, T124, T102; milestone S1 via T44/T57.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T43.a** token store and lifecycle: opaque prefixed tokens, hashing, access/refresh issue, rotation with reuse detection, revocation endpoint, connection cascade, token validation middleware for `/api` and `/mcp`, audience binding.
- **T43.b** discovery metadata and 401 contract: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 AS metadata, `WWW-Authenticate` + JSON 401 body on `/api` and `/mcp`.
- **T43.c** the consent sheet (shared UI component for device approval, PAT minting and, later, auth code) and the `agent_connections` principal model.

Concrete requirements (verbatim from the plan):
- Tokens: "opaque random strings with prefixes (`pf_at_`, `pf_rt_`, `pf_pat_`), stored hashed, revocable instantly. Access tokens last 1 h. A refresh token is single use: each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, and presenting a used one revokes the whole family."
- "The refresh family lives until the connection's consented lifetime ends (30 days, 90 days by default, or 1 year, picked on the approval sheet); after that a person connects the agent again."
- `/oauth/token` handles `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` (with T44) and `grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=pf_rt_…&client_id=part-cli`. `/oauth/*` takes `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and answers JSON (RFC 6749, RFC 8628).
- Success shape: `{"access_token":"pf_at_…","token_type":"Bearer","expires_in":3600,"refresh_token":"pf_rt_…","scope":"parts:read parts:write data:read data:write"}`.
- RFC 8707: `resource` = the workspace origin, `https://parts.<domain>/`, one resource for `/mcp`, `/api` and the CLI. Tokens are rejected on part hosts and on `/oauth/*`.
- Token claims model: "opaque, audience https://parts.<domain>/, sub=<person>, act=conn:<id>, scopes + spaces". All token kinds resolve to the same `(person, connection, scopes, spaces)` principal.
- Revocation: `revocation_endpoint` (RFC 7009 style, form-encoded). "Revoking a connection kills its refresh family, its access tokens and its PATs, and bumps its minter epoch, so every cap minted through it dies on the next request." Grants it made stay; the connection page lists them with "Undo all" (T45 renders it).
- AS metadata (RFC 8414 at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, also at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`; not an OIDC provider, no `id_token`) **advertising only what is implemented**: in Slice 1 `issuer`, `token_endpoint`, `device_authorization_endpoint`, `revocation_endpoint`, `scopes_supported`, `grant_types_supported` (device_code, refresh_token). `authorization_endpoint`, `code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]`, `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true`, `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`, `registration_endpoint` arrive with T124.
- Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` for the resource `https://parts.<domain>/`: `authorization_servers`, `scopes_supported`, `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`, `resource_documentation` → `/llms.txt`.
- 401: "Auth failures are HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`, on every surface, never an MCP tool result." Header: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://parts.<domain>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` (with `scope="parts:read parts:write"` where useful), plus a JSON body explaining the three ways to get a token (OAuth, device code, personal token) with links; error code `unauthenticated`, CLI exit 3.
- Scopes table (§3b):

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `parts:read` | find, get, history, diff, `part_check` (Slice 1: `part_get`, `part_check`, `part_link_for`) |
| `parts:write` | create, edit, restore, fork; `part_data` `snapshot_list`, `snapshot_restore`, `reset` (with the `edit` role) |
| `parts:delete` | soft delete to the bin, undelete |
| `data:read`, `data:write` | the part's `storage`/`db` documents and assets; with `data:read`, `part_check` renders against real shared data |
| `comments:write` | add and resolve comments (T50) |
| `share:household` | inward sharing (T52); consent toggle, off by default for CIMD/DCR/manual clients |
| `backends:deploy` | backend changes and write-only secrets (T102); consent toggle, off by default for every client |

- No admin scopes are obtainable. "A scope never gives you more than your person has."
- `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`, `oauth_clients` tables exist (T06); this bead owns their read/write paths:
```sql
CREATE TABLE oauth_tokens (hash BLOB PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('access','refresh','pat')),
  prefix TEXT NOT NULL, connection_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES agent_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  family_id TEXT, resource TEXT NOT NULL, issued_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at INTEGER, revoked_at INTEGER) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- The built-in public client `part-cli` row in `oauth_clients` (`kind='builtin'`) is seeded by migration or at start.
- After an import (T35) refresh-reuse detection is suspended for 24 h "to avoid mass family revocations".

## Not in scope

- `/oauth/device_authorization`, `/device` approval page and user codes: T44.
- Personal agent token minting UI and Connected agents page: T45.
- `/oauth/authorize`, PKCE, `iss`, CIMD, DCR, manual clients: T124.
- MCP server itself: T53. Discovery docs other than the two `.well-known` OAuth docs (`/llms.txt`, `/skill.md`, `server.json`): T56.
- Inward sharing by agents: T52. Backends scope enforcement: T102.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why opaque tokens, not JWTs:* "no key distribution or clock skew, and revocation is a single row. The cost is a DB read per API call, which is fine because `/api` and `/mcp` aren't the hot path." A small in-memory LRU of token-hash → principal with a few-second TTL is allowed, but revocation must take effect on the next call (PAT acceptance test in T45), so invalidate on revoke.
- *Why a facade AS:* Authentik's DCR needs an authenticated user and creates a provider+app per registration, and CIMD and RFC 8707 aren't documented; it can't serve MCP clients directly. Keep an `AuthorizationServer` trait so a future IdP with CIMD + resource indicators can replace it (partifactory then becomes a pure resource server).
- Token format: `pf_at_`/`pf_rt_` + base32 of 160 random bits (same shape as `pf_pat_<base32, 160-bit>`), so secret scanners and log redaction (T18 patterns `pf_*_`) match. Store `sha256(token)` only.
- Refresh rotation: `family_id` per connection grant; on refresh, mark `used_at`, issue new pair in the same family inside one writer transaction; presenting a refresh token with `used_at` set → revoke every token with that `family_id`, return `invalid_grant`. Race: two concurrent refreshes with the same token — the second loses and triggers reuse revocation (correct per spec; document it for the CLI, which must serialise refreshes).
- Audience: a token's `resource` is always the workspace origin; the content listener (:8081) never accepts bearer tokens at all, and `/oauth/*` endpoints ignore/reject `Authorization: Bearer` access tokens (they authenticate clients, not tokens).
- Consent sheet is the same sheet for device approval (T44), PAT minting (T45) and auth code (T124): scopes as removable toggles in plain words ("Read and edit parts", "Read and write part data", "Comment", "Share with people already in the household", "Deploy backends and set their secrets" — the last two off unless requested), spaces as toggles limited to spaces the person may consent, lifetime `30 days · 90 days · 1 year` (default 90), Allow (filled, triggers passkey) / Deny. "Who may consent: any person may connect an agent into their own personal space and the shared spaces they belong to. Only the admin (with step-up) may consent an agent into anyone else's space."
- Every write records `author = <person>, actor = <connection>`; the principal type carries both.
- The metadata must "advertise only what is implemented": a CI test compares advertised endpoints with mounted routes, so T124 flips fields on as it lands.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Refresh reuse revokes the family; a token is rejected on part hosts and on `/oauth/*`; the metadata documents validate; every 401 from `/api` and `/mcp` carries `WWW-Authenticate` and the JSON body".
- [ ] Access tokens expire after 3600 s; refresh returns a new pair and marks the old refresh used.
- [ ] Presenting a used refresh token revokes all tokens of its family and returns `invalid_grant`; suspended for 24 h after an import.
- [ ] Refresh fails after the connection's `expires_at`.
- [ ] Revoking a connection revokes all its tokens (access, refresh, PAT) and bumps `minter:conn:<id>`; a cap minted through it fails on the next request.
- [ ] A bearer token sent to a part host or to `/oauth/token` as auth is rejected.
- [ ] `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/openid-configuration` validate against RFC 9728 / RFC 8414 schemas and list only mounted endpoints.
- [ ] Every 401 from `/api` and `/mcp` (missing, malformed, expired, revoked token) has `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` and the JSON body; MCP never returns auth failures as tool results.
- [ ] Tokens are stored only as sha256; no token value appears in logs (canary).
- [ ] The consent sheet renders the scope/space/lifetime pickers and is reused by T44 and T45.

## Tests

- `pf_oauth::tokens::tests::issue_validate_roundtrip`, `refresh_rotates_pair`, `refresh_reuse_revokes_family`, `refresh_after_connection_expiry_fails`, `reuse_detection_suspended_after_import` (test clock).
- `pf_oauth::tokens::tests::token_prefixes_and_entropy` (format `pf_at_[a-z2-7]{32}`), `stores_only_hash` (schema/DB inspection).
- Property test `pf_oauth::prop::scope_never_exceeds_person_role`: random scopes × roles → effective rights ≤ the person's role.
- Integration `crates/pf-oauth/tests/revocation_cascade.rs`: mint cap through a connection, revoke, assert `cap.verify outcome="stale_epoch"` log event and 302/401 on the content listener.
- Integration `crates/pf-api/tests/unauthenticated_401.rs`: table of bad tokens × `/api/v1/part_get` and `/mcp` → 401, header and JSON body asserted; log event `event="auth.reject" outcome="unauthenticated"` with `request_id`, no token text (canary).
- Integration `crates/pf-serve/tests/no_bearer_on_part_host.rs`.
- Conformance `crates/pf-oauth/tests/metadata_validate.rs`: fetch both metadata docs, validate JSON schema, assert advertised endpoints == mounted routes.
- E2E `tests/e2e/consent_sheet.spec.ts`: render sheet at 360 px and desktop, toggles, Deny; keeps Playwright trace + `target/e2e-logs/consent_sheet/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §3b (How agents authenticate; Scopes; Revocation cascades), §4b (Auth for each kind of client; Errors), §5e `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`, `oauth_clients`, §5c import (reuse suspension), §7 Agents, Slice 1 "Decided for the slice"; docs/agent-contract.md "Connecting", "Token lifetimes"; decisions 8, 14, 37.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
