title: T43.a: Token store: opaque hashed tokens, refresh rotation with reuse detection, revocation cascade, bearer middleware
description:
## Goal and why

The core of agent identity: issuing, validating, rotating and revoking opaque tokens, and resolving any of them to the one `(person, connection, scopes, spaces)` principal the policy engine (T26) and every op use. Revocation must be one row and instant, which is why tokens are opaque rather than JWTs.

## Scope

- Token generation: `pf_at_`, `pf_rt_` (and the `pf_pat_` shape used by T45) + base32 of 160 random bits (`ring::rand`). Persist `sha256(token)` in `oauth_tokens.hash` with `kind`, `prefix`, `connection_id`, `family_id`, `resource` (= `https://parts.<domain>/`), `issued_at`, `expires_at`, `used_at`, `revoked_at`.
- Access token TTL 3600 s. Refresh token: single use; the family expires at `agent_connections.expires_at` (30 d / 90 d default / 1 y).
- `POST /oauth/token` (form-encoded, JSON out): `grant_type=refresh_token` with `refresh_token` and `client_id=part-cli`; the device-code grant branch is wired here and filled by T44. Errors per RFC 6749: `invalid_grant`, `invalid_client`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_request`.
- Reuse: a refresh token with `used_at IS NOT NULL` → set `revoked_at` on every row with that `family_id`, respond `invalid_grant`. Skipped (no family revocation, just `invalid_grant`) during the 24 h after an import (`kv` key set by T35).
- `POST /oauth/revoke` (`revocation_endpoint`): revoke a token (and its family for refresh tokens).
- Connection revoke API used by T45: revoke all tokens of the connection + set `agent_connections.revoked_at` + bump `epochs['minter:conn:<id>']` (T15 epoch API).
- Bearer middleware for `/api/*` and `/mcp`: parse `Authorization: Bearer`, hash, look up (optional short LRU invalidated on revoke), check `resource`, expiry, revocation, connection active and not expired; build `Principal { user_id, connection_id, kind, scopes, spaces, agent_name }`; update `last_used_at` (coalesced). Failures produce `unauthenticated` (T43.b renders the 401).
- The content listener and `/oauth/*` never accept bearer tokens.

## Not in scope

Metadata documents and the 401 body (T43.b); consent UI (T43.c); device codes (T44); PAT minting (T45).

## Design notes and decisions

- All writes go through the single writer task (T05) so rotation is atomic (mark used + insert two rows).
- Concurrent refresh with the same token: the loser sees `used_at` and triggers family revocation. That is spec-correct; the `part` CLI must serialise refreshes (note for T22/T44).
- `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `agent_connections` exists but connections are revoked, not deleted, so history stays.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rotation, reuse revocation, expiry and revocation behave as in Scope.
- [ ] A revoked token fails on the very next call (no stale cache).
- [ ] A token never appears in logs; only its prefix may (`pf_at_…`).

## Tests

- `pf_oauth::store::tests::{issue_access, rotate_refresh, reuse_revokes_family, reuse_suspended_after_import, family_ends_at_connection_expiry, revoke_single_token, revoke_connection_cascades}`.
- `crates/pf-oauth/tests/bearer_middleware.rs`: missing/malformed/expired/revoked/wrong-resource tokens → `unauthenticated`; logs assert `event="auth.reject" reason=…` with `request_id` and no token (canary `pf_at_CANARY…`).
- `crates/pf-oauth/tests/concurrent_refresh.rs`: two parallel refreshes → exactly one success, family revoked.

## References

PLAN.md §3b Tokens, Revocation cascades; §5e `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`; §5c import step (reuse suspension); docs/agent-contract.md "Token lifetimes, plainly".

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T43.b: OAuth metadata (RFC 9728, RFC 8414) and the 401 + WWW-Authenticate + JSON body contract
description:
## Goal and why

An agent told only `https://parts.<domain>` must learn how to authenticate from the error alone. The 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` is also what triggers an MCP client's OAuth flow, so it must be HTTP-level on every surface, never an MCP tool result.

## Scope

- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728): `{"resource":"https://parts.<domain>/","authorization_servers":["https://parts.<domain>"],"scopes_supported":[...],"bearer_methods_supported":["header"],"resource_documentation":"https://parts.<domain>/llms.txt"}`.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and the same JSON at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`: `issuer`, `token_endpoint`, `device_authorization_endpoint`, `revocation_endpoint`, `scopes_supported`, `grant_types_supported`, `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ["none"]` (public `part-cli`). Only implemented endpoints are listed; T124 adds `authorization_endpoint`, `code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]`, `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true`, `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`, `registration_endpoint`. No `id_token`, no `jwks_uri` (not an OIDC provider).
- Generated from one Rust struct so the "advertise only what exists" check is a unit test against the router.
- 401 on `/api/*` and `/mcp`: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://parts.<domain>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="parts:read parts:write"`, body `{"error":{"code":"unauthenticated","message":…,"hint":"Get a token: device code (POST /oauth/device_authorization), a personal token from Connected agents, or OAuth …","retryable":true,"details":{…links},"docs":"https://parts.<domain>/llms-full.txt#unauthenticated"}}`. CLI exit 3.
- Discovery documents are unauthenticated and contain no site secrets or user data (never list spaces, parts or people).

## Not in scope

`/llms.txt`, `/skill.md`, `/.well-known/mcp/server.json`, Markdown `GET /`: T56. MCP transport: T53.

## Design notes and decisions

- One error catalogue (T20) owns `unauthenticated`; this subtask adds the header and the "how to get a token" details.
- Body text names the three ways (OAuth after T124, device code, personal token) and points at `/skill.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both metadata docs validate against RFC 9728/8414 JSON schemas.
- [ ] Advertised endpoints equal mounted routes (test).
- [ ] Every 401 from `/api` and `/mcp` carries the header and the JSON body.

## Tests

- `pf_oauth::metadata::tests::{prm_shape, as_metadata_only_implemented, openid_configuration_alias}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/www_authenticate.rs`: for every registry op route and `/mcp` POST without a token → 401 + header + body; log event `event="auth.reject" outcome="unauthenticated"`.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/auth_is_http_401.rs`: MCP `tools/call` with a bad token gets HTTP 401, not a JSON-RPC result.

## References

PLAN.md §3b AS metadata; §4b Discovery table and 401 paragraph; docs/agent-contract.md "Discovery".

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T43.a: Token store: opaque hashed tokens, refresh rotation with reuse detection, revocation cascade, bearer middleware

title: T43.c: Consent sheet and agent_connections principal model ("<agent> for <person>")
description:
## Goal and why

Connecting is how an agent gets its own identity. One `agent_connections` row per (agent, person) (or per service), labelled "<agent> for <person>", carries scopes, spaces and lifetime, and is the minter for caps and the `actor` on every write. The consent sheet is where the person decides those, and it is shared by the device grant (T44), personal tokens (T45) and, later, the auth-code flow (T124).

## Scope

- `agent_connections` row creation API: `kind` (`oauth_code` | `device` | `pat`), `principal_kind` (`person` in Slice 1; `service` arrives with T64), `client_id` (NULL for pat), `user_id`, `agent_name` (≤ 40 chars), `software` (self-reported, unverified), `scopes` JSON, `spaces` JSON, `expires_at` (consented lifetime), `quota_versions_day` (NULL = default 500/day).
- Consent rules: a person may consent into their own personal space and shared spaces they belong to; consent into someone else's space needs the admin with step-up (T28) → `step_up_required`.
- The consent sheet (workspace UI, Stockroom): "This device says it is *Hermes* (hermes/1.4)" labelled unverified; scopes as removable toggles in plain words ("Read and edit parts", "Read and write part data", "Comment", "Share with people already in the household", "Deploy backends and set their secrets" — last two off unless requested); spaces as toggles; lifetime `30 days · 90 days · 1 year` (default 90 for device/OAuth; PATs use 30 d default, max 1 y); **Allow** (filled, full width; triggers a passkey assertion when the person has one) and **Deny**. Phone: single column, large type. Success: "Hermes is connected for you."
- Delegation recorded on writes: `author = <person>`, `actor = conn:<id>`, UI label "Hermes for <person>".

## Not in scope

Device-code specifics (code display, phishing banners): T44. PAT "shown once" flow: T45. Redirect host display: T124.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why one connection per (agent, person):* with one shared token every family request was "Hermes for the admin", landed in the admin's space and let Hermes read private parts while serving someone else — the confused-deputy problem.
- The sheet is a component with slots (header "who", body scopes/spaces/lifetime, footer extras) so T44/T45/T124 add only their parts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Creating a connection outside consentable spaces is refused (`forbidden {space}`), or needs admin step-up.
- [ ] Writes made through a connection record `actor_conn` and render as "<agent> for <person>".
- [ ] Sheet passes the contrast test and the 360 px layout check.

## Tests

- `pf_oauth::connections::tests::{consent_own_spaces_only, admin_consent_needs_stepup, label_format}`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/consent_sheet.spec.ts` (Chromium + WebKit, 360×740): toggles, lifetime default 90 d, Deny leaves no row; server log `event="connection.create"` with `principal` and no token.

## References

PLAN.md §3b One connection per (agent, person); §4a.6 Connecting an agent; §5e `agent_connections`; §4a.7 budgets.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T43.a: Token store: opaque hashed tokens, refresh rotation with reuse detection, revocation cascade, bearer middleware

title: T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
description:
## Goal and why

"Comments addressed to the agent" is one of shartifacts' best ideas: comment from your phone and have the agent fix it. partifactory adds provenance so prompt-injection from guests or other people is visible as data, never instructions. After Slice 1; feeds T73, T84, T85, T120 (comments rail), M2/M4.

## Scope

- `part_comments` op: `list` / `add` / `resolve` (and reopen); `to_agent` threads; anchors; `provenance` per comment. Scope `comments:write` for add/resolve, `parts:read` for list; roles per the matrix: `comment` and up may comment; public-link viewers only if the part opted in (`parts.link_comments`); guests never.
- `comments` table (T06): `id, part_id, thread_id (= id of root), parent_id, version_id, anchor JSON ({block?|file,lines?, quote}), body (≤ 16384), provenance ('person','agent','link_viewer'), author_user, author_conn, author_link, to_agent, agent_state ('open','claimed','answered'; P3), resolved_at, resolved_by, created_at, deleted_at`.
- Anchor = `{version, block | file + line range, quote}` (text quote for re-anchoring).
- Prompt-injection hygiene: every comment carries `provenance: person | agent | link_viewer`; results carry `contains_untrusted: true` when any comment is from someone other than the connection's person; MCP text rendering wraps such content in `<untrusted_content>`.
- Events `comment.added`, `comment.resolved` on the event log (T51). Resolve is audited (`audit` row `comment.resolve`).
- `/_rt` `comments.*` ops for page code (`claude.use("comments")` in T73) respect the role matrix; guests get 403.
- Add `part_comments` section to `docs/agent-contract.md` and join the T57 scenario's "comment to_agent" step. Register its MCP tool (T53 picks it up from the registry).
- FTS indexes comments (T76 update hook).

## Not in scope

Agent inbox/steward states (T84), phone long-press (T85), webhooks (T123). (The comments rail is this task's T50.b, moved here from T120.c in the polish round.)

## Design notes and decisions

- Public-link comments need an explicit opt-in "(spam and prompt-injection risk)"; labelled "untrusted for agents" for the owner.
- Comment bodies are content: never logged (T112 canary).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A public-link viewer's comment arrives with `provenance: link_viewer` and wrapped in MCP text; resolve is audited".
- [ ] Role and opt-in enforcement; guests 403.
- [ ] `contains_untrusted` set correctly.
- [ ] Contract section + registry test pass.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/untrusted_wrapper.rs`: link-viewer comment → MCP text contains `<untrusted_content>`; structuredContent `provenance: "link_viewer"`, `contains_untrusted: true`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/comment_resolve_audit.rs`: one `audit` row per resolve; log `event="comment.resolve"` without body.

## References

PLAN.md §3c Prompt-injection hygiene, Agent inbox; §3a role × runtime matrix; §4 ops table; §5e `comments`; docs/agent-contract.md Rule 6.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.

- Depends on (must be closed first):

title: T50.b: Comments rail in the wrapper (For the agent toggle, untrusted marker, resolve), Details 'Send to agent', budget 3 + type
description:
## Goal and why

The household loop is "comment on the phone, watch the agent fix it". This subtask gives the wrapper its comments rail, with the **"For the agent"** toggle, and the Details sheet's "Send to agent" button, landing together with the backend (T50.a) so the flow is testable end to end the day it ships. (Moved here from T120.c in the polish round: a UI built against an absent backend would have shipped untestable.)

## Scope

- **Comments rail**: a right rail (360 px on desktop, pushes the frame narrower rather than covering it; a bottom sheet on phones with the composer above the keyboard). Threads ordered by position then time, each with its anchor quote. **"For the agent"** toggle (the `to_agent` flag), shown as a blue chip (agent blue, never the signal colour), then "Hermes is on it" (P3 steward state, T84) and "Fixed in REV 14 · View diff" (from a later version referencing the thread). Comments from public-link viewers or other people carry a small "untrusted for agents" marker for the owner (from `provenance`). Resolve, reopen, "show resolved". The bar shows `Comments 3` (open count). Data via the chrome API thin view over `part_comments` (T50.a); the control appears only when `/summary.features` lists `comments` (T29.b).
- **Details → runtime errors → "Send to agent"**: files a `to_agent` comment carrying the error's message and stack (anchored to the version), so an agent learns about a viewer's error from its inbox/feed.
- Anchors from the frame (a selection or line) arrive over the wrapper ↔ part postMessage channel (identified by `event.source`, never `event.origin`); the trusted UI stays outside the part. Line anchors for `text` parts use the `L<n>` ids (T12).
- Click budget (§4a.7): "Comment for the agent | Comments → type → 'For the agent' → Post | **3 + type**", asserted by the budget counter.
- Stockroom styling; copy voice (plain, sentence case); hit targets ≥ 44 px on phones.

## Not in scope

Comment storage, op, provenance and events (T50.a); steward states and inbox (T84); long-press point-and-comment on phones (T85); the workspace editor's comment gutter (T55).

## Design notes and decisions

- Agents get blueprint blue so "for the agent" is never confused with an action the person can take.
- "Untrusted for agents" is shown to the owner, not to the commenter: it is a reading aid, not a judgement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Comment for the agent: 3 interactions + typing; the thread shows the blue chip and the stored comment has `to_agent: true`, `provenance: "person"`.
- [ ] A link viewer's comment shows the untrusted marker to the owner; resolve/reopen work and the count updates.

title: T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
description:
## Goal and why

One append-only event log is the agents' feed and the source of everything live. In Slice 1 it powers what the pixel test needs: open tabs on a part hear `data.changed` within 1 s of a write (the admin's tab shows the guest's paint), and the "being made…" placeholder cross-fades to REV 1 when the first version lands. Agents' delivery (`part_watch`, SSE on `/api`, webhooks) is T123. On S1's path; feeds T96, T79, T123.

## Scope

- `events` table: `seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (cursor), `at`, `part_id`, `space_id`, `type` (part.created, version.committed, build.finished, part.live_changed, comment.added, data.changed, backend.started, …), `actor` (`user:<id>` | `conn:<id>` | `guest:<link>:<g>` | `system`), `payload` JSON; indexes `events_part (part_id, seq)`, `events_space (space_id, seq)`. Surfaces render `actor` as `{kind, id, on_behalf_of}`.
- Append inside the same writer transaction as the change it describes; after commit, publish to an in-memory `tokio::sync::broadcast` per part (and global).
- Retention **30 days**: janitor job (T113) prunes; a `cursor_expired {oldest}` error exists for T123.
- `GET /c/<cap>/_rt/events` on the part host: `EventSource`, cap-authenticated exactly like `/_rt/v1` (`Origin: null` accepted, other non-null Origin rejected), `text/event-stream`, 25 s heartbeat comment, events filtered to this part:
  - `pf:version` `{n, live}` when `part.live_changed` (live reload, T79; and the v0 placeholder),
  - `data.changed` `{key, op: "set" | "delete", by: {kind: "person" | "agent" | "guest", name}}` once per changed key when someone else writes shared data (T96 emits them).
  - Guests and link viewers receive these too (read access).
- The **v0 "being made…" placeholder**: a part with `head: 0` serves a drafting-sheet placeholder (faint 8 px grid, title block `P-0215 · grocery-planner · REV 0 · Hermes for <person>`, "Hermes is making this. It'll appear here as soon as the first version lands.") that subscribes to `/_rt/events` and cross-fades (`--pf-d-3`) to REV 1 with no reload. If the first version doesn't build: "The first version didn't build. Hermes has the error."
- Ingress contract: SSE must survive proxy idle timeouts (heartbeat < Cloudflare's 100 s; Caddy smoke test in T89 holds SSE 60 s).

## Not in scope

`part_watch`, `GET /api/v1/events`, `Last-Event-ID` resume on the API, webhooks (T123). The data ops that emit `data.changed` (T96). Live reload behaviour in the wrapper (T79).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why one log:* nothing depends on MCP notifications, which stateless Streamable HTTP doesn't have anyway.
- Broadcast lag: a slow SSE consumer that lags the broadcast buffer is resynced (send a `pf:resync` hint, page re-reads) rather than blocking the writer.
- Events carry ids and keys, not content values (data values are read with `get`).
- The in-memory caches (live map, manifest LRU, epochs) are invalidated from the same stream (§5e hot-path rules).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Two tabs on one part get `data.changed` within 1 s of a write; the placeholder cross-fades to REV 1 with no reload; a 31-day-old event is pruned".
- [ ] Event append is atomic with its change; seq gap-free per commit order.
- [ ] `/_rt/events` rejects missing/foreign caps and non-null foreign Origin.
- [ ] Heartbeat every 25 s.

## Tests

- `pf_model::events::tests::{append_in_txn, broadcast_after_commit, prune_31_days}` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_events_sse.rs`: two SSE clients on one part, a shared write → both receive `data.changed` < 1 s; foreign cap → 404/401; log `event="rt.events.subscribe"` with `part_id`, no cap.
- E2E `tests/e2e/placeholder_crossfade.spec.ts`: `part_create` with no files, open `/c/<cap>/` **standalone with a test-minted cap** (no wrapper needed, so it runs before T29/T31 exist), then commit v1 → the placeholder document cross-fades to REV 1 without navigation (assert no `load` navigation event); keeps trace + server.jsonl. The same cross-fade inside the wrapper is asserted by T31.b's `wrapper_chrome.spec.ts`.

## References

PLAN.md §4 Events: one log, three deliveries; §2 Runtime calls `/_rt` (EventSource); §3c Live reload; §4a.6 "Being made…" states; §5e `events`; §5h Events log retention.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Two tabs on one part get `data.changed` within 1 s of a write; the placeholder cross-fades to REV 1 with no reload; a 31-day-old event is pruned
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T06: Schema v1 migration (the full data model), incl. the FTS5 table, with schema_test
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
- Unblocks: 
  - T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
  - T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
  - T84: Agent inbox and steward: part_inbox op, to_agent routing, open/claimed/answered/resolved, stalled
  - G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)
acceptance_criteria: Two tabs on one part get `data.changed` within 1 s of a write; the placeholder cross-fades to REV 1 with no reload; a 31-day-old event is pruned

title: T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
description:
## Goal and why

Agents need to hear about changes (a new comment, a finished build, a guest write) without polling hard and without MCP notifications. The one event log (T51) gets three deliveries: long-poll on every surface, SSE over HTTP, and signed webhooks to admin-configured URLs (Hermes is "just one webhook consumer"). After Slice 1; feeds T55, T58, T84, M2.

## Scope

- **`part_watch`** op (every surface, MCP included): `{since, wait: 25, part?, kinds?}`, `wait` default 25 s, max 50 s; returns early on the first matching event. Scope `parts:read`; only events for parts the connection can see.
- **`GET /api/v1/events?since=…&wait=25`**: same long-poll; with `Accept: text/event-stream` it streams SSE: `id:` is the event seq, `Last-Event-ID` resumes, 25 s heartbeat (under any proxy's idle timeout, Cloudflare's is 100 s).
- Event JSON: `{seq, at, part_id, space_id, type, actor: {kind, id, on_behalf_of}, payload}`.
- A cursor older than retention (30 days) → `cursor_expired {oldest}` (HTTP 410, CLI exit 4).
- **Webhooks**: to admin-configured URLs only (`[webhooks]` in site config; targets never set by agents, which rules out SSRF), same event JSON, signed with HMAC (`X-PF-Signature`, documented so any consumer can verify it), retried with backoff, event id as the idempotency key. `webhook_deliveries` table: `id, target (site-config target name), event_seq, attempts, next_at, status ('pending','ok','dead'), last_error, UNIQUE (target, event_seq)`; index `webhook_due`.
- Signature: `X-PF-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256(secret, t + "." + body)>` (recommended format; document it in `docs/` and the contract).
- Backoff: exponential with jitter (e.g. 10 s → doubling, capped at 30 min) for up to 24 h, then `dead`; the Health page shows dead deliveries.
- Add `part_watch` to `docs/agent-contract.md` (registry-match test, T56). `part watch` CLI alias (T22 registry-generated).

## Not in scope

The events table and `/_rt/events` (T51). Ops-alert webhook (T121, separate). Agent inbox semantics (T84).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why long-poll on MCP:* "An MCP client that wants a push feel calls `part_watch` in a loop."
- Webhook secrets per target from env (`_FILE` supported, T04).
- Delivery worker is a janitor-independent background task; rows pruned with events after 30 days.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Kill the webhook target for 5 min: deliveries retry and succeed after recovery; an SSE client resumes with no gap; a 31-day-old cursor gets `cursor_expired`".
- [ ] `part_watch` returns early on a matching event; respects `kinds` and `part` filters; max wait 50 s.
- [ ] Signature verifiable with the documented recipe.

## Tests

- `pf_model::watch::tests::{returns_early, timeout_empty, kinds_filter, space_filter, cursor_expired_31d}` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-api/tests/events_sse_resume.rs`: disconnect mid-stream, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, assert contiguous seqs.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/webhook_retry.rs`: target down 5 min (fake server), then up → delivered once, `attempts` > 1, signature verifies; log `event="webhook.deliver" outcome=…` with `target`, no body content.

## References

PLAN.md §4 Events: one log, three deliveries; §4b errors (`cursor_expired`); §5e `events`, `webhook_deliveries`; §5f Events for agents.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Kill the webhook target for 5 min: deliveries retry and succeed after recovery; an SSE client resumes with no gap; a 31-day-old cursor gets `cursor_expired`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
  - T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
acceptance_criteria: Kill the webhook target for 5 min: deliveries retry and succeed after recovery; an SSE client resumes with no gap; a 31-day-old cursor gets `cursor_expired`

title: T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
description:
## Goal and why

"Hermes, make a packing list and share it with the family" must be one turn. Inward sharing (to people and groups that already have accounts, or moving a part into Family) can't leak beyond the household, so agents may do it directly with the `share:household` scope. Outward sharing (public links, invites, groups, everyone-signed-in) is the exfiltration channel for a prompt-injected agent, so agents never get it: they hand the person a `part_link_for` deep link (T117). After Slice 1; feeds T58, T102, M2.

## Scope

- **`part_share`** op: `list` who can see it (the live sentence + grants); `grant` / `revoke` inward (people and groups with accounts, roles `view`/`comment`/`edit`); `move` to a space the connection may write (needs write access to both spaces). Always returns the link to post (the part's host).
- Scope `share:household` (consent-time toggle, off by default for CIMD/DCR/manual clients); without it → `forbidden {scope_needed: "share:household"}`. Within the connection's spaces only; the person must be the owner or have `manage` (owners and `manage` grantees share inward).
- Agent grants recorded with `grants.created_by_conn` → labelled ("Hermes shared this with the Family group"), undoable in one tap, listed in the share sheet and the activity feed; no message is sent. Audit row per change.
- Subjects allowed for agents: `user:<id>`, `group:<name>` (existing groups only). Never `everyone-signed-in`, never `link:`, never creating groups or invites, on any surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI, chrome API).
- Moves: "Move to Family" for agents = `move` to `family` (exists once `provision` created it, T32).
- Policy epoch bump on revoke (T26). Add `part_share` section to `docs/agent-contract.md`; join the T57 scenario's "share inward with a group" step.

## Not in scope

Share sheet UI rungs (T120), public links (T29, admin only), deep links (T117/T125), invites (T94).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 13 and 34: inward yes, outward no; no approval queue — "a deep link costs the person the same one tap ... and partifactory stores nothing pending".
- There is no request table for an agent to write to (schema test shared with T117).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "An agent without `share:household` gets `forbidden {scope_needed}`; with it, a grant to an existing group shows 'Hermes shared this' and one-tap undo; an agent can never create a public link, invite or group on any surface".
- [ ] Space restriction enforced; move needs both spaces.
- [ ] Every agent grant has `created_by_conn` and an audit row.

## Tests

- `pf_policy::agent_share::tests::{no_scope_forbidden, grant_existing_group, grant_unknown_group_not_found, everyone_signed_in_forbidden, move_needs_both_spaces, outside_spaces_not_found}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/no_outward_any_surface.rs`: iterate the registry and every route (MCP, HTTP, CLI, chrome API with an agent token) trying to create link/invite/group → refused; log `event="policy.deny" reason=…`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/agent_share_undo.spec.ts`: agent grants to Family group, owner sees label and taps Undo.

## References

PLAN.md §3b Agent sharing: inward yes, outward no; Scopes; §3a audience ladder; §4 ops table (`part_share`); §5e `grants.created_by_conn`; §7 Agents; decisions 13, 34.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): An agent without `share:household` gets `forbidden {scope_needed}`; with it, a grant to an existing group shows 'Hermes shared this' and one-tap undo; an agent can never create a public link, invite or group on any surface
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
  - T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
  - G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T120 (the share sheet's agent-made-grants list with Undo, T120.d, is what the acceptance and `agent_share_undo.spec.ts` exercise).
- Ownership of agent-made grants: this task = the data (`grants.created_by_conn`, audit, the undo/revoke endpoint, the `part_share` op); T120.d = the share-sheet list and Undo button; G05 = the feed entry.
- Log event name: `event="policy.decide" outcome="deny"` (T26's), not `policy.deny`.
- `move` semantics for agents: an agent may move a part only into a space whose grants are a superset of (or equal to) the current space's (personal → `family`); a move that would narrow the audience is `forbidden {space}` for agents and stays a people-only action in the UI. Every move is audited and appears in the activity feed (G05).
acceptance_criteria: An agent without `share:household` gets `forbidden {scope_needed}`; with it, a grant to an existing group shows 'Hermes shared this' and one-tap undo; an agent can never create a public link, invite or group on any surface

title: T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
description:
## Goal and why

MCP is how Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Hermes use partifactory, and it is "one of four front ends, not the system": every tool is generated from the operation registry (T20), so nothing exists on one surface only. The pixel-board test drives MCP with a device-code token. On the Slice 1 critical path (… T43 → T53 → T56 → T57); later ops (comments T50, event feed T123, sharing T52, design_system T54) and `part_check` itself (T80.d) add their tools when they land rather than holding MCP back: T53 is built and tested against the registry's typed `part_check` stub with a fake renderer, and T80.d (which depends on T53) wires the real op into the image-block path.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T53.a** transport and tools: `rmcp` 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, tool list/schemas/annotations generated from the registry, `structuredContent` outputs, error results, image block for `part_check`.
- **T53.b** auth, instructions and resources: bearer auth with HTTP 401 (never a tool result), `instructions` = `docs/agent-contract.md`, `part://…` resources as projections, `<untrusted_content>` wrapping.

Concrete requirements:
- Endpoint `https://parts.<domain>/mcp`, Streamable HTTP, **stateless** (spec 2026-07-28, compatible with 2025-11-25: `server/discover`, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers).
- Tools = ops with `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` and annotations (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`); `arguments` is the op's input, `structuredContent` its output. `rmcp`'s `outputSchema` root must be an object, so non-object outputs are wrapped.
- Slice 1 tools: `part_create`, `part_edit`, `part_get`, `part_check`, `part_data`, `part_link_for` (whatever the registry holds at build time).
- Errors: tool results with `isError: true` and the error JSON as `structuredContent`, plus a one-line text rendering — **except authentication failures, which are HTTP 401** with `WWW-Authenticate` (T43.b).
- Image outputs: an op output may declare one `ImageOutput {png_hash, width, height}` field (`part_check`'s `screenshot`, T80.d); the adapter renders it as an **image content block** (PNG, ≤ 1 MB, downscaled) in place of the HTTP `{url, …}` form. T53 tests the mapping with a fake renderer behind the registry stub.
- Accepts any bearer token: PAT (static header) or device-grant access token (and OAuth code tokens after T124).
- Config example in docs: `claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN"`.
- **No operation depends on an MCP-only feature**: no sampling, no elicitation, no notifications.

## Not in scope

The registry itself (T20), the ops' logic (T46, T49, T80, T96, T117, …), discovery docs including `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` (T56), OAuth (T43/T124), conformance suite (T57).

## Design notes and decisions

- T02's rmcp spike decides the exact rmcp version/API; pin it exactly.
- Stateless: no session state between requests, so horizontal replay and simple proxies work; `Mcp-Session-Id` not required.
- *Why generate:* "Every adapter iterates the registry, and no adapter defines an operation of its own."
- Auth on HTTP level is load-bearing: the 401 is what triggers an MCP client's OAuth flow (after T124).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "An MCP client connects with a bearer token (a PAT, or a device-grant access token); `tools/list` schemas byte-equal the T20 snapshots; auth failure is HTTP 401, never a tool result".
- [ ] `tools/list` derived from the registry; schemas byte-equal snapshots; annotations present.
- [ ] Errors as `isError` results with `structuredContent`; auth → HTTP 401.
- [ ] `instructions` equals the served `/skill.md` body.
- [ ] An op output with an `ImageOutput` field renders as an MCP image block (fake renderer); the real `part_check` wiring is asserted in T80.d.

## Tests

See subtasks; parent-level: `crates/pf-mcp/tests/mcp_pixel_smoke.rs` with the `rmcp` client: connect with a PAT, `part_create` the pixel board, `part_check` (`renderer_unavailable` until T80 lands; the test accepts either), `part_edit` fix, `part_data list` (joins once T96 lands); assert server logs `surface="mcp" op=… outcome=…` with `request_id`, and no content/token canaries.

## References

PLAN.md §4b Adapters (MCP row), One operation registry, Errors; §3c MCP resources as projections; §4c `part_check` image block; §5 Stack (rmcp 3.x); docs/agent-contract.md "MCP"; Slice 1 "What moved" (T53 ← T50/T51/T52 reversed).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): An MCP client connects with a bearer token (a PAT, or a device-grant access token); `tools/list` schemas byte-equal the T20 snapshots; auth failure is HTTP 401, never a tool result
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T02: Spikes: rolldown/oxc as libraries, rmcp 3.x stateless Streamable HTTP, Leptos SSR vs askama+islands
  - T20: Operation registry crate (pf-ops): typed ops, scopes, hints, executable examples, one error catalogue
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T49: Agent read path (Slice 1): part_get full content <= 32 KiB, file/range, version, history, diff, build log, runtime_errors
- Unblocks: 
  - T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
  - T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
  - T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
  - T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
  - T54: Jig design system: jig.css shared blob, @partifactory/jig, presets, design_system op, Jig as a part
  - T56: Discovery: Markdown GET /, llms.txt, /skill.md = agent contract, server.json, 401 bodies, op-section test
  - T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands

title: T53.a: MCP transport and tools: rmcp stateless Streamable HTTP, registry-generated tools, annotations, error results, image blocks
description:
## Goal and why

Render the operation registry as MCP tools with no hand-written per-tool code, so MCP can never drift from the HTTPS API and CLI.

## Scope

- Mount `rmcp` (version pinned by the T02 spike) Streamable HTTP, stateless, at `POST /mcp` on the workspace listener (:8080); support `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`/`resources/read` (T53.b), `server/discover`; honour `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers (2026-07-28) and stay compatible with 2025-11-25 clients.
- For each registry op: `name` = op `NAME`, `description` = doc comment (≤ 300 chars head, rest in description body), `inputSchema` = schemars JSON Schema, `outputSchema` (object-rooted; wrap non-object outputs as `{result: …}`), annotations from `HINTS` (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint: false`).
- `tools/call`: deserialize `arguments` with `deny_unknown_fields` (unknown field → `unknown_field` with "did you mean"), run the op with the request's principal and `surface="mcp"`, return `structuredContent` + a short text rendering.
- Errors → `isError: true`, `structuredContent` = the catalogue error JSON, text = `message` + hint.
- Image outputs: any op output declaring an `ImageOutput` field (`part_check`'s `screenshot`, wired by T80.d) is rendered as an MCP image block (PNG ≤ 1 MB, downscaled) plus the rest as structuredContent; tested here with a fake renderer behind the registry stub.
- Request id propagated (`X-Request-Id`/ingress header) into logs.

## Not in scope

Auth and 401 (T53.b), resources/instructions (T53.b).

## Design notes and decisions

- Snapshot test compares `tools/list` schemas byte-for-byte with the T20 JSON Schema snapshots: same generator, one source.
- Tool count stays small (≤ 12 + `part_inbox`) by design: near-duplicates cause wrong picks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tools/list` byte-equal schemas; annotations correct per op.
- [ ] Error mapping covers every catalogue code (table test).
- [ ] Image block for an `ImageOutput` field (fake renderer).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/tools_list_snapshot.rs` (byte-equal vs `crates/pf-ops/snapshots/*.json`).
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/error_mapping.rs`: each catalogue error → `isError` result shape.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/stateless.rs`: two independent requests without session id both work; a 2025-11-25-style client handshake works.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/part_check_image_block.rs` with a fake renderer.

## References

PLAN.md §4b Adapters (MCP), Errors (MCP rendering), One operation registry (`outputSchema` object root); §4c `part_check`.

## Dependency context

title: T53.b: MCP auth (HTTP 401), instructions = agent contract, part:// resources as projections, untrusted-content wrapping
description:
## Goal and why

Make MCP safe and self-explaining: auth failures trigger the client's auth flow at HTTP level, the server's `instructions` are the one shared guide, resources are only projections of ops, and content from other people arrives marked as untrusted data.

## Scope

- Bearer middleware from T43.a on `/mcp`; failures → HTTP 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://parts.<domain>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` + JSON body (T43.b), never a JSON-RPC tool result. PATs accepted ("some MCP clients only support a static header").
- `instructions` = `docs/agent-contract.md` (the same text as `/skill.md`, the top of `/llms-full.txt` and OpenAPI `info.description`), embedded at build time.
- Resources `part://recent` and `part://<name>` as **projections** of `part_find`/`part_get` (`part://recent` available once T122's `part_find` exists; until then only `part://<name>` via `part_get`). "Nothing is reachable only as a resource."
- Untrusted wrapping: when an op result has `contains_untrusted: true` (data docs from guests/others, comments from T50), the text rendering wraps such content in `<untrusted_content>…</untrusted_content>`; structuredContent keeps `provenance`.
- Scope errors render as `forbidden {scope_needed}` tool results (403 semantics), not 401.

## Not in scope

OAuth endpoints (T43/T124); `server.json` (T56).

## Design notes and decisions

- Server instructions and resources must not add any capability the registry lacks (§4b "MCP resources and server instructions are only projections").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bad/missing/revoked token → HTTP 401 with header.
- [ ] `instructions` byte-equal the served `/skill.md` body.
- [ ] Resource reads equal the corresponding op outputs.
- [ ] Untrusted content wrapped in text output.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/auth_http_401.rs` (missing, expired, revoked, PAT ok, device token ok); log `event="auth.reject" surface="mcp"`.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/instructions_equal_skill.rs`.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/resources_projection.rs`.
- `crates/pf-mcp/tests/untrusted_wrapper.rs` with a guest-written `__storage` doc read via `part_data`.

## References

PLAN.md §4b Adapters, shared guide, Auth for each kind of client; §3c resources, prompt-injection hygiene; §3b auth failures are 401.

title: T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
description:
## Goal and why

Agents must be able to **see and validate their own work before anyone opens it**. `part_check` renders a version of a part in a sandboxed headless browser exactly as a viewer would, optionally clicks and types through it, and returns a screenshot, a `blank` flag, uncaught errors, console lines and failed loads. It is the P2 headline feature and is in Slice 1: the `communal_pixel_editor` test (T97) has the agent create the board with `live: "after_check"`, run `part_check`, fix what it finds, and only then post `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`.

The `live: "after_check"` gate on `part_create`/`part_edit` uses the same check: a version that builds but throws never reaches people between an agent's create and its fix. The contract's worked session depends on this (v1 throws `ReferenceError: loadBoard is not defined`, so `live` stays `null`).

The renderer is optional (tier (b), a separate container behind a compose profile). With it off, `part_check` returns `renderer_unavailable` and `after_check` degrades to `always` with the warning `check_skipped`; nothing else degrades. **The renderer is never on the save path.**

On the critical path to S1 (… T62 → T80 → T97 → S1). Feeds T97, M2, and later T81 (thumbnails/screenshot cards), T58 (Hermes checks before posting). MCP (T53) no longer waits for the renderer: T80.d depends on T53 and wires the real `part_check` into MCP's image-block path when it lands.

## Scope

Subtasks (this bead is the integration/closure bead: close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end):
- **T80.a** sidecar container, internal network, internal TLS listener, Chrome lifecycle.
- **T80.b** renderer caps (subject `render`, 60 s, read-only) and the read-only shared-data view with a discarded write overlay.
- **T80.c** render queue (`render_jobs`), CDP driver (`chromiumoxide`), `actions`, collection of errors/console/failed requests/blank/height/timing.
- **T80.d** the `part_check` op, `GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>`, rate limits, and the `live: "after_check"` gate wiring into `part_create`/`part_edit` and the build worker live switch.

**Op `part_check` (registry, T20).** Input:

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | str | yes | — | |
| `version` | `"head"` \| `"live"` \| int | no | `"head"` | check before it goes live |
| `viewport` | `mobile` \| `desktop` | no | `mobile` | 390×844 or 1280×800 |
| `wait_ms` | int ≤ 8000 | no | `8000` | waits for `partifactory.ready()`, 500 ms of network idle, or this, whichever is first |
| `actions` | [Action], ≤ 20 | no | none | steps run in order once the page is ready; the screenshot is taken after the last one |
| `include_base64` | bool | no | `false` | HTTP only: add the PNG as `screenshot.base64` |

Action is one of: `{do: "click", selector}` or `{do: "click", x, y}` (CSS pixels, real pointer press and release); `{do: "type", selector, text}` (≤ 1,000 chars); `{do: "wait_ms", ms}` (≤ 2,000); `{do: "eval_return", expr}` (JS expression, promise awaited, JSON value ≤ 4 KiB returned as `value`). The first failing step stops the list. The whole check ends within 15 s.

Output: `{name, url, version, head, live, build, screenshot, blank, height, errors, console, failed_requests, actions, timing}`.
- `screenshot`: an MCP image content block (PNG, ≤ 1 MB, downscaled); over HTTP `{url, expires_at, width, height, base64?}`, `url` = `https://parts.<domain>/api/v1/screenshots/<id>`, fetched with the same `Authorization: Bearer` by the same connection, valid 10 minutes.
- `blank`: body text empty *and* the screenshot ≥ 98 % one colour. `height`: document height in CSS px.
- `errors`: `[{kind, message, stack?, url?}]`, `kind` ∈ `error`, `unhandledrejection`, `blocked_load`, `csp`. `console`: `[{level, text}]` (`console.error`/`warn`, first 50, truncated). `failed_requests`: `[{url, reason, status?}]`. `actions`: `[{i, do, ok, value?, error?}]`. `timing`: `{ready_ms, total_ms}`, `ready_ms` null if `partifactory.ready()` never called. Every `url` is a path within the part with the cap removed.
- Build still running → wait inside the 15 s limit. Build not `ok` → `screenshot: null`, `blank: null`, build errors in `build`. Version saved with `after_check` and its gate check running → wait for that check and return it.
- Errors: `invalid_input` (incl. a bad action), `not_found`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited` (30 per hour per connection), `renderer_unavailable` (HTTP 503, CLI exit 7, `hint`).
- Scope: `parts:read`. With `data:read` the page sees the real shared data read-only; otherwise shared storage starts empty. Personal storage always starts empty.

**Folded check** in `part_edit {check: true}` and `live: "after_check"`: `check` = `{version, passed, blank, height, errors, console, failed_requests, actions, timing, screenshot}`; `passed` is true when there is no `error` or `unhandledrejection` and `blank` is false. `wait` extends to build + check, up to 15 s.

**Gate**: `versions.live_gate TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'always' CHECK (live_gate IN ('always','after_check'))`, `builds.gate_check TEXT CHECK (gate_check IN ('pending','passed','failed','skipped'))`, `render_jobs.purpose` `'gate'`. Live switch (T13): on `ok`, inside the writer, `if version.n > live.n then live = version`, unless `live_gate = 'after_check'`, in which case it waits for the check to pass (or be skipped). Renderer off/down → `gate_check = 'skipped'`, warning `check_skipped` in `build.warnings`, behaves as `always`.

**Sidecar (verbatim)**: `chrome-headless-shell` pinned by digest + fonts (Noto subset with CJK and emoji), container `partifactory-render`, non-root, read-only root fs, tmpfs `/tmp`, `mem_limit: 768m`, `pids_limit: 256`, `cpus: 1`, default seccomp. Flags `--disable-gpu --no-first-run --disable-extensions --disable-background-networking --disable-sync --mute-audio --deny-permission-prompts`. Network: only a Docker `internal: true` network shared with partifactory; `--host-resolver-rules` maps `*-part.<domain>` and `blobs-part.<domain>` to the gateway; partifactory serves the same handlers on an internal-only TLS listener (`:443` on that network, self-signed `*.<domain>` cert generated at start, trusted via `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list`). Compose: behind a profile, off unless `[render] enabled`.

**Queue** `render_jobs` (DDL in T06): concurrency 1, coalesced per part (5 s debounce after a live change, newest only), one retry, a circuit breaker; Chrome starts on demand, stops after 5 minutes idle. Fresh browser context per job; hard timeout 15 s then the context is destroyed. Outputs also tag runtime errors `source: render`.

## Not in scope

- Screenshot thumbnails for the gallery and screenshot og cards for public links: T81 (P4).
- The generic MCP image-block mapping is T53.a; T80.d wires `part_check`'s `screenshot` into it and asserts the real image block.
- The prelude's `ready()`/error capture: T62. `window.storage` server side: T96.
- Hermes' policy on posting screenshots: T58.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why a sidecar, not in-process:* Chrome is large and risky; isolating it in its own container on an `internal: true` network means a page under check can't reach the internet or LAN (egress canary in §7).
- *Why production-identical URLs:* the internal TLS listener and host-resolver rules make URLs, CSP and the secure context match production byte for byte, so a check's result is what a viewer gets. Mirror-on-build means parts need nothing third-party.
- *Why read-only real data + overlay* (decision 43): a pixel someone painted shows in the screenshot, and a click + `eval_return` proves the write path without painting anyone's board.
- *Why mobile default:* most people open links on a phone.
- Concurrency 1 keeps RAM bounded on a household box; 30/h per connection prevents a looping agent from monopolising it.
- The gate check uses the same job path with `purpose = 'gate'`; a `part_check` on a gating version joins that job instead of starting another.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "`part_check` on a page that throws returns the error and a screenshot; a blank page returns `blank: true`; a seeded shared doc shows in the screenshot; a click action followed by `eval_return` reads the changed state, and the write is gone afterwards; with `live: "after_check"` a version that throws stays off `live`; an egress canary from the sidecar fails; sidecar absent -> `renderer_unavailable`".
- [ ] Throwing page → `errors[0].kind = "error"` with message and stack, screenshot present, `passed: false` when folded.
- [ ] Empty page → `blank: true`.
- [ ] Seeded shared `__storage` doc visible in the screenshot (connection with `data:read`); without `data:read` shared storage starts empty.
- [ ] `click` then `eval_return` returns the new value; after the check, `part_data list` shows no change.
- [ ] `after_check` + throwing version: `live` unchanged, `builds.gate_check = 'failed'`; passing version goes live.
- [ ] Renderer off: `part_check` → 503 `renderer_unavailable`; `after_check` behaves as `always` with `check_skipped`.
- [ ] Egress canary from the sidecar to an external host fails; renderer caps cannot persist `/_rt` writes.
- [ ] 31st check in an hour → `rate_limited` with `retry_after`.
- [ ] Screenshot URL works for the same connection for 10 min, 404/401 for any other token.

## Tests

- Unit: `pf_render::actions::tests::parse_limits` (≤ 20 steps, text ≤ 1000, ms ≤ 2000, value ≤ 4 KiB); `pf_render::blank::tests::uniform_98pct`; `pf_render::queue::tests::coalesce_newest_only`.
- Integration `crates/pf-render/tests/part_check_e2e.rs` (needs the sidecar via compose profile): `throws_reports_error`, `blank_page_flag`, `seeded_shared_doc_visible`, `click_eval_overlay_discarded`, `after_check_gate_holds_live`, `renderer_absent_unavailable`, `egress_canary_fails`. Each asserts log events `event="render.job" purpose="check|gate" outcome=...`, `event="cap.mint" subject="render"` and that no cap appears in logs; keeps the screenshot PNG and the job JSON under `target/e2e-logs/<test>/`.
- Conformance: `part_check` step in `tests/agent_surfaces/scenario.yaml` (T57).

## References

PLAN.md §4c Tier (b) and `part_check`; §3d Creation contract (`live`), build worker live switch; §4 Slice 1 op fields; §5e `render_jobs`, `versions.live_gate`, `builds.gate_check`; §7 Render sidecar; decision 16, 43; docs/agent-contract.md `part_check`, `part_edit`, Rule 3.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): `part_check` on a page that throws returns the error and a screenshot; a blank page returns `blank: true`; a seeded shared doc shows in the screenshot; a click action followed by `eval_return` reads the changed state, and the write is gone afterwards; with `live: "after_check"` a version that throws stays off `live`; an egress canary from the sidecar fails; sidecar absent -> `renderer_unavailable`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T15: Capability tokens: path caps, HMAC with daily HKDF kid keys, deterministic windows, epochs + boot floor
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T20: Operation registry crate (pf-ops): typed ops, scopes, hints, executable examples, one error catalogue
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
- Unblocks: 
  - T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T80.a: Render sidecar container, internal-only network and internal TLS listener
  - T80.b: Renderer caps and read-only shared-data view with a discarded write overlay
  - T80.c: Render queue and CDP driver: actions, waits, errors/console/failed loads, blank flag
  - T80.d: part_check op, screenshot endpoint, rate limit, and the live "after_check" gate

title: T80.a: Render sidecar container, internal-only network and internal TLS listener
description:
## Goal and why

The render sidecar must render parts exactly as production does while having no route to the internet or the LAN. This subtask builds the container, the compose service, the isolated network and the internal TLS listener that serves the same handlers to Chrome.

## Scope

- Compose service `partifactory-render` in `deploy/compose.yaml`, behind a profile, off unless `[render] enabled = true`. Image: `chrome-headless-shell` **pinned by digest** + fonts (Noto subset with CJK and emoji). Non-root, read-only root fs, tmpfs `/tmp`, `mem_limit: 768m`, `pids_limit: 256`, `cpus: 1`, default seccomp, `json-file` logging `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`.
- Chrome flags: `--disable-gpu --no-first-run --disable-extensions --disable-background-networking --disable-sync --mute-audio --deny-permission-prompts`, plus `--host-resolver-rules` mapping `*-part.<domain>` and `blobs-part.<domain>` to the gateway address of the internal network, and `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list=<spki of the generated cert>`.
- Network: attached only to a Docker network with `internal: true`, shared with partifactory.
- partifactory: when `[render] enabled`, start an extra listener `:443` bound to the internal network only, with a self-signed `*.<domain>` cert generated at start (keypair in memory), serving the content-listener handlers (part hosts and `blobs-part`) byte-identical to production.
- Chrome lifecycle: started on demand over CDP (`chromiumoxide`), stopped after 5 minutes idle; health check; circuit breaker state exposed as a metric `pf_render_up` and on Health (T36).

## Not in scope

Job queue, actions, collection (T80.c); caps and data overlay (T80.b); op wiring (T80.d).

## Design notes and decisions

- Self-signed cert + SPKI pin avoids shipping a CA and keeps the secure context (needed for `crypto.subtle` etc.).
- On-demand start: costs no RAM most of the day.
- The listener must refuse non-internal sources (bind to the internal network interface only).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker compose --profile render up` starts the sidecar; `docker inspect` shows read-only root, non-root user, limits, internal network only, log limits.
- [ ] From inside the sidecar, `curl https://example.com` (egress canary) fails; a LAN canary fails.
- [ ] Chrome loads `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<cap>/` via the internal listener with the canonical CSP header identical to the public listener's.
- [ ] Idle 5 min → Chrome process gone; next job restarts it.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-render/tests/sidecar_isolation.rs::egress_canary_fails`, `::lan_canary_fails`, `::internal_listener_headers_match_public` (diffs response headers from both listeners).
- `::idle_shutdown` with a test clock; asserts log events `event="render.chrome" action="start|stop"`.
- Failure artifacts: `docker inspect` JSON and sidecar logs under `target/e2e-logs/<test>/`.

## References

PLAN.md §4c Tier (b) Image and Network; §5b render sidecar compose profile; §7 Render sidecar.

- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T80.b: Renderer caps and read-only shared-data view with a discarded write overlay
description:
## Goal and why

A check must run the real prelude against the part's real shared data (so a painted pixel shows) but must never change anything. This subtask defines the `render` cap subject and the `/_rt` behaviour for it.

## Scope

- Mint caps with subject `render` (T15): 60 s window, `m: "render"`, read-only (`ro: true`), role as the checking connection's person but writes never persisted. A fresh cap per job; caps also carry `v` (pinned version) for the version under check.
- `/_rt` for a `render` subject:
  - `storage.get/getMany/list` shared: read from `data_docs` **only if the job's connection has `data:read`**; otherwise shared storage starts empty.
  - personal storage starts empty (empty `pf-boot` snapshot; for `render` subjects the snapshot is empty).
  - `storage.set/delete` (shared and personal): applied to an **in-memory overlay keyed by job id**; later reads in the same job see the overlay merged over the base; the overlay is dropped when the job ends (success, failure or timeout).
  - `errors.report` from a render subject → stored with `source: render` in `runtime_errors` (via T62's path) and also collected into the job result.
  - No events emitted for overlay writes (no `data.changed` to real viewers).
- Overlay limits mirror real limits (key 1–512 bytes, value ≤ 256 KiB) so behaviour matches production.

## Not in scope

The CDP driver (T80.c); `/_rt` storage ops themselves (T96); cap format (T15).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 43: "`part_check` runs the real prelude over a read-only view of the real shared data with a discarded write overlay".
- The overlay lives in the content listener process, not the browser, so the prelude needs no special mode: it behaves exactly as for a viewer.
- `data:read` gate: a connection that can't read data must not see it in a screenshot either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A render cap cannot persist any `/_rt` write (§7 Render sidecar line).
- [ ] Write then read in the same job returns the written value; after the job, `data_docs` unchanged and the overlay freed.
- [ ] Without `data:read`, shared `list` returns empty.
- [ ] No `data.changed` reaches an open viewer tab during a check.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_render_overlay.rs::write_then_read_same_job`, `::overlay_discarded_after_job`, `::no_data_read_scope_empty`, `::no_events_from_overlay`. Assert log `event="rt.op" principal="render" op="storage.set" outcome="ok" persisted=false`.
- Property test `render_cap_never_writes`: random op sequences under a render cap leave the DB byte-identical (compare `data_docs` dump).

## References

PLAN.md §4c Renderer caps; §2 capability format (`s: "render"`, 60 s window); §3a role × runtime matrix; decision 43; docs/agent-contract.md `part_check` "What the check sees".

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T80.c: Render queue and CDP driver: actions, waits, errors/console/failed loads, blank flag
description:
## Goal and why

The engine of `part_check`: a single-concurrency queue that drives Chrome over CDP, runs the agent's `actions`, and collects everything an agent needs to fix a page.

## Scope

- Queue table `render_jobs` (`purpose` ∈ `check|gate|thumbnail|og`, `status` ∈ `queued|running|ok|failed|superseded`, `request` JSON `{wait_ms, actions}`, `result` JSON `{screenshot_hash, blank, errors, console, failed_requests, actions, timing}`). **Concurrency 1**, coalesced per part (5 s debounce after a live change, newest only, older queued → `superseded`), one retry, circuit breaker (opens after repeated failures; `renderer_unavailable` while open).
- Per job: fresh browser context; viewport `mobile` 390×844 @2x or `desktop` 1280×800; navigate to `https://<name>-part.<domain>/c/<render-cap>/` (the content, not the wrapper); wait for `partifactory.ready()`, 500 ms network idle, or `wait_ms` (≤ 8000), whichever first.
- Actions in order: `click` (selector or x,y: real pointer press/release via CDP Input), `type` (focus + key events, ≤ 1,000 chars), `wait_ms` (≤ 2,000), `eval_return` (Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise, JSON value ≤ 4 KiB). First failing step stops the list, result `{i, do, ok:false, error}`.
- Screenshot after the last action, PNG; stored as a blob (`screenshot_hash`); MCP copy downscaled ≤ 1 MB.
- Collect: uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections (`error`, `unhandledrejection`), `console.error`/`warn` (first 50, truncated), failed and CSP-blocked requests (`blocked_load`, `csp`), document height, `timing {ready_ms, total_ms}`, blank flag = body text empty AND screenshot ≥ 98 % one colour. Strip the cap from every URL (paths within the part).
- Hard timeout 15 s, then destroy the context. Runtime errors also written with `source: render`.

## Not in scope

Op surface, screenshot endpoint and gate (T80.d).

## Design notes and decisions

- `chromiumoxide` chosen in §5. Fresh context per job avoids state bleed between parts.
- Waiting on `partifactory.ready()` makes checks fast for pages that call it (the contract tells agents to).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Throwing page yields the error with stack; blank page `blank: true`; click+eval reads changed state.
- [ ] Two checks queued for one part within 5 s → one runs, the other `superseded` (gate/check jobs explicitly requested are joined, not dropped).
- [ ] A page that never settles is cut at 15 s with partial results.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-render/tests/driver.rs`: fixtures in `tests/golden/render/` (`throws.html`, `blank.html`, `pixel.html`, `csp_violation.html`, `blocked_cdn.html`, `never_ready.html`): `::collect_error`, `::blank_detection`, `::click_then_eval`, `::csp_and_blocked_kinds`, `::timeout_15s`, `::urls_have_no_cap`.
- Unit `queue::tests::{coalesce, retry_once, breaker_opens}`. Logs: `event="render.job" job_id part_id purpose outcome total_ms`.

## References

PLAN.md §4c Driving it, Collects, Queue; §5e `render_jobs`; docs/agent-contract.md `part_check` actions and output.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T80.a: Render sidecar container, internal-only network and internal TLS listener, T80.b: Renderer caps and read-only shared-data view with a discarded write overlay
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Throwing page yields the error with stack; blank page `blank: true`; click+eval reads changed state.
- [ ] Two checks queued for one part within 5 s → one runs, the other `superseded` (gate/check jobs explicitly requested are joined, not dropped).
- [ ] A page that never settles is cut at 15 s with partial results.

title: T80.d: part_check op, screenshot endpoint, rate limit, and the live "after_check" gate
description:
## Goal and why

Expose the renderer as the registry op `part_check`, serve screenshots to the asking connection, and gate `live` on a passing check when a version is saved with `live: "after_check"`.

## Scope

- Register `part_check` in `pf-ops` (T20): input/output exactly as the parent bead's tables; scope `parts:read`; hints `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`; executable examples from docs/agent-contract.md (the pixel `click` + `wait_ms` + `eval_return` example).
- Behaviour: resolve `version` (`head`/`live`/n); if the build is running, wait (inside 15 s); if the build isn't `ok`, return `screenshot: null`, `blank: null` and the build's errors; if a gate check for that version is running, wait and return it.
- `GET /api/v1/screenshots/<id>`: same bearer, same connection only, 10-minute validity (`expires_at`), `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; `include_base64: true` adds `base64` over HTTP.
- Rate limit: 30 per hour per connection → `rate_limited` (429 + `Retry-After`, `details.retry_after`).
- `renderer_unavailable` (503, CLI exit 7) when disabled or the breaker is open, with a hint "carry on unchecked, and say so".
- MCP: `part_check`'s output declares `screenshot` as the registry `ImageOutput` field so T53.a's adapter renders it as an image content block (PNG ≤ 1 MB, downscaled); assert the real block end to end here (`crates/pf-mcp/tests/part_check_image_block_real.rs`, with the sidecar).
- Gate: `part_create`/`part_edit` `live: "always" | "after_check"` stored in `versions.live_gate`; on build `ok` with `after_check`, enqueue a `gate` job (mobile), set `builds.gate_check = 'pending'`; the live switch (T13) moves `live` only on `passed` (no `error`/`unhandledrejection`, not blank). Renderer off → `gate_check = 'skipped'` + warning `check_skipped`, live moves as `always`. `part_edit {check: true}` folds the check in as `check`; `wait` extends to 15 s.
- Events: `build.finished` then, on switch, `part.live_changed`; failed gate leaves `live` and emits a `build.finished` with `gate_check: failed`.

## Not in scope

The thumbnail/og purposes (T81).

## Design notes and decisions

- The gate reuses the check job, so `part_check` on a gating version returns the same result the gate used (one render, one answer).
- Only the requesting connection may fetch a screenshot: it may show shared data its person can read.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contract worked session reproduces: v1 throws → `live: null`; v2 fix with `after_check` → `head: 2, live: 2, check.passed: true`.
- [ ] Screenshot URL 200 for the owner connection, 404 for another connection, 404 after 10 min.
- [ ] 31st call in an hour → 429.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-ops/tests/part_check_op.rs::{waits_for_running_build, failed_build_null_screenshot, joins_gate_check, rate_limit_30_per_hour}`.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/live_gate.rs::{after_check_holds_live_on_throw, after_check_skipped_without_renderer, always_moves_on_ok}`; logs asserted: `event="live.switch" gate="after_check" result="held|moved|skipped"`.
- Snapshot of the generated JSON Schema (T20 snapshot suite).

## References

PLAN.md §3d `live: "always" | "after_check"`, build worker live switch, `wait`; §4c `part_check`; §4b error table (`renderer_unavailable` 503/7); docs/agent-contract.md `part_check`, `part_edit` check field, worked session steps 3–5.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T80.c: Render queue and CDP driver: actions, waits, errors/console/failed loads, blank flag; and T53 (MCP server), so the image block is wired here when `part_check` lands

- [ ] Screenshot URL 200 for the owner connection, 404 for another connection, 404 after 10 min.
- [ ] 31st call in an hour → 429.

title: T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
description:
## Goal and why

People edit parts in place, like Claude's artifacts, while agents keep editing the same part. Drafts live on the server per (person, part), so they survive reloads and device switches, and when an agent lands a version mid-edit the draft merges with diff3: non-overlapping changes merge silently, overlaps show a side-by-side resolve. Nobody's work is silently discarded. After Slice 1; on the M2 critical path (… T80 → T53 → T123 → T55 → M2).

## Scope

- `Edit` in the wrapper/workspace (hidden without `edit`) opens the editor on the workspace host with **Preview · Split · Source**; Split = file tree + CodeMirror 6 + live preview rendered from the **draft**.
- CodeMirror 6 vendored as a shared blob (the one JS dependency). Syntax in four hues (keyword: signal; string: agent blue; number/const: public-text amber; comment: `ink-3` italic), Plex Mono 13.5/20.
- Drafts: table `drafts (user_id, part_id, base_version_id, files JSON {path: text}, updated_at, PRIMARY KEY (user_id, part_id))`; autosave to the server (debounced). Preview via a cap with a `d` claim (draft id), never the live version; drafts and never-live versions need `edit`.
- Save (⌘S) creates a version through `part_edit` (whole-file `write` with `if_match`, `via = 'editor'`); a lease held by an agent shows "Hermes is editing this file until 14:32" with a blue dot and saving asks once (leases from T47 if present; otherwise skipped).
- Merge: on `pf:version`/event (T123 SSE) for a new head mid-edit, run 3-way `diff3` at line granularity (base, draft, head). Non-overlapping: merge silently, banner "Hermes saved REV 13 while you were editing. Your changes were merged." Overlaps open **Resolve** (Keep mine / Keep theirs / Edit per hunk). "Force" exists only for the person, never for agents.
- Markdown and slides get block-aware editing with pending placeholders when T48 exists.
- Phone: Source only (tap-to-edit text is T85).
- Draft rows are referenced by blob GC (T59) and cleaned when the part is purged.

## Not in scope

Tap-to-edit on phones (T85); leases (T47); block ids (T48); the history rail (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why not CRDTs:* agents submit whole edits; live human co-typing isn't a v1 goal (§9). `yrs` could later run inside one editing session.
- *Why server drafts:* personal state is server-side by design; a device switch must not lose work.
- Budget: "Small text fix by hand: Edit → (type) → ⌘S" = **2 + type**.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "e2e: an agent edit lands mid-draft; non-overlapping changes merge silently, overlapping ones show resolve".
- [ ] Draft survives reload and a second device.
- [ ] Preview frame uses a `d`-claim cap and shows draft content, never live.
- [ ] Overlap → Resolve with three choices; each produces the expected file.
- [ ] Click budget asserted.

## Tests

`crates/pf-model/tests/diff3_merge.rs` (golden cases: disjoint, adjacent, overlapping, delete-vs-edit); `tests/e2e/editor_merge.spec.ts::{draft_persists, agent_edit_merges_silently, overlap_shows_resolve, budget_small_fix}` with logs `op=part_edit via=editor`, `event=draft.merge result=clean|conflict`.

## References

PLAN.md §3c In place, like Claude's artifacts; §3d People and agents together; §4a.6 In-place editor; §5e `drafts`; §4a.7 budgets.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): e2e: an agent edit lands mid-draft; non-overlapping changes merge silently, overlapping ones show resolve
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Correction: `drafts.files` is inline JSON `{path: text}` (the DDL), so drafts hold no blobs and blob GC has nothing to mark there; drafts are deleted when the part is purged. (T59's reference list keeps "drafts" only for blob refs a future `blob:` write might add.)
- Tests added: `draft_never_served_live` (a `d`-claim cap serves the draft only to `edit`+ holders and never advances `live`), an autosave-debounce unit test, and `draft_second_device` (the acceptance's second-device step).
- Split into T55.a / T55.b (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: an agent edit lands mid-draft; non-overlapping changes merge silently, overlapping ones show resolve
