title: T56: Discovery: Markdown GET /, llms.txt, /skill.md = agent contract, server.json, 401 bodies, op-section test
description:
## Goal and why

An agent told only `https://parts.<domain>` must be able to find everything: what partifactory is, how to connect, every op with fields and examples. `docs/agent-contract.md` is the one page an agent reads; it is the MCP `instructions`, the body of `/skill.md`, the top of `/llms-full.txt` and the OpenAPI `info.description`. A test keeps its op sections equal to the operation registry so the docs can't rot. In Slice 1 and on the critical path (… T43 → T53 → T56 → T57 → S1); Slice 1 definition of done item 7 is "`/skill.md` is `docs/agent-contract.md`, and the test that regenerates its op reference from the registry passes".

## Scope

Discovery paths (verbatim from §4b):

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` with an `Accept` that isn't HTML | `text/markdown`: what partifactory is, the four ways to connect, and links to everything below (`Vary: Accept`; browsers get the UI) |
| `/llms.txt` | one paragraph, then links to `/skill.md`, `/openapi.json`, `/mcp`, `/llms-full.txt` |
| `/llms-full.txt` | the guide + every op's description, schema summary and examples, as one file |
| `/openapi.json` | OAS 3.1, ETag = build hash (generated by T21) |
| `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | RFC 9728 for the one resource `https://parts.<domain>/`: `authorization_servers`, `scopes_supported`, `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`, `resource_documentation` → `/llms.txt` (served by T43) |
| `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | RFC 8414, also at `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (T43) |
| `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` | MCP registry `server.json` shape (name, description, version, `remotes: [{type: streamable-http, url}]`). **Served, not published**; the public repo ships a template |

- `/skill.md`: Agent Skills format, frontmatter `name: partifactory` and a `description` that triggers on "make/share/edit a page, tool, doc, deck"; body = `docs/agent-contract.md` (embedded in the binary at build time, `<domain>` left literal or substituted with the deployment apex — recommended: substitute in served copies, keep `<domain>` in the repo file).
- `/agents.md`: an `AGENTS.md` snippet. `part skill install [--claude | --codex | --path]` writes `~/.claude/skills/partifactory/SKILL.md` or appends the snippet to `AGENTS.md` (CLI side lives in T22's generated CLI; this task adds the alias).
- **401 bodies**: every `401` from `/api` or `/mcp` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://parts.<domain>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"` **and** a JSON body explaining the ways to get a token (in Slice 1: device code, personal token; OAuth with T124), with links.
- **Op-section test**: an op section runs from its `<!-- pf:op <name> -->` marker to the next marker or `## ` heading; the generator owns its field table and its `Errors:` line; the description sentence, the `Output:` paragraph and the example are hand prose. The test regenerates the owned lines from the registry and fails on any diff in `docs/agent-contract.md` or the served `/skill.md`, and parses each example against the op's input schema. It documents only ops that exist; later ops add their section in the same change.
- GPT Actions lint in CI: every op has an `operationId`, descriptions ≤ 300 chars (`x-pf-description` carries the rest), ≤ 30 operations.
- Discovery documents are unauthenticated and contain no site secrets or user data: they never list spaces, parts or people. No A2A agent card.

## Not in scope

OAuth metadata content (T43), OpenAPI generation (T21), MCP instructions wiring (T53 consumes the guide), conformance execution of examples (T57).

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why one guide everywhere* (decision 38): "make me a packing checklist in partifactory" must be enough on any surface; one page avoids drift between MCP instructions, skill and docs.
- *Why served, not published* `server.json`: a private instance; the public MCP registry doesn't support private servers.
- *No A2A card*: partifactory is a tool server, not an agent (decision 11).
- `llms.txt` is cheap and harmless; no client relies on it.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A scripted agent given only the workspace URL creates and edits a part; docs regenerate in CI with no diff; a test regenerates each op section's owned lines (the field table and the `Errors:` line, from its `<!-- pf:op <name> -->` marker to the next marker or `## ` heading) and fails if `docs/agent-contract.md` or `/skill.md` differs, and parses each example against the op's input schema".
- [ ] `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://parts.<domain>/` returns Markdown with `Vary: Accept`; a browser gets HTML.
- [ ] `/skill.md` body byte-equals the contract (modulo the domain substitution rule).
- [ ] Changing a field's description in Rust without updating the contract fails CI.
- [ ] Every 401 from `/api` and `/mcp` carries the header and JSON body.
- [ ] Grep of every discovery response for fixture part names, space slugs and usernames finds none.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-ops/tests/contract_sections.rs::{owned_lines_match_registry, examples_parse_against_schema, every_op_has_section, no_section_for_missing_op}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/discovery.rs::{markdown_root_vary_accept, llms_txt_links, server_json_shape, no_user_data_in_discovery, unauth_401_body}`.
- `tests/agent_surfaces/blind_agent.rs`: a scripted agent with only `PARTIFACTORY_URL` + a PAT follows `/skill.md` to create and edit a part; logs `surface=http op=part_create outcome=ok`.
- CI lint job `gpt-actions-lint`. Optional nightly (non-gating): a small model given only the URL + PAT must make a packing list via discovery.

## References

PLAN.md §4b Adapters (skill file), shared guide, Discovery, Auth for each kind of client; §8 decisions 11, 38; docs/agent-contract.md Discovery.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A scripted agent given only the workspace URL creates and edits a part; docs regenerate in CI with no diff; a test regenerates each op section's owned lines (the field table and the `Errors:` line, from its `<!-- pf:op <name> -->` marker to the next marker or `## ` heading) and fails if `docs/agent-contract.md` or `/skill.md` differs, and parses each example against the op's input schema
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T20: Operation registry crate (pf-ops): typed ops, scopes, hints, executable examples, one error catalogue
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
acceptance_criteria: A scripted agent given only the workspace URL creates and edits a part; docs regenerate in CI with no diff; a test regenerates each op section's owned lines (the field table and the `Errors:` line, from its `<!-- pf:op <name> -->` marker to the next marker or `## ` heading) and fails if `docs/agent-contract.md` or `/skill.md` differs, and parses each example against the op's input schema

title: T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
description:
## Goal and why

"Any AI, any surface, one operation set" is only true if every surface behaves identically. One scenario file runs through four drivers, and normalised results, errors and audit rows must be identical across drivers and across auth kinds. Slice 1 definition of done item 3 requires it with device-code and personal tokens. Last task of the conformance chain (… T43 → T53 → T56 → T57 → S1).

## Scope

- `tests/agent_surfaces/scenario.yaml`: a list of `(op, input, expect)` steps. Full v1 scenario: create a part → get the link → edit with a stale base (auto-rebase) → a conflicting edit (expect `anchor_not_found` with a hint) → find it → share inward with a group → get a deep link for a public link (`part_link_for`) → comment `to_agent` → write `db` → `part_check` → restore v1. **In Slice 1** the scenario covers the Slice 1 ops (`part_create`, `part_edit`, `part_get`, `part_check`, `part_data`, `part_link_for`); the find, comment and inward-share steps join with T122, T50 and T52; `db` writes use `part_data` until T73. Every step's input is an example from `docs/agent-contract.md`.
- Four drivers against an ephemeral server:
  1. MCP via the `rmcp` client.
  2. HTTP via a client **generated from `/openapi.json`** (proves the spec is truthful).
  3. The CLI via subprocess with `--json`.
  4. **The skill file itself**: the example commands in `/skill.md` and `/llms-full.txt` are extracted and executed.
- Auth kinds: in Slice 1 device grant and PAT; T124's OAuth auth code joins as the third.
- Normalisation: ids, timestamps, request ids, screenshot URLs and hashes of time-dependent content replaced by placeholders; then results, error envelopes (`code`, `retryable`, `details` keys) and audit rows (`action`, `target`, `before`/`after`, with `actor` normalised to the kind) must be identical.
- The suite also validates `/openapi.json`, runs the GPT Actions lint and fetches every discovery URL.

## Not in scope

The ops themselves; the discovery docs (T56); the optional nightly small-model run (non-gating, may live here as a separate job).

## Design notes and decisions

- Every adapter iterates the registry and none defines its own op, so divergence can only come from adapter bugs, which this suite catches.
- Executing the skill file's commands keeps the agent-facing examples honest; the contract's examples are the scenario's inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Normalised results, errors and audit rows are identical across the four drivers and every auth kind that exists".
- [ ] 4 drivers × 2 auth kinds green in CI; a deliberate divergence (e.g. an adapter renaming an error code) fails with a readable diff.
- [ ] Adding a new op without scenario coverage fails a coverage check.

## Tests

`tests/agent_surfaces/run.rs` (nextest) with `driver_mcp`, `driver_openapi`, `driver_cli`, `driver_skill`; `normalise.rs` unit tests; each driver writes `target/e2e-logs/conformance/<driver>-<auth>.jsonl` (server logs filtered by request id) and the normalised transcript; the diff is printed on failure.

## References

PLAN.md §4b Conformance: one scenario, every surface; Adapters; Slice 1 definition of done 3; docs/agent-contract.md (examples).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Normalised results, errors and audit rows are identical across the four drivers and every auth kind that exists
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T22: `part` CLI generated from the registry (`part <op> --json`) + ergonomic aliases, env-based auth, dev token
  - T45: Personal agent tokens (pf_pat_) and the Connected agents page (list, revoke with cascade, New personal token)
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
  - T56: Discovery: Markdown GET /, llms.txt, /skill.md = agent contract, server.json, 401 bodies, op-section test
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
acceptance_criteria: Normalised results, errors and audit rows are identical across the four drivers and every auth kind that exists

title: T124: OAuth authorization code after Slice 1: /oauth/authorize + PKCE S256, iss, CIMD, DCR, manual clients
description:
## Goal and why

claude.ai and ChatGPT custom connectors accept only OAuth, and "Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow" is an M2 line. This bead adds the authorization-code flow to the token service from T43, so any MCP client can connect with a browser instead of a pasted personal token. It was deliberately kept out of Slice 1: "The authorization endpoint is the largest new attack surface in the plan (CIMD fetches behind the SSRF guard, DCR abuse limits, redirect-host display, consent for unknown clients), and none of it is exercised by the [pixel] test." Because T43 built the AS token side, this adds an endpoint, not a redesign. Feeds milestone M2.

## Scope

Flow (MCP authorization spec 2026-07-28, compatible with 2025-11-25):
```
claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp
  → POST /mcp → 401 WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", scope="parts:read parts:write"
  → client reads Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) → authorization server = parts.<domain>
  → client identifies itself: Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD, preferred) or Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591, deprecated, kept)
  → browser: /oauth/authorize (PKCE S256, resource=https://parts.<domain>/ per RFC 8707)
       → IdP or local-passkey login if needed (1 passkey tap)
       → consent sheet: "Claude Code (redirect: localhost) wants to: read & edit parts in [~me ▾]. [ ] Share with people already in the household. [ ] Deploy backends and set their secrets. Expires: [90 days ▾]" → passkey → Allow
  → authorization response carries iss (RFC 9207)
  → token: opaque, audience https://parts.<domain>/, sub=<person>, act=conn:<id>, scopes + spaces
```
- `GET /oauth/authorize`: `response_type=code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` (exact match against registered/CIMD `redirect_uris`), `code_challenge` + `code_challenge_method=S256` (required; plain refused), `scope`, `state`, `resource` (must equal the workspace origin).
- Codes: `oauth_codes` rows (`hash`, `client_id`, `user_id`, `redirect_uri`, `code_challenge`, `scopes`, `spaces`, `resource`, `lifetime_ms`, `expires_at` = 60 s, `used_at`), single use. `/oauth/token` `grant_type=authorization_code` verifies the PKCE verifier and creates an `agent_connections` row (`kind='oauth_code'`) and a token family.
- AS metadata gains: `authorization_endpoint`, `code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]`, `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true`, `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`, `registration_endpoint`.
- **Consent sheet shows the redirect URI's host** (spec MUST), with an extra warning for a localhost redirect from a CIMD client.
- **CIMD** (`oauth_clients.kind='cimd'`, id = the metadata URL): fetched through the mirror egress guard (T14): https only, private/loopback/link-local refused after DNS resolution, ≤ 5 KiB, 3 s, no redirects.
- **DCR** (`kind='dcr'`): for Cursor and Gemini CLI. Requires `application_type`, rate-limited (T30 limiter, keyed on client IP; `reg_ip_hash` stored), a registered client is inert until someone consents; "Unconsented registrations expire after 1 hour" (`consented_at IS NULL` + older than 1 h → purged; janitor job registered with T113).
- **Manual clients** (`kind='manual'`): the admin registers client id + secret + redirect URI in the admin area (step-up), for pre-registered-only clients like GPT Actions. `secret_hash` stored; confidential client auth at `/oauth/token`.
- `share:household` is off by default for clients registered by CIMD, DCR or by hand; `backends:deploy` off by default for every client.
- Joins the T57 conformance scenario as the third auth kind.

## Not in scope

Token rotation, revocation, 401s (T43). Device grant (T44). PATs (T45). The admin area shell beyond the manual-client form.

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 37: auth code is after Slice 1; every MCP client the slice needs accepts a static bearer header.
- CIMD and mirror-on-build share one egress guard so neither can reach internal addresses (§5d).
- The consent sheet is T43.c's component plus the redirect host and the localhost warning.
- `/oauth/authorize` sits on the workspace host, uses the person session; signed-out → sign-in → back (state preserved).
- Error responses follow RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 (redirect with `error=` only after `redirect_uri` is validated; otherwise an error page).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "OAuth conformance suite passes; a CIMD URL resolving to a private IP is refused; the consent sheet shows the redirect host; Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow and joins the T57 scenario as the third auth kind".
- [ ] PKCE S256 required; code single use, 60 s; `iss` in the response.
- [ ] CIMD fetch refused for private/loopback/link-local, > 5 KiB, > 3 s, or redirects.
- [ ] DCR rate-limited; unconsented clients purged after 1 h.
- [ ] Manual clients work with a secret.
- [ ] Metadata lists the new endpoints; RFC 8414 validation passes.
- [ ] Click budget: "Connect Claude Code (signed in) | (browser opens) → Allow → biometric | 2".

## Tests

- `crates/pf-oauth/tests/oauth_conformance.rs`: an RFC 6749/7636/8707/9207 conformance suite (code reuse, wrong verifier, wrong redirect, missing resource, state echo, iss).
- `pf_oauth::cimd::tests::{private_ip_refused, too_large_refused, redirect_refused, timeout}` with a local DNS stub; log `event="egress.refuse" reason="private_address"`.
- `pf_oauth::dcr::tests::{requires_application_type, rate_limited, unconsented_expire_1h}` (test clock).
- E2E `tests/e2e/oauth_code_claude_code.spec.ts` on the T24 harness with the virtual authenticator: an MCP client does the full flow, counts interactions (2), asserts redirect host on the sheet; keeps trace + server.jsonl.
- T57 scenario gains `auth: oauth_code`.

## References

PLAN.md §3b How agents authenticate (flow, AS metadata, CIMD, DCR, manual clients), §4b Auth for each kind of client, §5e `oauth_clients`, `oauth_codes`, §7 Agents, Slice 1 "Decided for the slice"; decision 37.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): OAuth conformance suite passes; a CIMD URL resolving to a private IP is refused; the consent sheet shows the redirect host; Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow and joins the T57 scenario as the third auth kind
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T14 (CIMD fetches use the egress guard, with a CIMD profile: https only, ≤ 5 KiB, 3 s, no redirects, vs the mirror profile of ≤ 3 redirects / 10 s / 10 MiB) and T30 (DCR registration rate limit).
- Testability: the T24 harness resolves `*.pf.test` to private addresses, which the SSRF guard refuses, so the full browser e2e runs with a `manual` (or DCR) client; CIMD is covered by unit tests with the DNS stub, plus one e2e CIMD case under a test-only `[unsafe] egress_allow_private = "on"` key that Health and `doctor` flag.
- Tests added to the conformance list: `/oauth/authorize` while signed out → sign-in → back with `state` preserved; `share:household` and `backends:deploy` default off on the consent sheet for cimd/dcr/manual clients.
- Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` op sections and the "After Slice 1" list are updated in the same change; T56's registry-match test stays green. (the Connecting section gains the browser OAuth flow; "the browser OAuth flow for MCP" leaves the After list).
acceptance_criteria: OAuth conformance suite passes; a CIMD URL resolving to a private IP is refused; the consent sheet shows the redirect host; Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow and joins the T57 scenario as the third auth kind

title: T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
description:
## Goal and why

"You watch the page change after asking." When a new live version lands, every open viewer sees it without reloading by hand: the household loop (comment from a phone, agent fixes, the fix appears) depends on it. After Slice 1 (P2), feeds M2 and the Hermes skill's demo.

## Scope

- Source of truth: `part.live_changed` events (T51's broadcast). Delivery:
  - **Framed (normal) view**: the wrapper listens (its own `EventSource` to `/c/<cap>/_rt/events` via the frame, or the chrome API's event stream — recommended: the prelude inside the frame receives `pf:version` on `/_rt/events` and posts `{type: "pf:version", n}` to the wrapper; the wrapper owns the decision) and reloads the frame `src` with the current cap.
  - **Standalone** `/c/` documents: the prelude's `EventSource` receives `pf:version` and handles it itself.
- Decision: a page with no unsaved personal state reloads in place (frame cross-fades `d-3`, never a flash of blank); otherwise a toast "Updated by Hermes · Reload". "Unsaved personal state" = the prelude's `localStorage` shim has pending write-behind not yet flushed, or the page called `partifactory` hook marking dirty (recommended minimal: pending writes only).
- The wrapper's version chip and agent activity line update ("Claude Code saved REV 12 · just now" for 30 s).
- Messages from the frame are identified by `event.source === frame.contentWindow`, never `event.origin`.

## Not in scope

The event log and SSE (T51, T123); the "being made…" placeholder cross-fade (T51).

## Design notes and decisions

- Wrapper-driven reload keeps the trusted UI outside the part (final-round F28).
- No reload storms: coalesce events within 500 ms; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "With a part open on a phone, an agent edit appears within 2 s; a page with unsaved personal state shows the toast instead".

## Tests

`tests/e2e/live_reload.spec.ts::{agent_edit_appears_within_2s_mobile_webkit, unsaved_state_shows_toast, standalone_prelude_reloads}`; logs `event=live.switch`, `event=sse.deliver type=pf:version`.

## References

PLAN.md §3c Live reload; §2 prelude (`pf:version`); §4a.6 Part view agent activity; §4a.5 motion.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): With a part open on a phone, an agent edit appears within 2 s; a page with unsaved personal state shows the toast instead
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Decided: delivery is the **prelude relay** (final-round F28). The wrapper's CSP has `connect-src` = the workspace only, so it cannot open its own `EventSource` to `/c/<cap>/_rt/events`; the prelude posts `{type: "pf:version", n, dirty}` by postMessage and the wrapper decides reload vs toast and swaps `frame.src`.
- Decided: "unsaved personal state" = pending `localStorage` write-behind **or** an edited form control (`el.value !== el.defaultValue` on any input/textarea/contenteditable, or a focused text control); a cheap heuristic inside the prelude, no new public API, documented in the contract's "What a page can do".
- Ownership: this task owns the `pf:version` plumbing and the reload/toast; the version-chip and agent-activity text updates are T120.a/T120.c's.
- Unit tests added: 500 ms coalescing, the dirty heuristic, `event.source === frame.contentWindow` (a message from another window is ignored), `reduced_motion_no_crossfade`.
acceptance_criteria: With a part open on a phone, an agent edit appears within 2 s; a page with unsaved personal state shows the toast instead

title: T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
description:
## Goal and why

The first moment of daily value is "Hermes makes a thing from Telegram and I open it on my phone". Hermes (the example deployment's chat agent) is a client of partifactory's public contracts, not a dependency: this task writes its `partifactory` skill so the M2 household loop works end to end. One connection per (agent, person) avoids the confused-deputy problem (with one shared token every request was "Hermes for the admin" and Hermes could read the admin's private parts while serving someone else).

## Scope

- **Pairing**: "Hermes, connect me to partifactory" → Hermes starts a device grant (`client_id=part-cli`, `agent_name="Hermes"`, `software="hermes/<ver>"`), sends the person `verification_uri_complete` + `user_code`; the person approves in their real browser (passkey + Allow); Hermes stores a map `telegram_user_id → {access, refresh}` and refreshes per the contract (1 h access, single-use refresh). Unpaired chat users get nothing and are told to ask the admin for an invite. Labels show "Hermes for <person>".
- **Making things**: create/edit with `live: "after_check"`; run `part_check` (with `actions` for interactive pages) before posting and fix what it finds; post the part's own host link `https://<name>-part.<domain>/` with `link_preview_options {prefer_small_media: true}` (the content-free card) and inline buttons **Open** and **Ask for a change**.
- **Sharing**: inward with `share:household` (T52), e.g. "share it with the family" → move to Family / grant group.
- **People-only actions**: call `part_link_for` and send its URL with one line saying what tapping it does (and that the admin must tap if the person isn't the admin). Never claim a part is public until it is.
- **Comment relay**: "Ask for a change" asks for text and files a `to_agent` comment with that person's own connection; Hermes watches events (`part_watch` / signed webhooks, T123), fixes, and tells the person in chat when the fix lands (live reload shows it).
- Screenshots in chat: Hermes' own setting (owner's direct chat only, never a group).
- If Telegram's in-app browser fails passkeys (T38 result), messages say "open in browser".
- Ship as a skill file in the repo under `examples/hermes/` (Hermes-specific code lives with Hermes; partifactory ships the example).

## Not in scope

Hermes itself; the `nest-family` profile (T65); the agent inbox (T84).

## Design notes and decisions

- Content from others is data, not instructions (Rule 6): relayed comments carry provenance; Hermes must treat `<untrusted_content>` as data.
- partifactory never messages Telegram itself (no notifications for people).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Scripted Telegram flow: pair -> 'make a packing list and share it with the family' -> link -> comment -> fix -> live reload; 'make it public' gets a deep link that opens the share sheet on the public rung".

## Tests

`tests/e2e/hermes_flow.spec.ts` with a scripted Telegram stub (bot API mock) driving the skill: `pair_device_code`, `packing_list_shared_with_family`, `comment_fix_live_reload`, `make_it_public_deep_link`; asserts server logs `principal=conn:* agent_name=Hermes`, `op=part_check` precedes the posted link, and two pairings yield two connections.

## References

PLAN.md §3b One connection per (agent, person), Device grant; §4 Example consumers (Hermes); §6 P2 Done when; docs/agent-contract.md Connecting, Rules.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Scripted Telegram flow: pair -> 'make a packing list and share it with the family' -> link -> comment -> fix -> live reload; 'make it public' gets a deep link that opens the share sheet on the public rung
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
  - T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
  - T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
  - T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
  - T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - T65: Hermes nest-family profile: family-space-only agent profile for the household chat

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T50 (comments with `to_agent` and provenance) and T79 (live reload), both needed by the acceptance flow "comment → fix → live reload".
- Testability: a skill file is prose for an LLM, so the deterministic CI test drives a thin reference client `examples/hermes/` (a script over the HTTP API implementing pair / create / check / share / relay) against the Telegram bot-API mock; the real-LLM run stays the optional nightly (as in T57).
- Skill text additions: a used refresh token revokes the whole family (never retry a refresh; serialise refreshes), and 401 handling (prompt the person to re-pair).
acceptance_criteria: Scripted Telegram flow: pair -> 'make a packing list and share it with the family' -> link -> comment -> fix -> live reload; 'make it public' gets a deep link that opens the share sheet on the public rung

title: T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
description:
## Goal and why

Every version is kept and blobs are deduplicated by hash, so the blob store only grows from superseded build output, abandoned uploads and purged parts. A mark-and-sweep GC, run by the janitor (T113), keeps that bounded without ever touching anything a live or binned item references. In Slice 1 (retention: "blob GC").

## Scope

- Janitor job `blobs.gc` (registered with T113; records `janitor_runs` with `action = 'gc'`, items, freed bytes, size after).
- **Mark** (set `blobs.gc_mark`) from: `version_files.blob_hash` of every version of live and binned parts (and manifests: `versions.manifest_hash`), `build_files.blob_hash` and `br_hash`, `builds.output_hash` and `builds.log_hash`, `drafts` (files referenced), `data_snapshots.blob_hash`, `assets.blob_hash`, unpruned `backend_images.tar_hash`, `shared_blobs` (seed/mirror/runtime), `mirror_cache.hash`, screenshots referenced by unexpired `render_jobs.result`.
- **Sweep**: blobs not marked get `unref_since = now` (if NULL); blobs with `unref_since` older than **7 days** are deleted from disk and `blobs`; marked blobs clear `unref_since`.
- Concurrency: a blob written after the mark phase started is never swept (compare `created_at` with the run start); writers re-referencing an `unref_since` blob clear it.
- Metrics: `pf_blob_store_bytes`, `pf_blob_gc_freed_bytes_total`.

## Not in scope

The janitor framework (T113); bin purge (T113's job; purge makes blobs unreferenced, GC collects them later).

## Design notes and decisions

- 7-day grace covers in-flight uploads (have/need), long-running builds and an export reading blobs.
- "Never deletes anything a live or binned item references" is the janitor's rule.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "An unreferenced blob is deleted after the grace period; a blob referenced by any version is never collected".
- [ ] Each reference source above keeps its blob alive (one fixture per source).
- [ ] A blob referenced only by a binned part survives.
- [ ] Freed bytes recorded in `janitor_runs` and `/metrics`.

## Tests

`crates/pf-janitor/tests/blob_gc.rs::{unref_deleted_after_7d, each_reference_kind_keeps_blob, binned_part_blob_survives, concurrent_write_not_swept}` using a test clock; logs `event=janitor.run store=blobs action=gc freed_bytes`.

## References

PLAN.md §5d Maintenance (Blob GC); §5h retention table (Versions and blobs); §5e `blobs`, modelling row "Every version kept".

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): An unreferenced blob is deleted after the grace period; a blob referenced by any version is never collected
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T08: Source manifests + versions: JCS canonical manifest, version id = sha256, n, parent, head/live pointers
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
acceptance_criteria: An unreferenced blob is deleted after the grace period; a blob referenced by any version is never collected

title: T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved
description:
## Goal and why

A part's name is its hostname and its link, so renames must be rare and must never break or hijack old links. The old host 301s to the new one forever, and a name that was ever used stays reserved, so a future part can't collide with an old redirect. After Slice 1 (P2), feeds M2.

## Scope

- Admin-only action with step-up (10 min): rename from the wrapper title (admin-confirmed) or the admin area. Validates the new name with T09's rules (`[a-z0-9-]`, 1–58 chars, no leading/trailing/double hyphens; not reserved; never used).
- In one writer transaction: `names` row for the old name → `state = 'redirect'`, `retired_at = now`; new `names` row `state = 'active'`; `parts.name` updated; bump `epochs['part:<id>']` (caps are host-bound); audit `part.rename` (before → after).
- Content listener: any request to `<old>-part.<domain>` (root, `/c/…`, `/l/…`, `/_pf/…`) → `301` to `https://<new>-part.<domain><path>` with the **query string stripped**; `Cache-Control` long-lived.
- `/p/<old>` redirects to the new host; `/grant?part=<old>` resolves via `names`.
- Chrome-API CORS never admits an old redirecting name's origin (T29 rule).
- Home-screen installs: the per-part manifest lives on the part host, whose old name 301s; personal state is server-side so nothing strands.
- Agents: `part_get`/`part_edit` by the old name return `not_found` with a hint naming the new name only if the caller can see the part (otherwise plain `not_found`).

## Not in scope

Name validation rules themselves (T09).

## Design notes and decisions

- Query stripped so a leaked `?…` can't ride the redirect; caps are in paths, not queries.
- Reserved forever (`names` is never deleted) — §4 Names.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Old host 301s to the new host with no query; the old name cannot be reused".
- [ ] Non-admin or no step-up → refused.
- [ ] Old-name caps die (epoch bump); new open works via `/grant`.

## Tests

`crates/pf-model/tests/rename.rs::{rename_reserves_old, old_name_rejected_on_create, epoch_bumped}`; `crates/pf-serve/tests/rename_redirect.rs::{root_301_no_query, c_path_301, cors_refuses_old_origin}`; logs `event=audit action=part.rename`.

## References

title: T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
description:
## Goal and why

Communal pages (a pixel board, a sign-up sheet, a poll) are useless read-only. `window.storage` with `shared: true` gives a part shared state that everyone who may write can change, with open pages repainting live when anyone else writes. Agents read and write the same documents through `part_data`, and undo vandalism with `snapshot_list` / `snapshot_restore` / `reset`. This is the data layer of the `communal_pixel_editor` test (T97) and sits on the S1 critical path (… T62 → T77 → T96 → T95 → T97 → S1). It was moved from P3 (T73) into P2 because the P2 acceptance test needs it (round 2c). `window.storage` keeps Claude's artifact API, so Claude-written pages run unchanged.

## Scope

Subtasks (this bead is the integration/closure bead; close only after all subtasks close and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T96.a** server-side `/_rt` `storage.*` ops: roles, `shared_data_writers`, limits, quotas, rate limits, `PfError` codes.
- **T96.b** prelude side: `window.storage` API (Claude-compatible + paging + `getMany`), `PfError` rejections, `data.changed` over `/_rt/events`, `partifactory.on("data.changed", fn)`.
- **T96.c** the `part_data` registry op (get/list/set/delete/snapshot_list/snapshot_restore/reset).

**Storage model** (`data_docs`, DDL from T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE data_docs (
  part_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('shared','personal')),
  owner TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- user id for personal, '' for shared
  collection TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- '__storage' for window.storage
  doc_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  body BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) <= 262144),
  rev INTEGER NOT NULL,                         -- CAS
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_by TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | link:<id> | guest:<link>:<g>
  CHECK ((scope = 'shared') = (owner = '')),
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, scope, owner, collection, doc_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
`window.storage` keys are `part_data` collection `__storage`, key = `doc_id`. Data survives versions; it is in every copy of `/data` and every full export.

**Limits (verbatim):** key 1–512 bytes of UTF-8, no control characters; value a string ≤ 256 KiB; shared data ≤ 5 MiB per part (`parts.shared_data_cap DEFAULT 5242880`); personal data ≤ 256 KiB per person per part (it's inlined as the `localStorage` seed); writes 60/min per guest (300 per IP), 600/min per signed-in person per part; reads 600 requests/min per viewer per part, a `getMany` or a `list` page counts as one.

**Who writes shared data** — `parts.shared_data_writers TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewers' CHECK (shared_data_writers IN ('editors','viewers'))`:

| Who | Reads | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the owner and people with `edit` or `manage` | always | always, before any sharing |
| signed-in people who can view the part | yes | yes, unless the part is `shared_data_writers: "editors"` |
| guests on a **Can view** public link | yes | never |
| guests on a **Can contribute** public link | yes | yes, within the guest limits (T95) |

Set by the owner ("Data: view only" switch, T31) or by an agent at create or in `meta`. Setting `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes that link (T95 implements the link side; this task exposes the hook).

**Events:** `data.changed {key, op: "set" | "delete", by: {kind: "person" | "agent" | "guest", name}}` on `EventSource('/c/<cap>/_rt/events')` (T51's SSE), one per changed key, delivered to every other tab; also an `events` row (type `data.changed`, actor `user:<id>`/`conn:<id>`/`guest:<link>:<g>`).

## Not in scope

- `db.*` ops and `claude.use("db")`: T73 (P3). Data leases (`data_leases`): T73.
- Guest caps, guest limits, freeze, contribute link mode: T95. Snapshot engine (taking, scheduling, restoring): T77; this task exposes it as `part_data` actions.
- The `/_rt/events` SSE transport itself: T51. `localStorage` shim: T62.

## Design notes and decisions

- *Why `viewers` by default* (as in Claude): a poll or checklist works for everyone who can see it; a dashboard is made read-only with one switch (decision 43).
- *One key per independent item*: the contract tells authors to write once per action and use one key per cell, so two people never overwrite each other; CAS (`if_rev`) exists for agents that need it.
- *Per-key `data.changed`* (final-round F12 adjustment): a roll back emits one event per affected key, so pages repaint with no special code path.
- Reads count per request, not per key, so a 256-key board loads with one `list {values: true}` without tripping limits.
- At 95 % of the disk budget `/_rt` writes get `storage_full` (T114), reads continue.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Two browsers on one part see each other's shared writes within 1 s; a `view` grantee's write is refused with `forbidden_view_only` once the part is `shared_data_writers: editors`; a 256-key board loads with one `list {values: true}`; an agent reads the same document through `part_data` and rolls the data back with `snapshot_restore`".
- [ ] Every role row of the table above enforced in `/_rt` and in `part_data` (matrix test).
- [ ] Every limit returns its documented code: `invalid_input` (bad key), `too_large` (value), `quota_exceeded` (5 MiB shared / 256 KiB personal), `rate_limited` with `retry_after`, `storage_full`.
- [ ] `data.changed` reaches the other tab within 1 s; the writing tab does not receive its own echo.
- [ ] `part_data get` of a key written by `window.storage.set` returns `{doc: {collection: "__storage", doc_id, data, rev, updated_at, updated_by, provenance}, contains_untrusted}`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_storage_matrix.rs` (role × op × `shared_data_writers` table-driven); `::limits_each_code`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/shared_data_two_browsers.spec.ts`: two Chromium contexts, write in A, assert repaint in B < 1 s; logs `event="rt.op" op="storage.set"`, `event="data.changed" key fanout`.
- `tests/e2e/board_256_keys_one_list.spec.ts`: counts `/_rt/v1` requests via HAR (exactly one `list`).
- `crates/pf-ops/tests/part_data_op.rs::snapshot_restore_roundtrip`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Runtime calls `/_rt`; §3a role × runtime matrix, who writes shared data, shared-data limits; §3c Persistent state; §5e `data_docs`, `parts.shared_data_writers`; decision 31, 43; docs/agent-contract.md "Shared data from inside a part", `part_data`, Limits, "Who can write shared data".

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Two browsers on one part see each other's shared writes within 1 s; a `view` grantee's write is refused with `forbidden_view_only` once the part is `shared_data_writers: editors`; a 256-key board loads with one `list {values: true}`; an agent reads the same document through `part_data` and rolls the data back with `snapshot_restore`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
  - T77: Per-part data snapshots of shared docs: on by default (daily keep 7), roll back, reset, JSON download
- Unblocks: 
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
  - T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
  - T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T96.a: /_rt storage.* server ops: roles, shared_data_writers, limits, quotas, rate limits
  - T96.b: Prelude window.storage API, PfError rejections and live data.changed events
  - T96.c: part_data registry op: get/list/set/delete and snapshot_list/snapshot_restore/reset

title: T96.a: /_rt storage.* server ops: roles, shared_data_writers, limits, quotas, rate limits
description:
## Goal and why

The server half of `window.storage`: every `storage.get/getMany/set/delete/list` call over `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` (text/plain JSON `{op, args}`) is authorised from the cap and the role matrix, validated against the limits, and committed through the single writer.

## Scope

- Ops and args:
  - `storage.get {key, shared}` → `{key, value, shared}` or `null` (missing key is `null`, not an error).
  - `storage.getMany {keys (≤ 500), shared}` → array in order of `{key, value, shared}` or `null`.
  - `storage.set {key, value (string), shared}` → `{key, value, shared}`; `storage.delete {key, shared}` → `{key, deleted: true, shared}`.
  - `storage.list {prefix?, shared, cursor?, limit? (≤ 1000, default 1000), values?}` → `{keys, prefix, shared, next_cursor, values?}`; `next_cursor` null at the end; key order lexicographic by `doc_id`.
- Personal scope: `owner = <user id>` from the cap subject; public-link viewers and guests have no person, so personal ops for them are refused server side (the prelude keeps their personal storage memory-only).
- Authorisation: cap verified by T16/T15; role from cap `r`, `dw` claim, and `parts.shared_data_writers` (read per request from the cached part row): `forbidden_view_only` (403, `details.scope: "shared"`) for a view/comment grantee when `editors`, and for a Can-view link always.
- Limits: key 1–512 bytes UTF-8 no control chars (`invalid_input`), value ≤ 256 KiB (`too_large`, `details.limit`), shared total ≤ `parts.shared_data_cap` (5 MiB) and personal ≤ 256 KiB per person per part (`quota_exceeded {kind}`), rates via `governor`: writes 600/min per signed-in person per part, reads 600 requests/min per viewer per part (`rate_limited` + `retry_after`); guest/IP write limits plug in from T95. Disk budget 95 % → `storage_full`.
- Commit: single writer; `rev` increments; `updated_by` = `user:<id>` | `conn:<id>` | `link:<id>` | `guest:<link>:<g>`; append `events` row `data.changed` and publish to the in-memory broadcast (T51) — one per key.
- Errors are returned as `{error: {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}}` with catalogue codes (T20).
- First data write on a part starts the snapshot schedule (T77 hook).

## Not in scope

Prelude API (T96.b); `part_data` op (T96.c); guest caps (T95); `db.*` (T73).

## Design notes and decisions

- Shared bytes total is tracked incrementally in a per-part counter updated in the writer, not by `SUM()` per write.
- `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Mode` checks are T16/T62's; this layer trusts the verified principal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Matrix test covers owner, edit, view (viewers/editors), comment, Can-view link, render (via T80.b), each op.
- [ ] Each limit yields its exact code and HTTP status (400/413/429/403/507).
- [ ] 1,000 concurrent sets from 10 principals: all committed, `rev` strictly increasing per doc.

## Tests

`crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_storage_ops.rs`: `get_missing_is_null`, `getmany_order_and_500_cap`, `list_paging_cursor_values`, `matrix_shared_writers`, `limit_codes`, `concurrent_sets_rev_monotonic`. Asserts logs `event="rt.op" op principal outcome latency_us` and that no value appears in logs (canary).

## References

PLAN.md §2 `/_rt`; §3a limits and who writes; §3c `window.storage`; §5e `data_docs`, `parts.shared_data_cap`; docs/agent-contract.md Limits, `PfError`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

title: T96.b: Prelude window.storage API, PfError rejections and live data.changed events
description:
## Goal and why

Give page code Claude's exact `window.storage` API, plus paging and bulk reads, and a way to hear other people's writes so communal pages update live.

## Scope

In the prelude (shared blob, `crates/pf-prelude`):
- `window.storage.get(key, shared?)` → `{key, value, shared}` | `null`; `set(key, value, shared?)` (string value); `delete(key, shared?)`; `list(prefix?, shared?, options?)` → `{keys, prefix, shared, next_cursor, values?}` with options `{cursor, limit (≤ 1000, default 1000), values}`; the options object may stand in for `shared` as `{shared: true, …}`; `getMany(keys ≤ 500, shared?)` → array in order. `shared` defaults to `false` (personal).
- Failures reject with `PfError {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}`, `code` ∈ `rate_limited`, `forbidden_view_only`, `quota_exceeded`, `too_large`, `storage_full`, `invalid_input`, `forbidden`. `PfError` is a subclass of `Error` exposed as `window.PfError`.
- Transport: `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1`, `Content-Type: text/plain`, body `{op, args}` (CORS-simple; never a preflight).
- Personal storage for public-link viewers and guests is memory only (no server call).
- `window.partifactory.on("data.changed", fn)`: one shared `EventSource('/c/<cap>/_rt/events')` (T51); calls `fn({key, op: "set" | "delete", by: {kind, name}})` once per key written by another tab or person (`by.name` e.g. "Guest 4f2a"); own writes are suppressed (server tags events with a per-tab writer id carried in the request).
- Reconnect with backoff; on cap expiry follow the T62 `pf:regrant`/`refresh` path and resume.

## Not in scope

The `localStorage` shim (T62); server ops (T96.a).

## Design notes and decisions

- Matching Claude's signatures exactly is what makes copied artifacts run unchanged.
- Suppressing self-echo avoids double repaints and flicker on optimistic UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contract's pixel board (docs/agent-contract.md worked session) runs unmodified: paints, loads with paging, repaints on another tab's write.
- [ ] `PfError` fields present; `forbidden_view_only` surfaces on a view-only part.
- [ ] No `OPTIONS` request in any HAR.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-prelude/tests/storage_api.test.js` (jsdom or headless): signatures, options-in-place-of-shared, getMany order, rejection shapes.
- E2E `tests/e2e/data_changed_live.spec.ts`: two tabs, one writes, the other's handler fires < 1 s with correct `by.kind`; HAR asserts no preflight; server logs `event="sse.deliver" type="data.changed"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3c Persistent state (signatures); §2 prelude bullet on `partifactory.on`; docs/agent-contract.md "Shared data from inside a part", "When a call fails".

- Parent task: T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T96.a: /_rt storage.* server ops: roles, shared_data_writers, limits, quotas, rate limits

title: T96.c: part_data registry op: get/list/set/delete and snapshot_list/snapshot_restore/reset
description:
## Goal and why

Agents read and write the very documents a page uses, and undo bad writes from data snapshots without a person, as an inward action.

## Scope

Op `part_data` (registry, T20) fields (verbatim):

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | str | yes | — | |
| `action` | `get` \| `list` \| `set` \| `delete` \| `snapshot_list` \| `snapshot_restore` \| `reset` | yes | — | |
| `scope` | `shared` \| `personal` | no | `shared` | `personal` is your person's own data |
| `collection` | str | no | `__storage` | `__storage` holds `window.storage` keys |
| `doc_id` | str | for get, set, delete | — | for `__storage`, the key |
| `data` | JSON (a string in `__storage`) | for set | — | ≤ 256 KiB |
| `if_rev` | int | no | — | set and delete only if the doc is at this `rev`; `0` = must not exist |
| `prefix`, `cursor`, `limit` | str, str, int ≤ 1000 | no | —, —, `100` | list only |
| `snapshot_id` | int | for snapshot_restore | — | from `snapshot_list` |
| `confirm` | `true` | for reset | — | reset empties the part's shared data |
| `request_id` | str | for set, delete, snapshot_restore, reset | — | |

Outputs: get `{doc, contains_untrusted}`; list `{docs, next_cursor, contains_untrusted}`; set `{doc_id, rev}`; delete `{doc_id, deleted: true}`; snapshot_list `{snapshots, policy}`; snapshot_restore `{restored, before_snapshot_id, docs}`; reset `{before_snapshot_id, deleted}`; writes add `replayed: true` on replay. A `doc` is `{collection, doc_id, data, rev, updated_at, updated_by, provenance}` (`provenance` ∈ `person`, `agent`, `link_viewer`; guests are `link_viewer`); `contains_untrusted: true` when any doc came from someone other than the connection's person; MCP text wraps such data in `<untrusted_content>`. Snapshot `{id, taken_at, reason, docs, bytes}`, `reason` ∈ `scheduled`, `contribute`, `before_restore`, `before_reset`; `policy` `{mode, keep}`.

Errors: `invalid_input`, `unknown_field`, `not_found` (part, doc or snapshot), `forbidden` (`scope_needed` or `role_needed`), `forbidden_view_only`, `if_match_failed` (`collection`, `doc_id`, `current_rev`), `request_id_reused`, `too_large`, `quota_exceeded` (5 MiB shared per part, 256 KiB personal per person per part), `rate_limited`, `storage_full`.

Scopes: `data:read` for get/list, `data:write` for set/delete; `snapshot_list`, `snapshot_restore`, `reset` need `parts:write` and the person's `edit` role, act on **shared** data only, and take a snapshot first (via T77), so each is undoable. Restore/reset emit a `data.changed` per affected key so open pages repaint. Idempotency via the `idempotency` table (only committed writes use up a `request_id`).

## Not in scope

Snapshot taking/scheduling/storage (T77); other collections like `_assets` (T83) and `db` (T73).

## Design notes and decisions

- Agents may roll back because undoing vandalism stays inside the part (inward); Freeze stays the admin's (T95).
- `provenance` + `contains_untrusted` are prompt-injection hygiene (Rule 6 of the contract).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The contract's `snapshot_list` and `snapshot_restore` examples run as written (T57 scenario uses them).
- [ ] `if_rev: 0` on an existing doc → `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`.
- [ ] Guest-written docs come back `provenance: "link_viewer"`, `contains_untrusted: true`.
- [ ] Restore with an open tab: the tab repaints (one event per key).

## Tests

`crates/pf-ops/tests/part_data.rs`: `get_list_set_delete_roundtrip`, `if_rev_cas`, `scope_and_role_errors`, `snapshot_restore_takes_before_snapshot`, `reset_requires_confirm`, `replay_returns_replayed`, `untrusted_flag_for_guest_docs`. Logs: `event="op" op="part_data" action outcome`, never `data` values.

## References

PLAN.md §4 Slice 1 op fields (`part_data`); §5c data snapshots; §3c provenance; docs/agent-contract.md `part_data`, Rule 6.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T96.a: /_rt storage.* server ops: roles, shared_data_writers, limits, quotas, rate limits

title: T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
description:
## Goal and why

A public link has two modes: **Can view** (default) and **Can contribute**. Someone using a part through a Can-contribute link is a **guest**, like a passer-by drawing on a shared whiteboard: guests write the part's shared data and never change its code, files or versions, and hold no tokens. This is what lets a signed-out phone paint the pixel board in the `communal_pixel_editor` test (T97) while the admin can roll back, reset or freeze. On the S1 critical path (… T96 → T95 → T97 → S1).

*Why a separate mode, not a role:* a communal page is useless read-only, but nobody outside the house should touch its code. Splitting "use the data" from "change the part" gives both, and the snapshot taken at the switch makes a vandalised board one tap to undo (decision 31).

## Scope

Subtasks (this bead is the integration/closure bead; close only after all subtasks close and acceptance passes end to end):
- **T95.a** link `mode`, guest caps from `POST /l/<token>/go`, guest identity, guest/IP write limits, shared-data cap, the 403 wall on non-data ops and `/api`, `/mcp`.
- **T95.b** switching semantics: snapshot on switch (`reason: contribute`), `shared_data_writers` coupling, Freeze (minter epoch bump), audit + step-up.
- **T95.c** share-sheet controls (Can view / Can contribute, Roll back data, Reset data, Freeze, copy text), guest events and activity-feed counts.

Schema (from T06): `public_links.mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'view' CHECK (mode IN ('view','contribute'))`, `public_links.frozen_at INTEGER` (last Freeze; bumps `minter:link:<id>`), `parts.shared_data_cap INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5242880`. No guest table: a guest is a `public_links` row in `contribute` mode plus the signed `g` claim; writes are labelled `guest:<link>:<g>` in `data_docs.updated_by` and `events.actor`.

Guest rules (verbatim intent):
- **Can do**: write the part's shared data through `/_rt` data ops (`storage.*` shared; `db.*` from T73), and call the part's backend as `role: guest` (P2a).
- **Never**: change code, files or versions; create, edit or delete parts; see history or source; share; comment as a person. A guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`), or any `/api` or `/mcp` route, gets `403`. Runtime errors from guest tabs are not collected.
- **Identity**: `POST /l/<token>/go` mints a cap with subject `link:<id>`, the `dw` claim and a random guest id `g`, shown as "Guest 4f2a"; per tab, signed, no cookie.
- **Limits, on by default**: 60 writes/min per guest, 300 per IP (keyed on the trusted client-IP header), shared-data cap per part 5 MiB → `quota_exceeded`.
- **Switching** to Can contribute takes a data snapshot first and sets `shared_data_writers` to `viewers` (the sheet says so); setting a part to `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes that link (back to Can view).
- **Freeze** = back to Can view, bumps the link's minter epoch, so open guest tabs lose write on their next request.
- **Visibility**: guest writes are `data.changed` events with actor `guest:<link>:<g>`; activity feed counts them ("14 guest edits today").
- **Copy**: "Anyone with the link can use it. Only you and people you add can change it."
- Admin-only with step-up (10-minute window): making a public link and switching it to Can contribute.

## Design notes and decisions

- Guest id as a signed claim inside the link cap (round 2c interpretation): a guest can't pick another guest's id; a forged or replayed `g` fails the MAC.
- A guest never has more than a signed-in viewer: hence the `editors` → freeze coupling.
- Rolling back and resetting are also agent ops (`part_data`), Freeze is the admin's.
- Freeze via the minter epoch (not the part epoch) keeps signed-in viewers' caps valid.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Switching to contribute creates a `data_snapshots` row with `reason = 'contribute'` (outside `keep`) and sets `shared_data_writers = 'viewers'`.
- [ ] Setting `editors` while contribute is active flips the link to view and bumps its minter epoch.
- [ ] Click budgets: Can-contribute link + copy = 4 (+1 biometric); Freeze = 2 with undo toast; Roll back data = 3 with undo toast.

Logs: `event="rt.op" principal="guest:l_..:4f2a" outcome="forbidden"`, `event="epoch.bump" key="minter:link:<id>"`.

title: T95.a: Guest caps from /l/<token>/go, guest identity, write limits and the non-data 403 wall
description:
## Goal and why

Turn a contribute-mode public link into per-tab guest identities that can write shared data and nothing else.

## Scope

- `POST /l/<token>/go` (on the part host, T29) for a link with `mode = 'contribute'`: mint a cap `{s: "link:<id>", r: 0, dw: true, g: <random guest id>, m: "link:<id>", me: epoch[minter:link:<id>], …}`; guest id is random 32 bits shown as "Guest " + 4 hex chars (e.g. "Guest 4f2a"); for `mode = 'view'` no `dw`, no `g`. Counting the open (`open_count`, `last_opened_at`) stays T29's.
- `/_rt` enforcement for link subjects:
  - with `dw`: shared `storage.*` reads and writes allowed (subject to T96.a limits); personal storage memory only (prelude) and refused server side.
  - without `dw` (Can view): shared reads only; writes → `forbidden_view_only`.
  - any non-data op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) → `403 forbidden`.
- Guests hold no token: `/api` and `/mcp` already require bearer tokens; add a test that a guest's context (cookies none, cap only) gets 401/403 there and that a cap in a bearer header is rejected.
- Limits (`governor`): 60 writes/min per guest (`g`), 300/min per client IP (trusted header, T89/T30) → `rate_limited` + `retry_after`; shared total ≥ `parts.shared_data_cap` → `quota_exceeded {kind: "shared_data"}`.
- `updated_by` / `events.actor` = `guest:<link>:<g>`; `data.changed.by = {kind: "guest", name: "Guest 4f2a"}`.

## Not in scope

Snapshot and freeze semantics (T95.b); UI (T95.c).

## Design notes and decisions

- The guest id lives where the cap lives (wrapper sessionStorage, prelude memory): per tab, no cookie, unforgeable.
- Errors reports from guest tabs aren't collected to deny a spam channel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each non-data op returns 403 for a guest cap; data ops succeed.
- [ ] Can-view cap shared write → `forbidden_view_only`.
- [ ] 61st write in a minute from one guest → 429; 301st from one IP across guests → 429.
- [ ] Editing the `g` claim breaks the MAC → 404 (unknown/bad MAC looks like not found).

## Tests

`crates/pf-serve/tests/guest_caps.rs::{go_mints_dw_and_g, view_mode_no_dw, non_data_op_403_each, per_guest_limit, per_ip_limit, forged_g_bad_mac, quota_exceeded_shared_cap}`; property test `guest_cap_never_grants_non_data`. Logs asserted: `event="cap.mint" subject_kind="link" dw=true`, never the cap itself.

## References

PLAN.md §3a "Can contribute" (Guest identity, Limits); §2 cap payload (`dw`, `g`); §7 Guests.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

- [ ] 61st write in a minute from one guest → 429; 301st from one IP across guests → 429.
- [ ] Editing the `g` claim breaks the MAC → 404 (unknown/bad MAC looks like not found).

title: T95.b: Contribute switching: snapshot first, shared_data_writers coupling, Freeze via minter epoch
description:
## Goal and why

Make every transition of a link's mode safe and undoable: there is always a "before the guests" snapshot, and Freeze cuts off open guest tabs immediately.

## Scope

Session-only handlers (people-only actions, no registry op; the chrome API `/api/chrome/v1/<part>/…` and the workspace share sheet both call them), admin + step-up within 10 minutes:
- `link.set_mode {link_id, mode: "contribute"}`: in one writer transaction: take an on-demand data snapshot via T77 (`reason = 'contribute'`, outside `keep`), set `public_links.mode = 'contribute'`, set `parts.shared_data_writers = 'viewers'` if it was `editors`; audit rows `link.mode` (before → after) and `part.shared_data_writers` when changed.
- `link.freeze {link_id}`: `mode = 'view'`, `frozen_at = now`, bump `epochs['minter:link:<id>']` (in memory + SQLite) so open guest caps fail on their next request; open viewers re-go through `/l/<token>/go` and get a view cap; audit `link.freeze`; undo (10 s toast) = set mode back to contribute (which takes another snapshot).
- Hook from T96/T31 `meta.shared_data_writers = "editors"`: if any active contribute link exists, freeze it (same path) and tell the caller.
- Roll back and Reset on the sheet call T77's restore/reset (snapshot first), same as `part_data`.

## Not in scope

The snapshot engine (T77); link creation and revoke (T29); the sheet UI (T95.c).

## Design notes and decisions

- Minter-epoch bump revokes only that link's caps, not people's.
- Freeze is the admin's, not an agent op: it's an outward-facing control.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Switch → snapshot row `reason=contribute` exists and `shared_data_writers='viewers'`.
- [ ] Freeze → an already-open guest tab's next write fails (cap stale), and a fresh open gets a view-only cap.
- [ ] `editors` while contribute active → link frozen, audit row written.
- [ ] Without fresh step-up → `step_up_required` (403).

## Tests

`crates/pf-policy/tests/contribute_switch.rs::{switch_takes_snapshot, switch_sets_viewers, freeze_bumps_minter_epoch, editors_freezes_link, step_up_required}`; E2E part in T95's `contribute_link.spec.ts`. Logs: `event="audit" action="link.freeze"`, `event="epoch.bump"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3a Undo and control, "Who may write shared data"; §5c data snapshots (on-demand outside `keep`); §5e `public_links.frozen_at`, `data_snapshots.reason`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T95.a: Guest caps from /l/<token>/go, guest identity, write limits and the non-data 403 wall

- [ ] Switch → snapshot row `reason=contribute` exists and `shared_data_writers='viewers'`.
- [ ] Freeze → an already-open guest tab's next write fails (cap stale), and a fresh open gets a view-only cap.
- [ ] `editors` while contribute active → link frozen, audit row written.
- [ ] Without fresh step-up → `step_up_required` (403).

title: T95.c: Share-sheet contribute controls (Roll back, Reset, Freeze), copy, guest activity counts
description:
## Goal and why

The admin controls guests from the share sheet in a few taps, with honest copy and undo instead of confirmations.

## Scope

On the "Anyone with the link" rung of the share sheet (T31 builds the sheet):
- Mode segmented control **`Can view` (default) · `Can contribute`**; under Can contribute the copy "Anyone with the link can use it. Only you and people you add can change it." and a note that switching makes data writable by viewers (sets `shared_data_writers` to `viewers`).
- While contribute is on: **Roll back data** (snapshot list, newest preselected → Restore; undo toast), **Reset data** (snapshotted first; undo toast), **Freeze** (undo toast). Comments for link viewers need the separate opt-in (not this task).
- In-sheet step-up ("Confirm it's you" with an inline passkey button, then the action completes after the biometric, no navigation).
- Deep link `#share=contribute` (T117) opens this rung pre-filled; nothing saved until confirmed.
- Activity feed and the sheet show guest counts from `events` with actor `guest:*` ("14 guest edits today").
- Stockroom styling: amber only for the public rung; danger for Reset.

## Not in scope

Sheet layout, other rungs, public-link URL/copy/open count/revoke (T31/T29).

## Design notes and decisions

- Budgets (§4a.7): Can-contribute + Copy **4** (+1 biometric); Freeze **2**, undo toast; Roll back data **3** (newest preselected), undo toast. Revocations/destructive actions use a 10 s undo toast, never a confirm dialog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] e2e counts interactions for each flow and matches the budgets.
- [ ] Undo after Freeze restores contribute mode.
- [ ] Guest-edit count increments after guest writes.
- [ ] Contrast test passes for the new states (amber/danger tokens).

## Tests

`tests/e2e/share_sheet_contribute.spec.ts`: `contribute_and_copy_budget_4`, `freeze_budget_2_undo`, `rollback_budget_3_preselected`, `reset_snapshots_first`, `guest_count_visible`. Visual regression screenshots light/dark/360 px. Server logs captured per SPEC convention.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Share sheet rung 5; §4a.7 click budgets; §3a Visibility, Share-sheet copy; §4a.9 copy voice.

title: T108: Insights UI (admin-only, Stockroom): Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds pages with table views and CSV/JSON export
description:
## Goal and why

"Insights is where the admin sees what's used, what agents do, and why something broke, without leaving partifactory." This task builds the analytics pages over the Insights store (T105): what agents call and how often they fail, which kinds and build methods are used, what's viewed, whether deep links handed to people get acted on. It is admin-only and first-party (no third-party analytics), and every chart is accessible (table view, contrast, light and dark) and exportable.

After Slice 1 (P2; feeds T109, T110 and M2 via T109). Depends on T105 (data), T31 (workspace UI shell and Stockroom components), T44 (device-grant connections, so per-connection agent pages have real connection kinds).

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close after all subtasks close and acceptance passes end to end):
- `T108.a` — Insights shell under `/admin/insights` (admin-only, 404 for others), the shared chart/table component with the dataviz rules, CSV/JSON export, and the **Overview** page.
- `T108.b` — the **Agents** and **Builds** pages.
- `T108.c` — the **Parts** and **People** pages (guests only in aggregate).

Pages, verbatim from the plan (§5g), with this task's scope noted:

| Page | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | parts created and edited per day; active parts; views; active people; guests; agents active; errors; build success rate; disk use against the budget; backup layer status |
| **Agents** | per connection: calls over time by op and by surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI); the error codes it hits most; `part_check` pass rate; median time from create to first good build; kinds and **build methods** it uses over time (server build vs prebuilt files vs images; frontend-only vs backend); deep links handed out (`part_link_for`) and how many were acted on |
| **Parts** | kinds over time; build methods over time; share of parts with a backend; top parts by views and edits; stale parts; largest parts; data-snapshot use; public links (by mode) and their opens; guest writes |
| **People** | who's active, views per person, invites sent and accepted, sign-in failures. Guests only in aggregate |
| **Builds** | queue and duration percentiles; failures by error class; toolchain versions; BuildKit cache hit rate |

The **Backends** page is T110. The Debug tab, per-agent call page, trace waterfall and log viewer are T109.

Rules: "Stockroom style; charts follow the dataviz rules, each with a table view, light and dark; every chart exports as CSV or JSON". Admin area nav (§4a.6): "People · Groups · Invites · Agents · Public links · Backends · Audit · Health · Insights". Colours from the `--pf-*` tokens (signal green for the one action colour, agent blue for agents, amber reserved for "Public link" only), contrast test from §4a.9 ("A contrast test in CI parses `tokens.css` and asserts every pair … fails under 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for `rule-strong`").

## Not in scope

Backends page (T110), Debug/trace/log UI (T109), the store (T105), metric collection for BuildKit (P2a; the Builds page shows "no backend builds yet" until then), alerts (T121).

## Design notes and decisions

- Reads go to `rollups_daily` for ranges beyond 30 days and to `events_raw` for drill-downs within 30 days; queries run on the insights read pool, never the main writer.
- "Deep links handed out and how many were acted on": `part_link_for` calls are `op` events; "acted on" = the corresponding share-sheet action (public link created / contribute switched, invite minted …) on the same part within 7 days by the admin, recorded as a `grant_decision`/UI event (F26: "T108 counts deep links, not share requests" — there are no request queues).
- "Create to first good build" = `part_create` event → first `build` event with status ok for that part.
- Guests: never individually listed; only counts (distinct `viewer_key`/`g` per day).
- No part content anywhere: titles shown come from the main DB at render time (admin is allowed to see titles); nothing content-like is stored in insights.db.
- Light and dark from the same tokens; charts render server-side as SVG or with a small island — follow the T02 Leptos-vs-templates decision.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each page renders from a fixture and matches its counts; a non-admin gets 404; every chart has a table view and passes the contrast test."

- [ ] Overview, Agents, Parts, People and Builds render from a fixture insights.db and every count matches the fixture's expected values.
- [ ] Any non-admin (including signed-in household members and agent tokens) gets 404 on every `/admin/insights` route and API.
- [ ] Every chart has a table view and CSV and JSON export with the same numbers.
- [ ] Light and dark pass the contrast test; colour is never the only signal.
- [ ] Guests appear only in aggregate.

## Tests

See subtasks; plus `tests/e2e/insights_pages.spec.ts` (admin with virtual authenticator visits each page in light/dark at 360 px and desktop, toggles table view, downloads CSV/JSON and compares to fixture; a household user gets 404); visual regression screenshots per PR; logs under `target/e2e-logs/insights_pages/` assert `event="http.request" route_class="admin.insights" outcome="ok"` and `outcome="not_found"` for the non-admin.

## References

PLAN.md §5g Insights (rules, pages); §4a.6 Admin; §4a.3 tokens and contrast; §4a.9 build notes; §6 P2; decision 32; final-round F26.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Each page renders from a fixture and matches its counts; a non-admin gets 404; every chart has a table view and passes the contrast test
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T105: Insights store: separate insights.db, content-free events_raw, salted viewer keys, daily rollups
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
- Unblocks: 
  - T109: Debugging UI: trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab (incl. denying decisions), per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail
  - T110: Backend observability: per-part log rings, restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN; Backends page
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T108.a: Insights shell (admin-only 404 gate), accessible chart+table component, CSV/JSON export, Overview page
  - T108.b: Insights Agents and Builds pages (calls by op and surface, error codes, part_check pass rate, deep links acted on)
  - T108.c: Insights Parts and People pages (kinds, top parts, public links by mode, guests only in aggregate)

title: T108.b: Insights Agents and Builds pages (calls by op and surface, error codes, part_check pass rate, deep links acted on)
description:
## Goal and why

Show the admin how each agent connection actually uses partifactory and where builds go wrong — the feedback loop for tuning the agent contract and the toolchain.

## Scope

**Agents** (per connection, "<agent> for <person>"): calls over time by op and by surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI); the error codes it hits most; `part_check` pass rate; median time from create to first good build; kinds and build methods it uses over time (server build vs prebuilt files vs images; frontend-only vs backend); deep links handed out (`part_link_for`) and how many were acted on (the matching admin action on that part within 7 days).

**Builds**: queue and duration percentiles; failures by error class (e.g. `mirror_failed` by reason, `builder_crashed`, timeout, compile errors); toolchain versions; BuildKit cache hit rate (P2a data; empty state before).

Both pages link a connection row to its per-agent call page (T109) when that exists.

## Not in scope

The per-agent last-100-calls page (T109); Backends page (T110).

## Design notes and decisions

- Data from `events_raw` kinds `op` (with `attrs.arg_keys`), `build` (`attrs.build_method`, `attrs.kind`), and `rollups_daily` dims `conn:<id>`, `op:<name>`, `method:<m>`.
- Percentiles computed from raw events within 30 days; beyond that, rollups hold p50/p95 as metrics (recommended: add `build_ms_p50`/`build_ms_p95` rollup metrics in T105.b's rollup job).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each chart's counts match the fixture.
- [ ] Deep links handed out vs acted on are computed as specified.
- [ ] Each chart has table view and CSV/JSON export.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-ui/tests/insights_agents.rs::calls_by_op_and_surface`, `::top_error_codes`, `::part_check_pass_rate`, `::create_to_first_good_build_median`, `::deep_links_acted_on`.
- `crates/pf-ui/tests/insights_builds.rs::duration_percentiles`, `::failures_by_class`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g pages (Agents, Builds); §3g build methods; §4 `part_link_for`; final-round F26.
