title: T109: Debugging UI: trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab (incl. denying decisions), per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail
description:
## Goal and why

Answer "why did they get a 403?", "why is this page broken?" and "what is this agent doing?" from the workspace, in a few clicks, without shell access. It is the UI over the request ids and traces (T106), log segments (T107), Insights (T108) and MCP activity (T53).

After Slice 1 (P2, feeds M2 and T110). Click budget (§4a.7): "Find why someone got a 403 (the admin) | ⋯ → Debug → the request | **3**".

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close after both subtasks close and acceptance passes end to end):
- `T109.a` — the trace waterfall and the log viewer (filters, live tail, download range).
- `T109.b` — the per-part Debug tab and the per-agent connection page.

Verbatim from §5g Debugging:
- "**Traces**: … The UI draws a **trace waterfall** for any kept request."
- "**The per-part Debug tab** (admin): recent requests (status, latency, surface, actor), builds with their logs, browser runtime errors (with version), backend logs (tail and search), events, and **the cap and grant decisions that denied access**, so 'why did they get a 403?' has an answer."
- "**The per-agent connection page**: the last 100 calls with their request and response shapes (op, argument keys and sizes, never values), errors and latency."
- "**The log viewer**: structured JSON logs, filtered by level, part, agent or request id, with live tail and 'download range'."
- From the dag2.py title: "a log viewer (filter by level, part, agent, request id; live tail; download a range)".
- Entry points: the wrapper's ⋯ menu "Debug (admin, §5g)"; the 403/500 error pages show the request id ("It's been logged as `req 8f1c…`"); Admin → Insights.
- Backend logs in the Debug tab come with T110 (this task leaves the slot).

## Not in scope

Persisting traces and logs (T106, T107), Insights pages (T108), backend logs/metrics (T110), runtime log-level switching (T36).

## Design notes and decisions

- "Denying decisions": the policy engine (T26) and cap verifier (T15/T16) emit `grant_decision` events with outcome and reason codes (`no_grant`, `stale_epoch`, `window_over`, `wrong_host`, `bad_mac`, `role_insufficient`, `view_only`) into `events_raw` (T105) and as span fields; the Debug tab lists them with the request id, subject and the grants considered (ids and roles only).
- Admin-only; non-admins get 404. The per-agent page must show **no argument values** — only keys and sizes — enforced by the type of what's stored (T105) and tested here.
- Live tail uses SSE from the workspace host (admin session), fed by an in-process log broadcast after redaction.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "From a 403 page's request id, the admin reaches the denying decision in 3 clicks; the agent page shows no argument values (test); live tail shows a new line within 1 s."

- [ ] 403 → ⋯ → Debug → the request shows the denying decision (≤ 3 counted interactions in e2e).
- [ ] Any kept trace renders as a waterfall with span names, offsets and durations.
- [ ] Per-agent page lists the last 100 calls with op, arg keys, sizes, errors, latency; no values (test with canaries).
- [ ] Log viewer filters by level, part, agent and request id; live tail shows a new line within 1 s; download range equals `logs export` output.
- [ ] All routes admin-only.

## Tests

See subtasks; e2e `tests/e2e/debug_403.spec.ts`: a household user opens a part they lack, the test reads the request id, then the admin follows ⋯ → Debug → the request with the click counter asserting 3 and the page showing `reason=no_grant`; artifacts in `target/e2e-logs/debug_403/`; server log asserts `event="grant.decision" outcome="deny" reason="no_grant" request_id=<id>`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g Debugging; §4a.6 part view ⋯ menu and error pages; §4a.7 click budgets ("Find why someone got a 403"); §6 P2.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): From a 403 page's request id, the admin reaches the denying decision in 3 clicks; the agent page shows no argument values (test); live tail shows a new line within 1 s
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
  - T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters
  - T108: Insights UI (admin-only, Stockroom): Overview, Agents, Parts, People, Builds pages with table views and CSV/JSON export
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - T110: Backend observability: per-part log rings, restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN; Backends page
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T109.a: Trace waterfall and log viewer (level/part/agent/request-id filters, live tail, download range)
  - T109.b: Per-part Debug tab (requests, builds, runtime errors, events, denying decisions) and per-agent call page

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Log event name for denying decisions: `event="policy.decide" outcome="deny" reason=…` (T26's) and `event="cap.verify" outcome=…` (T15/T16's); this task only reads them.
- The e2e that reads the request id from the 403 page: this task adds the mono `req r_…` line to the `403 · NOT SHARED WITH YOU` page (§5g: ids are on error pages; §4a.6 lists it only on 500) unless T27 already renders it. The 3-click budget count starts on the part host where the person was denied.
acceptance_criteria: From a 403 page's request id, the admin reaches the denying decision in 3 clicks; the agent page shows no argument values (test); live tail shows a new line within 1 s

title: T117: part_link_for deep links (public_link, contribute) and the share sheet reading #share=
description:
## Goal and why

Agents act directly within their scopes, but a short list of actions is people-only: public links, contribute links, invites, groups, everyone-signed-in, LAN access, admin. Instead of an approval queue, an agent calls `part_link_for` and hands its person a link that opens the right sheet pre-filled; the person decides there or doesn't, and partifactory stores nothing pending. In Slice 1 the actions are `public_link` and `contribute` (the pixel test's "make it contributable" step). *Why a deep link, not a queue:* a queue adds a second place to look and stalls the agent; a deep link costs the same one tap in the conversation the person is already in (decision 34).

## Scope

Op `part_link_for` (registry, T20):

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `public_link` \| `contribute` | yes | — | a public view-only link, or one guests can contribute to |
| `name` | str | yes | — | |

- Output `{action, url, who}`: `url` is `https://<name>-part.<domain>/#share=public` or `#share=contribute`; `who` is `"admin"` for both.
- Errors: `invalid_input` (an action that doesn't exist yet; the message lists the actions that exist), `not_found`, `forbidden`.
- Scope `parts:read`; every connection may call it whoever its person is; read-only hints. The link grants nothing by itself.
- Share sheet (T31) reads the fragment: `#share=public` opens the "Anyone with the link" rung, `#share=contribute` the same rung with Can contribute selected; nothing is saved until the person confirms; the wrapper (T29) keeps a `#share=` fragment in `sessionStorage` across the `/grant` hop and re-applies it after the cap is read.
- Opened by someone without the right: the normal sheet without that option, or the normal 403 if they can't see the part.
- Schema test: there is no request table or queue (`share_requests` must not exist; the only pending-person state is `access_asks`).

## Not in scope

Actions `group`, `everyone`, `admin` (T125), `invite` (T94), `lan` (T102). Public link creation itself (T29) and the contribute controls (T95).

## Design notes and decisions

- Contract Rule 4/5: the link is for a person to tap, never to post; if the person isn't the admin, the agent tells them only the admin can do this and to send the admin the link.
- Insights (T108) later counts deep links handed out and acted on.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each action returns a link that opens the share sheet pre-filled in the e2e suite; the link itself grants nothing (a person without the right sees the normal 403); there is no request table or queue to write to (schema test)".
- [ ] Signed-out open of `#share=contribute` → sign-in → wrapper → sheet opens on the rung (fragment survived).
- [ ] Non-admin person opening it sees the sheet without the public rung.

## Tests

`crates/pf-ops/tests/part_link_for.rs::{public_link_url, contribute_url, unknown_action_lists_actions, not_found_outside_spaces}`; `crates/pf-db/tests/schema_no_queue.rs::no_share_requests_table`; `tests/e2e/deep_link_share.spec.ts::{fragment_survives_grant_hop, prefilled_nothing_saved, non_admin_no_public_rung}` with logs `op=part_link_for outcome=ok`.

## References

PLAN.md §4 Ops table (`part_link_for`), "No notifications for people, and no approval queues"; §3b Agent sharing; §2 first-open flow (fragment kept); decision 34; docs/agent-contract.md `part_link_for`, Rules 4–5.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Each action returns a link that opens the share sheet pre-filled in the e2e suite; the link itself grants nothing (a person without the right sees the normal 403); there is no request table or queue to write to (schema test)
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T20: Operation registry crate (pf-ops): typed ops, scopes, hints, executable examples, one error catalogue
  - T29: Part-host root: trusted wrapper page, chrome API + CORS, /p/<name>, admin-only public links
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
- Unblocks: 
  - T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
  - T125: part_link_for after Slice 1: group, everyone and admin actions
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)

title: T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
description:
## Goal and why

The device grant is the default for headless agents (Hermes, the `part` CLI): "there's no secret to copy, and approval happens on the person's phone with a passkey." It is how the pixel-board agent connects in Slice 1 (T97: "an agent connected by device code creates the board"), and how each household member pairs with a shared chat agent once, giving one connection per (agent, person). In Slice 1 and on M2's critical household loop.

## Scope

- Client: one pre-registered public client `part-cli` used by every device-code agent; no per-agent client ids in Slice 1. The agent names itself with `agent_name` (required, ≤ 40 chars) and `software`.
- `POST /oauth/device_authorization` (form-encoded, JSON response): `client_id=part-cli`, `scope`, `agent_name`, `software`. Response:
```
{"device_code":"…","user_code":"KMQT-4XRA","verification_uri":"https://parts.<domain>/device",
 "verification_uri_complete":"https://parts.<domain>/device?code=KMQT-4XRA","expires_in":600,"interval":5}
```
- Codes: `device_code` is 32 random bytes (stored as `device_hash`); `user_code` 8 characters from `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, shown `XXXX-XXXX`; `expires_in` 600 s, `interval` 5 s. Polling faster → `slow_down` (+5 s). The CLI also prints a terminal QR.
- `/oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`: responses `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied`, `expired_token`; success = the T43 token shape. Codes are single use (`status` → `consumed`).
- `device_codes` table: `device_hash, user_code UNIQUE, client_id, agent_name, software, req_scopes, req_geo, status ('pending','approved','denied','expired','consumed'), connection_id, interval_s DEFAULT 5, last_poll_at, created_at, expires_at`.
- `/device` approval page (any signed-in person, for their own connection), T43.c consent sheet plus: the code in big mono with "Make sure this matches what the agent shows"; "**This device says** it is *Hermes* (hermes/1.4)", labelled unverified; coarse origin (country + network from trusted proxy headers or a local GeoIP database; "origin unknown" when neither is configured) and age ("requested 14 s ago"); scopes as toggles; space picker; lifetime (default 90 days); **Allow / Deny**.
- Allow needs a partifactory passkey assertion when the person has one (the admin always does); a person with none approves with their signed-in session alone (from T94 the page offers to register one).
- Phishing defences: when the request is over 2 minutes old, or (where origin is known) comes from a different network than the approving browser, a banner: "Only approve if you just asked an agent to connect". Typing a code by hand is limited to 5 attempts per minute per session.
- Each approval creates its own `agent_connections` row (`kind='device'`), so each (agent, person) is revoked separately. Two people pairing Hermes → two connections "Hermes for <person>".
- `part login` in the CLI (T22) drives this flow and refreshes its own token.

## Not in scope

Service identities (`principal_kind = service`, the Nest): moved to T64. Token rotation itself: T43. Hermes skill: T58. Passkey registration for people without one: T94.

## Design notes and decisions

- Codes are random, single use, short-lived; the user code alphabet avoids vowels and look-alikes.
- "A person connects every agent once, by design": there is no unattended bootstrap.
- Origin hint is optional (portability §5f "Device-connect origin"): without it the different-network banner can't fire, the age banner still does.
- Click budget: "Connect a headless agent on the phone | tap link in chat → Allow → biometric | 3"; "Pair yourself with a chat agent | "connect me" in chat → open link → Allow + passkey".
- Signed-out visit to `/device?code=` → sign in → return to the page with the code filled.

## Acceptance criteria

title: T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
description:
## Goal and why

`communal_pixel_editor` is **the** acceptance test of Slice 1 (milestone S1) and of P2 (M2). Slice 1 is frozen as exactly what this test needs, because the pixel board exercises every risky layer at once: the sandbox, caps, builds, agents, guests, live data and rollback. Shipping it end to end proves the core before anything is built on top. It runs in CI on every PR, on the T24 harness, and in the portability lane (T93).

## Scope

Subtasks (this bead is the integration/closure bead; close only after all subtasks close and the whole test passes in CI and in the portability lane):
- **T97.a** test scaffolding and the agent half: a scripted agent connected by device code creates the board in one `part_create`, `part_check`s it with `actions`, posts `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`.
- **T97.b** the admin half on Chromium with the virtual authenticator: sign-in, Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy with in-sheet step-up; later Roll back one snapshot and Freeze; click budgets asserted.
- **T97.c** the guest half on a mobile WebKit profile: signed-out open of the public link, paint, the admin's open tab updates within 1 s, and after Freeze the guest's next write is refused; plus wiring into CI on every PR and the portability lane.

The scenario (Slice 1 definition of done, item 1, verbatim): "an agent connected by device code creates the board in one `part_create`, runs `part_check`, posts `https://pixel-part.<domain>/`; the admin does Share → Anyone with the link → Can contribute → Copy (4 interactions + 1 biometric); a signed-out browser paints and the admin's open tab shows it within 1 s; the admin rolls back one snapshot and freezes the link, and the guest's next write is refused."

Environment: the T24 harness — Dex as OIDC provider, Caddy with an internal-CA wildcard cert for `pf.test`, `--host-resolver-rules` for Chromium and `/etc/hosts` for WebKit; workspace `https://parts.pf.test`, part host `https://pixel-part.pf.test`; render sidecar on (compose profile); published compose file with `_FILE` secrets in the portability lane.

The board: the exact HTML from docs/agent-contract.md's worked session (16×16 grid, `px:x:y` keys, colour validated against `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i`, `list("px:", true, {values: true})` paging, `partifactory.on("data.changed")`, `partifactory.ready()`), sent with `kind: "html"`, `name: "pixel"`, `live: "after_check"`.

## Not in scope

The backend variant `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (T104, P2a). The manual run on the example deployment with a real phone (Slice 1 done-item 2, recorded under T38's real-device pass).

## Design notes and decisions

- The agent drives the HTTP API or MCP with a device-code token (no browser OAuth flow needed — decision 37); the device approval itself is done in the admin's Chromium context (Allow + passkey).
- Interaction counting uses the shared §4a.7 budget helper (counts `click`/`press`/WebAuthn events along the scripted path), so a UI regression fails CI.
- Live-update latency (< 1 s) is measured from the guest's `/_rt` write response to the admin tab's repaint (polling the cell's computed style), with timestamps in the logs.
- Rollback uses the newest pre-paint snapshot (the one taken on the switch to Can contribute, `reason: contribute`), so the board ends empty: a deterministic assertion.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Runs in CI on every PR on the T24 harness and in the portability lane: the admin's steps (sign-in, step-up, share, roll back, freeze) on Chromium with the virtual authenticator, the signed-out guest on a mobile WebKit profile; the admin's interactions match the §4a.7 budget".
- [ ] Agent: one `part_create` → `head: 1`; `part_check` passes with `errors: []`, `blank: false`, and a click + `eval_return` returns the colour while the real data stays empty.
- [ ] Admin: Can-contribute link created in 4 interactions + 1 biometric; Freeze 2; Roll back 3.
- [ ] Guest paint visible in the admin tab within 1 s; `part_data list` shows the doc with `provenance: "link_viewer"`.
- [ ] After roll back the board is empty in both tabs; after Freeze the guest's next `storage.set` rejects (`PfError`), and the cell reverts.
- [ ] Required check in CI on every PR; passes in the portability lane with no vendor settings.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts` (Playwright projects `chromium-admin`, `webkit-mobile-guest`) plus `tests/e2e/agents/pixel_agent.rs` (or `.ts`) for the agent driver. Per SPEC logging: `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor/server.jsonl`, Playwright traces, HAR and screenshots on failure; the test asserts log events in order: `op=part_create outcome=ok`, `event=render.job purpose=gate outcome=ok`, `event=live.switch`, `event=audit action=link.mode`, `event=rt.op principal=guest:* op=storage.set`, `event=data.changed`, `event=data.restore`, `event=epoch.bump key=minter:link:*`, `event=rt.op principal=guest:* outcome=stale_epoch|forbidden`.

## References

PLAN.md "Slice 1: what ships first" (Definition of done 1); §6 P2 Done when (the five steps); §4a.7 budgets; §3a contribute links; §4c part_check; docs/agent-contract.md worked session; decisions 31, 35.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes, on the Slice 1 critical path. Priority P0.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Runs in CI on every PR on the T24 harness and in the portability lane: the admin's steps (sign-in, step-up, share, roll back, freeze) on Chromium with the virtual authenticator, the signed-out guest on a mobile WebKit profile; the admin's interactions match the §4a.7 budget
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
  - T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - S1: Milestone - Slice 1 ships (communal_pixel_editor end to end)
  - T104: Named e2e test `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (Postgres leaderboard) on Docker and Podman
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T97.a: Pixel test scaffolding and the agent half: device code, part_create, part_check, link
  - T97.b: Pixel test admin half: Chromium + virtual authenticator, contribute link, roll back, freeze, budgets
  - T97.c: Pixel test guest half on mobile WebKit, live-update timing, CI and portability-lane wiring
acceptance_criteria: Runs in CI on every PR on the T24 harness and in the portability lane: the admin's steps (sign-in, step-up, share, roll back, freeze) on Chromium with the virtual authenticator, the signed-out guest on a mobile WebKit profile; the admin's interactions match the §4a.7 budget

title: T97.a: Pixel test scaffolding and the agent half: device code, part_create, part_check, link
description:
## Goal and why

Build the shared fixture for `communal_pixel_editor` and script the agent's side exactly as the contract's worked session describes, so the test proves an agent can make and verify a communal app in one call plus a check.

## Scope

- Fixture `tests/e2e/fixtures/pixel.ts`: boots the T24 harness (or attaches to the portability-lane stack), seeds Dex users (the admin, one household user), resets `/data` between runs, opens log capture to `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor/`.
- Agent driver (MCP via `rmcp` client, or HTTP; parametrised): device grant `POST /oauth/device_authorization` (`client_id=part-cli`, `agent_name="Pixel test agent"`, `scope=parts:read parts:write data:read data:write`), hand `verification_uri_complete` to the admin's Chromium context, which taps Allow + virtual passkey; poll `/oauth/token` honouring `interval`/`slow_down`.
- `part_create {title:"Pixel board", name:"pixel", kind:"html", content: <board.html>, live:"after_check", request_id}` → expect `url = https://pixel-part.pf.test/`, `head: 1`.
- `part_check {name:"pixel", actions:[{do:"click",selector:"#b i"},{do:"wait_ms",ms:300},{do:"eval_return",expr:"window.storage.get('px:0:0', true).then(r => r && r.value)"}]}` → `errors: []`, `blank: false`, `actions[2].value = "#e4572e"`; then `part_data list prefix "px:"` → `docs: []` (overlay discarded); `part_get` shows `live: 1`.
- Return the posted link to the next phase.

## Not in scope

Admin share/rollback/freeze (T97.b); guest (T97.c).

## Design notes and decisions

The board HTML is kept as a fixture file copied verbatim from docs/agent-contract.md (with the fixed `load()` call) so the contract example and the test can't drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent half passes on MCP and on HTTP drivers.
- [ ] `live` moves only after the gate check passes.

## Tests

`communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts › agent creates and checks the board`; logs asserted: `op=part_create`, `event=render.job purpose=gate`, `event=live.switch result=moved`.

docs/agent-contract.md Connecting (device code), worked session steps 1–6; PLAN.md §3b device grant; §4c part_check.

title: T97.c: Pixel test guest half on mobile WebKit, live-update timing, CI and portability-lane wiring
description:
## Goal and why

Prove a signed-out phone can paint, the admin sees it live, and Freeze actually cuts the guest off; then make the whole test a required CI check and a portability-lane job.

## Scope

- WebKit context with a mobile profile (iPhone viewport, touch), no session, `/etc/hosts` resolution for `pf.test`.
- Open the `/l/<token>` URL: wrapper in public mode, `POST /l/<token>/go` returns a guest cap (`dw`, `g`); tap a cell; assert the `/_rt` write succeeds and record its timestamp; assert the admin tab repaint within 1 s (cross-context timing via shared test clock and log timestamps).
- After the admin's Freeze (T97.b): the guest taps again; the write rejects with a `PfError` (stale minter epoch / Can view → `forbidden_view_only` after re-go), the optimistic paint reverts, and the board's note shows "This board is view only." or "Not saved: …".
- `part_data list` by the agent shows guest docs with `provenance: "link_viewer"`, `contains_untrusted: true` before the roll back.
- CI: a required job on every PR, added to the forge workflow that calls the `ci/*.sh` scripts (T01 convention; `ci/e2e.sh` runs the same steps locally; the example CI workflow files are T126); T93 (the portability lane, after Slice 1) adds this spec to its lane; this subtask only makes the spec runnable from the published compose file with `_FILE` secrets so T93 can pick it up unchanged.

## Not in scope

Real-phone manual pass (T38).

## Design notes and decisions

Ordering between contexts is coordinated by explicit test barriers, not sleeps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Guest paint → admin tab < 1 s (p100 over 3 retries).
- [ ] Post-freeze write refused on the next request.
- [ ] Job required on PRs; green in the portability lane.

## Tests

`communal_pixel_editor.spec.ts › guest paints from a signed-out phone`, `› guest is frozen out`; logs `event=cap.mint subject_kind=link dw=true`, `event=rt.op principal=guest:*`, `event=data.changed`, `event=rt.op outcome=stale_epoch`. Artifacts: WebKit trace, HAR, screenshots.

title: G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)
description:
## Goal and why

Because partifactory sends people no notifications and keeps no approval queues, the activity feed is where people learn what happened: "Hermes shared this with the Family group · Undo", "14 guest edits today", "Shared with you". The plan relies on it in several places but no task builds it.

## Scope

- A per-person activity feed in the workspace (and a per-part slice in the wrapper's agent activity), built from the `events` table filtered to what the viewer may see: agent-made grants (with one-tap Undo, from `grants.created_by_conn`), moves into Family, versions saved by agents ("Claude Code saved REV 12"), guest write counts per part per day (from `data.changed` events with actor `guest:<link>:<g>`), and parts newly shared with the viewer.
- The gallery's **Shared with me** filter lists parts granted to the viewer directly or via a group.
- No messages are sent anywhere; nothing here is pending state.

## Not in scope

The event log itself (T51/T123), agent sharing (T52), guest links (T95), notifications (non-goal).

## Design notes and decisions

Read-time aggregation over `events` (30-day retention) is enough at household scale; guest counts are aggregated, never per-guest identities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent grant appears in the owner's feed within 1 s with Undo; Undo removes the grant and writes an audit row.
- [ ] Guest writes show as a daily count, no guest ids.
- [ ] Shared with me lists a part shared to the viewer's group and not one they can't see.

## Tests

`pf-ui` integration `activity_feed_visibility` (fixture events, a part the viewer can't see must not appear); e2e `tests/e2e/activity_feed.spec.ts` with server JSONL kept.

## References

PLAN.md §4 "No notifications for people, and no approval queues"; §3b Agent sharing; §3a Can contribute (visibility); §4a.6 Gallery filters.

## Dependency context

- Gap bead: a plan item that no task in the task graph owned; added during bead conversion.
- Depends on: T51, T52, T95, T120
- Feeds milestone(s): M2

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Re-worded against duplicates: the "Shared with me" gallery filter exists from T31.a; this bead makes it include group- and space-inherited grants and sort by when the grant was made. Guest counts in the share sheet are T95.c's; the agent-made-grant Undo component is T120.d's (reused here).
- Placement (the plan defines none): an **Activity** section on the gallery (a right rail ≥ 1100 px, a tab on phones) plus the per-part slice in the wrapper's Details sheet. Budget: "see what happened: Gallery → Activity, 1".
- Edge added: T123 (the "within 1 s" acceptance needs the workspace-host SSE `GET /api/v1/events`).
- Tests added: `agent_grant_undo_from_feed`, `guest_counts_no_ids`, `shared_with_me_group_grant`, and `event=audit action=grant.revoke actor=user:<owner>` on Undo.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An agent grant appears in the owner's feed within 1 s with Undo; Undo removes the grant and writes an audit row.

title: M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
description:
## Goal and why

Exit of phase **P2 Agents + the household loop**: the first moment of daily value, "an agent makes a thing from chat and I open it on my phone". *Why agents before invites:* invites serve people who aren't users yet and carry the most identity work. Critical path to M2 (14 steps): ... T16 -> T17 -> T62 -> T80 -> T53 -> T123 -> T55 -> M2.

## Scope (what P2 contains)

OAuth AS (device grant first, then auth code + PKCE + CIMD/DCR + manual clients), personal agent tokens, one connection per (agent, person) and service identities, MCP + discovery + the error contract + cross-surface conformance, `part_edit` with rebase, block ids, leases, notes, `part_get` full content and `render: "text"`, comments with provenance, the event log (long-poll, SSE, webhooks), live reload, inward agent sharing (`share:household`) and `part_link_for` deep links for people-only actions, **`part_check` + the render sidecar (the P2 headline)**, Jig, the source editor with drafts, renames, shared data over `/_rt` with live `data.changed`, "Can contribute" public links for guests, the Insights pages and debugging UI, and the Hermes skill with per-person pairing.

Direct dependencies: T44, T47, T48, T54, T55, T57, T58, T59, T70, T79, T80, T97, T109, T122, T123, T124, T125.

## Acceptance criteria (P2 "Done when")

- [ ] A household member pairs with Hermes, says "make a packing list and share it with the family" in chat, Hermes checks its own render (`part_check` screenshot) and posts the part's link, another family member opens it on their phone, comments, and watches the fix land (live reload).
- [ ] Claude Code connects with one passkey tap + Allow (T124) and edits a week-old part in one call.
- [ ] The named e2e test **`communal_pixel_editor`** passes in CI: (1) an agent is asked to make a communal pixel editor; (2) it creates it in one call, `part_check`s it, and posts `pixel-part.<domain>`; (3) the admin: Share -> Anyone with the link -> Can contribute -> Copy; (4) a signed-out phone paints and the admin's screen updates live; (5) the admin rolls back one snapshot and freezes it.

## Tests

T58 scripted chat flow; T124 conformance + Claude Code connection; T97 CI run; T57 conformance with all three auth kinds.

## References

PLAN.md §6 Phases (P2), §6a graph checks (critical path to M2).

## Dependency context

- This milestone depends on (blocks edges): 
  - T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
  - T47: Leases: part scope by default, optional file/block, TTL <= 10 min, person override, release on commit
  - T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar
  - T54: Jig design system: jig.css shared blob, @partifactory/jig, presets, design_system op, Jig as a part
  - T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
  - T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
  - T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
  - T59: Blob GC as a janitor job: mark from every reference, sweep after a 7-day grace
  - T70: Rename flow: admin-confirmed rename, 301 forever with query stripped, old name reserved
  - T79: Live reload for open viewers: pf:version from wrapper or prelude, silent reload or toast
  - T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
  - T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
  - T109: Debugging UI: trace waterfall, per-part Debug tab (incl. denying decisions), per-agent call page, log viewer with live tail
  - T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
  - T123: Event log for agents after Slice 1: part_watch long-poll, GET /api/v1/events SSE with Last-Event-ID, cursor_expired, signed webhooks
  - T124: OAuth authorization code after Slice 1: /oauth/authorize + PKCE S256, iss, CIMD, DCR, manual clients
  - T125: part_link_for after Slice 1: group, everyone and admin actions
  - G05: Workspace activity feed and Shared with me (agent-made grants, guest edit counts, shares)
- Unblocks: nothing

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans).

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Wording: Hermes "checks its own render before posting" (§6 Done-when; screenshots in chat are Hermes's own setting), so the T58 test `op=part_check precedes the posted link` is the oracle, not "attaches a screenshot".
- Direct dependencies now include G05 and T50 (comments are in this phase's Done-when; the edges T50 → M2 and T50 → T58 were added in the polish round).
acceptance_criteria: A household member pairs with Hermes, asks for a packing list shared with the family, opens the link on a phone, comments, and watches the fix land; Claude Code connects with one passkey tap and edits a week-old part in one call; Hermes attaches a `part_check` screenshot before posting; the `communal_pixel_editor` test passes

title: T45: Personal agent tokens (pf_pat_) and the Connected agents page (list, revoke with cascade, New personal token)
description:
## Goal and why

Personal tokens are for clients without OAuth: plain HTTP scripts, unattended agents (cron, CI, a server), and in Slice 1 every MCP client (Claude Code with `--header`, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI). "An unattended agent runs on a personal token its person made for it." Connected agents is where a person sees and revokes everything acting for them. Slice 1; feeds T57 (two auth kinds: device, PAT) and S1.

## Scope

- Minted from Connected agents (avatar menu) → **New personal token**, on the T43.c consent sheet: name, scopes, spaces, expiry (default 30 days, max 1 year). Shown **once**. Format `pf_pat_<base32, 160-bit>` so secret scanners and log redaction match it.
- Creates `agent_connections` (`kind='pat'`, `client_id` NULL) + one `oauth_tokens` row (`kind='pat'`, `prefix='pf_pat_'`, `expires_at`). Never refreshes; expired → ask for a new one.
- Used as `Authorization: Bearer` on `/api` and `/mcp`, conventionally via `PARTIFACTORY_URL` + `PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN` (CLI and skill file read them). Resolves to the same `(person, connection, scopes, spaces)` principal as OAuth tokens; marked "static" in the UI.
- Connected agents list: each connection "Hermes for you", scopes, spaces, last used, token type (`OAuth` / `device` / `personal token`), grants it made, with **Revoke** (10 s undo toast; revoke applies at once).
- Revoke cascade (T43.a): refresh family, access tokens and PATs revoked, `minter:conn:<id>` epoch bumped. Grants the connection made stay, listed with "Undo all" (`grants.created_by_conn`).
- Click budget: "Revoke an agent | avatar → Connected agents → Revoke | 3, undo toast".

## Not in scope

Token validation middleware (T43.a); device codes (T44); agent-made grants themselves (T52; this page only lists and undoes them once they exist).

## Design notes and decisions

- Open point: the plan specifies a 10 s undo toast on revoke but not its mechanics. Recommended default: undo within 10 s clears `revoked_at` on the connection and its tokens; the minter epoch bump is not reversed, so caps minted before the revoke stay dead and viewers re-grant silently. Record both the revoke and the undo in `audit`.
- Showing the token once: render with a copy button and the two env lines:
```
PARTIFACTORY_URL=https://parts.<domain>
PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN=pf_pat_…
```
- The MCP snippet shown: `claude mcp add --transport http partifactory https://parts.<domain>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $PARTIFACTORY_TOKEN"`.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A PAT works on /api and /mcp with the same scopes as an OAuth token; revoke takes effect on the next call".
- [ ] PAT shown once; only its hash stored.
- [ ] Same principal and scope enforcement as device tokens (shared test table).
- [ ] Revoke → next `/api` and `/mcp` call 401; caps minted through it die.
- [ ] Expiry default 30 d, max 1 y enforced.
- [ ] `pf_pat_` redacted in logs (canary).

## Tests

- `pf_oauth::pat::tests::{format_and_entropy, shown_once, expiry_bounds}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/pat_parity.rs`: same scenario with a device token and a PAT → identical decisions.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/pat_revoke_next_call.rs`: revoke then call → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`; log `event="auth.reject" reason="revoked"`.
- E2E `tests/e2e/connected_agents.spec.ts`: mint PAT, use it via CLI subprocess, revoke in UI (3 interactions), undo toast; server.jsonl and trace kept.

## References

PLAN.md §3b Personal agent tokens, Revocation cascades; §4a.6 Connected agents; §4b Auth table; §5e `oauth_tokens`, `agent_connections`; docs/agent-contract.md "Personal tokens".

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A PAT works on /api and /mcp with the same scopes as an OAuth token; revoke takes effect on the next call
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
- Unblocks: 
  - T57: Cross-surface conformance: one scenario via MCP, OpenAPI client, CLI and skill.md commands
acceptance_criteria: A PAT works on /api and /mcp with the same scopes as an OAuth token; revoke takes effect on the next call

title: T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
description:
## Goal and why

`part_edit` is **the one write op**: the common case is "change that thing from last week", so a small edit must be one cheap call (target p99 < 10 ms without a compile) that works even when other agents or people saved in between. It keeps the shape agents already know from Claude's artifact tools (`{old_str, new_str}` pairs, all-or-none, per-file `if_match` compare-and-set) and adds auto-rebase, idempotent retries and errors an LLM can self-correct from. In Slice 1 (the pixel test fixes its board with one `part_edit`); feeds T47, T48, T53, T55, T73, T85.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T46.a** edit application engine: the `Edit` variants, ordered all-or-none application, limits, anchor errors with best-match context.
- **T46.b** rebase inside the writer and `request_id` idempotency/replay.
- **T46.c** mode fields (`restore`, `delete`, `undelete`, `rebuild`, `meta`), `wait`/`check`/`live` plumbing and the op definition/output in the registry.

Input (Slice 1 contract): **`name`**, **`request_id`**, `edits` (≤ 64) or exactly one mode field (`restore: n`, `delete: true`, `undelete: true`, `rebuild: true`, `meta: {title?, tags?, description?, shared_data_writers?}`), `base_version` [head], `message` [auto summary, e.g. "app.tsx +14 −3"], `wait` [true], `check` [false], `live` (`always` | `after_check`) [`always`].
An `Edit` is one of:
- `{op: "replace", file?, old_str, new_str}`: `old_str` non-empty, ≤ 64 KiB, must occur exactly once; `file` defaults to the entry file.
- `{op: "write", file, content | blob, if_match}`: whole-file write; `if_match` is the file's current sha256, or `null` for a new file.
- `{op: "delete", file, if_match}` and `{op: "rename", from, to, if_match}`.
(Block ops arrive with T48, `claim` with T47, `backend` with T102, `notes` in `meta` with T122.)

Output: mutation shape `{name, url, head, live, build: {id, status, warnings, errors}}` plus `rebased_from` when rebased, `replayed: true` on a replay, and `check` when asked or `live: "after_check"` (check produced by T80).
Errors: `invalid_input`, `invalid_edit`, `unknown_field`, `not_found`, `file_not_found`, `forbidden`, `if_match_failed` (`file`, `current_sha256`), `file_exists`, `anchor_not_found` and `anchor_ambiguous` (`edit_index`, `file`, `context`, `lines`, `count`), `base_unknown`, `invalid_against_base`, `request_id_reused`, `quota_exceeded`, `rate_limited`, `too_large` (each file ≤ 2 MiB, each request ≤ 8 MiB), `storage_full`. HTTP: 400/404/403/409/422/429/413/507 per the catalogue (T20); CLI exits 2/4/3/5/5/6/2/7.
A build failure is not an error: 200 with `build.status: "failed"` and `build.errors: [{file, line, col, message}]` (or `{code: "mirror_failed", url, reason}`).
Scopes: `parts:write` (and `parts:delete` for `delete`/`undelete`), and the person's `edit` role.

## Not in scope

Leases/claims (T47), block ops and id carry-over (T48), the build worker and live switch (T13), the render check (T80), the editor's 3-way merge (T55), backend fields (T102).

## Design notes and decisions

- Optimistic by default, like shartifacts and Claude's artifacts; "Nobody uses pessimistic locks on source text, and partifactory doesn't either."
- Linearisable writes: "one writer task serialises all commits, so every part has a strict version sequence n, n+1, … with no lost updates. Rebase runs inside that same critical section (read head → apply → commit)."
- Whole-file replacement is compare-and-set per file (`if_match`), never a blind overwrite.
- Durable when acknowledged: blobs temp → fsync → verify → rename, manifest commit fsynced (`synchronous=FULL`) before the call returns.
- A one-line edit to a 40-file part writes 1 blob + 1 manifest (T08).
- Error messages say what was expected, what was found and the next call to make; the hint for an anchor failure states that nothing was saved and the whole batch must be resent.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Table-driven test of every error code; two agents editing disjoint anchors from one base both succeed; a retried timed-out edit returns the original result, never `anchor_not_found`".
- [ ] Every listed error code produced by a table-driven test with its `details` fields.
- [ ] Two edits from the same base on disjoint anchors → versions n+1 and n+2, second has `rebased_from`.
- [ ] Retry with same `request_id` + args after commit → stored result, `replayed: true`.
- [ ] Mode fields work and are mutually exclusive with `edits`.
- [ ] p99 < 10 ms for a small edit with no compile on the bench fixture (tracked).

## Tests

See subtasks; parent-level: `crates/pf-model/tests/part_edit_end_to_end.rs` (create → edit → stale edit rebased → conflicting edit → replay → restore), asserting log events `event="part.edit" outcome=… op="part_edit" part_id=… request_id=…` and that no `old_str`/content text appears in logs (canary).

## References

PLAN.md §3d Concurrency contract, Creation contract (durability), §4 Slice 1 op fields, §4b Errors table, §3c Quick edits; docs/agent-contract.md `part_edit`, Rules 1–2; §5a targets.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Table-driven test of every error code; two agents editing disjoint anchors from one base both succeed; a retried timed-out edit returns the original result, never `anchor_not_found`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
- Unblocks: 
  - T47: Leases: part scope by default, optional file/block, TTL <= 10 min, person override, release on commit
  - T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
  - T55: Workspace source editor: CodeMirror 6, server drafts, draft preview cap, 3-way merge and resolve
  - T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
  - T85: Phone editing: tap-to-edit text as anchor edits, long-press point-and-comment
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T46.a: Edit application engine: replace/write/delete/rename, ordered all-or-none, limits, anchor errors with context
  - T46.b: Rebase inside the single writer and request_id idempotency (only committed writes use up an id)
  - T46.c: part_edit mode fields (restore, delete, undelete, rebuild, meta), wait/check/live plumbing, registry op
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven test of every error code; two agents editing disjoint anchors from one base both succeed; a retried timed-out edit returns the original result, never `anchor_not_found`

title: T46.a: Edit application engine: replace/write/delete/rename, ordered all-or-none, limits, anchor errors with context
description:
## Goal and why

The pure function at the heart of `part_edit`: given a working file set and an ordered list of edits, produce the new file set or one precise, LLM-actionable error. Pure and deterministic so it can be dry-run on the base and re-run on head (T46.b).

## Scope

- Apply edits **in order**, each against the text as left by the previous one; all or none.
- `replace`: `old_str` non-empty, ≤ 64 KiB, must occur **exactly once** in the current working text of its file; `file` defaults to the entry. 0 occurrences → `anchor_not_found`; ≥ 2 → `anchor_ambiguous` with `count`.
- `write`: `content` (text) or `blob` (sha256 of an uploaded blob); `if_match` = current sha256 or `null` (= must not exist; else `file_exists`); mismatch → `if_match_failed {file, current_sha256}`.
- `delete {file, if_match}`, `rename {from, to, if_match}` (`to` existing → `file_exists`; missing → `file_not_found`).
- Limits: ≤ 64 edits per call, `old_str` ≤ 64 KiB, each resulting file ≤ 2 MiB, request ≤ 8 MiB → `too_large {limit}`; malformed edit → `invalid_edit {path}`.
- Anchor error details: "the failing `edit_index` and the current text of the best-matching region (normalised Levenshtein ≥ 0.6, otherwise the file's first 600 chars), ±3 lines, ≤ 2 KiB, with the line range", plus `similarity`. Example:
```json
{"error":{"code":"anchor_not_found","message":"edits[1].old_str was not found in index.html at v3 (you based on v2; v3 changed this region).",
 "hint":"Re-read lines 40-52 with part_get and resend both edits with a corrected edits[1]; nothing was saved.","retryable":true,
 "details":{"edit_index":1,"file":"index.html","context":"…","lines":[44,52],"similarity":0.83}}}
```
- Auto message summary per file ("app.tsx +14 −3").

## Not in scope

Rebase, idempotency (T46.b); blobs persistence (T07/T08); block ops (T48).

## Design notes and decisions

- Best-match search: slide a window of `old_str`'s line count over the file, compute normalised Levenshtein; bound the cost (cap the file scan at 2 MiB, early-exit on ≥ 0.95).
- Byte-exact matching (no whitespace normalisation): agents copy `old_str` from `part_get` content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each error variant reachable with correct `details`.
- [ ] Order matters: edit 2 can target text introduced by edit 1.
- [ ] Any failure leaves inputs untouched.

## Tests

- `pf_model::edit::tests` table-driven: `replace_once`, `replace_missing`, `replace_ambiguous_count`, `sequential_dependency`, `write_new_if_match_null`, `write_exists_conflict`, `write_if_match_mismatch`, `delete_missing`, `rename_to_existing`, `limits_64_edits`, `old_str_64k`, `file_2mib`, `request_8mib`.
- Property `pf_model::edit::prop::all_or_none` (random edit lists: either full success or input unchanged).
- Golden `tests/golden/edit/best_match/*.json` for context extraction.

## References

PLAN.md §3d Semantics, Rebase (error detail), Limits; §4b Errors; docs/agent-contract.md `part_edit`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each error variant reachable with correct `details`.
- [ ] Order matters: edit 2 can target text introduced by edit 1.
- [ ] Any failure leaves inputs untouched.

title: T46.b: Rebase inside the single writer and request_id idempotency (only committed writes use up an id)
description:
## Goal and why

Two agents editing different regions of one file must both succeed, and a retried timed-out call must return the original result, never `anchor_not_found`. Both happen inside the single writer's critical section so there are no lost updates.

## Scope

- Rebase algorithm (inside the writer, read head → apply → commit):
  1. if `base_version` is absent or equals head, apply to head;
  2. otherwise the base must exist and belong to the part, else `base_unknown {base}`;
  3. dry-run the edits on the base; any failure there is the caller's bug → `invalid_against_base {base, failing edit}`;
  4. apply the same list to head, where `write`/`delete`/`rename` compare `if_match` against *head*;
  5. commit with `parent = head` and `rebased_from = base` (`versions.rebased_from`).
- "An edit fails only when its anchor itself changed (0 or ≥ 2 occurrences at its turn)."
- Idempotency: **reuse T11.a's shared layer** `with_idempotency(principal, request_id, op, args_hash, f)` (the `idempotency` table, replay with `replayed: true`, `request_id_reused` on different arguments, "only a committed write uses up its id", 24 h purge). Do not implement a second one. This subtask wraps the whole rebase + commit in it, so the stored response is written in the commit transaction, and owns the `part_edit`-specific consequence: a timed-out edit retried after the network recovers returns the stored result ("already applied: version 12"), never `anchor_not_found`.
- The replay check happens before rebase/anchor evaluation so a replay never re-applies.

## Not in scope

Writer task itself (T05); version/manifest writing (T08); leases (T47).

## Design notes and decisions

- The layer is T11.a's (`pf_model::idempotency`), shared with `part_create` and `part_data` writes; arguments hash = sha256 of the canonical JSON input minus `request_id`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disjoint edits from one base both commit; overlapping anchor change → `anchor_not_found` with context.
- [ ] Timeout-retry returns the original result with `replayed: true`.
- [ ] A rejected write leaves no idempotency row.

## Tests

- `pf_model::rebase::tests::{base_equals_head, disjoint_from_same_base, anchor_changed_conflict, base_unknown, invalid_against_base, if_match_against_head}`.
- The generic idempotency unit tests are T11.a's; here only `pf_model::rebase::tests::replay_checked_before_rebase` (a replayed edit never re-evaluates anchors) and `rejected_edit_leaves_no_row`.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/concurrent_editors.rs`: 2–8 tasks editing disjoint anchors concurrently → gap-free versions, all succeed; logs `event="part.edit" rebased_from=…`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/timeout_retry.rs`: client times out after commit, retries → `replayed: true`.

## References

PLAN.md §3d Rebase, Idempotent every write; §5e `idempotency`, `versions.rebased_from`; docs/agent-contract.md Rules 1–2.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T46.a: Edit application engine: replace/write/delete/rename, ordered all-or-none, limits, anchor errors with context
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Disjoint edits from one base both commit; overlapping anchor change → `anchor_not_found` with context.
- [ ] Timeout-retry returns the original result with `replayed: true`.
- [ ] A rejected write leaves no idempotency row.

title: T46.c: part_edit mode fields (restore, delete, undelete, rebuild, meta), wait/check/live plumbing, registry op
description:
## Goal and why

One write op instead of many near-duplicate tools: restore, delete, undelete, rebuild and metadata changes are mode fields on `part_edit`. In Slice 1 the versions rail and bin UI are deferred (T120), so these modes are how restore, delete and undelete work.

## Scope

- Exactly one of `edits` or a mode field, else `invalid_input`.
- `restore: n` → new version whose manifest equals version n (via T11), `versions.restored_from` set, `via='restore'`; goes through the build like any version; result "Restored as REV 13".
- `delete: true` → soft delete to the 30-day bin (`parts.deleted_at`), needs `parts:delete`; `undelete: true` → back (fails after 30 days: purged). Bump the part epoch on delete.
- `rebuild: true` → rebuild head with the current toolchain/library set (opts the part into the current import map).
- `meta: {title?, tags?, description?, shared_data_writers?}` → no new version; `shared_data_writers` change rules: setting `editors` while a contribute link is active freezes that link (T95 implements freeze; this calls its hook if present). Writes an `audit` row for `shared_data_writers`.
- `wait` [true]: block ≤ 2 s on `build.finished`; with `check: true` or `live: "after_check"` up to 15 s for build + check; still running → `build: {status: "running", id}`. `wait: false` returns at once.
- `live` stored on `versions.live_gate` (`always` | `after_check`); gate execution belongs to T80/T13. If the renderer is off, `after_check` behaves as `always` and `build.warnings` carries `check_skipped`.
- Register `part_edit` in `pf-ops` (T20): typed input with `deny_unknown_fields`, `SCOPE`, hints (per op, not per mode: `read_only: false, destructive: false, idempotent: true` with `request_id`; delete is soft and undoable, which is why `destructive` stays false), at least two executable examples ("fix a typo", "stale base, auto-rebased"), every error with a hint.

## Not in scope

The check itself (T80), the live switch (T13), freeze/contribute (T95), notes in meta (T122), claim (T47), backend (T102).

## Design notes and decisions

- Version 0 placeholder parts: `edits` on a part with `head: 0` apply to an empty file set (create files with `write if_match:null`).
- Permission errors: a part the caller can't see → `not_found`, never `forbidden`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each mode works and is exclusive; restore of v3 creates v(n+1) equal to v3.
- [ ] `wait` timings respected (2 s / 15 s).
- [ ] Registry snapshot includes `part_edit` schema and examples.

## Tests

- `pf_model::part_edit::tests::{modes_exclusive, restore_creates_new_version, delete_then_undelete, undelete_after_30d_fails, rebuild_new_build_same_version, meta_no_version, editors_freezes_contribute_hook}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/part_edit_wait.rs` with a slow fake build worker: 2 s and 15 s ceilings; `check_skipped` warning with renderer off.
- Registry snapshot test (T20) updated.

## References

PLAN.md §3d mode fields, Build worker `wait`, Latest vs live; §3e Restore, bin; §4 part_edit row; docs/agent-contract.md `part_edit`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T46.a: Edit application engine: replace/write/delete/rename, ordered all-or-none, limits, anchor errors with context, T46.b: Rebase inside the single writer and request_id idempotency (only committed writes use up an id)

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.

- [ ] Each mode works and is exclusive; restore of v3 creates v(n+1) equal to v3.
- [ ] `wait` timings respected (2 s / 15 s).
- [ ] Registry snapshot includes `part_edit` schema and examples.

title: T47: Leases: part scope by default, optional file/block, TTL <= 10 min, person override, release on commit
description:
## Goal and why

"Optimistic by default, leases when coordination is worth it." Several agents (and people) can work on one part; an advisory lease lets one say "I'm editing app.tsx" so others back off, and the UI shows it ("Hermes is editing *app.tsx*"). Like Claude's `db.acquire`, advisory, never a lock a person can't break. After Slice 1; feeds M2.

## Scope

- `part_edit {claim: {scope: part | file | block, ref?, ttl ≤ 10 min}}`, part scope by default. `ref` is a path (file) or block id (block, T48).
- `leases` table: `id, part_id, scope DEFAULT 'part' CHECK (scope IN ('part','file','block')), scope_ref DEFAULT '', holder_user, holder_conn, holder_label, expires_at (<= created_at + 10 min), created_at, UNIQUE (part_id, scope, scope_ref)`.
- Others' edits to a claimed scope get `claimed {by: "Hermes", until: "14:32", scope}` (HTTP 409, CLI exit 5). A part lease covers every file; a file lease covers that file and blocks in it.
- A **person** can always override: their edit succeeds and the holder is notified (an event `lease.overridden` on the event log, delivered to the holder via T123/T84; in-UI notice "saving asks once").
- Leases auto-release on commit by the holder and on expiry. Re-claiming extends up to the 10 min cap.
- UI: a blue dot + "Hermes is editing this file until 14:32" in the wrapper bar and editor (render via T120/T55 from lease data exposed by `part_get`/events); gallery "Hermes editing" pill.
- Add `claimed` to the error catalogue if not present (it is in §4b: `claimed | by, until, scope | 409 | 5`).

## Not in scope

Data leases on `data_docs` (`data_leases`, T73). Editor UI (T55). Block ids (T48).

## Design notes and decisions

- Agents never force; "force exists only for the person, never for agents".
- Lease checks run inside the writer critical section with rebase (T46.b) so a lease acquired between read and commit is honoured.
- Expired leases are lazily ignored and pruned by the janitor (T113 job registration).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Agent B's edit to a claimed file returns `claimed` with holder + expiry; a person's edit succeeds and notifies the holder".
- [ ] TTL > 10 min rejected (`invalid_input`) or clamped (choose: reject, with hint).
- [ ] Release on commit and on expiry.
- [ ] Person override emits the notification event.

## Tests

- `pf_model::leases::tests::{claim_part_default, claim_file, conflict_returns_claimed, ttl_cap_10min, release_on_commit, expiry_releases, person_override_notifies}` (test clock).
- `crates/pf-model/tests/two_agents_lease.rs`: agent A claims `app.tsx`, agent B edits it → `claimed {by, until}`; B edits another file → ok; log events `lease.acquire`, `lease.conflict`, `lease.overridden`.

## References

PLAN.md §3d Leases, People and agents together; §4a.6 lease display; §4b `claimed`; §5e `leases`.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.

title: T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar
description:
## Goal and why

Long documents (a research write-up, a spec, a report) need addressing that survives edits: stable block ids let several agents fill sections in parallel without conflicts, comments anchor to blocks, and `part_get` can return an outline. This is the Claude-Docs-style "outline first, fill in parallel" pattern. After Slice 1; feeds T66 (slides: block = slide), T85, M2.

## Scope

- **Block** = a top-level comrak node: heading, paragraph, list (whole list), block quote, fenced code, table, HTML block or thematic break. In `slides`, block = slide. **Section** = a heading plus everything up to the next heading of the same or higher level.
- **Sidecar** `.pf/blocks.json` *inside the manifest* (versioned atomically with the text): `{v: 1, file: "index.md", blocks: [{id, kind, start_byte, end_byte, hash}]}`. Ids are 8-character Crockford base32, random, unique within the part, never reused.
- **Carry-over** after *any* commit touching a Markdown file (anchor edit, whole-file write, editor save): re-parse and match new blocks to old in three passes: exact `hash` match in order (LCS); then remaining blocks of the same kind in the same gap with token Jaccard similarity ≥ 0.5; then everything else gets a fresh id.
- **Ops** (new `Edit` variants in `part_edit`): `{op: "replace_block", block, markdown, if_hash?}`, `{op: "insert_after", block | "start", markdown}`, `{op: "append_to_section", heading_block, markdown}`, `{op: "delete_block", block, if_hash?}`. Errors `block_not_found` (404, exit 4), `block_changed` (422, with the current text). Rebase resolves by id, not offset, so block edits on different blocks never conflict.
- **Pending blocks**: `<!-- pf:pending id=<id> intent="…" -->` on its own line renders as a placeholder (`.jig-pending` / shell style, tag-coloured in the UI), and `replace_block` on that id fills it.
- `part_get` on a long doc returns the outline + block ids (wire into T49/T122 outline).
- Markdown renderer (T12) emits block ids as element attributes (`data-pf-block="<id>"`) for comments and phone editing.

## Not in scope

Slides runtime (T66), leases with block scope (T47 uses the ids), phone tap-to-edit mapping (T85), Jig styling (T54).

## Design notes and decisions

- Ids in the manifest, not a DB table, so block identity is versioned with content; `comments.anchor` and `leases.scope_ref` hold ids as text with no FK, re-anchoring is application logic.
- *No CRDTs:* agents submit whole edits; versions, anchors, blocks and leases handle that with far less machinery.
- Hash = sha256 of the block's normalised source bytes.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Ids survive an anchor edit, a whole-file replace and an editor save in golden tests; parallel `replace_block` on different blocks both commit".
- [ ] Three-pass matcher implemented with the thresholds above.
- [ ] Pending placeholder renders and fills.
- [ ] `block_changed` with `if_hash` mismatch returns current text.

## Tests

- Golden `tests/golden/blocks/{anchor_edit,whole_replace,editor_save,reorder,split_paragraph}/` (before.md, after.md, expected blocks.json).
- `pf_build::blocks::tests::{parse_top_level, crockford_ids_unique, lcs_pass, jaccard_pass_threshold, fresh_ids_never_reused}`.
- `crates/pf-model/tests/parallel_replace_block.rs`: two agents `replace_block` different ids from one base → both commit; log `event="part.edit" rebased_from`.
- `pf_model::edit::tests::{block_not_found, block_changed_if_hash, insert_after_start, append_to_section}`.

## References

PLAN.md §3d Long documents, Do we need CRDTs; §5e modelling decisions (block ids); §4b errors.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Ids survive an anchor edit, a whole-file replace and an editor save in golden tests; parallel `replace_block` on different blocks both commit
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done
  - T66: Slides kind plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides (block = slide)

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- The "editor save" golden is a whole-file `write` with `via = 'editor'` through T46 (T55 is not a dependency), so it is testable without the editor.
- Outline ownership: T122 owns the outline shape; this task exposes a `blocks(version) -> [{id, kind, start_byte, end_byte, hash}]` reader that T122 calls (headings degrade to no ids until this lands).
- Tests add a renderer golden asserting `data-pf-block` attributes on the rendered HTML.
- Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` op sections and the "After Slice 1" list are updated in the same change; T56's registry-match test stays green. (block-op `Edit` variants, `block_not_found`/`block_changed` errors, `.pf/blocks.json` in the Kinds notes; "block edits" leaves the After list).
acceptance_criteria: Ids survive an anchor edit, a whole-file replace and an editor save in golden tests; parallel `replace_block` on different blocks both commit

title: T49: Agent read path (Slice 1): part_get full content <= 32 KiB, file/range, version, history, diff, build log, runtime_errors
description:
## Goal and why

Agents must read only what they need, cheaply: the whole thing for the common single-file part, a slice otherwise, plus the errors viewers' browsers saw. `runtime_errors` closes the loop ("the agent finds out its page is broken without needing a browser"). Slice 1; feeds T53, T122, T57.

## Scope

Input: **`name`**, `version` (`"head"` | `"live"` | n) [`"head"`], `file`, `range` (`[first, last]`, 1-based inclusive lines, needs `file`), `history` [false], `diff_from`, `diff_to` [head], `build` (a build id).
Output: `{id, name, url, title, kind, space, version, head, live, build, files, content?, runtime_errors, history?, diff?}`.
- `files` is `{path: {hash, size, mime}}` (use `hash` as `if_match`).
- `content` is `{path: text}` for every text file when the part is **≤ 32 KiB in total**, otherwise only for the `file` (or `range`) asked for; larger parts return the file list with sizes.
- `runtime_errors` always the latest 20: `[{kind, message, stack, url, count, source, version, last_at}]` (`kind` ∈ `error`, `unhandledrejection`, `blocked_load`, `csp`; `source` ∈ `viewer`, `render`).
- `history`: `[{n, author, actor, via, message, created_at, build_status}]`.
- `diff`: `{from, to, files: [{path, status, added, removed, patch}]}` (unified patch; binary files show size change).
- `build: <id>` returns that build record with its log (`builds.log_hash` blob) as `build`.
Errors: `invalid_input`, `unknown_field`, `not_found` (also for a part outside your connection's spaces), `file_not_found`, `forbidden`. Scope `parts:read`.
Example:
```json
{"name":"pixel","file":"index.html","range":[7,7]}
→ {"id":"p_…","name":"pixel","url":"https://pixel-part.<domain>/","title":"Pixel board","kind":"html","space":"~me","version":2,"head":2,"live":2,
   "build":{"id":78,"status":"ok","warnings":[],"errors":[]},"files":{"index.html":{"hash":"9f2c…","size":1712,"mime":"text/html"}},
   "content":{"index.html":"…line 7…\n"},"runtime_errors":[]}
```
- `runtime_errors`: the store, its `errors.report` ingestion, fingerprinting, the ≤ 10/min rate limit and the `latest_20(part)` read helper are **T62.d's** (hence the T62 edge); this task exposes that helper's result in `part_get` output (shape `[{kind, message, stack, url, count, source, version, last_at}]`) and checks the `source: render` rows once T80 lands.
- **Reuse, don't redo**: version selection, `files`, `content` (the ≤ 32 KiB rule), `file`/`range`, `history` and `diff` are T11.b's `get_part`, already unit-tested there. T49 owns: the registry op (input/output types, `deny_unknown_fields`, examples), the `build: <id>` record-with-log field, `runtime_errors` in the output, the connection-space rule (`not_found` outside the connection's spaces), and the HTTP GET alias check (`GET /api/v1/parts/{name}` = `part_get`).
- Register `part_get` in `pf-ops` with examples (read-only, idempotent hints).

## Not in scope

Agent notes, outline with symbols, `render: "text"`, `part_find` (T122); `backend: true` (T102); history UI (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- 32 KiB threshold keeps the common case one call without blowing the model's context.
- Version resolution: `head` = newest committed; `live` = newest with an ok build (and passed gate); a version the caller can't see → `not_found`.
- Content returned as UTF-8 text; binary files never inlined.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "`part_get` on a 20 KiB single-file part returns the file; on a 100 KiB part it returns the file list, and a `range` returns exactly those lines; a viewer's uncaught error appears in `runtime_errors`".
- [ ] All fields and defaults as above; history and diff correct for any two versions.
- [ ] Out-of-space part → `not_found`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-ops/tests/part_get_op.rs::{build_record_with_log, runtime_errors_latest_20_shape, outside_connection_spaces_not_found, range_needs_file, version_live_vs_head, get_alias_equals_op, example_matches_contract}` (content/range/history/diff behaviour is covered by T11.b's `pf_model::read::tests`).
- `crates/pf-api/tests/runtime_errors_roundtrip.rs`: post `errors.report` via `/_rt` as a viewer, then `part_get` shows it with `source: viewer`, count increments on repeat; log `event="rt.errors.report"` without message text in logs (content canary).
- Contract example parse test (T56) for the `part_get` example.

## References

PLAN.md §3c Read only what's needed, Errors close the loop; §4 Slice 1 op fields and shapes; §5e `runtime_errors`; docs/agent-contract.md `part_get`.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: yes. Priority P1.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): `part_get` on a 20 KiB single-file part returns the file; on a 100 KiB part it returns the file list, and a `range` returns exactly those lines; a viewer's uncaught error appears in `runtime_errors`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T11: Part service: create (request_id, v0, fork, expires_in), get, history, diff, bin, undelete, restore
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1 (T62.d owns the `runtime_errors` store and ingestion that `part_get` exposes)
- Unblocks: 
  - T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
acceptance_criteria: `part_get` on a 20 KiB single-file part returns the file; on a 100 KiB part it returns the file list, and a `range` returns exactly those lines; a viewer's uncaught error appears in `runtime_errors`

title: T122: Agent read path after Slice 1: agent notes (versioned separately), outline with symbols, render:"text", part_find
description:
## Goal and why

Make "change that thing from last week" cheap for the next agent: notes tell it what a part is and how it's built, an outline tells it where to look, `render: "text"` answers "what's on the meal plan?" without parsing HTML, and `part_find` finds the part without knowing its name. After Slice 1; feeds T58, M2.

## Scope

- **Agent notes**: a short "what this is / how it's built / gotchas" doc per part, returned first by `part_get`. Versioned separately in `part_notes` (`part_id, n, body (≤ 16384), author_user, actor_conn, created_at`, PK `(part_id, n)`), so updating notes never creates a part version. Set via `notes` on `part_create` and `meta.notes` on `part_edit`. Indexed by FTS (T76).
- **Outline**: for parts > 32 KiB, `part_get` returns files, sizes, **symbols** (top-level functions/components/exports for JS/TSX, headings for Markdown with block ids from T48) + notes.
- **`render: "text"`**: returns the rendered readable text the search index already has (text nodes after rendering, minus `<script>`/`<style>`).
- **`part_find`** op: search + filters (`kind:`, `tag:`, `space:`, `by:`, `has:data`, `has:comments`, `updated:`); **no query = recent by me / this agent**. Over T76's FTS5 index with bm25 + recency. Scope `parts:read`; results limited to the connection's spaces.
- Add `part_find` section to `docs/agent-contract.md` in the same change (registry-match test, T56) and join the T57 scenario's "find it" step.
- MCP resources `part://recent` and `part://<name>` become projections of `part_find`/`part_get` (wire in T53).

## Not in scope

The FTS index and ranking (T76); comments (T50); search UI (T120).

## Design notes and decisions

- Notes as their own table so a notes edit doesn't trigger a build, a live switch or a version.
- Symbol extraction: oxc parser for JS/TSX (after T60) with a regex fallback for HTML inline scripts; keep it cheap and best-effort.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Notes edits do not create part versions; `render:"text"` matches the indexed text; `part_find` with no query returns recent parts by me or this agent".
- [ ] Notes returned first by `part_get`; max 16 KiB enforced.
- [ ] Outline with symbols for large parts.
- [ ] `part_find` filters work and respect spaces; contract section added.

## Tests

- `pf_model::notes::tests::{notes_versioned_separately, notes_no_part_version, notes_size_cap}`.
- `pf_model::read::tests::{render_text_equals_index_text, outline_symbols_md, outline_symbols_js}`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/part_find.rs`: fixture parts by different actors; no query → recent by me/agent; filters; out-of-space parts excluded; log `event="op" op="part_find"` with no query text in logs.

## References

PLAN.md §3c Discoverable, Read only what's needed; §3e Search; §4 ops table (`part_find`, `part_get`); §5e `part_notes`, `parts_fts`.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2 (epic "P2 Agents + the household loop"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Notes edits do not create part versions; `render:"text"` matches the indexed text; `part_find` with no query returns recent parts by me or this agent
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T49: Agent read path (Slice 1): part_get full content <= 32 KiB, file/range, version, history, diff, build log, runtime_errors
  - T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - M2: Milestone - P2 Agents + the household loop done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Notes indexing: T76's "index updates when notes change" has nothing to hook until notes exist; this task calls T76's `index_notes(part_id, text)` on every `part_notes` insert (test `notes_indexed`).
- `outline_symbols_js` is fallback-tolerant (headings and `export`s via regex) so it runs before T60's oxc parser is available.
- `part_find` excludes binned parts (§3e) and is limited to the connection's spaces; test `binned_excluded`.
- Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` op sections and the "After Slice 1" list are updated in the same change; T56's registry-match test stays green. (`notes` on `part_create`, `meta.notes` on `part_edit`, `render` and `notes` in `part_get`, plus the new `part_find` section).
