title: Phase P3 Claude compatibility
description:
# Phase P3 Claude compatibility

## Goal and why

Phase P3 makes anything Claude writes run unchanged: `claude.use` (`db`, `user`, `comments`, `artifact` incl.
self-publish; shared `window.storage` arrived in P2), Tailwind + shadcn (mechanism chosen on evidence: prebuilt utility
CSS, the Tailwind v4 browser build mirrored as a shared blob, or build-time class extraction), viewer uploads (assets),
and the agent inbox with stewards. The spec is shartifacts' compatibility matrix (credited).

*Done when (M3):* a page copied from a claude.ai artifact runs unchanged, including state persistence and self-editing,
and a viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox.

## Members

- T61: Tailwind + shadcn support for Claude-written parts, mechanism chosen on evidence
- T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
- T83: Viewer asset uploads: assets.put over /_rt, /_a/<id>, quota, listed and deletable by agents
- T84: Agent inbox and steward: part_inbox op, to_agent routing, open/claimed/answered/resolved, stalled

Phase exit: M3: Milestone - P3 Claude compatibility done

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".

title: T61: Tailwind + shadcn support for Claude-written parts, mechanism chosen on evidence
description:
## Goal and why

Claude-written artifacts very often use Tailwind utility classes and shadcn/ui components (`Button`, `Card`, ...). partifactory's promise is that "anything Claude writes runs here unchanged" (PLAN.md §1, the Claude-artifact compatibility row kept from shartifacts). Without Tailwind and shadcn, a large share of copied claude.ai artifacts render unstyled or fail to import. This task closes that gap for the `tsx` kind (and HTML parts that use Tailwind classes), and is part of the P3 "Claude compatibility" phase whose done-when is: *a page copied from a claude.ai artifact runs unchanged, including state persistence and self-editing* (milestone M3).

The plan deliberately does not pre-decide *how*: it lists three candidate mechanisms and says to pick **on evidence** (PLAN.md §6 P3, review item O13: "Tailwind is a P3 spike choosing among three options on evidence"). This task is that spike plus the shipped implementation of the winner.

Depends on T60 (the `tsx` kind: oxc transform + rolldown bundle in the build child, the library set `libset.toml` pre-seeded as shared blobs, import maps frozen into the build record, CDN-URL aliasing). After Slice 1, P3.

## Scope

1. **Evaluate the three options** against a corpus and write a decision note (`docs/decisions/tailwind.md`):
   - (a) **prebuilt utility CSS**: one large, precompressed Tailwind utility stylesheet built once, served as a shared blob from `https://blobs-part.<domain>/b/<hash>`, linked by the generated TSX shell;
   - (b) **the Tailwind v4 browser build, mirrored** as a shared blob (the in-browser JIT that scans the DOM at runtime);
   - (c) **build-time class extraction**: in the build child, scan the part's source for class names and emit only the CSS used (Tailwind's own engine or an equivalent run in-process; no network in the child).
   For each option record: corpus pass rate, CSS bytes (brotli) per typical page, first-render time on the mobile viewport, build time added (must stay inside the build child's **10 s deadline**, which covers compile and rewrite only), behaviour with arbitrary values (`w-[37px]`), dark mode (`dark:`), and with class names built at runtime (string concatenation).
2. **shadcn in the library set**: add the shadcn component sources used by Claude artifacts (at minimum `Button`, `Card`, plus the components the corpus imports) and their runtime deps to `libset.toml` (version recorded as `library_set_version`), seeded as shared blobs, with import-map entries so `@/components/ui/button` style imports Claude uses resolve. Recall the set already holds `react` and `react-dom` 18.3, `lucide-react`, `recharts`, `d3`, `lodash`, `papaparse`, `mathjs`, `three`, `chart.js`, `tone`, `plotly.js` and `xlsx` ("shadcn and Tailwind join in T61").
3. **Wire the winner** into the `tsx` build: the generated HTML shell (`#root`, "Tailwind per §6 P3") includes whatever the chosen option needs; HTML parts that reference the Tailwind CDN (`cdn.tailwindcss.com` is NOT on the mirror allowlist) get a documented answer: either the build maps the known Tailwind CDN script to the chosen mechanism with a `cdn_aliased` style warning, or the contract tells agents to use a static tag/`tsx`. Record which in the decision note and update `docs/agent-contract.md` kinds table in the same change.
4. **Toolchain keying**: the Tailwind/shadcn versions become part of `toolchain_version`/`library_set_version`, so the build cache key `sha256(source_manifest_hash ‖ toolchain_version ‖ library_set_version ‖ mirror_resolution_hash)` changes and old builds keep their frozen import maps (a library upgrade never changes an old part; `part_edit {rebuild: true}` opts in).
5. Golden corpus additions under `tests/golden/tsx/tailwind/` and reference screenshots.

## Not in scope

- The `tsx` kind itself, library set mechanism, import-map freezing (T60).
- `claude.use(...)` APIs (T73). Jig design system (T54) – Jig is separate and optional; Tailwind is for Claude compatibility.
- Adding `cdn.tailwindcss.com` or any new origin to the CSP: the canonical part CSP stays (`script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' blob: <blob>`, `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <blob>`); everything must come from the part host or the shared blob host.

## Design notes and decisions

- **Why on evidence:** each option fails differently. (a) is huge and can't do arbitrary values; (b) works with runtime class names but costs JS on phones and runs a JIT in every viewer's browser (allowed by `'unsafe-eval'`, but slow); (c) is smallest and fastest to render but misses classes built at runtime and must fit the child's 10 s budget with no network. The note must pick by corpus pass rate first, then mobile render time, then bytes.
- A hybrid is acceptable if the evidence supports it (e.g. (c) with a small prebuilt safelist), but must be stated in the note.
- Every artifact must be reproducible from its build record: whatever generator runs must be pinned and vendored (same rule as oxc/rolldown: "exact versions pinned and vendored").

title: T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
description:
## Goal and why

claude.ai artifacts call `claude.use("db" | "user" | "comments" | "artifact")`. partifactory keeps "Claude-artifact compatibility" as a core idea from shartifacts (PLAN.md §1): *anything Claude writes runs here unchanged, including state that persists and pages that save themselves*. Shared `window.storage` already arrived in P2 (T96); this task adds the rest of the `claude.use` surface to the prelude and the matching `/_rt` ops, so that M3's done-when holds: *a page copied from a claude.ai artifact runs unchanged, including state persistence and self-editing*.

P3, after Slice 1. Depends on T62 (prelude + `/_rt/v1`), T46 (`part_edit` engine, used by self-publish), T50 (comments), T27 (`/grant` and caps: role decisions), T96 (shared data over `/_rt`, `part_data`, `data.changed`).

## Scope

The prelude (a shared blob, first in `<head>`) installs `claude.use(...)` returning module objects. All calls go through the one CORS-simple endpoint `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` with `Content-Type: text/plain` and JSON `{op, args}` (no preflight). Auth is the cap in the path; the server accepts `Origin: null` (or the part's own origin for `unsandboxed` parts), rejects any other non-null `Origin` before reading the body, and requires `Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors` if present.

`/_rt` ops added here: `db.*`, `comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `user` (the full `/_rt` op list is `storage.get/getMany/set/delete/list`, `db.*`, `comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`; the **data ops** are `storage.*` and `db.*`).

Role × runtime matrix (enforced in `/_rt` and in every op):

| | shared `storage` / `db` | comments | self-publish (`artifact.publish`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| public-link viewer (Can view) | read | only if opted in | no |
| public-link guest (Can contribute) | read, **write** (rate-limited, size-capped) | no | no |
| `view` | read, write unless `shared_data_writers: "editors"` | no | no |
| `comment` | as `view` | yes | no |
| `edit` / `manage` | read/write | yes | yes |

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead: close only after all subtasks are closed and the M3-style copy-an-artifact e2e passes):
- **T73.a** `claude.use("db")`: the `/_rt` `db.*` ops over `data_docs` (same rows `part_data` reads), per-document CAS by `rev`, and **data leases** (`data_leases` table, like Claude's `db.acquire`).
- **T73.b** `claude.use("user")` and `claude.use("comments")`: viewer identity (including the guest answer "Guest 4f2a" computed locally), comments read/add over `/_rt` with provenance.
- **T73.c** `claude.use("artifact")`: self-publish with compare-and-set against live == head, through the `part_edit` engine, `via = 'self_publish'`.

End-to-end: a corpus of claude.ai artifacts that use `claude.use` (from shartifacts' compatibility matrix) runs unchanged.

## Not in scope

- `window.storage` (personal + shared), `data.changed`, `shared_data_writers`, `part_data` (T96).
- Comments backend, threads, anchors, provenance and MCP wrapping (T50) – T73.b only exposes them to page code.
- Viewer uploads `assets.put` (T83). Agent inbox (T84).
- Tailwind/shadcn (T61).

## Design notes and decisions

- **Why `db.*` lives here, not T96:** at the Slice 1 freeze "`db.*` was in both T96 (P2) and T73 (P3): it's T73, with `claude.use("db")`" (§10 Slice 1 freeze, ambiguity 8). `window.storage` is the Slice 1 data API.
- **One storage model:** `claude.use("db")` documents are `data_docs` rows (`collection` ≠ `__storage`), so `part_data {collection}` reads exactly the same row. No second store.
- Guests are web consumers only: a guest cap calling any non-data `/_rt` op (`comments.*`, `artifact.publish`, `assets.put`, `user`, `errors.report`, `refresh`) gets `403`. The prelude answers `claude.use("user")` for a guest **locally** ("Guest 4f2a"), without calling `/_rt` (§3a, decision F33: the guest answer waits for `claude.use("user")` in T73).
- `storage_full` at 95 % of the disk budget refuses `/_rt` writes; reads continue.
- Every failure rejects with `PfError {code, message, retryable, retry_after?}` using catalogue codes.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Self-publish with a stale version is refused with the newer version; a poll part works for every viewer while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data` reads".

- [ ] All three subtasks closed.
- [ ] A copied claude.ai artifact using `claude.use("db")`, `("user")`, `("comments")` and `("artifact")` runs unchanged on its part host (e2e).
- [ ] Role matrix enforced for every new op (property/table test across every role and guest/link subject).
- [ ] `docs/agent-contract.md` "After Slice 1" list updated (`claude.use(...)` moves into "What a page can do").

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_role_matrix.rs`: table-driven over subjects {link view, guest, view, comment, edit, manage} × ops {db.get, db.set, comments.list, comments.add, artifact.publish, user}; asserts status/`PfError.code`; asserts log events `event="rt.call" op=<op> outcome=<code>` with `principal` and never the doc body.
- `tests/e2e/claude_use_compat.spec.ts`: loads `tests/golden/claude_use/*.html` artifacts, exercises each module, asserts zero uncaught errors (from `runtime_errors`) and expected DOM state; keeps trace + `target/e2e-logs/claude_use_compat/server.jsonl`.

## References

PLAN.md §1 (Keep table: Claude-artifact compatibility), §2 Serving ("Runtime calls: `/_rt`"), §3a role × runtime matrix and "Can contribute" links, §3c "In place, like Claude's artifacts" (persistent state, self-editing parts), §3d data CAS + leases, §6 P3, §10 Slice 1 freeze ambiguity 8, final round F33.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P3 (epic "P3 Claude compatibility"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Self-publish with a stale version is refused with the newer version; a poll part works for every viewer while the part is `shared_data_writers: viewers`; a `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data` reads
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T96: Shared data over /_rt: window.storage, live data.changed, shared_data_writers, part_data for agents
- Unblocks: 
  - M3: Milestone - P3 Claude compatibility done
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T73.a: claude.use("db") and /_rt db.* ops over data_docs, with rev CAS and data leases
  - T73.b: claude.use("user") and claude.use("comments") for page code, guest-local user answer

title: T73.a: claude.use("db") and /_rt db.* ops over data_docs, with rev CAS and data leases
description:
## Goal and why

Claude artifacts persist structured state with `claude.use("db")`. partifactory serves it from the same `data_docs` table that `window.storage` and `part_data` use, so agents and pages see one truth and data snapshots (T77) cover it. Leases give pages Claude's `db.acquire` coordination.

## Scope

- Prelude: `claude.use("db")` returns an object with the Claude db API (get/set/delete/list over collections, `acquire`/release leases), each call a `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1` `{op: "db.<verb>", args}`.
- Server: `db.*` ops reading/writing `data_docs` with `scope = 'shared'` (and `personal` where the API exposes per-user docs), any `collection` other than the reserved `__storage` (and `_assets`, T83):
```sql
CREATE TABLE data_docs (
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  scope      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('shared','personal')),
  owner      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',               -- user id for personal, '' for shared
  collection TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- '__storage' for window.storage
  doc_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  body       BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) <= 262144),
  rev        INTEGER NOT NULL,                       -- CAS
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_by TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- user:<id> | conn:<id> | link:<id> | guest:<link>:<g>
  CHECK ((scope = 'shared') = (owner = '')),
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, scope, owner, collection, doc_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE data_leases (
  part_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
  collection TEXT NOT NULL,
  doc_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  holder     TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, collection, doc_id)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- Per-document compare-and-set on `rev` (`if_rev`; `0` = must not exist); conflict → `if_match_failed {collection, doc_id, current_rev}`.
- Limits as for shared data: doc ≤ 256 KiB, shared data ≤ 5 MiB per part (`parts.shared_data_cap`, `quota_exceeded` past it); writes 60/min per guest (300 per IP), 600/min per signed-in person per part; reads 600 requests/min per viewer per part.
- Writes emit `data.changed {key, op, by}` events (key = `<collection>/<doc_id>` for db docs, document the exact form) on `/_rt/events` so open pages update live.
- Write permission follows `shared_data_writers` and the role matrix: guests on Can contribute links write (rate-limited); Can-view link viewers never; `view`/`comment` write unless `editors`.
- Every write labelled in `updated_by`; documents carry `provenance` (`person`, `agent`, `link_viewer`) when read by agents.
- Lease semantics: advisory, TTL-bounded, holder = the viewer principal; released on expiry or explicit release.

## Not in scope

`window.storage` (T96), `part_data` op itself (T96; this task must just keep it reading the same rows), snapshots (T77).

## Design notes and decisions

- "Data (`window.storage`/`db`) has per-document compare-and-set (`rev`) plus leases, exactly like Claude's `db`, and is separate from source versioning" (§3d).
- `storage_full` refuses writes at 95 % of the disk budget, never reads/deletes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data {collection, doc_id}` reads (dag2.py).
- [ ] A poll part works for every viewer while `shared_data_writers: viewers` (dag2.py).
- [ ] CAS conflict returns `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`; lease held by another holder is reported, then acquirable after expiry.
- [ ] Guests write only via Can contribute links and within limits; Can-view never writes.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::rt::db::tests::cas_conflict`, `::lease_expiry`, `::size_limit_256k`, `::shared_cap_quota_exceeded`.
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_db_part_data_same_row.rs`: write via `/_rt db.set`, read via `part_data` op; assert identical `rev`, `updated_by`; logs `event="rt.call" op="db.set" outcome="ok"` with no body.
- `tests/e2e/poll_part.spec.ts`: two signed-in viewers vote; both see updates within 1 s via `data.changed`.

## References

PLAN.md §3c persistent state, §3d data CAS + leases, §3a limits and who-writes table, §5e `data_docs`, `data_leases`; §10 Slice 1 freeze ambiguity 8.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- `data.changed` for db docs: don't overload `key`; the payload gains `collection` and `doc_id` (keeping `key` for `__storage`), and the prelude's `on("data.changed")` consumer is updated. Final shape: `{key?, collection, doc_id, op, by}`.
- Claude's `db` is shared-only: no personal db docs (personal state is `window.storage`).
- Tests added: `view_role_refused_when_editors` (`forbidden_view_only`) and `can_view_link_never_writes`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A `claude.use("db")` document is the same row `part_data {collection, doc_id}` reads (dag2.py).
- [ ] A poll part works for every viewer while `shared_data_writers: viewers` (dag2.py).
- [ ] CAS conflict returns `if_match_failed` with `current_rev`; lease held by another holder is reported, then acquirable after expiry.
- [ ] Guests write only via Can contribute links and within limits; Can-view never writes.

title: T73.b: claude.use("user") and claude.use("comments") for page code, guest-local user answer
description:
## Goal and why

Claude artifacts ask who the viewer is (`claude.use("user")`) and read/add comments (`claude.use("comments")`). Supporting both keeps copied artifacts working, while the role matrix keeps guests and link viewers from acting as people.

## Scope

- `claude.use("user")`: `/_rt` op `user` returns the viewer's display identity for signed-in subjects (display name, a stable opaque id for this part, role). For **guests** the prelude answers **locally**, without a `/_rt` call, as "Guest <g-prefix>" (e.g. "Guest 4f2a") from the signed `g` claim carried in the cap; for Can-view public-link viewers return an anonymous viewer object (document the exact shape, matching Claude's API).
- `claude.use("comments")`: `/_rt` ops `comments.list`, `comments.add` (and resolve where the role allows), backed by the T50 comments service (`comments` table: `thread_id`, `parent_id`, `version_id`, `anchor` `{block?|file,lines?, quote}`, `body` ≤ 16384, `provenance` in `person|agent|link_viewer`, `to_agent`).
- Role enforcement: comments need `comment` or higher; public-link viewers only if the part opted in (`parts.link_comments = 1`, comment-role link); guests never (`403`).
- Guest caps calling `user` or any non-data op on the server get `403` (they never should, since the prelude answers locally).
- Runtime errors from guest tabs are not collected.

## Not in scope

Comments storage, threads, provenance wrapping for MCP (T50); agent inbox (T84).

## Design notes and decisions

- Round 2c interpretation: "Guests get `403` on `user` and `errors.report` too. The prelude answers `claude.use("user")` locally for guests." F33: the guest answer waits for `claude.use("user")` here; `partifactory.user()` is not defined anywhere and must not be invented.
- Never reveal more about other people than the part's audience allows: `user` returns the viewer only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Signed-in viewer gets their identity from `claude.use("user")`; guest gets "Guest xxxx" with no network call (asserted via request log).
- [ ] `comment`-role viewer can add a comment from page code; `view` can't (`forbidden`); guest gets 403.
- [ ] Comments added from page code carry `provenance: person` (or `link_viewer` for opted-in link viewers).

## Tests

- `pf_serve::rt::user::tests::guest_server_call_forbidden`, `pf_prelude` JS unit test `user_guest_local.test.js`.
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/rt_comments_roles.rs`: role table; asserts `event="rt.call" op="comments.add"` outcome per role, body never logged.
- `tests/e2e/claude_use_user_comments.spec.ts`: guest tab vs signed-in tab; HAR shows no `/_rt` `user` call from the guest.

## References

PLAN.md §3a role × runtime matrix and "Can contribute" (guest identity), §10 round 2c interpretations, final round F33, §5e `comments`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Ownership: T50.a owns the server `/_rt` `comments.*` ops; this subtask owns only the prelude `claude.use("comments")` module and the page-code role e2e.

title: T73.c: claude.use("artifact") self-publish with CAS against live == head
description:
## Goal and why

"Self-editing parts: `claude.use("artifact").publish(...)` lets a part save a new version of itself, using compare-and-set against the version it's running, which must also be head. Viewers with `edit` can do it. Public-link viewers never can." (PLAN.md §3c). This is the "pages that save themselves" half of Claude compatibility.

## Scope

- Prelude: `claude.use("artifact")` exposes `publish(...)` (Claude's shape: new content/files for the running artifact).
- `/_rt` op `artifact.publish`: requires role `edit`/`manage`; the request carries the version id the page is running (from the cap's `v`/served version); the server commits a new version through the `part_edit` engine (T46) only if `running == live == head`; otherwise refuses with the newer version (Claude's "a publish that loses a race is refused and handed the newer version to merge onto") using `version_conflict {head}` (409, CLI exit 5).
- The new version: `versions.via = 'self_publish'`, `author_user` = the viewer, `actor_conn` NULL; goes through the build like any version; `live` moves on an `ok` build (or per `live_gate`).
- Requires `request_id` semantics like every write (idempotent replay within 24 h).
- Limits: each file ≤ 2 MiB, request ≤ 8 MiB; `storage_full` at 95 % of the disk budget; per-person write rate limits.
- Viewers with `view`/`comment`, public-link viewers and guests → `403`.

The edit engine and rebase (T46); live reload UX (T79).

- CAS against live == head (not rebase): a page publishing itself has no anchors; a blind overwrite of someone else's newer version would lose work. Refuse and hand back the newer version.

- [ ] A retried publish with the same `request_id` returns `replayed: true`.

title: T83: Viewer asset uploads: assets.put over /_rt, /_a/<id>, quota, listed and deletable by agents
description:
## Goal and why

Parts like a photo board or a receipts tracker need viewers to add files from the page. M3's done-when includes "a viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox". Assets let a viewer add a file without changing the part's code, and let agents see and manage those files through the one data op. P3, after Slice 1. Depends on T62 (prelude, `/_rt`) and T26 (policy engine, role × runtime matrix).

## Scope

- `/_rt` op `assets.put`: `POST /c/<cap>/_rt/v1 {op: "assets.put"}` (body form documented: the file bytes travel as a separate upload in the same simple-request style — no preflight; specify the exact encoding, e.g. a text/plain POST of a JSON envelope for metadata followed by a raw upload to `/c/<cap>/_rt/v1/assets` with `Content-Type: text/plain` to stay CORS-simple). **25 MiB each** (`assets.size CHECK (size <= 26214400)`), counted against the **space quota**.
- Role: viewers with **`comment` or higher** ("assets upload" column of the role × runtime matrix: `comment` yes, `edit`/`manage` yes, `view` no, public-link viewers and guests no). A guest cap calling `assets.put` gets `403`.
- Stored as **part blobs** (temp → fsync → verify → rename), served at **`/_a/<id>` behind the cap** on the part host (`Cache-Control: private`, never in a shared cache), with `Content-Disposition` handling and the canonical CSP for document-like types (an uploaded HTML/SVG must never execute outside the sandbox; serve active types as `attachment` or sandboxed).
- Schema (exists from T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE assets (                                -- viewer uploads (P3)
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- a_...; served at /_a/<id>
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  blob_hash   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES blobs(hash),
  mime        TEXT NOT NULL,
  size        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (size <= 26214400),
  name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  uploaded_by TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- user:<id> | conn:<id>
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  deleted_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX assets_part ON assets(part_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```
- Agents: listed and deletable via **`part_data {collection: "_assets"}`** (`list` returns asset docs with `provenance`; `delete` soft-deletes, `deleted_at`). Results carry `contains_untrusted: true` when uploaded by someone other than the connection's person.
- Agent uploads for MCP clients: `part_create`/`part_edit {upload: [...]}` returning a 10-minute upload URL, so agents never base64 media through the model ("after Slice 1, with T83's assets; the field is rejected until then"). Implement here and remove the rejection.
- Events: `asset.added` (and a `data.changed`-style event for `_assets`) so open pages and the agent see it; `to_agent` routing of an upload notice is T84's inbox.
- Blob GC (T59) marks from `assets`; disk budget 95 % → `storage_full`.

## Not in scope

The agent inbox (T84), comments (T50), GC itself (T59).

## Design notes and decisions

- Body cap "25 MiB per media blob or asset" is from §5d; request bodies are capped before auth on unauthenticated routes.
- Assets are a property of the part's data, not its versions: they survive edits and are in exports (blobs referenced by assets are exported).
- Prompt-injection hygiene: asset names are untrusted; `provenance` labels them.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A viewer uploads a photo from a part and an agent lists it via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`".

- [ ] `comment` viewer uploads ≤ 25 MiB; > 25 MiB → `too_large` (413); `view` viewer and guest → 403.
- [ ] Asset served at `/_a/<id>` only with a valid cap for that part's host; `Cache-Control: private`.
- [ ] Agent lists and deletes via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`; list carries `contains_untrusted`.
- [ ] Upload counts against the space quota (`quota_exceeded` past it).
- [ ] `upload` field on `part_create`/`part_edit` accepted and returns a 10-minute URL.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::rt::assets::tests::size_limit`, `::role_matrix`, `::quota`.
- `crates/pf-serve/tests/assets_served_under_cap.rs`: wrong-host cap → 404; asserts headers; logs `event="asset.put" outcome="ok" size=..` without the name/content.
- `tests/e2e/viewer_photo_upload.spec.ts`: a comment-role person uploads a photo from a part; agent driver calls `part_data` list and sees it; artifacts: trace + server.jsonl.

## References

PLAN.md §3c "Assets (P3)", §3a role × runtime matrix, §3d big files (upload URLs), §5d body and size caps, §5e `assets`, §6 P3.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P3 (epic "P3 Claude compatibility"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A viewer uploads a photo from a part and an agent lists it via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
- Unblocks: 
  - M3: Milestone - P3 Claude compatibility done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T96 (`part_data {collection: "_assets"}` is T96.c's op) and T46 (the `upload` field touches `part_edit`'s write path).
- Decided: `assets.put` uploads as `multipart/form-data` via `FormData` POST to `/c/<cap>/_rt/v1/assets` (CORS-simple, binary-safe, carries filename and mime); `assets.put` on `/_rt/v1` first returns a short-lived upload ticket; the 25 MiB body cap is enforced before auth.
- Routing of an upload notice to the steward is T84's: T83 emits `asset.added`; T84 (edge added: T83 → T84) turns it into an inbox item, and the M3 e2e `photo_upload_in_inbox` lives in T84.
- Contract: `docs/agent-contract.md` op sections and the "After Slice 1" list are updated in the same change; T56's registry-match test stays green. (`upload` on `part_create`/`part_edit`, the `_assets` collection in `part_data`; "upload URLs" leaves the After list).
- Split into T83.a / T83.b (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: A viewer uploads a photo from a part and an agent lists it via `part_data {collection: "_assets"}`

title: T84: Agent inbox and steward: part_inbox op, to_agent routing, open/claimed/answered/resolved, stalled
description:
## Goal and why

"Comment from your phone and have the agent fix it" is a kept shartifacts idea (`to_claude` + `watch`); partifactory adds an **agent inbox** so a `to_agent` comment reliably reaches the right agent connection, and people can see it's being handled. P3. Depends on T50 (comments with `to_agent`), T51 (event log), T53 (MCP server, where `part_inbox` appears as a tool).

## Scope

- **Steward**: each part has a steward — "the creating connection and its person, changeable in the share sheet" (`parts.steward_conn`). A `to_agent` comment goes to the steward.
- **`part_inbox` op** (registry, so on MCP, HTTP, CLI): "work addressed to this connection across parts: `to_agent` comments and runtime-error spikes; claim/answer". Actions: list (open items for this connection), `claim`, `answer` (link to the version or comment reply that answers it), with `request_id` on writes. Output items carry `provenance` and `contains_untrusted`; MCP text wraps untrusted content in `<untrusted_content>`.
- **States**: `open → claimed ("Hermes is on it") → answered → resolved` (`comments.agent_state IN ('open','claimed','answered')`; resolved = `resolved_at`).
- **Stalled**: "A claimed request with no new version after 15 minutes shows 'stalled'." Computed from the claim time vs the part's newest version.
- **Delivery**: push agents (Hermes) get a signed webhook (the event-log webhooks, T123, targets in site config); pull agents get it via `part_inbox`; "the shared guide tells them to check it at session start" — add this to `docs/agent-contract.md` with the op's section (`<!-- pf:op part_inbox -->`, generated field table + `Errors:` line, T56's test).
- UI: the comments rail shows "Hermes is on it", then "Fixed in REV 14 · View diff", and "stalled".
- Scope: needs `comments:write` for claim/answer; `parts:read` to list.

## Not in scope

Comments themselves, provenance (T50); webhooks infrastructure (T123); notifications for people (non-goal: there are none).

## Design notes and decisions

- No approval queues: the inbox is work addressed to an *agent*, never something waiting on a person (decision 34).
- Steward changeable by owner in the share sheet; defaults to creating connection; if that connection is revoked, fall back to "no steward" and show it.
- Runtime-error spikes: define threshold (e.g. a new fingerprint or count jump in `runtime_errors` per version) as an open design point; recommended default: a new fingerprint seen ≥ 3 times in 10 min.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A comment for the steward appears in its inbox; claiming shows 'Hermes is on it'; no version after 15 min shows 'stalled'".

- [ ] `to_agent` comment appears in the steward connection's `part_inbox` and nobody else's.
- [ ] Claim sets `agent_state = 'claimed'` and the rail shows "<agent> is on it".
- [ ] 15 min with no new version (test clock) → "stalled".
- [ ] Answer/resolve transitions audited; contract section passes T56's regeneration test.

## Tests

- `pf_model::inbox::tests::routing_to_steward`, `::state_machine`, `::stalled_after_15m` (test clock).
- `tests/agent_surfaces/scenario.yaml` gains inbox steps; run on all four drivers.
- `tests/e2e/agent_inbox.spec.ts`: person comments "For the agent"; scripted agent claims; UI shows chip; logs `event="inbox.claim" outcome="ok" principal=conn:..`.

## References

PLAN.md §1 (Keep: comments addressed to the agent), §3c "Agent inbox (P3)", §4 ops table (`part_inbox`), §4a.6 Comments, §5e `parts.steward_conn`, `comments.agent_state`, §6 P3.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P3 (epic "P3 Claude compatibility"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A comment for the steward appears in its inbox; claiming shows 'Hermes is on it'; no version after 15 min shows 'stalled'
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
  - T51: Event log (Slice 1 part): events table, in-memory broadcast, /_rt/events SSE (data.changed, pf:version), v0 placeholder live update
  - T53: MCP server (rmcp, stateless Streamable HTTP): tools from the registry, annotations, resources as projections, instructions
- Unblocks: 
  - M3: Milestone - P3 Claude compatibility done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T83 (asset uploads, `asset.added`, become inbox items for the steward; this task owns that routing and the M3 e2e `photo_upload_in_inbox`), T120 (the steward picker and the "Hermes is on it"/"stalled" chips live in its share sheet and comments rail) and T123 (webhook delivery to push agents).
- Decided: a runtime-error spike is a new fingerprint seen ≥ 3 times in 10 minutes on the live version; one inbox item per (fingerprint, version); thresholds in `[inbox] error_spike = {count: 3, window: "10m"}`.
- Steward fallback: when `steward_conn` is revoked, route to the owner's most recent live connection with the same agent name (a re-paired Hermes), else "no steward" is shown.
- Tests added: a webhook delivery test for an inbox item, `asset_added_routes_to_steward`, `photo_upload_in_inbox` (M3 e2e).
acceptance_criteria: A comment for the steward appears in its inbox; claiming shows 'Hermes is on it'; no version after 15 min shows 'stalled'

description:
## Goal and why

Exit of phase **P3 Claude compatibility**: anything Claude writes as an artifact runs here unchanged, including state that persists and pages that save themselves. The spec is shartifacts' compatibility matrix (credited to Lane Birmingham, MIT).

## Scope

`claude.use` (`db`, `user`, `comments`, `artifact` incl. self-publish; shared `window.storage` arrived in P2), Tailwind + shadcn (mechanism chosen on evidence), viewer uploads (assets), and the agent inbox with stewards. Direct dependencies: T61, T73, T83, T84.

## Acceptance criteria (P3 "Done when")

- [ ] A page copied from a claude.ai artifact runs unchanged, including state persistence and self-editing.
- [ ] A viewer's photo upload reaches the agent's inbox.

## References

PLAN.md §6 Phases (P3), §1 Keep table (Claude-artifact compatibility).

## Dependency context

- This milestone depends on (blocks edges): 
  - T61: Tailwind + shadcn support for Claude-written parts, mechanism chosen on evidence
  - T73: claude.use(db, user, comments, artifact) in the prelude, self-publish CAS, data leases
  - T83: Viewer asset uploads: assets.put over /_rt, /_a/<id>, quota, listed and deletable by agents
  - T84: Agent inbox and steward: part_inbox op, to_agent routing, open/claimed/answered/resolved, stalled
- Unblocks: nothing

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans).

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- The Done-when's "a viewer upload reaches the agent" is owned by T83 (emit) + T84 (inbox routing); its e2e is `photo_upload_in_inbox` (T84).
acceptance_criteria: A page copied from a claude.ai artifact runs unchanged, including state persistence and self-editing; a viewer upload reaches the agent

title: T71: WASM component backends as an optional alternative to containers (only with an ADR)
description:
## Goal and why

P5, "later, only if needed". Containers are the backend model because "every language and every database already ships as an OCI image, and agents already know how to write a Dockerfile. WASM components stay an optional later alternative" (§3f). This task exists only if a real part is served badly by containers (cold-start, memory, density). Depends on M2a (backends done).

## Scope

- **Gate first**: an ADR (`docs/adr/NNNN-wasm-backends.md`) naming a concrete part that containers serve badly, with measurements (cold start, memory per part vs the per-part defaults 1 CPU / 512 MiB / 256 pids). Without the ADR, close this task as not needed.
- If adopted: a WASM component runtime (e.g. wasmtime with WASI) as a second backend kind, **under the same grant model and routing**: reached only at `/c/<cap>/api/*` behind the cap check and role × runtime matrix; cookies, the cap, `pf_` tokens and every `X-PF-*` header stripped; the signed `X-PF-Identity` JWT (HS256, per-part key, 60 s expiry, claims `sub`, `name`, `role`, `part`, `exp`) and `X-PF-Request-Id` added; no unauthenticated route.
- Same lifecycle semantics where they apply: one instance set per live version, health-gated `live`, rollback rolls back, scale to zero, quotas (`quota_exceeded {kind}`), logs captured per part with the same retention caps (50 MiB / 7 days).
- Network policy equivalent to containers: internet egress on, LAN/host/other parts blocked, per-part LAN allowlist honoured.
- Write-only per-part secrets injected the same way.

## Not in scope

Replacing containers; any change to the compose subset for container parts.

## Design notes and decisions

- Non-goal for v1 ("WASM backends in v1"). The ADR rule prevents building it speculatively.
- The §7 Backends lines must all pass for the WASM kind (escape attempts, LAN reachability, identity-header forgery, secrets).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "An ADR names a part that containers serve badly; a WASM component serves it behind `/c/<cap>/api/*` with the §7 Backends lines green".

- [ ] ADR committed with measurements.
- [ ] The named part's WASM backend serves behind `/c/<cap>/api/*`.
- [ ] Every §7 Backends line has a WASM variant and passes.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-runner/tests/wasm_identity_header.rs`, `wasm_lan_blocked.rs`, `wasm_secrets_write_only.rs`; logs `event="backend.request" runtime="wasm" outcome`.

title: T87: Optional S3-compatible upload of scheduled exports, and import --from s3://
description:
## Goal and why

Backup layer 3 in the three-layer table: "the scheduled export also pushed to an S3-compatible bucket (R2 is one example) | partifactory's, behind config | Not needed for v1 (P5)". An off-site copy without a separate tool. Depends on T34 (export, nightly schedule, keep 7).

## Scope

- Config (behind config, off by default): bucket endpoint, bucket, prefix, region, access key id and secret (secrets as `PF_*` env or `PF_*_FILE`, never in `site.toml`; e.g. `PF_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY`), retention count.
- After each scheduled export (`partifactory-<ts>.tar.zst` in `/data/exports`, optionally age-encrypted to the recipient public key), upload it to the bucket; never on the save path ("No save ever waits on a backup target"). Retries with backoff; failure is a Health row and (if enabled) an ops alert, never blocks anything.
- `partifactory import --from s3://<bucket>/<key>` downloads and runs the normal import (verify hashes against `MANIFEST.json`, load DB, forward migrations, write blobs, **bump the boot epoch**).
- Health / `doctor`: layer 3 shown on/off with last upload age.
- Drill: the monthly laptop drill can restore from S3.

## Not in scope

Export/import format (T34/T35); host snapshots (layer 1, host's job).

## Design notes and decisions

- Rejected earlier: a storage-agnostic sink outbox on the core path, Litestream (v0.5 dropped age encryption), R2 as a built-in (§10). This stays an upload of a finished export file.
- Encrypt with age when uploading off-site; recommend `--encrypt` be required for S3 upload (state as a design default: refuse to upload an unencrypted full export unless `[unsafe]` allows it).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Behind config; an export lands in a test bucket and `import --from s3://...` restores it".

- [ ] Off by default; enabling needs config + secret.
- [ ] Scheduled export uploaded to a test bucket (MinIO in CI).
- [ ] `import --from s3://…` restores an identical part set.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-backup/tests/s3_upload_roundtrip.rs` against MinIO: export → upload → import → compare part/version counts; logs `event="backup.s3_upload" outcome="ok" bytes=..`, secret never logged (canary).
- `pf_backup::s3::tests::retry_backoff`.

## References

PLAN.md §5c Backups (three-layer table, export, import, drills), §5b env contract, §10 round 2 rejected items, §6 P5.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P5 (epic "P5 Later, only if needed"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Behind config; an export lands in a test bucket and `import --from s3://...` restores it
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
- Unblocks: nothing directly

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T35 (`import --from s3://` is `partifactory import`).
- Decided: S3 upload requires `--encrypt` (`backup.age_recipient` set); an unencrypted full export is never uploaded off-site unless `[unsafe] s3_unencrypted = "off"` is set, and `doctor` fails when S3 upload is on without a recipient. A full export holds sessions, refresh tokens and optionally secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Behind config; an export lands in a test bucket and `import --from s3://...` restores it

title: T88: Semantic search (embeddings) alongside FTS5, hybrid ranking, off by default
description:
## Goal and why

P5, only if needed: "Later, additive: embeddings for semantic search alongside FTS5 (P5). Nothing in v1 depends on them." Helps "find that thing from last week" when the words don't match. Depends on T76 (FTS5 search).

## Scope

- Optional embeddings index over the same indexed fields as FTS5 (title, description, tags, agent notes, comments, extracted readable text — not code).
- Embedding model runs locally (no third-party service: "Third-party analytics or telemetry services" are non-goals and parts' text must not leave the box); model choice recorded in an ADR; vectors stored in SQLite (a table in `partifactory.db` or a separate file, decided in the ADR), updated when a version goes live and when notes or comments change.
- **Hybrid ranking**: combine FTS5 `bm25` (column weights title 10, tags 5, description 4, notes 3, text 1, comments 2) × recency `1 / (1 + age_days / 30)` with vector similarity (e.g. reciprocal-rank fusion); filters (`space:`, `kind:`, `by:`, `updated:`, `has:data`, `has:comments`, `tag:`) apply to both.
- Used by the workspace search box and `part_find`.
- **Disabled → FTS5-only behaviour unchanged.** The index is a capped store (add a §5h row and a fill-past-cap case to T115's test).
- A labelled query set `tests/golden/search/labelled.yaml`.

## Not in scope

FTS5 search itself (T76), `part_find` op (T122).

## Design notes and decisions

- p99 for `part_find` over 10k parts is < 5 ms with FTS5; hybrid may cost more — measure and record; keep FTS-only path as fast as before.
- New growing store must follow "every growing store has a cap…" (§5h) or `doctor` fails.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Hybrid ranking beats FTS5 alone on a labelled query set; FTS5-only behaviour is unchanged when disabled".

- [ ] Labelled set: hybrid nDCG@10 (or MRR) > FTS5-only, reported.
- [ ] Disabled: search results byte-identical to T76's golden results.
- [ ] Index capped and in the retention test.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-model/tests/search_hybrid_eval.rs` (labelled set metric).
- `pf_model::search::tests::disabled_matches_fts_golden`.
- Logs `event="search.query" mode="hybrid|fts" latency_us` with no query text.

## References

PLAN.md §3e Search, §5h, §6 P5, §9 Non-goals (third-party services).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P5 (epic "P5 Later, only if needed"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Hybrid ranking beats FTS5 alone on a labelled query set; FTS5-only behaviour is unchanged when disabled
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T76: Search: FTS5 over title, tags, notes, readable text and comments; filters; bm25 + recency
- Unblocks: nothing directly

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Decided: embeddings live in a separate file `/data/search.db` with its own writer (rebuildable, excluded from exports unless `--include-search`), keeping the frozen v1 DDL and the save path untouched; embedding updates run off the writer in a janitor-style queue.
- Edge added: T122 (`part_find` is T122's; this task changes its ranking).
- The ADR names the local runtime (e.g. `ort` or `candle` with a small ONNX model) and its binary-size / cargo-feature impact.

title: T90: Built-in ACME DNS-01 TLS (wildcard cert via a DNS provider plugin) for hosts with no proxy
description:
## Goal and why

The ingress contract normally puts a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, Traefik) or the Cloudflare tunnel in front. For a host with neither, the binary can obtain and serve its own wildcard cert: "OR (P5) the binary's own ACME" (§3 Topology), the "built-in ACME DNS-01 (P5, for hosts with no proxy)" adapter in §5f. P5. Depends on T32 (`provision` with the `DnsProvider` plugin trait) and T89 (ingress contract).

## Scope

- `[ingress] kind = "acme"` (site.toml `[ingress]` kind = proxy | cloudflare-tunnel | acme).
- ACME DNS-01 for one wildcard cert covering `parts.<domain>` and `*.<domain>` (DNS wildcards must be a whole label), using a `DnsProvider` plugin to set `_acme-challenge` TXT records (token `PF_DNS_API_TOKEN`, env or `_FILE`).
- The binary terminates TLS itself on the workspace and content listeners (routing by `Host`: `parts.<domain>` → workspace, `*.<domain>` → content), keeping the ingress contract's guarantees: client IP from the socket (no trusted proxy header needed), request ids generated, long-lived responses (SSE, long-poll ≤ 50 s) and 8 MiB bodies.
- Renewal before expiry (e.g. at 2/3 of lifetime), cert stored under `/data` (in exports? decide: exclude private key from parts-only exports; full exports include it or re-issue on import — recommended: re-issue), Health row for cert expiry, `doctor` checks coverage and expiry.
- The `:9090` ops listener remains plain and never exposed.

## Not in scope

Proxy example configs (T89, T126); Cloudflare adapter (T91).

## Design notes and decisions

- Adapter, never required: "Nothing. Without a tunnel the host needs an inbound port" (§5f). Default remains a reverse proxy.
- A failed renewal must never take the site down while the old cert is valid; alert at 14 days left.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "The portability lane passes with no proxy in front; the cert renews before expiry in a test with a short-lived ACME staging cert".

- [ ] Portability lane variant with `kind = "acme"` and no proxy is green (Pebble or ACME staging in CI).
- [ ] Short-lived cert renews automatically before expiry.
- [ ] `doctor` reports cert coverage and expiry; Health shows it.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/acme_pebble.rs`: issue + renew with Pebble and a fake DNS provider; logs `event="acme.renew" outcome="ok" not_after=..`.
- Portability lane job `portability-acme` (T93 variant).

## References

PLAN.md §3 Topology and ingress contract, §5c `provision` (DnsProvider, site.toml `[ingress]`), §5f Ingress + TLS row, §6 P5.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P5 (epic "P5 Later, only if needed"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): The portability lane passes with no proxy in front; the cert renews before expiry in a test with a short-lived ACME staging cert
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T32: `partifactory provision` framework: DnsProvider/IdpProvisioner traits, manual providers, ownership, family+system spaces
  - T89: Ingress contract: trusted client-IP header, request ids, Caddy example + maintenance page
- Unblocks: nothing directly

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T93 ("the portability lane passes with no proxy in front").
- Decided: ACME material lives under `/data/acme/` (mode 600), is excluded from every export (cert, private key, account key), and is **re-issued on import**; DNS-01 takes minutes, well inside the 15-minute RTO. Drills use the ACME staging endpoint to dodge rate limits.
- Adds the alert condition `cert_expires_14d` to T121's list (this task is the producer).
acceptance_criteria: The portability lane passes with no proxy in front; the cert renews before expiry in a test with a short-lived ACME staging cert

title: Phase P4 Family + Nest + phone
description:
# Phase P4 Family + Nest + phone

## Goal and why

Phase P4: family onboarding, embedding via `[embed] frame_ancestors` (the Nest, with its service identity), the Hermes
`nest-family` profile, slides + Mermaid, the optional OTLP export adapter, screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery
and opt-in screenshot cards for public links, and tap-to-edit text and point-and-comment on phones. (Notifications for
people were cut in round 2b, and approval queues in round 2c.)

*Done when (M4):* a family member opens a Nest-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it on the phone, long-presses to ask
Hermes for a change, and Hermes, watching the event log, tells them in its own chat when the fix lands.

## Members

- T63: Family onboarding: invite into the family space, first-run tour, personal space
- T64: Embedding via [embed] frame_ancestors and pf-embed.js, plus service identities (the Nest first)
- T65: Hermes nest-family profile: family-space-only agent profile for the household chat
- T66: Slides kind plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides (block = slide)
- T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
- T85: Phone editing: tap-to-edit text as anchor edits, long-press point-and-comment
- T111: Optional OTLP export adapter (traces, logs, metrics) to any collector; off by default, never required

Phase exit: M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans). Working convention (polish round): a task that has subtasks is an **integration/closure bead** (label `has-subtasks`): never start it as a unit of work; implement its subtasks (they become ready with their parent and depend on each other where ordering matters), then close the parent after its end-to-end acceptance passes. A swarm picks leaves with `br ready --exclude-label has-subtasks`. Every bead's `acceptance_criteria` field carries its checklist, so `br update <id> --check-acceptance` can tick items as they pass. Where this polish round deviated from §6a (one reversed edge, one UI slice moved to its backend task, three splits) the bead says so with "polish round".

title: T63: Family onboarding: invite into the family space, first-run tour, personal space
description:
## Goal and why

P4 brings the rest of the household onto partifactory. A new family member must land in a working setup: their own personal space, access to everything in `family` (inherited live), and a short first-run tour — without ever seeing the admin's private parts. Depends on T10 (spaces, live inheritance) and T94 (native invites + local passkey accounts).

## Scope

- **Invite into `family`**: from the admin area (Invites) or the family space, the admin mints an invite whose effect is membership of the household group (the group granted `edit` on `family`: `group:<household> → edit`), using T94's `/i/<id>` tokens (single or "up to N", 7-day default expiry, passkey-only), or with a provisioner, the IdP path (T40). The invitee: open → "What should we call you?" → **Create passkey** → lands on the workspace (budget: **3 + type**).
- **Personal space** created at first sign-in (`spaces.kind = 'personal'`, slug `~<username>`, `spaces_one_personal` unique index), owner-only grants.
- **First-run tour**: a short, dismissible sequence on first sign-in: what a part is, the gallery filters (`Recent · Mine · Shared with me · Family`), Move to Family, connecting an agent ("Connect an agent", the device page). Stockroom copy voice: plain, sentence case, no exclamation marks. Dismissal stored server-side per person.
- **Visibility check**: the member sees all `family` parts (effective access = max(part grants, space grants), inherited live) and none of the admin's private parts.

## Not in scope

Invite mechanics, local accounts, recovery (T94); Authentik invites (T40); Nest embedding (T64); the Hermes family profile (T65).

## Design notes and decisions

- Live inheritance is why this works: "everything in Family is the family's" stays true when someone joins later (§2 Space).
- Adding to `family` is an outward-ish admin action only when it means inviting a *new* person (admin-only, step-up); granting an existing account is inward.
- No notifications are sent; the invite link is shared by the admin in any channel.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A new family member invited to the space sees all family parts and none of the admin's private parts".

- [ ] Invite → passkey → member lands with the household group membership and a personal space.
- [ ] Gallery "Family" filter lists every family part; the admin's personal-space parts return `404 · NOT IN STOCK`/403 per audience rules (never title).
- [ ] Tour shown once, dismissible, not shown again across devices.
- [ ] Click budget for accepting the invite asserted (3 + type).

## Tests

- `pf_policy::tests::family_member_sees_family_not_private` (property over fixture parts).
- `tests/e2e/family_onboarding.spec.ts` (virtual authenticator): admin mints invite, new browser accepts, checks gallery; asserts logs `event="invite.enrolled"`, `event="grant.decision" outcome="deny"` for a private part; keeps trace + server.jsonl.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Space (live inheritance), §3a Spaces table, Invitations, UX click budgets, §4a.6 Gallery and Invites, §6 P4.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A new family member invited to the space sees all family parts and none of the admin's private parts
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T10: Spaces: personal space per person, live-inherited space grants, per-space quota config
  - T94: Native invites + local passkey accounts (no provisioner): /i/<id>, webauthn-rs, recovery, pf-* groups
- Unblocks: 
  - T65: Hermes nest-family profile: family-space-only agent profile for the household chat
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Group model: `family` carries grants for **both** the IdP household group (`group:<household>`, from the claim) and the local `pf-household` group (T94), so the IdP-less lane passes; the invite into `family` adds a local account to the local group (or grants the person on the space directly).
- First-run tour dismissal is stored server-side per person as the `kv` row `tour_dismissed:<user_id>` (across devices; the frozen DDL has no column for it), not in `localStorage`.
- Personal-space creation is T10's; this task only asserts it for the invitee.
acceptance_criteria: A new family member invited to the space sees all family parts and none of the admin's private parts

title: T64: Embedding via [embed] frame_ancestors and pf-embed.js, plus service identities (the Nest first)
description:
## Goal and why

The example deployment's household dashboard (the Nest) should show family parts inline. partifactory supports this generically: any site listed in `[embed] frame_ancestors` may frame parts, and a household-wide agent with no single person (the Nest's server) gets a **service identity** limited to `family`. P4. Depends on T27 (`/grant`, credentialed regrant endpoint for wrappers and embedders) and T44 (device grant: the service connects by device code once at setup). Service identities were moved here from T44 at the Slice 1 freeze ("service identities (T44 → T64)").

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after both subtasks and the Nest e2e/manual pass):
- **T64.a** Embedding: `[embed] frame_ancestors` from site config into the canonical part CSP and the wrapper CSP, embedding the part-host wrapper or `/c/` with a server-minted `src`, and `pf-embed.js` (the `pf:regrant` handler for embedders).
- **T64.b** Service identities: `agent_connections.principal_kind = 'service'`, spaces = `family` only, no human `sub`, writes labelled as the service, `requested_by` recorded as unverified; the Nest as the first service connection.

The canonical part CSP's last line is `frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace> <embedders>`, where `<embedders>` is the site-config list `[embed] frame_ancestors` (**empty by default**; the example deployment lists the Nest). The wrapper's own CSP has `frame-ancestors` = `<workspace> <embedders>`.

## Not in scope

Hermes' family profile (T65); Nest's own code and knowledge base (stays separate from partifactory; non-goal "Replacing the Nest's knowledge base").

## Design notes and decisions

- Portability: embedding is "`frame-ancestors` from `[embed] frame_ancestors`; `pf-embed.js`", default empty: "only the part's own host and the workspace may frame it" (§5f). The Nest is just one entry.
- Framed expiry: a framed part never navigates itself to `/grant` (a subframe navigation from an opaque origin is cross-site for `SameSite=Lax`, so a login page would render inside the frame). The embedder handles `pf:regrant` with a credentialed same-site call and sets a fresh `src`.
- Service identity rationale (§3b): agents that serve the whole household with no single person; one shared person token would be a confused deputy.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A Nest page embeds a family part on iPhone Safari and Android Chrome (manual pass recorded); an origin not in the list cannot frame it; the Nest's writes are labelled as the service".

- [ ] T64.a and T64.b closed.
- [ ] Manual real-device pass recorded (iPhone Safari, Android Chrome): embedded family part loads, survives cap expiry via `pf:regrant`.
- [ ] Origin not in `[embed] frame_ancestors` cannot frame the part host root or `/c/` (CSP blocks).
- [ ] Nest writes show "<service name>" labels in history and the activity feed.

## Tests

- `tests/e2e/embedding.spec.ts` (covering both subtasks): a test embedder page served from an allowed origin and one from a disallowed origin; asserts frame load/block, regrant after a forced short window; logs `event="grant.regrant" surface="embed"`.
- Real-device results recorded in `docs/device-passes/<date>-embedding.md`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 canonical CSP, Framed expiry, "The link to post" (Embedding), §3b Service identities, §4 Example consumers (the Nest), §5f Embedding row, §6 P4, §10 Slice 1 freeze (moved items).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A Nest page embeds a family part on iPhone Safari and Android Chrome (manual pass recorded); an origin not in the list cannot frame it; the Nest's writes are labelled as the service
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T27: /grant hand-off: path-only input, session auth, policy decision, wrap (#pf= fragment) and direct modes, regrant endpoint, 403 page
  - T44: Device grant (RFC 8628) + /device approval page with phishing defences; one connection per (agent, person)
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T64.a: Embedding: [embed] frame_ancestors in CSPs, server-minted src, pf-embed.js regrant handler
  - T64.b: Service identities (principal_kind = service, family only) and the Nest's connection

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T62 (the "survives cap expiry via `pf:regrant`" acceptance needs the prelude's regrant protocol).
acceptance_criteria: A Nest page embeds a family part on iPhone Safari and Android Chrome (manual pass recorded); an origin not in the list cannot frame it; the Nest's writes are labelled as the service

title: T64.a: Embedding: [embed] frame_ancestors in CSPs, server-minted src, pf-embed.js regrant handler
description:
## Goal and why

Let a configured embedder frame family parts safely, keeping the sandbox and cap model intact and handling cap expiry without a navigation inside the frame.

## Scope

- Config: `[embed] frame_ancestors` (list of origins, empty by default) loaded by `pf-config`, validated as https origins.
- CSP: the canonical part CSP's `frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace> <embedders>` and the wrapper CSP's `frame-ancestors <workspace> <embedders>` both take `<embedders>` from config. Nothing else in the CSP changes.
- Two embedding shapes:
  1. frame the **part host root** (the trusted wrapper, with its Stockroom chrome); the wrapper's own `#pf=` / `/grant` flow applies, but inside a frame the wrapper must not `location.replace` to `/grant` when it has no cap (that would render sign-in in a frame); instead it posts to the parent / shows a "Open in partifactory" link.
  2. frame **`/c/<cap>/`** directly with a **server-minted `src`**: the embedder's server obtains a cap for the viewer (service identity or the viewer's session via the credentialed regrant endpoint) and sets it.
- `pf-embed.js` (a shared blob): listens for `{type: "pf:regrant"}` from the framed part (identified by `event.source === frame.contentWindow`, never `event.origin`, which is `"null"`), calls the credentialed regrant endpoint (`POST https://parts.<domain>/api/chrome/v1/<part>/grant` or the embedder variant from T27) and sets a freshly minted `src`, with no navigation; also relays `pf:version`.
- Documentation `docs/embedding.md` with a minimal embedder example.

## Not in scope

Service identities (T64.b); the regrant endpoint itself (T27).

## Design notes and decisions

- Chrome-API CORS admits only part-host origins; an embedder origin calling it would need its own same-site status — embedders on the same registrable domain (like the Nest) are same-site, so the Lax session cookie goes along. Cross-site embedders can only use the server-minted `src` path; document this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Allowed origin frames root and `/c/`; disallowed origin is blocked by `frame-ancestors`.
- [ ] Expiring cap in an embedded frame recovers via `pf-embed.js` without a navigation.
- [ ] Default config (empty list) yields exactly `frame-ancestors <self-host> <workspace>`.

## Tests

- `pf_serve::csp::tests::frame_ancestors_from_config` (golden header strings).
- `tests/e2e/embedding.spec.ts` (shared with parent): asserts `event="grant.regrant"` log lines and no frame navigation (Playwright frame navigation listener).

## References

PLAN.md §2 canonical CSP, Framed expiry, Embedding bullet, wrapper CSP; §4a.6 Frame (`event.source` rule); §5f Embedding row.

## Dependency context
