title: T64.b: Service identities (principal_kind = service, family only) and the Nest's connection
description:
## Goal and why

"Service identities for agents that serve the whole household with no single person, such as the Nest's server: `principal_kind = service`, spaces = `family` only, no human `sub`. Writes are labelled as the service. A caller-supplied `requested_by` is recorded and shown as unverified." (PLAN.md §3b). This avoids the confused-deputy problem of running a household service on one person's token.

## Scope

- Schema (exists from T06):
```sql
CREATE TABLE agent_connections (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- c_...
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('oauth_code','device','pat')),
  principal_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'person' CHECK (principal_kind IN ('person','service')),
  client_id   TEXT REFERENCES oauth_clients(id),
  user_id     TEXT REFERENCES users(id),             -- NULL for a service identity
  agent_name  TEXT NOT NULL, software TEXT,
  scopes      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(scopes)),
  spaces      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(spaces)),
  expires_at  INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_used_at INTEGER, revoked_at INTEGER,
  quota_versions_day INTEGER,
  CHECK ((principal_kind = 'person') = (user_id IS NOT NULL))
) STRICT;
```
  (abbreviated; the T06 migration has the full DDL).
- Creating a service connection: only the admin, with step-up, via the device grant (`/device` approval page gains "Approve as a service identity" for the admin) — "device code once at setup, service identity"; typical scopes `parts:read`, `parts:write` in `family`. Spaces are forced to `["family"]`.
- Policy: the service acts with its own grants in `family` only; any other space → `forbidden {space}`. It is never `everyone-signed-in` and holds no personal space.
- Labelling: versions/grants/data writes record `actor_conn` = the service connection and author = the service (UI "Nest"), not a person; `requested_by` (caller-supplied) recorded in `audit`/event payload and shown "unverified".
- Revocation cascades as for any connection (refresh family, tokens, minter epoch bump).
- The Nest configured as the first service connection in the example deployment (site config only).

## Not in scope

Embedding (T64.a); device grant itself (T44).

## Design notes and decisions

- `versions.author_user` is `NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)`; a service has no user. Decide and document: create a reserved system user row per service (`users.auth_source` must be `oidc` or `local`; recommended: a `local` row with `status='active'`, `in_audience = 0`, never able to sign in — no passkey) so FKs hold. Record this as a design decision in the bead's PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Service connection creatable only by the admin with step-up; spaces fixed to `family`.
- [ ] Service write to a non-family space → `forbidden {space}`.
- [ ] Writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` shown as unverified.

## Tests

- `pf_policy::tests::service_identity_family_only`, `pf_oauth::device::tests::service_approval_requires_admin_stepup`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/service_writes_labelled.rs`: history row shows service label; logs `principal=conn:c_.. principal_kind=service`.

## References

PLAN.md §3b One connection per (agent, person) (Service identities), Revocation cascades table (Nest row), §5e `agent_connections`, §10 Slice 1 freeze (T44 → T64).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T64: Embedding via [embed] frame_ancestors and pf-embed.js, plus service identities (the Nest first) (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

**Decided (polish round): adopt the reserved service user row, with these specifics.** Alternatives rejected: making `versions.author_user` (and `parts.owner_user_id`, `created_by_user`, `part_notes`, `part_secrets.set_by_user`, `comments.author_user`) nullable needs table rebuilds of the frozen v1 DDL; attributing service writes to the approving admin recreates the "Nest for Chris" confused-deputy label §3b rejects; one shared `system` user loses per-service labelling in history (acceptable fallback only).
- One `users` row per service: `auth_source = 'local'`, `idp_issuer`/`idp_sub` NULL (the CHECK holds), `username = 'svc-<name>'` (the `svc-` prefix is reserved: T94.b's local-account creation and `admin bootstrap` refuse it), `display_name` = the service name, `in_audience = 0`, `status = 'active'`, no `passkeys` row (so it can never sign in; recovery links refuse it).
- `agent_connections.user_id` stays NULL for `principal_kind = 'service'` (its CHECK requires that); a new forward-only migration adds `service_users(user_id PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id), conn_id REFERENCES agent_connections(id), created_at)` to map the connection to its row. Only FK author/owner columns point at the service user, so history shows `author = Nest, actor = conn:<id>`.
- Every people-facing list excludes service users via that table: admin People, invites and cleanup lists (T42), the directory type-ahead and group pickers, `everyone-signed-in` (already `in_audience = 0`), directory sync (T25/T92 never touch them).
- Tests add: `service_user_cannot_authenticate_any_path`, `service_user_not_listed_anywhere`, `service_user_in_audience_zero`, `svc_prefix_refused_for_local_accounts`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Service connection creatable only by the admin with step-up; spaces fixed to `family`.
- [ ] Service write to a non-family space → `forbidden {space}`.
- [ ] Writes labelled as the service; `requested_by` shown as unverified.

title: T65: Hermes nest-family profile: family-space-only agent profile for the household chat
description:
## Goal and why

In P4 the household talks to Hermes (the example deployment's chat agent) about family things, and the results should land in the `family` space for everyone. A dedicated `nest-family` profile of the Hermes `partifactory` skill (T58) restricts what that profile can do to `family`, so a family conversation can never write into someone's personal space. Depends on T58 (Hermes skill with per-person pairing) and T63 (family onboarding).

## Scope

- A Hermes skill profile `nest-family` (lives with the Hermes skill in the example deployment's integration; partifactory ships the profile definition/template and docs as an example consumer, not a dependency).
- Connection consent for the profile: scopes `parts:read`, `parts:write` (optionally `data:*`, `comments:write`), **spaces = `family` only** (consented per person at pairing, or the service identity from T64.b for household-wide use).
- Defaults: `part_create` uses `space: "family"`; posts the part's own host link; runs `part_check` before posting; hands out `part_link_for` deep links for people-only actions.
- Server-side guarantee (not just client behaviour): a write by this connection to any space other than `family` is refused with `forbidden {space}` (details `space`, HTTP 403, CLI exit 3).
- Watching the event log (`part_watch`/webhooks, T123) so Hermes can tell people in its own chat when a fix lands (feeds M4).

## Not in scope

Hermes' Telegram integration and pairing (T58); embedding (T64); notifications from partifactory (non-goal).

## Design notes and decisions

- Enforcement is by the connection's consented `spaces`, so even a prompt-injected profile can't escape `family` (§3b: "Agent consent is limited to spaces").
- Hermes is an example consumer: nothing in core depends on it (§5f).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "The profile can create parts in `family` only; a write elsewhere is refused with `forbidden {space}`".

- [ ] Profile connection consented with spaces `["family"]` only.
- [ ] `part_create` without `space` from the profile lands in `family`.
- [ ] Write to `~<person>` → `forbidden {space}`.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-api/tests/space_limited_connection.rs`: connection with spaces=[family]; create elsewhere → 403 `forbidden` with `details.space`; logs `event="op" op="part_create" outcome="forbidden"`.
- Scripted Hermes flow (extends T58's harness): "make a chore chart for the family" → part in `family`, link posted.

## References

PLAN.md §3b (consent limited to spaces, Hermes row), §4 Example consumers, §6 P4, §4b error table (`forbidden`).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): The profile can create parts in `family` only; a write elsewhere is refused with `forbidden {space}`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T58: Hermes partifactory skill: per-person pairing, check before posting, comment relay, deep links
  - T63: Family onboarding: invite into the family space, first-run tour, personal space
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done
acceptance_criteria: The profile can create parts in `family` only; a write elsewhere is refused with `forbidden {space}`

title: T66: Slides kind plus Mermaid and KaTeX for markdown and slides (block = slide)
description:
## Goal and why

Decks and diagrams are common things agents make. The `slides` kind turns a Markdown file with `---` separators into a deck, and Mermaid/KaTeX make diagrams and maths render in `markdown` and `slides`. Block ids (T48) make "block = slide", so agents edit one slide with block ops. P4. Depends on T12 (kind renderers, markdown via comrak, `pf-shell.css`) and T48 (block ids, sidecar, block ops).

## Scope

- Kind table row: `slides` | entry `*.md` with `---` separators | build: "as markdown + the slide runtime (block = slide)" | served as: slide shell. Bin code `DECK`; Mermaid diagrams use bin code `MMD` where a part is a diagram.
- Build: comrak render per slide into the slide shell; the slide runtime (a shared blob: keyboard nav, 16:9 `.jig-deck`/`.jig-slide` classes from Jig when present) inserted at serve time like the prelude. Detection: a `.md` entry with `kind: "slides"` (or detection rule documented: `---` slide separators alone must not override `markdown` without `kind`, since `---` is also a thematic break — recommend explicit `kind: "slides"`).
- **Block = slide** in `slides`: the `.pf/blocks.json` sidecar lists one block per slide; block ops (`replace_block`, `insert_after`, `append_to_section`, `delete_block`) address slides; errors `block_not_found`, `block_changed`.
- **Mermaid and KaTeX client-side** ("Markdown / code: `comrak` + `syntect` server-side; Mermaid and KaTeX client-side"): their JS/CSS/fonts are shared blobs (mirrored or seeded, allowed by `script-src`/`style-src`/`font-src <blob>`), loaded by the markdown/slide shell only when a part contains a ```mermaid fence or `$…$`/`$$…$$` maths. "KaTeX and Font Awesome webfonts come through the same pass" (mirror).
- Golden slide deck in `tests/golden/slides/`.
- Contract: add `slides` to the kinds table in `docs/agent-contract.md`.

## Not in scope

Markdown kind and block ids (T12, T48); Jig itself (T54); slides editing UI beyond block-aware editing already in T55.

## Design notes and decisions

- Client-side Mermaid/KaTeX keeps the build child fast (10 s deadline) and needs no network; both libraries come from the shared blob host, so CSP stays unchanged.
- Parts remain unthemed by the workspace; the slide shell uses Jig styles (we "use Jig to render the kinds we render ourselves (Markdown, slides, Mermaid, code)").

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Golden slide deck renders; block ops address slides".

- [ ] Golden deck renders with N slides, keyboard navigation, no uncaught errors.
- [ ] `replace_block` on a slide id changes only that slide; ids carry over across edits.
- [ ] Mermaid fence and KaTeX maths render in both `markdown` and `slides`; nothing loads from third parties.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-build/tests/golden_slides.rs`: render output hashes stable; sidecar block count = slide count.
- `pf_build::markdown::tests::mermaid_katex_assets_only_when_used`.
- `tests/e2e/slides_render.spec.ts`: deck navigates with arrow keys; HAR shows only part host + blob host; logs `event="build.finished" kind="slides" outcome="ok"`.

## References

PLAN.md §2 Kinds table, §3d Long documents (block = slide), §4a.5 kind bin codes, §4a.8 Jig (`.jig-slide`, `.jig-deck`), §5 Stack (Markdown/code row), §6 P4.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Golden slide deck renders; block ops address slides
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T12: Kind renderers for Slice 1: html passthrough, text, markdown (comrak) and prebuilt files
  - T48: Block ids for markdown: parse, id carry-over across edits, block ops, pending blocks, .pf/blocks.json sidecar
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Decided: `slides` is never sniffed from `---` separators (they are also thematic breaks and YAML front matter); it requires `kind: "slides"`, and `part_create {content, kind: "slides"}` names the file `index.md`. The contract's kinds table says so.
acceptance_criteria: Golden slide deck renders; block ops address slides

title: T81: Screenshot thumbnails for the private gallery and opt-in screenshot og:image for public links
description:
## Goal and why

The gallery should show what each part looks like, and a public link may optionally unfurl with a real screenshot. Both reuse the render sidecar (T80). Thumbnails never leave the house; screenshot cards are opt-in per link "because unfurlers store images on their servers". P4. Depends on T80 (render sidecar), T75 (static content-free cards), T31 (gallery), T119 (card pipeline and titled public card).

## Scope

- **Thumbnail order of preference**: (1) a screenshot from the render sidecar (if it's on); (2) the agent's own (`meta.thumbnail`, PNG/WebP ≤ 256 KB); (3) a server-drawn SVG spec-sheet thumb (title, first heading, kind, first lines, a colour strip from the part's CSS). "So the grid never has holes."
- Sidecar thumbnails: `render_jobs.purpose = 'thumbnail'`, **600×375 WebP part blobs**, queued after a live change (coalesced per part, 5 s debounce, newest only, concurrency 1, one retry, circuit breaker); "The renderer is never on the save path."
- Served by the workspace at **`/api/v1/thumbs/<part>?v=<n>`**, session- and grant-checked, `private, immutable`, **never edge-cached**. Gallery cards use a 16:10 thumbnail; list view 72×45.
- **Screenshot og:image for public links**: per link, off by default (`public_links.screenshot_og INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`), toggled in the share sheet ("Use a screenshot as the preview", shown only if the sidecar is on); `render_jobs.purpose = 'og'`; the screenshot composited into the public card's thumbnail frame (T119 template) and served content-addressed at `/og/<sha256>.png`.
- Fallbacks: sidecar off/down → thumbnails fall back to the agent's own or the SVG thumb; nothing else degrades.
- Renderer caps: subject `render`, 60 s window, read-only (shared data read-only view, writes to a discarded overlay).

## Not in scope

The render sidecar and `part_check` (T80); card templates (T75/T119); gallery layout (T31).

## Design notes and decisions

- Private gallery thumbnails are part blobs (private), never in a shared cache, so revoking access really revokes them.
- "The audience decides the card, never the User-Agent": the root carries the public card only while a public link is active; screenshot only with that link's opt-in.
- SVG thumb uses no part code execution: derived from source text/CSS only.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Gallery tiles show screenshots when the sidecar is on and SVG thumbs when it's off; a public link without the opt-in never gets a screenshot card".

- [ ] Sidecar on: tiles show 600×375 WebP screenshots after a live change.
- [ ] Sidecar off: tiles show agent thumb or SVG thumb; no empty tiles.
- [ ] `/api/v1/thumbs/<part>` denies a viewer without access (404) and is `Cache-Control: private, immutable`.
- [ ] Public link without opt-in never has a screenshot og:image (security §7 render line).

## Tests

- `pf_render::thumbs::tests::coalesce_debounce`, `pf_ui::thumbs::tests::fallback_order`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/thumbs_grant_checked.rs`: headers and auth; logs `event="thumb.serve" outcome`.
- `tests/e2e/gallery_thumbnails.spec.ts`: with and without sidecar profile; and an og test fetching the public link root asserting the og:image hash equals the non-screenshot card unless opted in.

## References

PLAN.md §4a.6 Gallery (Thumbnails), §4c Tier (a) and Tier (b) (Outputs), §5e `render_jobs.purpose`, `public_links.screenshot_og`, §7 Render sidecar, §6 P4.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Gallery tiles show screenshots when the sidecar is on and SVG thumbs when it's off; a public link without the opt-in never gets a screenshot card
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T80: Render sidecar + part_check: headless render, actions, read-only data overlay, after_check gate
  - T75: Content-free preview cards (Slice 1): two static 1200x630 PNGs at /og/<sha256>.png
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T119: Card pipeline (SVG -> resvg PNG) and the titled public-link card
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- `meta.thumbnail` does not exist in the contract's `part_edit meta` yet: this task adds `thumbnail` (the blob hash of a PNG/WebP ≤ 256 KB) to the registry, `/openapi.json` and `docs/agent-contract.md` (T56 green), and owns the `meta.thumbnail` rendering path in the thumbnails endpoint (G04 owns the endpoint and the SVG spec-sheet fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Gallery tiles show screenshots when the sidecar is on and SVG thumbs when it's off; a public link without the opt-in never gets a screenshot card

title: T85: Phone editing: tap-to-edit text as anchor edits, long-press point-and-comment
description:
## Goal and why

On a phone there's no toolchain and no editor worth using. P4's done-when: "a family member opens a Nest-embedded part, fixes a typo by tapping it on the phone, long-presses to ask Hermes for a change, and Hermes … tells them in its own chat when the fix lands." This task gives the wrapper two phone gestures that turn into ordinary ops. Depends on T31 (wrapper chrome), T62 (prelude + wrapper postMessage schema), T46 (`part_edit` anchor edits), T50 (comments with anchors).

## Scope

- **"Edit text" mode** in the wrapper (⋯ menu / mobile bottom sheet): tapping any text in the preview makes it editable; saving submits **one `part_edit`** with `{op: "replace", old_str: <original text>, new_str: <edited text>}` against the source (requires `edit`). "It works whenever the text occurs exactly once in the source (Markdown maps to block ids)." Otherwise it offers **"Ask the agent"** with the text pre-filled (a `to_agent` comment).
- **Long-press any element to comment**, with an anchor `{version, block_id | selector, text_quote, rect}` (stored in `comments.anchor` JSON: `{block?|file,lines?, quote}` plus selector/rect).
- Both run over the **wrapper ↔ part `postMessage` channel**, "so the trusted UI stays outside the part": the prelude reports tapped text node, a robust selector and the bounding rect; the wrapper owns the UI and calls the chrome API (thin views over `part_edit`, `part_comments`). The wrapper identifies frame messages by `event.source === frame.contentWindow`, never `event.origin`.
- Mapping text to source: for `html`/`text`, match the exact text node string in the entry file (must occur once); for `markdown`, map via block ids (T48) to the block's source and replace within it.
- Mobile UX: hit targets ≥ 44×44, bottom sheets, no hover-only affordances; budget "Small text fix by hand: Edit → (type) → ⌘S, 2 + type" on desktop, phone equivalent documented.

## Not in scope

`part_edit` engine (T46), comments service (T50), agent inbox (T84), source editor (T55).

## Design notes and decisions

- Anchor edits rather than DOM serialization: the source stays the diffable truth (§3g reason 4), and a failed unique match falls back to asking the agent rather than guessing.
- The prelude never gets privileged UI; it only answers "what is at this point" messages, and nothing it says is trusted beyond being a proposed `old_str` the server verifies.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "On a phone, a typo fixed by tapping it becomes one `part_edit`; a long-press comment carries `{version, selector|block, quote}`".

- [ ] Tap-edit of unique text produces exactly one new version with a single replace edit (`via = 'editor'` or documented value).
- [ ] Non-unique text → "Ask the agent" with text pre-filled; no version written.
- [ ] Long-press comment stored with version, selector or block id, quote.

## Tests

- `pf_prelude` JS unit tests `tap_target_selector.test.js`.
- `tests/e2e/phone_tap_edit.spec.ts` (mobile WebKit profile, 360×740): fix a typo, assert one `part_edit` in server logs (`event="op" op="part_edit" outcome="ok" edits=1`), version n+1; long-press comment anchor asserted via `part_get`/comments API.

## References

PLAN.md §3c "Phone editing (P4)", §4a.6 Mobile, Comments, §4a.7 budgets, §5e `comments.anchor`, §6 P4.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): On a phone, a typo fixed by tapping it becomes one `part_edit`; a long-press comment carries `{version, selector|block, quote}`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T31: Workspace UI (Stockroom), Slice 1 part: sign-in, gallery, wrapper chrome, share sheet public rung
  - T62: Prelude (shared blob) + /_rt/v1: localStorage shim, fetch prefixing, blob workers, regrant, runtime errors
  - T46: part_edit engine: ordered anchor edits, write/delete/rename with if_match, rebase in the writer, request_id replay, modes
  - T50: Comments: threads, anchors, to_agent, resolve, provenance field + MCP untrusted wrapper (part_comments)
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- `versions.via` for tap-to-edit is `'editor'` (the frozen CHECK allows `api, mcp, cli, editor, self_publish, restore` only).
- Transport: this task adds chrome-API endpoints `POST /api/chrome/v1/<part>/edit` and `/comment` (T29.b's exact-origin CORS, session auth), because the wrapper lives on the part host and the ops API is bearer-only.
- The anchor fields `selector` and `rect` extend the `comments.anchor` JSON that T50 owns and `part_comments` returns; coordinate the shape in T50's contract section.
- `tsx` parts: the same exact-unique-match rule applies to JSX text; otherwise "Ask the agent".
acceptance_criteria: On a phone, a typo fixed by tapping it becomes one `part_edit`; a long-press comment carries `{version, selector|block, quote}`

title: T111: Optional OTLP export adapter (traces, logs, metrics) to any collector; off by default, never required
description:
## Goal and why

Let an operator who already runs Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana or any OpenTelemetry collector send partifactory's traces, logs and metrics there, without making any of it a dependency. Insights in the UI, `/metrics` scraping and stdout JSON already cover everything (§5f Telemetry export row: "None needed … What breaks if absent: Nothing").

Phase P4; feeds M4. Third-party telemetry services are a non-goal: "the OTLP adapter sends only where the operator points it".

## Scope

- Config (all optional; unset = off): `[otlp] endpoint` (gRPC or HTTP/protobuf), `protocol`, `headers` (secret values via `PF_OTLP_HEADERS` / `PF_OTLP_HEADERS_FILE`), `traces = true|false`, `logs = true|false`, `metrics = true|false`, `sample` (traces: export what the T106 tail sampler keeps, recommended default; optionally all).
- **Traces**: export kept traces (T106) as OTLP spans with `request_id`, `route_class`/`op`, `part_id`, `principal` attributes (the same redacted fields as the trace store); resource attributes `service.name=partifactory`, version.
- **Logs**: export the redacted JSON log stream as OTLP log records (reuse/merge with T107.b's OTLP logs push so there's one exporter config).
- **Metrics**: export the Prometheus registry as OTLP metrics on an interval (default 60 s).
- Batching, bounded queues, retry with backoff; when the collector is down, drop and count (`pf_otlp_dropped_total{signal}`) — never block or degrade serving.

## Not in scope

Any built-in collector, dashboards, or vendor-specific exporters; changing what is recorded (T105–T107).

## Design notes and decisions

- Export only the already-redacted data, so the T112 guarantee extends to the collector (add OTLP payloads to the T112 sink list when enabled in its test config).
- Use the `opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry-otlp` crates behind a cargo feature so the default binary size isn't affected much; recommended to keep it compiled in but inert when unset.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "With a local collector configured, traces and logs arrive carrying request ids; with it unset, nothing is sent and nothing degrades."

- [ ] With a local OTel collector in CI, traces, logs and metrics arrive; traces and logs carry `request_id`.
- [ ] Unset config: zero outbound connections (asserted by a network-namespace or socket counter test), no added latency beyond noise.
- [ ] Collector down: serving unaffected, drops counted.
- [ ] OTLP payloads contain no canaries (T112 extension).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-obs/tests/otlp.rs::traces_logs_metrics_reach_collector` (spins up `otel/opentelemetry-collector` with a file exporter, asserts records with the request ids of driven requests).
- `crates/pf-obs/tests/otlp.rs::unset_sends_nothing`, `::collector_down_does_not_block`.
- Log assertions: `event="otlp.export" signal="traces" outcome="ok|dropped"`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g rules (optional OTLP export adapter); §5f Telemetry export row; §5h "Logs out"; §6 P4; §9 non-goals (third-party telemetry).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P4 (epic "P4 Family + Nest + phone"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P3.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): With a local collector configured, traces and logs arrive carrying request ids; with it unset, nothing is sent and nothing degrades
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
  - T107: Log pipeline: stdout JSON always, rotating zstd segments under /data/logs, logs export/tail, push adapters
- Unblocks: 
  - M4: Milestone - P4 Family + Nest + phone done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

title: T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks
description:
## Goal and why

partifactory v1 lets a part be "a page plus, optionally, any containers it wants" (decision 28, phase P2a). The Docker Engine API is root-equivalent on the host, so exactly one small process may hold it: `partifactory runner`, running in its own container (`partifactory-runner`, the same binary). Everything else in partifactory (a large, internet-facing surface) talks to it through a fixed, typed, authenticated API, so a bug anywhere else can at worst ask for a *hardened* container, never a privileged one.

This task is the foundation of P2a. Every later backend task (T99 builds, T100 lifecycle, T101 routing, T102 data/secrets, T110 observability, T116 retention, T103 security suite, T104 the backend pixel test, milestone M2a) depends on it. It is after Slice 1.

- *Why a sidecar:* "the Engine API is root-equivalent on the host. Keeping it in a small process with a fixed API means a bug anywhere in partifactory's large surface can at worst ask for a hardened container, never a privileged one."
- *Why containers, not WASM first:* every language and database ships as an OCI image and agents already write Dockerfiles; WASM is an optional P5 alternative (T71).
- *Why egress on, LAN off:* "the useful things a small app does are on the internet. The dangerous thing a prompt-injected or vulnerable backend could do is reach the household's own devices, so that's what's closed."

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent bead is the integration/closure bead: close it only after every subtask is closed and the acceptance criteria below pass end to end, on Docker and on Podman):
- **T98.a** Runner spike: rootless BuildKit in a container, firewall rules on Docker (`DOCKER-USER`) and on Podman (netavark + nftables); go/no-go note.
- **T98.b** `partifactory runner` process: the fixed authenticated API (`build`, `deploy`, `start`, `stop`, `logs`, `stats`, `prune`) over the internal network with `PF_RUNNER_KEY`, `bollard` client, and the one container template enforced in code.
- **T98.c** One bridge network per part plus the firewall rules (egress on; LAN, host and other parts dropped), LAN allowlist entries applied as exceptions, `docs/backends-network.md`.
- **T98.d** The runner service in `deploy/compose.yaml` behind the `backends` profile (on in the shipped file), env contract entries, `doctor` hook point.

What the whole task delivers (verbatim from PLAN.md §3f):
- `partifactory-runner` is a separate container (the same binary, run as `partifactory runner`) and **the only process with the Docker Engine API**. Docker and Podman (whose API is Docker-compatible) both work.
- partifactory talks to it over an internal network through a fixed, typed API (`build`, `deploy`, `start`, `stop`, `logs`, `stats`, `prune`), authenticated with `PF_RUNNER_KEY`.
- It creates containers **only from one template**: not privileged, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, a read-only root filesystem with a 64 MiB tmpfs `/tmp`, a non-root user (UID ≥ 10000, forced even if the image asks for root), the default seccomp profile, pids/memory/CPU/disk limits, `json-file` logging with `max-size=10m` and `max-file=3`, and optionally the gVisor runtime (`[backends] runtime = "runsc"`).
- No host mounts beyond the part's own volumes, never the Docker or Podman socket, no host network, no devices.
- Network: each part gets **its own bridge network** (`pf-part-<id>`), shared only by that part's services. **Internet egress is on by default.** **The LAN, the host and other parts are blocked by default.** The runner installs explicit drop rules for each part network: RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local (including `169.254.169.254`) and IPv6 ULA/link-local ranges, the host's own addresses, and every other part network. On Docker the rules go in the `DOCKER-USER` chain. On Podman (netavark) they go in the runner's own nftables table. `docs/backends-network.md` documents both per host, and `doctor` checks that the rules are in place.
- LAN allowlist: a per-part entry (`host:port` or a CIDR) set only by a person (the admin UI, T102.d); the runner applies them as explicit accept rules ahead of the drops. Table: `lan_allow (id, part_id, target, note, added_by, added_at, revoked_at)`.
- Default per-part limits: 1 CPU, 512 MiB memory, 256 pids, 1 GiB volumes, 2 GiB images; global: 20 running containers, 4 GiB backend memory, 20 GiB images (enforced in T102.c; the template carries the per-container values).
- Required env: `PF_RUNNER_KEY` if the runner is on (env or `PF_RUNNER_KEY_FILE`).
- Compose: the runner behind the `backends` profile (on in the shipped file); it is the only service that mounts the Engine API socket. Moved here from T37 at the Slice 1 freeze.

## Not in scope

- Compose subset parsing, BuildKit builds, image allowlist, `part put --image` (T99).
- Container-set lifecycle, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback (T100).
- Routing `/c/<cap>/api/*`, identity JWT, WS/SSE proxy (T101).
- Volumes, secrets, the admin LAN UI, `backends:deploy` scope and quota enforcement (T102).
- Backend logs ring, metrics, Insights Backends page (T110); image/BuildKit cache pruning schedule (T116); the full §7 Backends suite (T103).
- WASM backends (T71, P5).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 28 (round 2c): backends in v1 as containers; only the runner holds the Engine API.
- The template is a code constant, not config: any `deploy` request that would produce a container outside it is refused by the runner itself (defence in depth even if the main process is compromised).
- Forced non-root: if the image `USER` is root or unset, the runner overrides it to a UID ≥ 10000; images that genuinely need root fail at start and that failure is reported as `backend_unhealthy` by T100.
- Docker vs Podman: the runner talks the Docker Engine API via `bollard` to either; firewall is the one place that differs (iptables `DOCKER-USER` vs nftables table owned by the runner). The portability lane (T93) uses Podman for the backend pass.
- The runner holds no partifactory DB credentials; it receives fully-resolved requests (image digests, env, volume paths).
- `PF_RUNNER_KEY` authenticates every call (HMAC of request or bearer over the internal network); the runner's API is never routed through ingress.
- gVisor (`runsc`) is optional; when configured, every part container uses it.
- If the runner is absent: backend parts fail with `backends_unavailable` (HTTP 503, CLI exit 7); frontends unaffected (§5f).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "The runner refuses any request outside the template; on Docker and on Podman a test container shows the template's settings in `inspect`, reaches a public canary, and fails to reach a LAN canary, the host and a sibling part".

- [ ] All subtasks T98.a–T98.d closed.
- [ ] `docker inspect` / `podman inspect` of a test container shows: `Privileged=false`, `CapDrop=[ALL]`, `SecurityOpt` contains `no-new-privileges`, `ReadonlyRootfs=true`, tmpfs `/tmp` 64 MiB, `User` UID ≥ 10000, default seccomp, pids/memory/CPU limits set, `LogConfig` json-file `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`, no bind mounts besides its volume, no socket mount, not host network, no devices.
- [ ] A request asking for privileged, extra caps, host network, a bind mount, a device or root is refused with a typed error and an audit log line.
- [ ] Unauthenticated or wrongly keyed calls to the runner API are refused.
- [ ] From a part container: public canary reachable; LAN canary, host address, `169.254.169.254` and a sibling part's container unreachable; on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] A LAN allowlist entry makes exactly that target reachable.
- [ ] `docs/backends-network.md` exists and documents both hosts.
- [ ] `deploy/compose.yaml` has the runner behind the `backends` profile, enabled in the shipped file, the only service mounting the Engine socket.

## Tests

- `pf-runner::template::tests::refuses_non_template_requests` (table-driven: privileged, cap_add, host network, bind mount, device, user root, socket mount).
- `pf-runner::api::tests::rejects_bad_runner_key`.
- Integration `crates/pf-runner/tests/inspect_template.rs` (runs against Docker and Podman in CI matrices): starts a busybox container via the API and asserts every inspect field; structured logs asserted: `event="runner.deploy" outcome="ok" part_id=...`, and for refusals `event="runner.refused" reason="template_violation"`.
- Integration `crates/pf-runner/tests/network_isolation.rs`: public canary (`outcome=ok`), LAN canary/host/metadata/sibling must time out or be refused; denied-attempt counter increments (`event="runner.lan_denied"`). Artifacts on failure: `nft list ruleset` / `iptables -S DOCKER-USER` dumps and runner JSONL logs in `target/e2e-logs/network_isolation/`.
- Feeds the §7 Backends lines run in T103.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Backends (The runner sidecar, Network, Permissions and quotas), §3 Topology, §5b Builds and deploys (compose file), §5 Stack (Backends row; runner spike), §5f Portability (Backends row), §5e `lan_allow`; decision 28; §10 Slice 1 freeze (runner compose service moved T37 → T98).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): The runner refuses any request outside the template; on Docker and on Podman a test container shows the template's settings in `inspect`, reaches a public canary, and fails to reach a LAN canary, the host and a sibling part
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T37: Deliverable: amd64 OCI image + deploy/compose.yaml + env contract + `partifactory deploy` with auto rollback
  - T04: Config + secrets loader: site.toml + PF_* env + PF_*_FILE, redaction, docs/env.md, config check
- Unblocks: 
  - T99: Backend sources and builds: compose subset, rootless BuildKit, allowlisted images, image upload
  - T116: Runner retention: image pruning (live + previous 2), BuildKit cache 10 GiB LRU, backend log rings, volume quotas
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T98.a: Runner spike: rootless BuildKit in a container and firewall rules on Docker and Podman
  - T98.b: `partifactory runner`: fixed authenticated API and the one hardened container template
  - T98.c: Per-part bridge networks and firewall rules (egress on; LAN, host, siblings dropped)
  - T98.d: Runner service in deploy/compose.yaml behind the `backends` profile

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- **Runner privileges, stated and justified:** installing `DOCKER-USER` (Docker) or nftables (Podman) rules happens in the host network namespace, which a plain container on an internal compose network cannot do. The runner container therefore runs with `cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]` and either `network_mode: host` or a tiny netns-join helper for the rule-applying step; it already holds the Engine socket (root-equivalent), so this adds no new trust boundary. T98.a tests the mechanism on Docker and Podman; T98.d writes it into `deploy/compose.yaml`.
- `doctor` check ownership: T98.c adds the `runner rules present` check to `doctor` itself (T68 is P1 and closes long before; its row says "backend firewall rules once T98 exists").
- "Disk limits" in the template mean: read-only rootfs + 64 MiB tmpfs `/tmp` (+ small tmpfs `/run`, `/var/run` if the T98.a spike finds stock images need them) + the per-volume quota (T102.a). No literal per-container disk field unless T98.a finds a portable mechanism.
- New config key `[backends] household_subnets = [...]` (the §7 "household's real subnets from site config"); T98.c applies it, T98.d adds it to `docs/env.md`.
- Shipped default `[backends] registries = ["docker.io"]` so `image: postgres:16` works out of the box (T98.d adds it to the env contract).
acceptance_criteria: The runner refuses any request outside the template; on Docker and on Podman a test container shows the template's settings in `inspect`, reaches a public canary, and fails to reach a LAN canary, the host and a sibling part

title: T98.a: Runner spike: rootless BuildKit in a container and firewall rules on Docker and Podman
description:
## Goal and why

PLAN.md §5: "A separate runner spike (P2a, inside T98) checks rootless BuildKit in a container and the firewall rules on Docker (`DOCKER-USER`) and on Podman (netavark + nftables)." These are the two riskiest mechanisms of P2a; finding that rootless BuildKit can't run inside the runner container, or that netavark ignores our nftables table, after T99/T100 are built would force a redesign. A 1-2 day spike with a go/no-go note de-risks them first.

## Scope

- Run `buildkitd` rootless inside a container (the runner image) on Docker and on Podman; build a small Dockerfile with network on; record what privileges/settings were required (e.g. user namespaces, seccomp/apparmor profile adjustments) and whether they're compatible with the runner's own container.
- Create a bridge network per test part; install drop rules for RFC 1918, CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10), link-local incl. `169.254.169.254`, IPv6 ULA (fc00::/7) and link-local (fe80::/10), the host's own addresses and the other test network: on Docker in `DOCKER-USER`, on Podman (netavark) in a runner-owned nftables table. Verify egress to a public canary still works, LAN/host/sibling fail, rules survive daemon restart (or document re-apply on runner start), and the same block applies to BuildKit build containers.
- Write `docs/spikes/runner.md`: results table per host (Docker version, Podman version, kernel), each item pass/fail, the exact rule sets, go/no-go, and fallbacks.

## Not in scope

Production runner code (T98.b, T98.c); the compose subset (T99).

## Design notes and decisions

- If rootless BuildKit can't run in the runner container, record the fallback options (separate `buildkitd` sidecar container under the same network block, or rootful buildkitd in its own container with no host mounts) and their security trade-off; the choice goes into T99.
- If netavark rewrites/flushes nftables on network changes, record the ordering/priority needed (own table with higher-priority hook).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/spikes/runner.md` exists with a pass/fail row per item per host and the versions tested.
- [ ] A runnable example (script under `docs/spikes/runner/`) reproduces each result.
- [ ] An explicit go/no-go with the chosen mechanism for T98.c and T99.

## Tests

The spike's script is the test: `docs/spikes/runner/run.sh docker|podman` prints a JSON results table (item, host, outcome); kept as the seed of `crates/pf-runner/tests/network_isolation.rs`.

## References

PLAN.md §5 (maturity check, runner spike), §3f Network, §3g Builds; §5f Backends row.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

Three more go/no-go spike items (each can block M2a):
- the privileges the runner container needs to install rules from inside a container (`NET_ADMIN` + host netns, or a netns-join helper) on Docker and on rootful Podman (netavark rule ordering);
- **the official `postgres` image starts under the hardened template** (forced UID ≥ 10000, read-only rootfs, 64 MiB `/tmp`, `PGDATA` on a named volume): the stock entrypoint writes `/var/run/postgresql` and chowns as root. If it fails, decide between a compose-subset `tmpfs:` key (list of paths) and the template mounting `/run` and `/var/run` as small tmpfs. T104's Done-when depends on this;
- a portable per-volume disk-limit mechanism (project quota vs periodic measurement with a soft quota vs loopback image), feeding T102.a.

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/spikes/runner.md` exists with a pass/fail row per item per host and the versions tested.
- [ ] A runnable example (script under `docs/spikes/runner/`) reproduces each result.
- [ ] An explicit go/no-go with the chosen mechanism for T98.c and T99.

title: T98.b: `partifactory runner`: fixed authenticated API and the one hardened container template
description:
## Goal and why

Implement the runner process: the only holder of the Engine API, exposing a small typed API to partifactory and creating containers only from one hardened template. This is the security boundary of P2a.

## Scope

- Subcommand `partifactory runner` (same binary), crate `crates/pf-runner`, Engine API client `bollard` (Docker or Podman's Docker-compatible socket).
- Typed API over the internal network: `build`, `deploy`, `start`, `stop`, `logs`, `stats`, `prune`. Authenticated with `PF_RUNNER_KEY` (env or `PF_RUNNER_KEY_FILE`); every request carries `X-PF-Request-Id` for tracing.
- The template (verbatim): not privileged, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, a read-only root filesystem with a 64 MiB tmpfs `/tmp`, a non-root user (UID ≥ 10000, forced even if the image asks for root), the default seccomp profile, pids/memory/CPU/disk limits, `json-file` logging with `max-size=10m` and `max-file=3`, optionally the gVisor runtime (`[backends] runtime = "runsc"`). No host mounts beyond the part's own volumes (`/data/parts/<id>/vol/<svc>`), never the Docker or Podman socket, no host network, no devices.
- Default per-container limits from the part's settings (defaults: 1 CPU, 512 MiB memory, 256 pids).
- Refusal: any request outside the template returns a typed `template_violation {field}` error and logs `event="runner.refused"`.
- Labels on every container/network: `managed-by=partifactory`, `pf.part=<id>`, `pf.version=<id>`, `pf.service=<svc>` so prune and doctor can find them.

## Not in scope

Networks/firewall (T98.c), BuildKit build execution details and the compose subset (T99), lifecycle (T100).

## Design notes and decisions

- The API surface is deliberately fixed: no generic "create container with these options" call. The main process sends `{part, version, service, image_digest, env, secret_files, volume, limits, role}`; the runner builds the container spec itself.
- Secrets arrive as values only for injection (env or files under `/run/secrets/`) and are never logged (type-based redaction from T18).
- Forced UID: set `User` to a fixed UID ≥ 10000 (e.g. 10001) unless the image already declares a numeric UID ≥ 10000.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every template field is visible in `inspect` on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] Table-driven refusals: privileged, cap_add, host network, bind mount outside the part's volume, device, socket mount, root user override attempts.
- [ ] Bad or missing `PF_RUNNER_KEY` -> 401-equivalent refusal; no Engine call made.
- [ ] `runsc` runtime is used when configured.

## Tests

- `pf_runner::template::tests::*` unit tests building specs and asserting fields.
- `crates/pf-runner/tests/inspect_template.rs` (Docker and Podman CI matrix), asserting logs `event="runner.deploy"` with `part_id`, `request_id`, and no secret canary in captured logs.

## References

title: T98.c: Per-part bridge networks and firewall rules (egress on; LAN, host, siblings dropped)
description:
## Goal and why

Close the dangerous direction (the household LAN, the host, other parts) while keeping the useful one (internet egress) open, for running containers and for builds.

## Scope

- One bridge network per part, `pf-part-<id>`, shared only by that part's services.
- Explicit drop rules per part network for: RFC 1918 (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), CGNAT (100.64/10), link-local incl. `169.254.169.254`, IPv6 ULA (fc00::/7) and link-local (fe80::/10), the host's own addresses, and every other part network. Household subnets from site config are added too (§7 tests them).
- Docker: rules in the `DOCKER-USER` chain. Podman (netavark): rules in the runner's own nftables table. Re-applied idempotently at runner start and on network create/delete.
- LAN allowlist: accept rules ahead of the drops for each active `lan_allow` row (`host:port` or a CIDR) of that part; rows come from T102.d via the runner API.
- Denied-attempt counting per part (log/counter rule) exposed via `stats` for T110.
- The same block applies to BuildKit build containers (T99).
- `docs/backends-network.md`: per-host documentation of both rule sets and how to verify; a `doctor` check hook (`runner rules present`) consumed by T68.

## Not in scope

The admin UI for allowlist entries (T102.d); Insights display (T110); the §7 Backends test suite (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

Egress is metered (bytes out per part, via counters) for Insights. Rules are owned (comment/table name `partifactory`) so the runner never touches rules it didn't create.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Public canary reachable from a part container and from a build; LAN canary, host, metadata IP and sibling part unreachable; on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] An allowlisted target is reachable and nothing else is.
- [ ] Denied attempts are counted per part.
- [ ] Rules restored after runner restart.

## Tests

`crates/pf-runner/tests/network_isolation.rs` (Docker + Podman matrix) with structured logs `event="runner.net.apply" part_id=...` and `event="runner.lan_denied"`; failure artifacts: ruleset dumps in `target/e2e-logs/network_isolation/`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Network; §7 Backends (LAN reachability); §5e `lan_allow`.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T98.a: Runner spike: rootless BuildKit in a container and firewall rules on Docker and Podman, T98.b: `partifactory runner`: fixed authenticated API and the one hardened container template

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- LAN allowlist `host:port` entries: netfilter needs addresses, so the runner resolves the hostname at apply time, re-resolves every 5 minutes (or at the DNS TTL if shorter) and re-applies the rule set when it changes; CIDR and `ip:port` entries apply as written. The admin UI (T102.d) validates the syntax.
- This subtask adds the `doctor` check `runner rules present` (not T68).
- The denied-LAN-attempts counter is owned here (runner `stats`); T110 only exposes it per part.
- Applies `[backends] household_subnets` from config in addition to the fixed RFC 1918 / CGNAT / link-local / ULA ranges.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Public canary reachable from a part container and from a build; LAN canary, host, metadata IP and sibling part unreachable; on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] An allowlisted target is reachable and nothing else is.
- [ ] Denied attempts are counted per part.
- [ ] Rules restored after runner restart.

title: T98.d: Runner service in deploy/compose.yaml behind the `backends` profile
description:
## Goal and why

Ship the runner as part of the deliverable so `docker compose up -d` brings up backends support, while keeping the Engine socket confined to the runner. Moved here from T37 at the Slice 1 freeze, because only P2a needs it.

## Scope

- Add `partifactory-runner` to `deploy/compose.yaml`: same image, command `partifactory runner`, behind the `backends` profile, **on in the shipped file**; the only service that mounts the Engine API socket (Docker `/var/run/docker.sock` or the Podman socket path, documented); internal network shared with partifactory only; `json-file` logging `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`; `PF_RUNNER_KEY` via `_FILE` secret.
- Env contract: `PF_RUNNER_KEY` required if the runner is on; `[backends]` site.toml keys (`runtime`, `registries`, limits) added to `docs/env.md` generation (T04 generator).
- partifactory reports `backends_unavailable` when the runner is unreachable.

## Not in scope

Runner internals (T98.b/c).

## Design notes and decisions

- The runner is on in the shipped compose file (round 2c) because backends are a v1 feature; operators who don't want them disable the profile, which shows on Health as a feature off, not a safety default off.
- The Engine socket is mounted only into the runner, never into partifactory itself, so the main process's large surface never holds root-equivalent access.
- The runner listens only on the internal compose network; it is never routed through the ingress.
- Podman users point the socket mount at the Podman API socket; the path is documented, not auto-detected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker compose --profile backends up -d` (and the default shipped file) starts the runner; `docker inspect` shows log limits; only the runner mounts the socket.
- [ ] With the runner stopped, a backend op returns `backends_unavailable` (503) and frontends keep serving.

## Tests

`tests/deploy/compose_runner.sh` smoke test in CI; asserts `event="runner.unreachable"` log line and the 503 error shape.

## References

PLAN.md §5b (Compose file), §3f, §5f Backends row; §10 Slice 1 freeze.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T98.b: `partifactory runner`: fixed authenticated API and the one hardened container template

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Acceptance replaced: "with the runner stopped, a backend op returns `backends_unavailable`" cannot run before T100/T102.c exist. Here: the runner health probe fails → `/readyz` shows a degraded `runner` row and `event="runner.unreachable"` is logged. The 503-on-op assertion moves to T102.c.
- The compose service states the runner's privileges (`cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]`, host netns or helper), the Docker or Podman socket path, and ships `[backends] registries = ["docker.io"]` and `household_subnets` in `deploy/.env.example` / `docs/env.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docker compose --profile backends up -d` (and the default shipped file) starts the runner; `docker inspect` shows log limits; only the runner mounts the socket.
- [ ] With the runner stopped, a backend op returns `backends_unavailable` (503) and frontends keep serving.

title: M2a: Milestone - P2a Backends done
description:
## Goal and why

Exit of phase **P2a Backends**: a part can bring containers (decision 28). *Why right after agents:* a backend is only useful once an agent can make and change one in a single call, and the guest and shared-data work of P2 is exactly what its acceptance test builds on. Critical path to M2a (15 steps): ... T62 -> T77 -> T96 -> T95 -> T101 -> T103 -> M2a; the runner lane (T98 -> T99 -> T100) is shorter and can start as soon as the compose deliverable (T37) lands.

## Scope (what P2a contains)

The runner sidecar (Docker Engine API; Docker or Podman) with the hardened template and a network per part (egress on; LAN, host and other parts blocked), the compose subset, server builds with rootless BuildKit, registry and uploaded images, a container set per live version gated by its health check, scale to zero or always on, routing under the cap with the signed identity header (WebSocket and SSE), per-part volumes in exports, write-only secrets, the LAN allowlist (people only), `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend observability in Insights, runner retention, and the security checklist's Backends suite.

Direct dependencies: T103, T104, T116.

## Acceptance criteria (P2a "Done when")

dag2.py: "The backend variant of the communal pixel editor passes on Docker and on Podman: a leaderboard service on Postgres, built by the server, live for guests, rolled back with its version, and walled off from the LAN."
- [ ] `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (T104) passes on Docker and on Podman: the agent adds a leaderboard service on Postgres in one `part_edit`; the server builds it; each guest's pixel count shows live; restoring the previous version rolls the backend back too; the backend reaches the internet but not the LAN.
- [ ] Every Backends line of the security checklist is green on both runtimes (T103); runner retention rows pass (T116).

## References

PLAN.md §3f, §3g, §6 Phases (P2a), §7 Backends.

## Dependency context

- This milestone depends on (blocks edges): 
  - T103: Backend security suite (§7 Backends) on Docker and Podman, staging and portability lane
  - T104: Named e2e test `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (Postgres leaderboard) on Docker and Podman
  - T116: Runner retention: image pruning (live + previous 2), BuildKit cache 10 GiB LRU, backend log rings, volume quotas
- Unblocks: T71: WASM component backends as an optional alternative to containers (only with an ADR)

## How this project is organised (read once)

partifactory is a self-hosted home for the things a household and its agents make: pages, React tools, docs, decks,
diagrams, plain text and small apps with their own backends. Each one is a **part** with its own host,
`https://<name>-part.<domain>/`, which is also the link you post. Every part runs sandboxed in an opaque origin with no
cookies, every view is a grant (a capability in the URL path), and every version is a manifest of hashes. Any AI can find
and use it through MCP, an HTTPS JSON API, the `part` CLI or a skill file, each with its own scoped, revocable identity.
It is one Rust binary plus optional sidecars, deployed as an OCI image + compose file + env contract, with no hard
dependency on any vendor (Cloudflare, Authentik, Gitea, TrueNAS, Telegram/Hermes and the Nest are adapters or example
consumers). Defaults are the safe choice; every growing store is capped. The idea comes from shartifacts by Lane
Birmingham (MIT), reimagined, not forked.

Beads: one bead per task (title starts with its T-id), subtasks as children of their task, one epic per phase (this
kind of bead), one milestone bead per phase exit plus `S1` (Slice 1). Labels: phase (`p0`..`p5`, `p2a`, `p2b`), `slice1`
for the 58 Slice 1 tasks (`slice1-subtask` for their subtasks), and one area label. Priorities: P0 = Slice 1 critical
path, P1 = rest of Slice 1, P2 = the phases' work right after Slice 1 (rest of P0-P2, P2a, P2b), P3 = later (P3-P5).
Dependency edges mirror the planning task graph (dag2.py, 121 tasks, 8 milestones, acyclic, no orphans).

title: T99: Backend sources and builds: compose subset, rootless BuildKit, allowlisted images, image upload
description:
## Goal and why

"Agents send source, and partifactory builds it" (§3g, decision 29). A quick `part_edit` to a backend's source means nothing until it is rebuilt; many AI clients (claude.ai web/mobile, ChatGPT, a chat agent in Telegram) can't build at all; a person editing in the UI or tapping a typo has no toolchain; and the stored source stays the diffable, resumable truth. So backends build server-side by default, with prebuilt or uploaded images as optional alternatives. A short, closed compose subset keeps the security surface small: "every key we accept is a key the hardening template has to reason about. A short list is one the security suite can cover completely."

## Scope

**Sources** (one per service):

| Source | How it arrives | Build method recorded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A Dockerfile + context | files in the part (`Dockerfile`, or `build:` in `compose.yaml`) | `server_build` (rootless BuildKit in the runner) |
| A prebuilt image from a registry | `image: <ref>` in `compose.yaml`. The registry must be in `[backends] registries`. The tag is resolved to a digest at deploy, and the digest is recorded | `prebuilt_image` |
| An uploaded image | `part put --image app.tar` (a `docker save` tarball), streamed to `POST /api/v1/images` (≤ 2 GiB, counted against the part's quota) | `uploaded_image` |

**Compose subset parser** — supported keys and nothing else:
- per service: `image` or `build` (`context`, `dockerfile`, `args`), `command`, `entrypoint`, `environment`, `expose` (one port, `main` only), `healthcheck`, `depends_on` (with `condition: service_healthy`), `volumes` (named only), `secrets` (names of the part's secrets), and `x-pf` (`role: main | worker | cron | dependency`, `schedule` for cron, `export` hook, `limits`);
- top level: `services`, `volumes`, `secrets`.
- Anything else (`ports`, `privileged`, `cap_add`, `network_mode`, `pid`, `devices`, bind mounts, `extra_hosts`, `sysctls`, `user: root`, …) fails the build with `compose_unsupported_key {key, service}`, and the error lists the supported set.
- A part with only a `Dockerfile` is one `main` service on its `EXPOSE`d port.

**Builds** (in the runner, via its `build` API): rootless BuildKit (`buildkitd`), build network on (apt, cargo, npm) behind the same LAN and host block as running parts (T98.c), a 10-minute timeout (`build_timeout`), CPU and memory limits (2 CPUs, 4 GiB by default), a build cache capped at 10 GiB with LRU pruning.

**Images**: registry refs allowed only from `[backends] registries`; else `image_not_allowed {ref, allowed_registries}` (HTTP 422, CLI exit 5). Tags resolved to digests; digests recorded in `backend_images`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE backend_images (
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  digest      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'sha256:...' as the runtime reports it
  source      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('server_build','prebuilt_image','uploaded_image')),
  ref         TEXT,                                  -- registry ref as written (prebuilt_image)
  tar_hash    TEXT REFERENCES blobs(hash),           -- uploaded_image: the docker-save tarball
  size        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pruned_at   INTEGER,                               -- removed from the runtime; kept: live + previous 2 versions
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, digest)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```

**Build records**: one build per target per version, `builds.target = 'backend'`, `builds.method` one of `server_build · prebuilt_files · prebuilt_image · uploaded_image`, `builds.log_hash` = the build log blob (last 20 builds per part kept, §5h), returned by `part_get {build: <id>}`. Backend build failures use the 200-with-`build.status: "failed"` shape with codes `compose_unsupported_key`, `build_timeout`, `backend_unhealthy`.

**Upload**: `POST /api/v1/images` streaming endpoint (≤ 2 GiB, quota-counted, stored as a blob; `tar_hash`), and `part put --image app.tar` CLI alias.

## Not in scope

Starting/health-gating container sets (T100); routing (T101); secrets values and volumes (T102); prune schedules for images and the BuildKit cache (T116); the backend security suite (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

- Parse errors are build failures, not op errors: the version still commits and `live` doesn't move.
- The parser rejects unknown keys by name (closed set, like `deny_unknown_fields`), so new compose keys never slip in silently.
- BuildKit runs with the network block applied (§7: "The same holds during a BuildKit build").
- Build method feeds Insights (T108 kinds and build methods over time).
- If the T98.a spike says rootless BuildKit can't run in the runner container, use the fallback chosen there.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "A Dockerfile part builds and records its digest with `server_build`; an off-allowlist image fails; every unsupported compose key fails with its name; a build still running at 10 min is killed".

- [ ] Dockerfile-only part -> one `main` service; build ok; `backend_images` row with `source='server_build'`, digest recorded; `builds.method='server_build'`, `target='backend'`.
- [ ] `image:` from an allowlisted registry resolves to a digest (`prebuilt_image`); off-allowlist -> `image_not_allowed` with `allowed_registries`.
- [ ] Table test: every listed unsupported key (and a random unknown key) -> `compose_unsupported_key {key, service}` listing the supported set.
- [ ] A build exceeding 10 min is killed -> `build_timeout`.
- [ ] `part put --image app.tar` uploads (≤ 2 GiB, counted against quota) and deploys as `uploaded_image`.
- [ ] Build log retrievable with `part_get {build: id}`.

## Tests

- `pf_build::compose::tests::supported_subset_roundtrip`, `::rejects_each_unsupported_key` (table), `::dockerfile_only_is_main_service`.
- Integration `crates/pf-runner/tests/backend_build.rs` (Docker + Podman): Dockerfile build, allowlist refusal, a `sleep 700` build killed at 10 min (test uses a shortened timeout via config); asserts logs `event="build.finished" target="backend" method="server_build" outcome="ok"` and `outcome="build_timeout"`.
- `crates/pf-api/tests/image_upload.rs`: streaming upload, size cap, quota accounting.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Sources, Services: a small compose subset; §3g Builds; §4b error table (`image_not_allowed`, `compose_unsupported_key`, `build_timeout`); §5e `builds`, `backend_images`; §5h (build logs, BuildKit cache); decision 29.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A Dockerfile part builds and records its digest with `server_build`; an off-allowlist image fails; every unsupported compose key fails with its name; a build still running at 10 min is killed
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks
  - T13: Build worker: isolated child process, build state machine, build records, brotli, live-pointer switch
  - T21: HTTPS JSON API generated from the registry: POST /api/v1/{op}, GET aliases, /openapi.json (OAS 3.1), blob have/need upload
- Unblocks: 
  - T100: Backend lifecycle: container set per live version, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- **When the allowlist applies:** the registry-host check (`image_not_allowed`, HTTP 422 per §4b) runs at **op time**: `part_create`/`part_edit` scan `compose.yaml` `image:` refs **and Dockerfile `FROM` lines** before the version commits (closing the `FROM evil.example/x` bypass). Digest resolution happens at build time. The op-time hook lives in the write path and is gated on the part having a backend; T102.c wires the `backends:deploy` scope check around it.
- Compose-parse errors stay build failures (200 + `build.status: failed` + `compose_unsupported_key`), as the plan says.
- `POST /api/v1/images` must appear in `/openapi.json` (T21's route↔document bijection test).
- Edge added: T22 (`part put --image` is a CLI alias).
- Split into T99.a / T99.b / T99.c (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: A Dockerfile part builds and records its digest with `server_build`; an off-allowlist image fails; every unsupported compose key fails with its name; a build still running at 10 min is killed

title: T99.a: compose subset parser (closed key set, compose_unsupported_key, Dockerfile-only -> main) and the op-time image allowlist scan (image: refs and Dockerfile FROM)
description:
## Goal and why

A short, closed compose subset the security suite can cover completely, parsed as a pure function, plus the op-time scan that refuses images from outside the allowlist before a version commits.

## Scope

- Parser (pure, `pf_build::compose`): the supported keys from the parent (per service `image`/`build`, `command`, `entrypoint`, `environment`, `expose` (one port, `main` only), `healthcheck`, `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`, `volumes` (named only), `secrets`, `x-pf` {role, schedule, export, limits}; top level `services`, `volumes`, `secrets`); anything else → `compose_unsupported_key {key, service}` listing the supported set (a build failure, 200 + `build.status: failed`). A Dockerfile-only part is one `main` service on its `EXPOSE`d port. `x-pf.schedule` is 5-field cron, UTC.
- **Op-time allowlist scan**: `part_create`/`part_edit` scan `compose.yaml` `image:` refs **and Dockerfile `FROM` lines** against `[backends] registries` (default `["docker.io"]`) before the version commits → `image_not_allowed {ref, allowed_registries}` (HTTP 422, CLI exit 5). T102.c gates the scan behind `backends:deploy` for agents.

## Not in scope

Building images (T99.b); digest resolution, uploads and `backend_images` rows (T99.c).

- [ ] Table test: every listed unsupported key and a random unknown key → `compose_unsupported_key` with the supported set.
- [ ] `FROM evil.example/x` and `image: evil.example/x` → `image_not_allowed` at op time; `image: postgres:16` passes with the default allowlist.

title: T99.b: server builds via the runner `build` API: rootless BuildKit, 10-minute timeout, 2 CPU/4 GiB, build records target=backend, logs, build_timeout
description:

title: T99.c: registry images pinned by digest, POST /api/v1/images (<= 2 GiB, quota-counted, in openapi.json), `part put --image`, backend_images rows
description:

Prebuilt images, from an allowlisted registry or an uploaded `docker save` tarball, recorded by digest so a rollback restarts exactly what ran before.

- Registry refs: tags resolved to digests at build/deploy via the runner; `backend_images` row `source = 'prebuilt_image'`, `ref` as written, `builds.method = 'prebuilt_image'`.

- [ ] `/openapi.json` lists the images route; the bijection test passes.

title: T100: Backend lifecycle: container set per live version, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback
description:
## Goal and why

A backend must follow its part's versions exactly like the page does: a broken version never replaces a working one, and rolling back the page rolls back the backend. And a household box can't afford every toy app running all day, so scale to zero is the default.

## Scope

- **One container set per live version.** When a version builds, its set starts next to the current one. Its health check (the compose `healthcheck`, or a TCP connect to the main port) must pass within 60 s before `live` moves. A set that fails ends the build `failed` with `backend_unhealthy` and its last 50 log lines, and the old set keeps serving. The old set drains for 30 s, then stops.
- **Rollback rolls back backends.** Restoring version 9 starts version 9's images (kept for live + the previous 2 versions; older ones are rebuilt from source, re-pulled by digest, or need the tarball again). **Volumes belong to the part, not the version**, so a rollback rolls back code, not data.
- **Scale to zero** is the default: the set starts on the first request (the proxy holds the request for up to 10 s; a cold start is typically 1–2 s) and stops after 15 minutes without one. **Always on** is a per-part setting (`parts.backend_lifecycle` in `('none','scale_to_zero','always_on')`) for workers and websocket games, counted against the global quota. `cron` services (`x-pf.role: cron`, `x-pf.schedule`) run on schedule even while the rest is scaled to zero.
- Restart counting and crash-loop detection (feeds T110 and the T121 ops alert "a backend crash-looping").
- State in the DB (verbatim DDL):
```sql
CREATE TABLE container_sets (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES versions(id),
  state           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('starting','healthy','unhealthy','draining','stopped','failed')),
  started_at      INTEGER,
  healthy_at      INTEGER,
  last_request_at INTEGER,                           -- scale-to-zero idle timer (15 min)
  stopped_at      INTEGER,
  cold_starts     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  UNIQUE (part_id, version_id)
) STRICT;
CREATE TABLE containers (
  id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                     -- the runtime's container id
  set_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES container_sets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  service      TEXT NOT NULL,
  role         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('main','worker','cron','dependency')),
  image_digest TEXT NOT NULL,
  state        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('created','running','exited','dead')),
  restarts     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  started_at   INTEGER,
  exited_at    INTEGER,
  exit_code    INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
- `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` ordering at start (dependencies like Postgres first).
- The live switch for a version with a backend waits for the frontend build `ok` *and* the backend set healthy (and the `after_check` gate if requested), inside the writer, as in §3d.
- Events: `backend.started`, `backend.stopped`, `backend.unhealthy` in `events`.

## Not in scope

Proxying requests and holding them during a cold start at the routing layer (T101 owns the proxy; this task provides "ensure running" and the 10 s hold primitive). Volumes/export (T102), logs ring and metrics (T110), image prune (T116).

## Design notes and decisions

- The 60 s health window and 30 s drain are defaults; the old set serves until the new one is healthy (blue/green per version).
- Images for live + previous 2 versions are kept so a rollback is fast; older versions rebuild/re-pull automatically (or report that the tarball is needed for `uploaded_image`).
- Idle timer uses `last_request_at`, updated by T101 per request (batched).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "A version whose health check fails never goes live and the old set keeps serving; restoring the previous version brings its backend back; an idle part stops after 15 min and its next request cold-starts in < 3 s on the CI box".

- [ ] Failing health check -> build `failed`, `backend_unhealthy` with last 50 log lines; `live` unchanged; old set still answers.
- [ ] Healthy new set -> live switch, old set drains 30 s then `stopped`.
- [ ] `part_edit {restore: n}` starts version n's images; volumes untouched.
- [ ] Idle 15 min -> stopped; next request cold-starts < 3 s (CI box), `cold_starts` incremented.
- [ ] `always_on` parts never scale to zero; cron services fire on schedule while scaled to zero.
- [ ] Restart counts recorded; crash loop flagged.

## Tests

- `pf_runner::lifecycle::tests::state_machine_transitions` (unit, fake runtime).
- Integration `crates/pf-runner/tests/lifecycle.rs` (Docker + Podman): unhealthy gate, rollback, idle stop with a test clock, cold start timing; asserts `event="backend.set" state="healthy"|"unhealthy"|"stopped"` and `event="backend.cold_start" latency_ms=...`; artifacts: container logs and runner JSONL in `target/e2e-logs/lifecycle/`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Lifecycle; §3d build worker live switch; §5e `container_sets`, `containers`, `parts.backend_lifecycle`; §5h Images retention.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): A version whose health check fails never goes live and the old set keeps serving; restoring the previous version brings its backend back; an idle part stops after 15 min and its next request cold-starts in < 3 s on the CI box
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T99: Backend sources and builds: compose subset, rootless BuildKit, allowlisted images, image upload
- Unblocks: 
  - T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
  - T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
  - T110: Backend observability: per-part log rings, restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN; Backends page
  - T116: Runner retention: image pruning (live + previous 2), BuildKit cache 10 GiB LRU, backend log rings, volume quotas

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- **Correctness fix:** the 60 s health wait runs **outside** the single writer task; only the pointer flip (`parts.live_*`) and the `container_sets` state update run inside the writer transaction, exactly as §3d does for builds. A health wait inside the writer would block every write.
- `x-pf.schedule` is a 5-field cron expression in UTC; a run is skipped if the previous run of that service is still running (logged `event="backend.cron" outcome="skipped_overlap"`).
- Crash-loop detection is **owned here, once**: 5 restarts within 10 minutes (configurable under `[backends]`) marks the set crash-looping and emits `backend.crashloop`; T110 only surfaces it (Health row, Debug tab, T121 alert).
- Split into T100.a / T100.b / T100.c (see the subtasks); this parent is the integration/closure bead.
acceptance_criteria: A version whose health check fails never goes live and the old set keeps serving; restoring the previous version brings its backend back; an idle part stops after 15 min and its next request cold-starts in < 3 s on the CI box
