title: T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
description:
## Goal and why

A part's own code calls its backend at `/api/*`; the prelude turns that into `/c/<cap>/api/*` like any same-host URL. Routing it under the cap means "there's no unauthenticated route into a backend", a guest reaches it and a revoked cap doesn't, and the backend learns who's asking from the one place that decided it without ever holding a credential. *Why a signed header, not a session:* "the backend learns who's asking and what they may do from the one place that decided it, without holding anything an attacker could replay elsewhere. A per-part key stops one part from minting identities for another."

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it after all subtasks are closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T101.a** Route + cap check + role matrix + header/credential stripping on `/c/<cap>/<api_prefix>*`.
- **T101.b** `X-PF-Identity` JWT (per-part key, mounted secret) and `X-PF-Request-Id`.
- **T101.c** The proxy itself: HTTP, WebSocket upgrades, SSE, cold-start hold, limits.

Verbatim from §3f Routing: on `/c/<cap>/api/*` (the prefix is set per part, `parts.api_prefix`, default `/api/`, `CHECK (api_prefix GLOB '/*/')`), partifactory:
1. verifies the cap exactly as for content (host, epochs, window) and applies the role × runtime matrix (§3a), so a guest reaches the backend and a revoked cap doesn't;
2. strips the cap from the path, every `Cookie`, any `Authorization` carrying a `pf_` token, and every incoming `X-PF-*` header;
3. adds `X-PF-Identity`, a compact JWT (HS256 with a per-part key, 60 s expiry) carrying `sub` (`user:<id>`, `guest:<link>:<g>` or `link:<id>`), `name` (a display name, or "Guest 4f2a"), `role` (`view` · `comment` · `edit` · `manage` · `guest` · `public`), `part` and `exp`, plus `X-PF-Request-Id`;
4. proxies to the part's `main` service on its private network, **WebSocket upgrades and SSE included**, with the host's usual 50 s idle and 8 MiB body limits.
The backend checks the identity header with its key (mounted at `/run/secrets/pf_identity_key`) and **never sees a credential**.

Role matrix backend column: public-link viewer (Can view) "as `role: public`"; guest (Can contribute) "as `role: guest`"; `view`/`comment`/`edit`/`manage` as themselves.

## Not in scope

Starting/stopping sets (T100 provides "ensure running"); rate limits per part for backend requests come from T30's framework (configured here as a route class); observability UI (T110); the security suite (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

- Interpretation recorded in §10 round 2c: the decision's `https://<name>-part.<domain>/api/*` is what the part's code writes; on the wire it's `/c/<cap>/api/*`.
- `X-PF-Request-Id` comes from T106's request-id machinery, so a backend log line links to the trace.
- Unsandboxed parts (`isolation='unsandboxed'`) use the same route; `Origin` rules follow `/_rt` (null, or the part's own origin for unsandboxed).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "An echo backend sees correct identity claims for a member, a guest and a public viewer, and never a cookie, cap or token; a forged `X-PF-Identity` is replaced; a WebSocket round-trips; a revoked cap is refused before the backend".

- [ ] All subtasks closed.
- [ ] Echo backend (test image) reports `sub/name/role/part/exp` correct for a member (`role: edit` etc.), a guest (`guest:<link>:<g>`, "Guest 4f2a", `role: guest`), a public viewer (`link:<id>`, `role: public`).
- [ ] Canary cookie, cap and `pf_` token never reach the echo backend.
- [ ] Incoming `X-PF-Identity` / any `X-PF-*` replaced.
- [ ] WebSocket echo round-trips; SSE stream flows through.
- [ ] Revoked cap (epoch bump) -> refused, backend never contacted (echo backend request counter unchanged).

## Tests

- `crates/pf-serve/tests/backend_routing.rs` with an echo backend image (`tests/images/echo-backend/`), Docker + Podman; asserts logs `event="backend.proxy" outcome="ok" role="guest"` and `outcome="cap_revoked"`; canary assertion on echo backend's captured headers.
- e2e `tests/e2e/backend_ws.spec.ts`: a sandboxed page opens a WebSocket under `/c/<cap>/api/ws` (Origin: null) and round-trips.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Routing; §3a role × runtime matrix (backend calls column); §2 Serving (cap verify); §5 spike item 12 (WebSocket/SSE from sandboxed documents); §7 Backends (identity-header forgery); §10 round 2c interpretations.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.

  - T100: Backend lifecycle: container set per live version, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback
  - T16: Content listener (:8081): part-host routing, /c/<cap>/ serving, serve-time entry templating, canonical CSP
  - T26: Policy engine: subjects, roles, effective = max(part, space grants), everyone-signed-in, role x /_rt matrix, expiry timer, audit
  - T95: "Can contribute" public links: guest caps, guest limits, snapshot on switch, freeze, share-sheet controls
  - T106: Request ids end to end + tail-sampled trace store (errors, slow, 1 %), 7 days / 2 GiB
- Unblocks: 
  - T103: Backend security suite (§7 Backends) on Docker and Podman, staging and portability lane

title: T101.a: Backend route under the cap: verify, role matrix, strip cookies/caps/pf_ tokens/X-PF-*
description:
## Goal and why

Make `/c/<cap>/<api_prefix>*` the only way into a backend, authorised exactly like content, with every credential removed before the request leaves partifactory.

## Scope

- Route class `backend` in the content listener for paths under `/c/<cap>/` + `parts.api_prefix` (default `/api/`).
- Cap verification identical to content (known `kid` → MAC → `h` equals host label → `e ≥ epoch[part]` → `me ≥ epoch[minter]` → `b ≥ boot_floor` → window not over); unknown kid/bad MAC → 404; expired/stale on navigation → 302 to `/grant?mode=direct`, subresource → 401 + `X-PF-Reauth: 1`.
- Role matrix: every role that can open the part reaches the backend with its role; guest links as `guest`; Can-view links as `public`.
- Strip: the cap from the path (backend sees `/api/...`), every `Cookie` header, any `Authorization` whose value carries a `pf_` token (`pf_at_`, `pf_rt_`, `pf_pat_`), and every incoming header starting `X-PF-`.
- `Origin` handling as `/_rt`: accept `Origin: null` (or the part's own origin when unsandboxed); reject any other non-null `Origin` before reading the body.
- Per-part request rate limit route class (via T30).

## Not in scope

JWT minting (T101.b), proxy transport (T101.c).

## Design notes and decisions

- Reuse the content listener's verifier as is, so content and backend calls can't diverge in what a cap means.
- Stripping happens before any byte is forwarded, and the incoming `X-PF-*` set is replaced wholesale rather than filtered by name, so new internal headers are safe by default.
- `Authorization` headers that don't carry a `pf_` token are passed through, so a backend can use its own scheme for calls it makes to itself; anything with a `pf_` prefix is dropped.
- Revocation is checked here, before the backend is contacted, so a revoked viewer never reaches app code (§7).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Revoked/expired/foreign-host cap never reaches the backend.
- [ ] Header stripping table test passes (Cookie, Authorization with pf_ token kept/removed correctly, X-PF-*).

## Tests

`pf_serve::backend::tests::strips_credentials` (table), `::verify_like_content`; captured log `event="backend.authz" outcome=...`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Routing steps 1–2; §2 Serving (Verify, Errors on the part host).

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Origin rule, stated: an absent or `null` `Origin` is accepted; any other value is rejected before the body is read (the part's own origin only for `unsandboxed` parts).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Revoked/expired/foreign-host cap never reaches the backend.
- [ ] Header stripping table test passes (Cookie, Authorization with pf_ token kept/removed correctly, X-PF-*).

title: T101.b: Signed X-PF-Identity JWT (HS256, per-part key, 60 s) and X-PF-Request-Id
description:
## Goal and why

Give the backend a verifiable identity for every request without ever handing it a credential, and stop one part from minting identities for another.

## Scope

- Per-part identity key generated at first backend deploy, stored encrypted (like part secrets, with `PF_SESSION_KEY`), injected into the part's containers as a file at `/run/secrets/pf_identity_key` by the runner.
- `X-PF-Identity`: compact JWT, HS256 with the per-part key, `exp` = now + 60 s, claims `sub` (`user:<id>` | `guest:<link>:<g>` | `link:<id>`), `name` (display name, or "Guest 4f2a"), `role` (`view`·`comment`·`edit`·`manage`·`guest`·`public`), `part`, `exp`.
- `X-PF-Request-Id` set from the request's id (T106).
- An example verifier snippet in the docs (and in the echo backend test image).

## Not in scope

Route matching, cap verification and header stripping (T101.a); the proxy transport (T101.c); how backends verify the JWT in their own code, beyond the example verifier in the echo test image.

## Design notes and decisions

- HS256 with a per-part key (not one global key) so one part can't mint identities another part's backend would accept.
- 60 s expiry, minted per request: short enough that a leaked header is useless, with no clock-skew problems because partifactory and the backend share a host.
- The key is stored encrypted like part secrets and is never returned by any op; rotation is a redeploy (new key file).
- Display names for guests are derived from the signed `g` claim ("Guest 4f2a"), so a guest can't choose another's name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Claims correct per subject kind; JWT signed with another part's key rejected by the example backend; a forged incoming header replaced.

## Tests

`pf_serve::identity::tests::claims_per_subject`, `::other_part_key_rejected`; integration via the echo backend in T101.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Routing step 3; §7 Backends identity-header forgery.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T101.a: Backend route under the cap: verify, role matrix, strip cookies/caps/pf_ tokens/X-PF-*

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- **Per-part identity key storage (decided):** derive it, don't store it: `key = HKDF-SHA256(PF_SESSION_KEY, info = "pf-identity/" ‖ part_id ‖ generation)`, with only a small `generation` counter per part in `kv` (`identity_key_gen:<part_id>`). No key material at rest, per-part by construction, rotation = bump the generation and redeploy (the runner re-mounts `/run/secrets/pf_identity_key`), and nothing for any op to return. (Alternatives rejected: a reserved `part_secrets` row would show in the secret listing and collide with the upper-case name rule; a raw key in `kv` is material at rest.)
- The verifier snippet lives in the backends section of `docs/agent-contract.md` that T102.c adds, and in the echo test image.

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Claims correct per subject kind; JWT signed with another part's key rejected by the example backend; a forged incoming header replaced.

title: T101.c: Backend proxy: HTTP, WebSocket upgrades, SSE, cold-start hold, 50 s idle, 8 MiB body
description:
## Goal and why

Carry requests to the part's `main` service on its private network with the transports small apps need (websocket games, live leaderboards).

## Scope

- Proxy to the `main` service's exposed port on `pf-part-<id>`.
- WebSocket upgrade (handshake carries `Origin: null` from sandboxed documents; accepted per T101.a) and SSE streaming without buffering.
- Limits: 50 s idle, 8 MiB request body (the ingress contract's limits).
- Cold start: if the set is scaled to zero, call T100's ensure-running and hold the request up to 10 s; past that, 503 `backends_unavailable` with hint.
- Update `container_sets.last_request_at` (batched) for the idle timer; count requests/bytes for T110.

## Not in scope

Authorisation and header stripping (T101.a), the identity header (T101.b), starting and stopping container sets (T100, which provides ensure-running), backend metrics display (T110).

## Design notes and decisions

- The 10 s cold-start hold matches §3f ('the proxy holds the request for up to 10 s'); past it a 503 with a hint is better than a hung page.
- SSE and WebSocket pass through without buffering, and the 50 s idle limit matches the ingress contract, so a backend that needs longer keeps-alive sends heartbeats like partifactory's own SSE does.
- `last_request_at` updates are batched (for example once per 30 s per set) to keep writes off the hot path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] WebSocket echo and SSE stream round-trip through the proxy from a sandboxed page.
- [ ] A cold request is held and served once healthy (< 3 s on CI); > 10 s -> 503.
- [ ] Bodies > 8 MiB -> 413 `too_large`.

## Tests

`crates/pf-serve/tests/backend_proxy.rs` (WS, SSE, cold hold, body cap); logs `event="backend.proxy" transport="ws"|"sse"|"http"` and `event="backend.cold_hold" waited_ms=...`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Routing step 4, Lifecycle (scale to zero); §3 ingress contract; §5 spike item 12.

- Parent task: T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: T101.a: Backend route under the cap: verify, role matrix, strip cookies/caps/pf_ tokens/X-PF-*, T101.b: Signed X-PF-Identity JWT (HS256, per-part key, 60 s) and X-PF-Request-Id

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Unit tests added: hop-by-hop header handling on `Upgrade`, idle-timer reset on WebSocket frames, and the batched `last_request_at` writer.

- [ ] WebSocket echo and SSE stream round-trip through the proxy from a sandboxed page.
- [ ] A cold request is held and served once healthy (< 3 s on CI); > 10 s -> 503.
- [ ] Bodies > 8 MiB -> 413 `too_large`.

title: T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
description:
## Goal and why

Backends need real state (a Postgres leaderboard), keys (an API key only the admin holds), and occasionally a door to one household device, each with the safe default. This task makes backend data part of the `/data` backup story, makes secrets write-only and per part (decision 34: "an agent setting a key already holds it, so the protection that matters is write-only storage and per-part scope"), keeps LAN exceptions people-only, and gates every backend change for agents behind `backends:deploy`, off by default at consent.

## Scope

Subtasks (this parent is the integration/closure bead; close it only after all subtasks are closed and the acceptance criteria pass end to end):
- **T102.a** Per-part volumes, volume quotas, and consistent export/import of volumes.
- **T102.b** Write-only per-part secrets.
- **T102.c** `backends:deploy` scope, per-part and global quotas, and the agent op fields `part_edit {backend}` / `part_get {backend}`.
- **T102.d** LAN allowlist entries (people only, admin UI with step-up) and the `lan` action of `part_link_for`.

Key facts (verbatim from §3f):
- Each named volume belongs to one service and is a directory, `/data/parts/<id>/vol/<svc>`, so a folder backup of `/data` covers it. Volumes have a per-part quota (default 1 GiB). `partifactory export` includes volumes consistently: for each service it runs its export hook if it has one (`x-pf.export`, e.g. `pg_dump`), otherwise it stops the service, copies the directory and starts it again. Data snapshots cover `db`/`storage` documents only; **backend volumes are covered by folder backups and exports, not by data snapshots**, and the part's Details sheet says so.
- Secrets: agents with `backends:deploy` set or replace a part's secrets directly (`part_edit {backend: {secrets: {NAME: value}}}`). People with `edit` set them in the part's settings. **Nobody reads a secret back**: no op, surface or screen returns a value. Listing shows names, who set each one, and when. Injected as env vars or files under `/run/secrets/`, stored encrypted with `PF_SESSION_KEY`, scoped to one part, never in versions, exports, logs or Insights, except an export with `--include-secrets`, which requires `--encrypt`.
- Permissions: changing a part's backend (a `compose.yaml`, a `Dockerfile`, an image, its lifecycle, its secrets) needs `edit` on the part, and for agents the **`backends:deploy` scope, off by default at consent**.
- Per-part limits (defaults): 1 CPU, 512 MiB of memory, 256 pids, 1 GiB of volumes, 2 GiB of images. Global limits: 20 running containers, 4 GiB of backend memory, 20 GiB of images. A deploy past a limit fails with `quota_exceeded {kind}`.
- Agent ops: no new tools for backends. `part_edit {backend: {lifecycle, secrets}}` changes settings, and `part_get {backend: true}` returns the container set's state, health, cold starts and recent log lines (`logs: {service, since, grep}`), never secret values.
- LAN allowlist: a per-part entry (`host:port` or a CIDR, e.g. "may reach the home-automation server on :8123"). Only a person sets it, the admin in the admin UI (with step-up). An agent that needs one gives the admin the deep link `parts.<domain>/admin/backends/<part>#lan`, pre-filled (`part_link_for {action: "lan"}`).

## Not in scope

The export/import framework itself (T34/T35; this task adds the volume step), runner network rules (T98.c applies the entries), backend observability (T110).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 34 (no approval workflow): agents set secrets directly; protection = write-only + per-part.
- `part_secrets.value_enc` is read only by the runner's deploy path; no op's output type has a field for it (schema/type test).
- Volumes belong to the part, not the version: rollback (T100) doesn't touch them.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "An export of a running Postgres part imports with its rows intact; an agent without `backends:deploy` gets `forbidden {scope_needed}` on a `compose.yaml` edit; a secret set by an agent is injected but no op, surface or UI ever returns its value; a deploy past the global memory quota fails with `quota_exceeded`".

- [ ] All subtasks closed and each of the four dag criteria demonstrated in one integration run (Docker and Podman).

## Tests

See subtasks; plus `crates/pf-backup/tests/postgres_part_roundtrip.rs` (the dag criterion end to end) with logs `event="export.volume" method="hook"|"stop_copy_start"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Data, Secrets: write-only, per part, Permissions and quotas, Network (LAN allowlist); §3b Scopes (`backends:deploy`); §4 `part_link_for`; §5c export; §5e `part_volumes`, `part_secrets`, `lan_allow`; decision 34.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): An export of a running Postgres part imports with its rows intact; an agent without `backends:deploy` gets `forbidden {scope_needed}` on a `compose.yaml` edit; a secret set by an agent is injected but no op, surface or UI ever returns its value; a deploy past the global memory quota fails with `quota_exceeded`
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T100: Backend lifecycle: container set per live version, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback
  - T34: Backups: hourly consistent DB copy, `partifactory export` (tar.zst, age, parts-only), nightly export on by default
  - T43: OAuth token service (Slice 1 part): opaque tokens, /oauth/token, refresh rotation, metadata, 401s, consent sheet
  - T52: Sharing by agents: share:household inward grants and moves (labelled, undoable); no outward path for agents
- Unblocks: 
  - T103: Backend security suite (§7 Backends) on Docker and Podman, staging and portability lane
  - T104: Named e2e test `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (Postgres leaderboard) on Docker and Podman
- Subtasks (children of this bead; close this bead only after all of them are closed and the acceptance criteria above pass end to end):
  - T102.a: Per-part backend volumes with quotas, and consistent export/import of volumes
  - T102.b: Write-only per-part secrets: set/replace, inject as env or file, never read back
  - T102.c: `backends:deploy` scope, backend quotas, and `part_edit {backend}` / `part_get {backend}`
  - T102.d: LAN allowlist entries (people only, admin UI with step-up) and `part_link_for {action: "lan"}`

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T35 (the acceptance imports an export of a running Postgres part; `partifactory import` is T35.a's).
- Sibling edge added: T102.c depends on T102.b (`part_edit {backend: {secrets}}` needs the write-only store and injection).

title: T102.a: Per-part backend volumes with quotas, and consistent export/import of volumes
description:
## Goal and why

Backend state must survive rollbacks and come back from an export on another host.

## Scope

- Named volumes only (compose subset), one per service, at `/data/parts/<id>/vol/<svc>`, mounted by the runner into that service only.
- Table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE part_volumes (                          -- /data/parts/<id>/vol/<service>; one named volume per service
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  service     TEXT NOT NULL,
  quota_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1073741824,
  used_bytes  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  measured_at INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, service)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- Quota: 1 GiB per part default; measured periodically; past quota -> `quota_exceeded {kind: "volume"}` on deploy and a Health row.
- Export step: `parts/<id>/vol/<svc>/` in the tarball, taken consistently: run `x-pf.export` hook (e.g. `pg_dump`) if present, else stop the service, copy, start. Import writes them back before the set starts.
- Details sheet note: "volumes are covered by exports, not snapshots".

## Not in scope

Secrets (T102.b), quota enforcement for CPU/memory/images (T102.c), the export/import framework and its MANIFEST (T34/T35), data snapshots, which never cover volumes (T77).

## Design notes and decisions

- One named volume per service, as a plain directory under `/data`, so any folder backup of `/data` already covers it (§5c) and no volume driver is needed.
- Export prefers the service's own hook (`pg_dump`) because a stop-copy-start of a live database is consistent but causes downtime; the fallback exists so every service is exportable.
- Volumes are deliberately outside data snapshots: snapshots are for undoing bad writes to small documents, while volumes can be gigabytes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Export of a running Postgres part imports with rows intact (hook path) and a hook-less service round-trips via stop-copy-start.

## Tests

`crates/pf-backup/tests/postgres_part_roundtrip.rs`; `pf_runner::volumes::tests::quota_measure`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Data; §5c export contents; §5e `part_volumes`; §5h Backend volumes row.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Ownership: this subtask owns volume-quota **measurement and enforcement** (deploy-time `quota_exceeded {kind: "volume"}` and the runtime rule: periodic measurement with a soft quota that stops the service and refuses deploys, or a hard quota if the T98.a spike finds a portable mechanism); T116 only registers the store, adds the budget accounting and the T115 retention row. The Health row says which mechanism is in force.
- Import ordering (volumes restored before the set starts) is a step this subtask adds to `partifactory import` (T35.a), hence the T35 edge on the parent.

## Logging (test convention)

Every test in this bead asserts the structured server events for the paths it exercises (`event=…` with `request_id` and `outcome`, per T18's field convention) and keeps the captured JSONL under `target/test-logs/<test>/` (unit/integration) or `target/e2e-logs/<spec>/server.jsonl` plus Playwright trace/HAR (browser specs) on failure, so a red run explains itself. Log lines never carry part content, tokens, caps or secrets (T18 redaction; T112 canaries). Spikes and UI-only subtasks log each item's result the same way.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Export of a running Postgres part imports with rows intact (hook path) and a hook-less service round-trips via stop-copy-start.

title: T102.b: Write-only per-part secrets: set/replace, inject as env or file, never read back
description:
## Goal and why

Let agents and people put keys into a backend without any path to read them back out or reach another part.

## Scope

- Table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE part_secrets (                          -- write-only: set or replaced by agents (backends:deploy) or people (edit); never read back
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (name GLOB '[A-Z_]*' AND name NOT GLOB '*[^A-Z0-9_]*' AND length(name) <= 64),
  value_enc   BLOB NOT NULL,                         -- encrypted with PF_SESSION_KEY; no op returns it
  inject_as   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'env' CHECK (inject_as IN ('env','file')),
  set_by_user TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),    -- the person (author)
  set_by_conn TEXT,                                  -- agent connection, if an agent set it
  set_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (part_id, name)
) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID;
```
- Set via `part_edit {backend: {secrets: {NAME: value}}}` (agents need `backends:deploy`; people `edit`) and in the part's settings UI. Listing: names, who set each, when.
- Injection by the runner: env var, or a file under `/run/secrets/<NAME>`; compose `secrets:` names refer to these.
- Never in versions, logs, traces, Insights, or exports unless `--include-secrets` with `--encrypt` (refused otherwise).
- Audit row per set/replace (value omitted).

## Not in scope

Injection mechanics inside the runner's container spec beyond env/file (T98.b), the export framework (T34), the T112 fuzz harness itself (this task adds secret canaries to it).

## Design notes and decisions

- Decision 34: no approval gate for secrets. An agent setting a key already holds it, so the protection is that it can't be read back and can't reach another part.
- The 'no value field in any output type' rule is enforced by types, not by review, so a future op can't leak one by accident.
- Encryption uses `PF_SESSION_KEY`; rotating that key requires re-encrypting secrets at start (documented as part of rotation).
- `--include-secrets` requires `--encrypt` so plaintext secrets never sit in an export file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A secret set by an agent is injected (the backend sees it) and no op, surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI, UI, chrome API) returns its value; canary value absent from logs, traces, `insights.db`, `/metrics`, versions and a default export.

## Tests

`pf_model::secrets::tests::output_types_have_no_value_field` (compile-time/type test), `crates/pf-api/tests/secrets_write_only.rs` (canary across surfaces; joins T112 fuzz), `pf_backup::tests::include_secrets_requires_encrypt`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Secrets; §5e `part_secrets`; §7 Backends (secrets are write-only); decision 34.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] A secret set by an agent is injected (the backend sees it) and no op, surface (MCP, HTTP, CLI, UI, chrome API) returns its value; canary value absent from logs, traces, `insights.db`, `/metrics`, versions and a default export.

title: T102.c: `backends:deploy` scope, backend quotas, and `part_edit {backend}` / `part_get {backend}`
description:
## Goal and why

Agents change backends through the existing ops, gated by an explicit consented scope, and can't exhaust the box.

## Scope

- Scope `backends:deploy`: "create or change a part's backend (`compose.yaml`, a `Dockerfile`, an image, its lifecycle) and **set or replace its secrets** (write-only). Consent-time toggle, **off by default** for every client." Consent sheet line: "Deploy backends and set their secrets" (off unless requested).
- Any `part_edit` touching `compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, image refs, `backend` lifecycle or secrets without the scope -> `forbidden {scope_needed: "backends:deploy"}`; people need `edit`.
- `part_edit {backend: {lifecycle: "scale_to_zero" | "always_on", secrets: {NAME: value}}}`.
- `part_get {backend: true}` -> container set state, health, cold starts, recent log lines with `logs: {service, since, grep}`; never secret values.
- Quotas: per part 1 CPU, 512 MiB memory, 256 pids, 1 GiB volumes, 2 GiB images; global 20 running containers, 4 GiB backend memory, 20 GiB images; `always_on` counts against global; past any -> `quota_exceeded {kind}` (429, exit 6). Registry/OpenAPI/contract updated (contract section added in the same change, per §4b).

## Not in scope

Secret storage (T102.b), LAN allowlist (T102.d), the consent sheet UI as a whole (T43/T44 own it; this task adds the toggle), runner-side limit enforcement in the template (T98.b).

## Design notes and decisions

- No new tools for backends: backend changes go through `part_edit` and reads through `part_get`, keeping the op set small (§4: near-duplicate tools cause wrong picks).
- `backends:deploy` is off by default for every client, because a backend runs arbitrary code with internet egress; a person must tick it on the consent sheet.
- Quota errors name the `kind` (cpu, memory, pids, volume, images, containers) so an agent can tell the person exactly what to free.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent without scope -> `forbidden {scope_needed}` on a `compose.yaml` edit; with scope, succeeds.
- [ ] A deploy past the global memory quota fails with `quota_exceeded {kind: "memory"}`.

## Tests

`crates/pf-ops/tests/backend_scope.rs`; `pf_runner::quota::tests::global_memory`; conformance scenario steps added for backends.

## References

PLAN.md §3b Scopes; §3f Permissions and quotas, Agent ops; §4 op table (`part_edit`, `part_get`); §4b errors.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Tests add log assertions: `event="op" op="part_edit" outcome="forbidden" scope_needed="backends:deploy"` and `event="backend.quota" kind="memory" outcome="refused"`.
- "Recent log lines" in `part_get {backend: true}` come from the runner `logs` API (T98.b) until T110's rings exist; T110 switches the source.
- Acceptance adds (moved from T98.d): with the runner stopped, a backend op returns `backends_unavailable` (503, CLI exit 7).
- The op-time `image_not_allowed` scan (T99) is gated here behind the `backends:deploy` scope check for agent writes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Agent without scope -> `forbidden {scope_needed}` on a `compose.yaml` edit; with scope, succeeds.
- [ ] A deploy past the global memory quota fails with `quota_exceeded {kind: "memory"}`.

title: T102.d: LAN allowlist entries (people only, admin UI with step-up) and `part_link_for {action: "lan"}`
description:
## Goal and why

Occasionally a backend legitimately needs one household device ("may reach the home-automation server on :8123"). That's an outward-ish decision, so only a person makes it, in the UI, with step-up; an agent can only hand over a deep link.

## Scope

- Table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE lan_allow (                             -- per-part exceptions to the LAN block; set by a person (admin UI), never an agent
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  part_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES parts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  target      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'host:port' or a CIDR
  note        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'may reach the home-automation server'
  added_by    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  added_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  revoked_at  INTEGER
) STRICT;
```
- Admin → Backends page: every part with containers, its state, limits and secret names (values never shown), and the LAN allowlist per part (add with step-up; revoke with undo toast). `/admin/backends/<part>#lan` opens it pre-filled.
- Adding/removing pushes the rule change to the runner (T98.c); audit rows.
- `part_link_for {action: "lan", name}` -> `{action: "lan", url: "https://parts.<domain>/admin/backends/<part>#lan", who: "admin"}`; read-only, grants nothing.
- No agent scope, token or op can create an entry (tested on every surface).

## Not in scope

Applying firewall accept rules in the runner (T98.c), the rest of the admin area shell (T28/T36), other `part_link_for` actions (T117, T125, T94.d).

## Design notes and decisions

- LAN access is a people-only action (decision 34), like public links: it's the one way a backend could reach household devices, so an agent can only hand over the `#lan` deep link.
- Adding an entry needs step-up (it's on §3a's admin-action list); revocation takes effect at once in the runner's rules.
- Entries are narrow by design (`host:port` or a CIDR), and the note field records why, so the admin page reads as an audit of every exception.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin adds an entry with step-up; the target becomes reachable; revoking closes it.
- [ ] Every surface refuses agent attempts; the deep link opens the sheet pre-filled; a non-admin sees the normal 403.

## Tests

e2e `tests/e2e/admin_lan_allow.spec.ts` (virtual authenticator, click budget), `crates/pf-ops/tests/no_agent_lan.rs`; logs `event="lan_allow.add" outcome="step_up_required"|"ok"`.

## References

PLAN.md §3f Network (LAN allowlist); §4 `part_link_for`; §4a.6 Admin (Backends); §3a admin actions needing step-up; §7 Agents.

## Dependency context

- Parent task: T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields (this subtask inherits all of the parent's upstream dependencies).
- Also waits for: nothing else
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Admin adds an entry with step-up; the target becomes reachable; revoking closes it.
- [ ] Every surface refuses agent attempts; the deep link opens the sheet pre-filled; a non-admin sees the normal 403.

title: T110: Backend observability: per-part log rings, restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN; Backends page
description:
## Goal and why

Backends (P2a) add long-running containers whose failures happen out of sight. This task makes them visible in the same places as everything else: the per-part Debug tab (T109), an Insights Backends page (T108's shell), the Health page and the ops alert (T121) — so a crash-looping backend is noticed and diagnosable, and denied LAN attempts (a signal of a misbehaving or prompt-injected backend) are counted.

Phase P2a; feeds T104 (`communal_pixel_editor_backend`) and T116.

## Scope

- **Backend log capture**: the runner (T98) streams each container's stdout/stderr to partifactory, which writes per-part ring segments with T107.a's `SegmentWriter` at `/data/logs/parts/<id>/backend-NNNN.jsonl.zst` (`log_segments.stream = 'backend'`, `part_id` set). Cap: **50 MiB per part, 7 days** (§5h "Backend logs (captured per part) | 50 MiB per part, 7 days | ring segments | Debug tab download; `logs export --part`"). Daemon-side `json-file` `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3` remains as set by the runner template.
- Lines carry service name, container id, stream (stdout/stderr) and the request id when the backend echoes `X-PF-Request-Id`; lines are backend-authored text, so they are **only** shown to the admin (Debug tab) and exported by `logs export --part`; they are not part of Insights analytics and the T112 canary rule for partifactory's own logs still applies to partifactory's log lines.
- **Metrics per part** from the runner's `stats` API and `containers`/`container_sets` tables: restarts (`containers.restarts`), cold starts (`container_sets.cold_starts`), CPU and memory, egress bytes (metered per part network), **denied LAN attempts** (counted per part from the runner's firewall drop counters). Exposed as Prometheus gauges/counters (`pf_backend_restarts_total{part}`, … ) and as `events_raw` `kind='backend'` rows + rollup metrics (`cold_starts`, `restarts`, `egress_bytes`, `lan_denied`).
- **Insights Backends page** (§5g): "running containers; cold starts; restarts; memory and CPU per part; egress bytes; denied LAN attempts" — using T108.a's shell, table view and CSV/JSON export.
- **Debug tab**: backend logs (tail and search, download), restarts and last log lines per service.
- **Crash-loop detection**: N restarts in M minutes (recommended default 5 in 10 min) marks the set crash-looping, shows on Health, and raises the ops alert "the build worker or a backend crash-looping" (T121).

## Not in scope

The runner and its firewall (T98), lifecycle (T100), routing (T101), runner retention and the backend rows of the retention test (T116), the alert transport (T121).

## Design notes and decisions

- Reuse the app-log segment code so backend logs get rotation, indexing and export for free.
- Backend log text is untrusted (agent/third-party code output); render escaped, never as HTML.
- Denied-LAN counts come from firewall counters (DOCKER-USER chain or the runner's nftables table), not from parsing logs.

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "A crash-looping backend shows its restarts and last log lines in the Debug tab and raises the ops alert; denied LAN attempts are counted per part."

- [ ] Backend logs captured per part, capped at 50 MiB / 7 days, downloadable and exportable with `logs export --part`.
- [ ] Restarts, cold starts, CPU, memory, egress bytes and denied LAN attempts are recorded per part and shown on the Backends page with table view and export.
- [ ] A crash-looping test backend shows restarts and last lines in the Debug tab and fires the ops alert (with T121's webhook set) and a Health row.
- [ ] A backend that tries a LAN canary increments its denied-LAN count.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-runner/tests/log_capture.rs::per_part_ring_50mib_7d` (scaled cap).
- `crates/pf-runner/tests/crashloop.rs::restarts_and_alert` (test image exits 1 in a loop; asserts `event="backend.crashloop" part_id=...` and one signed alert POST to a local receiver).
- `crates/pf-runner/tests/lan_denied.rs::counted_per_part` (runs on Docker and Podman in CI).
- `crates/pf-ui/tests/insights_backends.rs::page_matches_fixture`.

## References

PLAN.md §5g Backends page and Debug tab; §3f Lifecycle ("Logs from every container are captured per part …"), Network (denied attempts counted); §5h Backend logs and container stdout rows; §4 ops alerts.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

title: T116: Runner retention: image pruning (live + previous 2), BuildKit cache 10 GiB LRU, backend log rings, volume quotas
description:
## Goal and why

Backends bring the heaviest growing stores: container images, the BuildKit cache, backend log rings and per-part volumes. Without retention they would quietly consume the disk the global budget protects. This task caps each one, registers them with the janitor and the store registry, counts them in the disk budget, and adds their rows to the retention table test — while never pruning what a rollback needs.

Phase P2a; feeds M2a. Depends on T98 (runner), T100 (lifecycle), T113 (janitor), T115 (retention test).

## Scope

§5h rows, verbatim:
- "BuildKit cache | 10 GiB, LRU | `buildkit prune` on a schedule | —"
- "Images (and uploaded tarballs) | the images of live + the previous 2 versions per part; the rest pruned weekly | runner prune | —"
- "Backend volumes | per-part quota (default 1 GiB) | — | export"
- "Backend logs (captured per part) | 50 MiB per part, 7 days | ring segments | Debug tab download; `logs export --part`"
- "Container stdout from the Docker daemon | `json-file` with `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`, set by the runner on every container and in partifactory's own compose file | daemon-side | the part's Debug tab; `logs export --part`"

Work:
- Janitor job `runner_images` (weekly, `action='image_prune'`): per part, keep images whose digest belongs to the live version and the previous 2 versions (`backend_images` rows; set `pruned_at` for the rest and call the runner's `prune` API). Uploaded tarballs (`backend_images.tar_hash`) follow the same rule: unpruned rows keep their tarball blob referenced for blob GC (T59: "unpruned `backend_images.tar_hash`"). **The live version's image is never pruned.** Older versions are rebuilt from source, re-pulled by digest, or need the tarball again (§3f rollback).
- Janitor job `buildkit_cache` (`action='cache_prune'`): `buildkit prune --keep-storage 10GiB` (LRU) via the runner on a schedule (daily recommended).
- Backend log rings: register the 50 MiB / 7 day job for `parts/<id>/backend-*` segments (writer from T110; if T110 lands later, this task owns the job and T110 the capture).
- Volume quotas: the runner measures `part_volumes.used_bytes` periodically; at quota, writes inside the container fail (enforced by the runner's disk limit / project quota); Health shows each part's usage vs quota.
- Register every store in the T114 store registry and add their bytes (images + BuildKit cache) to the global disk budget ("counting `/data` plus the runner's images and build cache").
- Add the backend rows to the T115 retention table test.

## Not in scope

The runner itself and its container template (T98), lifecycle and rollback (T100), log capture (T110), volume export (T102).

## Design notes and decisions

- "Previous 2 versions" is by version order of versions that had a container set (`container_sets`), so a restore to one of the last three versions starts instantly.
- Never prune an image referenced by a starting/healthy/draining container set, regardless of version order (reference-safety guard).
- Run on Docker and Podman (Podman's prune API is Docker-compatible; verify in CI).

## Acceptance criteria

dag2.py: "Each backend row of the §5h table has a passing fill-past-cap case; the live version's image is never pruned."

- [ ] Image prune keeps live + previous 2 per part; the live image is never pruned, even when it's the oldest.
- [ ] BuildKit cache stays ≤ 10 GiB (scaled in test) after the job.
- [ ] Backend log rings ≤ 50 MiB per part and ≤ 7 days.
- [ ] Volume over quota is refused and shown on Health.
- [ ] Each backend row has a passing fill-past-cap case in the T115 test, on Docker and on Podman.
- [ ] Image and cache bytes count toward the disk budget.

## Tests

- `crates/pf-janitor/tests/retention_table.rs::fill_past_cap::runner_images`, `::buildkit_cache`, `::backend_logs`, `::backend_volumes`, `::container_stdout_limits` (inspects containers for `max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`).
- `crates/pf-runner/tests/image_prune.rs::live_image_never_pruned`, `::keeps_previous_two`.
- CI matrix: Docker and Podman. Asserts `event="janitor.job" store="runner_images" action="image_prune"`.

## References

PLAN.md §5h table (backend rows) and global disk budget; §3f Lifecycle (images kept for live + previous 2), Data (volume quota), runner template (`json-file` 10m × 3); §3g BuildKit cache; §5e `backend_images`, `container_sets`, `part_volumes`; §7 Operations (T115, T116).

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Each backend row of the §5h table has a passing fill-past-cap case; the live version's image is never pruned
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T98: Runner sidecar: sole Engine API holder, hardened container template, per-part networks
  - T100: Backend lifecycle: container set per live version, health gate, scale to zero, cron, rollback
  - T113: Janitor: one scheduled task for every prune, rotation, GC and checkpoint job, recording janitor_runs
  - T115: Retention table test: every existing §5h store filled past its cap comes back under
- Unblocks: 
  - M2a: Milestone - P2a Backends done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edges added: T110 (backend log rings, whose writer and rotation it owns) and T102 (volume quota measurement, owned by T102.a). This task registers those stores with the janitor/store registry and adds their T115 rows; it never implements a second writer.
- Live image never pruned, even when oldest; reference-safety guard (unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: Each backend row of the §5h table has a passing fill-past-cap case; the live version's image is never pruned

title: T103: Backend security suite (§7 Backends) on Docker and Podman, staging and portability lane
description:
## Goal and why

Backends are the largest new attack surface of v1: hostile images, prompt-injected agents writing compose files, and the household LAN next door. Every §7 Backends line becomes an automated test, run on both runtimes, so the hardening template, the network block, the identity header and write-only secrets are proven, not assumed. Feeds M2a.

## Scope

Automate every line of PLAN.md §7 Backends (verbatim):
- **Container escape attempts** from a hostile test image fail: mounts, `unshare`, raw sockets, kernel modules, writes to the root filesystem, setuid binaries (`no-new-privileges`), host paths, the Engine API socket. A fork bomb hits the pids limit and a memory blow-up kills only that container.
- **LAN reachability from a backend must fail**: every RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local and ULA range, the household's real subnets (from site config), the host's addresses, `169.254.169.254` and every other part's network. An allowlisted entry is reachable and nothing else is. Denied attempts are counted. The same holds during a BuildKit build.
- **Egress is on by default**: a request to a public canary succeeds from a backend and from a build.
- **Identity-header forgery**: a request carrying its own `X-PF-Identity` or any `X-PF-*` header reaches the backend with them replaced; a JWT signed with another part's key is rejected by the example backend; a request without a valid cap never reaches a backend. Backends never see a `Cookie`, a cap or a `pf_` token (canary).
- The compose parser refuses every unsupported key, an image from a registry outside the allowlist fails with `image_not_allowed`, and the runner refuses any request outside its template.
- **Secrets are write-only**: no op, surface or screen returns a value, including to the agent that set it; values never appear in versions, exports (without `--include-secrets --encrypt`), logs, traces or Insights (canary).
- Every line runs on Docker and on Podman.

Deliverables: hostile test image `tests/images/hostile/` (scripts attempting each escape), canary services (public and LAN canary), the suite under `tests/security/backends/`, wired into CI on staging (example deployment) and the portability lane (T93, Podman pass).

## Not in scope

Fixing findings beyond reporting them as bugs against T98–T102; the non-backend §7 lines (T38).

## Design notes and decisions

- The household subnets come from private site config at run time; the public repo has only placeholders.
- Lines not marked *(adapter)* also run in the portability lane, so no protection depends on an adapter.

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Every §7 Backends line is an automated test, run on Docker and on Podman, against staging and in the portability lane".

- [ ] One named test per §7 Backends bullet (and per escape vector), each green on Docker and Podman.
- [ ] Runs in CI against staging and in the portability lane; results stored as JUnit + JSONL.

## Tests

- `tests/security/backends/escape_*.rs` (mounts, unshare, raw_socket, kmod, rootfs_write, setuid, host_path, engine_socket, fork_bomb, memory_blowup).
- `lan_block_*` (per range, host, metadata, sibling, during_build), `lan_allowlisted_only`, `egress_public_canary`, `identity_forgery_*`, `compose_unsupported_keys`, `image_not_allowed`, `runner_template_refusal`, `secrets_never_returned` (canary across surfaces and stores).
- Each asserts the expected server log events (`event="runner.refused"`, `event="runner.lan_denied"`, `event="backend.authz" outcome=...`) and keeps runner/backend logs and ruleset dumps in `target/e2e-logs/<test>/` on failure.

## References

PLAN.md §7 Security checklist: Backends; §3f; §5f portability lane; decision 28.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Every §7 Backends line is an automated test, run on Docker and on Podman, against staging and in the portability lane
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
  - T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
- Unblocks: 
  - M2a: Milestone - P2a Backends done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T93 (the suite runs in the portability lane).
- Adds the Dockerfile `FROM` bypass case to `image_not_allowed` (T99 decision).
acceptance_criteria: Every §7 Backends line is an automated test, run on Docker and on Podman, against staging and in the portability lane

title: T104: Named e2e test `communal_pixel_editor_backend` (Postgres leaderboard) on Docker and Podman
description:
## Goal and why

The P2a "Done when" as one test: the Slice 1 pixel board (T97) grows a real backend in one agent call, and every backend promise holds at once: server build, live data for guests, rollback of code with the version, and the LAN wall. It's milestone M2a's acceptance test alongside T103 and T116.

## Scope

Scenario (from §6 P2a and decision 31):
1. Start from the T97 board (created by an agent connected by device code, shared by the admin as Can contribute).
2. The agent adds a leaderboard service on Postgres to the pixel board in **one `part_edit`** (a `compose.yaml` with `main` + `postgres` dependency with a named volume and `x-pf.export: pg_dump`, plus page changes calling `/api/leaderboard`), using a connection with `backends:deploy`.
3. The server builds it (`server_build`), the set passes its health check and goes live.
4. Signed-out guests (mobile WebKit profiles) paint; each guest's pixel count shows on the leaderboard live (backend sees `role: guest`, `sub: guest:<link>:<g>`).
5. Restoring the previous version (`part_edit {restore: n}`) rolls the backend back too (the old set's images start; volume data stays).
6. From inside the backend: a public canary is reachable, a LAN canary is not.
Runs on Docker and on Podman, in CI and in the portability lane.

## Not in scope

The frontend-only test (T97); the general security suite (T103).

## Design notes and decisions

- This is the backend twin of T97: it reuses T97's harness, agent driver and guest profiles rather than a new one, so the two tests stay comparable.
- The leaderboard uses one row per guest keyed on the `sub` from `X-PF-Identity`, proving the backend trusts only the signed header (never a client-supplied id).
- Rollback is checked by container set id and version, and volume rows survive it, because volumes belong to the part, not the version (§3f). The test states that explicitly so nobody 'fixes' it into data rollback.
- The LAN canary lives on the test host's network, never a real household address; real subnets are covered by T103 from private site config.
- Timing assertions (live updates, cold start) use generous CI bounds; tight numbers are tracked, not gated (§5a).

## Acceptance criteria

From dag2.py: "Passes in CI on Docker and on Podman, and in the portability lane".

- [ ] Every step above asserted; leaderboard counts per guest match their writes; rollback verified by version and container set ids; LAN canary blocked, public canary ok.
- [ ] Green on Docker and Podman, CI and portability lane.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/communal_pixel_editor_backend.spec.ts` (Playwright: admin on Chromium with virtual authenticator, two guests on mobile WebKit) plus agent steps via MCP; asserts server log events `event="build.finished" target="backend" method="server_build"`, `event="backend.set" state="healthy"`, `event="backend.proxy" role="guest"`, `event="runner.lan_denied"`; artifacts: `target/e2e-logs/communal_pixel_editor_backend/{server.jsonl,runner.jsonl,backend.log}`, Playwright traces, HAR.

## References

PLAN.md §6 P2a Done when; §3f The acceptance test; §6a T104; decision 31.

## Dependency context (from the task graph)

- Phase: P2a (epic "P2a Backends"). Slice 1: no (after Slice 1). Priority P2.
- Task-graph acceptance test (verbatim): Passes in CI on Docker and on Podman, and in the portability lane
- Depends on (must be closed first): 
  - T97: Named e2e test communal_pixel_editor (the Slice 1 acceptance test)
  - T101: Backend routing under the cap: /c/<cap>/api/*, stripping, signed X-PF-Identity, WebSocket/SSE
  - T102: Backend data, write-only secrets, LAN allowlist, `backends:deploy`, quotas, backend op fields
  - T110: Backend observability: per-part log rings, restarts, cold starts, CPU/memory, egress, denied LAN; Backends page
- Unblocks: 
  - M2a: Milestone - P2a Backends done

## Polish-round review: decisions and additions

- Edge added: T93 (the test runs in the portability lane on Podman).
- Fixture robustness: pin `postgres:<major>` by digest and mirror it into a local registry in CI (Docker Hub pulls are the flaky part). If the T98.a spike shows the official image can't run as UID ≥ 10000 with a read-only rootfs, the fixture uses a tiny `FROM postgres` Dockerfile that pre-creates its runtime dirs (also a realistic agent pattern).
acceptance_criteria: Passes in CI on Docker and on Podman, and in the portability lane
